You guys really need to revamp the menu! The only thing i would give it to them for is the ingredients were fresh and not frozen /microvawed like other restaurants. Sorry, but we won't be back!

I always love coming here. No matter how busy the staff is always willing to stop and say hello as well as serve the finest food. I always feel like I'm at home here. I usually get the eggs Benedict and am never dissapointed, but always challenge myself to try the specials. Breakfast is my favorite!

Really good sushi, nice atmosphere, good service. Can't say enough good about the place. Not sure why people have a hard time finding it. There are flags and signs all over the corner. Get the firecracker roll and the volcano roll, both are fantastic.
There's really nothing better they could do than maybe have more comfortable chairs. Their food is phenomenal,  top notch and very reasonable

The Farmacy was really disappointing.  My friend and I ate brunch here while visiting Philadelphia.  The potatoes with both of our meals were burnt.  I had a tofu scramble that tasted like air.  The restaurant ran out of bread.  Would not go again or recommend this restaurant.
The Salmon burger was amazing, opted for greens instead of the bun and added feta cheese.

Best meal in New Haven right now. First of all the interior is stunning. But the food is just spot on. Everything is simple, clean, and delicious, without trying to be French or Italian or whatever the concept is. It has influences from alot of places, but is most of all what was fresh and delicious around New Haven. The atmosphere allows a great long casual dinner, and on top of it all, the price is extremely reasonable. Two people with multiple drinks, apps, entrees, and desert and exactly 100 buck. I would pay alot more to eat that meal again.

Convenient location and parking in the city. Taste is same as average American Vietnamese cuisine. If you are looking for delicious pho, there are several alternate restaurants within 5 minutes drive. The bad service soured the okay food experience so I do not recommend the restaurant for a group experience.

I love it here, been coming for years!  The food here is fresh, modern and tasty. The weather was beautiful, we sat outside - they have a large patio overlooking busy Farmington Avenue; great people watching, not too noisy, plenty of shopping to do before and after lunch:)   The service was prompt and friendly.  We ordered light lunch fare and were not disappointed, as the food is always delicious.  A satisfying meal and experience all around.  A perfect spot for an upscale experience - price/value are in perfect accordance.  Recommended!

Good food, but my lasagna was bit burned, my girlfriend ordered a pizza and it was pretty good in a decent size, service was so slow, probably why my lasagna came burned, very very loud but overall a nice experience.

Delicious! Will definitely be stopping here again. Had bruschetta & pizza di carne with my husband. My daughters had the sausage zuppa and a flatbread pizza. We all enjoyed our food. Our waitress was very helpful and friendly. It is right off of Route 89 so a quick stop before we continue on our journey.

We put in our name and were told the wait was an hour so we decided to get drinks upstairs. After 20 minutes, they came to get us for our table. It's a gastropub so it's very small, but comfortable. We shared appetizers and small plates. The chicken liver on toast is very, very good, I loved it. We also got the Devils on Horseback which is a pickled pear in a prune wrapped by bacon. It was good, but too sweet for my own liking. I loved the gnudi with sheep's milk ricotta. It was so fresh. The pesto was absolutely perfect and it was not too heavy and not too light.
BYOB

So good! When I am missing some good Jamaican breakfast food ( and don't want to make it myself) I go here. Yummy. The people are so sweet AND the food leaves my feeling as if I just nourished myself. Great, healthy food without losing the amazing taste. The baked goods are also amazing. I believe it's family run as well. We have to continue to support businesses like this!

I really don't like having to give this place a bad review, but today's experience was pretty gross. Two words: Moldy bread. My girlfriend had not one, but two pieces of moldy bread included with her breakfast. Hopefully the first piece she ate didn't have any on it, but I guess we won't know unless she gets sick. We're talking some pretty big spores and I really wish I would have thought to take a picture. We told the waitress and she was polite enough about it, but not as apologetic as I would have figured. She offered to replace the meal for my girlfriend, but by this point she had understandably lost her appetite. My meal was ok, but needless to say, I was a little suspect of my meal at that point now too. I ended up going up to the counter to speak to the waitress and tell her that my girlfriend wasn't going to eat her meal. She said they were planning to take 10% off the bill, but I told her that was not good enough and I shouldn't have to pay for a meal that didn't get eaten. She obliged, which I appreciated, but honestly the classier move would have been to comp us the whole meal. Getting an order wrong is forgivable. Taking a long time would be understandable if a place is busy. Serving moldy food is unacceptable. It really is too bad that I'm probably going to have to scratch this place off my list of places to eat (at least for a while), because it does have a nice atmosphere in there and I'm told the ice cream is pretty good.
A little piece of Italy in NY! Employees are very nice, prices are ok, and the place is cozy. Tiramisu is the best I've tasted since Italy! Truly recommend it!

I went here for a vegan"Nice Kream" date. My friend ordered the 9oz O' Ginger Snap! and I ordered the 9oz Mr. Cookie Munster. First of all, if I hadn't walked in knowing it was a vegan restaurant, I would never known my nice kream was vegan. Both choices we made were phenomenal. We each tasted the others and found them both to be divine. The presentation of our order was beautiful. I'm very much looking forward to going back for a proper meal (Hopefully tomorrow)! As with most vegan/organic eating establishments, Positivitea is a bit on the pricey side. Our two 9oz nice kreams came to $18. If spending that kind of money on a regular basis isn't in your budget (it's not in mine) I would recommend saving a visit here for a special occasion, a little self indulgence or a well deserved treat. I HIGHLY recommend Positivitea. I'm looking forward to trying one of their vegan burgers and one of their uniquely named smoothies.
Great dumplings, Great Taste. Horrible decor and seating. Not for nothing, but the bathroom should be renovated.
Got the Pope Francis sandwich.. Sooo good! The mozzarella was fresh along with the prosciutto. The staff are super friendly and it's an overall cute atmosphere(:

the corn is amazing . Something I had never tried before and didn't expect to taste so great. Fish tacos are great too as are the margaritas. Would be great if they could sell singular tacos instead of having to buy the whole plate with rice and beans. Also the staff aren't the friendliest hence the 4 stars.

I was in the mood for some chicken and waffles. So on a Saturday afternoon my girlfriend and i went out in search of the perfect chicken and waffle. We chose this restaurant base on the reviews we figured it would be the one of the best chicken waffles in the city the wait was 40 minutes. the waitress was very dry and didn't offer us the daily specials it looks like she was in a hurry to take our order granted the food came out at a timely fashion.  the food was great. It was the service of the waitress that lowered the rating. Fresh lemonade and the coffee was good.

Still now I have no complain for this place -as they gave me according to my need serving for me long. So how can a settle them and leave them without putting any review. Each day many people making purchase at here but they didn't leave even a single review -whether the service good or bad should reveal for the next consumers.

We decided to for it another try and this time the food was so MUCH better. I had the shrimp and calamari in white wine cream. It was delicious. Of course the price was reasonable. One of the owners came to our table to ask us our opinion and suggestions of improvement. They strive for excellence here. I had to et another coffee and one major plus they weren't rushing us to leave. They allow you to enjoy your family and friends night out.
Grilled octopus was the best!  We shared a couple of appetizers, a wonderful greek salad, chicken kebob and a fresh perfect salmon.  Get the lemon potatoes---they're addictive!  Great place.

I was looking forward at dining at Crescent Grill after reading about the restaurant opening online. I decided to have the pre-fixe lunch here on a Saturday. The restaurant is in a "up and coming" part of Queens and is surrounded by warehouses. Once I entered the restaurant, I was greeted by extremely friendly staff. The restaurant interior looked like a remodeled industrial space. The pre-fixe menu consisted of three courses. First, my girlfriend and I received a plate of nibbles, consisting of smoked salmon, a smoked pork sausage and a two mushroom mini tarts. These were all decent; none were particularly impressive. The mushroom tart was notably watery. For my main course, I had a roast chicken. This was an excellent dish. The chicken was crispy and had excellent flavor, the sauce was rich and the mashed potatoes had excellent consistency. For desert, we were brought a plate of miniature pastries, including biscotti, a marshmallow, and a chocolate cookie. These were all slightly above supermarket level, extremely weak. After I complained to the waiter, I was brought a peach tart. The tart was quite a bit better, with good peach flavor, although the crust was too soft. The real problems started when the bill arrived. I was charged $5 for the espresso that I ordered with my desert. This was a single espresso, not a double expresso and the price was not listed on the menu. It did not come with any kind of pastry. I can understand getting charged $5 for an espresso at a two or three Michelin star restaurant that comes with some kind of pastry. I can't understand being charged $5 for an expresso at a casual restaurant in Queens. To add insult to injury there's an 18% mandatory gratuity on the menu. The restaurant counts the gratuity on the price of the food and the tax together, so the mandatary gratuity is actually over 20%. I will not be returning.
Pizza was thick and tasted alright. Didn't really enjoy their spumoni however the strawberry ice cream tasted amazing!!
Amazing! The best pizza I have ever had.  I never go to Brooklyn but I make my way there just to have this pizza.

I am feeling generous giving one star rating.  I usually don't even bother with bad reviews because I never return myself to these restaurants.  My experience was like a scene in kitchen nightmares and I was waiting for Chef Ramsey to come out and close the place down. I think the owner was sitting next to me at the bar, dress in I don't know what drinking a high ball.  80's music was playing, and the flat screen had some mature audience show on - I only said something after a woman starting pole dancing - asking if this was appropriate for dinner.  They changed it to the Giants Phillys game. I ordered Fettuccine an got Linguine noodles that were uncooked and hard - there was even a row of about four noodles that were stuck together - obviously frozen and did not break apart in boiling water.  The shrimp tasted as if they were freezer burned and a few were not cooked all the way through.  Obviously not fresh. The Alfredo sauce was just weird the seasoning was all wrong and it was salty.  The bread was absolutely awful - not sure what it was but nothing I have ever experienced before. A friend of a server came and sat on the bar and was offered a beer but he instead asks for a Sex on the Beach and started flirting with the waitress with sexual innuendos.  A server asked if he could go buy cigarettes and did a roll call to the kitchen who needed cigarettes for the cigarette run. The bartender server did a good job - her drinks were good - she did forget to bring me a water (I was the only customer sitting at the bar beside the owner and the Russian friend). For the cost I would never consider going to this restaurant again.

Found this great, local BYOB place a few blocks from where we live. We are vegetarian and there are plenty of options to keep us satisfied. The spicy agetofu and grilled rice cakes with sweet and sour sauce were phenomenal. We also had a sweet potato tempura roll, bibimbap roll, and an avocado, cream cheese, jalapeño tempura roll. The food was fantastic. The spicy Korean sauce s well as all other sauces are all homemade and to die for. The service was top notch and the staff are very helpful and courteous. It has simple, yet elegant decor and has the feel of a mom and pop type restaurant. Not overly commercialized and even during its busiest time, the service was great. Will be coming back here again and again!

Ordered traditional Filipino fare...shanghai lumpia, pancit bihon and lechon.  The lumpia was OK,  but my daughter was happy with the pancit.  I loved the lechon...such a big serving to share for 2. The leche flan was the best I have ever had!!!!!

EDIT: Overall the cafe is a fantastic place to go her some amazing teas. They are brewed fresh and anything you could want to add to it is there. Unlike other cafés you get real glassware for you piping hot teas. I'm glad the owner cares about what the customers have to say it says a lot about the business. EDIT: After talking to the owner about the situation everything was righted. It's safe to say I will be returning to the cafe on future visits. ----------- Last night (July 25, 2014) at about 10:35 PM my friends and I went into the cafe to get tea to end our night. We have been there many times and know what the teas we order taste like and just about how long they take to make. We order Jasmine Pearl tea, got the tea very quickly, which was surprising, and were then quickly rushed out of the cafe. Even though there was still 20 minutes left to closing and we weren't causing any trouble. While we were putting sugar and what not into our tea, the teen/lady that made the tea deliberately shut the lights of to that zone. We had to use our flash lights on our phones to read the packets to find the correct sugar. The lady seeing this snickered. Just before being removed from the cafe the lady's boyfriend walked in and they started to talk, she turned the lights on in the area where she wanted to sit, but would not turn the lights on for the sugar area so we could see. After being removed from the cafe, my friends and I got back in the car and noticed, our tea smelled odd. Knowing what the tea should smell and taste like, we discovered that the lady had given us Chamomile tea rather than what we ordered, which was Jasmine Pearl. All the times that we have come to the tea house the Jasmine Pearl tea NEVER had a tea bag in it, yet this tea did, tipping us off. I paid for the three teas we ordered (receipt number #DIS4). The receipt clearly say 3 Jasmine Pearl teas BUT WE DIDN'T GET THAT. We decided not to tip the person who made our tea since, as we discussed didn't earn the tip. On top of serving us the wrong tea, the lady was rude. She refused to let us pay with cash. She purposely turned the lights off in the area we were sitting. Served us the wrong tea knowingly, as the Jasmine Pearl tea has to be brewed which takes a couple of minutes, this lady simply through a teabag in a cup and poured FAR TOO MUCH water in. The tea even though it was incorrect STILL tasted awful due to the copious amounts of water and and the rips in the tea bags.

I just created an account which says something in itself. I am a very patient and understanding customer, however I feel a strong need to share my unfortunate experience with this restaurant because I have never felt so disrespected by a group of waiters, waitresses and hostesses until my visit at this restaurant. It's just not right. Where to begin...we were ignored for a while as we sat there and watched a nearby table get their waters and kimchi first. Our waiter took forever to bring out the kimchi, placed one mini dish on the table and suddenly left our tray of food on a nearby, busy counter, to take a phone call. He disappeared for about 10-15 minutes, while the three hostess just kept staring at us but not doing anything. They clearly knew there was an issue and did not take action....so awkward and confusing! We finally speak up and our waiter comes back and barks "what?!" to us, then proceeds to finally give us our kimchi. He ignored us the rest of the time, while others came and refilled our water in such a rush without even looking at us, just plain abrupt and rude with no manners whatsoever. We were once again ignored the rest of the time. We finally paid and my boyfriend still was kind enough to give a small tip that they didn't deserve. The waitress slapped the bill on the table and took his card without even acknowledging him. As we were leaving, she stopped us and questioned us for the small tip, asking for a higher tip and at that point I told her everything...making it a very uncomfortable experience all around as she questioned us making us even more upset. So disappointing! With so many bad reviews, why not make a positive change if people like your food? Is it not worth it?!

What a shame. I have been to different Xi'an locations around the city and am a huge fan of the food. All previous experiences were incredible, though the spice is not totally consistent every time, it is always great. I ate at this location a week or so ago and found that the food had NO flavor. The oil seared noodles, a dish I have had before countless times, was swimming in the water the noodles were boiled in and had little of the amazing oil and spice that is such an important part of the dish. When I asked the lady for a side of sauce she didn't understand me and I was unable to get the dish remade or a refund. This was especially frustrating since I knew what to expect from the dish and there was no understanding or effort to solve the problem. Sorry to say I will not go to this location again.

It's the college crowd, and I wouldn't have thought that they would serve decent food, but I was impressed. Wings are good, and if you go at the right time they are on special, the burgers are good, and the FRIES!!! The fries are beer battered and great.  Beer specials too. The music was pretty loud, and it was very dark inside, but for the prices you can't really beat it, if you're over 22 years old though, be prepared to feel old.

We had lunch here today and it was sooo amazing! The food was delicious and you could taste how fresh everything was! Gila and Tomi are absolutely amazing people! They made us feel so special and OMG the food! we had Suzanne Schnitnel, Chiken Shwarma, Hummus, Baklava, Chopped Salad and Iced mint tea!

Outstanding food, excellent service and a night to be remembered! That is how I recall my dinner at Ai Fiori last week. The food was perfectly prepared in accordance with what had been represented on the menu. The two pasta dishes that stood out were a spaghetti with blue crab that tasted even better than it looked. Great flavor and just the right amount of heat. The second was a ravioli in the classic Roman cacao e pepe style.

I have to say we were truely dissapointed......I grew up in west haven and honestly I even worked there as a busybody as one of my first jobs 20 years ago...my wife and I were out for a drive on sunday and decided to stop for dinner...asked for an outside table and the wait was short....   Downside.... Lobster bisque  was good but cold...I ordered the fried scallops and wife ordered the seafood platter. ..Honestly you can tell all the food is pre packaged  and frozen....and asking for a glass of water and more lemon seemed liked  I asked for the world to stop turning.... Upside.....nice views of water and was able to walk on the boardwalk.. I highly doubt we will be returning anytime soon except to use the bathroom when we are walking on boardwalk. ...Stowes was our first choice but line was out the door...
Good food great place to eat!!! Ordered a lava cake and was very good, the kind waiter gave me an extra scoop of icecream....very good place to eat
The quality of the food is sublime and the prices are reasonable! Will certain be a repeat customer and hope that the neighborhood gets behind this local restaurant!!! A+++
don't need to many words, the service and food are horrible, don't try to get there and experience it. you guys can get better Chinese food in Chinatown.

Was so excited to try Root and Bone since I'm a huge fan of Yardbird in Miami. Unfortunately the food was a bit of a disappointment. I had the half bird, waffle fries, and a couple drinks. The drinks were phenomenal and I highly recommend them but the food was so salty I think I'll be thirsty for days. Wish I liked it better!

Service is crap here. The pizza, however, is fantastic, amazing, and awesome. This is hands down my favorite pizza. Whenever I come into New Haven, I suck up the crappy service, long waits in the cold for this pizza. I always tell myself it won't be as good, but it always is. I usually get the plain tomato sauce and the clams pie. Both are extraordinary. The crust is incredibly thin, crispy, and light.. I love it. I should be sick of this place, but I keep coming back (10 years and counting). It is better than Pepe's, Moderns, and all other New Haven pizzas. It has made me a pizza snob.
Well I think everything it could be said about Yasuda was already told, the best japanese in Manhattan but it comes for a very high price. No tip, super expensive no refill coke.
I've been to this place for brunch and dinner. I think that their brunch deal is pretty good, for $16 you get 2 drinks, one coffee or tea and an entree. I like their crab cakes benedict.
delicious, but a bit heavy on salt and the price

We've been coming here for years and it never disappoints. There's not much to the decor, but the vibe is great. There's a bunch of tables and a long bar where you can eat. The bar separates you from the open grill and we love watching the grillmen at work. It's a tight space for them to work in, but they've got it figured out perfectly. And they turn out great burgers! Plus the fries are the real deal. Tried the wings but ordered them medium and were too hot for us. Mild would be a good choice if you don't like your mouth on fire. But we stick with the burgers and roll out of the place. That and a good on-tap beer makes a perfect meal.

Love this place. Came here on a Saturday and they had a live dj that played great dance music. Their mojitos are very good and they made it by hand (no pre mixes). Drink prices are fair. I was told they specialize in their sangrias but I didn't try it. Came here in their first few weeks of opening so it was pretty dead but I still had a great time.

Won't be back. Quality has fallen, now a has been..  Was not crowded, showed up for an early brunch.   Slow service, food was cold when it arrived, had to walk up to a waitor to get his attention as he was "reading a book" and did not see us waiving.  Food was NOT what was on the menu (Breakfast Burrito did not come with black beans as mentioned on the menu), but, by the time the food arrived we were so hungry, and late, no time to complain.  Food OK although cold. .  I was told the bathroom really, really, really needed an update.

Sorry but the place smells of moldy carpet. The food was just passable. The Tom gai Ka soup was good but the Pad Thai had too much sauce and the shrimp were not fresh. I have a bit of a stomach ache and I just left

Delicious!  They use nothing but fresh ingredients from the local farmer's market and have been for years (yes, "farm to table") Strangely, the menu descriptions almost undersell the product, which is always so much more amazing than it sounds on paper which is the best thing about Firebox.  The dish that sounds simple IS SIMPLE, but in no way BORING, but rather, "WOW" and the creative chef keeps creativity simple too as you try flavors and combinations you would not expect and not need a pocket Food Lovers Companion to understand.  The food is TASTY!   You can find some nice wines there as well, but the wine selection has dwindled over the years.  The bar is still cool, however.  The tap beer selection changes often and typically veers away from the pedestrian expectation.  Someone there loves beer and you can tell! What is underwhelming about the place however, is that they have lost steam over the years and it is never busy.  By that, I mean, empty.  The atmosphere is .....there is no atmosphere.  Stale.  The service is quite slow because they are staffed lightly, understandably so, as there is little business and the servers seem a bit bored.....  Once a hot spot, Firebox is not exactly on Fire anymore.  You can rack up a pretty good check - You'll be happy with your food for sure, hopefully the rest of your experience will follow suit.

Is it summer vacation for service at New York restaurants? Great food can't be saved by a cluster f...of mistakes in how the food appeared or often just did not at a recent dinner on the back patio.  Yes the food is good and the patio beautiful.  But if you want to average a 100 tab per person,  figure out this one.  When you serve a cheese course you need to bring a knife so we can actually eat it.   Maybe service is just a thing of the past.

My first visit here was on an apartment hunting trip back in January. Since then it has easily become my favorite beer bar in New Haven. The food has never disappointed me (aside from my standard plea for a wider range of vegetarian options) but the real star here is the beer list. Their selection always represents a wide array of styles from CT and beyond. Sours are always well represented - which delights me until no end. The bar itself is so spacious that even on a busy night, you won't feel crushed. Heaven for a beer nerd like me. Seriously.

this place is AWESOME... i used to live in the neighborhood and really wish this place was around when i was there.  i recently went here for drinks and ended up staying for a meal and more drinks.  the beer selection was great and full of beers i was very interested in trying.  the bartenders seemed knowledgeable and helpful.  there is no table service which was fine because i wasn't looking for a sit-down restaurant.  I had a few delicious beers and then got an order of the fries and the grilled cheese, which they knocked out of the park.  then i had a couple a whiskeys from an impressively long bourbon list.  the atmosphere is great, felt like brooklyn which is where i am living now.   all together this place was great and i and i will definitely be back

My husband and I tried to visit El Matador a couple of months ago based on a couple of recommendations from his boss. We arrived during normal business hours but the doors were locked even though there were people visibly inside. The only responses to us at the door were stares... Still... We decided to go back last night because we were craving authentic Mexican tacos. We ordered the sopes to share in addition to our tacos (chicken and steak). The sopes were good, but more explanation on the variety that is available would've been nice when I asked about them -- a guy at the next table had some that were different and looked even better than ours.  The tacos were very dry and had little flavor, but there was no salt on our table to help boost what flavor there was. The green and red sauces were good but still couldn't make the tacos moist enough to enjoy. Apparently there are other things to order than what is on the "to go" menu we were given to order from (that was just a plain paper menu with much wear and tear). My husband's boss said he'd had some very good soup and there were empty tables holding semi-empty dishes with beans, rice, etc. Neither was on the menu nor offered to us -- if either were part of the "special," They weren't mentioned. The man serving us was very brief and didn't explain anything even when asked, but two other customers who came in speaking Spanish were treated very nicely. Probably won't return. Total bill was over $30 for not a lot of primarily bland, dry food.
Every tiny restaurant but the food is very good , you can just spend ten bucks having a great meal. B2 is my favorite , convenient and proper price .
Pizza is delicious man!
Some of the best brunch food I've had in awhile. Big portions, great price and very friendly waiters. Will definitely return. Only downside was that they didn't accept credit cards and was cash only

The oysters were very fresh even though they were kinda smaller than I expected. I tried lemon grass mussels and it was really good.  Also tried Lobster Mac and cheese, Fish and chips. Both were ok but over priced. Overall, it was pretty good.
So we are basically forced to order another round of drinks AND leave this place because someone else has been waiting for the same table. A hundred dollars well spent.

The drinks!!! Oh man the drinks!!! I usually am not a drinker but if I drink I do it right... not once did I have to ask for my drinks to be stronger they were perfect, delicious! ... The food was good too, I don't do spicy and asked if my food was going to be spicy was told no, but it was... still good but had to trade with the bf his fish tacos were tasty :) desert was nice too.

Tonight a friend and I had dinner at Campania Coal Fired Pizza.  We were accommodated by the seating we preferred by the manager Arnold.  The staff were polite and helpful.  My friend and I shared the Fried Calamari Platter with the delicious red sauce along with the Ortolano Pizza covered with tomato sauce, fresh mozzarella, portobello mushrooms, artichokes and spinach.  The calamari was tender and fresh.  The toppings on this pizza complimented all the flavors of the vegetables as your taste buds differentiated each vegetable blending in with the fresh cheese and delicious tomato sauce. We each had a glass of Proseco wine served in a regular glass and not in a traditional wine glass.  This was a subtle hint that this restaurant is trendy, yet casual and wants their customers to feel at home.  The dishes of food are served  family style, which means just like an Italian household, there's enough for everyone at the table.    I recommend this new addition to Bay Ridge and wish it much success!

My favorite place! The breakfast is amazing and there's nothing like it in the area. The omelette is my favorite and they have REAL smoothies. The staff is friendly and the inside is clean, the food wait is short and the food isn't greasy.

This place has the best sushi that I have had in the Hartford area! It is a bit pricey but it's a great atmosphere and the food and service are just incredible. The Miso Eggplant, Aged Miso, and Irene's Paradise roll were my favorite!!

I came from Boston with a group of friends who recommended this place. I was reluctant to go, since I'm not a big fan of Greek food, but Ethos Meze East Village completely revolutionized my taste buds and I became a big fan of this restaurant and of Greek food. The candle lights, great music, dim lighting, and exemplary service creates an ambiance that is very classy and romantic. That night we had the beef tenderloin bruschetta and the scallops in addition to the fillet mignon. The tenderloin and the steak were hands down the best tasting steak I've had. This place was so good that I told my fiancé we had to come back for brunch before heading back to Boston. Needless to say the brunch did not disappoint either, I had the Italian omelette and my fiancé had the steak and eggs brunch special that was brought over with a pretty delicious portion of red and white sangria!!!! All for 15 dollars!!! I will definitely be coming back to NY with more friends so that they too can take part in the delicious and wonderful experience that I had in Ethos Meze East Village - Dr. Gonzalez
The soups are great, that's all I've really gotten there. The line can be long, but if you're not in a hurry it's a good place to go

If you like Greek food you have to visit The Greek! Best Greek restaurant i know in NY. Although not in the $$ group they do deliver excellent food at fair prices. You have to try their garlic bread and fried lobster!
Great food & service. Just the right amount of spice in my tacos and burrito it is DIVINE!!!

I was visiting from Houston and was visiting with my boyfriend who lived in VT, went to the bar and ordered a Vegas Bomb which is a pretty common shooter and a favorite of mine. the bartender, who had ignored me already for like five minutes despite the bar being half empty, told me she didn't know how to make one. normally, I would have been fine with this but then she decided to tell me that she thought I had pulled the drink name out of my ass and that I probably never had even had it before, then she asked me if I had gotten it from one of those Facebook pictures. I informed her that I ordered it all the time and had never had any difficulty and just asked her to give me something that she did know how to make. she gave me a look as if I had just asked her to sacrifice her children to satan or something and then just poured me a glass of Red Bull and a shot of the worst trasting whiskey I have ever had. I get it, long night or whatever, rude customers, and everyone around looked like they had just stopped wetting their beds so I get that she might not have been in the best mood but I wasn't even rude to her. I just wanted a shooter and not only did she act pretentious af but was rude and offensive. do not come here unless you're gonna get a sh**ty miller lite and want to gaze at a crowd of awkward hipsters.

Awesome meatloaf and really awesome raviolis. Skip dessert which are only just ok and get a delicious pineapple upside down cake martini instead! Free BBQ is hit and miss. Sometimes it's tender and falls off the bone and sometimes it's kind of meh...but also, it's free (pay as you wish and receive a coupon for that amount to return again later) Great patio and bar area. One of my favorite places to meet up a couple of friends in the summer.

Yuuuummm!  I had the sweet potato tacos.  The tacos were really simple and the ingredients were really fresh, especially the guacamole.  The atmosphere was really great -- lots of outdoor and indoor seating.
wonderful!

I cam here the Sunday night of fourth of July weekend with my boyfriend to the start of a little night on the town since we took the next day off. I read so many pleasant things about this place on Yelp that I had to see for myself. The decor was thoughtful, I felt like I walked into a classic Indian establishment. The lighting is on the low side which I enjoy. On the TV abvoe the bar some bollywood movies were being played. There's something to be said for the atmosphere, I could tell all of the other diners and bar patrons were having a nice night. The menu is quite nice. It has a variety of traditional Indian dishes with a twist. To start we had the fried okra which was tasty. Something I'd try to recreate on my own but I doubt I can execute it as nicely as the chefs. For entrees we had the lamb byrani and chicken tikka masala. At first we thought the portions looked small but they ended up being perfectly sized, we ate the entire thing. The flavors were delightful, meat was cooked nicely. Unfortunately I do have some criticisms for the restaurant surrounding the pricing. The low hanging fruit here is the plates are expensive and you don't get the bang for your buck as far as the meat. (Read: Stingy with the chicken and lamb in my entrees). If there's one thing I can't stand, it's paying $15 for a cocktail with a small amount of booze. This place does that. I'm cool with an expensive drink but I expect a good amount of liquor and  for it to arrive quickly. On to my next point that we ordered a second round to have a cocktail with our entree and 20 minutes had gone by before we decided to cancel it with the server. She said she had to check with the bartender to make sure he could cancel it. Thankfully it wasn't and issue but I find it unacceptable that we would have to wait 20 minutes for a cocktail on SUNDAY NIGHT when there were maybe 5 people at the bar. I think what was going on was the bartender was training the hostess and there's nothing wrong with that but it's not okay to let patrons wait that long for drinks. It was obvious that they weren't focused on training, more like hanging out behind the bar. I won't be back. I feel it's a tad overpriced.

Great night at this cool bar. Great atmosphere, cool soundtrack, perfect service from a charming Irish bartender named Stephen, awesome food! ( the flatbreads are yummy as is the spinach & artichoke dip) Definitely will come back!
Good not great. Tried corn with ground beef and corn with shredded chicken. Beef was better. Sauces were good. Came out hot. Not sure why it takes a half hour to cook an empanada.

Few days ago my friend and I decided to find something new, something interesting. The Eddy was the place that we have choosen. And we didn't regret! Situated in the East Village, having just a couple handfuls of tables, with lovely decor. Food and drinks were unexpectedly tasty. That's what we were looking for!

GREAT Hamden bar to visit with friend's,have a few cold beers and have some laughs. All the bartenders are GREAT and the TV's are ALWAYS set to the sports channel's. They also also have a pool table...

Been here a few times, and no fantastic experiences yet. The food seems to be frozen, and not just your typical pub food, it's BAD pub food. The beer list is extensive, but not reasonably priced. I read the review about going to the bowling alley, although I've never been there, I think I'm going to try there next time, I don't think I will be stopping back at Mcgilicudy's soon. The waitresses were all friendly, but not worth it for the food and prices.
Old fashion counter service. Buy a ripper and onion rings. Put their homemade relish on the hot dog. We ate a mid day snack for 10 dollars total. I recommend this place.

Chose to do dinner here based on Yelp reviews; was definitely pleased! Made a reservation, but the two floors don't seem to talk to each other, so they weren't sure where I was supposed to be. Outside of that, the place had good atmosphere, friendly staff, and was next to the Book of Mormon play. Though we didn't take advantage of it, they offer pre-order intermission drinks. My dining partner and I shared a pitcher of Brooklyn Lager; a nice amber that wasn't too hoppy, and had smooth flavor. We got a basket of bread cubes, seed to be a focaccia, dipped lightly in olive oil with a dash of rosemary. Good, albeit a little dry. I had the Spaghetti Alla Bolognese; thick noodle spaghetti, with a good helping of sauce. It came as is, no sides. Presentation was traditional, but clean. I thoroughly enjoyed it, and it was very filling, so be prepared to hold back if you have any antipasti or dessert to follow. My dining partner had Chicken Picatta. They really liked it. It came with some steamed garden vegetables, and crusted potato cubes. For a person who usually doesn't like vegetable, they ate them all! I tried their dish as well, and while the sauce was a little thicker and the chicken a little more breaded than I'm used to with my Picatta, I definitely liked. It lacked capers was the only thing of note. Overall, I would say it was a great dining experience! It's definitely $15~20, which is a little high if you're used to Dallas prices, but definitely well worth it! I would recommend, so long as it isn't busy.
Was pretty good food, though the portion sizes weren't quite enough for our tastes.

Small space and we had a large group . But they kept saying another 30minutes until we had been waiting for just about 3 hours. Had the vegetarian balls on vegetables. They were terrible . And the salad vegetables underneath was gross too. Our orders seemed to be mixed up for our mains and our Icecream sandwiches. We had two girls serve us over the night, one a bit rude the other one really friendly. Wouldn't return.
I gave this a 3 because the menu is limited.  The appetizers are the best.  I rather have a few appetizers and a drink.  I also enjoy the band Friday and Saturdays.
Unfriendly service. All dishes we ordered was just ok. A small bowl of rice cost ~$7. One of the most expensive bowl of rice I have even seen.

First of all...how many waiters do you have to flag down before you can get waters for the table. Read: four. Second, I haven't gotten the food yet but the aforementioned incident angered me enough to write an inflammatory review on yelp. Hey guys quick update, food was great - rating up to two stars. Still no water. Also not a fan of their rose wine. Vinay out.

It makes me sad to give CPB such a bad review! After all, their bagels are decent and I have had a great sandwich there, well; once. That being said, you just can't count on the sandwiches being consistently good. For example, I like to order the Western with deli ham. This sandwich tastes best with a generous helping of deli ham, which occasionally you get, but at other times it seems like they're deliberately skimping, maybe to save money? Then again, it could be the staff, which happens to be made up of under 21 refugees from the movie Twilight. They seem to be unconcerned about anything except getting you out of their face as quickly as possible so they can return to their vapid little lives, probably making fun of and otherwise dissing the customers. And don't even THINK about ordering anything a little bit different than normal, like a side salad,from these cretins. Even though it may be on the menu, they'll look at you like you with unveiled sarcasm, like you fell out of a tree, and have to go ask their manager if it's even available. And even if you end up getting what you want, it will suck, just like the service. I can't say enough bad about that. It makes me wonder of these twits aren't members of the family that are being forced into service on pain of death to save the place a few  paltry shekels. In any case, after trying this place several times, and despite the occasional good sandwich, I'd recommend hanging with hobos in the rail yards before subjecting themselves to this dining experience.
I was hungry, and the plate of dumplings I ordered was exactly what I wanted, very filling and delicius. The service was fast and good. Going back again

Pizza flavor was good, dough and crust were meh. We arrived at 615pm, three adults and two children. The place was fairly busy for the time. We were notified that we could be sat immediately only if we agreed to finish up by 730pm. That rubbed me the wrong way. Then we were given the specials. 2 appetizer and 2 pizza specials. Ok, great. We order. As we are waiting for our appetizers, we notice/overhear that the table next to us are offered additional specials since they are "known" customers. That rubbed me the wrong way.  Especially since the menu is extremely limited. The pizza special, soppressata with lemon was actually good. The marinara was good. The margarita was good. The appetizer meatballs were also good. The bread that came with the appetizer, while homemade, was burnt. The pizza was too doughy and chewy for it to pass as traditional Neapolitan pizza. The espresso was excellent.  It had a good amount of "schuma" and proper strength. Wait staff (all ladies) was very nice and also very pretty. We had been wanting to try this place for a very long time. The food was good but we won't return based on how we were treated as customers.

I have been here a handful of times and each experience was more than delightful. In fact this is my favorite noodle place in CT. The pho broth is flavorful and fresh and I dream about their mango bubble tea. I just wish that I lived closer so that I could go here more often.
Just had appetizers and drinks. Not cheap but good local food, good vibes. I'll go back

My first taste of dinosaur BBQ was many years ago in Syracuse NY. I fell In love with the mom and pop feel of the restaurant, and the sloppiness of the food. I actually had no idea a location opened up in Brooklyn until we had brunch at one of our favorite spots in Brooklyn. Dinosaur BBQ happened to be opening up on the same block as our brunch spot. My husband and I had dinner there and he absolutely loved it. On the weekend the wait can be pretty long but that's to be expected.

Simply the best pizza on Staten Island. Never the less, opinions on here are like (you know), everybody's got one. They do pizza excellent and meatball or sausage heros well. Also great Fried Calamari. If you're looking for anything else, don't look for it here. I see that most of the 1 star rants are from the typical food snobs who think anything on SI is horrible because it's not in Brooklyn or Manhatten and the one girl who wanted the world to revolve around her "food allergy". If you're eating issues are that difficult, please stay home. They aren't here to reinvent the kitchen for your exclusive problems. Stick with the good stuff and you'll never go wrong!

Wife and I went for the two day Pig Roast and Clam Bake last year. Last year we BOTH ordered Pig Roast and enjoyed it. We eagerly awaited this year's event. This year Saturday wife had Clam Bake and she absolutely LOVED it. I had Pig Roast and  liked it. Wait staff was very pleasant. We enjoyed their hard cider. I had thought that maybe we would go again Sunday and maybe switch dishes, but music was too loud so won't do that. We actually had to RAISE our voices to talk to each other at the table. I may be tempted to go for brunch, but a good idea may be to call on phone to get an idea of music loudness before going. They lose one star because of loud music, sounded like a disco.

Shockingly bad service -- I actually had to leave 10 minutes after getting there.  For the record, I absolutely adore Bayou's sister restaurants (Beso & Blue), so I went to Bayou with much excitement and anticipation. I'm going to spare you all the sob story and will hopefully be able to communicate it to Julian Gaxholli (owner/chef)...let's hope this is just a case of one bad apple.  But I will not be going back to Bayou until our sorry excuse for a server finds a new place of employment.

Wanting to end the night with a slice of pizza, this place totally delivered. Since it was close to closing time, they had just a few choices available. I had the lasagna pizza and my friend nudged me out on the mushroom slice. When the cashier handed over my pizza slice, it was much heavier than I would expect from a slice, so I guess #winning right?

Slightly more expensive than most Italian restaurants in the area, but well worth a few extra dollars.  They use interesting ingredients without crossing the line into fusion food. Lots of seasonal specials.  Each dish is unique -- not a "red sauce" restaurant.  Handmade ravioli is really a treat! Excellent service, pleasant ambiance, convenient parking. Also: Clean and naturally-lit party room, really nice spot for functions.

It's been almost a year since I've last had some chicken and rice with the infamous white sauce from the halal guys, time to make another trip to NYC. This time around I won't be a noob and bedazzle my plate with a volcano explosion of the hot sauce. Lesson learned. For someone who eats spicy, tears were literally coming out of my eyes. I digress, anyway halal guys ... Please open one in SF.
Roast pork with broccoli rabe and sharp provolone......Best sandwich I've ever eaten hands down. Completely reccomend

The gravy came out before the bread, and once we finally got the bread to eat the food was already cold. When we tried to tell the waiter he laughed at us. I would definitely not come back again, there are a lot better restaurants in the area and I would suggest going to those rather than wasting your time and money on this place. My family consists of very experienced diners. We have eaten at multiple lower and higher end Indian restaurants. This place has to be the absolute worst. We can accept that the food was not tasting the best today but the service was absolutely discussing. How dare you lough at a concerned customer. The food.....was so bad I do not wish to discuss my experience. Cold, late, disappointing.

I love this restaurant!  Great food and charming atmosphere.  The brunch menu is amazing.  The Nutella French Toast is sinfully delicious.  I also love the Sake Bloody Mary's (they are very spicy).  We have always had great service too!  If you go to weekend brunch be prepared to wait an hour or so.
Solid and cheap.  I got the short rib with handmade noodles not the best but ok.  I'll def try something else next time.

So while I give Taim credit for their creative 'falafel balls', I despise being asked if I'd like some "Israeli salad" with it. No offense, but that cucumber, onion, tomato- olive oil  combo has been a Mediterranean delicacy for thousands of years, and Israel is a fairly new country of European Jews (85%) who have only been introduced to the cuisine in 1948. Where is the Jewish flavor or contribution? Suddenly falafel is Jewish? Did the French call Morocco's couscous 'French'-- I think not.   The staff seems so programmed to always call it 'Israeli' salad, which is simply weird and mildly offensive. Secondly, tabbouli is not supposed to have more bulger grain than parsley. Either the cooks don't want to spend the day chopping parsley--or the grain is cheaper. All in all, the hot sauce is great, the pitas a bit thicker than I'd like -- and I'm impressed that they have Omba, (origin- Iraq).
Great food nice atmosphere will be coming back!!!!
Yum! Great homemade food from friendly people- you can't ask for more! Great naan and hummus!

Just left here and it isn't the best but isn't the worst. It's kind of in between, I had shrimp in garlic sauce with a side of rice. The rice was bland and a little over cooked and the shrimp was okay, it didn't really stick out. The service was pretty good. And the good wait time was short BUT my meal didn't come out very hot it was lukewarm.

This place is worth the wait you are bound to experience.  The food is top notch and the coffee was delicious. We went for breakfast and had three different items; all great.  Get the pancakes or the French toast or omelette; and make sure to have the biscuits.  You really can not go wrong.  Only problem they have is trying to accommodate everyone who is trying to get a seat but hey, they have takeout.

We had heard about this place via various Astoria postings on FB and were excited to try a new place in the neighborhood. Boy, are we glad we did! Everything was fabulous: service, food, ambiance...heck, even the fellow diners! We had the arancini (cheesy, yummy with just the right amount of sauce), the polpetti (my favorite...they did meatballs RIGHT!), the La Porchetta (just OK) the ravioli (delightful little home made pillows of goodness) and the tiramisu (creamy, flavorful and delicious). The service was outstanding. Everyone was attentive, but not obnoxiously so. The owner made it a point to come by after each dish was presented to see how we enjoyed everything. Our experience was really enhanced by the people working there. Truly a memorable meal. We will be back!

Stay away from the Sunday brunch. I do hope the rest of the week the food is better. This was the worst brunch I've ever experienced. The eggs were greasy. I sent it back and got the french toast which was just soggy bread drenched in sugar water with a mile of whip cream on top. We were the ONLY people there which I guess should have been a huge warning. Lesson learned.
I really like healthy food, but honestly this food just wasn't all that flavorful and left me wanting more. It's quick and convenient but eh.

I wanted to try out this eatery after hearing about from friends. But I was disappointed. Nothing was wow. I enjoyed the steamed mussels as it had a good chilli factor and the foie gras was good. Buttermilk chicken was on par to Popeyes chicken but a little more bland. Served with uninviting coleslaw. Service... 2/5, the girl seemed like she didnt want to serve us and her polite im happy waitress pretence persona was written on her forehead. I felt like this place was trying to be something they are not.... I would have recommended 3 stars but the service and long wait for fried chicken was disappointing. Hmm popeyes anyone?

I rarely write reviews. However, I felt it necessary to write this, as my experience was so negative that it was difficult to enjoy my meal. My friends and I decided to go for brunch Sunday afternoon. I was 1 out of an 8-person party, though 1 member of our group did not eat and only drank water. As a sidenote, I used to be a server and understand that an extremely busy shift can entail a lot of situations that are (sometimes) out of your control. It WAS very busy, so a wait was very understandable. We received glasses of water while we waited for a table, which was very appreciated. After about 25-30 minutes of waiting, we were seated outside because it was the first table available. I would estimate that we sat for about 10 minutes before our waitress actually came to our table (she breezed by several other times, saying she'd be with us in a moment), and at that point another employee had brought half of our party more water. Already, the group and I were feeling restless, hungry, and a little annoyed. The waitress introduced herself, counted how many of us needed more water, and then took our drink order. It took another 10-15 minutes to receive our drinks (where only 1 out of the 8 was an alcoholic beverage). After this, she would disappear for moments on end. We actually had to ASK her if we could put our food order in, and then waited another 30-40 minutes. The food was good. However, the overall experience made us rush through the meal just so we could get the heck out of there. The waitress was inattentive and borderline rude. Again, I understand being busy - but it's important to be kind and as attentive as possible to your tables; this is especially so when you are attaching an obligatory 20% tip to the bill. The manager has already been notified, so I found it unnecessary to use the server's name. I hope this experience was a fluke, but I can't say I'll rush back to Silk City for food anytime soon.

Second time coming to Blue and you can't go wrong with anything on the menu. Make sure you save room for dessert! The cheesecake is homemade and pairs extremely well with the pistachio gelato. The only thing I would suggest is dress a little bit more fancy but still casual, just no tank tops! They won't let you sit in the dining room with one on.

I went here last night and the food is amazing:) Here is a breakdown for my rating: 4 starts because: 1) The food was amazing. 2) The place is a cute place in the west village. 3) The manager gave us a second plate of dessert on the house. 4) The eggplant parmesan and the pasta with garlic / olive oil are amazing. The reason for not giving the extra star for the 5 stars: 1) The place is extremely small and when you are sitting there, the waiters are struggling to get through the aisles because the seats are packed together in a tight, confined place. 2) The place is a bit loud and noisy, which is fine (not a big deal). 3) When we arrived, it took a good 10 minutes to get a waiter to help us with drinks, even though we asked about 3-4 times to get someone to help us - I get it...the place is busy and is very, very good. But, they could certainly have some more waiters on staff to accommodate the large crowd, relative to the small place. Overall, this is a hidden gem and I will definitely be going back,.
The food was great!  Loved my spicy BBQ chicken. Didn't take long to be seated or served. Open 24 hours

Great service, but a&s isn't a solid competitor to other pizzerias on the island. I recommend Romeos, and Paesanos for some of the best pizza on the Island (in my opinion. Also, don't even think about coming here in the summer because it's super hot in the restaurant and they have no air conditioning or fans running. Oh, there is a fan working but it's pointed to outside of the restaurant to keep the hot breeze out. Ridiculous.
Ridiculously overpriced children's menu. $9 should get you more than a cup of rotini pasta with NOTHING else included.

Bruno's was the pizza I grew up with in Clifton. We were regular customers since the time they opened in the 1970s. My mom worked at McHenry's Drugs in the same shopping mall, and it was always a treat when she would bring a Bruno's Pizza home for dinner. I haven't lived in Clifton for over 30 years now. I've struggled to find a pizza that is as good as those I remember from Bruno's, and always wondered whether it was because of nostalgia, or was Bruno's really that good? I have my answer. I live in Oklahoma now, and this weekend was back in NJ visiting friends. Had some free time so drove back to Clifton for a nostalgia visit. Stopped at Bruno's for a slice. Nothing had changed - same layout, same pizza ovens, I think even the same guy behind counter. And the pizza? Every bit as delicious as I remember. Perfect crust thickness and crispness. Perfect amount of tangy sauce. Perfect amount of cheese. I took one bite and was instantly transported back to my moms kitchen table. To the little league end of season pizza parties in the back room. For that matter to those days as a CHS stoner curing a wicked case of the munchies. Bruno's Pizza set the standard by which all pizzas have even measured for my entire life. I'm 49 years old now, and it still does. Cliftonites, you don't know how good you have it.

'Twas recommended by a nearby business, and we were grateful.  Went there twice in two days.  The lunch salmon croquette sandwich was the best croquette I've had!  The Sunday brunch frittata was outstanding and so was the home made bisquit that came with it.  It was a pleasure to meet owner Donna Lewis who is also a chief cook.  She is a kindly force whose spirit can be found in the food.  The waiters were friendly, kindly.  My next trip to Manhattan will find me there, for sure.

The only thing good about this place is that the food was ok. Service was absolutely terrible and shitty, blatantly ignoring customers requests, never came and cleaned the table or refilled water, we had to ask for checks even though when they walked by multiple times, they could clearly see we were done. When we asked for check, he even ignored us first then handed it with an attitude. We gave them bad tips , they even chased us out of the restaurant to ask for money...they deserved no tips whatsoever, and they should feel lucky we even tipped them.

My fiancé and I love it here! The coffee, espresso, and chai teas are excellent and we especially love the little walnut pastries. The food selection is both exceptionally fresh/high quality and very reasonably priced. The staff are friendly and considerate and the atmosphere upstairs is perfect for reading/studying. I'm happy to make this cafe my regular go-to on my way to work or to stay and do work while enjoying the view of Washington square park.
One of my favorite places to eat. Just about everything on the menu is delish. I always get the churrasco steak. And I have to say the mojitos here are one if the best in the city.

Disappointing brunch. When we arrived the were out of Bloody Marys and Hashed browns. Not at promising start for a Sunday brunch... Waitress more grumpy than called for, did not listen, corrected the pronounciation of the names of the dishes. Ordered the fried chorizo: less than half of a sausage in homemade baked beans covered with a fried egg - not inspiring, cheeseburger: boring, no finesse or taste, and pancakes: at least that was big - but boring as well. Not a good place for brunch!

This place was recommended by a friend and it was delicious! My husband and I spent a weekend in Philly and tried a few different cheesesteak spots. This was the least flashy of the three spots we tried; however my husband and I both agreed it was by far our favorite cheesesteak! The bread was super soft, cheese was melted perfectly and the onions and meat were chopped and cooked to perfection. We both highly recommend this place for cheesesteaks! We didn't try the pizza but I must say it looked and smelled great!
I always enjoy eating here, the staff is friendly, good service, the food is delicious and everything is clean.

My girlfriend and I had an early flight into Newark and decided to yelp something nearby to eat. Originally we were going to Hell's Kitchen around the corner but it was not open yet. We walked around and found this Lebanese restaurant. Looked like the owner and her daughter were cleaving and getting ready to open. We waited a bit outside then walked in. After we went in the interior looked horrible, we did not get any water at all until we asked 15 mins later. We ordered a hummus which did not taste good, waited around to see if the server would ask us for our order which she never did. 40mins later I asked for my check. Paid and left. Horrible service. Would never go back.

SUNDAY AFTERNOON RUINED. Horrible douche fest; mindless staff. I created a Yelp account after 12 years in NYC (I'm only in my early 30s) to review this place, that's how offensive it was. I sat down for a nice late afternoon wine and salad on the beautiful quiet street. This is a cozy-looking, civilized-appearing place, not a frat-style club. Please note. Anyway. A few nice tables were also seated outside. I was asked whether I would order food, otherwise I couldn't sit outside. I said I would. A few minutes after I ordered, an obviously tipsy woman emerged from the bar and asked if she and her friends could finish drinks outside. Ok, so the ordering food rule isn't "across-the-board". Her friends (two loud blathering bros) stumble out soon after and they proceed to start playing music from their iPhones (Calvin Harris and Avicii, on two phones simultaneously...) and dancing on the sidewalk. The wait staff lingered listlessly by the front door. Finally 10-15 mins later, after this gang have been shouting and dropping F-bombs nonstop, bro! ... the host and servers told them they couldn't play their own music. Wow. They then argued - "...why not, had someone complained?!" The whole thing was utter nonsense. I paid my check ($40 for arugula salad and a glass of wine), left most of my wine and food, and got the F out of there, BRO!

1st visit this past Friday night: - BYOB which was fine for us - sat outside, which is a big plus - pricing on the kids menu (which has a good selection) was $5/entree....and good quality food/choices - my wife and I went with the lamb burgers.....and they hit the spot If you live in the area, are looking for outdoor seating/BYOB......give this place a try
I have never ever likes Mexican food, however this restaurant hits the mark. Food has great flavors, comes out hot, friendly staff, great drinks. Try it!
Worst Service in the world!!!!!! If I could give them a zero I would.  They cancelled by eid catering order 30 mins before I was supposed to pick it up.
The time to wait is too long, and the sushi is not fresh. Even the lunch box is not good
What a great little place. Food was great. We alter out orders to be off the menu. Very accommodating . Best little breakfast place !!

I came here with my boyfriend when we were in the area. We  choose this place after reading all the the good reviews but we did have a little trouble finding the place. We ended up ordering arepa de queso and arepa de chocolate to go and they were very friendly and offered us iced water while we waited. Having never had arepas before, I had no idea what to expect, but these were just so amazing! The arepas were made to order so it came out fresh, hot and warm... and so soft! They were so delicious that my boyfriend & I ended up coming back here again the next day.
Best tacos in Astoria so far! The service was really friendly. I highly recommend it!

This is the nicest food court I have ever seen and the food selection is so good. Num paang makes a great banhi mi, the truffle burger at umami burger, and sushi at blue ribbon! The list goes on and I can't wait to go back
They always take my order wrong and they add extra stuff in my order out of my order and charge me extra.

If I could go here every day of my life, I would. The 30's-era, prohibition vibe, live music, and drink specials are what make this a great spot to check out whether you're by yourself (and there to enjoy the variety of performances), or meeting up with a small, intimate group. The space can get a bit cramped, but the atmosphere is a groovy mix of big band/jazzy tunes, and well-lit intimacy.

Where can I start!? I love this place!  The food is excellent.  I like coming here for the Lunch Special because it is the best on Ditmars and the service is great.  You can get a full size draft beer or mixed drink with a gracious selection of Entrees.  I had the steak sandwich and my friend had the tacos.  Both items were delicious and well prepared.  I have also stopped in at night and sat at the bar to have a cocktail and an appetizer- the Lamb Lollies are awesome.

I was here for breakfast and had the egg dish that was scrambled with tomato, feta, and I think leeks. There was also a break ring with sesame seeds atop it. It took FOREVER to get the food. I think they made the bread fresh. It was all very tasty however. The place is small so don't come with a crowd. The menu is also really limited. I like it and would return when I am looking for a change of pace, but not if I were in a hurry. The pastries looked yummy, but I didn't try any.
Really good breakfast spot! Lots of delicious options. Indoor and outdoor seating. I see why all the reviewers like this place.
Enjoyed the food very much and the atmosphere and location were great. Off the busy path. The service was great and loved the spicy oil they gave is for the great oven cooked pizzas.

Amazing coffee with a laid-back beach vibe in the middle of little Italy/Chinatown - reminded us of home! The staff here were so lovely and welcoming and the coffee is house roasted from a sustainable source Nicaraguan producer. Sunny, light and filled with beautiful photos, this place is going to be a Sunday afternoon regular! The juices and snacks are fantastic - way above par for a cafe - and the chilled cucumber and lime water is free! The outback cap has to be the best value deal below Houston. Highly recommend this place!

Wonderful spot. Cool location and pleasant service. The portions are more than enough to whet your appetite. I'd recommend to anyone who has the taste for some good 'ol soul food. Probably the best I've tasted in the area, other than my mom's! LOL

We are New Yorkers and I was looking forward to eating here during restaurant week. Unfortunately, it seems the restaurant either deliberately overbooks the tables or doesn't know how to manage/honor reservations. This is not something you would expect in what is supposed to be a sophisticated New York restaurant. We had an 8:15 reservation and arrived at 8:05. The hostess said to check back again at 8:15 for our table. So at 8:15 we inquired again and were told it would be another 10-15 minutes. We told them we needed to pick our son up at the bus station, so we could wait a few minutes but didn't have too much extra time. At 8:30 we asked again and they offered us some complimentary champagne and said the table was still not ready. I noticed that there were several other parties who were being told similar stories and had made reservations that were not honored.  At 8:45 we were told our table would be next.  By 8:55 when our table was still not ready and we were out of time, we left. Wound up having felafel across the street at Olympic Pita. If you're in the mood for felafel and shwarma, Olympic Pita was great. The waitress was nice and the food was yummy. Wish I could say the same about David Burke fabrick but I doubt I'll get the chance to go back again. If you can't run your restaurant properly in New York, it won't last.

Tuesday morning we took a stroll on the Highline and pulled in Chelsea market on the way. Planned to eat at Los Tacos based on yelp reviews and were there for opening at 11. No queue. WOW. The title of my review says it all. Stunning tacos. Succulent, juicy and bursting with flavour. Had 3 each and left buzzing. GO!

My husband and I and our two children went to Osteria Giotto last night to celebrate my husband's birthday.  I had researched it here on Yelp and it seemed to get a lot of positive feedback.  We were BLOWN AWAY by how good this restaurant is!  We will definitely be returning!  First of all, its really cute and cozy.  A lot of people have mentioned that its tight and crowded- and while it can get loud because its not a very large space, we found it to be very comfortable- definitely bigger than a lot of restaurants in NYC!  Our waiter, Jeremy, was wonderful- very friendly and knowledgeable.  I have no complaints about the service- everyone was great and went out of their way to be helpful!  As for the food, hands down, the best home made pasta I have had other than when I was in Tuscany!  We had the seafood pasta special: crab, lobster, and shrimp in a light red sauce over home made linguine- YUM!  My husband had the lasagne special and it was also amazing.  We ordered a seared tuna appetizer (also a special) that was fabulous- crispy on the outside, rare on the inside served with a salad of avocado, tomato, and cucumber.  My youngest son is a picky eater (he's 7)- he had plain spaghetti with butter- even that was to die for- the pasta being homemade makes ALL the difference!!!  We also had dessert which was so delicious: my husband had the giandua special (hazelnut gelato with toasted hazelnuts, chocolate sauce and fresh whipped cream, I had the coconut gelato special served with fresh pineapple and toasted coconut on top.  The kids had chocolate gelato and chocolate mouse cake- everyone cleaned their plates!  For the quality of the food and the large portions, I felt the prices were reasonable.  Our check came to $151 and we brought home leftovers, but left extremely satisfied!! A few other things to note: parking is on the street, but we found there to be plenty of spaces available with just a short walk (it was a Saturday evening).  We ate indoors, but there is some outdoor seating as well. You definitely need a reservation! The restaurant is BYOB.  It says its not good for kids on here, but our kids are 7 and 12 and they loved it so I guess it depends on your kids. My advice- GO!  You won't be sorry!!

This is a Central Kerala themed menu with a few standard North Indian dishes. The service is fast and friendly. Our server was from Andra but seemed to know his way around the menu. The Chef has toned down spices to appeal for the American taste buds, which creates the opp for some interesting flavors thought I would not say the food was great. Interesting and good for a change.  I am also very surprised that there is no steak on the menu. Beef is a core kerala dish, and if Kochi is not serving beef then it would be quite a disappointment.

Tried to go there dr breakfast today   The place is tiny vintage which seemed novel. We waited 20 minutes fora table or place at the counter. No ones tells you how long the waist really is.  People waiting for checks and people waiting to pay their check. Short staffed. Completely overwhelmed but seems that's the status quo. Go if you have the time which we didn't. Someone said the food was good. There isn't an egg in the US that's worth the hassle for me!  We left.

I was at the Lobster Buffet last night and it was horrible!  From the moment we were seated I could smell a stench from the rugs..it was overpowering.  They need to change the rugs.  Then the food, gross! we had a 830 seating and all the food seemed like it was sitting there for hours.  I actually had to spit out an artichoke into my napkin as it tasted disgusting.  When it came to the lobster station they ran out of butter, are you kidding me?  I asked for medium rare prime rib, I was not accommodated either it was well done dry or nothing.  Then the dessert table, everything looked good but it was surrounded by shoe flies.  We had a few mudslides put us back 40 dollars but they were served in shot glasses.  The only thing I enjoyed was the lobster bisque had 2 cups of it.  We will not be back and I advise you go elsewhere for a nice dining experience.

Seriously a great place to get good food and drinks, complete impressed with service and the atmosphere!! I would say this is a must go! Tell Nick Peggy sent you! Jimmy Fallen and Stephen Colbert were here as well so it's a who's who place :)

The foods are good. But it takes so long for the food come out from the kitchen. It seems like they slaughter the animal on premises right after your order is sent to kitchen. You will see the restaurant is crowded all the time it is because the average wait is longer than you can't imagine. I really like the southern fried chicken. And I definitely will come here more often. PS. Make sure you eat something before you arrive. Otherwise you will complain at the table.

Yama is my favorite restaurant in the Upper Valley.  It has an earnest  unpretentious atmosphere.  The dining room is casual in a simple functional style.  We often see families with young (well-behaved) children. The staff is attentive without being intrusive and very patient with my terrible pronunciation of Korean dishes.  Everything from the barley tea to the little dishes of namul served as appetizer to the raw sushi (they also have deep friend varieties which I haven't sampled) to the bibimbap... it's always fresh and delicious and satisfying. I would eat here every day if I could.

This is my new favorite restaurant on Staten Island. From the decor to the dessert, I'm in love. Adorable outdoor eating area, exposed brick, PERFECT music all greet you upon walking in. Comfortable sized tables and super high ceilings. Getting to the important stuff, the food. Party of 5 ordered 3 appetizers: Mac and cheese : perfect. Calamari : capers and jalapeños?! Oh my goodness... French onion soup that you could tell was expertly made. Entrees we ordered: seafood risotto : gigantic portion. A little rich for my taste, but delicious. Short ribs : recommended by our waiter and we're incredibly tender with layers and layers of flavor. Duck breast : again, layers of flavor and tenderness (outstanding chutney on top too. Mmm). Prime rib : rivals the hardcore steakhouses on the island. Add on the exceptional service and delicious desserts (and watermelon sangria!!!), absolutely do not miss this gem. To long time islanders: the chef is formerly of the American Grill on forest avenue. No wonder it's fabulous. GO GO GO!!!!!

I was searching on yelp a good restaurant around Central Park for my 30th birthday and found Villagio interesting. It was worth the 2h30 NYC traffic. The service is top notch. Very reasonable prices. Portion were big and it's probably the italian dish I ate in my life. This is the place to go.

It was my first time there. My friend and I were really excited because we heard the food was great along with the service. So we looked forward to spending the evening there. We made a reservation, when we got there, we got seated by the hostess and she brought us water right away so that was good. It wasnt busy yet so it was quiet which was nice. Within 5 minutes of sitting down, we knew what we wanted but total 15 minutes went by and nobody stopped by our table to ask if we were ready to order or what the additions were for the night. Finally I flagged someone down and told him we are ready to order but we dont know who our server is and asked if our server is coming. His response was "Yes Yes". So we waited and waited...wondering WHO is our server, WHERE is he/she and WHY hasnt he/she served us... when we have been waiting for 15 minutes. We were so hungry too!! Then another 10 minutes went by (we checked the time), no server stopped by. I flagged another server down asking if he know who our server is because we have been waiting for 25 minutes and nobody came to serve us. He said he will take our order so that was nice of him i guess. We told him the appetizer that we want that was on the menu. He said they dont have that for the night. So we asked for his recommendation and he suggested he will get our server. Um....okay???? Then I think few minutes went by and the hostess that seated us came to our table. Notice its the hostess, not any server. She asked if we are ready to order.... and Im just thinking WOMAN, we have been ready for the last freaking 25 minutes!!!!! So we ordered our appetizer and entrees from her. After we got our food (at least no delay in getting our food), probably 10-15 minutes went by and our server turned up!!!!! And thereafter, he served us....stopping by a total of maybe 3 times asking if everything is good so far. The food was fine. Overall, I'm really really disappointed with my first time there. Nobody apologized to us for waiting, nobody even acknowledged that we waited about 30 minutes before someone asked if we are ready to order. It wasnt even busy so theres no excuse for making us wait that long. It doesnt even matter if the food is good. Because if the service sucks, the food sucks too. I mean who can enjoy their food at a restaurant when they were just given such a crappy service?

Soup Dumpings & Shanghai Noodles. Those are the only things you need to get when you're here. I think soup dumplings are good in general, but these are really as good as it gets. This is basically the only place you have to come to if you want to show people around NYC or if you're coming as a tourist or if you're just in the mood for some really amazing soup dumplings. The wait is pretty short (there can be a line because it's THAT popular & good), but the food comes out really fast, like EXTREMELY fast. Also, even if it doesn't seem like it, the waiters do understand english pretty well because there are a lot of non-Chinese people that come through the restaurant. However, the menu can get really overwhelming, but I swear you just need to keep ordering soup dumplings and a few plates of Shanghai noodles and you're set to go. There are either crab or pork soup dumplings. I recommend getting both at first and then ordering more of whichever based on your taste. Basically, if you ever get the chance, you HAVE to stop by here at least once in your lifetime cause you're going to keep coming back for more.
10 dumplings for $4? Sign me up. Cash only, not that fast, but pretty good!
Seriously delicious. Best vegan place i've been to in Brooklyn. Try the tofu benedict. We drive all the way from bensonhurst to come here!
