Katzs has been our lunch destination for almost a year now. Love the pastrami,corned beef,and patty melts.Coleslaw and pickles are really tasty too. We brought my mom,and she said it was the best pastrami she ever had in her 78 years. Keep up the good work,and we`ll be back soon!

We tried the successor to Grill Poblano tonight and we will be returning. Quiet, intimate on a Sunday evening. We shared the steak burrito bowl and were full. Food is quite good, service attentive and prices reasonable. Try them...you won't regret it. Air conditioning would be a nice touch, however...not that it was hot in there...just a little close on a hot evening.

Fantastic food and service every time! (Have been there upwards of 7 times) Superb chipotle pulled pork sandwich, and their maple syrup is otherworldly. By far a personal favorite in New Haven; definitely would recommend to anyone who hasn't been!

I came here to celebrate my friend's 18th birthday. We made a reservation for 17 people at 7:30, but they completely forgot about it and we finally got a table 20 minutes later. We ordered 12 wings for appetizers and only got 11 (split between 4 people). When we asked, they said they were out of wings and we had to wait for a VERY long time (sarcastic tone). The fries were salty, as were the burgers. Also, some of the food didn't come on time because they simply forgot about the order and many of them were wrong. However, the waiter was nice but it did take quite a while to get water.
when im at work and in the mood for pasta I always call est est est for their lasagna it is very tasty

I tried this place because I like fresh fish prepared simply. the Greek way with olive oil is healthy and tastes good. Must be a lot of others in manhattan feel the same way. Since we have seen a big surge in the number of Greek restaurants serving fish. The better ones have lavaki,dorado, St. Peter or other fish purportedly from the Mediterranean. All of these restaurants prepare the fish the basic same method. These restaurants as I see it , include Taverna with many name variations, and Ethos. So I decided to try Taverna Kyclades. It has a good selection of Mediterranean fish. Prepared well in the usual manner grilled  with olive oil with one side dish. So how did this taverna differentiate itself from so many other choices in the same genre. This taverna had great service, which was fast and efficient. What were the bad points, the dinning room is very loud, the prices are on the higher end compared to other Greek fish restaurants. And the portions are smaller then usual. And the Greek restaurants in the boros include 2 sides. The selection of fish was very good for manhattan where some Greek restaurants only have salmon and some form of red snapper.

Yes, I am going back. The staff are very helpful. The buffet is the best option. There was so many dishes to choose from. The taste was lightly spicy, and delicious. The best way to enjoy Indian cuisine is at a buffet. The service of the staff is very friendly and helpful. I will be returning
I was disappointed by this restaurant. The dishes were salty and it took a long time before they came out. We ordered the green curry and phat see ew. We also ordered dessert which was only mediocre.
They had great food but closed down now. I don't know if they are re-locating.

The food was great! The oysters were so fresh and so was the sea food platter! But what even makes this place better is the owner Jeff! He is so nice and welcoming that it makes me give this place a 5 and a must!!!!

I took my mom here for dinner for her birthday and we are both in agreeance that the food was delicious.  She got the salmon and i got the frutti de mare, both perfectly cooked and the broth in mine was so good with just the right amount of heat. We also agreed that server was not up to par.  She was miserable, didn't even introduce herself, and really hampered the experience.  We had a lovely time and will probably be back but will definitely request a different server.

Awesome food with good service....I like mediterranean cuisine a lot...the place I stay was not having any middle eastern food joints earlier....now I am a regular visitor to this place... Try any item that has lamb...

The perfect local bar. Aside from it being the sports bar of all sports bars, it is cozy, relaxed and a terrific place to get a sandwich. Roast pork with sharp provolone, chips, and an ice cold beer - perfect. Pretenders go across the street to that other place. Real Philly fans, and those who just dig a cool bar go to the Philadium.

Was looking forward to this place as we had heard some good things- however my advice would be to find another spot in old city to spend your brunch dollars.  The food was just not that good- my wife had the chicken biscuit sandwich which was flavorless and after one bite all the breading was off the sandwich.  I had a burger which was ok however the veal bacon as well as the patty lacked any flavor or taste.  The Bloody Mary was about the only good thing I have to comment.  The inside is cool but the food was just really forgettable and nothing about this place will have us making a return visit.  This place is a far cry from the delicious flavorful food coming out if Jason's kitchen at Ela.

What a horrible place to order breakfast. The eggs are runny and the cornbeef hash is the same can dog food I can get from the supermarket. The OJ was good and they did offer something else but I will go elsewhere to get a proper cooked and tasting breakfast.

Very, very good pizza; especially the cappacolla. Lovely ambiance, very rustic and simple. However, the wait staff can be a little snooty. When I began to order an "appetizer/starter" I was curtly cut off with, "have you been here before?" to which I replied that I had. She then said, "then you know how it works here, right? It'll come out when it comes out." So, the food is delicious and it's a very lovely space but someone needs to teach the wait staff to be a little more gracious and polite.

The service at this place is INFURIATING.  I asked three separate people for a refill on my water and got it about 20 minutes later.  Oh, and I was there on a LATE SUNDAY AFTERNOON.  Not exactly prime time.  We had to poke and prod to get bread, and when we handed over the card with the check, the waitress couldn't remember where she put it.   The real kicker here is that we gave ourselves a good amount of time to eat and get to our movie, but thanks to the lazy and unprofessional staff, we couldn't get there before the movie was sold out.  Food was average.  AVOID AT ALL COSTS, especially if you have some place to be in the next 6 hours...

Guys - I love this place, it's typically my go to while in Astoria. However, today I found a cockroach in my chicken plate combo. I was just about to take a bite and there it was buried in the chicken. Yes if was dead but it was big enough to completely gross me out to the point of vomiting. I have pics to prove it check if out just posted them.

So I've been coming here off and on for several years now. After deciding to head up to NJ today and get some szechuan food and reading the reviews, I felt a need to comment. First of all, the restaurant's service is awful. I have come here with "American (non-chinese)" friends and my family (all chinese). It has always been terrible service. That being said, the food is authentic and really tasty szechuan. This means very spicy and big flavor. They also have hotpot, though I have never had it. Staples such as mapo tofu, fried chicken with chills, Shui Zhu Yu (water-cooked fish) are all really good. It's definitely on the pricier side, but it is worth it. I agree with the other reviewers that if you receive the English menu without these authentic dishes, you MUST ask for the other menu. Unfortunately it is very common place for authentic restaurants to have an english menu that is completely different and basically the same as a takeout/delivery "restaurant." It is not worth getting; you have the get the authentic stuff. So expect bias and mediocre food but, go for the good food. My rating is for food, not the service (probably a 2/5).

I stopped in here for a bite to eat post apartment hunting in nearby Prospect Lefferts Gardens. While PLG left little to desire beyond Caribbean food, G. Lee's came on the radar as a twenty minute walk to at least four star barbecue. Now I am a Texan born girl raised in the land of backyard bbq, Southern California. I am difficult to impress when it comes to bbq. I prefer a wet sauce style bbq and G Lee's offered more of the dry rub variety of bbq. I split the meat lovers plate with two sides of greens and jalapeño mac n cheese. Let's start with the pros...the mac n cheese was great, just spicy enough and cheesy enough. The greens were well seasoned but a little dry. The ribs fell off the bone and were huge. And the pulled pork...oh my goodness gracious. Delicious. The chicken was too dry and in general I could've used about a pint of bbq sauce to make this meal a bit more palatable and like a strong three star rating. Drinks were cheap. Décor was also cheap and kitchy. Service was quick and friendly. So for a neighborhood that needs help and quick, G Lee's will do the job for now.

I love Archie's. It's a classic neighborhood pub! Tasty pub food, with a warm and friendly atmosphere. Great people working there too--wait-staff, bartenders, and kitchen staff! I highly recommend Archie's.
Yum Yum Yum. Get Harissa for a little kick (not too spicy at all). The fries are crunchy, which I loved with their sauce. Date banana shake was also good, unique and refreshing.

My husband and I decided to give this place a try after checking out there menu and yelp reviews. Plus it wasn't too far of a walk from our hotel. We were quite disappointed with the place though. I don't think I will be returning. The food was decent and the staff was friendly but the atmosphere inside the restaurant turned me off. The hostess asked us if we would like to eat outside on the patio or inside the restaurant. Well seeing as it's late July and we've been in the heat most of the day we asked that we be seated inside. However, the place was so hot and the front door was wide open. We basically had to sweat through our meal which made the experience pretty awful. I had the Victors favorite pizza and my husband had a chicken Parmesan sandwich....both recommended by our server. They were both good choices but not great.

Place was a ghost town but we walked around the neighborhood and ended up back here. menu very limited...but everything our party of three ate was great. Service excellent (maybe due to very few people there). Calamari tasty and not chewy. Mac and cheese wonderful and the ribs were great. Burger sort of average...nothing special. Atmosphere decent....seems like the nicest resteraunt around.They do need a liquor license.

I'm truly baffled by the amount of 5 star reviews for this place!! I'm sure it has something to do with the novelty of Ramen in the area, but as far as the overall experience goes, it doesn't  come close to deserving it! First of all, there are waaaay too many people working here. The space is tiny, and filling it with staff that doesn't have much to do just makes for uncomfortably  crowded dining. Also, it's super loud, and I was able to hear the servers chatting more than I could hear my date.  I get what they're going for here, but with the 90's music blasting and the brightly colored furniture, the whole thing feels gimmicky. As far as food goes, everything we ordered was super salty. The spicy miso was  dense and tasted like someone dumped a taco seasoning packet into pan drippings.  And, as someone who isn't a big pork fan, the giant grey chunks that floated in my bowl did little to change that opinion. If the flavor they were going for was 3 day old reheated leftovers, then they nailed it! On a positive note, we went on a weekend night and didn't have to wait for a table.
I did not like the calamari......owner spent about 40 minutes kissing my butt.....but the food and prices are not in sync...food essentially sucks.

Awesome steak and night out for 4 friends from Colorado. atmosphere was great and the service was wonderful  (our server was Laura). I ordered the Cowboy Rib eye special cooked medium rare + (perfect temp). If you are looking for a good steakhouse on the island and don't want to spend an arm and a leg then go to this place.

I regularly went to the location on Hamilton Ave growing up. That pizza was amazing. After moving back I found out about the move and tried the new location.  The pizza was amazing, just like the old location, I couldn't understand the bad reviews. But I went this Sunday night and while the edge of the crusts were okay, towards the center of the pizza the crust was similar to an unsalted soggy cracker, if you can imagine what that would taste like. It may just be an issue with some of the chefs dont cook it right. Soggy tasteless crust this still beats every other pizza joint out there, with the exception of the other DeLorenzo's. Palermos is okay too but my stomach is always sick afterwards.
nice authentic food, love the mussels, french onion soup, steak and fries but the best best best is the crepe with poached pear with home made chocolate sauce, aka what the heaven tastes like!

I am sitting outside of Roberta's now so pissed off that I reactivated my yelp account just to review them.  I've been to this place 3 times because the food is excellent. 3rd times the charm - because I'm never coming back. On Top Chef someone said people go to a restaurant for the food. They return for the service. Well, not returning. The first time I came I was a hipster with my girlfriend. Great date, great food. The second and third time I've come here i've been a mom with her wife and baby in tow - and gotten TERRIBLE service. We had to wait over an hour (time we were told was 45 mins), our service was slow, and the hostess and servers were unfriendly - no thank you's, you're welcomes - Nada. I asked the hostess with a snotty attitude this time around if there was a problem because we had a kid with us. Of course she denied it. I went to look around the restaurant and there were other families - older kids, and white families. Listen,my family doesnt look like hipsters - but they were living in this neighborhood way before this neighborhood looked like this - before Roberta's, before organic stores, when the danger was bullets not elitism. So, Roberta's, you better remember why and how you are here and pay more respect to the neighborhood, people, and communities you serve. Its more diverse than Morgan st. We crossed Bushwick ave to enjoy your food. Well, we won't any longer.

Ok...So I've read many of the reviews and I must say my personal experience was mixed.  I wanted to like this place.  Cozy is one thing, but for the price/quality...way too tight.  The food was mixed.  The quail very small, but tasty; The potatoes were good; and the skirt steak was very nice...however...they over did the garlic...which was practically raw!!!  My girlfriend and I could not get the taste out of our mouths until the next day. You know...I understand that everyone wants to stand out from the crowd, but sometimes delivering quality traditional  tapas is what most people seek.
nice feel to the restaurant.  but $9 for an 8oz mimosa just threw me off this place.

I came to the pancake house at around 9 on a Sunaday. It was not extremely packed, but it was still quite full. The first thing that stuck out to me was the noise, the resturant was very loud. The second thing to come to my attention were the carved tables. Many people have drawn all over the tables and the result is a very unique art form that is both creative and pretty epic. However, on to the food. I oredered the pancake sampler. I've never had their pancakes before, but once I took a bite, I was hooked. This place really has the best pancakes I've ever seen, and I enjoyed them immensely. The apricot pecan pancake was exceptionally good. It was very sweet, but the pancake still managed to taste light and airy despite all of the toppings. These pancakes ready made my day. All in all, eating here was a fantastic dining experience.

This was the first time we went to this restaurant.  The atmosphere is nice. Parking situation during a wedding is terrible. Food is extremely pricey. Service was ok, not great, just ok. We went on a Saturday night And we got a table quickly. They where very busy. I really wanted to like this place. The food was not great, but very expensive! Fish and chips for $20?   Over priced and the food isn't that great. Sorry.

Love the food here. The service is also great. One of the best restaurants in the city. The only small thing: when you have a reservation here, you can still wait for a bit of time. But, overall, I love this place. And it's worth the wait. Some of my favorites: the chicken sandwich and the caesar salad.

Intimate, friendly, elegantly old world without a speck of pretension. Delicious wine selection, all very reasonably priced. I had two quartinos - of a Malbec and a Montepulciano. My friend had a Pinot Grigio and then a glass of Prosecco. We did not try the food, though it looked and smelled wonderful. We spent around $30 each. We lingered for about 3 hours over great conversation and found the ambiance well suited to inspire creative dialogue and discussion - well, the combination of good ambiance and good wine seems historically proven to be a facilitator of innovation so I suppose that makes sense! Brilliant use of the tiny space. The design is spot on and really maximizes the square footage without creating any sense of a crush even at the busiest times. The service is good and the servers are absolutely charming. It is no question that I will be regularly returning to this gorgeous dear little place.

Short wait for a table for 2 late on a Friday night.  Got family-style seating at big table in back, which was fine. Packed and noisy and dark (needed my phone as a flashlight to read the menu) but service was great as was the food. Menu is mostly interesting take on comfort food. Good selection of craft beers from all over including several I'd never seen before. That said, I'd forgo the beers for the cocktails - especially the rosemary vodka lemonade.
who run bushwick?!?!?! the anchored inn run bushwick!!!!! not bad music. you weak!! play loud!!

This place is outstanding. Their kababs are the best I've ever had. The gyro platter is unbelievably good. The white and green sauce they make is a perfect accompaniment to any meal. If it wasn't so bad for you, I would eat this every day. The food is VERY filling and it'll keep you satisfied for a day or two. The MECCA sandwich is like heaven. So good. I could order everything on this menu twice, and be happy every time. Next time you need a fix on rice, amazingly slow cooked meat, or some flavors that will wake up your taste buds from the same old same old, this is the place to go.

Based on the reviews I thought this was a nice place to try out, but turned out to be a disaster. This place has a policy that is the customer is always wrong no matter what happens. Just because you have business doesn't mean you should be rude. Save your self a headache and just go to "SEA" in Williamsburg Brooklyn, you won't regret it! They don't accept credit cards which means they most likely file the wrong amount when tax session comes along, anyone wanna send IRS over ?

The ingredients were extremely fresh and I really enjoyed watching the pizza being made. The only reason why I would give this place 4/5 stars is because I like my pizza crust less burnt. Also if the owner reads this review I hope you will consider calling your customers 20 minutes before the pizza is ready. That way we can pick it up fresh out of the oven so it doesn't get soggy from the sauce. Thanks!

Great experience!  We just had dinner at this delightful restaurant and had a wonderful time.  Nice wine selection in an intimate environment - the tables are pretty close to each other but we didn't mind.  The appetizers and dinner selections were all amazing.  On the night we were there, they had an heirloom tomato and mozzarella said which was perfectly seasoned.  Service was attentive, very happy to stumble upon this place!

Service was horrible and so was the food. Here for work and thought the place looked decent. Should have Yelped before I came in.  Waited a good 15min before I waived down a server to order a glass of wine, water and a broiled seafood platter.  Took another 15min for wine to come. Never received the water until I asked for it along with the check. Never received serving utensils until I asked for them either. Would never come again.

Food was okay but very poor customer service. Was excited to see this new burger place open with some healthier options. Ordered a burger+shake combo. Followed the waiter's suggestion of the black bean burger over the turkey. Got the double berry protein shake first. Tried it and could not get past the taste (and I've had healthy fruit+protein shakes before).  My bf took a sip and also did not like the taste. Told the waiter I didn't like the shake when he brought our burgers and he insisted on telling me how it was a "healthy and good shake" before taking it away.   The black bean burger was okay but had no seasoning and was a bit mushier than I expected. Description said 2 patties but it was one huge patty about an inch thick.  The green sauce on the bottom bun really gave the burger all the flavor.  Tried a little of the salmon burger which was better and also had the green sauce.  Was going to ask about the sauce but forgot when we received our bill.   I had to ask why they were still charging for the shake that was barely touched before being taken away. The waiter insisted again that the shake was good and there was nothing wrong with the shake. He also stated that the only problem was that I didn't like the shake - going on to say that if I didn't like the burger and threw it out, he would charge me for it too. Apparently, to him, the customer is wrong unless he/she agrees with him. I had to point out that I had no issue with the burger, that I simply couldn't drink the shake because it tasted odd, that the cup was virtually untouched, and that I have had similar fruit & protein shakes before so it was purely my dislike of that particular shake.  I also pointed out that he didn't offer me a replacement or even water when he took the shake away but was charging me for the nearly untouched shake anyway.  Only after arguing with him did he finally agree to take off the shake. The food probably only ranked 3 stars. If he hadn't felt the need to belittle my opinion of the shake & just removed the shake from the bill to begin with, I would have upgraded the place to 4 stars for customer service alone. The fact that the waiter decided that it was better to treat a customer so poorly made me wonder about the other location in Newark. That's when I saw all the bad reviews that showed similar customer service issues and that our waiter was actually the manager or owner based on his picture in his replies to the reviews. In fact, some of the Newark location reviews are actually for the Kearny location because they only recently added this site on yelp.

Amazing Brunch, high quality food, beautiful presentation. This place is a hidden gem along the west side highway in the meatpacking district. Friendly service also. The eggs benedict was stellar, the ricotta pancakes creatively presented and quite tasty (with real maple syrup) and the asiago truffle omelette is a must. Seriously this place is a standout for brunch.
Solid food quality. Veal and gnocchi cooked to perfection. Waiter very knowledgable about wine and menu...also accommodating for picky kids!

My boyfriend and I had a great experience here except for a little snobbiness from the French waiter. We both got the seared scallops with gnocchi and mushrooms. The food was 5 star quality, so delicious. And we got Tuna Tartar as an appetizer, never had it before. Also very good! Eating on the ship was very different, but enjoyable. We got to watch boats, jet skis, ships go by on the river. The only downside is the ship has a old musty smell to it. But after awhile, you don't smell it anymore.

Went there tonight with my family, the waitstaff was excellent and very attentive to our table and needs. Although it was crowded when we arrived we were able to sit sooner than expected which made us very happy. The food is excellent our waiter recommend some of their most delicious items on the menu and we were more than satisfied to say the least. Definitely try this place out if your near by you won't be disappointed.
It was amazing to find so many gluten free options! I had the angel food cake and it was excellent.

My family and I stumbled upon this restaurant a few weeks ago totally by chance. I normally steer clear of restaurants that offer more than one type of cuisine (K-Top offers four!) but we were tired and hungry and the person who greeted us when we walked in and asked to looked at a menu was so friendly and inviting that we decided to give it a try. Am I glad we did! The food was fantastic! We returned last night with another family, and even their picky toddler loved it. Between our two visits we have tried several dishes, at least one of each type of cuisine. Every dish we've tried has been worthy of ordering again. And the service is top notch. When I asked our server if the recipe of one of the dishes had changed from our previous visit, explaining it was good but not nearly as good as the last time, he checked with the chef and then reported back that it had. He then offered to take it back and have it re-made using the old recipe! We took him up on his offer and within minutes he returned with a fresh dish made of the previous recipe! K-Top is also very reasonably priced. I think everything on the menu was under $20. It's hard to recommend any one item because they've all been so good, but I have to put a plug in for the pineapple fried rice, which is served in a half pineapple shell. My only criticism of the place is the way the name is written. The K and the P are so abstract that we literally thought the name of the restaurant was To! Following our first visit we were telling people about this great new restaurant in Chinatown oddly named To. We almost couldn't find it in a Google search when our friends wanted to check out the menu in advance. Despite its confusing name, I sincerely hope people will give this restaurant a try because it is truly a find.
Soup dumplings are the draw here and everyone in the know here seemed to be ordering it.  Good service not surly to those of us who look clueless.

We came here for the first time during restaurant week and now we'll definitely be coming back on a regular basis. The service was top notch, the atmosphere was cool, and the food was spot on. Between the four of us, we ordered most of the appetizers and four of the entrees. Not a single plate was left uncleaned. Everything was a hit, including their guacamole, the ceviche, the special grouper, the chicken, and the ropa vieja. And the desserts were unbelievably good--the pineapple upside down cake and the coconut custard mango sorbet (my wife can't stop talking about how good this coconut dessert was). Excited to go try their brunch, the menu looks awesome.

Good prices for rolls so you can get a good variety. However the rolls themselves are quite small so the cost is average to other places I'm the area. The sushi was good and there was a nice selection of apps and salads to add variety to the meal. Overall we would come back if we were in the area and in search of sushi but we wouldn't go out of the way to come here.

This place good is OK.  But the service is terrible. At first they greet you nicely,  but after you order then they ignore you.  I spoke to 2 different waiter and they totally ignore what we ask.  I had to ask for 2 cup of ice water for my kids 3 times before they bring it to me.  I can understand if it was busy but it was not that busy at all.  They just totally ignore our request.  Totally bad service. I will not be returning to this restaurant again.

Since MP has opened I have been here many times.  The octopus (as everyone says) is awesome!  I have never been disappointed with the food here.  The outdoor cafe area is a nice place to sit at night at have a cocktail and an appetizer.  Definitely one of the nicer restaurants on Ditmars, which means it can be a little pricey!

The meal I had here was so incredibly delicious that only a modicum of good manners prevented me from licking my plate.  Seriously - it was that good. This place is on the dressy side of casual without being formal.  It's also a little on the pricey side, but in my opinion well worth it. If I had a foodie friend who I wanted to impress or was planning for a date night or a business dinner Tip Top would be my number one choice.
cheap drunk, giant tuna neck for $13, fresh and succulent Udon is excellent served al-dente with flavor broth and quality meat would def come back!

This place is definitely historic and has quite the feel to it. I would say, you have to either go to Pats and/or Genos on your Philly trip just to experience it. The steak was good, not great, but good. I got the extra cheese with whiz and provolone. I would recommend it. The service is spotty at best, but what do you expect... A little bit sketchy of an area, but worth the cab ride over.

Great service! The cashier is absolutely wonderful and everyone was very welcoming. They constantly shout in Japanese which is pretty cool. The food is on point! Wait is a little long, but it's expected because it's very popular. Everything runs very smooth.

Went there for Sunday brunch. First of all, it wasn't busy at 1 pm. Beer selection was great! Food was great! We had the burger on French toast and an omelet. The French toast burger was amazing! The omelet was an omelet but hey...nice and fluffy. We will be back.
Really good brunch spot. Duck confit was off the charts. Service was solid, and the atmosphere was great. Would recommend it to anyone.

Just had a fantastic lunch at The Crabby Shack today! My lady and I stopped by during their soft opening for lunch. I hadn't eaten yet and was ready for some serious seafood. After talking with the helpful server we decided to do the King Crab Platter and the Crab Cake Sliders. Both were amazing! Luckily this wasn't our first date, so my girlfriend was un-phased when a claw cracked and went flying in her direction. The seasoning in the crab cakes and on the crab legs were fantastic! We honestly didn't even need butter. Our server had mentioned that there have been people who eat the platter on their own and I may have been able to as well, but with the crab cakes it was very filling. Their drink selection was a bit limited, but it is their soft opening, so I don't hold it against them. I will certainly be looking forward to having a nice beer with a meal there in the future though. As we were eating the staff in the back of house came out to see how everyone was enjoying their meals. They're all incredibly nice and a real pleasure to be around. Bottom line: Great food, great hospitality and a great inclusion to the neighborhood! If you're in Crown Heights and you're getting seafood somewhere else, you're wasting your time! 5 stars! Will crack crabs again!

The customer service was very bad, also one of the waiters asked for a 15 percent tip, he insisted and we refused.  We had the Sukiyaki, the meat was bland and the seasoning was too sweet.  We're from LA where Ramen and Shabu is prime.  I guess we had high expectations, try another spot!
Food and service were excellent!!! Our eyes were bigger then our stomachs but we didn't mind because the leftovers were just as delicious!

I live a block away from here and would live here if I could.  I've tried many Brasilian spots and this one is the smallest, but by far the best.  And what's better is that it's like being home. Very comfortable setting and warm atmosphere. Always busy and bustling and the food is always fresh. Even if you don't go for the BBQ meats(served in the back through a window not many notice), their buffet selection boasts a huge variety that includes both hot and cold foods, soups, and various meats and fish.  It is especially great for those days when I need food comforting.  And don't forget to top your meal off with a brigadeiro or a slice of brigadeiro cake and you're good to go.

I take down tacos at this spot at least once a week, sometimes twice. A lot of NYC spots pursue cool -- and that can def come off cheezy contrived. This place tho has a genuine cool vibe. Like Jeter or John Mayer Live in LA. Place fills up but you don't feel crowded. Great volume control on the music. They played a couple songs from the late 90s, early 00s that I liked. Highly recommend the Tecate. Get 3.

Very unimpressed. Ordered the minestrone soup - was more like a bowl of pasta sauce only bland and without flavor. Chopped salad was fine, but nothing special at all - deconstructed so I got to mix my own veggies on the plate - stupid. The biscuits and gravy was the best thing we ordered and it too was a disappointment. The sausage gravy was okay, nothing wrong with it, but nothing special either. The biscuits were so over cooker that they were solid on both sides. You're not suppose to have to saw through a biscuit. Better bunches at most diners, couldn't believe the price point verse quality. Won't be back.

The first thing that caught my attention when I walked through the door was how packed this place was. I know large crowds are to be expected pretty much anywhere you go in Times Square, but it still caught me a little off guard. Once we were seated, our waiter came over to our table and asked if there was still a member of our group with a gluten allergy. Everyone in my party was impressed with this because our reservation was made several months in advance. There were three couples in our party, so we decided to order one dish per couple that we would share with the group. Our choices were the house salad, the veal saltimbocca, and a pasta special that included rigatoni, lasagna and possibly the best cheese ravioli I've ever had. The portions were huge and the food in general was good but not great. I'm not sure that I would visit again, but only because I don't live in NY and there are so many different places that I want to try every time I visit. I would definitely recommend going there at least once, though, especially if you're with a large group.
terrible service.  inattentive waitstaff. cocktails are all ice, no drink. do not waste your money here.

It seems that Russet Restaurant in Philadelphia does not welcome wheelchair users! We made a reservation at Russet for dinner. I told Russet that our daughter uses a wheelchair. They never informed us that the restaurant wasn't accessible. We traveled over an hour to get there. But, when we got there, there was no way for our daughter to enter in her wheelchair. It was quite a shock to learn this AFTER we arrived! Shame on you, Russet, in this day and age! I am posting this so that no other wheelchair users will have to experience this.

Used to love this place but won't be back. The service is so terrible and the food is so overpriced. I haven't been in a year because of the service. Just went back and it was the worst ever. We went early on purpose because the staff can't handle the crowds. Got there at 11:40. There was one table there. We got our menus and drinks and no one came back. More tables filled in and we flagged someone down for our order. We both ordered wraps but I asked for mine as a salad. No problem. The sandwiches come with two sides. Our waitress asked what we wanted so we picked one. She said they come with two sides but we probably don't want the other. Why wouldn't we?? We're paying an arm and a leg for a sandwich of course we want what comes with it. Our food came out last. 10 min before we had to leave to get back to work. Mine was in sandwich form not salad as requested. I didn't have time to fix it. It was supposed to have corn chips in it- I had one chip at the bottom of my wrap. Whatever. No one came back to see how lunch was. When we asked for boxes and the check the waitress gave us a dirty look. I paid cash my friend asked for half the bill on her card. The waitress came back and put the whole thing on her card. My friend was furious with the whole situation so went and asked to speak to a manager. No manager onsite but she spoke to an older woman about our experience. Another waitress was sitting in the back and looked up and rolled her eyes at my friend. Totally uncalled for and unprofessional. We want to love this place but I'm done. There are SO many other options in Glastonbury that are happy to have the patronage and can provide the level of service equivalent to the price you pay. Also, when you visit the Bean in the winter you have to wear your coat and scarf. Just not worth the time and money.

I have been enjoying Chicken Galore my entire life. The chicken is always so juicy and the crunchy yumminess on the outside is crave worthy. Fries are delicious, but get a side of nacho cheese ;). Been having the fish and chips special every year during Lent, and to this day it is the only fish I will eat.

This is my second visit and it was so good!especially the skirt steak and grilled octopus.... It's truly a hidden gem! And enjoyed afterwards with music and drinks in the lower level hookah lounge really nice set up!!!

Food: 3 Atmosphere: 3 Service: 1 Cleanliness:1 Note: We did not order Pizza. Overall, seems like a good place if you are a regular,  sadly, we were not and it showed. We came for a quick dinner this evening. We had to find an employee and ask to be seated.   We then waited a while (well over 5 min) before anyone took our drink order.  We had to ask for our table to be cleaned as it was still dirty from the table prior.   Our server returned with silverware and then quickly walked away before we could order our food. The staff seemed very overwhelmed with the amount of people in the restaurant.  While we waited, another party came in and were greeted at the door right away, obviously a regular. They were sat and their entire order (drinks and food) was taken and we still had not even gotten our drinks. Later, when we finally got our food (small hot chicken breast grinder with cheese, sauce and peppers as well as a large hot turkey grinder with lettuce, tomato and mayo) we were surprised with the large portions.  The chicken was breaded,  which was not mentioned on the menu. The final bill came to $26, which included a soda, beer (bottle only, they do not have beer on tap) and our two grinders.  We noth came home with leftovers, which is a positive although not enough to make up for the service. When it came time to pay we had to go to the main counter and ask for a box and the check.  When the server did not return to collect our money (we waited more than enough time), we again had to get up to find her.

Terrible brunch experience. Arrived on a 4 year party. Could see that brunch was still clearly being served the bartender said they stopped serving brunch an hour ago. I got no food, I was not offered anything. How hard would that be to offer some eggs and toast? Never going back there

Empire diner Second time for brunch and again service was terrible. Asked for an egg on my burger and was denied. The reason was that they don't do sides of eggs... ITS BRUNCH TIME. This was an addition not a sub. I was willing to pay well for that egg. Telling a customer no?! The staff (our server: Lindsay) acts like we are bothering them by coming in and wishing for good service. Server forgot we order beers and it wasn't like they were busy. Only 7 sat tables. The chef running the line wasn't busy either; she was leaning on the line and chatting with the staff... So why couldn't i get an egg?!? Especially when a dish literally has an over easy egg. Thanks. And thank you for slamming down the check. Awesome. Don't recommend eating here. Do take out. The food was great!!

So amazing !! This is my second time coming here. The food is so authentic and delicious, I love to eat and here it's always a challenge to finish the whole plate!! The portions are awesome and the service is friendly. Highly recommend :)

I really wanted to like this place, but it's just so poorly run. Unorganized, the guy at the register didn't even have cash to give change, and everything was super slow. Also it hotter in there than it was outside. The chicken itself was really good, but we just felt miserable sitting in there. Definitely would recommend take out or delivery tho

First off. This rating is for service and not the food. I have to stress that first. That being said I can't begin to say how disappointed I am in the service (or lack there of) I received tonight. I actually frequent this restaurant and have for years. Tonight I attempted to bring 7 of my friends along to enjoy dinner here for a birthday celebration. When we arrived we asked what the wait time would be. The hostess who was very nice told us 20-25 minutes for indoor or we could be seated immediately outdoor. The 8 of us were talking and another woman arrived at the hostess station and told her it would not be 25 min but 45 to an hour. So we asked to be seated outside. The hostess explained that if we chose to eat outside if it rained there would be no guarantee we could be moved indoors. We agreed and that was fine. The hostess then mentioned to the other young lady (who I would later find out was named laney) that we chose outside and she was worried about the rain. Laney told her "well that isn't our problem". During the time that I was speaking to the hostess the other young woman kept repeating what the hostess was telling me. I'm an adult and I can hear plenty well so I knew what she was saying the first time and didn't need a third party repeating it. While the hostess sat the rest of my party I stuck around to ask the young lady if there was a problem or if we had done something to annoy or offend her. She simply stated she wasn't referring to us she was talking about something else. Ok. After the hostess sat us, no one ever arrived to take our order. No one even brought us water or asked if we wanted a drink. Nothing. To be so worried about us possibly eating in the rain, yet no one cared to try to get our order in a timely manner.   After waiting with no sign of service what so ever, I picked all of our menus up and returned them to the hostess. I have never been so disappointed in the service I've received here. It's one of my favorite places to eat but tonight it left a bad taste in my mouth.

My friend has always raved about how the food from The Halal Guys is, and I decided to give it a try because I just came out from a meeting really late, and I gave it a go. It was ok. I mean I didn't experience what my friend explained to me, but for a try it was just okay....

Really not sure what the other people were eating, but when I checked out this restaurant based on the decent reviews, I wondered if I was missing out on something. Regardless of what my boyfriend or I ordered, the food was tasteless. Should've taken the pro-tip from the guy sitting across from us who poured a ridiculous amount of sriracha and cilantro into his broth before doing anything. My bowl of noodles also came with a fried egg, and the yolk was almost completely green. Tendons were also suspiciously stiff and hard to chew. On the bright side, they give you a lot of noodles and the dumplings are pretty good.
Really friendly staff serving excellent Stumptown coffee in a small, cool spot in Hell's Kitchen.  Worth a visit!!

Some of the worst service I've ever received at any type of dining establishment, bar or restaurant. Which is a shame, because the food was pretty good. We asked for a table and were told to wait at the bar, and we'd be told once one was available. It wasn't particularly busy. Weekday night. The bartenders both dismissed my friend and I because we weren't part of the after work cocktail crowd, begrudgingly asking for our ID's as if we were wasting her time. The man (I believe the manager?) who told us he'd let us know about a table becoming available forgot about us, and I saw a bar top table open up and grabbed it. The bartender then told us, painstakingly, that we'd have to close out if we moved from the bar. She had labeled out tab on her register as "kids". Sweet. Once at the table someone took a food order, and we never saw that waiter again. The food came out and was good. No one came and checked on us ever or asked if we needed anything like another drink. Eventually, the man whom I believe was the manager came over, and we were finally able to ask for the bill. If you don't want younger people to leave bad tips, don't assume they're going to and overlook them. Because then we had a reason to leave a bad tip.
The food here is great, I had the Cali burger and truffle fries so good.

Don't eat here unless you like dirty water from the vents falling on you and your food.  When I complained, the waitress at first wouldn't believe me, but when she couldn't deny the big drops, said, "Yeah, they do that sometimes." I asked for the manager and when he eventually showed up, his main comment, aside from a shrug, was that we should have moved.  Right, that's the customers' job to find a table for themselves that's not too gross to sit at. Oh, and the chicken salad was bland.

This is a must stop if your visiting and looking for a place to get a authentic cheese steak in Philly.  The food was better than Pat's which is across the street.  I was really hungry so I got a sandwich from both places!  I feel like I got the real Philly cheese steak experience!  There are plenty of famous celebs and politicians on the wall with Geno.  Apparently quite a few of them stop in for a cheese steak there.  Bring Cash.

The service here is terrible. The bartender is incredibly rude and the food is mediocre at best. The main bartender yelled at us and was very rude to us because we wanted to pay a check between three credit cards.

The service was great! For starters I would recommend downloading the app NoWait that way you can "wait" in line without actually waiting at the restaurant. Since I wasn't aware of the app I waited about an hour or so but my boyfriend and I just walked around the area until we received the text that our table was ready. Anyway now for the food, the food was good! Not the best brunch I've had and definitely pricey (about $50 for two) but it was a nice place for a one time thing to try something different, especially since I went there for breakfast on my birthday. It's a small place so expect to sit very close to the table next to you. Last but not least, the milkshake I had was DELICIOUS!

Honestly I think the simplicity of walking in and buying a huge slice of pizza and being able to stroll about the eclectic soho neighbourhood makes this pizza joint! But on top of that, this is the most flavoursome pizza I have eaten, with a perfect combination of sauce versus cheese the margherita is perfection, seriously.
Thiru has wonderful personality. He has a very loyal clientele that keeps him very busy during the day.
Just perfect. In every way. Food service wine. Gnocchi. Paperdelle. Yum
I love the place, the food is truly Italian and the staff is friendly. Astoria needed a place like this, I am so happy they finally opened because the prices are also really good.

The atmosphere is classy but not stuffy. We (the 4 of us) went for the tasting menu and were surprised on the quality and ingenuity of the chef. He even came out to personally serve us on course. There were pre-tasting bites: all surprises. The fish dish was excellently cooked, and the lamb was served two ways: as delicious sweet breads and as a loin. The raw scallops usually are not afavorite of mine, but very enjoyable at this fine place. The meal was very very expensive, but we were celebrating a fine event. I would recommend this place for a fine meal to impress.

99 Restaurant was a nice place to go.  The menu had a number of items I could have chosen.  We had a small group but the service was very good and accommodating.  Their outdoor patio provided a covered but pleasant alternative to the indoor seating. I would recommend this restaurant to others.

This spot is NYC's PREMIER TATER TOT CLUB. Most good NYC nightclubs will charge you at least a grand for table service. But I was able to score a table at American Retro for FREE. So sick. At first I was pissed that they didn't offer (traditional) bottle service. But after I threw a bit of a fit, the manager explained to me that we COULD get bottle service - just that the bartender would have to serve it to me and my bros one drink at a time. Seemed like a pretty tight idea. Wonder if more places will start doing that? Sickest of all, Retro (unlike every other premier NYC nightclub I've been to - and I've been to A LOT of premier NYC nightclubs because I'm a wealthy businessman/sex addict) offers a wide variety of tot-based dishes. My boy J-Dubb got an order of "Pizza Tots" - an Italian take on the grated-and-fried potato dish. I went with the "Tot-chos" - Mexican-style tater tots. Long story short, I don't see myself ever going to another nightclub that doesn't offer tots. OTHER REASONS RETRO IS NYC'S HOTTEST TOT CLUB - Conveniently located next to a Mobil gas station - Also down the street from Larry Flint's Hustler Club - which doesn't serve tots despite the pricey cover - Retro has this dope robot-DJ that will play whatever song you want in exchange for a dollar. - There's not a ton of room to dance, so me and J-Dubb just played skee ball and split "Disco Tots" instead.

Been here multiple times. Food, just OK at best. Nothing special including the onion rings that every one raves about. Burgers small and very ordinary. Ice cream is OK but again nothing special. About on a par for a homemade ice cream store. They have a "policy" that dictates that a Sunday "must" be served in a Sunday glass or you have to pay extra for a "custom order". Sounds silly and ridiculous because in a Sunday glass the ice cream drips over the glass and all of the syrup is on the bottom of the glass. Therefore when you put the spoon in to get to the syrup the ice cream goes over the top and you lose about 20% on the table or plate below. What possible difference it can make to the store is beyond me. I wouldn't go here for the best ice cream and certainly not for the food but if you want to visit a 50's ice cream parlor and a Sopranos' site, then it's worth a visit.

Not a good experience, and not worth a second try.  Ordered the yellow and red beet salad. only has red beets...Ok .. Stuff happens.. the salad was ok but not what I thought it would be for the $$.  Then we ordered two pizzas. We choose the make our own.  Base price to be $7 plus $2.50 per topping... We DID NOT want the margherita pizza.. at $10.50 I believe.  The waitress said to us well you will get the margherita with toppings, and I said, that is not what your menu shows.  I want a regular pizza, not a magherita.  I think I was speaking another language! Sure enough.. we got margherita pizzas! I did no eat mine, as I don't care for this type of pizza.   When the bill came they had charged the $10.50 plus toppings instead of the $7 plus toppings. They adjusted my bill by 10% which did not correct the price to what was on the menu.  I guess they did not want me to be satifield and wanted the $$ instead.  I was not going to continue to argue.  I just want the bad experience to end!!! Do they not know the difference between basic pizza and a margherita? Or are they just trying to upcharge the customer? They did give us complimentary gelato, which I did not eat. It looked to be Cherry Vanilla. My opinion-- OVER PRICED and not worth the bang for your buck.  Pizza is like ice cream.. 100's of way to make it! Everyone likes something different! I will pay good money for good food.. this was not it!

The food was pretty good, but what makes this a 5 is how amazing the owner was. I've never been to an establishment where the owner was so attentive. He custom made my order and even gave us a sample of items that aren't even on the menu yet! The food itself is almost a fusion of Indian food with a comfort food feel.

I had lunch here today and it was ok. The pad Thai was a bit too tangy and overly sweet. They have great lunch specials however the service is not very attentive and it's extremely slow. They serve Thai ice tea in mason jars which is super cute however that isn't enough to make me come back. If I want better Thai I'll just walk up the block and go to yum yum they have better food and slightly cheaper prices.

been going here for years before it got upscale and I enjoyed it either way. But the food quality has gone down but their servers are great and fast they monitor your drinks and are attentive. The manager is clueless and they change too much management get your management together the food overall though I have to say is good but sometime bland and overly priced
best deli in montclair yummmm
Tried to go to The Burger Joint at 2:30 but the wait was one hour. Walked to Graso. Good BBQ Burger and Rosemary Fries.
Great service and great food with a very nice atmosphere, what else can you ask for?

wow, if I had seen these reviews before we came here, I would have talked my friends out of coming here.  fortunately, I did not, and we had an absolutely great experience here. when we got here, the restaurant was pretty empty for a Saturday night, which is kinda sad, because the food was great!  we had ordered the chicken schnitzel, the bahn mi, lamb ribs, pickled mussels and the pig head!  but really, the two dishes that stood out were the lamb ribs and the pig head!   as gross as a pig's head looks, it was really good.  I came with a bunch of Filipinos, so they were super excited to order this thing.  This is pretty much like Lechon, but you didn't need the lechon sauce at all, really tasty.  I would highly recommend it if you have more than 2 people since there's a lot of meat on the head.  The lamb ribs were REALLY tasty too, and probably would have been my favorite dish had we not ordered the pig head. since we had already been day drinking down the street at the Ides, we didn't order any alcohol.  Also, who's this chef?  apparently, Top Chef Season 2 winner is the exec chef here.  I didn't start watching Top Chef until about Season 4, so I had no idea who Ilan Hall is.  no matter, he cooked a great meal for us and even came by our table to take a picture with the group and the first pig head he's sold! overall, it was a great dining experience and the wait staff was excellent as well.  hopefully, the ratings will get better for this restaurant because it definitely is a gem.

First things first: Open Door is awesome. More people need to come through. Open Door, being a gastropub, caters to the likes of fine food AND alcohol. The food is always amazing everytime I come. My favorite has to be the chicken p esto sandwich, the beet carpacchio salad, the rice and beans, and the chip trio which has friend corn chips, eggplant and plantains. Soooo delicious. Im going to state right now, that if you have had a "bad" experience, its worth another try. Open Door strives to impress. Nick, the owner, is very personable, getting to know each and everyone of his customers. He trains his staff on the rule that a happy staff gives way to a happy customer; a pleasant experience. The  bar may get rowdy, but what can you expect from people having a good time? The bar creates an atmosphere, most definitely. Gerard is a fantastic bartender always anticipating and ready for your next beverage, Billy will amuse you with his charm and his fun puns and jokes, always ready to put a smile on your face. Wyatt is able to do all, (it may be his awesome beard,) Hes always ready to please, and bend over backwards. And lets not forget Thomas, friendly, always on his grind, experimental -always ready to create something new and different. The staff is great. The food is great. The alcohol always delicious. With a name like Open Door, they cater to everyone. Young, old, from LIC or Timbuktu, always ready and happy to serve you, the only wish to be a part of a community, to connect and be connected. This place deserves more service, hence the 5 stars.
this place was a definite must try when in Manhattan...

I came here the other day for lunch with a friend. It's absolutely wonderful place. I ordered tuna burger which mentioned in many reviews, and it was delicious. The service was excellent. Would definitely go back.

This restaurant was amazing! After reading the yelp reviews, my boyfriend and I decided to eat at Jones. The reviews were 100% accurate. The food was delicious, and the vibe of the restaurant was very fun. I would recommend ordering the mac n cheese....so creamy and cheesy!

Delicious food and great cocktails just off the park.  I've eaten here twice now and both times I was greeted by the owners who clearly care about their customers.  Cute place, great for a quick bite or a romantic date.  I can't wait to go back soon!

Great bar and restaurant.  They have an Awesome beer selection.  The corn dip is a must get, it's cheesy and delicious.  The cheese burger was great and so was the Mac and cheese. My only complaint would be for 14$ they should give you more fried chicken or at least 2 sides instead of 1.
Went to the restaurant serving pizza and pasta. Amazing dishes food was reasonably priced. We waited upstairs at the Birreria where we tried some great italian beer. Lidia and Mario we salute you!

Our group of 5 was treated like "royalty" by our waiter Emin. He attended to our every needs and thoroughly explained what we were ordering.  We were surprisingly seated in a lovely upper level curved shaped booth overlooking a fantastic view of the entire restaurant. This was our first visit and it won't be our last. The food was excellent and professionally prepared and served. The deserts were over the top and exceeded our expectations! Tony's Di Napoli is located at a very convenient location next to several theaters in the area. Don't pay attention to Dana C's review. We got more than what we paid for. A true bargain in mid-town!

Great neighborhood restaurant. We've eaten there a few times since moving to the area and the food is consistently great.  The servers are always so kind and efficient. Prices are reasonable and the portion sizes are perfect. The restaurant appears clean on the inside and carryout times are quick. Highly recommend this restaurant, its one of the best in the area!
Culmination of price, taste, amount, service is what gets this place 5 stars. Wait sucks, deal with it. At least it tastes better than the cronut and you don't have to wait as long =P

The food is outstanding! I've been several times and each time I order something different and I'm blown away. The staff are great. I have to say my favorite thing about this place is that they do not rush you, they let you sit and enjoy your meal...even if it's just a snack, they want you to savor it along with your wine. Speaking of wine, that menu is fantastic as is the by the glass options. Can't recommend this place enough.

I gave this two stars instead of one because this establishment is all about family and I respect that so much. However, I bought a grilled chicken salad from Andro's and was surprised by a dead bug (cannot specify which rodent) in my salad, after eating half. Call me a liar, but.. I had a bug in my salad. It is time to update this establishment and clean it out. It's been here for way too long to still have the same nasty sticky tables and chairs. I will never eat here again, BUT if I saw that it was cleaned up and remodeled, I would be a loyal customer again, because ultimately, the food is great.

Love this place, The atmosphere is very nice and the food is above average! Only reason why giving 3 instead of 4 starts bcuz how packed the place is. Also the service is kinda slow, still love it tho!

Menu is rather simple but tasty. There are tacos and quesadillas with either corn or flour shells. I preferred the corn. No seats at the stand so either find one in the public area or be prepared to eat standing. This is a great value meal for NYC, just realize the rating is for the food and not the complete dining experience as this is not a restaurant.

First time I tried Kochi in September 2013, soon after its opening, and visiting often after that. Kochi is the best Indian cuisine that I have ever tasted in North America. I feel like home when I am in Kochi. The food has authentic Kerala standards. The staff in Kochi are very welcoming, friendly and enthusiastic in doing their job. Owner Thomas, chef Mathew, and the serving staff, all have professional training in the field and you can identify their talent by tasting the food. I tasted a number of items including Kerala puttu-kadala curry, kappa-meen curry, Egg curry, different snacks including halwa, neyyappam and all of them were great!  Kochi offer lunch buffet every working days. They recently started offering dinner buffets on Mondays and is having amazing variety dishes. Among the side dishes, what I like the most is their appam--simply amazing! Rice payasam is one of their best dissert! Kochi deserves a six star, but I can only give a five. I would definitely visit Kochi again!
Food was terrible, when we comment on the Pork  having to much fat, the waiter said this is a characteristic of the dish. We had travel all the way from South Jersey to this terrible place

Been looking forward to this spot opening up in LIC for over a year. We need restaurant diversity! Service took forever.  The bar selection was a joke, but bartender said more types of tequila and wine and vodka were coming.  Come on Jose Cuervo?? Ceviche Mixto had so many fillers on the side it wasn't really Ceviche. (try Casa Enrique's Ceviche, it's perfect) Pulpo al Olivo which is supposed to be thin slices of Octopus has a thick mayonaise type of sauce that completely smothered it and oozed all over the plate.  It's octopus for goodness sakes! Aguadito de Pollo (Cilantro rice chicken soup) was very salty and the chicken was beyond fatty.  The broth was this yucky brown color.  Not what I expected. Chupe de Camarones (Shrimp Chowder. Lima Beans ,corn and Huacatay.  Fried Egg) It was just disgusting...  3 of 4 of us were completely perplexed. The Jalea (Crispy fish, squid, mussels and shrimp)  was actually tasty. Over all maybe I'll visit in a few months.  Only the first week it's been open but hasn't the owner's dad been in the same business for over 20 years? Total Waste of time and money...  Good luck on your visit!

We had a fantastic meal at this place. Skip the table service and go up to the bar. Tim, the bartender was AWSOME! We really enjoyed talking to him during our meal :-). Will definitely come back next time we are in NY.

This place has a friendly staff and what I thought was delicious food. I went there last night for restaurant week! But sadly about midnight it was clear I had eaten something bad and was up all night sick with food poisoning. I had the corn soup/fried chicken/Creme brûlée. The only thing I thought may be off was the Creme brûlée. It had a odd warm butter on it and it wasn't a pleasant temperature. Too bad. Pretty pricy to get food illness! Not recommending this place but I really wanted to. Beware.

I have been going to Comerio on and off for 15 or so years. If you want some AWESOME home cooked yummy Spanish food, This is the place to be! I get the white rice and beans and the potato ball (as I call it) stuffed with hamburg... Mmmmmmm!! I can't write anymore because my mouth is watering at this point. If your in the area def stop in and eat (or take to go). Oh and their prices, AWESOME! paid $10.50 for a order or rice and beans 2 potato ball and 2 cans of soda when my bf and I went in a few weeks ago! Cannot beat that.
Know the guys for a couple years and know they love to cook and got to try the bacon ranch
Always a must when in Center City Philly

We had the address of this restaurant and were right in front of it but could not believe how small it is. We took a subway there and it is a short walk from the subway. It is a small, friendly restaurant in which the food is fresh and presented in large portions. Be prepared for HOT food arriving to your table. Service was satisfactory as this one gentleman had the entire dining room.

Amazing cute place! Amazing Staff Amazing food. Went there two days in a row because I missed it! This place is definitely for a romantic or nicer occasion, however, I don't think it would matter if you went in casual. The place is absolutely gorgeous and the food was AMAZING. I went there for dessert, and I got the Italian Ricotta Cheesecake. If you don't like too sweet of a dessert, this is what you should get!!! I asked the waiter (BENJAMIN is awesome) which drink would pair nice and he was RIGHT!!! It complemented PERFECTLY. Also, paired my friends dessert nicely as well! He had the Blueberry cobbler (warm) with dark chocolate gelato with the malbec! Benjamin has the most gorgeous eyes and is incredibly helpful and friendly!!! Even when I went back, the other waiter helped pair our food very nicely as well!! The Margherita pizza was AWESOME! with the white wine! THIS IS A MUST  GO!!!! I will def come back!!!

3.5 Stars. Came for an early dinner on Sunday night in the summer. Seated right away at a table for two near the window, far enough away from the hustle and bustle, though very close to our neighbors, not really a bother, but be advised, you could be nearly bumping elbows with folks. We were served promptly by a very efficient, and attentive, if not the friendliest server (everybody is allowed to be tired of working I suppose). Just as a little snack to start we had the deviled egg. Very tasty, with a spicy kick, though far too salty for my taste, personally. 3 stars. Both my date and I ordered the burger, mine I asked for rare, which...yeah I suppose it was nearly there; delicious, however it was cooked. The roquefort cheese on the burger added a very unique and strong flavor, and they used just little enough of the cheese so that it didn't overpower the beef itself. Again, for my tastes, the cheese was too salty, but the flavor was distraction enough. Onto the perfectly grilled bun I added a dash of ketchup (which I don't think is your typical brand...not over-sweet) and it was lovely overall. One minor thing...the burger is served with fries...I won't even call them shoestring, more like "angel hair" fries. I discovered there is such a thing as too thin. Tasty though they were (anything deep fried with salt and rosemary is bound to be), I actually found it rather difficult to eat them. I resorted to a rather bizarre technique of smushing my burger into a pile of them and eating the ones that stuck with a bite of my burger. Strange I know, but effective. I seldom find myself enamored with French fries, but when I do, they are thin, but I can also tell that it's potato that I'm eating! Burger: 4 stars Overall a very good experience, and even though I can't help but feel like some of what I am paying for is rent in the West Village, I do like the neighborhood as much as the owner apparently does, and will almost certainly return. Food: 3.5 Service 3.5 Atmosphere: 4 Price: 3

Quite an experience.  We arrived early for a special evening, a birthday dinner with my boyfriend.  After a drink at the bar we sat down at our table next the servers station.  We were not pleased but sat down anyways.  Our waitress started to take our order and told us initially not to order the pita spreads.  Quite a strange place to have the waitress suggest we do not order certain menu items.  Nevertheless, we ordered an array of bar bites, spreads, an appetizer, a veggie, and an entrée to share. What came next was just completely terrible.  The bar bites, pita spreads and appetizers were all brought out at the same time.  Our table was too small so they took away our water and bread.  While still eating they began to clear away our plates.  In disgust  we let them continue as we looked in shock.  Then within 30 seconds they brought our veggie and main dish.  No break between the first course and second course.  We decided to wait to eat as we wanted to enjoy our evening, not feel rushed.  Within a few mins the waitress asked us how our meal was and to enjoy it - we haven't begun to eat.  Upon eating the tarragon chicken we notice the only thing we tasted was salt! Then we began to notice the waitress waiting around at the server station right next to our table watching and waiting for us to be done.  Following that the busboy began to do the same.  Romantic evening huh?   In disgust we decided to pay our bill and leave.  We spoke to the manager Melissa Gervasi who did not seem to show any concern or solidarity.  She instead gave me a few nods, said yes with a smile and told me to make a reservations through her. From a nice, well reviewed establishment I expected to have what should have been a 4 course meal last longer than 45 mins.  I would highly suggest looking past the name bobby flay if you want a truly relaxing, enjoyable, eating experience.  I will never be back at Gato.

Huge fan of this Vanessa location. Cheap pricing, sizeable amounts of tasty food, and quick service. Amazing coconut bubble tea. I eat there before I go to see bands. Minor negative is seating. Be prepared to stand and eat or eat outside by the garbage that's outside. Other than that, it definitely worth it.

Food is pretty good but last time I was there two people at my table commented separately on how the "sea bass" in the tagine tasted remarkably like tilapia. Kind of a cheap short cut in my book. I'll still be back because of the convenience of location and beautiful interior. I'll just be sure to order vegetarian dishes from now on.

We arrived on Sunday just 5 minute before they closed their kitchen for the afternoon.  Technically speaking they could have still served us, and they were extremely rude about.  I do not recommend this place.  Further, the place was empty which infuriates me even more.

We went at Nerai on Saturday for dinner.The food and the cocktails were excellent. Very nice atmosphere .They must have the best octopus we ever had. Konstantin,the waiter same  as last time,surpass our expectations.We will go back soon.

Absolutely delicious!!! The bread and the dipping sauce were so yummy. I ordered the caprese appetizer, and I love that the tomatoes and cheese were placed on top of bread! My boyfriend ordered the cheese pizza, and it was the perfect mix of sauce and cheese! I would definitely come here again!

Great food but way too noisy. Even when you ask the staff to turn down the loud music so that you can talk, they refuse in a passive-aggressive way. Will not return - I don't want to have to wear ear-plugs when eating breakfast!
The pizza is Ok...just as good as others. it's the poor attitude of the help. One and two word answers to questions and just an unfriendly vibe is given.

Ahoy octopus, you gettin' in my belly! Love a good Greek restaurant and I'm so happy this place opened up months ago so I do not have to trek into Queens for their delicious dessert. Sometimes I wish I can fast forward the meal just to get to the dessert! Odd layout though. I had to wait for a table and ended up just loitering the area and bar because there weren't any room to wait in the front without being in the way of other customers coming in.

If you want a quick bite this is definitely a great place to check out.. food is better then most Mexican restaurant I came across and you get a good portion of food... the menu is very simply burritos, tacos, or plato... service is rather quick so if you in a hurry like I'm always in don't worry...
Best pizza in the land of pizza.  The Spumoni is great to boot.

I stopped in on my way to the train around 5:30 PM on a Monday. I ordered the traditional mac & cheese. It came out piping hot & delicious. Staff was very courteous & owner was on site and very personable. Was surprised at the number of unusual dishes like grilled mascarpone with Nutella on brioche which I will definitely return to try. The place was very clean and the decor was bright & appropriately cheesy. A mother came in with two young children who seemed very excited about the kids meal options. Some outdoor seating available in this very pleasant little neighborhood. No alcohol is served but you are welcome to BYOB. Prices very moderate. An excellent alternative to traditional fast food options.
Jeff the owner is a great host. Also a pleasure to meet his mom who serves up incredible Fish Soup and Curry! So happy to find this fantastic place during family vacation to the big apple.

Kind of an odd place - big space, with room for more tables. Seems a little disorganized. But a great breakfast value with decent coffee. Check the specials board outside because there is no evidence of them inside, in writing or from the server. Our waitress never smiled, but provided perfect service. Would definitely return. The doughnuts are pretty amazing.

Amazing fresh salad, mac and cheese, and hot chocolate.  This place is beautiful, clean, and the staff is very nice.  A "must go" if near Yale in New Haven. The only bad thing is that it is a little bit more expensive than most places, BUT totally worth every penny!
Wow!! In the area for a movie and tried this place based on the reviews. Awesome food, great prices and friendly staff (and owner). Would not hesitate to come back. PS - Try the calzone!!!

Tink's is a small cozy restaurant with cute decor. All of the food sounds fantastic, but it didn't quite live up to expectations. I wasn't completely disappointed, but I just didn't think anything was terrific. I especially did not like the burrata.

Came here for my bday with a few friends. The menu is quite small but the food was decent. One of our friends had to stand cause they were limited with seats. They surprised us with a plate of salmon over corn appetizer. We had clams w/pasta, scallop zucchini and tuna/salmon appetizers. Then ended it with some whiskey bread. Really nice place for a date. Waiters are friendly!

We regularly get take out from Dusal's...at least once a week. Pizza, salads, sautéed spinach, mozzarella sticks, and the Dusal's burger - yum. It's true, they are the best in the immediate area. I will say that when we got our pizza a few nights ago...and it was 75% burnt...I had to wonder who felt it was a good idea to send it out. Please Dusal's...your reputation is on the line with stuff like that.
Good coffee! Will make it a point to stop here every time I'm in Philadelphia in the future.

Super nice people here. Very welcoming. Great pizza at a very fair price. Crispy crust to the point of the slice. The only way to serve it. Two slices later and I'm ready for the afternoon. We'll be back next time we come to SI.
So good and filling! Prices are awesome. Line is worth the wait
Wow great food and price... you won't be disappointed.
It's nice place to eat Malacian food . I order rotti with curry . It was delicious . And the rotti was so soft . I also order Malician noodles they were awesome . Their servers were friendly .
I've been ordering from here and I just so happened to find a big eyed mosquito in my Lo Mein noodles. Throwing this menu out!

Excellent restaurant. I'm originally from Caracas but have live in DC for over 24 years. I was thrilled to find this spot. The food, ambiance and price were great. I had tequenos for appetizer, a Reina Pepia arepa for main dish and shared a cachapa. The drink of choice, Polar beer. This place reminds me of the many low-key restaurants in Venezuela. I will definitely come back when I'm in NYC.

I come here all the time to eat. From all three of taim locations this is the best once. inside is very small and never any place to site. But food is never disappointing.  Whole weet falafel sandwich is a must try
Chips, Margaritas, and food that comes out super fast and is pretty good for some tex-mex. I actually asked a friend yesterday to go and overnight me some but the wait was a bit too long

Definitely the best sushi I've ever had. I always get spicy salmon roll, out of control roll, spicy tuna crunchy roll, tuna avocado roll, rainbow roll, volcano roll (extra spicy), salmon roll... Just about anything you get is delicious. The Chinese food is also very good, especially the honey walnut shrimp. I just tried the love boat sushi for two and it's very good, a lot of sushi so you won't have to order more.
Hands down the best pizza available anywhere. From the classic cheese to the white clam to the garden pizza... Simply delicious!

Loved, loved, loved this restaurant.  Vital is the perfect restaurant for those committed to eating clean. The jerk portobello mushrooms were delectable and the moist tamarind bbq chicken popped with flavor. Chef Kwame is a genius in the kitchen.
Amazing food! Super fresh ingredients. Love the ambiance  and energy. I will def be coming back!

B rated. This place is so dodgy. They for a VERY short period had an A which they place in the middle of their front window. When they revert back to a B, they hide it behind the bamboo pot plant out front. Food is average diner quality etc.  I gave up on coming here a long time back due to shitty hostess. Constantly told 15 minute wait which always turns into 30-45 minutes.

One of the best lunches I've had in ages. Devils on horseback--so good. My mom loved the Mrs Palmer. Her trout was one of the best fish dishes she's ever had. Loved my smoked trout. Awesome bananas foster. Please read other reviews for descriptions of the ambiance. It's super cool, I'm just still too full and sleepy to continue.

Good fun old dairy queen. Everyone is very clean, tidy and friendly they have great staff there. Obviously everyone loves their ice cream its amazing it's pretty clean and gets really packed on Fridays and Saturdays.

The food is so so.  We have had better yakitori elsewhere.  The picture of the food do not look the same as the real food.  We had the grill squid, tempura rolls, yakitori samplers, seafood pancake.  The rolls is the best. The rest is forgettable.  Oh they automatically added 20% tip.  No wonder they don't really care about your customer experience. The karaoke system takes some getting used to.  The room is not sound proof though so you can definitely hear the loud music in the lounge area.

Came by myself they were nice sat at the bar got a local brew. The food was great! The clam chowder is not what you expect it is fantastic! The hostess was really nice. Parking was a pain but the people and food overwhelmingly make up for it!!
Great bahn mi (order the #8). Quick and friendly service. I eat here at least 3x per month. Love this place!

Although the food was great here, the service was absolutely terrible. When we arrived, the restaurant was not busy at all. We made awkward eye contact with the waitress a number of times hoping to get seated, but no such luck.
