But honestly, I think it is a reasonable expectation on the part of the consumer to not get food poisoning when going out to a somewhat more upscale (and expensive) eatery.

The chicken is the most popular of this place is nothing subreal,but the lomo is nothing to do with real Peruvian lomo . Personally Peruvian paella  for me has to be very home made and this one is not , so the big frozen calamar that means for me it has not high quality.

Same thin crust delicious pizza as always!!  The owner and her daughter are very kind, the place was very busy on a Friday night! Live music and karaoke for the family!! Quirky but fun!! Try it and see for yourself.  Very reasonably priced as well.
Amazing pickles, and got a side of tasty mac and cheese that was twice as big as I thought it would be. Also, friendly servers and amazing beer! What's not to like?

I went here after hearing and seeing good reviews.  Food wasn't terrible but really nothing special.  With long waiting, seated in cramped, poorly ventilated place, my husband and I got spicy ramen with broiled egg and pork. The ramen looked and tasted very greasy, very small portion, shared table, no credit card accepted. Still have hard time believing this place has such many great reviews and so many ppl willing to wait for an hour or two. Maybe I don't have taste bud for ramen.

I am definitely keeping this restaurant in my favorite list. And really thanks yelp for helping me to found this place. My sister and I are love love love the food. They have a very reasonable price and we'll organized happy hour menu. We tried their beats salad,Smoked salmon,and wine. It was delicious！
the pho here is consistent and cheap. It is my go-to spot in philly, and the service is quick and efficient.

I love de mole! I live very close and go there about twice a month, and sometimes order delivery too. The service is so friendly, especially Luis, who is the most gentlemanly, attentive waiter in new york city! I order the vegetarian burrito and the cheese quesadilla. It's absolutely delicious. On some occasions, I have ordered their fresh juices. They are FRESH...you can see them make it.  Surprisingly, they have a few vegetarian options on their menu, which is a HUGE plus! It's really affordable in terms of price. It's a cute little place but can get really loud at times. Overall, the meal, service and atmosphere was all really good.
Just moved from Brooklyn and Dough Donuts. I  really liked the Donuts made fresh and oil free and a sane size.  Calling all cars ala jack Webb to come and get your coffee and Donuts right here!

We were looking for Indian food near our hotel, and the concierge recommended Indieblue. My friend and I shared two appetizers and half-servings of three entrees. Over the last 15 years, we have probably gotten together for 3 meals a year at conferences all over the world. We agreed that this was the best meal we've ever enjoyed together. The food was absolutely stupendous, and the service was marvelous too.

I've been to this Diner three times now and always had breakfast. They make fresh hash browns (the shredded kind) and they rock. The pancakes are good too, they don't beat Tops Diner in Newark but they are worth eating for sure. My girlfriend loves the Chicken Salad and the Monarch Turkey wrap.  For basic kind of eats, we give it a thumbs up.  We've not tried any of the entrees.

Since the very first moment you walk in it feels different, Jacky the hostess, Caroline the manager,  Sergio at the bar and Angie the server made me feel like if I was the only costumer there, great staff. I had first the tlayuda de chapulines, never thought insects were so delicious. Then I tried the enchiladas de conejo, I'm mexican and I had never tried some enchiladas like those, amazing. For dessert I had the black ant nest and it made it the perfect meal, the chef Cesar is so talented, of course I will recomend all his desserts and everything about this place
Rib eye cooked Medium is worth the price! A pitcher of House Sangria with the Rib Eye is the perfect combination for me. Quality food, well worth the price !
Just had a great dinner with friends after a round of golf. Our Clams were missing a few in our app but the manager quickly handled it with another order and the rest of the food was amazing.

I love Indian food and I have yet to find a place that combines delicious food with great décor and atmosphere, then I discovered this place.  Came here for a girl's night out dinner and cocktails.  We started with cocktails, I had Singapore Sling which was fantastic! The food was absolutely amazing - Crispy Okra, Tiger Prawns and Butter Chicken Masala are a must! All of our entries came with rice and Naan, which is a bonus. This was probably the best Indian food I've ever had.   The place is very intimate and has character, if I lived in the neighborhood I would definitely be a regular!
Best pizza I've had in Brooklyn. You need to check it out!!

The BEST sushi and service ever!! These guys always have a line out the door, and people come from far and wide to enjoy the delicious menu options. I love Johns roll, a little spicy. They give complimentary mussels, and little dessert yoghurts. My 5 yr old daughter loves going there, they give her little training chopsticks and a kid size chicken teriyaki. Yum!!!

Been ordering here for every week and I still don't understand why we didn't stop sooner. Biryani is bad. It's flavorless. Enough said. It's just white rice cooked with some vegetables. The chicken here is also rough and dry which isn't too good to my taste buds. The cook here is very inconsistent, some weeks is good but majority of the time the food is bad. They also definitely do overprice in what they give you. I do not recommend going here unless this is your last choice.
Soooo lame. Food was yuck - cold and ugly. Service was absurdly inept. Sat on back patio which was nice. Even gave me the wrong check.

Food is great but not intelligent service at all.  How does someone who comes in ten min after me get their lunch first.  Then fifteen min after that i decided i had waited long enough.  The manager tried to tell me that my food takes longer cause its a steak sandwich...  sorry but i had a salad with my lunch they couldnt have occupied my hunger with that first? Only saving grace was they  let me have my beer free

Poor customer service . Booked a table two days ahead and when we arrived they said they couldn't find our reservation in the system (even though I confirmed twice with the guy on the phone) But glad that they still have us seated at the scheduled time. The food is delicious, best beef we have ever had. But the waitress rushed everything the whole time. When we were still grilling the final pieces of beef, our waitress asked us what we wanted for dessert. One minute later, mochi ice cream was served. Another one minute later, she gave us the bill when we hadn't started the dessert yet.   They should definitely improve their service to live up with their name. We expect a Japanese restaurant to have the very high standard of service.
Great meat, very nice salad bar. I enjoyed the meal quite a bit.

The best staff in the business, hands down. Not too pushy, very welcoming, very professional and more importantly for New York City....PATIENT !! In the downtown area near Stone Street this is a great place to see some real history and experience a little part of New York City circa 1800. Strongly recommend the pie and a pint
Good concept and variety but the young staff are disorganized and the place gets messy because of it.
Food, service, lunch special was great!!! Thanks again!!

Lol...this place was packed with asians. This place is all about the pig but more specifically its about pig feet and intestines! We ordered the Hakata Tonton hotpot. It was delicious. Amazingly rich broth. I expected to see little porky trotters floating around in the bowl. In reality, they looked more like knuckles. If you are cool with a chicken bone, then you'd be fine with these. I was a vegetarian for five years and managed not to faint. The best thing in the pot were the dumplings. I wish we'd had like a dozen more! All were great, especially the sashimi and salad. Highly recommend!!

Su Khum Vit is to Thailand as Broadway is to New York, and as any naïve diner like me would assume, authentic name = good food. Luckily, this is one of the cases where my judging of the book by its cover worked in my favor. It was a cute little place tucked away on 51st Street, as the name might imply. Not a bunch of tables, but they have great food and nice staff. Had some nice little appetizers; curry puffs had to be my favorite, though. Pad Thai was a bit on the sweet end, but I enjoyed the chicken in it. If you need some decently priced Thai food in Midtown East, not a bad choice here.
I love the atmosphere and my wine glass was always full! Thanks so much Scott, my friends and I will be back again soon!

This review is only for brunch - I've never been for dinner. The oysters were fresh, the Bloody Mary's were perfectly spiced, and everyone's main dishes were  exceptional. We had the caramel apple donuts for dessert and they were the highlight of the meal - I don't normally like donuts but these were unbelievably delicious! Plus, our server was attentive and friendly.  All in all a great Sunday brunch experience!
All the time I walk by this place I feel like buying a meal even if I'm full that's how good these guys are. This is the freshest halal food off the street you would get in NYC. It is addicting !!

This shit is good, damn good. It was good enough for me to finally make a yelp account. With apologies to my favourite local Indian place, but they have you beat. The samosa was the best I've ever had. He wasn't kidding when he said the vindaloo was hot - I'm sure I'll be as hot coming out  in the morning - but I want my vindaloo hot. When an Indian guy says his food is hot, you know it's damn hot. The naan was great as was my partner's chicken tika. There were a few things missing. There wasn't a crabby old Indian woman filling my glass with water every few minutes. It was a guy and he smiled while pouring water. I would have liked a paneer option as an app. It's on the second floor, so kinda hard to find, but hunt it out. You won't be disappointed.

I've only been here a couple of times. The first time I went with my wife and had dinner - I ordered the Jerk chicken and it was AMAZING. I highly highly highly suggest you order the jerk chicken, it was so tender, so moist with just the right amount of spice. We had a male server/bartender who seemed to be running the place because he was the only one working but he did a great job and was very nice to us. The second time I went by myself and had a few drinks, which were good. Again, only one server - they need to get more people there to help out, especially during busy times. I like this place and I intend to return.

I've always been skeptical about pancake places. I mean, how different could they REALLY be? How many different ways could there possibly be to make a pancake? They always end up tasting the same anyway right? Then, I met OPH. One thing that (strangely) caught my attention is the lack of those classic 'sticky menus' that pancake joints and diners are famously known for. A small detail, yes, but important. If they take time to wipe down their menus, imagine how clean their kitchen must be! The food is amazing! Light, fluffy pancakes and crepes with fresh fruit spilled over my plate. My Mother, however, stared in disbelief at the massive omelet that she was expected to devour. OPH is famous not only for their delectable pancakes, but for their monster omelets, which consist of 6 (yes 6) eggs! Maybe I should have mentioned that to my Mom, but the look on her face was very much worth it! If you're looking for amazing pancakes and enormous omelets, OPH is the place!
Go-to spot for large groups and special occasions. Excellent wine list, food is so tasty, and the atmosphere is high energy and fun. Can't wait for another fabulous time here.

Ponty Bistro is one of my favorite restaurants in New York City. The staff is super friendly and the food is always delicious. The mussels are to die for. I have yet to find better mussels anywhere. The steak is always cooked perfectly and the mac and cheese is good too. There drink specials are also a plus. Good for a date as well as dinner with friends
Great place!!  Very much like the beer halls in Germany.  Lots of good beers on tap, lots of seating.
Mood Cafe, is a great place for a heathy snack also a awesome heathy meal at a great price!

Really enjoyed this place! The ambiance is really nice and modern looking, the staff was SUPER friendly which I always look for when I go out to a place. We got $5 cabernet for happy hour that was delicious & the burger I had was great. My boyfriend had the chicken sanwich w avocado which was really fresh! I definitely would recommend this place for an after work spot!

Horrible customer service. Placed order on phone and waited over 40 minutes. I spoke with one of the workers and asked him what happen with my order. He told me to wait outside and he would get back with me but kept ignoring me. Didn't have a chance to have my lunch.

Wonderful dinner on a quiet Saturday night.  Calamari was best ever!  Veal chop delicious, as was the sushi grade tuna, grilled to perfection.  Our server, Gina was a delight. We were told that end of July, beginning of August is slow, so we enjoyed a quiet and enjoyable evening.

Torn between 3 and 4 stars. Gave it a 3 because the side dish (lemon potatoes) tasted better than my main dish chicken kebab. Portion size: good Service: good Food:The chicken kebab flavor was good, but the chicken was so so dry, overcooked. Lemon potatoes are a must-try! Price: Great. Atmosphere: Great
Every time I go to south philadelphia i make it a point to stop at both Pat's and to geno's. I love them both. there is little difference between the two.
try it just to say you had it i guess
Great food and drinks.  Great catfish y'all.

One of those little hole in the walls. Cash only. It's all about the hot dogs. I bet you can't eat just one. Yes it small inside but it's big on flavor. Amazing creation of dogs. True they may not have all of the at all times but the list is big enough to find a great one. I say try them all!!!

I was staying up in Smuggs a few weeks ago and my bf and I were searching for some good vegan food. I'm so glad I found this place! I had a sweet potato quesadilla  on the first visit that was yummy. The dip that went along with it was great and I put it on the little side "salad" and cleaned the plate. I also had a molasses ginger cookie (probably the highlight). But we liked it do much we came back a second time and I got the ELT. It was even better than the quesadilla. Loved the eggplant bacon and maple aioli. Awesome sandwich! The scone we got for dessert was kind of dry, but the meal was great. The atmosphere is also very cute and pleasant and the two guys behind the counter answered all my questions about how to make my own eggplant bacon  I would highly recommend this place!

My family (hubby and 15 year old twins, boy/girl) had to do our yearly comparison on our way back to Pittsburgh from Ocean City.  This year is was Sonny's vs Campo's.  Both places had a little bit of a wait, both had a variety of cheeses and toppings as desired, but Sonny's also had burgers and french fries/onion rings.  Well, we stuck with the usual, 2 steaks from each, both with Whiz, and one wit/one wit-out.  BY FAR Sonny's had the most flavor, right amount of Whiz, and onions were perfect, meat was well seasoned and cooked.  Campo's was soaked in Whiz, and though I like cheese, it was toooo  much.  Our only complaint....didn't notice the Parking Kiosk, and found a parking ticket on our "free" spot lol!.  No complaints on service at either place.

Quality homemade pastas and wine in an intimate atmosphere. I enjoyed the spaghetti with zucchini and shrimp (a bit heavy on the oil, but still delicious...could have been a touch lighter).  Tried my friend's dishes - tagliatelle with meat sauce and lamb ragu.  All very good!  Would try every pasta on the menu.

I came here for restaurant week. Definitely impressed and will return! Service: A++. Seated immediately (although I did go around 8:30pm). Waitress was really nice and was very attentive. Did not have to constantly wait for her to come to re-fill or such. Was warned that the portions are smaller due to price value so no surprises there. The 3 course was a good portion for one person anyways. Food: Escargot: Too too much garlic, but good otherwise. The sirloin with the potato puree was delicious and cooked medium perfectly! I wanted to try the almond brulee, but they ran out : (   I did try the cranberry bread pudding with ice cream and it was delicious. Summary: one of the best restaurants in Bloomfield. Great experience!

What a great spot!  I love when restaurants care about their customers.  I came here with a big group and they are so accommodating to all of our needs (and we have a lot of needs). The best part though was the food, super flavorful and satisfying.  Here are all the items that everyone must try, calamari, sugar cane with bacon, mixed seafood with red spicy sauce (i dont quite remember the name).

So I haven't (yet) done a comprehensive coffee tour of Philly but this place is spot on....lattes are excellent (similar to Blue Bottle in my hometown), ambience is nice, baristas are legit, and the location is just seedy enough.  Have been going here the last few mornings and Square One is just adding to my impression that Philly is about to have a there there.

Went to Box 63 through a recommendation and really glad we did.  It was for a Saturday morning brunch (around 11:30) -- the food was outstanding.  The gringo burrito was really good and the service (Jamie) was extremely helpful.  We had to catch a train after we ate and Jamie called a cab company for us, and even stood outside to watch for the taxi while we finished paying, etc.  Extra level of great service that we aren't entirely used to. Definitely check this spot out for brunch. (For what it's worth, the pancakes looked amazing too.)
Food is good and decently priced, one owner lady has a very bad attitude, but other than that, check the place out

You're better off popping into  a cheap chain restaurant. Very ordinary cuisine at extraordinary prices, slow service, a misleading menu and ridiculously poor value for money. If you're not overly particular, ihop could provide the same meal with more bang for your buck. If you'd like to get what you pay for, head over to Malcolm X Blvd and roll a dice. I promise, any place will be better. Extremely disappointed with my $23 brunch that added up to 3 regular pancakes, scrambled eggs, ONE sausage link and a flute of pastuerized orange juice (not the freshly squeezed OJ that they advertise).

The atmosphere is amazing. I can come on a date with my husband or bring the whole family. The chef makes the best calamari around. Reasonable prices and they have every sporting event on tv. I recommend this place highly!!!!  Awesome!!!
Meatball sliders were delicious, pork chops and steak and halibut were good too but not great. The dessert on the other hand was phenomenal, absolutely phenomenal. Would go back just for that.
Good veggie sandwich but it was overpriced and the interior is filthy and falling apart.
Great food big enough for one or two or three. Amazing hospitality and fantastic puddings. The staff are very afishent and very consideret. I would love to go back there again and again.

OK, so Your in Newark Airport and this place does not do anything to make you think you are anywhere else.  Newark Airport is an ARMPIT, this place is probably better than some of that standard airport food, but not much better. So if you are stuck in the Airport it is OK, just don't expect anything more than Airport quality mediocre food.

I honestly can't believe a place like this exists. My fiancé literally gagged on his food tonight. We're convinced they adhere to the concept of "sustainable" by actually serving their neighbors garbage. I don't know where all the 5 star reviews are coming from. There was nothing fresh about this place. The rice was old and the fish smelled like it had been left rotting under the boardwalk. In opposition to most of the other one star reviews, the service was probably the only good part of our experience. Service was quick and waitress was friendly. We're not masochists though, so we politely paid our bill and ordered pizza across the street.
Love this place. It is quite busy during the weekend but it is totally worth it. The food is delicious and you will not be disappointed.
Nothing short of amazing customer service, food was made in 5 minutes. The employees are great. Food taste excellent. One of the best places to go in NY hands down.

Disappointing almost all around. Wife and I went for lunch. Lemonade was incredibly sour (maybe it's supposed to come that way?) but semi refreshing. I had a cup of the corn and lump crap soup. All I could taste was the red bell pepper added to it. It was overpowering. Sent it back after mixing it well and trying 3 or 4 spoonfuls. Thankfully it was taken off the tab. The wife had fish and chips. The fish was tended but very dry. I had the surf and turf burger. That was the only reasonable portion of the menu. All around disappointing.

Another fine meal.   Hubby had the ribeye special.  He's in love.  Wants me to figure out how to do an expresso cumin rub.  It was accompanied by grilled asparagus and cheddar mashed potatoes.  Yum! I had the shrimp and crab royale.  Very good.  Pasta was al dente.  A true pet peeve of mine is mushy pasta.  Yuck.   This was perfect.  Right amount of sauce.  Shrimp and crab were fresh.  Another hit out of the ballpark!

I go to pinto often for their lunch deals. 8 bucks for an appetizer and lunch. I usually get the mushroom appetizer which is delicious and both the red and green curry are great. Place is really nicely decorated and service is great but due to the small size it sometimes gets pretty full.

This Burger place is my favorite, so many choices. I go there all the time. Staff is so friendly, place is clean. They also have Groupon in the market, which saves me money too. Best of Luck to the owner.

After reading all these reviews I made a special trip for this wonderful sounding Chinese take out....Big mistake.  Real fried rice is brown from seasonings with bits of egg and what ever you ordered i.e. chicken.  There's was greasy brown rice with lots of meat and onion.  The dumplings were alright nothing I couldn't get at any other Chinese take out.  Wasted time and money,  I don't understand all these rave reviews, just another take out place.

its small but the food is good! They're always open, service is quick. I went straight for the Mac & Cheese, didn't realize it was such a popular item but OMG, I savored every bite, I just wish it was bigger it's a small plate but it was delicioussss. Fun, hip, friendly staff. Open 24Hrs?? Will I come back again?  possibly.  especially for brunch!

Great place Great food Great vibes Everything is perfect the music the food everything goes well had a great outdoor eating space. The food is always cooked fresh. My 3rd time coming here basically my weekly spot . I recommend this spot who wants great food The seafood is slamming and the jerk chicken is great
Worst place in Vermont. Stank and filled with assholes. Never go here. You've been warned.

Absolutely worst customer service. Not sure if it was the owner but behaved like one. She writes your name down in a list and doesn't allow you to stand around inside. It was hot outside but she still insured you wait outside. A person who doesn't treat her customers well how the F can she serve good food. If you are arrogant shove that arrogance up your... Don't show it to your customers..!!

A wonderful, welcome addition to the numerous restaurants in Carroll Gardens. Simple, delicious French food without pomp or circumstance. The bar is perfect for a solo glass of wine or an evening with a friend/date, and the patio/restaurant is ideal for friends and family, particularly when you're sharing one of the delicious flambés or a cheese plate, which you most certainly should! Set back from the hectic-ness of Smith Street, it's worth the extra five-minute walk. Haven't tried brunch, but I hear it's wonderful, and owners Damien and Jeremy couldn't be nicer or more hospitable. It's definitely my new-neighborhood go-to!

When you arrive, at first you think this is not a good place but when you cross the door you find a very Japanese style restaurant with a good service and good food. I strongly recommend miso cod fish and rice with snow-crab
Great service was a nice bar to come for a late night drink I had a glass of scotch The Glenlivet 12 Year old I would recommend this place nice clean bar

I had a good experience at this new place. The menu idea is neat. 29 burgers, and one that changes every month (#30). I tried the veggie burger and it was delicious. It seemed pretty busy but the food came out quickly. Burgers don't automatically come with fries so expect to pay a little extra if you want fries. And $4 for sweet potato fries!? However the size of the burgers is sufficient for the price, though I wish it came with something else to complement it. I would recommend trying this place at least once because of the variety of burgers.

I went in late night and got a Ruben panini.  The food came out as follows: - There were literally only 3 slices of corned beef. I opened it up and counted. Three! There was barely any meat. - The panini was actually served in pita bread.  Meh? I was picturing a nice, crispy, pressed panini roll / ciabatta. Not a floppy, flour pita. - There was SO much sauerkraut it overpowered the flavor.  Picture 3 pathetic slices of corned beef and an inch of kraut. I ended up scraping most of it off. - It wasn't even pressed or grilled, just warmed, probably in a microwave. Not 1 char line on the thing. - The iced tea I ordered was served in a small paper cup?!? Have you even been to a NJ diner that uses small paper cups for your beverage? - Naturally the waitress never offered a refill when I finished it in 2 minutes. This place was very disappointing.

Fabulous!!! Tight quarters inside - unbelievable food ensures you don't care.  Guacamole Fresh, Fresh, Fresh. The ceviche was awesome, guacamole was very good. I had the spicy jalepeno margarita & it was excellent! The food portions are small and a little pricey & the place is super packed. Service is awesome!! And friendly !!! Next visit will be brunch. !!!  And soon!!!

Can't say nicer things about this place !! I friggin love it !!! The food is an A+++, the ambiance is beautiful , staff is great and there's a great jazz lounge downstairs !! Eat in the back garden if you can !!
The mango kulfi is amazing!! This is a place you must try! Outstanding service with phenomenal service!
I never stuff my face until I can't walk but I couldn't help but to!   The lasagna was the best I've ever had.

The food was much better before the fire. I love IHOP but this place should be ashamed. Got the hearty ham and cheese omelette and when it can out looked like someone threw it on the plate all falling apart. It also had a white garlic tasting sauce on it. When I asked the waitress about it she stated it was a white cheese sauce. Now I have gotten the hearty name and cheese omelette more times than I can count but never has it bad a supposed white. cheese sauce on it. I gave up at that point and just ate it anyway seeing as I was hungry and didn't want to wait for another bad attempt at a simple dish. Won't be eating at this one anymore until they get there act together.

This Venezuelan food was BETTER than I had in Venezuela. The Arepas were more like latkas! And friendly??? The staff was so nice, we felt like kissing them good-bye when we left the place. We started with the Arepitas Con Anis Y Nata which were pretty tasty. He seemed happy with his pork, rice, and beans. I loved the Hallaca I had (essentially a corn tamale). Finished it off with a really good Tres Leches cake. Service was decent, nothing to complain about. Decor is nice with pictures of Venezuelan people and Venezuela adorning the walls. I'd definitely come back here to try something new. Recommend.

This restaurant was right-next to our motel and open late, so we gave it a try despite the average reviews (we had no other options really).  It was a Friday night and they had a live band which was actually pretty good.  I ordered a steak which was below average and came with access to the self-service salad bar.  The salad bar was a tragedy, at least by west coast standards.  Quite honestly, they should just get rid of it and serve side-salads, because when you see the presentation you will want to cry a little. We sat out on the deck area, which was really dark and could've used some additional lighting.  While getting eaten alive by mosquitoes, I found it difficult to talk to my fiancé, because of the large umbrellas on the table, which were unnecessary and obstructionist at night.   This isn't reading like a a great review, right?  Rest assured the wait staff is actually quite friendly, and the beer is really good.
Great service.  Delicious coffee and a great selection of sandwiches and treats.  Also great location by the park !!!

You can easily fill yourself in 5 - 8 $ here with good chicken / lamb verieties. I was not really a fan of middle - eastern cuisine but this place has now become a regular for me. The food is good, price is reasonable and the staff is also very friendly. I have tried the felalel, hummus, chicken shawarma wrap, lamb kabob, chicken tenders, lamb skewers, kabob skewers - and it is pretty good looking at the quantity and price (not very spicy). You can eat there or order for pickup/delivery. I usually order online and pickup my order in 10 - 15 minutes. The place is good to sit and eat if you are in a group of 4-6 Here they also have a good variety of in-house pizzas and the american style fries, grinders, sandwiches and usual stuff. If you are loooking for a change from the usual - this place is highly recommended

This might be one of my favorite restaurants in the entire city. Now that I don't live here anymore, it's one of the places I miss the most. My go to order was the salade lyonnaise and the macaroni au gratin. Almost drooling thinking about it! Will definitely be stopping by the next time I'm in town.

Staff was nice. Food was OK. Came here for brunch on Sunday at 3pm.  I ordered the Eggs Benedict with the $25 prix fixe, I should've taken I picture of it but it was pretty sad looking.  The first course was a plate of "savory" items that honestly looked like it came out of a box at the grocery store.  The yogurt and fresh fruit was delicious though.  Entree was decent,  nothing extraordinary.. probably won't order this again.  My friend and I never received our "sweet" course (I'm guessing because we had brought a cake for a birthday? Regardless, the "sweet" course should've been brought out because we paid for it.) Pros: tasty bread basket for the table, there's a shuttle service for local residents (call to ask if you're within the vicinity), clean atmosphere,  good for large parties,  $15 bottomless drink specials, friendly staff Cons: food was underwhelming.. my boyfriend's turkey burger had a burnt bun that was inedible. Prix fixe brunch is a rip off,  stick to the regular menu items. Pretty disappointed after seeing such great reviews on Yelp. Also, at the end of our meal the staff (about 6 people) surrounded our table. We thought they did that because they were closed, turns out they weren't. The entire restaurant was empty so it wasn't like they needed the table either.  Very awkward and rude.

Went there for the first time several weeks ago and had an amazing experience.  Yes they do cost a little more than the usual Vietmanese, but the quality is worth it.  Their bahn mi sandwiches and veggies rock!!  This place hands down is one of the best restaurants in NYC!!

I don't care if this pizza joint has a two hour wait, opens from 6pm to 11pm, or closes on Tuesday.  It's still my favorite pizza joint in New York.  I've had a lot of pizza and by far this one is for me.  The pizza is just so nicely baked, it's amazing. Sucks I live in California now and I am sad I cannot find anything that remotely compares.
i has the ny steak which was done to perfection. service was good, atmosphere very nice. my husband ordered the chicken which was just a chicken leg.. very dissapointed,,$23;00 for a chicken leg????
crazy packed on a saturday afternoon, but the variety of beer and the burgers are as good as it gets in forest hills at these prices!  great atmosphere to be in

Not a great experience here.. my husband and I arrived right after they opened so we were the first and only customers in the restaurant. The coffee wasn't brewed, which was fine, but after ordering a cup and being told it would be a little bit yet, it was forgotten and never delivered. The food was ok, I can't even remember what we ate. The worst part about the whole experience was the service. Our server was nice enough, but a man who I can only assume was the owner, was in and out, arguing with the waitress about workplace drama and scolding some young boys who were in and out of the kitchen. It just wasn't very professional; management is so quick to respond to negative reviews online but being a little more attentive in person would have a greater impact on customer satisfaction!

I've had dinner at Don Pepe (3) times in the last year.  Each time was on a Saturday night.  The first visit as in August of 2013 and the parking lots were empty.  Everything went well.  We were seated quickly, the food was very good and the sangria was delicious.  The one thing I didn't like is the waiter grabbed a second picture of sangria in record time when my wife said she wanted more.  I objected but she said let's get another one and the waiter blew out of there and was back in 90 seconds with a small pitcher.  We could not finish it (at least without being officially declared a drunk driver) and we couldn't take it with us so that was a waste.  The 2nd visit both parking lots were packed.  Not looking good but we walk in and there's plenty of people around.  We're greeted by the Hostess and she says a table for 2 will be 10 minutes.  I'm puzzled but optimistic.  I'm thinking how can it be only a 10 minute wait?  Well it turned out to be almost an hour.  Half way through I gave thought to leaving but it was already pretty late for dinner and to start over at another restaurant is not a chance I wanted to take.  It was apparent that we were LIED to.  Again the food and the sangria were very good.  The third time we take my kids and parents for a party of 6.  We ordered appetizers and then the entrees.  We ordered (4) items figuring that would be enough.  There is no way one person can eat the whole portion of the items we ordered not to mention my two daughters.  When the bill came we were charged for sharing two plates which was $13.00 when tax & tip are included.  This irked me because when the appetizers are included there were (6) items in total ordered.  I did not want to make of deal of this because we enjoyed having dinner with my parents but couple this with the sangria which was subpar and I won't be coming back any longer.  There are plenty of very good Spanish restaurants very close by in Newark.
Service sucks, its overpriced, and the food is just barely above garbage

I LOVE this place! Was my 2nd time there last night, The owner is so sweet and kept making sure we understood the menu- she was delightful. Our waiter was informative and attentive Special of the night.. MY FAV! Grilled Octopus!! Brussels sprouts are amazing. swiss chard .. amazing.. LOVE LOVE LOVE. Wait.. I just hate the stool chairs with no backs.. wish there was more seating.. But otherwise it's awesome. Wish ya'll were UES.

The staff here is so friendly - the hostess, bartenders, servers - all of them!   You can see their camaraderie and knack for hospitality shine through in the way they treat both the patrons and each other.   The food, every single item, was incredible. I have to recommend the mussels and clams linguini because I devoured them both. The oysters and uni totally worth the wait. Will be back soon.
The salteñas are to die for!! I met one of the founders today at the Williamsburg Smorgasburg and he was super nice. Great food+great people=BLP

Here for my girls birthday had to drive an hour and the service has been amazing. They have been so accomodating and very patient. The food is so delicous. I would highly recommend this place.  Great food and great music.

Great time,  food and drinks at Blend on the Water.  The lobster dishes are definitely fresh shucked lobstermeat - amazing.  The service was especially good at the bar.  Priscilla was exceptionally great bartender, very attentive... and attractive ;) .  Breathtaking view of the Manhattan skyline - can't wait to go back!

This place was highly recommended so me and friends went to check it out. The atmosphere was alive, music was GREAT and the food is FANTASTIC! The service was fast and Up to my expectation. The bartender Priscilla was always checking up on us to make sure we were taken care of. The coconut mojito she made us was AMAZING! My friends & I will definitely be going back and I will recommend Blend to all my friends and co- workers.
Lunch buffet is good. Food is tasty. Staff is very friendly. Keep up the job

PISSED!!!!! DISRESPECTED !!!!!! I went there yesterday 8-8-2014 AT ABOUT 9:30. I ordered take out. My total came up to $ 21.46. I handed (Libby the cashier) $40 in her hand and she dropped  all my bills and coins on the counter separately for me to pick up. So I laughed in disgust and grabbed my change and my food headed for the door. But upon leaving I notice that the WHITE guy behind me was not treated the same he paid his money and had his changed placed in his hand. So when I got in the car, I called back to the restaurant and ask to speak with a manager. The young lady who answered asked what was wrong, I explained what just happen.  The voice on the other in was the offender. She said" oh that was me I should not have done that" I said may I ask why ? Libby said "oh I don't know" Libby had no reason for treating me rude and that pissed me off even more. I WILL NEVER GO BACK AND SPOKE WITH FRIENDS IN MY AREA AND FRIENDS WHO DO REVIEWS FOR RESTAURANTS to never go in there especially if you are of color. Libby didn't want to touch me. Maybe this was the reason I didn't not enjoy the food. The experience  made me sick to my stomach.

Dear Taim family, I have been trying to come here for a while now and i finally did with my girlfriend. Sadly, i was disappointed to have eaten there. We both commented on the same things which are: falafels too salty, and seasoning not that great. Why put tahini on the side? Aren't you supposed to add it to the falafel? You don't have the freedom to add whatever toppings you want. I wanted a falafel with eggplant inside... WHY COULDNT I? Also, the babaganoush... Come on, i didnt even taste it. And also, why would you mess a falafel by adding jalapenos? I couldn't eat jalapeños and the staff did not let me know. Thats inconsiderate. The staff: put on a smile on your face when a customer is being nice to you. Whats wrong with you people? Being bitchy isnt gonna get you anywhere. Conclusion: best falafels? Dont know about that. :(

I was so surprised because my impression to NY sushi place was just expensive and average quality compared to the real sushi place in Japan but this place is really authentic and awesome. The size of sushi might be small you feel but this is intentionally done to focus on the taste of best balance of flesh fish and rices. Very classy. If you want to be full, just ask "Omakase" so that they continue to make sushi for you by checking your preference. Every time you eat one sushi, you can reset your taste by drinking Japanese sake and restart to try next sushi. In that way you can enjoy this place's super tasty sushi. This is one of world best place in eating sushi I have had.
Overrated. Totally burnt, soggy mess of a pizza. And the wait is in no way justifiable. I do not understand the local obsession with Modern Pizza. Pepe's all the way!

I finally ended up eating here after many months of hearing great things from other people. I had tried the Mezze plater with some fresh pitas for appetizer and the hummus and baba (grilled eggplant) was outstanding. Then the friendly waiter proceeded to recommend us the specials. There are about four specials...2 fish dishes one bronzino, the other salmon with pistachio and olive crust. The next specials were a chicken Tajin and a Lamb Tajin. I requetsted for the Salmon, and my friend had ordered the Lamb Tajin. The salmon was very tender, and fresh, but I kept looking over at my freidns plate because the Lamb Tajin smelled so good, and she licked the plate clean. The service was outstanding, and the restaurant was packed. The owner was very nice to us when we left and asked us how we liked the food, and overall a great ambiance and delicious food !!

I have never written a review before but this place made me want to share. I work in old city so I end up eating here every now and again. Judy is the bartender/waitress that's usually on duty during lunch when I'm there and she is fabulous! Seriously, such a sweetheart. The food is always really good, and I always get a paloma while I'm there. I've tried ordering them from different bars since I first discovered them at Lucha, but no one seems to be able to make them like Judy. The atmosphere is relaxed, good food, good drink, good people. This is a good place to go unwind and hang. Definitely go and get a paloma.

I went for dinner with a couple friends and the margaritas and guacamole were AMAZING! I got an El Santo and then a Pineapple Jalepeno margarita. They have house infused jalepeno tequila, definitely worth the try! For dinner I got the chicken enchiladas which were also very good. Service was excellent, it was busy and my waitress still was quite attentive with our table. Overall a great experience and I will definitely go back.

Blerg.  I went here with a friend on a saturday during the world cup.  It was a 1PM game and we arrived at nearly halftime.  They only served brunch.  Until 4.  On a Saturday.  It seemed strange to have breakfast items so late on a Saturday.  While we were trying to figure out what breakfast item sounded appealing to go with the beers we had already ordered.......we waited....and waited.  Our waitress never came back.  Someone else brought our beers.  A busboy was kind enough to refill our chips to finish our guacamole.  We never saw her again.  For 2 hours.  I had to go flag down the bartender to pay our bill.  Very tempted to just walk out, but I cannot do that in good conscience.  Not a great experience.  Wont be back

Here are good guys waiting as I love to the place much. Highly recommend the place they are so professional and friendly too to the custimers, Foods are yummy and decent price. Must come back at the place. Greatly thanks for the service. Coming

One word: Lacking. I ate at the restaurant for restaurant week, and the carnitas in the sauce was awesome. I was craving it again so I had the carnitas tacos when I saw the food truck. I gave it 3 stars, because it was a solid average. Coming from Texas, I've eaten from many food trucks and Mexican restaurants. Meat was cooked alright slightly too dry, but flavor and salsa verde just didn't do it for me. I was disappointed : ( I do recommend trying the restaurant if you get the chance though.

Best chicken and waffles in the burg! Hands down! Winner! Winner! It's literally our weekly brunch addiction. The staff are really nice- so friendly and welcoming! Good music, great vibe! Love it- so happy we live so close!

High quality and absolutely delicious Chinese food. They have a wide variety of Chinese food and extensive menu.  Spicy boiled fish,  xiao long Bao and chicken soup are very good! Also I would recommend the authentic Chinese vegetable dishes
The best and juiciest Xiao Long Bao I ever had in New York.  Deco is nice and clean, staffs are friendly.  The BEST！！

Excellent Indian fare in a beautiful setting. Delicious dishes, really fresh ingredients, large portions, and varied menu that goes beyond the usual Americanized Indian dishes. Dining room presided over by either the owner or manager (not sure which), but she really knows what she's doing and remembers her customers. Must try dishes include the chicken chop, korma, and anything out of the tandoor. We've eaten three meals here over the last year and each was memorable.

Fabulous salads, fresh and crunchy. My daughter said "I usually don't like crunchy but this is the right kind of crunchy." We walked in just as they were closing and they stayed open just to serve us, and all the veggies were still super fresh. The service was a bit slow but I think that's because they had already packed everything away and had to rake it out especially fie us. The proprietors are super friendly and helpful and even though we didn't show them the Yelp offer, they gave us ice tea on the house.
best cafe in old city district. great food and great price. get the spicy chicken salad sandwich!
The environment and the music rocks! But the bartender is a little more interested to talk with girls than other people. The budget is very good. I would back again
Food terrible. "Modernization" of classic staples with terrible execution. Good service is the only thing keeping this from being a one-star review, but who needs bad food served to them well?

My boyfriend brought me here when we were visiting Penn.  This is the first Greek restaurant that I've ever been to.  The store was packed with people and my food didn't come on time.  We ordered couple of gyros and taste was good.   However, I didn't like how it was so packed and loud. May be I can compare to other Greek restaurants but purely based on my first visit and impression, it was OK.

The frozen ravioli I get from Costco is better than the dish I got here. The ravioli pasta itself was undercooked and there was so little filling inside that I couldn't really tell it was braised beef on the inside. The lamb ragu and bucatini carbonara were not bad, and the eggplant parmigiana was mediocre at best. The plates look big on first glance, but it actually isn't that much food

I used to go to this place years ago when the food was actually good. Went the other day for lunch and food quality went down. Got the drunken noodles and pad see ew the noodles were so dry and hardly had any flavor. But what really put me over the edge was they were going to charge me 50 cents to have no ice in my thai iced tea. They fill those slim glasses with so much ice there's barely any tea in there! Never going back again.

The food is okay. I don't like kids at bars, especially after 9:00 on Saturday. They were running around the back yard like it was a gym. This has happened many times here. If this annoys you, don't go here

This is the best pizza I have ever tasted. The ingredients are so fresh that you will understand why I gave a five star. Tried peporoni and mushroom pizza and it was delicious. Served wid some good selection of tap beer. My favorite Brooklyn Lager ;) If you r in New York City,  you got to try this place
Best Guacamole around. I was able to customize my own. The staff was very attending. Cold drinks on a warm night. If your looking for authentic mexican food. This is the place to stop in.

Ate here recently on a Friday night around 7pm, there was no wait for seating, but they only had 1 space for a party of 3-4 that was occupied, so my party of 4 had to sit in a row at the bar - difficult to really interact with everybody in the group, they could probably do better with maximizing the space but on the bright side it gave me the chance to really focus on my food. I got the thai iced tea (not very sweet fyi, but I enjoyed it) and the beef pho. I had originally felt very conflicted coming here because there were such mixed reviews from other yelpers, but I'm glad I visited because it was probably one of the best bowls of pho I've ever had. The broth was amazing, I practically drank it all, there was a LOT of high quality beef in my bowl, in fact, I ran out of noodles with at least 5 large pieces of meat left. And I didn't feel like it was too rich or too small as others have claimed. I also got to introduce a vegetarian friend to pho here and she really liked the mushroom/tofu. Overall, this little restaurant felt really clean and organized with friendly staff and a well priced menu. I would definitely come back here, but should limit my party size to just 2.
Insanely priced. 4.25 for two mediocre pancakes that don't even come with enough syrup? Cmon. Bagel was good, but what bagel isn't? Nice can of 7up, tho.

Read the reviews before dining here!! This place is surviving only on it's merits as a bar (not so hard, just make sure you have the booze in stock)- do not eat food here!   Atmosphere: Bar style setup (dark, stools, small tables, etc.) with what seems like a decent patio... until you sit out there for dinner. It's filled with flies and gnats because of the over arching grape tree- charming until it's not. Service: Slow, uninformed, distracted, and without leadership. He was not familiar with the dishes, spoke the oyster descriptions like a script and we never saw him after the food was delivered. It's important to know that in this scenario, we were the ONLY table in the restaurant. The Food: Disgusting. Old, smelly seafood, cloudy oysters, greasy cheese bowls, complicated and overdressed salads topped with stale bread. Issue handling: Abysmal- I complained to the server that the oysters ($4 each!!) were clearly spoiling and that we left them on the table. (we had to finally come inside to get our check because the server was having drinks with friends inside.) He forced us to pay for them and told us to email the manager! Management: A complaint to the manager did little- he did offer to give us more of the disgusting food as appeasement, but I simply cannot stomach the idea of ordering greasy, spoiling food from this place. The issue remains unresolved as I asked for a partial refund of an over $100 check for a terrible meal- and received no response. This is a sad representation of East Coast seafood, a worse insight in to what this neighborhood has to offer- and more importantly, a restaurant I would never recommend to anyone.

It's so fresh!!! I love this place! When you walk in the set-up is so nice! It's fun and easy to read! You can choose how you want your pizza made to satisfy all of your cravings! It seems to be really healthy. It's taste so good especially the red sauce they use tastes amazing! I love the tomato zing it has to it! I ordered the Margarita Pizza! The best choice (-;
This is a very nice chill spot. I just wish the seats can be less sticky and gross. Other than that the food and drinks are the BOMB!!!

The best little bagel shop I've found in Philly! Their front tables, inside tables, and back patio tables, make it possible to cater to whatever type of eating setting you are looking for. The staff is always very welcoming and friendly. Not to mention how delicious their food is! I also definitely recommend their mint iced tea as a lovely morning or afternoon pick me up! I will be going back for quite some time.
The old King Chef was much better!..  I didn't like this place.. Great Location though!  I don't think I would go back.
I always go for the H16 with Brown rice. I love the ginger book and bok choi. Always great can't complain. When I want Chinese this is the place to get it

So delicious. Everything here was uh-mazing. I'd say order everything but that's unrealistic.   Love the ambiance, pretty cozy with soft lighting and the requisite candles. The seating may be a bit claustrophobic for some (my girlfriend included) but you're not in danger of constantly bumping elbows. Now for the important stuff: the food. The ceviche was mediocre; I feel like I've had better elsewhere. Everything else was great. Based on the fantastic food and service we enjoyed here, we will definitely be back.

Great food, superb baklava and Borak. My favorite hookah is the monster flavored one; highly recommended. The only good hookah bar in the area definitely. Also there are belly dancers for entertainment and it's BYOB.
this was my first time eating thai food. the staff was very nice and attentive. their pad thai was excellent. definitely going back very soon!

Went to The Smith with friends for the first time and loved it! For someone who is gluten free, there are plenty of options. The staff is also knowledgable about what is and is not gluten free, which seems like it should always be the case but sadly it's not. They also carry a gluten free beer which made my day!

When I lived in North Jersey I was a big fan of this place.  I enjoyed all of their specials and would order from here at least twice a week.  Great Risotto and pasta dishes.  Proportions were very generous and the food was always fresh.  I miss not having a place like this nearby.
Shrimp Fra diablo was excellent , also the pork flank with barque glaze ( the special of the evening was very good!

Someone posted that the steak tartare is no good but I just ate it and... AMAZING. I have eaten a lot of raw beef in my life. Cows flee upon sight of me. This stuff was super good. Also, Zucchini pasta. Good sauce, but more importantly the preparation was fab. Don't expect anything that really tastes all that much like pasta but instead get ready for one of the most awesome zucchini-based dishes since anyone ever thought zucchini could form the basis for a dish. Cocktails were also excellent. Top marks for the Louis XIV. Great atmosphere, and while sitting at the bar I keep seeing people emerge from the underground staircase behind the bar which is frankly hilarious. Will definitely be back!
... What a dump LOOOL. How did they get so many reviews. Definitely turned off right now.

This restaurant was amazing! The service was great and the waitress was really nice and was very aware right when we put down our card she came, and totally not pushy off course! The food was AMAZING and very quick, and the price was very low, wich was also great! Totally loved this place, coming back tomorrow again!

Came here on weeknight for restaurant week. The service was okay. Felt a little rushed though. The food? Not so great. I had the rack of ribs & shrimp combo with mashed potato. The ribs were so dry. The shrimp was okay considering it's just fried breaded shrimp. The garlic mashed potato was good, but it was a little cold. My bf ordered from the prefixe menu. The crab cake appetizer was good, the tomato & fresh mozzarella salad was alright & the entree? Not so great. He had the prime rib & lobster tail. The prime rib was dry & bland but the lobster tail was good. They told us 20 minute wait... We arrived at 8:30pm... We didn't get our entree until almost 10pm. We had to wait for the kitchen to catch up because they were backed up.... Would I come back again? Probably not in the near future.

Visited this venue on a random Saturday afternoon while walking through the neighborhood. The decor of the place along with the name of the establishment just lured me in! The place is cool, young and inviting! We sat at the bar because we were looking to have a few drinks and maybe a small bite to eat. Unfortunately, the staff this particular afternoon was less than friendly, engaging and/or interested in our business. I cannot say they were rude because it would be unfair but their inattentiveness was really a sour note to what could've been a pleasant experience! My girlfriends and I are friendly, easy going people that just like to go out and have a good time experiencing new things. We are engaging, like to ask questions and maybe exchange a few laughs but this staff would not even make eye contact long enough to get a word in! Needless to say after the second drink we decided to find somewhere else to eat and just leave. I would like to mention that on our way out we decided to have a Cuban cortadito and the young man that we met at the coffee counter was a breath of fresh air! He made delicious cortaditos for us and told us it was his first day on the job (hope the bad attitude does not taint him) and if I happen to be in the neighborhood again I would stop in just for his coffee and friendly smile! Word to the service industry personality and friendliness should be a job requirement!

Stopped by for brunch, wasn't too impressed with their menu and $10 bloody mary's. Service was rather poor, asked the waitress to split up the bill for our party of four and she refused and said we should have told her thats what we wanted to do right when we sat down. Rather unpleasant experience, meaning that I will never be back.

Bank & bourbon says it all. Brink your bank and they'll bring the bourbon. They steak was very very good mostly cooked to perfection. Nice atmosphere for a date or one on one meeting!!! Thanks philly!!!

Got a chance to try the break room fries today. The portion and taste was not worth it's price ($6.43 w/ tax)..especially in Chinatown...there wasn't anything special about the break room fries...the fries tasted like Cajun fries from Popeyes (but less salty)..the tots were ehh..ordinary tots...nothing special about the bacon (5 to 9 bits)...the egg was like an ordinary breakfast egg..I  wish there had been more cheese because only the top had a slight cover of two cheese and the rest of the fries were naked..I can also taste the multiple uses of the oil for frying the fries and tots...no bueno...btw jalapeños didn't play it's role in giving off a spicy kick. Ohhhh but there is happy hour mon-fri 3pm-5pm  for $2 tacos and other items on their list..maybe that would be worth the trip.

I've never had a bad experience here.  I get the eggs benedict almost every time, some of the best bennys I've ever had.  It can be very busy on weekend mornings, so prepare yourself for a line.  It's definitely worth it though!
$10 for an omelet and it comes with a plastic knife and fork. The worst service I have experienced in a long time.

My friend and I had brunch today and were not impressed with the food or how expensive the meal was. An egg white omelette with spinach and feta came out as a 4 inch round flat egg with raw spinach leaves and cubes of feta on top.  My friend asked for dry rye toast and was charged  $4.00 for two small pieces of toast. We could've bought two loaves of  bread for that price. All in all a huge disappointment.  Only positive was the friendly server.

There was a roach in my daughter's Margarite Pizzette. The waitress took at look at it, took the tray to someone else and just took it to the kitchen and got another one. No sorry or nothing. All in all, we ordered 5 dishes, which included 2 Pizzettes. We all had to stop and wait eating so my youngest wouldn't eat all by herself.  The Bistecca and the Arrabiatta were however really good. Some of the best skirt steak I've had.
I had the Billy Burger with the lettuce bum. At first I was thrown off by the lettuce bun, but it was delicious. By far I think it was the best burger I've ever had.

This place is so gross. If you know anything about being Italian or food for that matter do not order from here. Everything is obviously frozen! Calamari is inedible, subs are well.... sad, and the rest is just bad. Never ordering from here again.
Overpriced, unsatisfying flavor combos. I expected much better and it felt like an awkward date where you know it's not going to work out. Not compatible.
YOu gotta have it!!! delishhhhhhh.

To be completely frank, I wasn't expecting to like this place very much; however, I was pleasantly surprised with the cheese pizza and hot wings. The food was decent, not overly greasy. With prices this low, I will certainly be ordering from here again. One thing I didn't like is that the delivery took a while--an hour or so for a small order less than 5 miles away. The delivery men were very kind and polite though.

We ate outside on the patio.  It took 20 minutes for us to get a menu, and another 20 minutes to place an order.. We ordered a pitcher of sangria that was served with a dirty paper towel in it. The bartender nor waiter  saw it. It was disgusting. When we told the staff all they said was that they did not know how it happened. No one said sorry. Served us a plastic plates and fork to share the antipasta. Had to ask for silverware and napkins that other tables had. Never served bread.   Seafood Venice was drowned in tomatoe sauce. Grilled shrimp was supposed to be served over rice, but came with potatoes . By the time they brought the rice out in a bowl we had finished eating and even had our dishes cleared . There was no fork to eat the rice. The steak was ok, thus the 1 star. The bathroom and hall by the kitchen smelled of raw sewage. We asked 3 times to speak to a manager. A woman claiming to be the owner came to our table and never said sorry for the sangria or rice. She claimed she just heard about it moments before. She kept making excuses. She was too busy in the kitchen to speak to us and it was the staffs fault. When we told her it was not our problem but the managers problem she told me I was rude. She did finally offer to buy us another pitcher of sangria. We declined. NEVER again. NO professionalism. NOT a smoke free reseraunt . Could not enjoy it,  if I tried.
Good food, good service nice atmosphere. Reminded us of a little restaurant we ate in Milan. Would like to go back for dinner. My only hang up is the waiter over charged us for one of our dishes.

Not sure what all the negativity is about this place. I have been alive over 50 years and have been to many, many sub shops and this one is the best. Lets understand here people that this is a sub shop and not fine dining. The sandwiches are loaded with whatever  meat, turkey or cheese you ask for. Many of the other franchises don't come close to the amount of meat they put on their sandwiches. The girls and owners are very courteous and friendly here. I go here about once a week and my son and wife have been there on many occasions. My guess is that the negative reviews are just the few crazy people that we all encounter in life. As for this place "I'll Be Back!"

Easily THE best burger I have ever had. Next time I am back in New York (I'm from Texas) I will totally go back. Usually I am not a big burger person but this burger was nothing short of amazing. The fries were also very good as well. If you are in Brooklyn, go. You will not regret it.

This place is pretty disgusting. The salad bar hardly has anything in it and what it does have is not fresh at all. When it came with my meal I could only find cucumbers that looked edible and ended up eating half of one and leaving the rest. I ordered something I thought would be fool proof and couldn't eat it at all: linguine with garlic and oil.  The pasta was so over cooked it was like mush and the garlic were huge slices all over the top that not only were burnt but tasted like maybe they'd been sitting in the refrigerator for a week or two. My meal also came with chicken noodle soup which appeared to be one of those bags you add water too, with maybe 1 piece of chicken. When the waitress saw I didn't like my meal she did have the pasta taken off our bill but charged me $10 for the salad bar and soup...most expensive half a cucumber and half eaten cup of soup I ever had! This was our last attempt and will continue going to the nutley diner which is always fantastic with much better atmosphere and fantastic wait staff. It's worth the extra few minutes it takes to get there.

The perfect way to. Spend a Saturday night .. Clean and cozy perfect atmosphere for an intimate night with your significant other..delicious wings. & Henry makes a mean drink.. So happy to have found a local spot we can enjoy

This is my favorite go-to spot in the neighborhood for happy hour or late night cocktails as well as a casual dinner.  The happy hour is fabulous with great wines as well as fantastic cocktails (2 for 1!).   And I know I can never go wrong with the sumac chicken or the double-cut pork chop (if that's available on special). I do have to give a special shout-out to my favorite bartender, Henry.  He made sure to reach out to me one of the first times I sat in the restaurant.  The second time I arrived, he remembered not only my ams, but the type of drink I liked.  He has a way of making people feel special, therefor making the bar/restaurant feel special.

It's about what I expected. Greasy meat and onions on a great piece of bread but it's part of the Philly experience. We got there right before a huge lunch rush which lasted the rest of the time we were there. I'd venture to say that a Whiz wit would be awesome at 2am on the way home from the bar though. I'll try Pat's next to compare, then I've gotta get a roast pork that people rave about. I love sandwiches!
The tostones were amazing... the rotisserie chicken was flavorful, pork was cooked perfectly, service was quick, and the cafe con leche was to die for.

Had lunch there today, food was not good at all and spent $80.00 should have just thrown out car window. Calamari  was over cooked , ox tail was not  right meat tasted  off.. Good  Luck  but I told  u all

Amazing place! Very busy for breakfast so I recommend calling ahead! I had blueberry pancakes and my family had a sandwich and omelet. All of the food was absolutely delicious! Fun atmosphere and fun people! We went at the very beginning of January and it was nice to get out of the stereotypical New York Times Square hustle and bustle restaurants!

One of the few coffee places in Upper East serving genuine Italian espresso and the derivatives. Excellent quality coffee in chilled atmosphere with friendly Italian baristas. Additional pluses are the shady courtyard and the spacious, clean bathroom with the NYT on the rack.

I came here for a romantic dinner with my boyfriend for a special occasion. It is somewhat new york-sized restaurant with decent food. More than anything the decor was top notch. Service was attentive and the staff was extra friendly For the two of us with non-alcoholic beverages, it came to about 105$ including tip.

Beautiful restaurant, fantastic food, great service, romantic ambience. The reason for only 3 stars?  I went there with my husband for a nice quiet dinner.  There was over an hour wait for an outside table on the water so we opted for inside since it was late. The noise level was almost unbearable. Not only couldn't we hear each other but the waiter had to ask us at least three times to repeat our order. We didn't stay for dessert. Couldn't wait to get out of there. Too bad

Got the Chicken Saag. It was a bit bland for my taste. Husband got vindaloo and said it was tasty. Friendly staff. Food was a bit overpriced for the portion size. Rice and cheese naan was a bit dry and tasteless. Overall not bad, but I wouldn't come again.
great food, but horrible attitude.  If you enjoy abuse from a seriously bitchy host and waiters, then this place is for you.
I am giving it 4 stars because the food was good... But you would think when you order $24 poached eggs you would think they would be runny not hard boiled inside

love love love this place! I have tried the tom yum soup and the noodle soup in the picture (some sort of beef noodle soup) and both are delicious! My favorite dish here is the Kwaytiew Neur Sub, a beef noodle bowl.This particular dish is so tasty and is especially nice on a cold winter day.  I love that they bring you the spice tray (their version of it) without you having to ask.  I love spicing my dish up with the crushed red pepper and adding some flavor with the picked jalapenos. I LOVED EVERY THING ABOUT THIS PLACE !!!    a must !!!   if your in HK !!  wo- hoo !

The food is fresh. A gourmet variety of pizza available and local beer! A great casual hangout and doesn't feel touristy. Also, really great service. Everything was very timely and they always made sure that we were well taken care of. Nothing else I can ask for.
Great drinks and service! Want some great martinis? This is the place to be! After you drink at this place you would never want to go anywhere else. You MUST make reservations in order to come in.

My daughter had her wedding after-party at The Bahche on Aug. 9, and we can't say enough good things about Corina (the events manager), the staff (who are all extremely helpful and friendly), the food (so delicious it disappeared very quickly), and the venue (perfect for dancing inside and relaxing outside). Corina was solicitous and helpful throughout the process and couldn't do enough to make sure everything was perfect. So, we highly recommend The Bahche if you're thinking of a venue for a party in Brooklyn where you want to dance and listen to amplified music or, as in our case, just great loud music from bands with a lot of horns and drums! Bravo, Bahche! Well done!

Our Order: Stuffed Mushrooms Mixed Pickles Oysters Apple Crisp Molten Lava Cake Coffee Stuffed Mushrooms: They were ICE cold. When I say this, i mean it tasted like it was microwaved then left to sit for 25 minutes. My group absolutely hated them. Mixed Pickles:This was interesting to me, because last time I was here they served us 3 different kinds of normal pickles. 1 Small kerby, 1 bigger normal style pickle, and 1 other half-sour pickle. This time we got something completely different. 2 pieces of pickled cauliflower, 4 pickled string beans, 1 normal pickle. Really nothing special this time around, mainly because i was expecting different. (and there is no description?) Oysters: These were served with a small side of pickled onion. Honestly we didn't even get a spoon to put it ON the oysters! I asked for cocktail sauce....they don't have it. Apple Crisp: For those who have never eaten apple crisp, it is sliced, baked apples with a cinnamon crisp topping served warm, with a healthy scoop of vanilla ice cream. Sounds delicious, right?.....This was served cold, with a teaspoon of ice cream on top. Edges of the topping were burnt. Was jut poorly done. Very upset with the way it turned out. Molten Lava Cake: My sister ordered this, and was complaining that the "lava" was cold and the edges were also burnt. Coffee: we ordered 2 coffees. One of the members in my group asked for a small refill. Turned out they were totally out of drip coffee. (and didn't seem to be willing to put another pot on. They close at 1AM. Why not?) I will never return here.

To be honest, I have no idea how this place is so highly rated. I waited over a half hour now for my food and the coffee is absolutely terrible. There are people who came in after me -like 20 minutes after me- who were served before me. I ordered the creamed chipped beef. I was surprised to see it was not served on the toast. That would be ok, except the toast was heavily buttered. The result is, of course, that the dish becomes to salty from the butter. And that is ignoring the fact that I am now eating cream with butter. The home fries were pretty good, but I wish there were more. I was never offered water.  The whole experience was just disappointing. There is really no reason for me to come back, not with better options right on Main Street.

I'm sorry to say my meal wasn't very good. I ordered the swordfish on a bed of angel hair pasta with pesto sauce but, the entire meal was drowning in pesto sauce. It looked like they just dumped 3 cups of pesto on top of my meal. The fish was also a little under-cooked. I didn't go there for sushi. The appetizers we ordered were very good! I like the atmosphere and the friendly staff and sitting on the rooftop! Sadly our waiter  is not included in the friendly staff category he didn't really seem to like his job very much. When he asked how our meals were I told him ( in a very nice way) there is too much pesto sauce on my meal, he kind of shrugged & just looked at me for a bit  then asked if I wanted to return it. Of course we all know you don't ever send any meal back to the kitchen! Well, at least I don't.  I would go there again but I would only order the appetizers which are a meal in it's self.
The chili paste was not very spicy, too sweet and overpowering in the pad led moo krob.

My wife and i went to Dominic's for the first time yesterday after receiving a promotional menu from then in the mail a few weeks ago. We walked in and were greeted and seated immediately by the hostess.  This is the only reason for the one start. It was all downhill after that.  Unfriendly waiters, mediocre food, cobwebs and dead flies on the wall and 20 minute wait between finishing desert and getting the check so we could leave.  We will not be returning and will, stick to our regular Italian restaurant Venezia in Woodbridge.

I applaud the pizza and beer concept. 5 stars for the beer, 1 for the pizza. I grew up on NY style pizza and this does not come close. If you're from the south or out west you might like it, but I would personally stick to the wine.

Monday, August 4th, My friend and I decided to enjoy the summer weather and so chose to eat at the Rooftop Birreria at Eataly located at Fifth Ave & 23rd, NYC.  We got a great table location as the scenery was fantastic.  The Flatiron Building was "smack" in front of us.  We had a nice breeze and the ambiance was lovely and very summery.  When the waiter (Daniel) came to the table, he recommended we order a particular drink on the menu.  We really didn't have a chance to look at the menu but took his suggestion as it sounded refreshing.   When he came with the beverages to take our order, we told him what we wanted...ONE appetizer to share and TWO chicken dishes from the small menu, one for each of us.  We were presented with two menus and wanted to order off the smaller menu.  But it now appeared to us that he was pushing the chicken entrée off the larger menu, which we thought was odd.  We made it clear we wanted the chicken from the smaller menu.  He tried to explain that the chicken on the small menu chicken was the same thing as the chicken entrée on the larger menu. We thought this was strange having two menus with one being obsolete.  We gave in and ordered what he told us to order form the larger menu.  It was becoming ridiculous, and after all, we were hungry and just wanted to order lunch. We were perplexed as to why Daniel was insisting we order off the larger menu because the chicken entrée had a different description than the chicken we wanted on the smaller menu.  We agreed that it should not be this hard to order a simple lunch.  It seemed as though the waiter was just not listening to us as it seemed a struggle to get our point across...one asparagus appetizer to share and one chicken entrée for each of us.  The fact we told him we wanted to share the appetizer stuck in his mind because he apparently presumed that we also wanted to share the chicken because when a server presented our lunch, it was not what we had ordered...only ONE chicken dish was served, not TWO which is what we ordered. We told the server when he came with the food, we ordered TWO chicken dishes, one for each of us...NOT ONE and that we ordered ONE appetizer to share.  So, he took the food away, and a few minutes later, a woman named Rebecca came to our table asking what the problem was with our order.  We explained the mixup to her...the two different menus and the fact that we only received one chicken entrée when we ordered two.  Her attitude was not nice as we sensed she didn't want to really know what the issue was...she was condescending and seemed as though she just did not want to understand.  Also she did not clarify the reason for using two menus. Ultimately we did get our lunch (the chicken entrée that we really did not order, but at this point..."what the heck.").  Although the food was very good, the workers Daniel and Rebecca made the simple task of ordering from a menu that was presented to us a very difficult task.   Bottom line:  The service was horrendous, but the food and the ambiance was great.  In spite of this confusion, we did enjoy the rooftop scenery, the food, and the order debacle turned into a scene from a comedy show, which provided us with  a bit of laughter.

I am new to the area and this restaurant.  I took out a combination dish of Shrimp with vegetables fried rice egg roll and mixed egg drop wonton soup. Also had a small BBQ spare ribs on the bone.  The food was fresh and delicious. Two people ate this food so there's plenty of value here.  I only gave four stars because it's my first time and I would have to try it again to raise it to five stars.
Liked the food, But disappointed with the price it's expensive for what I got.

Heres the bottom line , im ALWAYS right and will never steer you wrong , if I say it sucks , it SUCKS , if i say its awesome its AWESOME ............ bottom line , take a date here sit near window , enjoy the best priced wine bottle list ive seen anywhere and have some ridiculously awesome pasta especially the Gnocchi , After that walk back to Manhattan over the bridge at night , great spot........romantic and 10 ft from the restaurant , and then enjoy getting laid  , you are welcome
Just had a fabulous meal here. Super delicious upscale Mexican. I had the pork shoulder platter. Korean beef tacos were awesome too! Highly recommend this place.

From the moment they started construction on this place, I was eager to check it out. Two Hands has that specific hipster vibe where you just know from looking at it that good coffee is to be found inside. Finally got my chance to check it out yesterday, and while the coffee did not disappoint, everything else did. During my 15-minute wait in line, I decided on an iced coffee and the baked egg roll, only to be told they were sold out of the latter. At 10am. On a Saturday. At a breakfast establishment. I settled for the avo toast. As a lifelong New Yorker, "NYC prices" rarely faze me, but $7 for mashed avocado on a piece of bread the size of an iPhone is ridiculous. They can probably get away with charging these prices since there's nothing else like this place in the neighborhood, but I prefer not to feel like I've been robbed first thing in the morning. Next time I'm in the neighborhood, I'll hit up Baz or Nolita Mart instead. Their decor and coffee is on par with Two Hands', but blessedly come without such a pretentious crowd.

Try the Lamb Balti(Balti Ghosht). Restaurant is not expensive and food is really good. Not like other restaurant where very dish tastes the same. Biriyani is also good and not overrun with spices. And the staff is awesomeee. Very courteous and helpful, never had a bad experience. (I have visited the restaurant around 10times). They also have a grocery store attached to the restaurant.
