Note that the eggs were runny, so if you do not like runny eggs request them to cook it all the way through. The panini came with a side of greens and the olive tapenade was absolutely brilliant! There were alot more delicious items on the menu that I do want to come back and try but for now this was satisfying enough! Check out more reviews of NYC restaurants at my blog, whatsaachisays.blogspot.…

Low quality ingredients. The salad was barely edible and the dressings are overwhelming. Tomatoes almost rotten and the chicken was dry and flavorless. For a place that makes just salad they can't event get that right. Also they chop everyone's salad and toppings on the same cutting board which isn't very considerate for vegetarians. I would not come here again.

We have been to Tashan several times and decided to have our wedding welcome dinner there. The food (which was actually from Tiffin I believe) was excellent. All our our guests raved about it. The space is very very nice and it comfortably fit our large group of 45 guests. The staff were very accommodating of our needs (we wanted to have a microphone for some speeches etc). Bennett, in particular was extremely attentive and friendly.

Soup is OK. I ordered Chicken Soup, I read the review and I thought it would be in a good portion of the soup. It turned out that it's a really small bowl. You cannot even consider it as an appetizer. The appetizer was OK. The soup tasted great but was too small. The service was great and our server was wonderful.
My favorite Thai restaurant. Love the whole fish fry and the noodle soups at this place.
Great local joint to get chicken fingers. Great service too. I liked the fingers

This place is great! I came here with a family friend and really enjoyed the rolls. When I came they were having a sale which made our bill cheaper. I had the eel and avocado roll, the New York roll and the California roll. Always my favorites! However, the reason why I had to to take off one star is because we sat there waiting for 50 minutes without the food coming out. I understand sushi takes an exceptionally long time to prepare, but this was eat too long and we were STARVING. Bottom of the line, service was alright, food was awesome and scenery/ambience was good. Try to come during September-October for their Autumn sale and December for their holidays sale.
The dream
I grew up taking trips to the city just for these guys. Cheap, fast and good. Don't go as often now but when I do little has changed.
Simply Heaven. No Comments on Lamb over Rice, Just Heaven
All I can say is that it lived up to the Hype.The line was long but it went fast.Roast pork,broccoli rab and provolone is a great combo.

Despite the bad reviews I decided to give this place a try. I should've known better and trusted the community. I'm currently waiting for my food and watching the ONE AND ONLY man taking the orders, cooking the food and dealing with the money. It actually crossed my mind to leave but it wouldn't be right. So far I have seen him microwave the rice, burn the meat on 2 orders, try to get every last bit of sauce from the bottle which came out slightly watery and scoop the soggy salad into containers. What I have seen as portion wise is upsetting. 2 chunks of chicken, 3 sad slices of gyro meat. I understand the lunch prices are low but im used to the food trucks in NYC where you can get double the qualilty, double the portion and a lot fresher than what this place is serving for the same price. On top of the food prep and quality the wait makes you want to walk out and go to Wendy's next door. Now that im eating my food, it has hot sauce on it which i didnt ask for. Luckily i have a tolerance for it. Wouldn't recommend to any of my friends.

My friend and I went here a couple weeks ago and the food was amazing. I want to go back and try their different udons and ramens. If you go make sure to try their pork buns it is so so so good! The only thing I didn't like about this place is that the workers kept staring at me and my friend. Although attentive service is more than welcome I felt really scrutinized while eating so despite the yummy food I was slightly uncomfortable. My friend also agreed with me

food was delicious and well priced but the wait staff was constantly staring me and my wife down. it seemed like they wanted us in and then out, which would be understandable if it were closing time. it was 6 pm on a saturday and we were one of the three tables in there.

Been going to the Pancake House since I was little! One of the best places to get breakfast!!! Love it!!! It tends to get crowded on the weekends and sometimes parking spots are limited.  Over all friendly service and the family that runs the Pancake House is amazing!  I highly recommend the Dutch Baby and of course the pancakes or waffles are to die for!!!
look, it's a classic NJ bar and it's cheap. what else could you want? sorry, it is not "scene," but that train left this place before prohibition

My review is for the take out food. They are busy but the service is fast, I used to place the order by phone and drive there after 15 minutes to pick up the food. The portions are big and delicious. The girls at the balcony and cash register are very friendly and attentive. Every time they open the recipient in front of me to confirm the order. It was always correct :)

Consistently good food, Shanghai Bun has never dissapointed of the times my family and I have gone. Would recommend one "pork soup bun" appetizer to start (comes in 6 so adjust to group size) but you can't go wrong with anything on their menu! The Guava drink is refreshingly sweet and the menu is full of well priced items for lunch and dinner combos!

This place was DELICIOUS. We scooted over for a quick brunch before a show at the nearby Knitting Factory club. I had the goat cheese crepe with figs, honey and caramelized onions and let me just say that it was heaven on a plate.

Geno's Steaks - Tourist Trap #1A Tourist Trap #1B goes by the name of Pat's Steaks. Yes these are the two Cheese Steak places that you will see in the Philly Commercials and people around the country associate with Philadelphia. For that reason they can sell what ever they want and people will still line up! aka "The Tourist Trap" It bothers me, being a Philly native, that most tourist's think that this is what a Philly Steak is, and they have to eat low grade fatty gristled Crap! Its sad and embarrassing to know that people from around the country, and around the world think that choking on gristle is just part of enjoying a Philly Steak. I'm giving Geno's and Pat's 2 stars instead of 1 because, Hey, at least you get an iconic photo-op in front of the place! Just do yourself a Big favor and eat somewhere else!

We went at midnight on a rainy Sunday and were the only ones in line. I ordered my cheese steak properly and my order was repeated properly, but came out wrong. I ordered one cheesesteak, whiz, with onion. Didn't get the onion. No big, there was a line by the time I opened it and having worked in similar places like this I wasn't going to complain. I went to get my soda at the next window and stood there for about 2 minutes while an older guy talked to a younger guy, and both of them acknowledged I was there but didn't bother coming up to take care of my order. When the older guy did come up he was still in his conversation and blaming the young guy for not telling him I was there. That  was the extent of the experience, now moving onto the food. I had Pat's across the street the day before so I wanted to try a handful of different places during the week. The sandwich itself was really good, but not quite my favorite cheesesteak I've had. There's really not much more to say I guess. There's hundreds of places across Philadelphia to get a good cheesesteak but this one in particular doesn't stand out. It might have warranted a 4 or maybe even a 5 if I had gotten what I ordered and they didn't waste my time so they could chat. I wouldn't expect anything more than standard service and it didn't deliver.   Also, I was a little put off by the whole "freedom fries" and "Speak English because this is America" stickers. That's somewhat ironic coming from a place that has a huge international tourist following. The freedom fries thing is long past too. I'm as patriotic as the next but that just seemed tacky.
PIZZA ONLY I always get the Margherita slice.  thin crispy crust, fresh mozz & tomato topping. I miss this pizza dearly. apparently BYOB!

It's Sunday morning and your body is going through withdrawal from the lack of alcohol in the past 6 hours. Most people would call this a hangover, but I call it a sign, a sign that you need to get to Knock and have their famous Knock-out mimosa. Like a good workout regimen, day drinking isn't going to get you anywhere unless you push yourself. This mimosa comes with an added shot of orange vodka, which makes the already beautiful waiters and bar tenders look even better. Who knows, maybe this liquid courage will even push you to find that Sunday afternoon cuddle buddy we all are looking for. Just don't take mine. Pro-tip: sit outside for extra good eye candy, and to work on your tan.

This place is cute and fun, but there is typically a wait and the food is not always worth it. Many of the items we ordered to share we're smaller than expected so order more than one of everything if you are with a group (they are priced well so it's worth it). Still a good night out with girlfriends though!

Since my review, I have returned for lunch and dinner several times and the food is consistently prepared well.  Honestly, it is so hard to even rate one plate over the other as a favorite. Everything is so good at Titanic!!  For appetizer, I appreciate the shrimp in garlic. The shrimp is very fresh and does not have that fishy farm raised flavor like some other places. I have tried everything from stuffed shrimp, pork tenderloin with shrimp, sirloin steak, steak on a stone, broiled red snapper, cod fish, and surf and turf.  Each dish was excellently prepared in it's own way. If I would have to choose a favorite, I would choose the pork dishes because they remind me of a home cooked Portuguese meal.  Please keep doing what you are doing Titanic, and we will keep coming back for more!!

I needed a nice, nutritious meal after a long day of traveling hungry and dehydrated. Thank you, ReViVer! I ordered the grilled mahi with the sauces on the side. Also got a free tea, thanks Yelp! You can choose green/black. They have Truvia (not Splenda!) packets, something unseen in Northern California. The food came out in a meal prep container like bowl. I love it. My mom, however, said it had no taste. I like it low sodium, sorry ma. She went and bought cookies/treats from the Bread Factory across the street afterwards to make up for it.
The bartenders suck...they have no formal training and seem inexperienced. but over it's not at all a bad spot for a Tuesday in the "hood" and it is hood

Tried this place for the first time. Food was pretty good, customer service could definitely use improvement. When I called to place an order for pick-up, the person who answered the food was talking so incredibly fast I could hardly understand them and was rude from the start. I had a question since it was my first time ordering and it was answered curtly. They also did not ask if I wanted soup and salad or soda but I didn't want soda so it didn't matter this time.  After finishing, they said "10 minutes" and abruptly hung up without asking my name or number.   However, when I picked up the food, the person who helped me was friendly. The restaurant seemed clean. There is no hostess stand or counter for pick-up,etc. so when I walked in, I did not know where to go to pick up my order. One of the people making sushi at the sushi bar saw me and called someone to come help me. It worked out fine, but pick-up seems like it could definitely be a hassle during busy hours. I ordered the kitchen lunch box (chicken teriyaki.) The chicken teriyaki was delicious and the soup was good. The rice and salad were fine as well. However, the shumai hardly had anything in it. I could taste some semblance of some kind of vegetable and a very slight taste of something else, but it was mostly the dough. The California roll was okay. It was kind of mushy and warm (which might have been from the soup sitting on top of the container--I got there within the 10 minutes and the bag was already packed). I thought there was too much avocado and when I tried to pick up the pieces with chopsticks, they started to fall apart, with the rice falling off the sides in large chunks. The pieces were also smaller than other places I have been too. However, there was a good amount of food for a reasonable price (although the quality wasn't the best all-around). I will try this place again, but I will try dine-in.

I really enjoyed my food. I had the open face turkey sandwich with cranberries & Cabot cheese. So good. Service was also good & we enjoyed our time there. The fresh fruit served with my meal was excellent. My husband had the curried beef & he liked it quite a bit.

Terrible service from the rude waitstaff! Food was subpar which went hand in hand with the ambiance, service and cramped size of the restaurant. The current reviews of the restaurant seem to most accurately reflect the true colors of the restaurant. This is a solid one star establishment. Don't pick this place based on the overall reviews. 4 stars is what this place absolutely is not !!! Make sure to read the current, recent reviews. This place is on a downhill avalanche to the bottom, if it hasn't already reached the bottom. The large man here definitely has a large man complex , mixed with know it all attitude. What are you doing in the service industry much less managing a restaurant. You wouldn't last a day in San Francisco bro.

I definitely love this restaurant!!! They have the most traditional Korean food. You got to try the Tofu soup! IT IS AMAZING!!! Lunch time in business day you can have lunch combo as tofu soup with BBQ. I ordered the first combo in the menu. BEST ever!!!

Really like this spot especially with the patio outside. It's casual and comfortable enough to bring the kids, and the food is always good. Our favorites are the pizza, eggplant trio appetizer, and the pork chops. The pasta with sausage, broccoli rabe and   cannellini beans is delicious too!
The owner is very nice, takes care of his customer personally. Food was very good. The stuffed cabbage is delicious, my favor is the okra with lamb. Love the desserts and the Turkish tea.

Overall we had a nice dining experience- the food was freshly prepared and cooked well. We enjoyed our entrees (both specials) and especially loved the polenta fries as our side.  We were able to bring some of our favorite wine from our wine cellar to enjoy since this is a byob, which was a big plus for us.

I went here for happy hour on a Tuesday with a friend, and I enjoyed the goat cheese with fig and pickled tomato dishes I got. They were tasty and fresh. However, I felt that the service was very nearly terrible. The bartender was unhelpful and very inattentive. When my friend asked for a recommendation, he simply said it all depended on your own personal taste and walked away. I liked the ambiance at this place, but the poor service was simply inexcusable. I wouldn't go back here again, despite the affordable happy hour menu. It doesn't help that there were only two options available on the happy hour menu for vegetarians.
Delicious food, friendly service, and convenient location. Bring quarters for parking, and definitely try any of their specialty cheesecakes!

Their sandwiches are great. Their fries are great. The hire from within the neighborhood, and aren't overpriced (yet). I'd suggest trying this place out. I've ordered from them many times (I always do takeout because the space is small) and will miss them terribly after I move in a few weeks. Recommended: The duck confit sandwich and the cuban sandwich. And to the other yelpers posting negative reviews, I guess technically you CAN write a review without ever having eaten at a place, but seems a bit irresponsible to me. If you want to complain about racism, I think you might want to build your case a bit. One insensitive sandwich board does not mean they're too racist to function.

I picked uo dinner to go for the first time tonight.  I ordered the pastor tacos and since it was taco Tuesday they were 5 for $5. Overall they were pretty tasty. Like other reviewers have suggested the salsa is no joke. I made the mistake of taking a huge bite of salsa Roja and my mouth has not been the same. The mild salsa is definitely do able. Looking forward to trying other things on the menu.

The place looks inviting, with thousands of Nutella jars of various kinds. However, the staff is anything but kind. We waited in line for 15 minutes, only to hear the staff say: "we're done for the night, come back for breakfast"... It was closing time, sharp! How rude can she be? If your time is so valuable that you don't want to work an extra minute, close the door 15 minutes prior to closing time, so you don't waste other people's time... shame on what could be a good place, and I know Nutella is awesome awesome chocolate, too bad you hired retarded staff.
original and innovative sushi with a focus on sustainable ingredients

The food is good, and the bar area and outdoor seating are very nice, however the dinning room does not have the best atmosphere (a little cafeteria in feeling because it's so large and bright). I would rate it higher but the pricing is a little high- they typically offer  coupons and specials but if I'm going out to eat I don't want to worry about bringing a coupon.

One of our staple go-to places in montclair for a fast, casual family dinner. Burgers are great and in the summer the blueberry pie is amazing! If you are lucky enough to be there when they have it, order it at the beginning of your meal to make sure they don't run out. We usually get the calamari salad for an appetizer- you can have them split it for you if you are sharing. Overall a great spot especially if you want to enjoy your meal outside.

I have a new favorite sushi place in town! Bleu Sushi was exactly what I was looking for. The other night my girlfriend and I went out in center city looking for a new sushi place to try, when we stumbled upon Bleu Sushi. We were very happy with the service and the ambiance upon entering the restaurant. The staff was extremely accommodating and the interior was intimate. We had a lovely dinner- excellent sushi and dumplings. The owner greeted our table and was very hospitable, making the experience all that much more intimate. I look forward to eating there again in the future and ordering takeout. Additionally I was impressed with the value and the quality. Excellent food for a great price, without out any attempts to nickel and dime you. Bleu Sushi is as good as it gets!

Another quality Chic-fil-a with a friendly and attentive staff. They'll help you carry your tray and always show much patience when my little guys trade their toy for a ice cream. We enjoyed an awesome magic show on family night and have never left disappointed.
Love their burgers; I just build my own! And the red velvet milk shake? Yummmy! Oh, their onion ring are my favorite and they have really nice customer service!

I've been to this establishment twice...I'll provide both experiences. First time was grand opening week in Q2-2014. Service was bad, kitchen is absurdly slow. Drinks came 25 minutes after the order was placed. Place was not busy at the time, perhaps 2-3 tables. Despite the bad service and waiting, the food was okay although a little overpriced($19 bucks per person for a burger, drink, side with tip). Okay so it was grand opening week, lets chalk this up to being a new restaurant. Now, its August 2014, about 5 months for the restaurant to get settled in a very popular location with tons of exposure and traffic. A coworker and I decided to give it a second chance. Can't be as bad as the first time right? Kitchen was still very slow, drinks were on time. Food took about 20-25 minutes to come out. I'd understand if this place was packed at lunchtime but again, there were only 2-3 tables. How hard is it to cook some burgers and deep fry some french fries? Food was their only save. burgers are fresh and not greasy. Not a bad burger at all.   Management seriously needs to step in and do some time studies or work flow optimization. Considering the location, this place should easily get 10-12 tables during lunch, a lunch special menu would be a good idea, who wants to pay $20 bucks at lunch for a burger? Lots of potential here, too bad the place is probably run by idiots. Staff is super friendly and nice, but that doesn't mean good service. Honestly wouldn't be surprised if this place closed soon.

To start, I will say that while working in Newark I visited Harvest Table for lunch more than any other place. While there are other tasty places around, I never felt I was eating as healthy or as clean (for my body) a meal at places other than Harvest Table. I liked the dressings (Sesame Ginger and Teriyaki Wasabi) for my salads, which was my usual order. The salads are probably somewhat overpriced, and the ingredients are not nearly ideal in freshness or flavor. I am a huge fan of the workers, both the salad maker and the women who work the register. The music was always to my liking. Like others have mentioned, for the area this is a place well worth checking out and even going to consistently. However, in a place such as, say, New York City, I would say this place is worth checking out but not a consistent winner. I preferred my homemade lunches, but when I was short on time or energy in the morning, I usually ended up at Harvest Table.

This is such a great place. Easy to find on bleecker in the heart of the village, it's a great option for those nights when you're just not sure what you want. Not only is the food excellent, well prepared and flavorful, but it's gluten free! You can even get gluten free bread here! It's like heaven for anyone with a true gluten allergy. The only thing you'll need to beware of is the crowd. It's not a large space, and you can feel a bit in top of one another, so it's not the new option for a night when you want some privacy for a good conversation. You're going to hear everyone around you and vice versa, but for a casual night of homey, but interesting food, this is a great place.
Still five stars over the course of several more visits over the past few months. Definitely admire the consistency in food quality.

I love this place. The food is not cheap, but it really is excellent, and the atmosphere is charming. Good lunch spot. Be careful with the bar...the pounds add up fast and you can easily walk away with a $16 plate because everything looks sooooo good (and it is). I avoid this risk by ordering the roasted tofu sandwich just about every single time I go there. I would love to try other things, but I just cannot tear myself away from this amazing sandwich. The first thing to know is that it is huge, so you will not leave hungry. It has an amazing blend of flavors and textures. You can't go wrong with this sandwich.

On a busy day at work my co worker and I decided to stop for a meal. The facility is located on a mall strip and to many this might be a turn off but don't let the location fool you. Entering the establishment you are greeted by friendly staff who is willing to assist. People complain that things changed and the food isn't the same.... Regardless of your opinion in my personal experience the service is great. I had 2 slices of pepperoni pizza and my only complaint is it was a bit greasy which is y I give them 4 stars but aside from that, the speed of which I got my meal was impeccable again kudos to the team at Arlington pizza.

Pleasantly surprised. Really nice staff and delicious food. Started with the Char Grilled Octopus Salad. Main course was Akdeniz Levregl imported mediterranean sea bass. I have an picky palette, so I must say that the char flavor was a bit powerful and the seasoning (if any) did not show. However it was juicy and the natural flavor of the sea bass left me finishing my plate. My wife had the Adana Kebab hand chopped lamb. The meat was succulent and flavorful. The rice was of good select. All followed by Turkish tea (wasn't special, could use a mint leaf). Ended with my first time tasting the desert Kunefe.... WONDERFUL! I will be returning to try the rest of the menu.

Ordered take out pizza last Friday night.  Didn't think to look at the pizza before leaving.  When I got home there were 3 large burn spots on top and the entire bottom had burn spots all over.  I would have been better off ordering from Pepe's and driving into New Haven.  Don't cheat yourself and order good pizza and drive a little further.

I enjoyed my dish of Ravioli De Pollo consisting of homemade chicken ravioli, asparagus, arugula & parmesan, in garlic & oil. It was cooked perfectly - just enough el dente to let you know you were eating at a restaurant that knows it's Italian. However I made the grave mistake of ordering a Tricolore Con Parmigiano which is arugula, endive & radicchio, with slice parmesan cheese. I felt that made my entire meal too bitter with the arugula in both dishes. It overpowered both and made the meal too bland. The wine was delicious and they have a very nice selection. The server was friendly and efficient (although I wish he had warned me about the match up of salad to ravioli) but overall he was excellent. I doubt I would eat here when I'm back in the area but only because the menu was northern and I prefer southern Italian dishes.

We eat out very often, and this is my favorite dinner spots. We've never had a meal where we weren't more than satisfied. While the set menu is always appealing, the specials typically catch our attention and are delicious. Great spot if you are in the mood for fish or (fresh!) pasta. We've also enjoyed the risotto on a few occasions (always a part of the specials) but beware if you want to eat the delicious appetizers and desserts because it's heavy.

Great spot for drinks- have tried many different cocktails on large menu and enjoyed all of them. The food is not quite as good as the cocktails, but still very nice and they have a good amount of options to share with a group.

I was searching for a vegetarian restaurant for my weekend in Burlington and I'm so glad I found this one! It was a lovely atmosphere, wonderful staff, and excellent food! It's on the pricier side for a meal but worth it for such a treat! We got the tacos (good but the mushrooms were a little weird) and the noodle pot. The spring rolls to start were also great!  Fun time trying new and creative vegetarian food, will go back next time I visit!

Two stars for the cheap drink prices and wide range of the hours their open. Very good ribbs on Wed/Thurs only. Old man bar, AWEFUL bartenders, the absolute WORST and cult like crowd. Go to the Town Pub down the street!!!!

Went there the 3rd day of the soft opening.  I had the amazing lamb shank, and my wife had an as delicious grilled skirt steak.  Great service, cooked just right.  Great prices and and great customer service.
Great service from Ann, she was very experienced and it showed. Food was excellent, beautiful ambiance, all around great experience!
Very nice - convenient location and nice selection.   The escargot was perfectly done and the dinners were nicely prepared.

I've been coming to Georgie's for several years now, ever since I was diagnosed with celiac disease and discovered they have a gluten-free menu here.  The GF choices are really great, there's an entire separate menu instead of just a few things marked "GF" on the regular one. I've come here so often more than half the staff recognizes me, and they're always friendly and ask how I'm doing. They also always point out when they have a new GF menu item or dessert -- this past weekend they even had GF cupcakes, which of course I had to try, and which were heavenly. I've gotten to be good friends with one of the servers, Sophia, and have come in a few times just because I know she's working. Although I've only ever tried the GF options, I've brought a lot of other non-GF people here, and they tell me the rest of the menu is really good as well. I'm so happy I found this place -- I love coming to a restaurant where I can count on all the employees actually understanding what gluten-free really means, and always being happy to see me.  Highly recommended. :)

Yummers. If I lived in New York, this would be my new hangout. Also, quite friendly. Definitely try the back room, which is built like a library. I enjoy that they maintain an homage to Elaine's, which used to be in this location.
The food is amazing here, tons of gluten free options as well and they have dedicated gluten free fryers! I love their chicken cornmeal empanadas!
Loved the place, loved the food, loved bringing my own booze and what i loved the most was that S'mores bread pudding!

I've been there twice. The first time, I had French toast and baked sausage egg and both of them were amazing. The second time, I had waffle with fruits and steak&egg. The steak&egg was great but the waffle was just so so.
Burger was ok. Came out lukewarm. Fries were nothing special. Waitress/bartender could have been nicer.
By far the best Ruben I have had. I got the half n half. One half was corned beef and the other pastrami. Best kosher deli ever!!!

The worst service ever, the waitress made me and girl move from a table saying it's only two of you take the smaller table,  ok we did, 5 seconds later  another spanish couple came sat at the table we originally sat at she didn't say shit, she didn't ask them to move to a smaller table, This waitress acted as if she didn't want to take our order.

I love this place. My favourites are the French Toast,Tomato Mozarello Sandwich and the Ravioli. They are one of the very few places that serve freshly squeezed juice (Orange and Grapefruit). The service is excellent and the decor is just fabulous. Ram

I wanted to like it. The waitress was the only saving grace. She was sweet and tried her best. All food was made from frozen chicken tenders and frozen fried mozzarella. Both chicken and mozz were soggy and inedible. My boyfriend ordered chicken florentine and I ordered chicken francese. We both got the same sauce which tasted like Heinz gravy on our meals. We did not eat much. We won't come back.

I'm pretty disappointed that the owner's response to my review was, in not so many words, "don't let the door hit you on the way out." Rather than address the service failures (understaffed, long wait time for food, unsatisfactory food/drink, incorrectly charged for items), the owner (Kathy K.) felt it would be more productive to tell me to "get a life" and remind me that I'm not in the south. It seems a little hypocritical for Butcher Bar to defend their low-quality BBQ (seriously, is that brisket boiled??) by saying "this isn't the south," but also use their website to tout that their head chef, Orlando Sanchez, hails from Austin, TX. I was born and raised in Houston and lived in Austin for seven years, Kathy, and trust me, with your subpar food and arrogant refusal to address complaints, you wouldn't last a year in either city. Good luck with your expansion and your new bar space. I sincerely hope you make better cocktails than BBQ.

I have been to this establishment many times.  This passed Sunday was an exception.  They were out of so much, not surprising and I give most restaurants a pass if it's a Sunday as most businesses won't deliver.  I also had stopped by on Saturday for drinks and saw that the restaurant was rather busy.   So, I am not upset, it's clear that this is a farm to table fresh made restaurant so I accept when things aren't available.  The things I loved are the bbq chicken, mussels and steak.  I got these on Sunday and they were amazing.  Perfect bbq sauce, I would like to buy some of their sauce!   The bread I got with my mussels was equally delicious, we asked for a few more orders.  We got a few cocktails and those were good as always.  The food is always delicious and I will always go back for an amazing upscale home cooked feel.   My issue with Sunday night was actually the service, I try and ignore bad service or perhaps an annoying waiter.  I have gotten this one guy several times and I have come to the conclusion that I will call ahead and ask who's waiting tables.  The waitress is great, attentive, courteous, kind and is constantly checking even from afar.  The regular bus boy wasn't there and he makes such a difference too, always checking on my table and filling my water or also putting in orders.  Sunday was some other kid who clearly hasn't got a clue.   So, between the waiter, who, once again is an awful bumbling idiot and his sidekick I was not impressed with my service.  I was enjoying drinks and the waiter finishes up and sits down at the bar.  You shouldn't hang out at work but even before he sat down, he was more attentive to talking to the bartender, friends at the bar and watching tv. I bring in clients and friends for dinner, plus the occasional date.  The food stands on it's own but the waiter is the face that I interact with and was incredibly embarrassed bringing a business associate.      As for the restaurant, in general it's great.  I genuinely love this spot, it's farm fresh product that I would never make at home, I think the cost is spot on and it's a perfect place for a date or dinner with friends.  I would come back but only to sit at the bar or if the waitress is working.   Questions: if you are fine dining establishment why does your staff wear jeans and sneakers.  Why, why, why are your tv's always on? Suggestions: Get rid of that waiter asap, he's rude, not knowledgeable and doesn't care to ever check on my table.
their masa ceviche is amazing, i ordered that twice last night. Do not forget to try their eggplant sandwich. good AYCE price. Must have green tea ice cream to be your dessert.

The worst Chinese food I have ever tasted. We ordered pork fried rice and coconut chicken for take out and had it delivered. We took a few bites and had to throw the rest away and make something else. It was absolutely disgusting and inedible.
the pizza was sooooo good words cant explain, my mouth wanted to keep eating but my stomach wouldnt let me!! :'(
THIS place is a legend  but ever seince it went from the ITALIANS to the MEXICANS/MIDDLE easterns owners - the Quality of the Squares went down !
Great Bar. Awesome food great service and a very good beer selection. Will definitely return in the future!

I had been waiting a bit to go into this restaurant and was surprised to see they aren't all that. I bought 4 chicken dinners with mac n cheese and one with fries and pull pork sandwich. I was surprised the chicken wasn't properly seasoned, bland really, even the crust had no flavor, the sandwich I bought for hubby he said was too small and was flavorless too. For what you are getting it is way overpriced. I wont be going back anytime soon. The restaurant is tight so we had to wait for our to go order outside.

Had the 5:30 Chef Tasting on a Friday evening. What a wonderful time. It was $70 for one person (plus tax and tip) and you can bring your own wine if you are into that. Had 6 courses plus a dessert. Some of the best food I had - ever.

I recently moved to the area in the last month and have tried this place twice in the last month. The first time I went with a friend and we ate there. The service was just below average which for us meant they seated us, took a while to take our order and we had to track them down to get the bill and again to pay the bill. As for the food, we shared an Ortolana and a forgettable appetizer. The Ortolana pizza was burnt on one side and a little cold. I was underwhelmed but willing to try again. Two nights ago I ordered pickup since I live a few blocks away and ordered the Market Salad, the Fave E Cicoria and the Salsiccia. Once again, I was extremely underwhelmed. The pizza was missing  sausage on half of it and once again it was burnt and needed some seasoning. I'm sure at one time this place was good but they've gotten seriously lazy. I'll stick to Lombardi's.

Hands down one of the best brunch spots for the TriBeCa locals! This may come off as quite random, but they have the best chocolate milk i've ever had! Service was also A+. The wait was quite long, however one can expect that on a sunday morning. Other than that, i recommend the place to anyone visiting town.

China Pavillion is the BEST chinese restaurant anywhere.  I now only like their food.  If I go somewhere else I'm very disappointed.  I always get Kung Pow Four Flavor or Beef with scented ginger and both have a wonderful flavored oil for a sauce instead of a gravy.  Everyone is so nice to you there.  They did the inside over a while ago (years) and it is so clean and pretty.

I have been going to China Pavilion for years!  I love the pineapple chicken.  I love it all but that is my favorite!  The service is as awesome as the food.  The restaurant is also clean!  Always a good choice.

Great ribs and pulled pork and decent brisket.  Probably the best ribs I've eaten in a restaurant.  Service is good.  Wine list is as poor as the food is good.  They're missing a trick on that one.  We would have drunk much more wine if we'd been able to find a decent bottle.   Homemade pies for dessert were also very good. I'd definitely go back - as would every member of our party of seven. David G

So, we visited this place some zillion times only to wait outisde for hours and return home with a burger or sandwich from subway. Fially, we got to get inside the place. The place is too crowded and we eagerly waited to taste food. Personally, I didnot enjoy what I was given. I am a vegetarian. hence, my choices were limited and the waiters were too impatient to serve as there were to many people. We got our check more faster than our food and how long we waited to get inside. I am not sure how non-vegetarian is. it is worth a try. But I haven't visited this place again and do not plan to.

Not. Good. Ordered the lamb platter and received a dish with crumbly, dry, tasteless lamb, unseasoned and undercooked rice, white sauce that is basically seasoned mayo (consistency and all), a few shreds of soggy lettuce, and to top it all off, wet pita (which is usually my favorite part of a platter like this). I hope this was just a bad day at Spice End because if not, I'm not sure what these other reviewers are tasting. I've had far better at the food truck on Drexel's campus...and for less than 1/2 the price.

Just OK...but worth another try...maybe. We were very excited with our first visit to Argicola this past weekend.  Upon entering we were impressed with the decor and good looking crowd by the bar.  However, we were a little let down when the hostess led us downstairs to the 'wine cellar', a fairly sizable rectangle shaped room with about ten tables.  We were one of only three parties in the room...felt like maybe it was the 'dungeon room'...guess that's what I get for making reservations for a Saturday night only five days in advance. Anyway, we ordered the cheese board and flat bread appetizers and enjoyed them both.  The wait staff was attentive and knowledgeable about the menu and wine list.  However, when the main courses came we all felt a little let down and underwhelmed.  The portion sizes were below average and pricey.  I had the ribeye (boneless) with fingerling potatoes...cooked exactly the way I wanted and tasty...however I felt the $47 price was a bit high.  My wife had the same experience with the scallops...small portion (three scallops), very nicely done, but pricey. You can't help but think that maybe this place is using their mantra, 'farm to table', and Princeton locale as a kind of 'Jedi mind trick' to make everyone think it's worth it no matter what the cost.
my favorite pizza in New Haven

We went here on our anniversary. I am a vegetarian so a friend of mine suggested this place. We were suprised to see the menu. They have vast vegetarian options and I really enjoyed my platters. Try Sambusa, and crepes. They are yummy. The place is cute and staff were very cooperative. Prices are reasonable.

This is the best sandwich shop in the area! Why more people don't talk about it, I'm not sure.  The cold cuts are sliced individually for every sandwich so everything is always fresh. A half sandwich is really a whole and a whole is really a double.

We didn't have the best first experience here, but after trying it again we really enjoyed our meal. Loved the dirty chai drink- exactly what I needed after a long night. My husband has the roast beef with cream cheese, pickled blueberries sandwich and it was amazing. I went a little more basic with the fried egg and hash breakfast sandwich and it was tasty. Love the overall atmosphere/vibe as well.

speedy service, awesome tacos, loads of chips, big drink menu! Stopped into loco on a recent Thursday with a friend.  The atmosphere is extremely relaxed and family friendly. The menu at loco is simple - starters, salads, quesadillas and tacos. We had some straightforward queso & salsa with chips.  No complaints about it and additional baskets of chips are free.  I order a grilled fish tacos and a shrimp taco and would order both of them again.  Typically $3 tacos at places like loco are a little wimpy, but there's were robust and delicious. My friend had a chicken taco that I was rather jealous of.

Excellent lunch today at Paul's Diner - I'm a vegetarian and have found that not many diners have grilled vegie wraps and if they do that they're not so great.  The vegie wrap here was terrific - very tasty and fresh;  the sweet potato fries were delicious and cooked as I had requested.  There were several other vegetarian options.  Service was courteous, prompt and attentive.  My friend's lunch special croissant sandwich was also excellent.. Extensive menu.  We were looking for a place to meet in that area - glad we ignored the not so great reviews and went to Pauls..
Aweful! Over priced! No flavor! Go else where! I had the shrimp veggie tempura ....2 dinky shrimp and a few veggies. No flavor at all!

Such a cute spot with really delicious food. Have been here a few times already so far (it's new)- once with my girlfriends and everyone loved what they ordered, and a few times with the family who now requests it every Sunday. The weekend brunch is especially good- it's very fresh and the specials are fun/different (I'm still dreaming about the cannoli stuffed french toast). The staff is super sweet and very accommodating- they even brought out a water bowl for our dog on a busy Sunday.

I can't get enough of this place! I've been for breakfast, lunch, and even brunch on the weekends with my friends and I have never left without being satisfied. I think they only opened up a few months ago but every time I go it's always a nice sized croud! The food is obviously amazing but I think I enjoy this place so much because the atmosphere it brings is absolutely adorable. It has seating inside and out which is nice for these beautiful summer days. It is connected to an equally adorable book store which makes it a great spot to come relax and enjoy a coffee while reading that new book you picked up next door. And let's not forget the FREE WIFI. It's right next to Watchung Train Station so I usually stop in to grab something quick before going to NYC. Great food, great enviorment, and great people at this new hot spot! I highly recommend it.
This is my favorite place in town! Could not say enough about the sweet owners and amazing food! Must try!!!!!

Best ramen I've ever had. The flavour, spice, heat, and helping are outstanding. The pork slices are cooked with a blow torch to perfection; I loved the pork buns! This place is always busy, so make sure you put your name down on the list.

No - seriously.......this is SUCH a great cafe. They have a chicken sandwich with a champagne dressing that is like nothing....nothing I have ever tasted. It takes chicken sandwich to a level of which it has never dreamed. The bread - so crunchy and that dressing.....omg.....  everything else I have had there is very good. BUT the chicken sandwich....a MUST try.......

came here about an hour before our show we had to attend about a block away in the theater district. we needed a very nice restaurant to go to for my 30th birthday but in decent time so we couldn't be late for our show. it was just before the dinner time rush and it wasn't as busy as i thought it would be. nothing to really complain about. the food was good. menu had enough to choose from and fast service. i asked to put a rush on the food, but i didn't really have to as it seemed everyone else got their food fast as well.

They may be rude but the food is so good. It is best to avoid the barbecue items late at night. It is better to catch it during the day. Cheap + good food + open till late at night. Can't ask for me and makes me a regular to Noodle town after partying. The egg noodles, roast pork on rice, roast duck on rice, beef in egg sauce-- all these are very good. Try the noodle soups as well. My favorite: Salt baked shrimp. Those salt baked shrimps with the hot sauce on side are the best stuff you can have after one too many drinks! One can try the salt baked combo as well. The portions are just right and the food is just so tasty you want to go back over and over.

Loved it!  We got the sesame pancakes and pork dumplings.  A ton of food for under $10. The only complaint we had was the was nowhere to sit down and eat it!  We just stood on the sidewalk and ate it.

Palma. I've been going to Palma for years, and always enjoyed its simple but very good Italian food and its charming hosts. Last night I chose it for a birthday dinner. IT WAS AWFUL. I found out they had changed the executive chef. The menu was weird, and fancied up--a gluten free pasta (really?!) and some yellow tail tartare thing (this is an Italian restaurant.) We waited twenty minutes for our reservation and we were seated by a sullen young woman in short red shorts, who seemed to feel her shorts made up for her lack of apology or even charm. The food was REALLY BAD. The bread was soggy and cut in teeny pieces, appetizers were unrecognizable. My pasta, a very simple spaghetti with mozzarella and tomato WAS INEDIBLE, undercooked, and tasteless. My friend's chicken Milanese was like breaded cardboard. The calamari were free of any flavor. The charming waiters had disappeared and replaced by guys who were OK, but with no particular investment in our evening. There used to be a roof that was open around the sides even when it rained, so it was always pleasant. Now they have a hard roof that they had pulled over a day before rain--too much trouble to do it later?--and it made the garden hot and very very noisy, and made it seem more of a fake construct than a real garden. As what I guess was an apology for the lousy food, they brought some lousy deserts without asking if we wanted any desert at all. Worst tiramisu in history. I am guessing that tourists have found this garden "charming", and it is now so packed even early on a Monday, it has nothing "local" about it. Ah, the ever important buck. And it is not cheap, not by the standards of great small Italian restaurants in the village and Soho like Picola Cucina on Spring Street. I was so disappointed. As somebody said in a comment here about brunch, "it was typical NYC brunch food". That's the problem: In NYC, nobody should settle for typical anything when there is so much that's really wonderful. I will never go back here, and really feel a bit heartbroken that one of my favorites--I have lived in Greenwich Village all my life--has gone so downhill so fast. DO NOT GO...there are four other good places next door on Cornelia Street, including the wonderful Pearl and the delightful Gigot.

Food was amazing. Came to dinner because it was recommended by my sister. The atmosphere was great and it was byob which is why the bill isn't as expensive as other Italian places. Went with a total of six and paid 140 and that included 6 meals and two appetizers. The only downfall I would say is the wait time we had. Almost two hours! But the food made up for it. I recommend going during the week or for early dinner. The later the reservation the later u will eat.
Best service I ever had... Branzino was delicious

This is a review for Saturday lunch only. My fiancé and I were in the area and we were so hungry so we decided we were going to this place instead of my usual across the street. He really likes this place because they have pretty much everything from hot dogs to Chinese dim sum, it's actually quiet a sight when you are standing right there in the aisle. You look to the left you have your typical American food, then you look to the right you have yummy dim sum steamed up in the little bamboo thingy. I thought the selections were mediocre++, not the best but much better than your other tropical Chinese/Japanese buffet. Seafood/sushi choices were decent. Maybe they would have more choices if we went during dinner. Overall, I'd go back again for sure. Service was fast, as soon as they see an empty plate they came right up and cleaned it up.

Really mediocre dim sum. It was super close to our hotel and the service was quick, since they had just opened when we went. Otherwise, the food wasn't great and the tables were too small to fit the dishes we ordered plus drinks plus the spice tray. Food tastes like it's frozen and reheated. Cheap, but wouldn't go here again.
One of the best ramen in NYC. This Japanese ramen joint is about as authentic as you can find without even going to Japan
Dirty!
Poor Service!
Some of the top pizza in Brooklyn, and that is saying a lot! I just did a pizza tour and got to enjoy an amazing white pie here......seriously, seriously GOOD.
Awesome food! The black bean burger was full of flavor, calm ambience, and customer service was fantastic. Great lunch spot right by the water!

This was one of my favorite places I got a cheesesteak while visiting Philadelphia. It was midnight on a Saturday and had about 10 people in line ahead of me and the wait time was really short. These guys were cranking them out. There was a sign that made it clear how to order and that was the only way to order. I ordered one with whiz, with onion, with peppers. I also had one with American on my trip. It came out with a good amount of cheese and I liked that the meat was chopped instead of layed flat, it made it seem like there was more that way. I moved down to the fries/soda window and it was the same thing. In and out of there in no time. As far as the cheesesteak goes, it was a pretty standard cheesesteak. I say that in the best way possible. Cheesesteaks are awesome and its not hard to make a good one. It came out hot, the meat wasn't overcooked, the bread was good, and it had plenty of cheese and onions. Perfection. I was hungry and was looking for a good cheesesteak and it was exactly what I was looking for, plus they were fast and everything came out right. The vibe of this place is awesome too. Its not flashy with a thousand neon lights, and its a little divey, but its just right.

Excellent restaurant. The staff there are very friendly. Most are really from India and Nepal. To my unrefined sense of taste to Indian food, the taste wasn't bad. We had triditional curry chicken and nan and Indian rice. All are very good. Worth coming back. The area is in west village. Good for late munchie after some drinking.

For every compliment I want to pay this place, there always seems to be a complaint the goes with it: 1. The food I've eaten was usually pretty good! ... However half the menu seems to be unavailable (no lamb burger, no skewers, no reuben ... Wth?) 2.  The servers and bartenders are all knowledgeable.  Especially impressive service considering the bartender looked pretty uncomfortable rolling off the laundry list of things that weren't available ... ... However the staff always seems to completely change and the food seems to come out of the kitchen REALLY slow. 3.  The whiskey list was impressive! ... Again though, a good deal of what's listed is unavailable and some selections are a bit overpriced. To be fair, it was explained the whiskey list was changing extensively soon 4. The draft list is the best reason to go! ... Not so much for the cocktail menu though which is uncreative, pretentious, and overpriced With a spot this good, with the servers trying as hard as they are, I can't help but walk away with the impression that this place SHOULD be better than it is. It just can't seem to stop tripping over itself.  I prefer Growlers (about two or three blocks away). Selection isn't quite as good as The Barrel House's (should be), but they definitely have their act together when it comes to running their business ...

Amazing! My husband and I celebrated our anniversary here recently. Great atmosphere, great drinks, and the food is phenomenal! For drinks, I recommend the Rosa Margarita, it's delicious. For food, try the Queso De Mariscos and the Molcajete de Pollo. You won't be disappointed!

I went for the first time with a couple of friends and we all thought the food was fantastic!! I got the chicken and shrimp hibachi dinner. Both the chicken and shrimp had great flavor and the chicken was not dry, which I have experienced in many other hibachi restaurants. The fried rice was a little bit different (they seem to use a different sauce) but was excellent!! However, the menu does not clearly state in all hibachi dinner sections that the fried rice is $2 extra. I have never seen an extra fee for fried rice at any other hibachi place I have been to, but the rice was definitely the best I have ever had!! The restaurant was clean and there is ample parking. There is no designated waiting area which caused some confusion. We sit an area with tables and chairs we assumed to be the waiting area (others had done the same) but then a waitress from the bar area came over and asked if we wanted anything, so it was actually the bar area.  The service here is adequate. The hostesses were not rude but were definitely not too friendly. We were brought our drinks and our order was taken but the waiters did not come back once during the meal to see if we needed anything or to see if everything was okay. The chef was pretty good but definitely not as enthusiastic as I have seen elsewhere. We are definitely all coming here again!!!
The best crab I have ever had! Their crab legs and crab rolls are to die for! Great atmosphere and friendly service. I love this place!  You need to check it out!

Had dinner one night and split the tacos for two. Good sized portion, but they failed to tell us that they add an adobe sauce which in our opinion was super spicy. So much that it killed all flavor. The next night we were walking by after dinner and decided to sit outside for a quick drink and try the nachos. After waiting over 30 minutes, the nachos arrived. The delay was due to a banquet that was going on inside. Would have been nice if our waitress would have told us. Once again, the adobe sauce was added heavily...we couldn't eat the nachos. Shame, it's a nice looking restaurant with outdoor seating and good ambiance. But if you don't have a palate for hot food, save your money and go elsewhere.

stellar cocktails, cheese board is wonderful.  I haven't eaten dinner there yet but I plan too.  The staff knows their product, so important for a restaurant.  I enjoy their patio area except for when the dumpster is full behind the building and it smells.

Service was a bit on the slow side despite not being very busy. 14 Dollar burger was incorrectly cooked both tries- ordered medium rare and got a hockey puck. My friend's bizarre fish and pasta dish was rather tasteless. Wouldn't go back again.

We were in the area and celebrating our 25th wedding anniversary and found this restaurant on Yelp! We were pleasantly surprised with not only the food but also the atmosphere. Our waitress Beth was excellent, attentive and personable. If we are in the area again we will return!!

The food was good, not great. The restaurant is crowded and very noisy.  A waiter (not ours) removed our  half full wine bottle from the cooler in the middle of our meal and it had to be retrieved from the kitchen. In all, we were somewhat disappointed.

A hidden gem in my favorite town of Bloomfield! I recently moved here and stumbled upon this place looking for a great steak to eat! My server Sue was extremely polite and knowledgable. The 10oz Pan-seared Filet Mignon was to die for!. Med-rare, melted blue cheese crumbles with port wine reduction over the steak. It was a perfect combination along side of my favorite homemade garlic mashed potatoes. The only place I know that has the strongest cocktails and welcoming staff. This place is just like home!
amazing cappuccinos  ... the black & white crêpe is amazing with yummy fresh berries ... very cute place to sit over coffee with a date or a friend :) i'll definitely be back soon
If you have not been it is a must, excellent meal and nice Borolo wine with dinner. Make it a point to go there if you have not.

Very good pizza and we love the rock shrimp. If they don't have the pizza combination you are looking for, they are willing to do a special pie for you (we love olives and artichokes on a white pie). The inside is a little dated, but the staff is very friendly and it's good for a large group.

So I live in Mass, but my fiancé brought me here (multiple times now) claiming it was the best pizza in the world. Now I don't know about the best pizza in the world, but I have to admit it is some of the best pizza I have ever had. We love the margarita and the simple, yet delicious, original tomato. The pizza is extra crispy and is always served up fast. We also love getting the liters of soda here because its made at a local beverage co nearby! It is also in a great location in downtown New Haven which makes it great for a night out or to get dessert at Libby's right next door! Cons: It is ALWAYS mobbed here, unless you go right at open (11) or randomly during the week. This may seem picky, but the napkins here are horrible lol They basically have no purpose. Also, parking is usually very difficult on a busy night night like Friday or Saturday.
Don't waste your time on this place the staff is rude and very slow service. The BBQ is just ok there are better places in Brooklyn to go.
Good food. At a decent price.  They even made us a request for food. The food also came pretty quickly

The T-bone steak was very nice. It is  seasoned very well and cooked perfectly. The only downside for me is the overwhelming amount of butter. It is a bit heavy. Also, the service is not quite on par. We waited for quite a while just to get salt and pepper.
This is my favorite wraps spot in NYC... Love The Howling.... pumpkin seed & date dough was a unique twist...

After eating the traditional whiz and onion cheesesteak for a couple days around Philly, my friends and I wanted to get something slightly different so we headed to Tommy DiNic's. It was 1pm on a Monday and there was a decently long line but we got through it really fast. The girl taking orders and getting sodas was hustling for sure. I ordered the roasted pork with provalone and hot peppers. This might have been the best sandwich I found in Philadelphia. The meat was unbelievable, it went really well with provalone, and the peppers were blistering hot. Its really nice to order hot peppers at a sandwich shop and get an actual HOT pepper instead of cherry peppers. The rest of the market was really cool too but it would be hard for me to try anything else when I know I can get that sandwich again.
This place is great. My favorite bar and I have been there since the day they opened. Great beer selection. Always something new. Servers are the best and really know there stuff.  Love the burgers!

Can't say I agree with the negative reviews below. This location is consistent with all other Jersey Mikes I've been to. They've never been too busy, even during lunch, and  quite friendly and familiar for a chain. We've always enjoyed their food and consider the "mini" to be large enough for a lunch sized portion.

I got to Peaches Hothouse on a Saturday at 8pm. We had a party of 6 and the place is really small so we had a wait of almost 2 hours. The good thing is they let us order drinks and sip them outside on the bench. We finally got to eat i order the fried green tomatoes- delicious!. I got the fried chicken hot- it wasn't spicy to me. and the mac and cheese which was also really good. Ill be back just won't go on a sat. night with a  large party.

This would probably be OK to good pizza in some place, but in New Haven, with so many great pizzerias, this is just a mediocre pizza fare with mediocre service to boot. I came to pick up my pizza and decided to eat eat there, but regretted it quickly- the place is tiny and people constantly struggle to squeeze past my seat, when I asked for a cup of water I was handed a tiny flimsy plastic cup that the guy filled with lukewarm water from the faucet.  I thought about buyingt a drink from the fridge selection but then noticed they have no recycling bin for plastics or cans, so I decided to pass. Too many places with better service and food in this area to come back here again.

I came here when visiting Hartford, Conn. Firstly, the service was very slow until we had a waiter come over to our table.  Secondly, I thought the cuisine was not what was expected. My boyfriend and I ordered a tomato pie and a caesar salad. The tomato pie was very small for $18 and this should be an appetizer plate instead of under the entrees section. The salad for $9 was not fresh! The lettuce was brown, which should of not! It was loaded with caesar dressing to hide the color as well. Also, our waiter was not very helpful and was very disrespectful as I explained that I was unhappy with the meal. Usually a waiter would be happy to make the customer feel at home and try to resolve any issues. This was not the case! I will not return.

I recently found myself hanging in Brooklyn for the day, and my friend Toni and I wound up at Bijan's at the recommendation of a colleague.  While I usually follow my own favorites, I'm glad I listened this time. The space has a creative vibe and being an artist, I loved that they had abstract impressionism on display.  Didn't even pick up a menu yet and I was like "yessss, like that".   The specialty cocktails are inventive (and tasty).  I don't usually go for a second drink (lightweight!) but I indulged this time, haha. I had the Lime Sumac Chicken and it was amazing, just right. For dessert, I had the Tiramisu, which I was told is a family recipe.  Verdict: To. Die. For. The service was great and how I like it: casual, efficient and not overbearing.  Also bonus was the music selection: eclectic yet fun.   I'll definitely be back!!

I love a good Italian sandwich so when I read the article on Philly.com I knew this was a place I wanted to try. I walk past it on my way to work and today was the day. I walked in to find a modern style deli counter with large paper rolls hanging on the wall with the menu written out. The menu was simple with about 8 sandwiches on it. The Capri caught my eye first since I love fresh mozzarella but after looking at all the choices I went with the Italian Stallion. All fresh Italian meats and cheeses including salami, coppa and sharp provolone served on a seeded Italian roll. The pepperoncini aioli was excellent with the right amount of spice.  It was the right balance of meat, cheese and bread. I will definitely be back to try the Capri and the Uncle G...roasted turkey with crispy pancetta? Yes, please!!

that place Outdoor seating available The place is big so you can seat there chat and chill for hours The food is delicious The Mac and cheese is delicious you must try it It's enough to share And try the peel shrimp I didn't care much for the drinks but the food was delicious Affordable for 2 we spend $110 but we had 2 drinks 2 meals 2 starters and the staff is very friendly Parking is available around  we literally spend 4 hours there chatting

If you are going for Henry's, you should definitely get a delicious homestyle breakfast sandwich served on a bagel with your choice of toppings, any time of day. Usually very busy and you will never be surprised to spot a familiar face when picking up your sandwich. Calling ahead is your best bet!

The best rodizio! My family and I have been coming here forever. Everyone has their birthday here! The sangria is amazing. The menu is huge so it can fit anyone's appetite. Iv tried a few places in the area and Fernandez is for sure the best!

I was surprised to see how high this was rated! Went in shortly after what i'm assuming was a re-opening. My boyfriend and I stopped in a few days after we noticed the place. The staff was friendly, but a bit slow. I have a feeling they were all new. The place was pretty empty early on a Wednesday night and we were sat at a table RIGHT by the door. I didn't think of it until other people started coming in and could just stare at me eating. You could also see the line for Fudruckers at our table. The manager came to greet us with homemade chips. THEY WERE DELICIOUS. Boyfriend ordered a beer and ordered a Sangria. Sangria was actually pretty good, a bit too sweet. Waiter took our order. We both ordered burgers. My first sign to run away was when my waiter didn't ask how I wanted my burger cooked. Food came out at a reasonable pace and was ABSOLUTELY DISGUSTING!!!!!!!!! Considering how pricey this place is i was APPALLED. The menu advertises 100% fresh and homemade ingredients. COMPLETE AND TOTAL LIE. The "kobe" burgers seemed like frozen patties that had marinated in the dirt of the stove-top. It was rubbery and there were charred parts around the edges that I actually thought I chipped my tooth on. Nothing on my burger was fresh. The fries were stale. And gross. I'm usually willing to give things a second chance....not this place.
After going here for many years, I had a really disappointing few experiences.  Ownership didn't seem to care.  I won't be going back, bummer
I go about twice a week for my coffee... Besides the coffee always being so fresh it is great to be greeted at 630 am with a smile... Makes the start of your day even better

It's okay....came here weeknight with friends for dinner and couple drinks. Wed was karaoke night which was mildly entertaining but was still not too crowded with the most random group of customers. Place has two entrances, one for bar and one for restaurant which I didn't really get since they brought you to the same place. Food was average. We ordered salads and wings. I would only come here for beer and bar food for drinks after work. Nothing special. They do have specials each night and coupons going around in papers. We stayed for two hours and had four different waitresses. None of them seemed to care. Don't get me wrong, they did their job and were not rude but again...nothing special. We had to flag them down if wanted something and they brought us check before asking if we were done.
Good happy hour, would definitely visit again!

Charming place. Good tasting food, although very small portions that add up VERY quickly. Small wine pours that make a regular glass of wine 1 & 1/2 times the price of every other place. They claim they're 4 oz pours, but more like 2-2 & 1/2. But wine pours should be 6 oz. not 4 oz to begin with.

Great place that we stumbled upon! I had the pork belly wafco, and it was so delicious! I went with my 2 year old, and while they had bar side seats (no high chairs) they were so sweet to him! Will definitely go back!

I do not get the good reviews- Dry ribs Bland brisket The worst German potato salad ever--- Food sucked! The lighting was so bright I swear I left with a sunburn Beers were cold and they did have a great selection Wine they offered two- One was out So...Merlot only Idk- I'll be back for a beer but definitely not for dinner I really was hoping this place would be great It could be Needs a whole new concept as the BBQ thing simply isn't workin!

I finally got  a chance to come to craft house...if you are looking for some really good comfort food like  beef brisket...chicken&waffles.. mac& cheese etc..you definitely need to try it out. I don't drink but the company I was with said they was very happy with their drinks/ top beer selections.The place is amazing in/out with a nice ambience to it.
Thai girl on UES seeking Thai food. Finds Up. Takes parents. Parents raaaaave, Thai girl scores big. The end. Get: Grilled chicken plus sticky rice Minced chicken basil rice plus egg Crispy pork

By surprise we were there on Taco Tuesday. Five tacos for $4.99. What a treat! We had five tacos de carnitas and five tacos al pastor. They were both scrumptious. A small bag of homemade crispy chips for each was a freebie. Also included were various sauces-- the fiery pickled onion was great. We know where we will be next Tuesday!
The food was great and they gave huge portions of food.  The decor was super sexy and they played fantastic music. My favorite are the stuffed shells, Amazing!!! : )
All the food is solid here, however it's their brazilian/american style burgers that keep me coming back. Check out their desserts as well. And the acai shake!
OMG these are so yummy! I had two vanilla, two strawberry poppy, and two rose petal. At first I was skeptical but after the first bite I was HOOKED!!!! Yum
Really funny how Honest Tom's tacos is down the road from here, but between the two, Cucina has my vote. Best truck in the world, hands down, would definitely recommend.

I give this place one brown star because it sucks sh*t ! It's Dirty and the ADT alarm beeped loud the entire time no waitress or waiters were around we asked was the chef Mexican in their advertised authentic Mexican cuisine and she said he was American the homemade guacamole was bought out of a store tasted like plastic waitress was a b*^ch was mad that we asked if they had Mexican soda acted like she didn't have time to answer question mean while we were the only ones in there we ordered a bunch of food waited 30 minutes no one was around to say it's coming or u want more to drink so we walked out Thumbs down for this place and the pizza place down the way we ate at was fuckkng gross as well dirty and run by junkies it's obvious here in Wilmington or lake placid New York bring ur own food or go to the most expensive restaurants they have so u know u will get a good meal but shop around for ur restaurants walk in inspect ask questions look at menu and wait staff if looks clean and wait staff looks clean give it a whirl! Oh yeah and it's owned and operated by Asians sushi or Mexican same place two menus bahahaha
So good!!

This is a little cozy deli, the food r amazing the bread they use is light and has a slight sweet taste and the tuna salad is divine. Everything is done with care and passion, customer service r friendly and warm welcoming. Definitely recommend to friends and family...

I am only in philly for the second time, so I had never heard of Burgerfi before. However being from New York I am well acquainted with this type of classy burger joint. They have been a new trendy thing popping up everywhere in the NYC area for a few years now. However Burgerfi exceeded my expectations. I was with a group that had food restrictions so we could only order the onion rings and french fries (largest sizes of each) and it was more than enough for the 5 of us to snack on. To make it a little more interesting I asked Shandae (I got the name of the lady at the register because she was that good) for a bunch of the sauces too. Many restaurant workers get annoyed with this kind of request, especially with customers who are just snacking. However not only was Shandae totally cool about it, but I got little sides of alllllll their fry toppings- all the sauces/seasonings, the melted cheese and chilli! After such an amazing experience I cannot wait to return when I can order burgers too. While the food being well above average was part of why my dining experience was so great, it is even more because of how amazing Shandae's service was- the perfect blend of friendly, professional, and understanding!
Nice place great service good food Kind of expensive Had the beef burger on gluten free bun w/ sweet potato fries & a side of the house mustard.

Although it's a bit pricey it's so worth every penny.  I go often and have never had a bad meal or bland anything.  Always 3+ vegan baked goods in my experience.  Love the atmosphere.  My kids love it here, too... 8&5.  Highly recommend supporting this local joint

We like this for delivery- food is good, but the few times we've eaten at the restaurant the service was lacking. The thin crust pizza and house salad are tasty (tip- must ask for the dressing mixed in for the salad ). The cheesy garlic bread is a good value when getting delivery for the family.
Great stop! Perfect coffee, delicious baked goods, clean restroom, ve

Went to cafeteria at 10:40pm on a Wednesday night with a table of 5, walked in and there were about 5-7 empty tables in the restaurant and told by the hostess that it was a 20 minute wait.  When I questioned him he said that they only had two tables for large parties because the plates were too big and didn't fit on other tables. We decided to wait anyway and while we waited the manager continuously told us to move out of the entry way. When I questioned him about why we couldn't be seated he said that they were a high volume restaurant and couldn't move tables together for us because their drunk inebriated customers who were going to come in in an hour were more valuable. Extremely disappointed and will not return.

Yelp, please change the price to "$$$".  There is no way that this is "$$", that and indication of cheap, but this place isn't cheap at all.  I order 10 piece of sushi, and ended up with a $35 bill.  That's $7 for an order of 2 piece, may be Sushi at Newark is expensive.  I live in SF, even SFO sushi bar is not this pricy.

I hate how the place isn't so easy to find, but hearing good things about it, I went there with a friend, and it was WELL worth the trip. It's a classic "family-oriented" diner with amazing burgers and fries, as well as the best omelette I've ever had. I would DEFINITELY recommend the san diego omelette.

This has got to be the best pizza I have ever tasted in my life. The spinach artichoke pizza has a great crust with so much flavors. I'm from Boston and I dream of this pizza! The wait staff is super friendly and the ambience is a real chill spot. The beer I remembered was very cheap for a large size.

It was my first time in Philly and I came here with a friend during my short stay. The happy hour $3 drink deal with oysters was perfect after my long day in a conference hall listening to who knows what. I ended up having the steak for dinner which was done well and huge. Definitely got more than what I paid for. Their beer selection is all decent.

FINALLY!!!!! GOOD latin food in this area!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Visited this spot with the hubby on Friday night and I was very impressed with the service and food. This establishment just opened, so I know it will just keep getting better in time. I appreciate wait staff that are attentive and food plates that are big enough to get you full! Thank you Jora, we will be back!!
Chicken cutlets are great and awesome catering trays. It is on the expensive side, but you get what you pay for. The fresh mozzarella is great

Best prices for lunch! They have set menus everyday of the week from 12-3pm that is $7.50 for a soup or salad, an entree and a drink. How can you go wrong with the deal! I have come here a million times especially for the chicken it is the best! Oh and the Lomo Saltado too definitely can't forget about that. Will continue to come back for a long time!
I had the fish n chips and was probably the best I ever had...different choices of tarter sauce too.

This review is long overdue. My husband and I love this place. Mostly because we love the escargot appetizer. They have other wonderful dishes as well like the seared filet mignon topped with foie gras and the seafood linguini. This restaurant is BYOB which is a also a plus. But I'm hearing that they have started their own wine menu recently. Only thing is that its very noisy inside and can be a bit crowded at times. Its also better to make a reservation.
The turkey samich place is mmmm....drool worthy!

Carmela's pizza is the real deal. If you want true Italian pizza, hand crafted, by a true Italian, look no further. Rick and his wife came direct from Italy and opened this family operated establishment. The love good food, and they love making good food. When good people, with a passion for food open a restaurant, there is nothing but gourmet bliss. I live in Texas, where Chuckie Cheese is essentially the pizza standard, but I grew up in CT so I know a good pizza. Hands down, this is without a doubt, the BEST pizza in CT, and quite possibly New England. Don't let the location, or the modest decor fool you; these guys know what they are doing.

Came here with my wife for dinner shortly after arriving in Hartford with the train from NYC. We were promptly seated outside which was enjoyable. She ordered a salad which was drenched in dressing and otherwise rather tasteless. I had the meatloaf, which was terrible. The food was too cold, the meatloaf was bland and lacked spices, and the beans were unsatisfying. Mashed potatoes alone did not cut it for me .... Next time I would try another place before coming here again. We left disappointed.

Family and I stopped in and ordered a bit of everything.   The scallion pancakes are excellent as are the fried dumplings.    We shared a table with a mother and daughter from England,  so if you enjoy a social aspect to dinning this is a great place.    As a reminder bring cash.
Owner is awesome. Food is delicious. Ambience is solid. All good in the hood.
Awesome food!

Cute BYOB with a hidden little patio in the back. The pizza is very good- interesting combinations and we've loved them all. The sausage fontina pie was our favorite so far, and the special pie with corn was delicious. The meatballs are excellent and the special salads are always really fresh and out of the ordinary.
The best pizza and Spumoni ice cream know to MAN! Such a Brooklyn Staple and with good reason! Love this place!
Funnel Cake good!

Just had lunch today with a friend. I have visited Georgia, and the quality of the dishes is absolutely on par with the local cuisine. We had some eggplant salad, the khinkali (small dumplings) and a khachapuri (like a pizza filled with cheese and eggs on top). Reasonable pricing, great service and a good atmosphere, with a back garden that would be great for taking someone on a date.
