They have a wine menu, very important on a restaurant from a country that claims to have invented wine. It's a shame they don't have Georgian beers, but maybe that is asking too much. Even though they could have had a more traditional decoration, I highly recommend this place.
Mushroom Swiss Cheese Burger with GoldBurger's special sauce DEEEELISH!!! Perfectly done!

It is always a great thing to see the red Hong's cart on church street. Fresh and extremely delicious dumplings made right in front of you. This can mean a line and a wait, but if your hungry and in the mood for these yummy dumplings definitely worth your time.

Wow- has this place gone downhill! My family has been going to the Townhouse since before I was born and they were originally located in New Haven. As a child we would always grab quick family meals at their old location in Branford. The food was great (especially the seafood dishes) and all of the staff, including the members of the family who own the restaurant, were always so warm and friendly. We were heartbroken when they were forced to suddenly close at their old location, but were beyond excited when they re-opened at their current spot. Unfortunately that amazing service that was previously offered at their old location did not transfer to the new one. Although their food has remained pretty good, the service has seriously gone downhill. Due to the poor customer service, i.e. some of the waitresses were very impatient and stand-offish when taking our orders and would be snide when pointing out when our meals had come out wrong, we decided to stop going in for meals and resorted to doing take-out. But tonight was the "straw that broke the camels back" moment. I placed an order for two hot-opened faced turkey sandwiches, but when we sat down at home to eat we realized we had been given pot roast instead of turkey. I called the Townhouse to let them know of the mistake. The father of the family who owns the restaurant answered (someone I have become a familiar with as a loyal customer since childhood) and he had remembered taking my order but repeatedly insisted that I had told him roast beef- which isn't what we had gotten anyways. When I told him that I was certain I ordered turkey he became quite hostile and kept saying to me "Well, what do you want me to do about?"Realizing that he was not a believer in the "customer is always right" motto I let him know of my family's disappointment in the direction his business has been heading and that I would no longer be ordering from them. And while I do not think the Parthenon's food is quite as good as the Townhouse-sigh-I will be ordering my turkey sandwiches and all other diner food cravings from them from here on out, just to avoid having to fight with someone to get what I originally ordered.

I went in for brunch and had the pork roll sandwich with an avocado on it, and it was delicious. It also came with home fries that were great. The service was also prompt and not overwhelming. I also got a coffee and a wheat beer to accompany the meal. Would go back.

Went here for the first time and I gotta say the food was very good and the view of the city was amazing..  Our waitress was very nice and made sure we had everything we wanted and more..  I will be returning in the near future for sure.

Now Il Falco is open in LIC.  WOW!  The atmosphere is crisp and clean...old world Italian elegance.  The food, service, staff and atmosphere was top notch!  High-end Italian food with a loving flare!  It is a must if you are in Queens!

My friends and I went to The Happy Rooster for dinner last Thursday night and had a great experience. We were greeted with nothing but kindness and our food was PHENOMENAL! I had the veal chop which was the best I have ever had, my friends had the lobster rolls and fish tacos - all three meals were outstanding. We moved to the bar after dinner to enjoy some cocktails and our bartender Diane was so sweet and attentive. I cannot say enough good things about the service and the food at this place. I will definitely be going back.

My family of 5 ate at this restaurant last night.  The atmosphere was cool.  Sports bar all the way.  Beer menu was good.  Make sure you get the 16oz of beer for $1 more.  The food...well....three of us ordered the corned beef dinner with cabbage and potato.  We were all VERY disappointed!  The corned beef was shredded (not sliced) and not moist.  It was basically a small shredded pile along with a few very wilted pieces of cabbage and 1 small potato (hard) cut up set in a bowl of hot water.  The price was $9.99 which was reasonable but I would have rather they charge a bit more and give you a better meal!  My husband ordered the Reuben with slaw and loved it. My daughter ordered a pulled pork sandwich which was just okay.  Overall the place was just okay but a disappointment.  Stick to the beer/bar thought process and forget the restaurant for the supposed Irish dinner.  Shame!

I went back to Taim last night and it was as delicious as ever! All of the falafel flavors are vibrant, the bread is soft but absorbent, and the sauces are incredible. The prices can't be beat either. It's very cramped inside, but grab a falafel and eat on the street.
I had the chicken bacon ranch wrap and it was very tasty. There is minimal seating and no facilities, but a great place to stop while wandering church st.
Maybe the best pizza in New Haven. Best sauce at the very least. Always makes me happy in my fat belly.
best pizza in brooklyn!!!  ...(enough said!!!)
great patio, the friendlist owner, and some tremendous beers. christy's makes me a happy, fat baby.

We went to On20 with friends at the end of August to help them celebrate an anniversary. I had been there for lunch with a friend before and at that time the experience could not have been more perfect. This time it was far less so. The food was excellent and well portioned. I got the fish and everything was cooked to perfection. They also took care of my gluten restrictions so gracefully. But my friends ordered the pork and reported later that it was surprisingly tough. The real problem was the pacing of the meal was off. Though we mentioned we wanted wine with dinner, perhaps because we ordered from the Prix Fixe menu, the food came out and we were never offered another chance to order wine. The server was young and seemed very inexperienced. The dinner felt rushed when earlier it had been leisurely, with time between courses. The worst part - the cocktails were terrible. Worst Cosmo I've ever had. And yep - I'm kicking myself for not sending it back.  I've run into this recently where it seems that young bartenders don't tend to drink what they serve. My friends Margarita was terrible as well. Martinis are a pretty simple thing to make and make well. (I confess my husband is a former bartender from the old school.) But I didn't think it was a lot to expect a good one in a place that prides itself on excellence. As with any dining experience I think you have to balance cost and what is possible. So here's the grade for the other night. Drinks -F, Food - A/B+, Service-C, Atmosphere - A+. Don't get me wrong - I will try this place again -because the food is terrific - but if it do I may not do the Prix Fixe. I think the experience may improve. And next time - I'll tell them how to make the drinks. :)
healthy and tasty.

When I have worked a twelve hour day, having to listen to the wretched person behind the bar where I sat because even though there were plenty of empty tables that remained empty during my brief visit to this place that embodies all that is wrong in the new york dining scene, tell me that she did not get me the glass of water I asked for three times because she had "17 other things to do." Whatever, I get it, but it's not like I hadn't already ordered a bottle of wine. But even if I hadn't - it's your job.  Just do it.  Don't complain.  I am not the cause of the 17 other things you have to do - which given how slow the restaurant was, well, it's just completely laughable.  Her glacial pace may have actually led to her having 17 things to do, but when I ask for a glass of water for the third time, just please give it to me, and spare me the behind the scenes BS. Was so upset because when I challenged this 17 task juggler, she made me feel like I was wrong, that I gave my friend with whom I was dining my credit card, left my meal and wine on the bar and went home. So, brava, you won.   And, if the best thing a place has going for it is a burger, bearnaise, toast, wtf, they really need to step up the service.

My husband and I went there on Sunday night because we were already on the area. The food was delicious and the service was very friendly. I recommend the kale salad, sweet potato au gratin and the chicken, although they said there menu changes frequently bases on what's in season.  Restaurant is small and tables are close together.
Great food great people great all around. Highly recommend this place. Never had anything I didn't like!!!

Check out my blog at whatsaachisays.blogspot.…! Now on to the review, I'm not sure if this is a hidden gem, but Galli was amazing! Located on Mercer street in Soho,a perfect comfort Italian meal to end or start of your day. I would say end just because the vibe at this restaurant is really cool. As you enter, a narrow path with dim lights some even red, comes a bar and then a huge space for seating in the back. Brick walls, accommodations for large parties and small, and plenty of hip hop R&B  music in the back to go along with the meal, could that be a more ideal dinner place? The menu is simple and not full of a hundred different dishes, You have your basic appetisers, salads, a speciality in calamari and parm, mains, and then pastas which looks like a pretty balanced menu if you ask me! OH and don't forget the dessert. Here is what we ordered: FREE BREAD- and it refills... Mozz Chips $11- This may sound super typical and you may ask the question of why we ordered greasy mozzarella sticks at a nice restaurant? They were SO heavenly. WOW. the cheese was melted perfectly, breaded to perfection it did not even feel oily or greasy. The pomodoro sauce was the perfect compliment, made it feel more elegant. Penne Vodka- This was by far my favourite dish, and solely the reason I would recommend this restaurant to other people. Sometimes you get pasta and the restaurant is greedy with their sauce leaving your pasta to dry, but this had plenty of sauce, plenty of flavor, and the perfect vodka sauce I was looking for. Fussilli Pollo- Garlicky, Chickeny (is that a word?) with a little bit of greens, this dish also looked super appetising. Everything was sweeped clean. My friend said the chicken was moist and great and the pasta oozed of garlic which she loves! NOTE: The portions are really big! One pasta can definitely feed three people so be cautious of when you order! We unfortunately were too full to try the dessert but the tiramisu sounded great! also NOTE: the restaurant is noisy, so if you want a quiet dinner this is not the place for you! One thing I need to complain about is the bathroom, it was not very sanitary. The servers were very attentive, sometimes a little too attentive, but always asking us if we wanted something more, they refilled our bread immediately and got us any toppings as soon as we asked. Nonetheless, Great meal on an average Tuesday night!
Whoops wrong place. My bad :-/

So love this place.. I came here by myself around 2 pm and got sitted right away while people are still waiting in couples or group outside. I didn't know what to order so I ask the service for recommends so she said take the spicy miso with pork, ok done due.. After tasting the first sip of the soup I felt like I was in heaven the soup was so rich and flaverful and the noodles were perfect aldente.. I definitely recommend this place if you love ramen.

We went for the "deal" and ended up spending a lot more - more than I normally pay for a dinner out. But it was because everything was so good! Get the Happy Hour special. And the salads. And mussels. Great food.
Great food, excelent service...a quiet place if  you are tired of the crowded timesquare!

Went to Omar's today for lunch. Found a parking spot right out front.  The neighborhood felt safe and I liked being able to see my car from inside the restaurant. The guy behind the counter was friendly and quick to take my order.  After thinking about getting a fresh juice I ended up ordering a Cuban sandwich and a cappuccino instead. Oh Good Grief - they were both DELICIOUS. The cappuccino came while I was waiting for the Cuban and it was ridiculously good - topped with whipped cream and a dusting of cinnamon. Tasted like they put something extra in it to make it extra delicious but I'm not sure what (evaporated milk maybe?).  Then the Cuban sandwich came. They were premade so it really only took a few minutes. It was crispy and buttery and flavorful to the max. The meat was obviously seasoned for a while before going into the sandwich and the cuts of meat were thin and tender. I'm not a big meat eater - not a fan ethically and also because I don't particularly like the taste - but this was melt in your mouth deliciousness.   I'll be going back and trying other things - can't wait!

Every time I think they've thought of it all they amaze me again.  I just had a focaccia pizza sandwich from pizza one and it was absolutely incredible.  I will never go to another pizza place as long as pizza one is around.  Everything from their menu to staff is excellent but their creativity with pizza is absolutely phenomenal.  If you haven't tried it I feel really bad for you.

FOH Staff = Excellent. Probably best in town. our water glasses were refilled many times. our server checked in on us appropriately. the hostesses did not forget about us while we were waiting and notified us as the status of our table a couple of times. First impressions - The salsa they give you is the smallest portion of salsa ever... my guess is its 1-2 tablesppons at most. I definitely don't mind a long wait if the food is worth it (like at Sushihana) however, the food at villalobos was lack luster at best.  I ordered 3 tacos - al pastor, tinga, and camarones.  the chicken in the tinga taco tasted like it was simmered in Campbell's tomato soup and was weirdly dry.  all of the tacos were dry. perhaps if they gave you a tiny bit more salsa we could have used that to. I wont be back. Casa Piquin blows this place out of the water (even with that strange smell).

Disappointment at best... both service & food were sub par. Service: slow waitstaff, confused about who was our waitress because many people came to our table, they didn't refill our water glasses or chips, waitress brought out wrong food and on top of that it was cold. Food: We ordered the traditional guacamole which was the highlight of our meal. Along with this we also ordered the chicharrones (crispy pork skin) which was incredibly hard to even bite into, it tasted stale and my friend couldn't even take a bite it was that hard... we sent those back to the kitchen and they took it off our bill. The time in between the appetizer and our mains (we ordered taco) was ridiculously long. I don't mind waiting in a restaurant for food, but when it comes out less than lukewarm and tastes like it was cooked the day before I get upset. We had the chicken, pork, fish, and shrimp tacos which were all unmemorable. Overall the staff looked confused and were not prepared, good idea for a restaurant but the menu was not executed well. I feel bad because it's the opening week, hopefully the staff are able to sort out these issues.

Villalobos is an excellent Mexican restaurant in the heart of downtown Montclair. Yesterday I ordered the fish & verduras tacos and a margarita (virgin but they are BYOB). The verduras taco was quite tasty. The corn was fresh & crisp and had the right amount of smoke. The fish taco was battered and topped with cole slaw. Their house-made tortillas taste even better than the ones at a typical Mexican food cart. Both accompanying salsa's (salsa verde and regular salsa) were fresh, well seasoned and authentic. I actually ended up ordering the same thing for lunch today along with an order of guacamole that was legit. It's really dangerous working directly next door to them so I'll have to schedule my visits. Adam, the owner, is a great dude. Go, you won't be disappointed!

Love this place! A wonderful addition to the neighborhood - casual, affordable, and really delicious, fresh food and great staff and service to boot. We've both eaten in and gotten delivery - I always get the fish taco and the garlic shrimp - YUM! The chicken tostada is great too. Guacamole and torta milanesa are other favorites. My kids love this place too. A family owned business that I'm happy to support!

I went back to McLadden's to see if my first good experience could be repeated. This is a fun place and has a great atmosphere. I've read lots of the positive and less than positive reviews. I can understand the criticisms but I think those writers are unrealistic. This is a place that is really trying. The staff are all smiling and helpful and look pretty busy. The beer selection is great and the food is good. The French onion soup is delicious and the sandwiches were really good. (Once I had fish and chips that I wasn't crazy about - too soggy) The personality of a restaurant is important for me - even more than the food. (The kitchen is the lowest point in this pub.) This feels like an Irish pub where families, singles, and couples are all welcome and comfortable. Whenever I am in the area, I am going to go here.

Went there last night for a friend's birthday.  There were four of us and we arrived at 6:30 and were seated immediately.  Young woman who sat us was all smiles and very welcoming. We looked through menu and decided on roti canai and crispy wontons for our appys.  There were both hot and delicious.  We shared four entrees , Pad Thai with Seafood, Black Pepper Beef, Pattaya Ginger Chicken, and Crispy Basil Chicken.  Each had a unique flavor and was prepared and presented nicely.  The seafood in the Pad Thai was not plentiful but the noodles were delicious.  I would order with chicken next time.  The Pattaya Ginger Chicken was fresh and light. We all enjoyed passing and sharing!  We finished with the mango coconut flan for the group to taste.  Pretty presentation and very tasty.  Prices are reasonable.  Our bill was 85.00 for all the above which I consider a bargain.  It is a BYOB so we all enjoyed our favorite wine with dinner.  I would definitely return again!!

It takes a special kind of finesse, skill, & attention to even the most minute details to be able to realize an authentic Italian dining experience here in the U.S. Rizzuto's does this...flawlessly. Having grown up in Italy, where authenticity is the fundamental ingredient in the creation of all meals whether made in a modest country farm house or in a Michelin-rated Milanese restaurant, I'd like to think I have a penchant for all things Italian...especially when it comes to food. (In other words, if I might suggest, modestly, that I'm a credible source- which is dubious in the case of many yelpers!) The beginning of this summer was my first introduction to rizzutos. I was invited for pre-drinks at a nearby venue, and we then carried on into rizzutos to take advantage of their happy hour menu.  First impressions are everything. The GM, a very hands-on, articulate guy, John, ushered us into the bar area and introduced us to a bartender, Jen, and told us she would accommodate us in any way. Excellent first impression. The aroma from the wood fire was intoxicatingly delicious. Just. Like. Italy. The wine selection spoke to the owner's (Bill I believe his name is whom I have yet to meet and would love to hear his story!) awareness of Italian fine wines...with some very fine Barolos. The open, limitless feeling of the interior space was reminiscent of a roman restaurant...vibrant, colorful and full of energy. The happy hour bites were extremely reasonable and were absolutely delicious...the little savory dishes abided by American happy hour conventions, but maintained an Italian flare...which my guests and I appreciated. I've been back a few times for dinner, and wi continue to do so. It's a place I now insist in taking all my foodie friends and family. The cheese plate was also indicative of the well informed chef & owner. Sourcing not only Italian delicacies like the dreamy burrata, but also an homage to local artisans like Cato corner right here in colchester ct. For dinner...one must try the braised veal osso buco which is heavenly adorned with goat cheese infused polenta and (my favorite!) kale! The pastas, in particular the pappardelle are made in house, and are terribly authentic. I rarely take the time to expend this amount of effort to extol the virtues of something...but this place is most certainly deserved of it.

Great service, great food and drinks, and the inside of the restaurant is beautiful! The prices for tapa and drinks is very reasonable and great quality, especially compared to other tapas places in the ironbound. Great if you want to catch a game at the bar or have a romantic dinner in the back restaurant.

Brought my family here for dinner and we were thoroughly stuffed before our entrees arrived. The servings for their appetizers were actually enough to be a considered a meal. They also served us a generous amount of bread. I tried their ribs with sweet and spicy tomato sauce and it was so delicious. It was actually a new taste I have never had before. I usually do not deviate from the more familiar tastes, but this was a great new discovery for me. I am eager to return here for this same treat or perhaps go on another adventure with their menu. We arrive at the restaurant at seven in the evening on a Friday and we were able to get a table for four without any wait. The other popular Greek restaurant across the street appeared to have a much longer wait. This place is certainly worth trying if you appreciate Mediterranean foo.

Get the sticky buns, you wont regret it. I don't understand all the negative reviews for waiting time, I'm a frequent here (as I work down the block), and all hours of the day I never see any lines, or when I do, everyone is served quickly. Really good on the wallet as well, when it came time to assess the damage done to me, came out to $15 for a really filling meal. Would definitely recommend.

Pork dumplings and the peppers.. Obviously show up early as it's always packed. If you like Raamen, definitely a great choice. I also recommend hitting up the small bar in the front of the house, great bar tenders! HOLLER WITH A DOLLAR, pW

A local hangout with good food and a great selection of draft beers, where you are likely to meet your friends and be served by your next door neighbor's son or daughter, who probably played in the marching band or sang in choir with your kids.  It's that kind of place. .

My wife and I had a NJ Transit layover in Rahway, so we decided to find a local spot to eat. We discovered the Rail House, which is across the street from the train station.  Food was excellent. The only flaw was the service, a little slow.

Excellent ramen + great atmosphere. The restaurant is usually crowed with a long wait if you have a group larger than 2. The chicken buns were a little spicy but tasty. And since I was in a chicken mood, ordered the ramen with chicken (add the egg for $2 more). This was some of the best flavorful ramen I've had in a long time. Highly recommended.

I was excited to try The Eddy for dinner after I saw the review on Tasting Table.  The service/ atmosphere/ food itself was great.  Nevertheless, I cannot recommend eating dinner here due to the price to portion value.  I finished my dinner plate with 4 forks full of food.  This is not the restaurant to go hungry to.  My friend and I had to go to another restaurant after to get a more fulfilling meal.

The food was OK but should have been better.  I also felt that we were nickel and dimed on some items, which at these prices should not happen.  Monkey Bread was good BUT with $30 plus entrees there should be some bread that you don't have to pay for (Colicchio and Sons at the same prices has the same type of fresh baked bread for free as an example).  Also, we were grossly overcharged for gin and tonics $15 per gin and then $5 EXTRA for tonic (which was cheapo Seagram's tonic) - $20 for a gin and tonic is not cool ever especially when its flat and nothing special.  The lamb I ordered as an entree was cold.  It did not say it was a cold dish.  The veggies were hot on the plate, but the lamb had obviously not been made fresh.  I told the waiter that the lamb was cold.  It came back lukewarm and the plate was burning hot, obviously they just stuck it in the oven.  It was inedible.  So while some may have a great meal here, beware that they may cut some corners and they to charge you more than they should.

Let me start out by admitting a bias.  I don't like more West Hartford eateries.  Most are pretentious, and are over-priced for 2nd-rate food and drink. Noodles & Co. breaks that mold.  The service is down to Earth.  Extremely polite.   The food is excellent.  I usually get the noodles with vegetables, and/or soup.  The veggies are always fresh and delicious, the noodles always cooked just right.  The soup is equally excellent.   The beverages: their coffee is excellent, as are their bottled cold drinks.  If there's one thing I can fault Noodles & Co. on, it's their cold drinks machine.  It's one of those you see at more and more establishments now, where you can mix and match dozens of varieties of sodas, waters, flavors.  It's not awful, but it's not as good as the actual products are if purchased from dedicated machines or in bottles or cans.   Outdoor dining is on a nice little patio, with some cool gas-fired torches that add not only ambiance, but light and warmth.  Thank God there's no TV anywhere to be found. I'd also rate Noodles & Co. an excellent value.  So we have down-to-Earth, friendly, professional personnel... excellent food... excellent coffee... an excellent value... what's THIS place doing in West Hartford?  (Answer: being special.) Phil

This is my first time here. I had the special: Chipotle bacon cheeseburger with crispy onions. It was delicious, cooked just right. And the hand-cut fries were perfect. The service was friendly and attentive. My son had the Apple-brie burger,  and while he's not great with descriptions, he devoured it. This is a great place in a convenient location. And the prices were extremely reasonable, especially considering the quality and size of the portions.
Affordable healthy gourmet food. Excellent!
The food is fantastic. Nice service.
One of the best restaurants in nyc.  Get there early and stay late.

Great American style food with fresh ingredients from around the Colchester area along with nice homey environment. I believe that the cooks and other employees are very professional but also very fun and nice.
Fine dining experience, excellent service - portions are adequate (not too much or too less), can get a bit pricey when combined with starter, drunk and  a dessert. But overall a good experience.

I am a HUGE fan of customer service.  This place has been in business for 11 years and they are proud of their "art".  For them, it is not just a function of financial gain or means, it is customer oriented experience and a zen environment.  Equally as important!  The food was really tasty and carefully prepared.  We quite enjoyed the stuffed chicken wings (a first for us), then we also had black pepper shrimp and the ginger chicken dish, both excellent!  They take the time to grow their herbs fresh and pride themselves in bringing forth authentic flavor.  It's truly a hidden gem.  I hope they never change their baseline as they grow, which is wonderful personalities and well prepared cuisine.  We plan to go again on ladies night very soon!

I really love The Monk Room. The Caesar salad is heavenly with the whole anchovies and the maple dessert is super tasty. I've sampled a few of their other dishes with nothing but happiness and indulged in a few yummy Snowbird cocktails.  It's probably the closest place I've found in Newark that's hipster (IPA's on tap!) - which I sort of like :-) My only suggestion/concern: the prices are a bit high. If this was in Hoboken or on Grove Street the prices would be fine. And the place is inexpensive compared to NYC. But for downtown Newark, where there's a lot of gov't and non-profit workers, it's a bit much. The price definitely limits how often I go - especially with other places in the immediate area offering $2 drink specials and much cheaper salads. Maybe have a half price lunch or dinner? Or offer happy hour specials that include  food?
The mood is very chic and welcoming. The food is delicious but the portions are soooo small! It is a great spot if you are in the area and want to enjoy a meal with friends.
Highly recommend this place food was excellent. We had the lamb sand which and chicken pasta both were fresh and the prices were awesome between 9-16$ per meal
No introduction is necessary. The lamb over rice is my poison and have never been dissapointed.

Thought this was a cool looking pub from the street, so we decided to come  in and have a few drinks and supper. It wasn't particularly busy, so it was surprising that there was no hostess or staff to greet the four of us. We just sat ourselves down at an open table and went to the bar to order our own drinks. Eventually the waitress came over with menus.  We had burgers, buffalo wings, and a chicken caesar. Sadly, I had to send one of the burgess back because it was overcooked and then had to wait a long time to get a replacement. Bummer. The fries were pretty good, admittedly, but on the whole, the meal and service was average. They seemed indifferent to us being there. I don't get it.

Ordered the veal marsala. The veal was a little tough and the pasta overcooked. Called it in as a to go order and arrived 25 minutes later and still had to wait 15 minutes. I could see if it was packed but it was 8:00 on a Tuesday night.

Absolute favorite neighborhood place to go for great tapas.  The menu is very creative and every plate tastes delicious.  I love coming here with a group of 5-6 people and sharing a whole bunch of different tapas dishes.  HIGH RECOMMEND!
The hibachi was on the salty side for me but the sushi is some of the best I've had! Definitely coming back for the sushi!!

Ehhhhh the cheesesteak is forgettable, definitely tourist trappy. I didn't try Pat's so I can't compare but I probably won't go back to try them either. Also not a huge fan of the over the top ~patriotism~ theme going on here but to each his own.

First of all, you have to try their homemade butter! As good as it gets!! I tried the cinnamon and the pumpkin and both were absolutely to die for! I got the pancakes based off a former recommendation and I was definitely not let down (especially coupled with the homemade butter)! The bacon and eggs were great, too but after tasting all of them, I was especially impressed with the pancakes! Also, the coffee was delicious as well! The place is small and sort of crowded, but it fits the restaurant itself. There are so many things to look at on the walls and it got voted the greenest storefront in 2009 and 2004 (I think those were the years at least). I'm not from here so I loved watching all the people and the noise going through the restaurant! You will not be disappointed going to Tom's, promise!

This was my first time trying Jahan Kabob & grill and it was amazing!!! I had the falafel pita with French fries (the lunch special) it is the best falafel I have ever had!! The combination of flavors from the hummus and tzatziki plus the fresh vegetables was perfect!! The fries were even amazing. I will definitely be  going back again and would recommend this place to anyone. The restaurant itself is very clean and looks nice.

After reading these reviews, we figured this place would be a great place to go for a bite. We walked in and the place was empty and the woman was reading a book at one of the booths. She had us seat ourselves in the dark dining room. All the tables were dirty and sticky but at this point it was too late to turn around and leave. The food was edible but was not very great. I got the chicken francese and the sauce was way too creamy and thick. The older man and woman were arguing in the front during our entire meal. Horrible experience, bad food, won't go back.

all in all my favorite indian restaurant in new haven. I have got to say I love their buffet special. my favorite dish on here is the chicken tikka masala. I've been to indian restaurants all around but none are as good as at zaroka.
10/10! Great food, great service, affordable! Quick! A Cuban sandwich a day will keep my hangover at bay! Go check it out! So worth it! The meat melts in your mouth. And that garlic sauce

We don't go to NYC often anymore, so when we do, we look for a good place to eat. Based on what I read about Hu Kitchen, this was our choice for lunch today. It was a HUge mistake. And not an inexpensive one. I had what was reviewed as this amazing vegan lasagna - the Grandmaster Veg - that was supposed to have eggplant, carrot, green cabbage, cashew, marinara, garlic and chili flake. What I had was a lasagna look alike thing that had a ton of shredded carrots, onions, what I suspect was a vegan cashew cheese substitute, some traces of marinara, and whatever made up the dark tasteless topping. I had some curried cauliflower on the side which was tasty but cold. My wife and son both had rotisserie chicken that was no different than what we can make at home with a side of mixed veggies that were simply sauteed mixed veggies. Both bland and everyday. A huge place where you order like a cafeteria and hope to find a seat because the place is packed. Mostly younger professionals who get upset and roll their eyes when you ask them to move their large, expensive leather bags so you can sit down and then proceed to occasionally glance at you, roll their eyes, and move their bag closer to them while you eat. (O.K., that's pretty much descriptive of most places in NY now.) The staff were neither friendly nor unfriendly. They just put the stuff on the plate. Its impossible to really get any questions about the product answered since they're in a rush to serve the next person like any cafeteria. Oh, well. Live and learn. There are probably 15 other vegetarian / vegan places in the same neighborhood. They don't have to worry.

Obao is a bustling little kitchen that has provocative style with spicy dishes to entertain everyone. The interior of the space features raw elements: wood logs line the walls with monolithic panels of mirror and linear lacquer paneling. Its a contemporary aesthetic that looks to be a reinterpretation of the 5 classical elements. My boyfriend and I visited Obao, he looked into exotic flavors and found Obao to be tantalizing based on their offerings. He ordered Lak Sa, a colorful mildly-spiced soup with large fresh noodles and whole chunks of shrimp. I took a taste, it was amazing. A sharp flavor with a warm touch. It was delicious. I ordered the Vietnamese Pork Chop which featured white rice, veggies and a vinegar based sauce that complemented the softer flavors wonderfully. The pork was cooked to perfection with colorful grill marks and just the right amount of moisture for a succulent dish. Our only qualm was about service turnaround. The waitstaff are well informed, polite, and very friendly. However the time it took to receive our check and my card back was a little long. Long enough to casually finish our drinks. So in conclusion, if you're looking for an exotic escape in flavor, Obao is just what you're looking for.
Great iced coffee!!  Yummy egg sandwich.  Spacey dining area with free WiFi.  Probably the nicest people in Philly work there.
Had brunch and lunch here. Good food. Come with an appetite,or you'll be so stuffed. Fast service. Awesome Bloody Mary menu.
Consistent and delicious. You can't go to Princeton and not eat here.
14 for slice pork? 17 for chicken? No no Go get something else. Not recommend ! Not come back

Have always ordered pizza for pickup since I live locally and after recently always will, was with another couple for a long evening it was early around 1015pm when I tried to get a pie after a few drinks when your little hissy fit host, wanted to charge me my wife and the couple we were with $6 a head for a cover for some metal band in the back, that's $24 before I even order a pie !!!!!?I told him repeatedly I'm just here for pizza, I asked him how can I get to eat without paying a cover charge, instead of solving the problem and handing me a menu while I stood behind to front door red-faced he replied you can call in, yes he is right but what the hell type of service is this !?!? After  exchanging some words he started flicking his fingers towards a server who I'm guessing was busy working for her to go fetch a menu, it was then I walked out the door, can't stand laziness, this would never happen at pepes lucky you have good pizza
beautiful decoration inside with great relaxing atmosphere. The fried rice with thai tea is the best combo for me
Food was fresh and very flavorful.   My group was really happy with their orders and I really liked the tacos so much I had 8.  It's a good place to stop in and get your Mex-On.

Food is great service is great they have an awesome beef tips and caprese salad the fried brussel sprouts are unbelievable the bacon and blue mussels were amazing. They make a great makers mark Manhattan.
There is no better place to get macarons in NYC! My favorites were the vanilla and salted caramel. It's definitely worth a stop if you're in the city!

We used to LOVE Chengdu 23 a couple of years ago but it has gone totally downhill.  The last 3 times there, the meals have been horrible.  Tonight we were served hot and sour soup with a chunk of ginger that looked like an octopus and it was the size of  my pointer finger!  The beef dish we ordered - I would swear it was not beef.  It was mealy and did not seem like beef.  Who knows what it was??  My husband complained and at least we didn't have to pay for it.  We are both home with really bad stomach aches.  Don't go!!!!!

WOW!!!!!! I am business man who travels all over the world and I was stopping buy a local business in the corporate center, I was looking for a place to get a quick lunch and stumbled upon Cranberrys Goumet Cafe. It was a large place that was very clean and bright! It took me a while to order because the menu was very extensive, I ordered a Chicken salad sandwich!!  WOW!! was it big! I took one bite and WOW was it delicious!! The best chicken salad sandwich I ever had! I couldn't finish half of it so I took it home for later. My 16 year old son ate it and wondered where I got it because his word "awesome" I told him up in Cranberry, NJ exit 8A, we live off exit 2 he was bummed it was so far away. But next time I am traveling on the turnpike and going by exit 8A I am popping in and bringing home some sandwiches. Love this place!!
Don't order the grilled cheese. Not tasty. I gave it 5 stars because I think it's a great place for a drink.

I fondly call this place the "Capital of Hippie Food".  Meals here are inextricably linked to a long chain of Vermont-special memories.  One of the owners used to make delicious little tofu cubes at the Onion River Co-op about 15 years ago. He's still making those lovely tofu squares you will find them at Stone Soup. You never know what you are going to find on the hot bar, because they change the menu every day to take advantage of what's fresh, good or just inspired.  I've found every dish to be delicious and as a vegetarian who loves dairy, it's great to see options for all eaters. Had an amazing plate yesterday with cheesy millet, a vegan casserole a creamy tofu stew and that great old standby, steamed kale.  The toppings are all there - brewers yeast, local hot sauce, braggs amino acids, gomasio, etc.  The Ceylon Tea/Lemonade blend added a nice slightly sweet drink treat to the meal. You might not find any of these dishes here - but whatever you do have, it's likely to be well prepared, well seasoned and good for you. I'm not a huge fan of eating healthy for the sake of eating healthy.  Flavor and a nod to the sense of the pleasure of eating are equally (if not more) important. Yes, it's a bit pricey  - but anyone who shops healthy in a decent market should understand that freshness and quality don't come cheaply.  If you're looking for a cheap meal, go to Olive Garden.  If you want quality, freshness, bright flavors and food that nourishes you, head on over to Stone Soup. Stone Soup is a unique treasure that should be visited by anyone who appreciates good home cooked food in a casual setting.  I'm happy it's still around. And lastly, THANKS to you guys for hanging in there all these years and still producing food you can be proud of and the Burlington community can continue to enjoy.
Cheesecake was delicious! Very smooth and creamy. "Something Else" steak sandwich is excellent. Great service.

I've only been to Cafeteria twice, and the first time was 5 years ago, however I remembered it being a good experience. I was disappointed to see that the polenta fries were not on the menu, however all I had to do was ask the waiter and he excitedly said I could order a side. They were amazing, and if you don't get the steak that they accompany, ask for a side order! The Wedge Salad was good, but a heavy start to my Mac and Cheese. They have 3 types and then a sampler of all 3. Yum. I regret that I forgot to take pictures until dessert came, but I guess I was too wrapped up in my cheese. I stated aloud "red velvet yodels" and the waiter heard and became so excited that he sat down and described them! His description really sold them, and they did not disappoint. Red velvet cake with cream cheese frosting rolled up and dunked in chocolate that hardened, served with a SIDE of vanilla milkshake! Well done. Beyond. All of the servers were great and it truly is affordable. It's said to be open 24/7, but it doesn't give the vibe of a late night messy haunt, so I assume a nice crowd comes in and keeps it classy.

Not Worth the Wait!! This place has come highly recommended from lots of people and the first time my wife and I went it was a decent experience.  Food was good and service was average at best.  We came back a week later with the mother-in-law who was visiting.  We were seated about 3-5 minutes after a group of 4 who arrived shortly before us.  Both parties orders were taken within 5 minutes of being seated, which was great.  About 15 min later the first parties food came out and they dug in.  My party continued to wait for another 45 minutes, during which time our server never once checked in on us or let us know what was going on.  At that point my wife asked for our food to be put in to-go boxes.  The group who had been seated 3-5 min before us had since finished their meal and paid before our food finally came out with the excuse of, "sorry, when it gets busy it takes 30-45 minutes for food to come out."  I don't know about that, in the hour we were there only one table was served food and our orders were taken basically at the same time.   That being said, the food was decent again.  Not amazing but better than your average diner food.

By far the worst afternoon bar for a couple of pops and food I Have ever been too.. hands down.... The place had no soul/vibe..My dead grandmother in the ground has more personality than this joint. Maybe a off day but shit..had a better time at work  eating lunch on the job.. Food was ok at best.. just like any other bar with a bar menu.. Maybe just a off day... or bad timing on our part.... I really wanted to like this place....

I never write reviews but I got so annoyed but this place that I felt I had to. I got out of a broadway show and found this on yelp and  called them to make sure they are open and after they verified that I walk a couple of blocks there so they can tell me that they closed the kitchen at midinight and everywhere it said 1am then I argued because it was just 11.40 and I just wanted sushi! Uncooked food. But they replied "Too late for food, have a drink we have drinks!" Really?

Excellent, Superb! Read reviews which had a wide range, but my experience with family could not have been better. Service, Environment, ambience were superior. Simply elegant décor. Food was terrific, but uneven. There were dozens of options. Price more than reasonable at $51 for the lobster buffet. Lobster was terrific, roast beef was very good (a bit tough, but flavorful), appetizers were exceptionally tasty. Roast Pork was dry. But given the variety, it did not matter whether 1 or 2 items could have been better. All in all, it is the bargain of the century. Waiters were helpful and attentive. The desserts without exception were outstanding!
I am definitely coming back. Great food. Nice atmosphere.
Go there. Eat anything. You will have no regrets. Outstanding service and unforgettable food.

This is a great place for delicious, inexpensive, fresh lunch. I love going here when I need a quick sandwich, quiche or soup. The guys behind the counter probably have the best customer service of any lunch spot in Princeton and the food is consistently good. The only thing I'd add are more salad options (spinach, mixed greens, etc), but otherwise this place gets a BIG thumbs up!

Absolutely amazing selection of vendors surrounded by amazing history. I recommend getting a roast pork sandwich from DiNic's. We did the food tour, which was really interesting and resulted in many samples from the market including snapper soup (it's turtle, and delicious).
I would love to bring my mother here

After a disastrous trip my first time I decided to give this restaurant a little bit of a second chance. Our waitress was fantastic at getting our party of five seated and drinks ordered. The menu offers good choices with a simple format. The disappointment came when the amazing looking steak was placed before me. With great anticipation I claimed my knife and fork and set to slicing morsel from the serving. Try as I might I could not cut loose desired bite. So I moved to a different place with same result. I looked up to find waitress and she vanished like a fart in a Texas tornado. Finally as the rest of my family was near finished with their meal I found a member of waitstaff and request a different menu item. Service was again prompt and my second entree was far superior. I do warm the consumer to be very picky here and suggest the chicken fried steak.
Very fresh and tasty food. Many different options for a reasonable price. Very friendly staff with quick service.
Now they have four dumplings for 1.25?? How is this goin on, they are clearly ripping people off
Friendly and prompt service. The food was nothing short of fantastic and full of flavor. It's a hopping joint that would also be great for some evening drinks.

Ordered the broiled salmon, which is served over quinoa and spinach.  Unfortunately, the spinach was riddled with sand.  The salmon was overdone.  This place was a favorite, but apparently it changed management / ownership a while back.  Don't think I'll return.

Just had THE worst experience of my life at this restaurant!  The waiter was rude, and the owner was even worst! The 'All You Can Eat' crab legs are not all you can eat. There is a limit of 5 clustered. A complaint was made about the smell of second cluster of crab legs. There was a strong chloride/ ammonia smell to them. The waiter debated with us about it and when the manager was requested and approached the table,  he was rude as well. He didn't ask what our issue was but immediately started to get defensive. He walked away in the middle of us talking to him! I asked him what are we going to now, he responded (never turning around face me) "I haven't decided yet!" After several staff members walked by our table to listen to our conversation,  the owner returned to tell us he was making a special batch just for us. Needless to say, that made us uncomfortable so we declined and asked for the check. When the check was bought to us the waiter was rude and argued with us again!  It was a horrible experience!  I will NEVER return!  Enter At Your Own Risk!! Beware!! Beware!!

I was a regular at the restaurant as soon as it opened. lunch or dinner became a routine. my favorite thing on the menu has to be the shawafel. great customer service, and the food was the best mediterranean food I have had in new haven. I have yet to try their personal pizza, but from what I see I think It'll be my new addiction. a great atmosphere and a convenient place to get food. being a college student in downtown and only a limited time between classes stops you from going to any other place because of the crowds. But at pitaziki even with the crowds you'll be in an out of there faster than you can say tzatziki.
I love this place! Always busy, but their service is not bad at all. Absolutely, food is amazingly delicious!! While waiting the table, they give complimentary wine. Their dessert also amazing!
I have dined in and ordered out at Spumoni Gardens. The pizza is always superb.
Incredible food! Came for lunch and was extremely impressed. Had the oysters and braised short rib, out of this world!
Excellent food, service and ambiance! Mike Fin our waiter ROCKS! Thanks for a great time!

I work at an elementary school. Hoping to provide new takeout menus for our 100+ staff is a fun summer routine. Was hoping for a new menu to add to our teacher lounge...I have never experienced such poor customer service. I ordered online, called an hour later to find out why I hadn't received my order, found out they hadn't started cooking, and proceeded to wait another hour for my order. At 3:15 when I finally received my order-- my coworker discovered she had received a chicken pad thai instead. We called to complain only to be told to wait for us to receive a corrected order. An hour later after we had given up hope, the owner showed up just to tell us that we had been wrong and that he was sure it was pork. At this point, we were frustrated since it was now 4:30. He just HAD to be right, and kept insisting we were wrong saying that this was a waste of his time and money. Ordering lunch at 1 PM only to have it arrive 3 hours later... I wonder if he expected us to wait and NOT eat. Apparently he did as he poked around the remains of our lunch that we had eaten because we were starving. We not only HAD to calm him down and take the blame, but then PAY him for the pad thai he brought. No apologies from him. Just us apologizing to him, paying him so that he would stop yelling in our main office, and then us shaking our heads and giving the lunch to someone else in the office. I can't believe this is how they treat people.
Delicious!  Friendly staff, clean space & potatoes, potatoes POTATOES!!!!  The Smashed Hit was loaded potato paradise & the mashed pie was enough for 2!  Will definitely be back again.
Had to wait 15 minutes but my oh my was it worth it! Chicken and Biscuit is phenomenal, who knew syrup and hot sauce worked so well!

No indian taste. The samosa chat was very good . Paneer chilly was horrible. The paneer is like a stone. You cannot bite it at all. Ambience is not so great. They might have some items on their menu for takeout. Not suitable for dine-in at all
Great flavor, wonderful service.  Crust is a bit hard, could be because it was a reheated slice.

First you need 4 friends go there with you. Food are so fresh and delicious but also huge. Need to try the hot pot! They are real traditional Korean food, if you like Korean food then you got to go there.

Ok, went BACK to Blend and... Had another good 'ol time. For after work, just want some drinks and good food; very good. Alexis (again) was attentive (as usual) and fun (as usual). This time, spoke with both managers, Carlos and ... I forgot his name (eep). Very gracious and courteous. If you work or live nearby, go around 6 during the week. Not too loud and everyone was on point. :)

Wow, worth traveling from Manhattan for the delicious food. I live near Il Mulino, but its generally out of my price range when looking for a place to eat. Il Falco has an excellent selection of meats and pastas, along with a tasty Nero D'Avola that I thoroughly enjoyed.

Not sure if the management/bar owners are aware that the in-house live music walks around with a 'tip bucket' asking for money in-between sets. Not only is this unprofessional but the musician interrupted my conversations multiple times that I had last night demanding for money. This is almost as awkward as show time dancers on the train & bums asking for money on the corner. STOP THIS NOW.

The restaurant is quaint and dark and perfect for a date although the place was empty besides one other table and they placed us right next to them so we asked to be moved. The dumplings were delicious but my Pad Thai was a bit soggy. I like for the noodle to be soft but not like it would be inside a soup. I wanted to try something new but I think I'll stick to Circles for now.

Would definitely give a 4. Traditional North-Indian cuisine, albeit may not be an Indian cuisine. Could get the taste of all the items. Good thing about ordering a buffet is that you can pick any other item that is served and not available at the stalls. Dessert's pretty average, don't expect too much given an average price. Food's good. Ambience is average and sometimes cramped  up if more than 10 people. And yeah, on a sunday you'll not be enjoying your lunch/dinner given the crowded locality. Would suggest to give a visit on weekdays.

The best sushi in New York City---as simple as that. It's expensive, yes, but you get what you pay for. A refined dining experience, although Chef Yasuda is definitely missed since moving back to Tokyo.

My favorite little cafe! Their service is fast and their presentation is impeccable. You must try the chai tea! I have made the 20 minute trip down multiple times just to grab a cup! They even sell bags so you can make it at home. What a great place!

This is one of my favorite place to eat dosa . I love their all dosas and other indian food they served . I had tried their chicken saag and chicken biryani it was so awesome . I also like their masala chai . They all are very friendly and give best customer service all the time .

I pass this place every day after work and went in for happy hour that began at 4pm. Got there, saw a wheel and spun! But didn't know how it worked so it was useless that I landed on the mousse dish. We waited to be seated in back for the specials. Was told we couldn't order from dinner menu till after 5 because kitchen crew was on break but we could order from happy hour menu. We started with dry flavorless chicken meatballs and sauteed mushrooms and was onto our 3rd glass of wine before we able to finally order the BJ burger which was served with chopsticks??? Service was really crappy from 4pm all the way till we got our bill at 8. It was confusing as to who was servicing our table, one person took food orders, another one took drink orders then they disappear and then they switched it up on us. The three stars are for the atmosphere. I doubt I would go again.

I really love this place.  The food is good, very fairly priced and it's BYOB.  I come with my boyfriend and we usually order a burrito, a quesadilla, rice and beans, some tacos and cokes with real sugar.  Only thing I don't like is pickled onions, but some people do.  If you want a chill place to get some good mexican food and not break a 20$ bill this is the place.  Awesome mole sauce, and really nice guys behind the register.  I always tip because they are so pleasant but technically  I don't think they are servers, you grab your food and bring it to a table yourself.  love it
It's always a good place. Not a long wait & they ave no problem with picky orders.  The manager has been there a long time & it shows.  Its well run & food is fresh

Went with my mom and sis to the Firebox to have some catch up time with the girls and some good food. We were not let down! The waitress was so friendly and did not rush us. We spent about 3 hours there (by choice!) just talking and enjoying the fantastic food, ambiance, and service. I ordered the cheese plate for an appetizer which was very elegant and creative. My sister teased me for ordering the french fries but put her foot in her mouth (as well as half the bowl of fries) after trying them. By far the BEST fries I have ever had! The duck was delectable, so juicy and cooked medium to perfection just as I requested. My family and I will be returning and we just love how the Firebox is "Farm-to-Table" using only fresh local ingredients. Definitely worth the money and drive.

This place is no joke.  Worth every penny.  Shrimp and grits, gravy smothered chicken, biscuits, AND matzoball soup?! all of which I have tried, and each have blown my tastebuds to southern heaven.  I recently tried the turkey leg dinner.  Delicious.  The cocktails are dangerous too.  I've had most of them, my favorites are definitely the apple pie moonshine which tastes like apple pie and the jam jar.  Downside is they are almost always packed with a 30 minute wait.  A must try, if you're willing to get addicted.

There are many things to pick from, with various levels of "spicy" which I found very nice. I got chicken with cashews and noodles which I found delicious. The servers were very nice and the restaurant had a nice atmosphere to it. I also got the fried ice cream which was out of this world.

What is so great about this place. I went way out of my way to come here last Sunday afternoon. You have to order brunch which I didn't feel like so I went with the steak and eggs. The table next to us ordered after us. By the time they had eaten and were paying there bill I asked where our food was. When it came the waiter said the steak takes a long time causing the delay. My steak was very rare in the first place but I did say rare. But it was also cold so if that's what held up the meal it should come to me hot right. Other than that the food was OK but it was outweighed by snobby pretentious lousy service. See ya. Oh and way overpriced.
Si quieren probar comida mexicana, deben ir a este lugar, RIQUÍSIMO, el mejor sabor mexicano que he probado en EU.

WOW! Hands Up The BEST Thai Restaurant Outside Of Bangkok! Prices Are Very Reasonable (Cash Only), And The Food Portions Are Bangkokin!  What's Really Cool About This Place Besides The Authentically Delicious Food Is That The Restaurant Is Literally (4) Restaurants In One! A Beautiful Outdoor Seating Area With A Fountain Completely Helps The Ambiance.  Definitely (2) Thumbs Up!
amazing white.

Best ramen in NYC - but expect to WAIT at least an hour unless you visit during "off" hours. I always order the vegetarian ramen with extra avocado. The pork buns are delicious as well. I like to sit at the counter and watch the chefs. Be ware, it's no frills. Not fancy. And it's a tiny joint. But the food is great.
Bubble TEA is out of this world highly recommend this place.  Their food is really good too. I'm glad I work  near by so I can come here frequently.

We have been here more than 5 times already, so short version of my review: it's very good quality and taste! The pho is amazingly good, absolutely a perfect balance of rich and clean tasting broth and quality of the beef (even noodles taste good too)! Besides pho there are salads which are good as well as bahn mi. Every time we come here we are surprised by the new items on the menu. Today was a delicious pineapple desert dish. So we will back again and again.

This isn't a normal traditional sand which shop. Its something a lot different. Instead of subway where they toast the bread and put maybe 3 slices of turkey they put a lot of meat and toppings. They stream tge meat and cheese! What other sand which shop does that? This is the best sand which shop. I recommend the club on a sub or the turkey bacon ranch.
Great bang for the buck. Excellent tacos and the sauce is amaaaazzzing!!!! Keep up the good work!!!
wonderful Chelsea neighborhood brunch/lunch spot. food was deliciousness, service was impeccable.
Horrible everything.

Salt alert! My wife and I dined at the Astoria location. We were seated across from the bar. Very noisy. At times could not hear the server. But the main complaint was the over salting of everything. From the veggies, fish, salad. We ordered dover sole "for two". The price was for two but not the portion. I have visited many other Greek rest. for fish and have had a satisfying portion of fish. I don't know what all the praise is for this place. It is more of a scene. If you want a serious meal search elsewhere.
mmm...pork buns.

Food was good but came out very quickly and was often cold in the middle. The flavors were nice and sangria was good so I could forgive the lack of warmth. However, service was horrible. Wait staff often leaned by the corner of the bar and took a while to get our drinks. Didn't even have an opportunity to tell them how the food was because she didn't come back until we were ready for the bill once we ordered. Had a discrepancy on the bill and was made to feel incompetent when it was their mistake. Would have given it a second chance if it weren't for the service.
Great food! Unique. Retro decor was entertaining. Chicken pot pie was amazing and the risotto delish! Ambiance relaxed, retro, comfortable.
Dry, greasy, nothing special.  Arrived at 11, quick service.  You go here for the history and the experience, not for an amazing bit to eat. Still glad I went
The food was exceptional! My mom and I had ramen and the steamed buns with chicken! I wish I had four stomachs and try more dishes. Oh and the service was quick. Must go place!

Had a great time at The Eddy. Intimate restaurant with a mixologist on hand serving bright and inventive cocktails that fittingly kicked the off the evening for our group. The refreshing bourbon daisy drink arrived in a lovely antique tea cup and my wife's parlor friar beverage was likewise delicious. Executive Chef Brendan's eclectic dishes were skillfully executed with the pillowy gnocci, pickled ramps and char rillette particularly tasty. Overall, a wonderful relaxed evening and we will certainly return soon.

LOVE! LOVE! The Crabby Shack! A quaint place - I could see in the Vineyard or Hamptons. The food was so good and very fresh. We had crab legs, crab cakes, crab roll and crab tacos, steamed broccoli, new potatoes and corn - very fresh! Not too over seasoned, just lightly seasoned and tasty, not too salty, the legs were very buttery too!  They crab legs are servedin a plastic bag that they pour this butter sauce in and when you open the bag the butter sauce is in your basket and you can dip the crab meat in it. I can see them adding some shoestrings fries and dipping sauces. (in the future) When I left I was very full and happy. :-) I went with a friend from Maryland and she ordered crab legs and a crab role to go. For dessert they had BCakeShop cupckaes, yummy and the best old fashion banana pudding. I say old fashion because it was just like your mother made it not too over the top, just vanilla pudding, bananas and vanilla wafers. SO good. The decor is classic and the bathroom I want in my home. I will definitely go back! Congrats to the ladies for making this dream a reality! I am waiting on the franchise...Harlem, LI, Hamptons, Vineyard, Philly Baltimore, DC...and the list goes on!
Their pizza is out of this world! My husband I always go here when we're in the mood for a pie and they've never disappointed!  Friendly staff, quick service, delicious food! Definitely recommend!
The food was wonderful, however I wish the veggie meatballs were vegan!  The sides tasted great.
The "chicken parmesan" was delicious. We got one order and shared with three people. The place could be cleaner, however; its popular so it's a lot of just wear and tear.
Very bad place. Rude people work in there and food is just grose. It f#&&@ up your stomach and appetite. $$very dam expensive . For the price and the quality of food is just now rite
Once again Becco didn't disappoint.   Missed reservations early due to traffic but they were kind enough to serve us after our show at 10pm.  Braised short ribs were excellent.

The barista that served me was totally full of himself. I don't pretend to be a coffee expert, but I did pay my way through college working at an espresso bar so I'm definitely not the idiot he treated me like. I ended up just ordering an iced coffee. When I asked for skim milk he said "Our skim milk is 2%." WTF?!? No, your skim milk is non-existent. YOU DO NOT HAVE SKIM MILK. That is totally trivial. I would have been fine with 2% milk if he treated me with the slightest bit of dignity and said, "I'm sorry, we don't have skim but we do have 2%." Needless to say, although I live a few blocks away, I will not be returning. If you're in the area, go to Ninth Street Espresso at 56th and Park. The people there are way nicer and so is the space.

So, I ordered some wings today and asked for them to be crispy.  The woman told me that they can't make them crispy.  Um...wtf?!    You just cook them longer.  I ordered 1/2 one flavor and 1/2 another and asked if they can put them in separate containers, and she said "I'm sorry, but we can't do that because we're corporate."  Again, wtf?!  Lastly, we asked how much sauce do we get for the 40+ wings that we ordered, and she told us that it comes with only two small sauces, any extra would cost more $$.  Such a rip off.  Overall rating:  wings themselves are a 3.5, but company's policies and/or incompetent employees bring rating down to a 2.0.

This place is the best I used to come here after school for some awesome and delicious Vietnamese hoagie and bun buo hue. The place is very calm and soothing where u can enjoy your food in peace. Also the workers here are so nice. For an asian I tried out a lot of places but this place has the best food for a cheap price.

Great spot, awesome service! My boyfriend & I love going here for after work drinks. Especially when Jimmy Fransioli is behind the bar.  He knows how to make great cocktails & most importantly, he's a people person. Anytime I'm not sure what I'm in the mood to drink, Jimmy mixes together one of his cocktail specials with all fresh ingredients which always taste amazing.  Highly recommend!

This was the perfect easy delicious lunch experience with the family.  Todd was so funny and engaging...our kids would like to live here with him.  The grilled cheese is over the top and the patty melt was amazing.  Elena's eggplant side is a must try if they haven't run out already.  If the weather is nice, this is one of the best patios.  And to top it off, they have a very selective list of craft beers.
Delicious fresh food and fast delivery! I got the Thai dumplings and tom yum. Tom yum had the perfect amount of spice - and the dumplings were loaded with fresh flavors. I would recommend!

THE BEST PIZZA. You might need to wait - it's worth it. Paulie will come over to your table, if you are a girl or have a girl sitting at it - flirt, search for compliments, tell you you look like Diane Lane when she was young. Vegan? Paulie's got your back - too many choices to try them all. Get the dessert pizza. do it.

I had Maddy Classic Burrito a few times.  It is a good burrito.  I tried the enchiladas which were okay.  The mole sauce seemed skimpy usually they smother things in the mole.  The chips were very good, fresh and crispy.  My friend had the steak tacos said they were okay seemed bland.  We like Maddy's for Lunch and I will stick with the burrito.

Asked the waiter what kind of Sam Adams they had on tap.  He told me there was only one kind of Sam Adams.  Ordered the fish and chips.  I got 3 fish stick sized pieces of fish and 10 waffle fries.  What is this, a meal for ants?

I've been here twice for drinks and have really enjoyed it. Went last night for dinner and unfortunately did not have the same experience. The kale salad was good, but the oysters were just OK and the meat board was awful. We did not end up ordering meals. Disappointed to say the least.

I love their pupu platter, potato salad and soup. They are amazingly delicious. I usually go there on Monday because they sell a bottle of wine for half price ;) The outside is lovely place to eat there!!
This cart makes my heart sing happy songs (and my tummy)! DELICIOUS, fresh, warm and heavenly!
I took my girlfriend to this place for her birthday and it rocked. They have the best pad thai i have ever had in new york city. prices are cheap and the food is great.

Went to Tavern on Jane last night with my sons, husband and a work colleague.  We love coming to the city for work, and it was a rare treat to have my family along. Big disappointment, which was such a shame considering all the good reviews and all of the truly great places to eat in the city.  First, it's a bar, just a bar. And sort of a smelly, not so clean bar.   It's way loud, though the music was good.   The food was so completely average.  The service got progressively worse as our waitress must have clocked out and didn't tell us and then we weren't really paid attention to.  And the bill for 5 of us was over $300 - no bottles of wine or anything fancy.  Probably 5 wine/cocktails total, couple of burgers and 3 entrees. 1 dessert.  But all so very average.   Only exciting thing about the night was the big drug bust right outside.   I wanted a cozy, Village place with brick walls and candles...had brick and candles, I guess. Not sure what everyone is so excited about.

I have been there many times. It's a nice place to sit down for a coffee or a drink. It has a laid back and nice atmosphere. Staff are nice. I wish they had a larger pastry selection and more latte drink options.

Very crowded but not more than usual for a place that has a bar. However I was pretty thrown off when I walked in and the bar was right in front of you and you had to walk past the bar to get to the hostess station. The food was pretty good and the server was also very good and attentive. It's a nice place to go on a Friday night.

Pretty tasty! A lot in the menu and if you are not familiar with this type of food be prepared to ask a lot of questions there's just not enough description on the menu itself so we sat for five minutes and asked a lot of questions before making our decision since it was the first time we were there! I highly suggest the owner has pictures Of every dish. we sampled a few of the different entrée selections and it was plenty of food. The rice is especially tasty. We did like the kebabs and they had very nice char grill flavor to them and they were a good quality piece of meat! It's not our every day type of food but a welcome addition to the Morrisville area -you must try it at least once... I'm sure you will be back - we will be too!

Literally my favorite restaurant in the entire world. I've eaten there about 4 times just this summer it's so great. I usually get the Ricky Ricardo's Ribs which are boneless short ribs in an apricot sauce. It's reallllyyyy good I love it. It has a sweetness to it and it's just all around really good. It comes with rice and black beans and Yuca which is a latin potato which is also very good. As for the tapas I've had the chicharon de pollo which is just chicken lollipops. They're really good but can be a bit salty. I've also had the chicken empanadas. Now I've had homemade empanadas from various places and I can't say these are the best ones I've ever had. The drinks and flavors are great but it is BYOB and they'll mix sangrias for you. The atmosphere is very fun and the waiters are very friendly. It can get a little crowded especially in the winter when the outside isn't open. Most times you'll be pretty close to people next to you so the restaurant does get pretty loud. The only reason I didn't give it 5 stars is because the noise level with the people and the music can make it hard to hear one another. But overall it is a wondering restaurant and I genuinely enjoy eating there.

Came to this place after driving 32 miles for it as Yelp reviews made it pretty attractive. A great brunch place to be at, Excellent service and food, of course. Potions are huge, none of us six could eat even half of our orders. I would recommend the owners to add some pics to the menu, we had to order using the pics on Yelp. Will be back again whenever in Philly area.

now i have ordered from this place several times almost each time they have messed something up. but today was the last straw for me. i ordered large pastrami and american cheese sub( got swiss or provolone  ordered spinach got lettuce) medium tuna salad sub large oven roasted turkey sub hot dogs( barely cooked and they forgot to bring it the first time so we had to wait an additional 20 minutes ) small ham and salami sub was very disappointed with service this time and they are usually okay
The nicest wait staff around. Risotto to die for. Only wish they'd been around when my office was around the corner. I'd have taken a time share on a table. Love this place!!!!

Bistro Les Amis was introduce to us by our niece who was graduating from NYU.   This place was amazing.  It was a crazy busy day and I just needed a place to unwind. I had a mint lemonade with a spike of vodka which was refreshing and a tuna nicoise. The tuna was cooked to perfection with a pepper coating.  Got to sit back and watch the sites.  Great place to people watch.  The waitress was sincere and funny.  Plus I got to practice my French.  Merci!

I'm not a New York native, so when I visit Little Italy, it's a bit of a hit or miss when choosing a restaurant.  Benito One was luckily a fantastic choice! My family went there for lunch, and the lunch special consisted of a salad, pasta platter, and entree for a very reasonable price. I had the chicken parmigiana, a salad and linguine with red sauce. I loved it! My sisters got the chicken francese and rigatoni bolognese and enjoyed it as well. The wait staff was really attentive and personable.   Highly recommend Benito One!!

The food was excellent.  If you're looking for something a little different and extremely delicious,  this is the place to go.  The best dishes were the lamb ribs, lamb neck, and poutine.  I also tried the schnitzel,  rabbit, carrots, and peas.   They were all great.  One tip: if you want the pig's head, order it as soon as you get there.  It takes an hour to cook, so I didn't have a chance to try it.  Next time!
Awesome atmosphere. Eric (bartender and girlfriend) very welcoming. Guacamole unbelievable. Definitely a must see!

Food is not worth for the price. The service is terrible and unprofessional. We ordered chicken katsu, it comes chick teriyaki, and we ordered vegetable tempura,it didn't come to our table! We saw with our own eye. We strongly WON'T recommend anyone visit this restaurant!S

I hesitated to write this review immediately following my meal at Marrakesh, because it was not going to be glowing to say the least.  But the fact that the evening I spent there still botherd me, I felt that I must share my experience with Yelp readers.  In May, a group of about 20 women went to Marrakesh to celebrate a 50th birthday.  Reservations were made in advance and we were led to a cozy private room.  At first, all was well,l but when we asked to have the air conditioning turned down, we were accommodated, but just briefly,  Before too long, the air was back up.  During some birthday toasts, we asked for the music to be turned down, which it was, but before too long it was turned back up.  This happened at least three times.  During the course in which a whole chicken is served, I asked for a fork - I was dressed up for the occasion and really didn't want to eat a whole chicken with my hands.  What I was given was the smallest, cheapest plastic fork imaginable.  Later, a few of the guests left early, leaving a tiny space open in the private room.  The hosts tried repeatedly to sit other diners IN OUR ROOM and seemed surprised that we didn't want strangers joining our celebration.  I can't imagine that the strangers would have wanted to sit with us either.  At 11:00 p.m., the hosts made it clear that we had to leave, despite the fact that restaurant was still busy with many other guests.  As we were told to leave, we asked the hosts to call us a few cabs in order to return to our hotel.  This apparently was not a viable request and our group walked quite a distance to our hotel.

Stopped in for a burger and fries for lunch today. Food was tasty, staff was very friendly, service was quick, and price was great. Can't beat that! Looking forward to trying their bagels next time I'm in the area.

Ordered take - out and got gnocchi and falafel gyro. It was very bland. From the brief time I spent at the bar, the ambiance seemed nice and the bartender was friendly. For its price, the food was disappointing.

I would not suggest using the online ordering through their website but once that issue was corrected, the food was delivered fast, the staff is very nice and the burger, fries and shake I got were AWESOME.  Great food, just call if you want delivery.
Naan and rest of the items are more far better than any rice item. They make good curries, butter chiken, tikka masala, palak paneer....
Just had dinner here.. the wait is too long. The food is awesome!  Love the crabs and shrimp. Wonderful

I only go to this place because of location, and convenience.  The food is pretty good, but it is pricey and the service is not very good.  The lady behind the counter is rude and the waiter's couldn't really care less.  I would not go out of my way to come here.  I've gotten egg rolls, pork fried rice, boneless ribs, general tso's, and they were all pretty good.

This is a great new little spot on Astoria Blvd.  Its really a pure takeout spot.  Food was very very good and very fresh.  They made the dumplings in front of me.  They have several sauces they use, all were delicious.  Had the chicken empanada, playeros, and pork dumplings.  We will definitely be back again soon.

Delicious!  The dumplings are so fresh!  As with many Chinatown holeinthewalls, don't be turned off by the crumby décor and rundown interior.  This food is good and fresh made!  A classic Chinatown experience.

My colleagues and I have been ordering and coming here for over ten years. The last experience was unacceptable. We are in the service industry so we are not ones to complain. The waitress...Asian with facial discoloration. The most rude woman, if you can call her that, said, "I work here all the time and I've never seen you" after that and more, we still left a 25% tip. She then chased us down the block, saying we didn't pay our bill. This woman is a vindictive thief and should not be allowed to treat loyal customers like this. After tracking down the owner, she was unwilling to accept or take responsibility for the psychotic employee, who accused us of not paying. Once again, we always pay and tip 25% or more.
