It would have been a 1 star review had we discovered after the fact that we paid for something we did not even order.

Just wasn't up to my standard. Burger falling apart while I'm trying take the first bite. They put cold blue cheese on it. Didn't even think of letting it warm up a bit on the burger. The sautéed mushroom n onions where a joke. Bacon cooked till dried up and burnt. Just not the best. Beef was good. But cooks should take more pride in what they are putting out to custies.

I had the worst experience at this restaurant.   The staff was incredibly rude. I attended a group dinner for a birthday and there were no menus given nor was a price mentioned for the items.  I was not planning on eating a large meal and was told there was $5 charge for splitting the meal. The bill came and was told $43.00! When trying to discuss this matter, I was called cheap and so was another guest.  When asked for another glass twice by one of the guests, the waitress told her that she heard her "two days ago" with an attitude, meaning ok I heard you I am assuming. But she didn't get her glass.  When trying to change an entree for something else, another guest was given an attitude.  I would not recommend this restaurant.  SAVE YOUR MONEY!!

Excellent Thai food and lovely service. The crazy noodles (drunken noodles or kee mao at other Thai restaurants) are fantastic with any type of protein. Spicy level goes from 1 - 5; I love spicy food and grew up eating a lot of Thai food outside DC. The 5 here was appropriately intense. Great portions. The thai spring rolls are a nice appetizer, also tried the beef satay and it was great. Thai ice tea wasn't the best I've ever had, but decent. For an affordable price this is a great choice!

We have dinner in here once a week.  It's a nice relaxing atmosphere. No rushing us out, the staff is just as relaxed and friendly.  The food is so amazing I often crave it. I haven't had a single thing on the menu I have not loved. This place is not for you if you are in a hurry or high maintenance.
Good dumplings but everything else was mediocre.  Will not be going there again any time soon.

We chose this place because of the high review on yelp . We went this afternoon and the place was so empty,only one table customer,maybe some in the backyard,for sure they are not busy!We ordered BBQ rib sandwich and grill sandwich from a woman!After 20-30minutes,we were still waiting for our food! I finally asked the woman how long we should keep waiting, she told me another 15-20minutes! Wtf! I am sure she or the staff in the kitchen skipped or forgot our order! We decided to leave without any food! BTW,at least 3 flys flying in the restaurant,I wonder if the food there is clean enough! The service is not attentive,I saw a customer coming from backyard to ask for the ice water on a hot summer day! I will not give any star if possible on yelp!

Never heard about this place but I came in for a late dinner. I had the Green Bird burger with truffle frize. It took them more than 30 minutes to get my order while the waiter kept apologizing. The food was McDonalds level and cost me 25 bucks including service. That's what I call a scam. For that price, any bistro in the village woukd give you a decent class meal and a hug. Don't bother.

This is such a great place! The breakfast is delicious whether you get omelettes, eggs with bacon, etc. is just so good! The people are very friendly and reasonable prices. Overall this place is really good!

Last review for a weekend of reviews: Took some out of town friends here for lunch today. Decent. Pats got a new sign across the street, that people in line in front of us were talking about. Now to the steak.......kind of fatty. Thought "the chewy fat" would be cut out while on the grill. The "wiz" sauce or actual cheese will have you craving more! Who cares what it is....wow! Will return for sure.

If you want some real Puerto Rican home cooking then this is the place to come to. Prices are very reasonable- you'd be hard pressed to prepare a meal for the same price at home. The food is tasty and fresh. The cooks and wait staff are very friendly and seem to be family, uncles, aunt etc. Try the rotisserie chicken and roast pork. Pop out the back through the kitchen and you can see it all cooking. If I lived in the neighbourhood I'd be a regular, as it is I live in New Zealand

Really great pizza.  By far the best sicialian slice I have ever had. Really an awakening experience.  It's pretty neat to go in for a slice and look at peoples faces.  After the first bite you just see a smile.

I have eaten dosa all over the world including the mother country, and Thiru makes the best dosa I have ever eaten. The batter is crisp while at at the same time remaining moist, His pondicherry has vegetables so fresh they taste like home grown. Well worth coming from Washington D.C to try - I was skeptical when friends told me about him, and now I am a believer.     And having read the other reviews, anyone giving less than a four or five star clearly should stick to McDonalds, since they do not deserve to be reviewing such great food.

Quaint diner. I was in CT for two nights and both nights I went to this diner! Our server is really the reason that I gave this place 4 stars (her name was Shade) and their banana pancakes! It's a diner, so in comparison to other diners their prices are BEYOND reasonable, and the food and the service is fast and friendly

This is my favorite place to get brunch in all of NYC. The scrambles are out of this world and so is the french toast. They also make my favorite bloody mary in town. The food is excellent. Everything we had from the duck meatloaf to the BBQ oysters, to the steak was really tasty and delicious. The drink selection was good as well, though I do think they could use a few more wines on their list. All in all you will have a great time with amazing food in an awesome area. Worth checking out

Strangest experience I've ever had in a place in my life.  On a Saturday (8/16/14) headed in to the place with my wife.  Sat in their outdoor area.  Waitress seemed nice enough.  Gave us a beer menu at 5pm with about half the selections crossed out....No big deal, order a few drinks (one of the uncrossed selections also wasn't available, so about 4 of their 10 beers were orderable). Drinks come and we order some food.  30 minutes go by and don't see our waitress, ever again (food neither)...Manager guy that was hanging out also gone...The back space still had one waitress and plenty of other workers in the area...they sit a table next to us...the waitress that was still there takes the order of the seated couple and food comes out for them about 40 minutes after we ordered (the place only has burgers and hot dogs so it's not like we ordered anything complicated).   They weirdest and strangest situation I've ever been in, in a bar/restaurant in my live.  ...We just left money for the one round we bought (and got) and left. I imagine it's was an isolated situation, hate to give it the 1 star, but that's what happened while we were there......I'm sure there's a legit story about something strange where something happened with the waitress and manager and why they weren't there any longer and why no one thought to cover the tables left stranded by their absence.  (Party of five in front of us also looked like they were getting really mad with menu's hanging out at their table for about 35 minutes without someone coming by to take an order). I will definitely head back in one time and I'm sure it'll be cool.

Literally the best Asian food in Connecticut!!   Coming from California, I have pretty high standards for KBBQ and Asian food in general, but this place is definitely on point.   Seoul BBQ gives you so many delicious side dishes, and huge meat portions!  Everything is so tasty, and I'd highly recommend the combination meals because they come with so many different soups and sides so you can try a bit of everything. The restaurant itself has a lot of space, is well ventilated, and clean, which are important factors for me as well.   Finally, I'd just like to add that I'd give 6/5 stars for the great service!!  Ask for Doan! I had the same server the two times I was here, and he was always so attentive, friendly, and even cracked some funny jokes :P  The entire staff seems to enjoy working with one another here.

If Paula Deen ate here she would have a heart attack because their butter is to die for. My favorite breakfast spot hands down. I usually order a couple some pancakes, some eggs, meatloaf, and coffee. Yes, I finish everything.
Disgusting bathrooms, rude waiters and mediocre food!  Managers need to go to charm school. This place needs to be closed down.
Staff is great and food and margaritas are always on point!!! I just wish the crowds would go away as I'd eat there a few times a week.
I used to come here and last few times the margarita has decreased it's size.... it gives me the feeling that the business isn't going well or not well managed. Very disappointed.
Excellent food, good service, nice decor and affordable price. I would come back again

AS SIMPLY SAID CONSULTING Restaurant Customer Service Reviews Name: Sakura Gardens Japanese Steak House Address: 120 Hebron Avenue * Glastonbury, CT 06033 Review Categories: Ambiance / Cleanliness: 4/5, Food & Drink: 4/5, Manager Visibility: 5/5, Product knowledge: 4/5, Service: 5/5 Summary:   Ambiance / Cleanliness: This restaurant was clean and well maintained. Lightening was good and atmosphere was upbeat. Food & Drink: Filet Mignon with shrimp, salmon, and fried rice. Drinks were Mai Tai's Food temperature, Preparation, Presentation and Taste:  (Hibachi style dining). Food was prepared on site, seasoned to perfection, and cooked beautifully. The taste was great, the filet was moist, tender and tantalizing to the palate. The salmon was well balanced, seasoned to taste and finished with a traditional Japanese sesame seed blend. Both dished came with fried rice and vegetables. Manager Visibility:  The manager Christine was visible and engaged with customers as she visited tables to ensure customers were satisfied with their service. Service: The level of service was outstanding. Upon entering, we were greeted and seated promptly. Our waiter Scott, was very knowledgeable about the products offered and was engaged with us. On several occasions, our waiter checked to verify that we had everything we needed to make this an enjoyable dining experience. There was an issue with an appetizer and he promptly corrected the error by notifying the manager, who removed it from the bill. Our chef Chad was excellent, not only was he entertaining, but he remembered us from our previous visit. He was able to tell us exactly what we ordered and where we sat.  He indicated that he takes pride in serving and preparing food for his guests. With a well trained staff guided by manager Christine, this restaurant has become one of our top choices for dining out in Connecticut. Regards, AS SIMPLY SAID CONSULTING

I came here on my mission to find the best pizza across the country so waited an hour and a half because of the wait for this pizza but I was not disappointed! They have very nice employees and an amazing pizza with a crust that goes through a three day process, first rising, second put into balls, and last being refrigerated. This process is totally worth it because that crust was heavenly next to the homemade fresh mozzarella and the tasty tomato sauce made in a 999 degree, 6000 pound wood fired oven that makes the pizza in 90 seconds. I got a tour of the room where they make the fresh ingredients by the owners of the restaurant after a delicious free Nutella calzone dessert, and I will come back next time I can!

In our short trip to NYC we visited this place twice. Excellent rolls at very reasonable prices. The chai is great as well. Very well managed and their Manager Scott is very friendly and runs a good operation.

Best pizza in the area.  For a while, I thought that there was nothing very memorable around here.  As soon as I had Joe's though, I decided that this is going to be the place we order from.  The crust was perfect, and not just the right amount of cheese.  We had some of their wings as well and were not let down.  If you're in the area, def order from Joe's!
Overcooked seafood, clumsy waiters, stale bread..Seafood pasta was okay. .Will not be returning.

The counter women definitely could smile a bit more.  But the catering staff was stellar.  When I showed up there to book them to cater an event the two women behind the counter seemed as though they couldn't be bothered and I was an annoyance.  But Tom greeted us and smiled and made us feel welcomed. The food was amazing.  Our guests loved every dish and even made note of where the food came from for later visits.  I will definitely go back and recommend the deli to others.

I have some favorite moments in my life that are not matched by any others. The days my children were born, the day I married my husband and today, the day I discovered Sandra's Next Generation.   I have never written a Yelp review and I always find something negative about places that I go to eat. However, there is not one thing that I could say that would be negative about Sandra's, except that they are in New Haven, Connecticut and I am in New Hampshire. Our server was Miguel and he could not of been more patient, welcoming, nice  and helpful. I had never had soul food and everything on the menu looked amazing. I asked him his favorites which he told me and did not mind when I asked again and again and again and asked him what he would choose. There was a special on the menu of Caribbean rice with chicken and muscles. It sounded interesting. When I asked Miguel about it, he offered to bring us out a sample. The four of us shared it and it was amazing! All of our eyes lit up when we realized that the food, if all of that was as good as this rice, was going to be outstanding. We placed our orders and waited for the food to arrive. While we were waiting we were given cornbread! One bite and it was heaven! There was a light coating of butter on top and it was the best cornbread I've ever had in my life.  We were even given seconds. Then the food arrived! The plates were heaping and the food was hot and fresh. I had the candied yams, the Caribbean rice  and barbecue ribs. All I can say is it is the best meal I have ever eaten in my life! My husband had the fried chicken smothered in gravy with rice, macaroni and cheese and green beans and my daughter and her husband both had fried chicken with two sides. We just kept looking at each other with smiles and delight and could not stop commenting on how wonderful the food was. We were all in total agreement! When Miguel came to clear our plates we had all finished every drop of food on our plates! They may have been huge but the food was too good to leave any to waste. If you are in the New Haven area, or going to be visiting, this is a must eat at place. A great family run business that has a great atmosphere, is clean, everyone that works there was very friendly and the food was amazing! You will not be disappointed.

When u walk into San remo you notice the 70s 80s original decor  .we ordered a half plain pizza and half pepperoni pizza and garlic knots.the knots smelled great but we're actually alill bitter and tastes less at times .the sauce was so so regular canned style sauce  by the taste.they offer 4 different size pies and they put they're pepperoni under the cheese which wasn't the worst or the best .I have have to rate this older pizza parlor at just that a regular place .I wouldn't  go driving 30 minutes to eat they're but if your local and looking for a regular stop this at be good enough.prices weren't terrible .

I've been there 4-5 times in last year and wings are excellent.  However, the bartenders aka waitstaff are not very good.  If I go to a restaurant or bar and the bartender or waitstaff are slow or unprofessional I always give them a one time pass and say maybe they are having a bad day, understaffed, etc but when I've been to an establishment 4-5 times for the excellent wings and cheap drinks AND the same issues with the waitstaff and bartenders show up just about every time than I want to call attention to it.  I've been there on Saturdays early and late when crowded. I've been there on Friday for happy hour and Wednesday for happy hour.  These are the issues I see.  2 bartenders for bar and they both sometimes disappear for 5-10 minutes at a time.  Unacceptable when it happens over and over.  Orders will come out at different times meaning the wings come out first than maybe the fries or clams come out 10 minutes later.  Unless requested as an appetizer than main meal this is unacceptable yet it happens all the time.  Attitude of a few bartenders leaves a lot to be desired.  They will be snappy, surly and full of excuses when order or drinks are incorrect.  I am not argumentative or confrontational by nature but if an establishment wants my hard earned cash than they have to have more than good food.  I do not like leaving a bar or restaurant feeling like the workers couldn't be bothered by my requests for professional service.
3.5 stars Stop right now and walk about 5 blocks from this bakery and go to Metropolitan. Le Bus isn't particularly awful but Metro has better French staples and pastries.

Is it cause I went at an off peak hour? The Old Fashioned was quite disappointing compared to spots like Apotheke, Amor Y Amargo, Penrose and etc.. or it was simply not the style I prefer. It was okay.

A Spanish restaurant run by an American with extremely slow service. I absolutely despise when you walk into a restaurant absolutely excited to try the food and you're welcomed with poor service. The host ignored my boyfriend when he walked in first until she saw me and had to ask me for how many in the party. Why? If he came in first, why did you have to look over him? Finally we get to a table. The waiters must have walked past us a couple of times until after 30 minutes we had to ask the busboy to get a waiter to take our order. They made us feel absolutely invisible and disrespected. We drank two Watered down Estrella Damms and left after that. Please, don't judge your customers by their appearance. We had enough money and dignity to be worthy enough of this place but we won't ever think about giving it a second chance.

Food was ok, not excellent, but ok. Service is bad. And non-sense. I was there for brunch, everything went fine until the bill arrived. I paid it properly (plus tip), and added all the coins I had in my pocket (I'm a visitor and returning home today) from this trip extra to the bill+tip. Waitress told us that she usually did not accept the coins and went back inside. A couple of minutes later, a young lady (supposed manager) said that it was unacceptable and I could take the coins home, telling that actually that was insulting. I was simply astonished by such attitude. I won't be back, neither recommend anyone to go there. There are better options in the neighbourhood, such as Joseph Leonard - Cozy, nice people, amazing food!

I went here the other day since I live very close and was planning to have lunch with my godfather, who also lives nearby. I'm glad we chose Moonshine -- we were seated quickly and we ordered quickly. I got the Chicken Piccata Ravioli, which was delicious. There was plenty of chicken and for $10.50, it was so worth it. I was going to rate it a 4 because the shining star of the dish, the goat cheese filled ravioli, was delicious but they didn't give enough (4 or 5 on the plate, compared to two whole chicken breasts....not that I'm complaining). I asked our waitress if I could order some to go with some of the chicken I brought home, to which they happily obliged. Since I'm eating the leftovers now, I figured I would give them a shout on Yelp. So good! I'm planning to go back with my fiance tomorrow night so she can try. Will do an update after my second meal, but thanks Moonshine for a great for impression!
When I'm in quick need of a lunch fix, I go go to go go. Okay, enough of my lame lines. All that is needed to be said is that the food is quick, tastes delish, and well priced for midtown.

This is a cleverly designed restaurant that has the appearance of an old diner. Apparently menu varies from day to day. The Black Manhattan is a wonderful cocktail concoction. The music is deafening! Asked the waitress if they could turn the music down. She did. It lasted for about five minutes. If having your ear drums blasted out is the Williamsburg idea of a vibe then I'm over Williamsburg. The food here is great just don't expect to be able to talk to anyone at your table without screaming at them!

We love Patsy Grimaldi!  Favorite pizza in Brooklyn, and Patsy is such a nice guy.  Don't bother standing in line at Grimaldi's (no longer owned by Patsy) for the pale imitation when this is the real thing!

ok,..I will start by saying when I lived in NJ and would go after work once a week and the place had different ownership this place was great. Yes its in the hood, but never a problem. Went a few weeks back to check it out with some friends...I was like WTF! The crowd flipped on this place. I felt like I was Mike J Fox in "Back to the Future". food was whack, crowd was really whack . Music and drinks were the best thing here. I have spoken.
The tom yam fried rice is just takes you to a whole different level. It is juicy, fresh and spicy. The staffs are so nice and the they bring the best service.
Best Vietnamese food in the area. Very fast and good service. My kids live eating there

THINY THIN:  It's a pizza so thin, they named it twice!  You can't get a pizza like this anywhere else around here!  The Thiny Thin is basically just a hard crust with no dough, a sprinkle of cheese, and toppings.  You'll need several pieces to fill you up, so kick it off with a few other starters.  The table salads are huge and can be split several ways (at least 2 or 3 for a good sized salad).  Although the wings are good, they were so hot my nose actually ran.  A basket of bread and to-die-for garlic knots comes on the table, but if you're still hungry - try a pasta entree.
Cheese cake is to die for.   Service is quick.  Sandwiches are very good.  For NYC the price is reasonable.  Perfect place to dine before a musical.
I LOVE TINA'S! Thank you Tina for making such yummy food! I tired everything from the empanadas to the pernil. The Moro is AMAZINGGGGG! ALWAYS NEED THE GREEN SAUCE!!!!!

I'm here now, waiting for a 2 top for 1 hour, and then no waiter so the manager comes to take our order (?) wtf... Diet Pepsi comes after 10min... Food still not here... Neil Patrick Harris in da house, who cares I want my damn food! Soooooooo slow... Slow slow!!!

Absolutely fantastic. Friendly service and super-flavorful food... I could have eaten my weight in that hummus, man. They must put crack in it... Perfect in every way. The lamb kebob I ordered was so perfectly cooked and taste Delicious. My mouth is watering just remembering this meal. Well-done, y'all... I'll be back

I'm a Ginger Root regular. I'll confess, I've only ever had the lunch buffet. Unlimited sushi and Chinese for $8?! Being that it's a small buffet, the selection isn't huge, but the sushi is very good and there's a decent variety of sushi and rolls. No sashimi, but that's okay. I'm a sushi fanatic, so I don't end up having the Chinese food too often, but everything I've tried has been excellent. Honestly, the best Chinese food I've had anywhere in Glastonbury. But it's the unlimited sushi that keeps bringing me back!

Dining in at Il Porto is a bad idea. This is strictly a review of the on-site restaurant. My best friend and I are fans of the Spinaci salad. We've ordered it dozens of times for delivery over the past few years. Naturally, when we arrived to eat in house for only the second time in these few years, we ordered the same salad. But this time, we felt sassy. So we asked the waitress if we could add steak to said salad. She said it would be the same price, no problem. That seemed weird, but we rolled with it because she seemed generally bored by our existence and we were starving. What actually arrived was two 16oz steaks, cooked beyond saving. We had ordered the steak to top our salads medium rare, we instead received very well done steaks, no Spinachi salad. We told the waitress, and she half apologized but did not seem to want to take our steaks back. And, again, we were starving: so we ate them. Then the check arrived. It was exorbitant. The manager/owner(?), a man who had been walking outside to yell into his phone right next to the seating area repeatedly throughout the course of our dinner, decided to explain to us exactly why it was our fault that the bored ESL waitress had ruined our order, then told us that he'd only charge us for one of the steaks (he actually charged us for one and a half steaks, but apparently assumed we couldn't do basic math). The whole thing was demeaning and sketchy, and we watched him yell at the waitress through the doors while waiting for our revised check. We didn't argue a second time, because the experience had been icky enough and we just wanted to get the hell out of there. TL;DR: continue to order delivery from Il Porto, sure. But don't go in for dinner. Ever. (Actually, Il Porto, can I recommend that you just totally shut down your dine-in restaurant for good? Because you're bad at it. Really, really bad.)
Had their chicken pot pie and it was great.

My boyfriend and I had always driven by and thought they wrote clever poems on their chalk board outside so it intrigued us to try it out.  We went to get brunch there today. We sat outside which was nice and ordered there "famous bacon bloodys" for $6 which tasted like tomato juice and horseradish. They serve them in smaller glasses than a regular pint. The brunch menu was sub par with chicken salad a wrap and burgers so we decided to play it safe went with a typical turkey burger and their Angus burger. .. When my boyfriends burger and fries came out there was an obvious clump of hair stuck together by what appeared to be boogers. (Barf) Not trying to be a jerk he just pointed it out... she said sorry took the food and 10 minutes later came back with a burger and fries without booger hair.. The food was average but obviously the customer service was poor. The check cane and nothing was taken off. We weren't going to ask but honestly if you want people to be satisfied leaving your restaurant then maybe say sorry for the gross additives and comp the meal or at least something.

Ordered 3 times from this place and the order came out wrong EACH TIME. I was being charged extra for side food that would never be in the delivery bag.Plus I found that the food NEVER taste the same. I don't know if they are changing the chef often but it's over priced for the taste of that food. Won't ever come back.
Your lemonade just saved my life. In fact,  That was one of the BEST lemonades I have ever had. It was so good I just had to have another. All time hangover cure fo' sure.
Great burger but the fries were the best part of the meal. We went in at 1:30 on a Thursday afternoon and sat right down.

It's a cute place.  I live very close so I used to come here a lot to meet friends and have a nice early morning meal. Then I learned more about the French cuisine.   The food is perfectly good but I value a good croissant & a French baguette above all else.  So, if you want really good French food travel into town for Metropolitan Bakery or Meil Patisserie. Otherwise enjoy!

I love this spot in Fitler Square, close to home! I'm really impressed with their extensive menu, Well done Chef! One of my favorite its their Pate sandwich, any sandwich you choose you won't be disappointed. Neighborhood place, cozy atmosphere and French cuisine! What else can you ask for?

This place is amazing! Make sure you start with Chiang Mai Fries (which are amazing!!) and then get the Tom Kha and I finally get the Pad Thai! I had the papaya pad thai and my friend got the traditional pad thai and both were absolutely amazing!

Their rice is SO GOOD ASK THEM TO ADD LIME JUICE with the cilantro rice and then add their queso cheese let me tell you YUMMIEE. I put the veggies in my burrito because I try to not eat meat and honestly its just as filling as putting the steak in! It is pretty pricey. After I get a drink it totals out to like $11. Then I get hungry once I drive home. It's great as a snack or get two if you have a big appetite especially when you havent had dinner. The place is super clean and I think the staff is friendly. They dont rush you and they definitely cater to what you want. Unlike Moes or Chipotle the service is good because they take the time for you to decide what you want and there isnt a huge line all the time. The queso burrito is by far my favorite
Probably the best deal for the best food ever! I had to search for the place but it's well worth it. For the cost, I don't think I've ever found a better deal for food that good. Highly recommend it!

I remember I ate here three years ago with two hot girls and a friend of mine man the food was really good that was the first night I tried habanero sauce whew it was spicy I had like 3 cups of water lol but anyway went really well with the food I ordered I had a chicken salad I think it was good i would definitely go back here

We want it all, decor, service and food.  This restaurant is the bomb!!  My husband and I were in NYC and had only one open night for dinner.  The place we wanted wasn't available and it's easy to go to NYC and spend an hour searching for just the right restaurant only to be disappointed in the end.  I've had that happen. We turned to Yelp to avoid that outcome.  We both used our phones to search.  The way I search on Yelp is if I find something good, I make note, then try to top it.  Once I narrow down my selections, I check out their website.  We enjoy small food quantities, high quality, with an emphasis on artistic handiwork and will pay for it.  Anyway, long story short, we both ended up with Vitae; already a good sign.  We called and made a reservation to be on the safe side.  A few hours later, we entered into a really neat restaurant that smelled delicious.  It's a very modern take on a 70's feel, perhaps with a little rustic and art deco thrown in there.  Just enough of everything so it felt warm and inviting, quaint and extremely hip. You get the picture, we were already happy at the door.  The server was outstanding!  His delivery was excellent, his knowledge of all beverages, down to the knowledge of the casks used in the malt scotches.  He knew the menu well and was helpful in our making selections.  In other words he took his job very seriously.  When he walked away, we looked at each other and said, "That's what I'm talking about."  After ordering, which was difficult in itself because so many things were appealing, the food began to arrive.  It was all fabulous from start to finish.  The meal had to have been one of our finest ever.  If you want it all too, give Vitae a try.

Stopped here on a whim with my husband today and we are very glad we did. The location was very conveniently located off CT-15, which we were traveling on en route to NJ.   The waitress greeted us immediately and was very friendly and welcoming. We were seated and offered drinks right away. My 'small' chicken noodle soup was a HUGE generous portion. I can't even imagine how big the next size up would be! Our food came out in a timely manner and it was all delicious.  I got a half meat bologna on whole wheat and added some fresh mozzarella. Once again, even having ordered half meat, the portion was amazingly generous. I saved half the sandwich to bring home.   My husband got the French dip sandwich (he chose brisket), which typically comes on a hero roll, but they had run out and asked if a hard roll was acceptable to him (it was). His sandwich was actually then served on not one but two hard rolls!  He pretty much had an entire sandwich leftover to bring home.  We also shared a potato knish, which was very good as well. Overall we were extremely happy with our meal here and will definitely try and return whenever we are traveling through the area. Definitely recommend to anyone who loves classic deli food with great friendly service, fair pricing and generous portions.

They say "you can't make a meal out of side dishes."  It's true. The service and fig salad were both phenomenal, but that's about it. Upon entry we were courteously greeted and made our way to the packed bar to get a drink until our table was ready. We were promptly seated and greeted by our friendly server. We started our meal with e delightful fig salad. It was light and refreshing and the vanilla bean vinaigrette was amazing. After that we had the "ricotta." I understand the limitations of ricotta with vegan meals, but they had used way too much lemon in the tofu mixture. The texture was there, but it honestly tasted like Trix cereal. Sorry, vegans, Trix are for kids. From there we an order of the chickpea fries. We were warned ahead of time that the portions would be tapas style meant to share ("to gain the full experience"). The fries came out on a plate that looked like someone just smeared aioli with their finger across it. The fries were stacked perfectly like a little chickpea log cabin... All ten of them. They had the taste, texture, and appearance of Lincoln logs. There was barely enough aioli to cut down the dryness of what I can only assume was reclaimed fried hummus. To cap off our meal we had baby leeks with romesco (Which admittedly I was excited to read as romanesco... Not the same thing) and the heirloom beans. Both tasted wonderful but were laughably small, even as tapas. Throughout this experience we sampled many of the drinks, all of which were served in glasses barely half full, is there a liquor shortage we're unaware of? Is this place supposed to be prohibition themed? No, they actually don't seem to have a theme. From their crystal chandeliers to the green lamps above the bar to the LED lights on the bar and book shelves, from the teal painted walls to the curtained wall with classic black and white films projected on loop, there's a whole lot going on without much to say. Charlie was a sinner, but he also probably had the appetite of a small bird. Guys, I think Charlie was a bird. It is their logo after all.

I went to Ting Wongs for the first time today. I had the young Chow fried rice, it was as good as I have heard! The wonton soup was not what I expected, lots of greens and they were wonton balls... again it was very good! The only thing negative I have to say is... hot tea in a water glass?? Peculiar at best!! I highly recommend this authentic Chinese restaurant! I work in the city and I will be back again and again!!
Brunch...off the hook! Dinner, bar menu...it just goes on!  FABULOUS!

Only ever had the pizza....Sicilian slice is great and as good as advertised...Their regular pizza slice isn't bad, but nothing separating it from other spots in Brooklyn.   Guys that work there are cool and look to keep the line moving.
Went to Amada last week. Had high expectations and was very appointed. The wait staff was pretentious and insincere.  The food was average.

The food and service was excellent! My favorite thing about the menu was the unique offerings on the menu!  We had a fried corn on the cob (delicious and wasn't heavy which is surprising since it was fried) , VLT sandwich (braised and fried veal bacon , lettuce tomato ), octopus salad (yummy), and for dessert blackberry cheesecake with a pretzel bottom (incredible blend of salty and sweet ) and banana bread with bacon and pretzel in it!  The prices were reasonable.  Looking forward to my next visit.
GREAT FOOD!  recommend making a reservation

I couldn't believe my luck coming across this delightful and down to earth honest Southern eatery. My guidebook promised much from this highly rated restaurant and they were spot on. I adore catfish and they served this just cooked with a nicely seasoned crispy crumb. I'm never very sure about grits but was completely bowled over by the addition of cheese and would want them served this way every time. I was then knocked out by the blueberry and rhubarb pie, which was something I'd love to eat again, anywhere. This is one place I will surely make my way to again when I'm next in Brooklyn.
Healthy and fresh

My wife, friend, 12 year old, and I ate at Tink's Restaurant last night and all four of us loved the meal. I had an awesome Grouper Oscar with crab meat, it was lightly breaded and very tasty. My wife had Tuna, friend had snapper with a butter sauce, and 12 year old had a small Ceaser Salad, which was great, and fettuccine Alfredo and ate it all. Prices are a little high but in line for the quality and choices of food. I was able to take a taste of all 4 meals and all of them were outstanding. First time ever that we all agreed that our meals were great and we all would get the same thing again.

My friends and I went to Tuome last night for dinner.  It was delicious (more to follow).  Service was also fantastic.  The waiters were super nice and the chef chatted with us for a while and was great. We ate all of the smalls, one big and one side.  The chicken liver was yummy.  The spring rolls were good but the sauce they came with was fantastic.  The soft shell crab was crispy and light with another yummy sauce.  The pork for two was delicious, although the noodles were a tad spicy for me.  Lastly the corn is amazing.  Hope this restaurant succeeds; they sure were looking great week 1!

I was there on 8/17/14 with some friends. Our waitress was Felecia and she did an awesome job. She was professional, attentive, she gave us suggestions and was on point with our order. The food was good, the view was amazing and we will definitely be returning and recommending this place to our friends.

I certainly cannot complain about the food. It is always great and perfectly seasoned  to leave my taste buds craving for more! Their menu is the main attraction, to me at least. It is honestly the only thing that keeps me returning to the venue.
Hole In the wall.  To crammed for my tastes. I got the egg scramble which came with a side salad.  The side salad wasn't very fresh.
This is our new jam! Just moved to the area and found this gem right down the street. Very small and intimate, food is on point and our waiter was so knowledgeable! We'll be regulars here no doubt.

Great prices on huge portions of food.  If you have a tex men craving, this is the place to go in jersey. Except everyone else knows about it too and you are almost always guaranteed a 30 minute wait.  I've tried almost everything on the menu and it's all good.  Oh yeah, if you want to get a nice buzz going. Get a margherita New Orleans style.  Sneaky strong!

If I could I would give this place zero stars. Stumbled upon it one day by accident and had a pleasant experience, decent food and reasonably priced. Decided to do pick-up on my way home tonight and received the wrong order. I called to report my complaint and instead of an apology all I received was a snotty attitude and an argument insisting I had the correct item and then she hung up on me! I know the item was incorrect since I has previously ordered it. So RUDE and POOR customer service with mediocre food

It was my first time trying sushi and OH MY GAWD was I impressed . California rolls and cucumber rolls were on point -they also  offer a huge selection of meets including chicken skin , eggs rapped in bacon, the Japanese works . While I do not know much about Asian cuisine , I would recommend this place if you're in Philly, China town

Pfft, this place. Very limited options if you have certain dietary restrictions. Be sure to ASK what is actually in the food. My only dietary restriction is pork. No pork, but I can and will eat anything else -- seafood, chicken, gluten, you name it. I get it. Soup dumplings have pork in it, so I wasn't too disappointed that they didn't have any non-pork alternatives to this. So I ask about regular steamed dumplings -- no other meat options, only pork. No worries, I was able to get vegetable dumplings which were decent. I scan over to the fried rice section. I get excited to see "Crab fried rice". There were other kinds too. Chicken fried rice, shrimp fried rice, etc. I confirm with the waitress that it is only crab in the rice, and vegetables here and there. She says there is indeed pork in it. There is pork in a dish called "Crab fried rice". It was not called "Pork crab fried rice." Not "House special crab fried rice" (which I would assume have other meats). Just CRAB FREAKIN' FRIED RICE. I found it odd, but I shrug and politely ask her "Would it be possible to just have crab in it? I'm really only looking for just crab in fried rice. OR are there any fried rice dishes that have NO pork in it?" First off, no. They have no fried rice dishes without pork in it (no matter what it says). Second, I have never gotten the RUDEST face from anyone ever (Sidenote: I live in NYC -- I don't find rudeness to be uncommon). She gave me a look as if I ordered fried rice without rice in it. With extreme hesitation and a few more seconds of her rude and condescending look, she agreed. Brings me my dish. The rice had nothing in it. Had some onions. Eggs here and there. But that was about it. Crab fried rice is the most expensive rice they have, and it didn't even have crab in it. CONCLUSION:  At this place, all meats are pork. If you order chicken, shrimp, crab, or any meat... you will not get it. You will get pork. Or nothing at all.

The food was decent and cooking on the rock is fun. The steak on the rock should have been marinated or seasoned bc at the end of the meal it is basically beef cooked on a griddle. My husband ended up taking it home and plans to season it and finish it on the grill. I had the salmon & baked potato. Nothing special - I expected a more fresh & flavorful meal since we were in VT during the summer. Same held true for the salad bar. It was a decent bar that include the basics of what you would be looking for. I just felt like everything should be farm fresh at this time of year in such a rural, country area.   Prices were extremely reasonable. 24 oz porter house was $21.95 and the maple salmon was $16.95. Would have been happy to pay more for fresher/more flavorful food, but at this price you get what you pay for.

Well, this place was given a rare rating in my guidebook and I couldn't agree less. The restaurant is a self-styled food lovers paradise but the palate was mediocre. I had rhubarb gazpacho which had not been anywhere near a gorgeously tart piece of rhubarb. I followed this up with (too thickly rolled) ravioli stuffed with ricotta and nettle, which lacked any of the zing associated with nettles, not least because it had been masked with a far too rich caramelised butter sauce. I tell people where to eat and where not to, this is in the latter category.

The food is truly delish here but I just cannot give a rating above 3 stars to any restaurant especially a real Italian place when they do not drain the pasta well! Please realize that the water in the pasta kills the sauce !!! Makes for a very unpleasant eating experience. Otherwise this place rocks the food. This visit I had the shrimp and veal parm combo. Veal was very tender and flavorful, the shrimp a bit over breaded and not as flavorful. Also tried the plain cheese pizza and it is good old school Northern Jersey pie! Will come back again but will ask the server to make sure the pasta is well drained before sauced!

Soooo... Where to start... Started the evening with amazing cocktails (Pink Picket Fence and the Rosemary vodka cocktail that I can't think of the name (too many cocktails). Let me just say, they were amazing. I'm born  and raised in New Orleans and these drinks were top notch. When we walked in we noticed the huge portions so only order two entrees and an appetizer for three people. Which was WAY too much food. We probably have enough to all eat again. We ordered the mash potatoes with mushroom gravy (amazing), the honey chicken and pickles sandwich (fucking amazing), and the mushroom and Mac and cheese (holy balls, fucking amazing). We also ordered a pickle sampling. Our waitress (who was adorable and nice!) said we should hold out for dessert and I'm so glad we took her advice. The biscuit bread pudding is TO DIE FOR. It was insane. I am so excited to heat up the left overs. The only thing I have against this place is that it is so freaking dark in there. I get it, you want a certain ambiance, but I had a really hard time reading the menus. It's really not a big deal when you measure up to how good the food was. I wish I could rate this restaurant higher than 5 stars. I've been to a lot of great restaurants but this hits the top 5 I think. Highly recommend!

Great food/service/decor, a little bit pricey but nothing crazy, outside seating, BYOB & you can have wine delivered :D love this place.  Parking sucks on the weekend & it can get crowded. We ate Mahi advocado (3 small) tacos app, crab cake entree w/ a tasty chipotle sauce, surf & turf entree perfectly cooked scallops w/ delicious short ribs & cheesy polenta.

I've had a whole bunch of the famous cheesesteaks in Philly, so when I heard about this place I was skeptical. I ordered my first steak classic, whiz & onions. It was the best I've ever had. Cheesesteaks are a humble food, but Delilah's ups the ante with great bread (no pillowy garbage) and steak that's cooked to order (not sitting on heat before you get there). A small fry is massive, and they're crinkle-cut because Delilah's loves you. This is a true Philly cheesesteak, not just in name but by design, owned by a hometown dude and featuring a full wall mosaic mural by renowned Philadelphia artist Isaiah Zagar. Again, the details matter, and Delilah's Steaks gets them right.

BELIEVE THE HYPE.  Man I love this pizza.  I started going here way before food network and the popularity and the pizza is good.  Its so good it will ruin you for other pizza trust me.  It doesn't help that Lombardi's has some really hot waiters too.  Make sure you get plenty of the sauce and try the chopped garlic.
the pizza is fair at best

Called up and ordered food, one of the workers picked up and took my order and said to come in ten minutes.  When I got there, he said there was no order and told me that I did not call (basically calling me a liar) then I showed him the number on my phone and that the call lasted 12 seconds.  He said maybe I called and didn't say anything? These workers are rude and need to get organized. Apparently they have short-term memory issues too.  Advice  when ordering food - get the persons name, so they can't lie when you get there!

Found this great place on our first trip to New York.  It became our gathering spot.  A great place to sit and have a drink or dine.  The out door patio was a wonderful place to enjoy the evening with our friends ( great NYC atmosphere ) The owner Graham is really a fantastic guy -- knew our names right away - made us feel right at home. He also makes a mean cocktail. Went out of his way for us. Thank you ! All the food was very fresh and really amazing.  The burgers, mac n cheese, home made tater tots, tacos and fries were off the charts.  There was not an item we ordered that didn't hit a home run in taste and presentation. We will definitely come back to see our friend Graham and to dine and drink in his fine establishment. Out standing!!

Everytime I'm in the area I stop by here. It's the best! - seasonal strawberry lemonade is super delicious. It's a nice balance of sweet, tart, and is just generally very refreshing. - the pulled pork: this came highly recommended by the staff at urban cookhouse,but I just didn't prefer it. Mine was inexplicably served with a side of salsa. Don't get me wrong, the salsa's good, but it didn't pair well with the pulled pork. Also comes with 2 slices of white bread (no orange :( roll).  As an FYI the "fork and knife" section of the menu come with a side of salad (I'm guessing this changes seasonally, but in my case a broccoli salad with grapes and a sweet dressing & Mac and cheese which is solid, but not out of this world good). -the downhome: ham & pineapple is smoky and just the right amount of salty-sweet. When the turkey is hot, it's really good, but when it starts to cool down, it gets a little dry. Live this place clean good healthy food. This is as healthy as it gets for takeout. Also ordered catering from them it's legit.

Finally I have a minute to review one of my absolutely favorite spots in Bay Ridge.  Every time me and my boyfriend visiting Campania, we have such a pleasing time. Efficient service, delicious food, cozy atmosphere, and last but not least, is the music. LOVE IT! They play soul music and oldies...Al Green, Frank Sinatra.. not too loud, not too quiet, very tasteful like the place itself:-) And just a few words about  Jimmy- Professionalism, Charisma, Smile:-) With Love, Ammon and Liliya.

Very fresh chicken tenders, though I imagine they were pre made.  Tomoato soup delcicous.  And lots of tvs on different stations, so that was convenient for those in the group who wanted yo watch news and others, a race.

This place was amazing. The decor is really fantastic, the reclaimed wood and antique vibe. Loved the betsy ross flag in the front room, as well as the eagle behind bar. The book shelf with the POS system and check arriving in a small book was a great little touch. Food was excellent, my date and I shared the squash soup, mussels, duck fat fried potatoes, and sautéed spinach. Everything was amazing and cooked to perfection. Timing was excellent to and our waitress was very sweet. The drinks were great. All around this was one of the best restaurants I have eaten at.

Don't judge a book by its cover, and in Makoto's case, don't judge a restaurant by how it looks on the outside. The food is incredible, the seafood is fresh, and the service is impeccable. And for all-you-can eat sushi and hot items from the kitchen for $22.50--drinks included!--it can't be beat. It's a 45-minute drive (without traffic) from Manhattan and well worth the trip!
The food was great, waiter are very nice and helpful, the place is clean， quite and Comfortable，just little bit overprice ,but still will go there again

Oh geez. Where to start. Something nice first: the owners put a lot of thought in to the looks of this place and it has a very cool vibe. But the food is just really bad. We had several appetizers. Ceviche was good, but the tuna and watermelon had no taste at all and the gazpacho actually tasted like dirt. Like a handful of soil. The tacos were no better. I had a chicken taco which was very dry. I also had a fish taco and it had raw jalapeños in it. Which is fine, but they weren't listed in the description. So it was a really surprising bite. The acoustics are also really terrible. Couldn't hear my friend right next to me. We wanted to like this place but probably won't be back.
CRAP service on a not-busy Saturday afternoon!!!  Over-priced+poor service=no thanks!!! The only good thing about this joint is their french fries....

We had lunch today at the weekend buffet brunch.  The food is amazing -- everything was wonderful, but especially the eggplant, and the carrot/pineapple cake, and the BBQ sliders, and the Caprese salad and the green beans, and the friendly staff.
Best pizza in Morris County!!!

Went to Fuel for takeout. Paid with a credit card. After I signed the receipt and gave it back to the cashier, she wrote in a tip. Found out when I checked my bank statement. Called the restaurant and eventually received a refund. Restaurant gave the excuse that receipts get mixed up. The reality was that the cashier knowingly stole money in the form of a tip on a credit card charge. Food tasted fine (ordered a salad).

Just found my new "go to" spot in this place. Being there was like being on an afternoon vaykay! Very cool menu options. I went with the lobster with green (I know - boring - but I'm watching calories) The amount of lobster that was on my salad was incredible! My husband had the fish & sweet potatoe fries. He loved it as well! Can't wait to be back! And my guess is that the one earlier review that was negative - probably came from a uppity person because how could you be so unhappy with a gem like Shad Row

Ended up here by accident and will be coming back on purpose - and often! Happy, clean, friendly atmosphere. Fresh, healthy,  AMAZING food ranging from traditional favorites to more exotic ones. Very reasonable. The grilled calamari was light and delicious. The dolmades are hands-down the best I've ever had. Went with 7 people and had appetizers, main courses, and desserts and everything was perfect. Also loved the table visit by the owner!
Really really good food. Service was great and it's not what you imagine when you think of a diner..more upscale. lots of options to choose from. Will definitely make this a regular spot.

Don't understand why all the good reviews. ordered the dragon roll and didn't realize their version doesn't have eel in it. rice was undercooked which is the worst thing on top of dry non seasoned sushi rice. kinjo does have decent wings but as a japanese place it's pretty mediocre for the price.

We enjoyed everything! From the service,  to the decor,  to the food.  We decided on apps - calamari,  figs, and bufola on focacio bread and a small pizza.  Our palates and tummies were pleased!   Looking forward to returning and enjoying a main course.

****update***** While I haven't been back, I did receive a message from the manager of Crow and Pitcher apologizing for my experience there and offering to make it up to me with brunch or dinner on them. I think that restaurants that pay attention to their reviews and service are great and I applaud their effort to improve. If going to the neighborhood again, I may take them up on the offer. Went here yesterday for brunch with a couple friends. it was not very crowded, no one sitting inside when we arrived, and we wished they had tables for 3 outside. They had a two top with 3 chairs but it would have been really crowded. If you are just two people the outdoor seating is nice. We asked a server for recommendations and she suggested the Brunch Burger. She said it was decadent but really good. I ordered it. my friends ordered the poached eggs and the french toast. Both the burger and the french toast were very large dishes but the poached eggs seemed like an appetizer in comparison, though he said they were really good. The bloody mary's are pretty good, they do come with bacon, fyi all vegetarians. I wanted to love my indulgent burger. But it was WAY overcooked. I had asked for medium rare and it was well well done, rubbery and tasted burnt. the sausage was also overcooked. The egg on top was done nicely but it couldn't save the burger. The fried french toast "buns" were also fried a bit too far. So was the french toast my other friend got. Burnt deep fried dough is not very good. I was so disappointed in the burger. I didn't send it back because I thought it would still be ok but I really regret not sending it back because I didn't enjoy that meal at all.
You want Brooklyn brick oven pizza?  Look no further...there is always parking and the vibe fits all with rooftop dining, sports bar, or intimate dining.... Enjoy
Overall mediocre food. Pat's and Geno's are both overrated. The lesser of the 2 evils is Pat's. Don't waste a trip to Philly.
Best pork bun!!! We love their ramen, the soup it's not as strong as totto's, but we love ippudo's ramen soup better!

I really, really like this place. Banging ambiance. Fast and friendly service. Lotion in the bathroom. All they're missing is french fries. Kudos for the delicious, fresh, very well seasoned crab roll...with 2 types of creamy aioli. But I could have really used some french fries. The potatoes were probably organic and the broccoli was not over cooked. For $2 I could have really used an entire ear of corn instead of half an ear, but because y'all looked out for the parents with a baby high chair I forgive. All in all, a great restaurant, but come y'all...add some fries to the menu. Peace.

So close to awesomeness.  The location is perfect with indoor and outdoor seating.  It is very nicely decorated and the wine selection is great. Lovely place with excellent service. Jorge is a fabulous waiter and will really look after you. The ossobuco was melt-in-your-mouth tender. Loved the shaved broccoli salad. Also great wine selection. I will definitely go back for wine and dessert!

Consistently great. I just moved from San Francisco, and I used to eat at the one downtown. The West Hartford location is just as good. My favorites orders are the Chinese Chicken Chop Salad (480 cal), and the Japanese Pan Noodles with Steak (790 cal). Each are about $9 and great for lunch or dinner. Service has always been excellent, and polite. They offer takeout, so save yourself time if you want to pick something up. I'm pretty good at complaining, but this place is definitely an exception :)
Very tender steak.  Wish it was seasoned just a little more but the fresh mozzarella more than makes up for it. :-)

I will NEVER return to this place.  I just left there without finishing eating after witnessing a racist incident by one of the employees.  A guy behind the counter, who was perhaps in his 40s, was hassling a young Spanish boy (who was no older than maybe 12).  He was telling the kid how "this is the US. We speak English, and you need to learn English too."  The kid had done nothing wrong and was about to leave.  He asked the guy a question and was treated like dirt in return.  My girlfriend complained to the manager about it, who couldn't have cared less either.

Really some of the best Chinese food I've ever had. Very fresh. The best items on the menu are: - The Wonton Noodle Soup (with Beef Stew is always a good option, and the roast pork or roast duck a good second option) -Pan Fried noodle with Shrimp, so ginger-y, garlic-ky and delicious -Sui Mei is tasty -steamed roast pork buns. Really nice service too. Way to go HK.
The worst vanilla shake ever.  Do they know to put syrup in it ? Ice cream plus milk is NOT a shake. It is ice cream and milk.  So disappointing. Zero stars on the shake.

I got the buffalo chicken salad it was really yummy! The chicken pieces were small it wasnt big chicken fillets so the flavor meshed really well with the lightness of the lettuce and feta cheese. The service was really good overall great experience. My friend got the pasta she loved it and my sister loves their mac and cheese!

Came here with my boyfriend for his birthday , no disappointment here. Brisket was  on point. Mac n cheese  and whiskey sour pickles were finished before we got started on the jerk ribs. Siracha wings were ok, but  the coleslaw was amazingly l light and refreshing. I think we will be here a fee more times to try out the rest.

Visiting from Rochester NY and found Giorgo's on yelp. Staff was extremely friendly and was able to sit our 8 person group quickly. BYOB was awesome perk and the food did not disappoint.Our dinners were excellent, portions were fair as was the price. Owner came out and greeted us during our meal which was a nice touch. Restaurant is in safe charming part of the city and would highly recommend to tourist and locals alike.

A neat atmosphere, decent food, okay service. The place is located in an old historical house (the Deming house).  If you take a second to walk around, it's kind of neat.  I ordered an appetizer and a beer and sat inside at the bar (plenty of outside seating also available).  It was busy, as it was a Friday evening, but it took me a while to get my menu and to get my check at the end.  The food was good,  minus the hair I found in the sliders that I ordered.  The staff is friendly.  I went there a few days later and ordered another appetizer and beer and it was slower so that meant better service (and no hair this time).  They are dog friendly, as you see many people with leased dogs on the patio.  They have live music on certain evenings on the patio.  It appears to be the place to go in Wethersfield.

Ordered for delivery. Food was delivered very quickly however was disappointing. General TSO chicken was very oily, the chicken with cashew had a strange aftertaste, hot & spur was decent. Would not order from there again.
Was just at this restaurant again and they have changed the menus substantially.  Food was subpar and will not go back.  It is a shame given how good it used Tao be.
I have been here twice and both times I had really bad experience..The food was bad and the staffs were very rude and unfriendly :(

Go elsewhere for breakfast. Although the wait staff was nice, the food was a waste of $50(!!). The potatoes came out undercooked- which they corrected. Hummus was the most bland I've ever had. Coffee refills are not free! We got topped off and got charged for a full cup! That's BS.

FABULOUS Chinese food. I have been searching for great Chinese for one year in the Tom's River area. I have finally found it. Not too salty is the first thing. They really know how to make Shrimp with Lobster Sauce. Not the cornstarch laden goop most all restaurants try to pass off these days. Theirs has a lot of ground pork, eggs , green onion and very large shrimp. Every dish we have had is delicious. Reminds me of eating in Chinatown. I would recommend trying it. The only complaint we have is they are really not an eat in restaurant. They have a few small tables, but not a formal restaurant. We can only hope they move in that direction, but for now I am so happy to have great food that I can live with take out.

*For all the veggie people out there* The vegan pizza menu is awesome here- their vegan ricotta and vegan sausage on the simply red pie is so delicious. My boyfriend and I go here a few times a month, not a cheap bill for pizza but definitely worth it every time.   *I love the chili oil they serve to put on top of the pizza
The stir fry is really good. They use fresh vegetables and meat. If the stir fry comes with sauce, make sure to ask for light sauce, or else they will put a ton of sauce on the dish.

Neon sign said open, dude was making pizzas, there were pizzas in the counter - and they refused to acknowledge I existed, immediately kicking me out even though there were 15 other patrons. Very rude and completely unnecessary.

First time here. Had a coupon. Good martini's. Nice salads. My salmon alla senape was very good. Wife's salmon granchio was too salty. Service was above average with friendly staff. We will return at some point. Nicer atmosphere inside than you would expect when viewing place from the outside.

I have been a regular at Cucina for years and have brought many people there and everyone loved it.  The waiters are efficent and very helpful with making decisions as to what you might want to try if they are new specials.  Charlie was extremely helpful and efficent.  The Executive Lounge is warm and inviting and happy hour is fabulous.  Gabby, one of the bartenders, is right on top of things.  Have never had a bad meal and Chef Constantino is out asking the patrons if they are pleased.   I would definitely recommed this restaurant.  It is very family friendly with Chef Henry, the pizza man, as the kiddie magnet!  The atmosphere is very much like Tuscany!  Outdoor patio is a plus!  Make sure you ask for Charlie or Eddie.  I love this place!

I discovered this place 3 years ago and I thought it was great. However, fast forward to today and the quality of the food has definitely gone hill.  If you guys are trying it for the first time now, you might not notice but it used to be a lot better.  I hope that it was just an off day.

it's one of the better places for hot pot but somewhat overpriced. the lighting and loud music reminds me of a club which is pretty horrendous for a hot pot dinner. the sauce selection is also lacking.

Went for dinner here with my family and the place was just okay. I got the maki combo which was decent. I mean, the maki combo is a classic sushi menu so they shouldnt really mess that up. My brother got the chicken teriyaki, which in my opinion tasted realllly bad. Honestly, getting the chicken teriyaki at sarku instead of from here would be a much smarter choice.
This place is amazing from the minute you walk in until you walk out.  The beer was light how I like it and the flatbread was amazing.  The waitress was incredible, I will definitely be back!

We go here more often than I thought we would due its proximity to our home and delicious food, plus it's on Savored and Scout mob so that makes it better value for money - without those it is a little on the pricy side for what you get. I ordered the rack of lamb, it was slightly overlooked but the flavors of this dish made up for that fact. It was a savory, delectable meal. I purchased a Groupon for this restaurant and was pleasantly pleased with my lunch experience.  As other Yelpers have cited, this restaurant is desolate around 2ish. I had the entire restaurant to myself which was awesome. Service was good (just one waitress), decor is blegh in my opinion, and prices are reasonable. JUST GET SOME DAMN SHAWARMA ON THE MENU!
This is definitely over-rated. The hot and sour soap is particularly disappointing. It is so watery and tasteless. It is $7:00 for a bowl per person. Most of the dishes are small portions.

ok. I am an official "regular" as they know my drink before I even sit down. With that said, officially my fav place. Always meet my friends from Jersey here. Good food. music varies from jazz to R@B. Bartenders vary like any other place and I have my favs like any body else. Sangria made by Monica is the absolute best!  My one wish is that they kept a dress code here. Sometimes I feel like there is a tug of war with they types of crowds that come here. Its interesting.

My absolute favorite restaurant in crown heights. The wait staff are so helpful, and really cool. I've been here way too many times to count! I love everything on the menu, many do not know they have brunch, and boy is it ever deeeeeelicious. Everybody I've taken here LOVES this place. Don't miss out!

This is my third time eating here during my meal break.  Wow!  Good eats!  I usually get either the shrimp Ceviche or Ceviche de Mariscos which was the best I had in a very long time since I was kid staying at my grandparents in South America.  Phenomenal!!  I don't eat seafood just anywhere either, but here- anytime!  Seafood is very hard to pull off and make it flavorful if you all me.  And if you ask them to make your food extra spicy hot, they will oblige you, and it comes out perfect!  Que rico!!  Today I had them make me a Saltado de Pechuga without the fries, which is not on the menu, but I asked them to do it, and I asked them to make it extra hot-  omg, perfection in a dish!  YUMMY!  Too bad I'm working, a draft beer would have gone nicely with this dish and rice.  I'll definitely be back here again!! P.s. just found out that the draft beer doesn't work, but they still have bottled beer and nice selection of liquor.  Definitely should not be a deal breaker since the food is so banging! P.s.  My bad!  This is the restaurant in Kearny that I was reviewing, but don't fret, they're both owned by the same family and from what I heard, the food is excellent at both places!  The address here is 307 Kearny Ave. Kearny, NJ

The food here is definitely fresh and delicious and while the service could have been better, it wasn't really bad.  We had to signal for the server's attention a bit, rather than being approached but when we signaled, the response was immediate. But what gives this place just two stars is that they don't turn on the AC.  I'm sorry, it's the dead of summer in NYC, the AC needs to be on.  They had the front windows open with two small fans on the sill blowing in.  The fans are the type you'd use at home.  All that did was blow the hot air into the restaurant and not even much of it.  There was another fan of the same type in the back facing the front.  If they are trying to save money by not using AC then they should at least have ceiling fans installed.  It was not even the hottest of evenings when we were there and it was still extremely uncomfortable.  Really blows the experience. We won't go back until the weather cools or perhaps if the front windows are closed we might step in to see if AC is on then.  The place only has the one exposure, the front, so there's no cross breeze.  Dog and Duck and Claret also open their windows and don't always use AC but at least they both have double exposures so if there's any breeze at all, it will be a bit better.  But even those places close up and run AC when it's very hot and humid. It's a shame about the heat because otherwise Venturo really is a unique little spot in the 'hood, nicer than most.  But being comfortable and not feeling like you're about to pass out in the NYC summer should be a no brainer.

Great food, awesome menu selection , the service was absolutely great . I had the steak meal and platanos as well as the appetizer sampler .. all of it was cooked fantastically and addicting!! The cafe con leche is also a must have!

I used to eat here fairly regularly.  Last time I found out the entree I like went from $18 up to $24 -- that's a 33% increase! and the appetizer I get went up 25%.  I know prices increase but this seems extremely high.
I really love their food and the atmosphere is really nice, just needs a little more elbow room but it's a very nice restaurant and again the food is delicious. Their prices are fair.

Nothing special, I definitely don't see what the big deal is about this place, it's WAY too crowded for such a small place you're basically on top of each other and that's not appealing to me. The service sucked and we had 4 different waiters come to the table, all with bad attitudes. The food was okay once again nothing special. Won't be going here again if it's up to me!

I came a long way from Virginia Beach, VA to enjoy a weekend out in about around NYC. We don't have many Thai restaurants in VB, so my friend decided to take me to Pok Pok. After hearing about how great the fish sauce wings I wanted to try more of their menu. We arrive around 5:30 pm and the hostess said it would be a 40 minute wait. No problem, so we put our names down and head across the street to get a couple drinks and try the wings at their sister bar, The Whiskey Soda Lounge. After 30 minutes, I go over to check and the hostess said our table will be ready in about 10 minutes. So we close out our tab at the Whiskey Soda Lounge and head over. We sit down and receive menus and water. Our Server, MATT G., again his name is MATT G., never introduced himself and gave such a bad attitude, it made me hesitant to try the place. I gave him the benefit of the doubt because my friend and I also waited tables while attending college and just thought maybe he was busy, and will come around. I ordered the Khanom Jiin Sao Naam, and the menu is misleading because I was under the impression it would be hot noodles. I took two bites and immediately regretted my decision. My friend got the  Muu Paa Kham Waan, I tried that and it was delicious. Now as a prior server, I understand to make the customer feel like they have an enjoyable dining experience. I would expect sympathy from a fellow server, but alas I was surprised to MATT G.'s reaction. I asked MATT G. if there was any way I could exchange the dish I had with another entree, while telling him it's not what I expected.  Instead of apologizing and asking what he could do to make the experience more enjoyable, his first question was "Well, What did you expect?" Taken aback, I answered honestly, and said I thought the dish would be hot, it didn't say in your menu that these noodles would be cold. After adjusting his tampon like he just started his period, Without saying anything else, he takes the dish away from the table, puts a menu down in front of me. I tell him I'll just have the same dish my friend is having. He rolls his eyes and takes the menu back up. At that point I lost my entire appetite and just wanted the check and the meal to go. Another server brings my new entree out, and I immediately ask for the box and the check. The other server brings me back a box and I quickly empty it into the container. We sit there for another 15 minutes with both our plates empty and MATT G. still hasn't come by with the check. He finally comes and clears off the table, still with the worst attitude like he heard he just got Syphilis. After we pay the check, I still say thank you, and he doesn't say a word to me. He doesn't say anything to my friend either. I give the food that I did try - the fish sauce wings and the Muu Paa Kham Waan (boar collar meat) 5 stars. I want to give MATT G. just the single server out of the entire restaurant 0 Stars for service. Hey MATT G., if you want to serve tables, treat your customers as you want to be treated. Not like they are a nuisance or a hassle. Because although the food was delicious (besides the cold noodles) no one wants to be treated like shit when they go out and pay money for a dining experience.

Honestly I've been going here since I was 4 since I live 2 blocks down but as of recently I feel like the food isn't as good as before. I ordered a penne vodka sauce pasta and 2 slices. Fist of they ended up giving me spaghetti with burnt tasteless chicken and the slices well the crust was burnt black. Then to top it off the workers were drinking beer which I found unprofessional and disgusting. I honestly don't know what happened to the place I feel like they've let go.

I would say this is the best seafood restaurant in Philly it really is that good. Me and my sister did the prefix menu and neither of us were disappointed.  We love fish and seafood but both are generally not a fan of squid or octopus, somehow both of tried the octopus the chef prepared and we loved it.  I don't think I'm comfortable saying I love squid or octopus now, but I would eat it again if it came from little fish. Also I wasn't expecting much from dessert since obviously the specialty is fish, but the dessert was equally good as the rest of the meal. The service and ambiance was perfect for a quiet little dinner. The restaurant is ideal for a date night since it has an open kitchen you can watch the chef cook and smell what he is creating will getting tipsy on your byob beverage of choice.
The food here is excellent. On top of that the service was attentive, warm, and helpful. I highly recommend this place. Worth every penny!

Decent selection on the beer. The mixed six pack is a nice option, but some of the beer I chose tasted a bit stale. Some that I've had and enjoyed, just didn't taste quite right. Sign by the register was funny, but perhaps should have been a warning?- Maybe a bit old? One beer was clearly marked as expiring in June, when it's august. I steamed clear of that one due to brewers labeling. If so, maybe just lack of turnover in stock, but just a caution that this may be a better place for some Corona than Victory or Dogfish. Haven't tried the food yet but might be back based on other reviews.

food was delicious i have nothing but great things to say - drinks were even better - i had this watermelon mojito and it just hit the spot.  i had the server surprise me since I couldn't decide on what to get (it all just sounded so good!), anyhow he picked the dish with the poached eggs, chips and i think it came on a griddle - whatever it was, it was amazing and blew my taste buds out of the water... top notch place here.

It's entirely possible that I'm self-hating, but there's a reason these reviews (or on most other joints) are so split. Just look who's writing them. Would you really trust their taste? There's a reason why this place is where it is - on top of an Urban, and on the same street as SEA. I don't think anyone who has a clue about Brooklyn visits anything but the entrance to the L on this street. It's perched itself up high but all it is, is perpendicular to SEA. That should tell you enough. High concept, execution problems. Great ideas in the contrast of dish ingredients but execution was a problem all around. From the two, "It's my first day" servers to the arson-suggestive cocktail to the undercooked monkfish, the experience left me wishing I came on a better, more together evening. Poutine, peas, and schnitzel executed nicely, nice flavors to mesh. Poor with the not-quite-fermented enough celery broth, lacking barnyard complexity or proper viscosity to hold up to the crisp, gummy monkfish, porgy that yearned to be elevated. My mezcal-based apple cocktail tasted like what happens when a scorned farmer's wife finds out he's been screwing the organic lamb instead of her, and sets the entire orchard ablaze. Oh, and the banh mi poutine was introduced to the table as "a fusion of Korean and Canadian dishes" - to which I responded, "banh mi is Vietnamese". "Oh, shit. That's a big mistake, huh?" Yup.

The hype is real! With great reviews and high expectations visiting Sandra's for the first time, it would have been exceptionally easy for it to fall short. Sandra's met expectations and then quickly exceeded them with perfectly cooked food bursting with flavor. Everything I tasted was outstanding. Not only that, but the service was some of the best I've ever experienced - personal, caring and attentive.

I had the cheesesteak with friend onions for lunch today and it was absolutely delicious!  Best cheesesteak I've had in a long time.  Not only was the food terrific but the staff and owner were incredibly friendly.  I had such a great experience here, this is definitely going to be my top destination for lunch in the area!  Great food, great prices, very friendly staff and ownership.

I was left dissatisfied! After being born & raised in Israel, and eating Falafel quite often, this place here was a disappointment. I've been in the U.S. 4yrs now, mainly between Chicago & Atlanta, I've had fantastic falafels in both those cities. But my Philly experience didn't quite make the cut. After searching for the best Falafel in town, I came up on this place. DONT BELIEVE THE HYPE! The sandwich was dry, the falafel balls are dry and lack flavor, and the salads need some hint of lemon juice like authentic Israeli salads. I asked for spicy, and I'm 100% there was nothing spicy on my sandwich. Over all, not a good experience, would never recommend it to others!!! If ever in Atlanta, try Pita Palace! They have all the authentic Israeli salads made fresh daily! They also have schwarma & schnitzel! And is run by israelis....YUMMY!

I wish I could give zero stars. In no way would I ever consider this to be authentic Mexican food. Bland in every way possible. Seemed like someone made a microwave meal in the back and brought it to me on a plate. Terrible terrible and EXPENSIVE. Save yourself a bad experience and go elsewhere. Even taco bell would have been a better meal.
