Mashed potato bacon pizza is awesome!  I have tried many other places throughout the country, there are always different variations of this pie but I feel Bar has it nailed down.
Food was delicious. I had the gyro combo plate and it was plenty of food and very good. They are very friendly and the restaurant is very clean. I would go back again next time I am in town.
Best Italian food I've ever had!  Cheap bill everytime! Try the Chicken Parm!

Terrific little neighborhood place! Came in Saturday night and really enjoyed dinner & wine. In truth, my smoked chicken with red beans & rice was a little on the cool side, but tasted so good, I happily ate it anyway. My friend loved the fried chicken and the biscuits and turkey smoked collard greens were the best I've ever tried. Wait staff are charming, energetic and fun, and the chef, who is from Natchez, Mississippi came by to ask how we were enjoying our food. I normally squirm when that happens, but this guy is courteous and charismatic. My one gripe would be that the price of a bottle of wine runs high -$38 and up, whilst the food is in generous portions and very reasonably priced. It would be nice if they had a couple of cheaper wine options. However, that is the only complaint, because this is good quality food, cooked with care and pride, which is the main thing really, right?

This was our second time eating here for dinner!  Very accommodating staff who handled our group of 7! Very friendly, efficient and knowledgeable of the menu!! This was their last night before closing for vacation so they they had limited numbers of the entrees-only one lamb dish and two chicken-so we had to opt for the veal medallion.  It was slightly over cooked to my liking, however the side dish was excellent.  Pork cheeks with pasta was outstanding along with the chicken.  Kudos to the hostess as she was able to secure the large group for outside seating even though they do not take reservations specifically for that area!   Will definitely be back!  Felt special as the head chef came out to spend some time talking to us and thanking us for our business!!
Simple good burgers.  A New Haven staple.

I have been eating here for 25 years. It is a Hartford landmark as far as I am concerned. Run by the carbone family for 75 years and as good as the 1st time I went. Caesar salad made table side with dressing prepared almost from scratch while you watch. Great pasta dishes for vegetarians and plenty of fantastic meat and fis dishes as well. Banana foster prepared and set on fire ramble side is a great finisher. Dig it!!
Stopped in for a meal before a show at the Forrest Theater. Service was excellent and the food was top notch. Ricotta to start was delicious.

We went to Ginza after learning that a nearby sushi place that we wanted to go to first was closed. The interior was pleasing and surprisingly chic, despite its location. the waitrons were nice enough and easy to get a hold of. The sushi and the food was delicious! Presentation was great and we were wowed with the signature rolls that we ordered. We ordered hot tea as well, and were pleased with the attentiveness of the staff at keeping our cups filled. The most disappointing part of the meal was the wait. My party ordered twice seperate times, with hour waits between the orders. The first time, we ordered takoyaki and three rolls of sushi -- we expected to wait a little bit but were astounded at how long it took to get out food. We did not come during a full dinner rush either -- it was Sunday night at 7PM. We weren't satisfied with the first order, so we got one more roll of sushi. We ended up waiting for another hour -- still very hungry -- and ended up getting seaweed salad to make up for it. We were happy with the food. We were still willing to order food at the end, but we were afraid of waiting another hour to eat and decided to leave. Ginza makes great sushi and has great food -- but our visit was marred by really long waiting times. I thought the sushi was also a little overpriced ($15 per signature roll? Wow) and there are other deals in nearby areas. But it was a good visit all in all.

I've been going to bleu sushi since it opened and I must say the quality of fish is great and everyone is so nice and friendly and delivery is always quick. However, with all these positives I only give it 3 stars because now that bleu sushi has been here a while the amount of food you receive for what you pay for is just not equal.   I always order sashimi either as a sashimi appetizer or sashimi chirashi or a la carte.  The sashimi pieces are about half the size as other sushi places but they charge the same price.  This made sense when they had their $1.00 a piece special but now that everything is back to the regular price it's just not worth it.  I will frequent other sushi places that have the same quality but give more for my money like yellowtail sushi or sumo sushi.
My waiter Will was really pleasant, nice smile and very friendly. The place was very chill. Food tasted good. Also, the owner was really nice and awesome. Awesome place!

My husband and I went in for lunch yesterday and were pleasantly surprised. We were fans of the previous restaurant on this site, Asian bistro, so we were disappointed when it closed. We wanted to give its successor a shot and I'm certainly glad we did! The first thing we noticed was the gorgeous decor. It's very tastefully decorated with two dining rooms--we were surprised at how large the second one was! The waitstaff was attentive for the most part--it took a while to get our check, but we weren't in any rush, so it wasn't a huge issue. I attribute the slowness to the fact that we were the only table in the restaurant (understandable at 2pm on a Sunday afternoon) and they wanted to give us our space. Our waiter was very knowledgeable about the menu and gave recommendations, even going so far as to pull out the special "secret" menu with the more authentic dishes on it (usually reserved for customers who are more familiar with authentic Chinese food) when my husband mentioned that he was hoping to try Szechuan hot pot. We started with the Peking Duck roll appetizer and I also had a bowl of wonton-egg drop soup ($2ish). The soup was average; no better or worse than any other restaurant I've been to. The scallions in it were very fresh and gave it a nice pop of flavor. The Peking Duck roll was outstanding. I've never had duck before in any form, let alone Peking style, so I was pleasantly surprised to find that the duck had a delicate, non-gamey flavor. I was expecting small, spring-roll sized rolls, but we received two large rolls, well worth the $8.95 price tag. My husband had the Szechuan hot pot with chicken ($15). Now, I'm not a fan of spicy stuff, and as you can see from the picture, the broth in this dish is hellfire red, so I was wary of it (and rightfully so--it's hot!!). However, beneath the heat there is an outstanding flavor. It was definitely too spicy for me to do more than taste, but my husband said that while it was indeed hot, it wasn't painfully so (as long as you have a tolerance for spicy food). He pointed out that while he was sweating, he wasn't crying, and while his tongue was numb, he wasn't hurting. There were tons of veggies and chicken in the soup and it was way too big a portion to finish at lunch--he brought it home and shared the leftover with a friend that evening. I had the beef Pad Thai ($13). It was average, as far as Pad Thai goes, which was expected Fusion House is primarily a Chinese/Japanese restaurant, not a Thai restaurant. It was certainly not the worst Pad Thai I've ever had, and it had an interesting flavor, different from any Pad Thai I've had elsewhere. Our check came to $40, which is a bit much for lunch, but we did order an expensive appetizer, so it was not unexpected. We will definitely be going back to Fusion House for their all-you-can-eat sushi deal and to try a few other dishes on the menu (I saw at least 4 that piqued my interest and we're in their delivery radius, which is a big plus in my book).

I spent the Saturday night went to dinner with friends, but the menu is not good, don't have. The stek a lot of salt without flavor was not delicious. And then we decided to go out and go to another bar. I'll be back here

I was visiting New York for the third time this year and i went to this italian restaurant in Nolita strongly suggested from a friend of mine. I don't usually go to italian restaurant abroad since i'm italian myself but i have to say this was one of our best italian meal ever,i was really impressed,the thin crust pizza cooked in a wood burn oven was deliciuos,we had grill calamari and zucchine cake amazing. Tiramisu at the end is a must. Great service and rustic ambience. Best place visited in NY so far. 5 stars

After much anticipation we tried Anthony's take out only. Three times in two weeks!! The first time I ordered the famous wings & the lunch chicken sandwich with roasted peppers, arugala n fresh mozzarella. Wings were great sandwich was also delicious a lot of the stuff on it that over powered the chicken. We also noticed that the chicken was very unevenly distributed more on one side so we had to adjust. It still needed more chicken to satisfy the amount of other stuff. I was also asked if I wanted to try the awning pick up?? Which means u pull up on the side by the black awning n they come out n deliver your order to you....well of course I said yes! Upon arrival I waited for a good 8 min I was in a hurry so I thought well they must not know I'm here! So I went in!! . Just an FYI...take out order #2.... Well this was a real doozy!!! Ordered a small pizza 12" IAsked for 1/2 mushroom 1/2 prosciutto,and an Anthony's favorite sandwich from the lunch side ( consisting of fresh mozzarella,prosciutto, arugala and fresh tomato on focaccia bread.) again they ask about awning pick up I say yes in hope that they will come out btw this is around 5/6 at night. So I pull up n wait about 4 min...two girls  comes out!! They tell me it's like 15$ or so....so I tell them I think you have the wrong order , my cost should be more around $20 ish. So she says oh that's because we gave you a lunch size pizza! Why? Well because we don't do half and half on pies!!!! REALLY?? So you gave me as a lunch pizza? Yes with mushroom!! And a side of proscuitto !!! I'm like your kidding right? I tell her go back in and see if you can just get me a plain lunch pie and I will put the proscuitto on myself. She comes back hands me my order and says nope they don't have one. I'm thinking who decided to make this executive decision? I asked y didn't u call? Couldn't find your #!!! Well then next best thing...just give the customer what they asked for and suck it up!! Nope....so I Leave very pissed bc I got two grown kids and myself to feed with a pie the size of a dinner plate and a sandwich that when I get home has hardly any mozzarella on it....they must have an arugala garden somewhere bc again I got a lot of arugala like the first sandwich but not much of the other stuff!! Wow I was so disappointed and hungry to!  1,2,3 strikes your out. So we try again, this time my hubby orders a large pie with sausage and onion and a plain pie. He gets home and says wow guess how much for two pies? 39.99!!!! I said what the heck you got gold on it? NO....just two toppings ....but Anthony's charges 2.99 for the first one and 1.99 thereafter!! Would not be so bad if they actually gave you the toppings to make it worthy...but talk about skimping!! And the crust was burnt!! A. Big no no in my book. Listen, I have had pizza in many places including Italy. NYC, and the famous Wooster street in new haven, ct!! You want to talk about outrageous pizza!! Try it one day!!Peppis is awesome...and Tollis in East Haven!  The pie is good I'll give them that but it's not worth the price they charge! Sorry...flour,water,sauce cheese....it's not justifiable in my book. You r paying for the high end coal oven and the liquor license!  I think I'll stick to bradlees pizza it's worth every $1.00!!!!! She gives you a Pie with sausage on it not a few crumbs scattered on!!! Staff needs to know how to figure out different situations....and the #1 thing..never let the customer go home without  making the situation better then it was!!

I've enjoyed the Guilty Plate ever since I discovered it earlier this year. My only complaint is that it's gotten very popular, and the last time I went there was literally a line out the door! Even when I've had to wait it felt like I got in fairly quickly. The staff has always been nice, and accommodating, and the food is good. As someone else mentioned, there is nothing necessarily original or spectacular on the menu, but they do basic breakfast food very well. It's a safe "go to" for your breakfast needs.
Best sushi in the area. Their food is fresh and delicious. This is our go-to sushi spot.

A very pleasant and tasty dinner.  Friendly and informed staff.  Wonderful little plates of savory yumminess (the rare steak was a bit overboard on the garlic).  Very good wines by the glass.  Casual and airy room, perfect on a summer night.

Never I mean never get food from here. The food is horrible. I ordered from here twice and both times they messed up my order and when I called to ask them to fix it they didn't understand me and didn't care to fix my order. A waste of money!
No longer a byob as of 8/18 when I called.  Said there's now a 20$ corkage fee. Bummer but still rate them 5 stars for their great food.  Shame not our byob go to anymore :(

Very gluten free and vegetarian friendly- food was excellent, portions were appropriate, waiter was knowledgeable an capable- was a really nice and affordable family style dinner (we went on Sunday for the family style dinner)

Over priced entries that have small portions and not very good tastes by Chinese food standards. The food is not typical Sichuan food, but a dried-up version of Americanized hybrid. We have been there once and just see now that Groupon is offering vouchers again with this restaurant. We feel obligated to write this review. This restaurant is obviously working hard to attract American dinners. There are many Chinese restaurants that are better or much better in that area, even if you don't want to go the China Town in NYC. This restaurant deserves only one star if just rated by the value of its food.

This place appeared to have great reviews but was really so-so.  I wasn't greeted for about 5 minutes while standing there. Food was good, but really just average Drinks were better than the food - unique combinations

Wow. From start to finish, our meal was exceptional. We decided to try Roia after reading a few reviews, and we were really intrigued by the ones from the vegan wedding, as we have a few vegetarians in our group. The service was attentive and friendly, but not obtrusive. The cocktails were inventive and delicious. And the menu, while smaller in size, offered so many great choices that it was difficult to choose. We loved everything we ordered! The presentation was simple but elegant. The combinations of flavors and ingredients felt fresh and new, and we were excited to taste each dish as it arrived. It's hard to pick our favorites, but a few standouts were the gnocchi with roasted tomatoes, the burrata pugliese and the apricot torta. It's rare to have such a lovely experience at a restaurant, and to feel inspired by a meal. Roia is a wonderful find, which we plan to visit again soon. Five stars all the way!
Excellent

my friend and i had dinner at cabana the other night. service was good, the food was excellent! the portions were large, perfect for sharing and so delicious!!!!!!!!  i look forward to my next dining experience.

Thought I was down south.  Definitely not healthy food served here.  Creamed chipped beef?   Steak-ums from the food store?  Canned vegetables? Ever heard of "FRESH, REAL AND HEALTHY"?  If your not a regular, a local or like low quality food forget it...drive on.

Food was amazing. We had the  Crab risotto and the octopus for and app and for entree the Squid ink fettuccine  and the  halibut. The fettuccine was great.. Everything taste fresh and the service was great. I defiantly recommend Gato and I will defiantly be back.

First time here and was a bit disappointed. - mac n cheese was bland and the breadcrumbs gave it a strange soggy sticky texture - duck fries were salty and sad - the sour flights were good - service was great

This place would be OK, i guess, if the dishes were $8. at these prices I expected something more. as in good food, nice place. The service was incompetent, and each of our party's dishes came out at a different time.  i ordered a  dish that said "spicy" and it was not even a little spicy. same for several other people in my group. even the Tom Yum was bland! my friend had the pad thai and it was soaking in a pool of oil. the spring rolls were skimpy and came with a flavorless watery dipping sauce. the water came in nasty looking, plastic pitchers that were broken and grimy. the waitress reached across our plates as we were eating over and over and never asked how the meal was or if we wanted anything...i usually don't mind that kind of thing and i know this all sounds harsh and possibly spoiled but seriously this was crummy service, not very good food, and overpriced. and i left hungry. thumbs down. do not recommend.
The scallop n marrow tacos are amazing...

Delicious food!  It was so fresh, second time I was there was for brunch.  Poached plum pancakes and a breakfast wrap tasted like ingredients came from a garden or field that morning.  I would have given 5 stars but I had gone there the first time and had horrible service.  The gentleman didn't know the basic questions and never came back to my table.  We wanted to go to a good brunch place and heard good things about this  place.  We were so happy we went again, we had a a female server who suggested cocktails that were superb.   I will go back!  Well priced for what we got, we were all stuffed when we left.

Not up to the standard... food taste varies.. and it is becoming pathetic day by day.. and the cost gosh its expensive... the only food I find to taste better is crab masala.. the rest everything is waste of money.. I would not go here again.. Everyone comes for the authentic chettinad biryani, hope they know this.. It would be great if they can do something to improve the quality.....
Holy meow the pho is expensive, but definitely amazing!!
Let's just say that I never used to be a fan of calzones, and now I am. That was darn tasty. And BYOB? Yes, please.

Unfortunately Gaslight was a total let down.  I first asked the waiter if i could get the pulled pork sandwich but without the pineapple salsa on top, the waiter told me that this was impossible and couldn't give me an explanation as to why not.  Rather than giving me more time to order since I was totally caught off guard by such a simple request he continued to ask for my order and all I could come up with was fine the pulled pork sandwich with the pineapple salsa on top.   The food comes out and there is absolutely no reason why the salsa couldn't have been taken off it was sitting perfectly on top and it wasn't baked into the pork or the avocado spread. My only other assumption was that my sandwich was actually premade because the meat was cold and the focaccia bread was completely soggy so I couldn't event pick up the sandwich and had to use my fork and knife. To make matters worse at the end of the meal one of the waiters spilled ketchup on one of my friends at the table even into his hair and white polo shirt. And rather than offering a complimentary drink or something else all he was given was a napkin and water. Worst service I've ever experienced at a philly restaurant will definitely never go back.

I have always had a good meal to begin with here, but in an hour or two I always feel sick. It can't be just a coincidence.  Service is okay, it's overly crowded and always a long wait which I never feel is worth it.

Authentic wonderfully fresh delicious food.  I have never been disappointed here and have eaten almost everything on the menu at some point.  The dumplings, oh the dumplings... I believe I fantasize about them.  They're freshly made and often run out, so get there early.   The service is superb, they always have the nicest guys who are so friendly and go out of their way.  I highly recommend trying House of Chao more than once.

Dine in or take out this is the freshest and most authentic Chinese cuisine anywhere for many miles around. Every dish we tried was full of flavor without being at all greasy, simply but elegantly presented. Ingredients are obviously very fresh and rich in flavor and hue. Service was prompt and polite without being intrusive and the prices are very, very reasonable for this caliber of fare. Wish we lived closer, it's a trek for us but well worth it!

After hearing a lot about this establishment we made it over for sandwiches one day.  I wasnt impressed.  I felt that it was more for the grad students.  Sandwiches were overpriced.  The interior is beautiful though, if we had to go back I would but there are plenty of other choices.

First off this place is amazing the atmosphere is so aesthetically pleasing that I would recommend everyone to come by just to read a book and hang out. I came by the other day with only enough time to get a pastry and a latte.I was immediately hit by all the delicious smells.then when I got to the register I was greeted by this girl with a huge smile on her face. She made it seem like that was a great plave ro work. I placed my order, for an eclair and vanilla latte. Upon receiving the éclair I was distracted and ended up leaving without my latte! I was halfway down the street when that same girl came running after me with my drink.  Maison really has a great staff who cares.  I'll definitely be returning. Not only for the great staff but as well for those éclairs!

This place used to be good. Recently visited them around 5ish in the evening for a wads sambar. Surprised that they gave old wadas which were hard and no crunch. The chutneys were stale. I am going to avoid this till is hear about some changes. Totally disappointed in quality.
The lobster rolls are so good comparable to some of the other well known lobster rolls out there. The New England lobster roll is Delicious! The fries & chips are good also.
good food if you are in the area, but not the best place in the city for raw bar. the chowders are excellent.

Our friend told us about this place being authentic chinese food. We ordered multiple dishes and the service was impeccable. The lobster with ginger and scallions was outstanding. I had roasted duck and it was chewy with some pieces but altogether good for the price. General Tso's chicken and the eggplant dishes were delicious. We had a very good experience eating here.

Food was average; nothing to run home and brag about. The service was terrible, staff was nowhere to be seen, people on here are posting about how their water came late...at least they got some. My date and I are still waiting for our cheesecake it's been 20 minutes.
As good as my Lebanese friend's Mom's cooking.
Best go-to bar in the area. Cheap and good food, and has a nice casual atmosphere

I normally don't write reviews but my experience here was so notably poor that I feel the need to stop others from wasting their time and money. LIC is a great neighborhood in need of some quality food options. I visited on a Monday night hoping that it would be as good as it looked from the outside. Tl;dr - another mediocre LIC restaurant that sounds better than it is. Food - good, maybe even pretty good. Space - clubby, nice if you like that kind of thing. Service - horrible, absolutely terrible, stay away. The play by play of what went wrong during my dinner service follows. We were seated under a  loud speaker, we asked politely for it to be turned down (it was a Monday night!), and it was. Then it was turned back up 5 minutes later. This happened 3 times during the meal. The wait staff was inattentive. All 3 in my party sat with no water and empty drinks,  when the waiter checked in on us he completely missed this. We needed to ask. The wait was unacceptably long wait for our main dishes, 50minutes for 2 paellas and a steak. The waiter delivered some silverware for a steak, "your meals will be right out". Our food showed up 15min later (and the runner didn't know who's dish was who's). We needed to ask our waiter and 2 different runners for our check, which arrived nearly 15 minutes after we first asked for it. We almost walked out to see if people would notice. Blend o blend, I hope you improve, until then I wont be back. PS. Mr. Manager, I see you replying to negative reviews. Please don't waste your time on me, instead, please spend less time at your computer and more time at your restaurant making the service not suck as much.

It's not a sit in place... But if u want a banging corn beef or hot pastrami sandwich jump off the parkway at exit 144 and stop in to grab a bite! I hadn't been here since I was a little girl but decided to stop in! They have not lost their touch! I ordered a 1/2 corn beef & 1/2 pastrami on rye with Russian dressing. They pile the meat so high, you only need half the sandwich. They also give you two slices of a pickle. The Deli is combined with a liquor store so you can get dinner and a drink all in one spot. The people are pleasant and the price is more than fair... The decor is the only thing that leaves you wanting more... Don't expect anything fancy... It's a classic mom and pop!
A lovely gem in the neighborhood that's cozy with a great wine selection and delicious food. Great for dates or catching up with a friend.

This is my go-to for lunch pho. I literally look forward to my delicious bowl of pho from Vietnam before my friday night. Vietnam pho the soup is most important taste, they're soup just taste the right one...

The gluten free accomondations are almost as good at Max's Oyster and Max's Fish. The food is normally superb, the service top notch, the managers always check in during dinners and are a pleasure to speak with. I have had salmon which was a tad dry once, but mostly, the food is 5 stars ridiculously good. Unfortunately, Max's Downtown doesn't use Dee's Gluten Free bread which is AMAZING (but other Max's establishments mostly use Dee's GF Rolls) and the Chef at Max's DOwntonw insists on making his own. They are crumbly and dry, made of corn maybe, and not delicious like Dee's GF Free Bread Rolls. I always look forward to the GF Rolls at Max's Restaurants and was a disappointed with the corn dry odd Chef's GF version of the rolls. Can't go wrong with the food here - or the atmosphere. Fantastic date night spot or special occasion place. Always dress up and don't forget to valet your Lamborghini in front of the restaurant so patrons can take pictures with your car :). {True Story}
OMG..... Had a great time at Frames NYC.... The people and music was great (Naomi the bartender)....

I was admittedly hesitant to dine at Mistral given the "uniqueness" of the menu (who wants to Google ingredients in each dish on the menu before ordering?)... but finally decided to give it a try and was pleasantly surprised! Pros: Small plate style means you can try many of the unique menu offerings; Lovely outdoor patio; BYOB helps to keep final cost more reasonable Cons: Pacing of dishes was too fast to enjoy each one
Dinner was excellent as usual. Love my drunken noodles. Fine family run operation. Never a bad meal here at Mai Thai!!!!!

Two words: Dollar. Oysters. EVERYDAY (yes, sat and sun incl). From four til closing.  CLOSING!! That's unheard of. Long gone are the days (weekdays, mind you) of rushing to a restaurant after work trying to catch the end of their oyster happy hour. Granted it does take some time for them to come out but their staff are all so sweet that I'm not even mad. Service has always been top notch. Yes, Barn Joo. You've made me one happy diner.

I had lunch here with 2 co-workers and wanted to say that this establishment was on point.  I would definitely try dinner here as the restaurants view is one of the best in the city next to John Davenports

Excellent!  We loved this spot, I'm not sure how long this has been open but we saw it over a month ago and finally went in.  There is a little bit of everything.  The interior is simple and the chairs not terribly comfortable for long dinners.  The service was nice and they were able to answer all questions that our table had.  We certainly had a lot of questions too, regarding ingredients and questions about what is recommended.
Yet another staple for New Haven.  It's a place you need to go to, at least once if you can.
Best Happy Hour Specials in Philly! $5 mojitos, margaritas, or sangria and $5 quesadillas, tacos, and guacamole everything is delicious and really great service!

The food is terrible. It was over priced and poor quality. Extremely noisy ( summer time and their kids are out of school.. I guess ) , messy ( small staff... I guess ) , and unprofessional owners... My job ordered lunch from there a few times and we no longer will be. I really enjoy going to local mom and pop places, but NOT this one. Do yourself a favor and try somewhere else.

If there were more stars, I will never hesitate to rate as many as I can! If anyone is a super fan of spicy food, this must be the great place for you! Some of my my friends didn't like spicy food so they ordered different kinds of XLB but we still enjoyed a lot Dandan noddles and special fish. I think it could be the ever best place to enjoy Chinese food for most people~~~ :-)

The "Nachos Grande" is super tiny, and you barely get more than 5 chips--was also super greasy, and the chips kept breaking because they were so oily. Service is poor--this was not the first time that I have had unsatisfactory service. Will not be coming back.

This breakfast and lunch shop is located near the old city. Cute cafe with friendly service. We had the special sandwich and tuna melt, both great. Huge selection of soft drinks and juices. Free wifi.

Thai Kitchen is a good place to grab lunch. There aren't that many Thai options in Hillsborough, so this is my go-to for squid Pad Thai. Food comes out quickly, it's cheap, it's consistent. It's not phenomenally good food, but it's not bad. I came here for dinner once with the family, and I remember that we had a duck dish that was really good. If you want really spicy curries though you have to ask for more "elephants"!

The Iris Cafe showed up in the New Yorker, so I decided to check it out. Apparently they have a new 23-year-old chef, and I have to say that his creations are unbelievable. They are not just creative, they are delicious! For dinner, everything they serve is small-plate, and they recommend you order 4-6 plates between two people. Between the two of us, we had the kale croquettes, the beet and summer squash, the garganelli with peas and prosciutto, the scallops, and a cheese plate. Each dish was innovative and delightful--for example, the scallops are served with plums, cucumbers yuzu kosho. And let's not forget about the dessert! I overheard our neighboring table order the Earl Grey crème brûlée, and waited our entire meal to order just that,  but when the menu came and had "s'mores" on it, there simply was no other possibility. The dessert consists of a chocolate mousse covered in a perfectly toasted merengue, with a dollop of salted caramel and crumbled graham cracker. Our waitress was delightful and very knowledgeable about both the menu and history of the area. Throughout the course of the meal, I learned quite a lot about the neighborhood and their restaurant. The room was intimate and quiet. The kitchen is in the room with everything else- directly behind the bar, and the vibe is relaxed and slow-paced, a world apart from the city. If you want stretch the romantic evening a bit longer, take a walk along the Brooklyn Heights Promenade afterward for incredible nighttime views of Manhattan, the Statue of Liberty, and the Brooklyn Bridge. For two of us, the cost (including drinks and tip) was $150. We went on a Saturday evening around 8:30, and were easily sat without a reservation. If you're on the fence, just GO!

My husband & I Just had dinner here and it was fantastic. You can taste  the authenticity in the food. You can tell in every dish we had that it was made fresh on the spot. I love that it is a BYOB too. The owner and staff are very friendly! We will def be back! Must try the guacamole!!!
Highly recommended! The place is tiny, so it's hard to get a seat, super good food though.
Pizza is ordered by the pie. There's usually a long line and it's very touristy. Cash only.

History, on the half shell. I HAVE TO eat here every time I go to NYC. Super affordable. They've got counters so you can just grab an open seat and get some AMAZINGLY FRESH seafood. If the stone shell crab claws are in season, treat yourself. Otherwise, clam chowder, clams casino and your choice of oysters is the way to go. Dress nice enough and go to the Big Fish Seafood Bistro speakeasy for a drink after. I'll leave it to you to find it. ;-)

Strictly on food, this place is a 2.5-3. Hit or miss, but theres the occasional dish worth trying (paneer tikka kabab). Other than the rare star though, theres nothing very good or very bad. Its fairly middling. Service is atrocious. Counter staff isn't above lying to you, nor trying to cheat you out of a few bucks here and there, nor charging the mandatory gratuity on the post tax price(so I guess more cheating you of a few bucks here or there). All told this place is a 1.5 but ill round up because they are accomodating of food requests (extra spicy, more sauce, whatever your desired customization may be).

Excellent Services!!! Elvis is the most professional waiter I have ever met. He helped us to make some very tasty BBQ beef, shrimps. And not to metion he also put his secert ingredients sources on mussels and eggplants. Wow!! It was just Yummy!!! How can you tell a waiter is professional or not? Even he had work for 9 hours by the time he served us and was tired, he still had a very friendly smiling face throughout the night.

Unimpressed!  For what they are charging I wanted something original and creative.  I didn't see anything exciting on this menu.  It's quite disappointing, we will not try this restaurant again.  Service also was not good, I went on a busy night.  I had to repeatedly ask for another beer mostly because my cocktail was poorly made.  There was so many other places in town to try.

The Peasant Grill has become our family's "go to" restaurant in Hopewell.  Everything that we have ordered has been excellent; the homemade soups are amazing, sandwiches are piled high and a meal in themselves.  The spinach salad has become a personal favorite with the homemade dressing "to die for".  Meatballs and lasagna are also favorites with serving sizes more than sufficient.  The baked good are all made on premise too.  I'll be coming back here!

I go here for lunch more often than I care to admit since I work within the mall. The food is always fantastic! I've never had an issue with the food or the staff. I also like how they ask for a donation to firehouses, and it only rounds your bill to the nearest dollar.

For airport dining, this is pretty good. Was a little warm inside: probably due to their half open air kitchen. Bartender was super friendly. Greeted us and chatted us up. Place was clean and had pretty good basic drinks. Pricey but it's the airport. Ordered lobster roll, buffalo shrimp and a Caesar salad. Salad was pretty good. I was craving a light lunch and I got it. Shrimp were TINY but super spicy. Lobster roll was very good and the sweet potato chips had a zing to them. Definitely plan on coming early for future flights to relax here. They even have tons of outlets under the bar to charge your stuff!!

I had been telling my wife I wanted to try Ricaltons since before they opened. It looked like it was going to be a nice gastro pub. My family of five went to eat there last night and I wish we had looked at the menu before we sat down. The menu is RIDICULOUSLY expensive. The kind of money you'd only spend on a special occasion for amazing food and quaint atmosphere. Ricaltons has neither of those. It's obvious they spent a lot of money remodeling the space - but it has the feel of a pub or high end sport bar. The food we had was ok, my chili rubbed salmon was moist and had good flavor but the portion was tiny. The potatoes that came with my wife's pork chop were burnt and oddly unseasoned. My 2 young boys had burgers and the buns were gigantic, overwhelming the burger inside. Our server was very nice and attentive. However we were the only people eating in the gigantic upstairs dining room. I'm not sure how Ricaltons came up with their menu and pricing strategy but I think it is going to seal their fate if they don't change it soon. Change the menu to solid gastro pub food and knock $5 to $10 off most of the menu items and then maybe it will stay open long enough to recoup the investment. I know I won't be back until That happens.

love love love this place!!! the BCT roll is amazing- who would think that bacon and sushi would be so amazing together? awesome ambiance, reasonably priced, friendly staff and delicious food! my favorite sushi place in the city :)

I had high hopes for the Brothers Moon as I loved the restaurant exterior and the idea of a local bakery.  The meal was we had was somewhat lackluster and the service seemed slow.  The bakery selection was sparse and the muffin I did order was really too greasy.  I keep telling myself to try them again but then talk myself out of it when there are better places in the area.
Amazing food. Stopped in for Lunch around 2pm.  Clean restaurant and good service. The prices are a little high but it's NYC.  I had the shipwreck and the wife had a Lobster BLT.  Both were amazing.
Super-friendly staff and management coupled with delicious and healthy food make this place my go-to. My favorite is the Bacon Chicken Cheddar Ranch but their Superfood salad is a close second.

Cavatelli and half vodka half rubirosa supreme pie is the way to go. The cavatelli is always cooked perfectly. The pizza is thin and very tasty with a nice crisp to it. Staff is super friendly and food comes out fast. Come here for a casual night out.

I love this place, it's so great.  A hole in the wall and dive bar feeling but it's wonderful.  Fair priced, don't expect the fine china and it's very much like something you'd find in a vacation town.
AMAZING!!! Oh so ahmmazing. Checked out their Coney Island location also and its just as good but with a larger menu.

So I finally got to taste this pizza and it was well worth the wait (which I confess was a bit long).  But I would do it again.  Pizza done to perfect with succulent pepperoni.  I will be back for sure.  Again and Again and Again... Loved it.

This Oyster House dame of restaurants remains a favorite. It provides 4 separate types of seating to fit your mood (counter, dining room, quiet back room, and oyster bar itself), has easily the largest and most varied selection of fresh oysters in the city, and has a menu that meets virtually every seafood lovers desire and price point (the pan fried at $11 is a meal in itself). Above that, it has an INCREDIBLE wine list that, unfortunately, gets overlooked due to its length, with a bunch of rare and wonderful wines (Stony Hill, anyone?), and enough great wines by the glass to satisfy any oenophile. The low ceiling makes it a bit noisy, but it adds to the character of the place.

Love this place--their chicken paprika is awesome.  Stuffed peppers are good too, but frankly the chicken paprika is so wonderful that I just never order anything else any more.  Service is friendly and efficient. Like many ethnic restaurants in New Jersey, it is located in a strip mall and has that strip mall vibe going on, but ignore that.  The food is wonderful.
The best fries in NYC, Thick, hot and crispy. The amount of sauces to chose from in endless. A must try when in the Village.
The steak isn't that flavorful.  It's as simple as that!
Service is excellent. Atmosphere is contemporary. Plating and details show attention to presentation. Hopefully, will get back to this with more time. Decent ramen and kaarage. Service excellent.

Had the Seared Tuna Tataki and it did not disappoint. The tuna was perfect, and along with the avocado and tomato, the salad made for a light and refreshing meal. Just a small warning: my friend ordered a bowl of ramen and complained that it was only sub-par. However, I recommend the salad for those who want a lighter dinner.

El Vez is a great place for drinks w friends, but I wouldn't recommended for dinner. I came here on a tuesday night. I sat by bar, the service was lame. This isn't a place for authentic Mexican food. If you like quality food and good drinks go to Barbuzzo, which is a block away from EL Vez.
Had dinner, it was good.  I would try again it was late.  I sometimes think that restaurants aren't always as good near closing time.

Great new French spot in the UES. The food was absolutely fantastic. Tried the Roasted Fig & Prosciutto and the Roasted Dijon Salmon. The drinks were amazing and you can't go wrong with the tartines. The owners of the restaurants are also great people! Don't be deceived by the location. It's definitely worth a trek if you are not in the area. I highly recommend this place. Can't wait to try their brunch menu.

Hi, After pathetic ANJAPPAR FOOD, we chose to try this restaurant.. Food is awesome. Biryani, chicken and fish varieties.. everything is good out here.. so never again to anjappar...We would definitely stick on to this restaurant henceforth.

The menu is limited. Will not recommend if you have a big appetite. I'm Japanese so I expect exceptional service everytime I eat Japanese food. I had no expectations since I'm not from NYC but I've ate at a variety authentic restaurants around the world. There were many problems eating here. First, the waiter kept informing us while we were ordering we had to spend a minimum of $6.00 even though everyone ordered food. Second, we asked TWICE for water. We could've asked more than twice but we were trying to be patient. Waitress never came so we walked to the water pitcher and poured our OWN water. Third, since we didn't know it was cash only, half of us had to walk to the bank to get cash. While the other half was waiting for them to return, the waitress came up to us and told us to hurry and finish since they were closing. I don't mind waiters telling us when they are closed and say it in a polite way but the lady was very rude and they were still open for another 15 minutes. We even told them we were waiting for others to come back for cash so we can pay for the bill. I was surprised by my experience I tipped under the 15%. As we left we they literally yelled at us and say we didn't pay them the tip that is required by law. Our argument is tip is earned, not expected. I'm very generous with tip but they simply didn't earn it. Fair enough. She was sooo angry and didn't even apologize for their horrible service. The ambiance is quiet and dark. It has the potential to make you feel you are at a tea house in Japan. As we sat, we were greeted by the waitresses. The first page of the menu had instructions, such as minimum charge $6.00 person.  This place is CASH ONLY! Cheapest beer is $6.00 so it's easy to reach the minimum. I didn't have the food but looking to my right it looked amazing, but definitely overpriced. I ordered the brick toast with red bean and sesame ice cream. Nothing special about it except the sesame ice cream. Not worth $13, I've spent much less on better desserts.

First of all I have to say finding this place was pretty hard but it was totally worth getting lost for a bit. The moment I walked in I was greeted by the workers. I didnt expect the place to be such a small place but as I got used to it. I realized it was a great spot for alll of my friends and I to just hangout and get some food. And now onto the food. Everyone recommended me the fish tempura tacos, porkbelly taco, breakroom fries , and breakroom burger, and of course their famous mint lemonade. They definitely did not disappoint. The burger was cooked perfectly and putting a runny egg on it with porkbelly omg. I definitely would recommend this place. I can honestly say it's the best burger and tacos of ive had comparing the burger to shake shacks. I definetly would pick breakroom burger over shake shack anyday. The price is good and the foods made to order so its fresh. I definitely recommend this place and have already told at least 20 of my friends and they all have loved this new little spot and they also have become regulars here.

I REALLY like Brooklyn Stoops. Like a lot. It's proximity to my home is actually a bonus, not a selling point. My boyfriend and I frequent here for the awesome happy hour and the relaxed and chill vibe (no pretensions!). The food has always been top notch (I really love the tilapia sandwich...) - and the bartenders are great! They are always doing pretty much everything on their own - so sometimes things may take a little longer, but this is a low-key bar, not a high end restaurant. If you are in need of a lot of attention - go elsewhere for your fix. This past weekend, the bartender actually bought my friend and I a round because our food was "taking so long." Mind you, we didn't even notice how long it was taking and the food came out about 3 minutes after she apologized. Much appreciated!

I've always been pleased with the sandwiches at Stacks. The Maple Cilantro Turkey is my favorite... or maybe the Buffalo Chicken... or the Cuban Missile. The sweetness of the turkey on the Maple Cilantro is just so perfect! All the components just go together so well, and the bread is great too. Soft, yet sturdy enough to hold up while eating. Ingredients always seem fresh, and their house made sweet pickles are DELICIOUS. I would buy a jar of those any day.
They always seem to get my order wrong. Some of the staff is nice but always feel like the management is suspicious of all customers. I'm done trying this place.

What can I say other than horrible. The interior is dirty and in major need of a remodel. There is nothing in the dessert display cases. They lost their liquor license. The menu is not extensive. While, it's nice most meals come with a cup of soup, I'd make a bet that it comes from a can. Cream of Broccoli I had which lacked flavor. I ordered a grilled chicken sandwich which was ok. The roll that it was on did not appear fresh. They were out of honey mustard sauce which I found to be unacceptable. People who were in our group, couldn't even order certain dishes. They were out of turkey and something else that I can't remember. How can you be out of so many things. The tackiest thing that I saw was the lack of ketchup on the tables. When we asked for ketchup, we were given a container of Americas Choice, which obviously bought as a 10 for 10 special. All and all this place was terrible and don't foresee it staying open much longer as there were minimal people in there. If there were 4 tables occupied, that was a lot. I know this place has been on the decline for a while, but this is rock bottom.

Food was great, service was really good too. Everyone was very courteous. Fantastic vegetarian options, just the right amount of spice. While the portions looked small we had the 3 course meals, and the entres were very filling with the appetizers.

Farm to table flatbread. A favorite dinner spot in Burlington using (all?) mostly local ingredients made over a wood fire stove. They also have a great in house brewery. The most delicious pizza in b-town!
A very cozy and romantic wine bar, just a step off broadway, with an interesting and tasty menu. The host is very welcoming,  and will good care of you

By far the best tasting food I have ever had in NYC. The taste, the spices, the service! A true delight for my taste buds! Checked out the new Harlem location (144 West 139th Street) and the decor and food blew me away! The truffle mac and cheese, ginger martini's, looking forward to my next Ponty Bistro dish!

The food here was good,  it wasn't amazing but then again there could always be the off night.  I would certainly try it again.  My girlfriend loved what she ordered, they have a decent wine selection.  I would recommend it overall to try.

There are so many choices in Little Italy, it can be somewhat overwhelming.  I have been to several of the restaurants and Pelligrino's is a standout.  The service was impeccable.  I had the lasagna and it was simply the best that I have ever had, it was so flavorful and the portion size was just right.  I tried my sister's fettuccine Alfredo and it too was awesome.  I had ordered that dish last week at a competing restaurant and this was definitely better.  The sauce was creamier and thicker, it really clung to the noodles.   Another thing that really made this restaurant stand out from the pack was their tomato bread.  Unique and delicious is the best way to describe it. One if my friends who generally doesn't like bread with her meal scarfed down several pieces.   A total of eight thumbs up from all of us!!
The food is ok,,They mess up take out orders a lot though
Valenca is a must atleast 1/month if not more for my wife and I. Order a filet mignon on the stone and a nice bottle of Esporão. You will not be disappointed.

I don't know if it was the 90s music or the great ambiance but this place gets me. I came by myself for dinner it wasn't too busy and the food was great. That was all lovely but this review is mostly about the service. Sophia was my waitress and she is a natural.  She must have seen the bored look on my face because she came up and apologized that my Pizza was taking  longer than expected to come out. WHAT? Anticipating the needs of your customers? AMAZING!  I was impressed. 30 seconds later Luis arrived with my Pizza. I asked him for Sophia's name but he is new and didn't know.  But Luis didn't leave it at that, he found out and came back to me! Unheard of! Sophia is great, she came back to check on me and really seemed like she was having fun -- she even picked up trash off the ground when she saw it -- this girl's as star! But even more impressive was the staff's teamwork.  I never felt uncomfortable asking for anything even from the other waitress Victoria.  Victoria saw me spacing out and stopped to make sure everything was ok.  She was helpful without being intrusive and seamlessly lent Sophia a hand when she had too much to carry.  Great job everyone! Don't separate this team, and sounds like maybe get the bartenders on board? :)

Eh...yeah that about sums it up. Patio seating in tiny, really low, cheap plastic chairs. The poured concrete table was chin height. Made me feel like a child.  Our waiter forgot our order and had to come ask us what we had ordered 20 minutes after we placed it. My Buffalo chicken fingers and onion rings were okay. The rings were obviously fried in the same oil as the fish... Hubs said the meatloaf was pretty good. The thing I enjoyed the most was the music piped outside.

Lots of hype, mediocre food. $29 pan seared halibut over 3 slices of heirloom tomato in a watery flavorless broth. Not happy about that. on the plus come before 7 for $5 old fashions. My friends we're happy with their burgers though.

Awesome staff & manager made our big group of out-of-towners very comfortable and welcome!  The food was wonderful; everyone seemed very happy with their meals. Salads were delicious, also loved the scampi and gnocchi.The portions are not huge, but with this kind of upscale Italian cuisine, I don't think they should be. We were quite content. Atmosphere is nice, old-world Italian flair. Cute place, right near Princeton but not too college-student-y. Highly recommend!!
Ahi burger was my fav over Manly and truffle. Free wifi and clean bathrooms. All good
Nope. No comparison to pats, and some rude ass service to boot. Go across the street.
Awesome sandwiches and always quick. The food quality is exceptional and the flavor is delicious. The neighborhood is great and needed this place. Love it!

Had Brunch this weekend. Staff was fine, atmosphere too, but the food was so-so. For example: biscuits and gravy. The biscuits were more like pieces of cake than actual biscuits, and the dish -- which should be smothered in gravy -- came instead with about a teaspoonful of the stuff. When I asked for more they obliged, but then charged $5 extra for the honor. Really don't see what all the fuss is about, certainly it's not worth a long wait, folks.

Brooklyn's pizza is sincerely the best pizzas I have eaten. So many varieties it's amazing. They don't only have pizza the array of things on the menu is simply amazing. Great service and very accommodating. I simply love this place!!!

Love this place, have already eaten here a few times, it is very clean and the guys that work there are super friendly. I had an order of chicken tacos, which came with 3, was able to choose my own toppings and it was delicious. It also comes with white or yellow rice and beans, unfortunately no refried beans were offered. They made the order in front of me and I was out pretty quickly. For a few bucks more you can get a soda and salsa/chips with your order, overall pretty inexpensive. I don't know what the first reviewers issue was with cleaning supplies near the bathroom,  if you ask me, it's a pretty dumb complaint.

I have been going to this diner for years and I always liked the people and the food. Their wraps and french fries are always good and they now sell alcohol if you feel like a drink. It's a nice place to just relax and eat some comfort food.

Took my sister out for a birthday dinner here and it was definitely one of the best dining experiences I've had in NYC. If you enjoy wine then this is the place to go! The ambience is perfect for a fancy-ish wine and tapas dinner, the service is courteous and prompt, and the food was AMAZING. The owner was around and suggesting wine pairings as well which made the experience even better. Definitely going back next time I'm in the city!
That first time at Obao. OMG!!! Nice place Excellent food. I order Rib sugar cane so yummy Calamari love it Pad thai so good Grill pork & shrimp I would like to come back here with my friend again.

Not good... I felt like we were in a tourist trap rather than a gourmet restaurant. The atmosphere was nice and the service was fine but the food... Nothing to write home about. They gave us bread and some tasteless tapenade to start.. Then we ordered salads. I've had many a caprese salad, but this was awful.. Instead of Balsamic vinegar they put on a rancid olive type oil.. My SO's Caesar wasn't much better. For the main course my salmon was overcooked and so were the veggie sides... I could barely eat half... The linguini and clam sauce was just okay. The restaurant was not cheap either... $9 for a small pour of red. Would not go back!
Great this is the burger spot in northern liberties! Also got a milk shake on the way out really really really good.... Really good lol!

I give this place. 4:5 only because the food was delicious. I ordered the salmon with goat cheese and chicken with sundried tomatoe panani. Im not giving it 5 stars because when I first walked in I wasnt greeted by the workers or seated or given menus. I had to personally walk and ask them. 2nd I ordered an ice latte and an iced coffee. I timed them and It took them about 35 min to have our drinks at our table . The latte tastes fine but the ice coffee just tasted like water. But overall I left satisfied because the food was delicious and I definetly will come again. I just hope their customer service will improve.

This is my favorite place for pizza/wine in the city! The mood and atmosphere here is very romantic and is the perfect spot for a cute date night. The pizza here is made right in front of you and is/tastes fresh. The seasoning is a bit salty but overall not a problem! I recommend all my friends to come here for a casual and/or a fancy night out.

I've never had a bad meal at Geronimo.  First of all, they have the best tequila menu in town, and make tremendous drinks.  We often order tapas and appetizers and share - and we've brought everyone from carnivors to vegetarians - no complaints. Some very clever options, too!  Go. Drink. Eat.  A very handsome restaurant, with whimsical, tasteful decor and lighting. The only drawback is that it can get quite noisy - but I'd overlook that for the food.  Just reserve early!
Wow.. Spot is amazing! Their caipirinhas are no joke! Also a must try is the quesadilla de champiñón! Amazzzzzzing!!!

Ate at the airport location.  Not only was the food good but our server,Terri, was wonderful too.  Gave us a great recommendation.  She was so sweet. Highly recommend eating there when at the airport. Gate E

The music and the cocktails were good, but the bartenders have no respect for customers. I've been scolded in very rude manners for asking if i can order. After that we sat at the bar and also took us another 30 mins to get the bartenders attention. It is really employees only. I'm regretting spending a beautiful tuesday night here. Horrible, horrible place.

I was very excited to try this place due the pretty great reviews, I left disappointed. I went at 7:15 on a Wednesday night which apparently is not the night to stop by- we were the only ones in the whole place. I ordered the sweet tea and thought it was meh. Too sweet overall. Then when my boyfriend and I went to order the waitress told us they were not only out of cornbread*, they were out of three sides (dirty rice, red beans, and potato salad)! So I ordered the ribs with greens and candied sweets. The ribs were very fatty and while the candied sweets had a great flavor, they were very mushy. The only redeeming part of my meal was the greens. They had a little spiciness to them which I though was delicious. My boyfriend had the pulled pork with greens and mac & cheese. The reason I gave this place two stars instead of one is because of the pulled pork. It was some of the best we've ever eaten and I'm not usually one for pulled pork. Very tender and the BBQ sauce was tangy and sweet- my favorite. He loved the greens but said the mac & cheese was so-so. Lastly, we wanted to order dessert and were excited by the options listed, however when we went to order, they were out of everything but peach cobbler. We decided not to bother. I may try this place again for the pulled pork but at lunch time instead of dinner time. Maybe they won't be out of so many items if I go earlier in the day. (* the waitress did come over later with one small piece of cornbread, saying she remembered she had one left. The small piece I had was tasty but not extraordinary)
Love love love this place! Their classic lasagna is to die for! And their pizza are delicious. Lovely atmosphere and great service. Afterwards we ate gelato. Yummm
Good pizza! Great owner!! Donate pizza for the homeless for a buck, hell yeah!! Support this business!!!!
This is one of my all-time fav lunch spots in midtown! The Katsu Curry is the best in the city!

Went to Diner last night because I somehow remembered it as a cozy and delicious neighborhood bistro (I lived in Wburg in 2000 long before hipsters invaded like ants to a deserted picnic.) Alas, we were led to a rocking table outside where one of our two chairs was also doubling as a door stop. The warm, unmistakable smell of rotting carcass permeated the breezy night air. Our waitress approached and in hungry expectation, we awaited the menu presentation. Instead, she informed us there would be no antiquated written list for us to hold in our hands. While jotting down words on our paper table cloth with a pen, she rambled a list of culinary vocabulary as if reading from a Cordon Bleu text book. When she was finished, we looked down to see a mouthwatering description of choices that read exactly as such: Starter, Salad, Blue Fish, Fish, Hen, Meat, Big Meat, Pork.   We asked for GASP! a printed menu because our lesser brains couldn't remember anything she recited aside from, "Tonight we have some food." But clearly we are consumerist morons because she scolded us and pronounced, "Our menu changes daily and it would be a total waste of paper to print out menus everyday." Somewhere, in the annals of my memory, I seemed to recall seeing this phrase on sheets of deconstructed trees at another eating establishment: Menu Changes Daily. But I've traveled a lot and eaten at a lot of places so who knows, I could be totally making that up. Embarrassed that our short term memory loss prevented us from deciding between Meat and Big Meat, we made a mad dash for Marlow and Sons, which happened to be right next door. The odor of decomposing corpse immediately vanished. I marveled at the chef's DAILY selections on the printed menu that was placed directly into my hands. And after a delicious meal of local Blue Fish with Cannellini Beans with Croutons and a Brick Chicken with Green Beans, we were offered a giant bag of complimentary pastries to take with us. In fact, as I write this, I'm nibbling these buttery delights and reminiscing about our delicious dinner at Marlow and Sons. My memory of Diner is now fading, going, going, gone...

Went here after purchasing a Groupon, which offered one shared appetizer or salad and two entrees. I made a reservation using Open Table, but called ahead saying we would be just a bit late. They said not to worry. We were instructed we could only order pasta--no chicken, beef or fish dishes--with the Groupon even though it says "two entrees." When we asked to speak to a manager to clarify, it looked like our server told someone who might be a manager to come over, but she never did. (She may not have been a manager.) She sent over the newest server on staff, who explained that Groupon made a mistake. She was nice enough but said she didn't know what was going on with Groupon since she had only been there for four days. Okay, it happens, we shall order pasta. Food was actually decent. The carpaccio was standard, but the linguine was quite yummy. It took them awhile to come back to us to wrap our food and bring us the bill even though it wasn't very busy. The women working in the restaurant wear jean shorts. It doesn't seem like a jean shorts kind of place. I found that to be unprofessional in what looked like a nice place. By the menu and the look of the decor, they should at least be in all black (one of the servers was) and be more attentive to the customers. I get home hours later and had an email that Paprika canceled my Open Table reservation, even though I called and said I would be late (no more than 20 minutes) and we did actually eat there. So, I lost my points there. The entire experience was just very odd. If a restaurant doesn't want to participate in a Groupon deal, don't.
Great place to be introduced to Filipino food if you've never tried. You won't be disappointed. Staff is knowledgeable and friendly. And holy smokes, gotta get that garlic fried rice!

I love this little place. My dad works across the street and comes here for lunch.  I thought there were nothing but office buildings back here. So if you don't know the area you would never know this was here. Great place to eat. Not to expensive. Nice little eat and go. Food I like. Sandwiches are delicious.
Definitely order a bunch of tapas instead of an entree. Surprisingly cheap if you skip drinks. I prefer Beso to its two sibling restaurants Blue and Bayou, which is pretty high praise.

I've tried the deep fried clam strips and they are really good. They taste fresh and lightly battered. I think you can get a half order of the clam strips if you ask nicely. A full order is a meal in itself. I've also tried their milkshake which was not too thick and relatively inexpensive. I am shocked at some of the 2 star ratings for this place.
Great salads and service. I got a steak once. Asked for it medium, but got it well done and it tasted real bland.

I don't like hurting a restaurant's reputation, however, my experience here could have been more exceptional. I decided to dine out, treating my best friend on her birthday, and the place seemed very relaxed and dimly lit. So we went in and saw their menu, and decided to order something that wasn't pasta. We went for the fish. I had the sea bass and she, the salmon. In all honesty, the portions of side potatoes and broccoli was quite ridiculous. I was hoping I would at least get a more filled section of veggies, but no. Same with the Salmon. It was alright, I've had better bass before. The salmon was not bad, in fact juicy and cooked well. I was kind of jealous of my best friend. But another thing that turned me off, other than the food, was the service. Our waitress was oblivious and negligent. I remember calling her over to look at some dessert options but she flat out ignored me. That would've been extra on my tab and in her pocket. I wish I could remember her name and face, so I guess this is karma cutting her some slack. I feel even worse for not remembering the busser who acted more like a waiter than she. He was so sweet, filled up our bread basket, and although I had already changed my mind about the dessert, his vibes were amazingly kind. I hope he gets promoted whoever this gentlemen is. Lastly, the pasta dishes looked more filling as I saw an employee bringing them to a table near us. I believe in second chances so I might just keep it simple and try the pasta....just not in this location.

Recently held my wedding reception dinner at Sea Fire Grill and it was a wonderful experience. The staff was very accommodating and attentive, the meal was excellent and the response from guests was rave reviews all around. If you are planning a party of up to 28 or just an intimate meal for 2 I would definitely encourage you to think of Sea Fire.

Visited today again, this time for dinner and drinks - amazing experience of excellent food and great service. Candied bacon was a surprise of taste and creativity; skin and bones... let me not spoil it by describing - it will be another interesting dish to try. Tuna sashimi were too salty for my taste, but were loved by my companions and their presentation was amazing.

Visiting NYC and wanted to explore Greenwich Village. Picked this place based on Yelp reviews and it didn't disappoint. I had the french toast and my friend had the biscuits and gravy. Each was absolutely amazing! I will definitely go back next time I'm in town.
Best seafood....Excellent!!!

They have the tastiest, most delicious spicy hot chocolate the world has ever known. It is thick and creamy and such a delectable kick. It's my ultimate guilty pleasure. Frequented the place often when it was chocopologie, but now am pretty excited it's a bar! Very small space, really intimate and adorable. None of that crazy noise from 500 people in a huge bar. Super cute. Hand crafted chocolates delivered freshly made, so you gotta get there early before they run out because they go fast. No mass stocking of mass produced crap. I love this place for the spicy hot chocolate alone, but the rest makes it absolutely charming. A hidden treasure.

We would love to be able to give you input as to the quality of the food but we never got that far. We called up to see if three of us could get a reservation. No deal, but no worries. "It's never busy on Tuesday night." We showed up and, alas, it was quite busy, but no worries, only a fifteen minute wait. After forty minutes the party of four in front of us asked why they weren't being seated at the empty table in the corner. They were informed that the "policy" was that it was only for parties of five. After they were seated at a table for four we continued to wait and watched a group of five saunter in and sit right down.  Finally, after waiting fifty minutes the young host seated us. There were no apologies for our long wait, no effort to make us feel welcome, and we continued to wait. We decided that enduring any more time in a place where we felt so unwelcome didn't seem appetizing. We left, got some delicious take-out food from The Good Times Cafe in Hinesburg, went home and had a pleasant dinner in a dining room where we felt very welcome.
Great menu. Interesting. Service is tops.

I had read some less than wonderful reviews on Yelp, and waited a bit to see if the tide changed any before visiting.  But, I was in the mood for Indian food so went there on a Friday night.  This is a huge place, maybe 25-30 tables, there were maybe 8 of them occupied.  I actually liked that, whatever it's underlying message, as it was comfortable.  Since this BYOB, we sat at a booth and settled in.  Service, which I had read was bad, was very good and we were greeted promptly.  I will say the server was not warm, but he was professional and attentive.  The food came during the expected period of time, and the appetizer came quickly (was Vegetable Samosa and was really really good).  The entrees came when we were comfortably done with the appetizer.  I had chicken korma which was fantastic and my wife had an eggplant dish that was also excellent (and I don't like eggplant, but liked this).  The order of Naan bread was equally good, and the white rice was cooked properly.  So, in the end the food was very very good, although it did stick with me far into the night.  Service was good.  I would like it to be a success, as it is a nice option to have in Nutley which is typically Italian and Steakhouse food.

Really great staff but very basic chicken. There really isn't anything craft about it. Chicken tenders fried in a pretzel batter is hardly craft. I guess I was expecting a little more variety. On the up side, the dark chicken tenders were pretty tender.The white tenders lacked flavor. Additionally the avocado on the mixed green salad is actually guacamole. I was excited to try this place but can't say I'll be back.

This was my home bar for the 3 years I lived in Philly. Why? Great bartender, Karl, amazing Host, delicious food, lovely decor, and always someone new to meet our something interesting going on. So many memories were made here and now I have so many stories to tell. I highly recommend it if you're in town.

Supposed to be the best hamburger in town, however the awful service downgrades it to the worst. Go to minetta's tavern or the corner bistro.  We waited an for food to arrive at 10:45pm and we saw two people arrive and seat 30min after we ordered and got their food 15 min after they sat down. They didn't even apologize for this messed up mistake or offer anything. It's overly pretentious and horrible customer service. Totally not worth it unless you want to wait an hour to be seated and an hour for food to arrive and get nothing for it.

We excitedly went to Gato expecting Bobby Flay magic!!  The blond haired receptionist was rude and did not seat us on time...only after asking a different male receptionist did we get some courteous service.  Overall the service was very good...but , the food, oh so disappointing.  First of all....sooooo SALTY!!!! everything!  We had the crab risotto (SALT), potatoes (SALT), broccolini (SALT), cauliflower (probably least SALTY but SALTY, and the entrees...pork chop, rabbit, all sooo SALTY...without the saltiness they would have been good.   SO DISAPPOINTING, BOBBY!!!!!

This place should be 5 stars. The xiao long bao here is as good as the street vendors in shanghai. Lots of soup inside the dumpling, which is the authentic way to do it. The pork is the best but the shrimp is also ok. I've been here every time I'm in NYC, which is about 7-8 times in the past couple of years. There might be a line outside since the place is really popular. I haven't been to any of their other locations but this one is enough to satisfy my cravings. One more thing, the seating is combined tables, so you'll probably be seated with strangers unless you are in a big group of 7-8 people. Check this place out!
Hand made noodles

Best restaurant in Philadelphia! I moved to Philly from Italy around 4 years ago and it's hard to find a great italian restaurant that is authentic and innovative at the same time! The server was attentive, remembered us from previous dinners and the kitchen was able to perfectly accomodate my mom's dietary restrictions. Our appetizers were the squid, the pork terrine and the fried cauliflower. The paccheri with eggplant fries and swordfish is just perfect and tastes just like something I would get in Sicily. My mom's scallops were cooked to perfection, very juicy. The cacio e pepe is creamy and perfectly al dente! The kitchen staff was really nice and sent us a corn and heirloom tomato salad to try and a rice pudding. I hate rice pudding but I just devoured this one! It had cherries and pistachios on it! The staff went above and beyond to accomodate us and just made my birthday dinner really lovely!

Awesome place! I have tried various spreads, grilled octopus, chicken souvlaki and seafood special. Everything was soooooo delicious. Should go! Service was good, food was surprisingly delicious, atmosphere was clean and simple. Little bit noisy but everything is so good. Great greek experience! Highly recommend!!!

If you are looking for a great spot to unwind after work,  this is definitely it. The food is top notch, and the service is even better. They have something for everyone to enjoy, and you should check out the downstairs where you can pour your draft beer from your own beer taps! The decor matches the experience. All around great place.
Great food. I'm only visiting in this area and I happen to see this place so I checked the reviews and no regrets. Don pepe you rock. The salmon is sooooooooooo good.

ALL THE APPS ARE GOOD, but I especially loved the oxtail springroll, octopus (XO sauce is amazing), fried deviled eggs, and soft shelled crab. The spicy peanut noodles that come with the pig out are delicious and I loved the short rib. Brussels sprouts are always a good pick and definitely get the RICE (OMG yum). The drink list is pretty unique too-they have this delicious ginger ale that I'm obsessed with.

Been here a few times: major turn offs are that a. It's cash only, b. poor service, c. no A/C. Come on. It's 2014, cut the greediness. Drinks and food are relatively decent. I'm really not impressed by the customer service, especially after they sneakily tried to charge our party an obnoxious 40 dollar cake fee for my friends birthday. First of all, we didn't have a cake, my friend just had cookies. Seeing as we didn't need you to light a candle, get plates, or slice anything, what the hell was that for? Anyway, besides being horrified by the surprising fee, the manager argued with me saying that it's a standard. Okay...10 dollar cake fee, fine, 40 dollars? Nope. After arguing with me for ten minutes he finally just begrudgingly said take 40 dollars off then. I'm grateful for it, don't get me wrong, but would I, friends, or coworkers return after being disrespected as a customer? Most certainly not.

Food and drinks are phenomenal,  authentic (I go with Peruvians). This isn't my first time here and it won't be my last. Thank you so much. The Lomo saltado, Leche de Tigre and the Anti Cucho are simply to die for!

I wasn't impressed with the choices on the menu nor the taste of what my friend or I ordered. But it does have a great bar staff and the most amazing view of nyc. Would definitely return but for appetizers and drinks not a full meal
Every now and then I eat somewhere that reminds me why Anthony Bourdain has the best job in the world.  This is one of those places.

My review is completely based on food since I haven't dined there, I had takeout. I tried chicken corn soup and chengdu chicken. The soup was good but chengdu chicken seemed like an americanized version (sweet and saucy). Maybe, I'll try dining here sometime soon and update my review soon.

We were in the area for our daughters birthday.  She loves PEZ and we visited the museum in town.  After we did some shopping at AC Moore and at the check out we inquired about a good place to eat.  The clerk bragged about this place as a great non-fast food place to eat.   The 4 of us were greeted and seated immediately.  We did get hot bread and butter served. It was very quiet but just after the regular lunch rush. The waitress asked if we needed anything from the bar.  Coke comes from the bar.  I inquired about coffee for my husband and she said that does not come from the bar.  ok. The bread was very crusty and hard to bite into the crust. 2 drinks were brought as per our order.  Then she took our food order.  I ordered the veal parm Panini, the girls ordered the steak Panini, and hubby ordered lasagna. The waitress asked 1 about a drink but not hubby.  Since he ordered a regular dinner he got a salad.  When the waitress brought it, she then "remembered" coffee was discussed earlier.  Hubby decided he would stick with water at this point.   The food came in a reasonable amount of time.  The Panini's were large, we wanted to cut the halves into quarters and had a tough time due to the bread being tough.  The steak Panini's were barely seasoned.  Could see onions but no real flavor.  1 was sent back and another veal ordered.  The veal started out good but half of veal was pounded so thin that all you could taste was breading.  It was tough eating the bread too.  The bottom was tough to bite through and very chewy. Then there is the lasagna.  Hubby had me take a taste.  It was horrible.  Tasted like regular ground beef used with no seasonings and the sauce was very bland.  We were very disappointed.   Looking at the reviews on the way over and after hearing from word of mouth - I just couldn't hold back. I would never recommend this place to anyone. I hope the "chef" does better at dinner?!

I went there for some sangria which was fine but I got hungry and knowing the hit or miss reputation this place has I figured to play it safe and just go with a cheeseburger! The roll was stale and the burger itself was tasteless! There is know ketchup or anything on tables.  My friend ordered sausage sandwich that was raw in the middle and had to return! Not sure what I was thinking because Wendy's and Burger King are less than a mile away. Yes I said it! Fast food would have been better not to mention cheaper too!!
This was great food and the prices were good too, family owned and operated, very nice people!!
Had the omakase and extra orders of uni. Yumm. Was hungry later on in the night and ended up in ktown for dinner #2.

Don't let the deli-looking, plastic neon fool you-- Ltauha is a full on restaurant (minus liquor license). All I have had so far was a delicious burger with great french fries. Tasted just like Dumont burger!!! They do need to serve alcohol or at least be BYOB before they get the permit, but it is very promising and I will absolutely be back!

Great food; pork buns are a must! Ramen was excellent. We learned the hard way that this place is a byoc (bring your own container) we had no way of taking the ramen home. Other than that, everything was fantastic!
