My Fiance and I went this evening and had a stunning meal. We were out  running errands and just stopped in for  a nice dinner. This being out first time, lets just say we where both not dressed in a manner that we would deem acceptable for a nice place such as this. The staff  including the chef did not shun us or make us feel out of place. The wine list and menu where more than i expected, we where greeted with a wonderful amuse bouche  (tempura squash blossom) after receiving our bottle of wine. I can go on and on about how wonderful everything was, but i would rather you just go and try  it for yourself. My fiance had the Duck Raviolo and I had the Crescent Duck both where absolutely delectable. Chef Francesco personally stopped at every table and had a chat, which to me was a wonderful show of class and taste. Thanks again for a wonderful evening and we will be back. By all means if you love great cuisine please check this place out
Can't get enough of the banh mi's and vietnamese iced coffee. Super cheat eats, fast and delicious. Cash only.

BBQ is my favorite, my friends also like to have some BBQ at least in a week. Last week we friends decided to hang out for no reason. We decided that place for the whole plan. We reached there for dinner. The atmosphere was awesome like always, as I have been visiting it from last couple of months. I for myself ordered, which was not just great but also had amazing delicious taste. I am very happy to experience it again and again. The staff, like always was wonderful and quick. They served us in a decent way. Whenever we wanted to have some BBQ I always recommend this place. Loved it.

I decided to try Trattoria L'incontro because of all the good reviews on yelp.  I  made the mistake of not reading the negative reviews.  Lesson learned. The service is fast and satisfactory but not fine.  They are trying in my opinion to do way too much at this restaurant.  Way to many specials and not attention to detail.   My meal was rather bland and not special looking.  Not sure if the pasta was homemade or out of a box.  I could not determine any distinct flavors at all.  I am not mentioning the specific dishes because it didn't matter at all.  We had 4 and they all were unimpressive.   I must say everyone in the restaurant seemed happy and they do pack them in.   Given that I don't think I will be back.

Popeye's in Waterbury frequently runs out of ingredients, is always dirty in the kitchen, and has employees who are only eager to leave and not please anyone. I went there and was literally insulted by the manager for no reason other than I was asking why I waited 20 minutes only to be told that they didn't have what I ordered. As a manager of an establishment, wouldn't you think that wasting 20 minutes of a customer's time would be worth apologizing for? Not the case here. I was talked down to and told that I could file a complaint on the web site. When I did file a complaint on the web site, I never heard back from anyone. This was over a month ago. If you spend your money here you are telling Popeye's that it's okay for their employees to be rude to customers and that frequently running out of items that they advertise as having is fine and acceptable. I myself will wait for Chik-fil-a to open instead of go here. If I need my fried chicken fix in the mean time, I will go to KFC Oh and the uneducated, rude, and unhygienic manager's name was Nesby or Nesmy or something.

The food is fantastic and the prices are ok. The service is awful- they want to pump up the number of customers so if you show up solo they'll ask (in their bored way) if you want to sit at the bar. If you say no they'll refuse to seat you.

If I could use profanity I would. Overpriced, overcooked food. My husband ordered Sesame Chicken and shrimp fried rice (with a WHOLE THREE shrimps) The order arrives wrong : General Tsos and NOT sesame as ordered and stated on receipt. Cool. No problem. We call back to let them know, the owner seemed nice until the driver appeared angry and unruly. He BARGED into our home demanding the food. In which, the owner told us to keep because we explained it was already on our plate when we discovered it was wrong. The driver literally stood in our kitchen tremendously out of line, arguing loudly and uninvited for about 10 minutes. I have never received such rude service in my life. STAY AWAY, YOU MIGHT HAVE A STRANGER STANDING IN YOUR KITCHEN.
great soup dumploings
Dude! This was by far the best pizza I have ever had! If you visit NYC you must go and visit this place. Hands down the best!

I love this place. The meatballs, the sandwiches, the pastas, the lobster ravioli...I love it. I don't go here all that much, its more of a treat on a day when I have time to drive around. Robbinsville is a bit away from where I live in PA. That said, it's worth the drive and makes for a great treat. The cannolis are about the best I've had, I need to explore NYC Italian shops some more..well and go to Rome too. I don't have any complaints really. I do wish the proscuitto they sell was not of Boars Head Co. There are other companies that make proscuitto, wish they would get it from someone small, artisanal. Beyond that, with La Stalla in Newtown up for sale, I wish Dolce & Clemente's would consider buying it and taking over the Sleepy's next door. Make a nice size Italian market. The area would love it. Di Brunos would probably feel they'd need to open up some place in Bucks County as well especially as Eataly plans on opening up a store in Philly. Competition...it's good for the tastebuds!

I have only ever ordered for delivery to Port Richmond and have been very happy with almost every order.  There are very few Indian restaurants in Philly, and even fewer in the northeast corner so I was thrilled to have them deliver. I usually order a little extra for a leftover meal the next day. If you have not tried Indian before and you try delivery or takeout they place little labels on each of the containers. I don't need that but can see how helpful it is to anyone trying something for the 1st time. The Biryani is quite good and, to me, very spicy. My standard is the chicken tikka masala and palak paneer. Both very tasty. Murg Malai Kabob was a very pleasant surprise and is now my new favorite. Delivery guys are all very nice and always deliver within the estimated time they state when the order is placed.
This was the best pizza I have ever had! The atmosphere was perfect! The staff was efficient and friendly. We had a great experience and will definitely be back next time we are in town.
Good Food and service

The food here is very delicious and the portions are pretty generous. The seafood risotto was delicious and not too salty like other places.  Free (warm) bread and olives for the table.  Caesar salad was crisp and flavorful.  Flan dessert was a steal at $8.  Beers and wine were reasonably priced.   The rigatoni was very good. The pasta was cooked well and the tomato cream sauce was very good paired with sun dried tomatoes and chicken. The trefunghi was good as well. Will definitely go back whenever I have the chance! Truly a great place to eat in the city.

The pizza looked great. Too bad ours never showed up. Seriously, we sat down and immediately ordered, just one large pizza. Simple. One thing. We waited. And waited. And waited. The table behind us cleared. A new party sat down. No pizza. They ordered. No pizza. They got their pizza. Still NO PIZZA. At that point, we asked our waiter (who, by the way, looked at us with a blank stare, had no freakin clue what we were asking for, and CLEARLY forgot to put in our order). He told us that "the kitchen was busy" and that it was coming "soon." No apology. No attempt to make haste. Ten minutes later, STILL NO PIZZA!!! So we left. That's 45 minutes of my life that I can't get back. HORRIBLE TERRIBLE SERVICE, STAY AWAY!!!!!!!!

Everything we tried (8 dishes between 3 of us) was superb, Each dish had too many ingredients to list but we had the lacinato kale, salt and pepper shrimp, broccoli rabe, black spaetzle, Korean Hamachi, braised pork cheeks, sweetbreads and duck confit...The kitchen produced plates that were hot, spicy, flavorful, and ripe without missing a beat. The wait staff were spot on, attentive yet unobtrusive. If we had any room left we would have sampled more food but just couldn't do it. I absolutely would return and try the dishes we missed.

Surprisingly great pizza. I expected this place to be not good, but we have it a try anyways. Wow. Excellent pizza. Great people. I haven't tries the delivery yet but driver are in and out of this place all day long. I will be back.

I have been to Vietnamese restaurants all around the world, from San Francisco to London, Miami to New York and most of the Pho places on the other side of town in Philadelphia... As for Stock, this is by far the best experience I have had at any of them. The Pho is way better than The Slanted Door in San Fran which is supposed to be among the best in the world. The green mango salad is something I crave, which only gets satisfied by Stock's rendition of the dish. My mouth is seriously watering just thinking about it. When I'm in town I always make a point to stop by. The dishes are very reasonably priced, we've ordered the whole menu every time we've been, and made it out for super cheap. The love put into the dishes reflects the chef's interest in keeping the original Saigon flare, offering the volume restaurant style speed of service but superior, fine dining precision on the raw dishes of beef and fish. I actually started my yelp profile here to speak highly of the restaurant, because my experience has been amazing every time, and that's 4 times since the restaurant opened just several months ago. The service was great, love the simplicity of the decor and it's so refreshing to see a non-ethnic cook behind the dishes. The only complaint is that I had a short wait the last two times, but luckily, the neighborhood (Fishtown) has a few bars and other spots to check out, Johnny Brenda's and some Steven Starr locations around the corner. I'll be back for sure!!!' Just waiting for them to open up locations in Miami and New York... Please hurry!!

I didn't know this place. And now I can say that is one of my favorite brunchs in Brooklyn. I tried the Brisket with eggs and it was great. The drinks also were very tasty and the banana bread as a desert it's also a good deal. Atmosphere is nice. Service could be a little bit improved. But I definitely recommend.

I am huge fan of the fast food like burgers etc. that is why I needed to try that place. This place is as great as was heard. It was recommended by my friend and I should also heard praises of the salon and YES it is amazing The whole staff was active and great. They seem to be helpful. I LOVED THIS PLACE.

The waiters were very attentive to ever need, food was exceptional especially the scallops and oysters. As for the tacos, all of them were wonderful the shrimp could've used a little more flavor but it was still delectable. Decor was great and prices were affordable, would definitely come back as well as highly recommend to anyone.

Very cool restaurant. When we arrived we were quickly greeted. Host greeted us like he knew us. It was pooring outside so for some reason I expected all staff to be in a bad mood. All staff was incredible! We had a tight seating area after we walked through the kitchen. I also felt a little weird waking through the kitchen but it was cool seeing the kitchen in action. Waiter was very helpful and food was incredible.
Un moment magique, tres bon marché, pas tres propre mais des fous rires.... des decouvertes ... si vous etes de passages  à New York, il faut y aller et gouter les trucs les plus bizarres....

I read that Veronica's kitchen was typically open until about 3 PM. After wanderning for a while looking for it (some sites say it's on front st. -- this seems to be outdated information, I found it on water st.) I was incredibly disappointed to see it closed up. This was a shame as I was excited to try it, so I poked my head around back and there were still two workers who seemed to be cleaning up. I asked if they were closed and they said they could try to throw something together for me. They didn't have any sides left but made some jerk chicken for me. They were incredibly friendly and seemed happy to help me rather than annoyed about making food after they thought they were done for the day. For $6 I got 3 pieces of jerk chicken on top of what seemed to be some sort of cabbage and carrot salad. The chicken was absolutely incredible, maybe the best I've ever had. Incredibly flavorful with a great crust, while the chicken itself was tender and falling off the bone. It had a great balance of heat and flavor.. Definitely my favorite place I ate at during my last trip to New York, and is my go-to recommendation when someone asks for food in the area

If you find yourself experiencing Mac & Cheese withdrawals... Like you need a fix, right now! Go here. It arrives in a Cast iron pan of its own. It's great to share or to take in a doggy bag, that's how much it serves. Nuff Said!

It's funny that I feel so strongly that original dokebi is a waste of time but that this location is the go-to spot for me and my bf (esp if we don't feel like cooking). the decor is perfect for a romantic date, the staff are the friendliest and super attentive, the food is slightly pricey but worth it. I recommend the soon du bu seafood stew and of course the dolsot bibimbap. I've tried the burritos a couple times and they were pretty whatever, but my friends claim the tacos are decent. Just stick to the more traditionally korean dishes and you won't be sorry. Little dokebi will is at the top of the list of reasons I am currently lamenting getting priced out of greenpoint

You won't regret going here instead of Chipotle. Homemade, fresh food.  I like the pork burrito best but they're all good.  Nice staff. You can see the cooking facilities are cleaned well & it's fun watching the kitchen staff cook the food.

I visited for my first trip to New York ever and took a lovely lady on our first real date here and everything was flawless. The food was class A and the drinks were delicious. The atmosphere was great and the service was exemplary. I would recommend this to anyone and everyone in the financial district In Manhattan. I had flank steak with yuca croquettes and I was incredibly impressed. Everything was perfect and it was such a good deal. I will return here on my next trip.

I would go back in a heartbeat for the food, but service left a lot to be desired. It took at least fifteen minutes for a server to even come over and say hello. The rest of the meal followed suit taking a long time to get wine and food. At the end of the night we were the last table upstairs, the dining room downstairs was still full and the restaurant was still open for another hour yet they put all the chairs up around our group and shut the lights off on us to get us to leave.
delicious food, great service and cocktails

I always believed that pasta was one of these dishes that were hard to mess up: you can make ok pasta, good pasta, or excellent pasta, but you couldn't really make _bad_ pasta. Well, I'm happy to say that I was wrong. Osteria Morini clearly established that with enough will power, you can make bad pasta. Soaked in oil and salt to the point where you wonder if that's just the dipping sauce for the stale bread, my noodles really didn't deserve their fate. One of the worst restaurants in New York (don't worry though, there's still a line of hungry fashionistas waiting for a table).

Hands down the best cheese steak.  I've had all the other ones inlcuding Geno's, Jim's, Steve's, etc.  You have to get it Wiz Wit (cheese whiz, and with fried onions) and it's the best.  Their cheese fries is also excellent. The lines are long if you go prime time, but sometimes it can be long even at late nights.  Must bring cash!  The parking can be horrible at times and it's the the nicest neighborhood so I would go with friends definitely.

Short line on a rainy day in Philadelphia...also at like 2pm. I ended up getting the Cheeseteak Wit & Provolone. I love provolone so definitely was the cheese of my choice. The meat was juicy, but again - the sandwiches was huge. How can a person finish that and sides - like fries? Too much food for me. I chose Pat's over Geno's since I read my friend's reviews and it appeared they liked it better. Since I was only had one meal dedicated to cheesesteaks, I decided to choose the one of my friends favorites. The food comes out a lot faster than I thought it would have. Since it was slow, the person at the register was probably a bit nicer than it would have been if it was busy. Also you know, a girl by herself. Overall, good experience and next time I would have liked to do a cheesesteak-off between the two places.
Bergen Hill in a nice environment. Perfect for a date. Can get quite busy at the typical dinner hour due to its popularity.
An excellent brunch place, the egg benedict tasted really good. I didn't enjoy smelling secondhand smoke from another customer sitting at the table next to me though
It was cheap. Guess you get what you pay for. Gave me the worst diarrhea of my life. Think I rather pay more and go to one of the better Chinese restaurants in Wayne for dinner from now on.
the best bbq in ct

Last week was there for light dinner. Ordered baked stuffed shrimp; this wasn't bad at all; I rather enjoyed it. Also ordered NE clam chower. This was terrible. Very few clams, potato was puried but worse of all a very harsh hot after taste like way too much white pepper. This was very poor. Nothing about it to recall clams, new england or chowder. Waitress didn't seem to notice I left 95% in the bowl at the end of the meal. Stay away from this item.
Carmine's is the best! Had dinner here last night on a Saturday night. The place was rocking, they were very very busy our server was awesome enjoyed our meal thanks again, and never disappointed

My 2nd time here. Our waiter seemed to disappear. Eventually the bartender noticed our table and another were being ignored and came over but he was covering the crowded bar. I took forever to get a another drink and our check. not going back

I went here for dinner two nights ago with a friend since we noticed it had positive reviews on Yelp. We were quite disappointed. I got a chicken with mixed vegetables dinner and my friend got sweet and sour chicken. Both dishes were lackluster and saturated in sauce. I usually take home a doggie bag when I have left overs but didn't bother this time. We won't be going back.
Spinach and garlic in tin foil with no spice. No thanks. Go for the noodles. Still not great. The cameras over every table are comforting , though.

A very nice, friendly and exclusive restaurant, definitely worth the trip down to the south of Manhattan. The food was very good and had nice presentation. The service staff really worked hard to give you a top service experience and they succeeded. The sommelier was very good and had a humble approach in a positive way. The wine list was really nice. I rate it 7 out of 10. (7/10) If you wanna experience a perfect love couple dinner this is the place.

I very much like the staff and ambiance at Perilla. Small, intimate, relaxing. The menu is rather limited. Four of us shared the signature duck meatballs with mint, tasty but small for $15. The honey gem salad my husband and I shared was SO SALTY that it made my ankles and feet swell up. I can honestly make a much better balanced salad at home, sorry to say. We shared the hake and tilefish, both good but flavors weren't mind blowing at all. I did prefer the crunch of the pistachios combined with raisins and puree with the tilefish. The chocolate souffle was good, very small, as was the cheesecake. For the competitiveness of dining in NYC, it's not a destination I would return to. And quite pricey.
The customer service was terrible. Waited for 15 minutes and was never asked to take an order. They didn't seem to care much.
Poor service. Nobody was there when I entered. After 3 mins a guy came and seated me. Food took long time to be served. Good was ok. If you are really hungry, please go some where else

Love Rockys pizza and their calzones! Great New York style pizza! We are from NY and when we first moved to Vermont we were in south Burlington and had a hard time finding a decent pizza place. Once we moved to Essex junction and found Rockys we couldn't have been happier. I definitely prefer being in NY and getting NY pizza, but they are a great replacement. They are friendly and quick and the ice cream is good too!
ABSOLUTE WORST!!!!!!!!!!! I got out to eat a lot and I've never come across such a rude waiter. If you are considering going here..DON'T.

Great service here. Appropriately attentive service from our waitress, Maureen. This was the second time she served me and last night she worked delicately around four friends catching up. Summer special Mediterranean lobster bisque was delicious. Summer special eggplant lasagna was too heavy on cheese for my liking, but still good. A beautiful restaurant. Always great service and good food.

One of the best chicken/gyro plates I've ever had. It's also convenient that the sauce is on the side so that when you get it to go, the container doesn't get soggy. You get a great amount of food for the right price. Depending on the time of day, the line can be a bit long, but it moves along well. It is so worth the wait. Definitely would go back over and over again.
Hands down the best halal place in NYC. This is my go-to spot after a night of drinks.
its great price in the huge amount(espeically in NYC!) but it actually taste the same just like other halal food not really stunning

Always busy no matter what but for good reason. Roast pork with rabe, peppers and cheese is the best sandwich I have ever had! Everything I go to the market I get it as a staple along with trying other things in the area.

I had Chris' grilled cheese and it was DELICIOUS! I'm not much of a coffee drinker but the owner recommended their house blended iced coffee and it was great..I will be back every time I'm in the neighborhood.

Beware if you are thinking of placing a catering order.....I ordered a sandwich platter (which was delicious) but when I went to pick it up they tried to charge me double!  And tried to give me sandwiches without any meat, contrary to my order! I filled out an order form two weeks prior and a manager showed me how the bread would be sliced to make 10-12 sandwiches for one platter.   So I ordered one platter and asked for 4 sandwiches to be made without meat.  When I asked the flavors I would be receiving, I was brushed off with, "whatever the chef would like to make that day."  This should have been my first warning sign.  All of this was in writing and placed in a binder.  I didn't get a copy of what I wrote down as my order,  a second bad sign. On my scheduled pick up day, I called in the morning to confirm my order would be ready for the afternoon.   They said it would be and nothing more.  When I arrived hours later, I wad told "there was a problem with the order" and that they "tried to call," which they did not. Turns out the "problem" was of their own inventing.  They said they needed to use double the bread to fill my order.  They took 24 sandwiches out of the fridge;  I didn't order anywhere near that amount!  And not a single one had meat.  When I refused to pay double and said I would only pay for what was on my order form, they conveniently couldn't find the form.  The counter attendant called the manager on the phone who continued to insist that I pay more, at least 1.5 more for a platter. The counter attendant finally relented, put prosciutto in 6 of the sandwiches,  and only charged me for what I ordered.  Then she threw in a free box of six more.  Still confused about that since they were determined to charge me more. Bottom line: if you order catering,  get everything in writing and watch them like a hawk.  The female manager with the prominent French accent can't be trusted on her word alone.  This is a poorly managed business.  The food is good, so it would be a shame if that is their undoing.

Great little bagel shop. Not fancy and not particularly pretty which means it's reeeeally good. They now have whole wheat everything bagels. (I am a visitor and the last time I was here they weren't offering.. Not sure when they started selling these.) The bagels are delicious and have tons of flavor on both sides. I definitely used the last of my ketchupy bagel to pick up the flavor that fell off onto the plate! They also sell chicken cutlets, heroes, chips, drinks, macaroni salad, potato salad, etc. There are 4-5 tables inside and people rotate pretty quickly so if its packed when you walk in, you'll likely get a seat by the time you pay and get your food. They look a little scattered behind the counter with 4-5 people doing everything per order (rather than one person doing all meat, another person staying at the register, etc) but they definitely get it done and satisfy. My friend got a BLT on a croissant.. But I recommend you order a Taylor ham, egg and cheese on whole wheat everything bagel with salt, pepper and ketchup... and enjoy!
Avoid this place at all costs. I found a hair in my burger. Not worth your time or your money.

I had been a regular visitor of this place. However yesterday I took my parents (my dad is 74 years old and my mom is 65 years old) to this restaurant along with my husband. My husband was going around the Hell's Kitchen area to find a parking spot while my parents and I reserved a table for 4. I was told the wait is 20 min. After about 20-25 min when we didn't get called, I enquired about the table. And hence I get told by Bill and Fa (the host at the entrance) that the restaurant does not entertain incomplete parties (my husband was still searching for a spot around the area to park the car - it was taking longer than usual as it was a Saturday). I asked bill and Fa if it wouldn't be better if they could have informed me about this when we were waiting. Fa seemed least concerned and started entertaining other customers while Bill behaved indifferent. Since my parents are pretty old and my mom was a diabetic I asked for a table then and there even telling them that I will order for my husband. Fa said 'ok' so i waited for the next 5 min and when I check back again, Bill and Fa remain firm on not giving us a table and entertain other guests who have come after us. I then said I will change the table number to just 3 guests if they could give me a table right then. Both bluntly replied without even looking at me : 'we do not have a table ready right now' .. After my husband entered the restaurant (finally after finding a parking spot in the city) they made us wait for another 10 min before giving us a table. Room service host doesn't not have courtesy for their customers or even mannerisms on how to treat the elderly. I guess they are getting paid for being rude.as much nice as their food is, i am never turning back there again!
Go for pat's! but i think they're both over-rated to be honest...

CASH ONLY. BUT- Great turnaround, the wait isn't long, the service is fantasitc, and the food was perfect. Nothing fancy, but just well-done pancakes (Danish), home fries  (get the hot sauce to put on 'em), and french toast which pair wonderfully with the home-made flavored butter. Sometimes all it takes for 5 stars is to deliver perfectly on a simple premise. Good food, served quickly with good service, at a great price. Done.

The waitress was very nice and tried to help out our gluten free guest. We sampled most dishes on the menu, and found good, solid food, but very few exceptional dishes. The squid was good, octopus okay, meatballs fairly tasty, the melted cheese very salty. Fried appetizers were a little greasy, but also not bad. The artichoke moussaka was tasteless.The best dish on the menu was the simple lamb chop; perfectly cooked medium rare, juicy and flavorful. Overall I would not mind returning for a second look, as we love Greek food. However, there were few "knockout" dishes.
Make reservations! fills up quickly and for good reason. Excellent food, service, and atmosphere. Will become a favourite when visiting East Village.

A bit overpriced but honestly so very delicious. They have coupons in Valpak so look out for them. I'm a New Yorker so I've had many of bagels. It's no H and H but it's good. They could have better hours.

The BeeHive Oven Café is one of those rarities in New York, but particularly in a self-important Williamsburg, that feels genuinely like home. I and my boyfriend were greeted by John, the friendliest man that you may ever meet in New York, and he showed us to our table in the cozy space. Say hello to John, ask him questions, he's an absolute stand up gentleman. Adorable pasta strainers for shades, a humble staff, a drool-worthy menu, inventive riffs on classics drinks (try the Prickly Pear Lemonade. Just... just do it) and the wine and beer selection of a veteran Brooklyn spot, this place surprised and delighted me in the best way. We shared the jezebel wings (delicious, chutney like, the perfect balance of sweet and spicy), downed our Prickly Pear lemonade (seriously, get it) while munching on the welcome plate that each table receives (veggies and a delicious buttermilk dressing). I then had the Moselle while my boyfriend created his own biscuit sandwich (re-read that sentence: you can create YOUR OWN BISCUIT SANDWICH). The Moselle came with fried chicken a fried egg, collard greens and hot sauce which I opted out of and am happy I did so because I was really able to experience the delicious taste of the Beehive Oven's fried chicken. We're talking on par with Sweet Chick a few blocks away and the Redhead in the East Village. Treat yourself to it. I can't let you know how my boyfriend's dish was mostly due to it being gone by the time I was halfway through with my own food. He sighed a hearty appreciation though, which is a great sign given how particular he is. Not wanting to miss out, I ordered the Prickly Pear Mimosa (are you seeing a theme here?) and ordered a slice of the Red Velvet Cake with the boyfriend opting for the Banana Bread Pudding. The mimosa was delicious but the cake took the ... well, the cake. Soft, buttery, delicious and MASSIVE. I almost couldn't finish it and then found the will and courage to devour it entirely. The atmosphere at the Beehive Oven is comfortable and inviting, the prices cannot be beat, the food is delicious, the staff is friendly, and I'm writing this mostly because I want this place to be massively successful. That said, it's a hard to think that it might get too popular, because I don't want to have to wait for the phenomenal biscuits. Or the Prickly Pear lemonade. Which you should get.

Cheese steak sandwich was very filling and low priced. Garlic cheese bread hit the spot. The bread was a bit chewy on the sandwich but I did get it to go and waited a while to eat it. I would definitely go back. They have a minimum order amount for credit cards.

Food is average- we had cheap clams which were pretty good for the price, chowder soup (not so much), and their chicken sandwich is pretty tasty with a side of macaroni and cheese (delicious!).  But the space is what makes this place one to remember.  It's view of the water is great and since we first started going to Brooklyn crab, they have made their mini-golf free. Great for budget-friendly fun! The staff definitely needs some attitude adjustments though. Girl named Valerie was very rude and brought this rating down.

I am awake and will shortly get dressed and make my way to Clinton St. There is always a line at BEFORE THEY OPEN..grrr. But it is SO SO GOOD. I have been eating breakfast here daily for the last 3 weeks. My pregnancy cravings are thoroughly met here.

This place is awesome!!!!   Five stars if you ask me.  Chrissy is awesome as well and always greats me with a smile on her face.  Whether it's the Bacon Blue Burger, or a Cheese Steak, there is nothing that does not taste fabulous here at Sonny's. The atmosphere is always pleasant and the shop is always clean. As far as I am concern, Sonny's has the best food made in Philly.

The food here is delicious but beware of wait time on weekends.  They also do not take reservations so it's first come first served.  We waited roughly an hour and a half on a saturday night.  All that aside, the food was fantastic.  Also a great atmosphere, but not for those who like a quiet dinner.  There are many large parties here and it's also BYOB so there are many loud people.  Overall, the food is great and the atmosphere is fun and exciting.  Definitely a must try!!!!!

The stars are for the food and cocktails preparation at the bar. I definitely recommend it. The decor is well done its like walking into a world of roses and the scent is beautiful. The staff as a whole did not make my experience better. As i said, the stars are for food and cocktails
This is a pretty good dim sum restaurant.  Although the service is not great, the taste is excellent and the price is pretty reasonable.

I made an account just to post this review, because I was so unhappy with my experience here last month: I was here with a friend on Saturday night & the bartender/waitress was extremely rude and befuddled when we asked about happy hour, which was clearly written on the menu. She first said it didn't exist, then when we pointed it out on the menu she said it was 12 noon not midnight, even though the menu clearly read "Midnight, 12 am until close." The funniest thing was that she accused us of writing it on the menu to "trick" her. What? It was your choice as a restaurant to create "menus" out of old cardboard boxes, items written hastily in marker. Have people written fake specials on in the past and demanded such prices? Such poor customer interface means I won't be coming back

BAD BAD BAD DO OR DIE Everything is deep fried without any taste that really really doesn't need to cost you this price. You are in BUSHWICK  in the middle of nowhere hello, and you charge 20 bucks for a tiny piece of chewy fish that taste oil?(and everything else's was as fried as the fish.I couldn't eat that.

The food was good, great tasting, fresh and great quality. Our waitress and table runner were just amazing, incredibly attentive but not so much so that it felt intrusive. Decor is a distressed Parisian style, although in some places a little over done so that is looks grubby, but I assure you it isn't. Highly recommended.

Best Japanese food I have ever tasted if you haven't been here you MUST try it, the food is delicious!!! The staff is nice and hibachi is good also, I recommend trying the noodles and the salad also if you think the salad is good you can buy it there too! I would give this a 5  because of the hibachi anyways I'm already about to eat so come try it too! KOTO is the best!!!

My husband Rick and I were going to come here before going to a Phillies' game but  instead we opted to eat lunch here.  And it was a good thing we did too.  It was crowded enough already--imagine what this place is  like before a ballgame! Chcikie's & Pete's is well known for their seafood--particularly shellfish.  I ordered the Jumbo Lump Crab Cake sandwich, one of the best I've ever eaten, but man-o-man, "Jumbo" is right.  Good thing I was able to walk it off afterwards!  Rick wnated t do the touristy thing and order a Philly Cheesesteak.  Well he went for the  lobster topped  Philly and did it ever look good too! And yes we did split ad order of their famous Crabfries!

It should not take 45 minutes to get two tacos. Period. End of story. Let me back up. My wife & I love tacos. We joke around that we would probably eat them once a day. And the tacos at Gueros are, for New York at least, really quite good. Far better than the fare served at the entirely overrated Chavellas. But: tacos are not fine dining. They are not slow food. They are the kind of thing you get with a beer on your way to someplace else.  They should not take 45 minutes to arrive, they should not be consistently forgotten and misplaced, and you should not get half your order and then never get the other half. The bottom line is: Gueros is a place I have gone to many times, always hoping they will have solved their weird logistical issues, the kind of issues that make ordering for pickup, showing up, and then grabbing a seat if there is one the most surefire way to get what you want in a reasonable amount of time. I'm not the kind of person who trashes a place for a single screw up, or a single incident, or even two or three. The thing is, though, that Gueros is the kind of place where you have a 33% chance of not getting your food on time, or (like today) at all. There will eventually be a shakeout on Franklin Avenue wherein the large number of amateur hour businesses eventually fade away to be replaced be people who actually know what they are doing.  Gueros, however, will be around for a long time, because there will always be a horde of hungry Pratt kids who don't mind, or are too drunk to notice, they just waited an hour hour a taco. Too bad. I like the food here. They just don't know what they are doing when it comes to logistics.

We went to Halvorson's tonight and were quite disappointed.  When we sat down, the table was wet, but we didn't read much into it.  As we waited for waters, we watched the waitresses eat their wings in the register/side bar area.  Another patron came in to say he had a reservation for 8 people, etc.  The employee said they had tables x,y,z reserved for him and pointed him outside.  He pleasantly commented that "he hasn't worked here in a while, so wasn't sure what that meant."  She then continued to give him directions to the table instead of leading him to it. As we sat, we noticed the a/c duct was dripping water into our food/drinks.  We moved and then told the waitress why. . .she said ok, but made no effort to offer replacement food/drinks.   As we were leaving, my husband walked with the stroller, fighting with a heavy door as parent with small kids typically do.  One waitress watched, the other was making her way out to one of her tables outside,  blew past him, obviously having forgotten something, and left him there fighting with the door.   We have eaten here numerous times, obviously why we went back, but were not impressed.  The staff was lacking common courtesy and regard for others. The food was good, but the drinks we weak and tasteless.

We had a lovely meal on a Friday night at Marc Forgione. The restaurant has a great, laid back comfortable feeling about it. It was busy but friendly. We arrived early and enjoyed some time at the bar sampling some unique cocktails. The food was great, the service was fine, not over the top but efficient. I would definitely go back and try other dishes. The striped bass was so flavourful and cooked perfectly. Would definitely return.
I give 5 stars for their salad. The bacon-mashed potato pizza - was not for me. But definitely will go back for their other pizzas.

The really good thing about this restaurant is the atmosphere, and that is also what lured us in, together with what at first glance looked to be an interesting menu. Italian dishes and different seafood like soft shell crabs and oysters looked good on paper. We ordered pasta and soft shell crabs and it turned out to be far from interesting. It was not bad, but Im not often this bored with a meal. Actually I barely kept up interest to finish. The service followed the same path. Our waiter was polite and correct .
I really like this place. Good vibe. People are friendly and relaxed. I like the coffee and the pastries are well made.  I have not had the pizza but I will be back.

After 2 brunch dates and a visit for lunch I have to say that I've really enjoyed each experience, especially for brunch. The brunch menu includes interesting choices and the portions are plentiful. The service is friendly  and not once did I feel rushed. For the price ($21 currently) you receive a plate full of pastries and another with fruit, your choice of a number of entrees, and coffee, including unlimited cappuccinos, juices and so forth. I'm not sure about the inclusion of alcoholic beverages, but they had me at cappuccino! Portion sizes for most entrees are massive, good for a late lunch/dinner. Try the Eggs BLT or Breakfast Quesadilla, delicious and filling.
I love this place. Good food, inexpensive and a short walk from my work! Service can be a bit slow so go on an off hour. Tiger rolls are great and try the desserts!

Had a truly wonderful meal with friends, however I must admit listening to hard rock during my meal was a little odd. I felt like I was in a Bikers bar. Besides the atmosphere that was different, the food was amazing. Had the spinach salad and the special pasta of the day. It was truly delicious and loved the portions, not to BIG so was able to finished every little bite. Satisfied.

The Food at this place is just great. Their food that they have for lunch is so YUMMY. Once you try it you just get hooked on it. Their variety is really good too,You can probably eat their a whole week, by having different types of food. The only things that I don't like their is their dumplings, which do not taste too good....other than that ... everything is a GO!!!

Just ate here last night, and I can't wait to go back. Decor - simple, clean, and very cool looking. Service - nothing better then a family run business, you feel like you're at home. Super friendly and attentive. Price - very reasonably priced, 'nough said Last, but certainly not least FOOD - had the guacamole to start, delicious, and the abodo taco and the fish taco. GET THE CHEESE ON THEM! It was so good, and both were very well prepared, flavored, and were healthy portions. Support your local family owned businesses and go enjoy this fantastic cuisine!

The food and the presentation were excellent!! Unfortunately, our server wasn't friendly. He was tall and looked miserable. He never smiled and I wondered if like serving us. It was dark and dreary and the space downstairs was way too tight. Otherwise excellent food and friendly hostess.

After reading a few reviews here yesterday, I thought I'd drop in this morning and order some breakfast sandwiches and a side of cornbeef and homefries to go. I arrived at 10:30 after any breakfast rush. Only a couple of customers happily eating in the corner. Ashley greeted me personally, super mom like and adorably friendly. I ordered for me and my wife, and sat down to wait for the food. It only took about 11 minutes and she said I looked hungry so she had given me some "extra".  I dipped into my wallet to pay the bill, and was embarassed to realize that I did not come prepared with enough cash. She said don't worry about it and smiled and accepted my $18. (Sandwiches $5 ea, plus large styrafoam takeout container)  When I got home to my wife and we opened the carry out bag, we discovered Ashley had given us not only what we asked for, but a heaping extra helping of bacon and sausage. I look forward to returning to Ashley's Restaurant when ever I have time for comfort food in the late morning.

Hudson Eats is a tough place to get to if you don't already work in the building. I traveled from Water st. and thought my commute was over once I passed the hoards of tourists near the 911 memorial but no, there are several other hurtles to get by first. Due to construction, your trip will have an abundance of drywall-scented turns as though you are walking through a maze in a new construction. I'd recommend giving it till the winter for them to get finished with the installations. Once you get in, it is very clean and has lots of options. Most people will go for lunch and it will be an expensive one as the offerings here are smaller versions of their higher end brother sites. Overall, the feeling is that of an overpriced mall cafeteria. My lunch was from "skinny pizza" which I cannot really recommend. I spent 15 bux on lunch and was still hungry. I noticed other big names such as Blue Ribbon sushi, Num Pang, Black seed Bagels, Umami, Dos Toros, Digg Inn and Tartinery. If this place were more accessible, i'd give it an extra star but it is well out of the way for most people.

I hadn't been before, and the shopping center it is located in was rather shabby, so I didn't know what to expect. Walking in, the decor was a pleasant surprise. The restaurant was more up-scale inside than your average chinese restaurant, with more of the modern, japanese decor of a sushi place. It was the kind of place I would feel comfortable bringing colleagues. The booths were spacious, and the lighting was attractively designed The staff was really attentive, though that may partially be because the restaurant was, sadly, nearly empty at lunch time. The food came out really quickly, which made me think that they would be a great place to come for a mid-week lunch during the work day. The appetizers came out within 5 minutes, the entrees about 10 minutes later. The food was tasty. We each ordered soup; I had the miso soup and my friend had the hot and spicy soup. Both soups were very good. The hot and spicy was much spicier than many other places we have tried it, and they definitely didn't skimp on tofu or veggies in either. Neither soup was too salty, and they came out piping hot. We also tried the peking duck roll appetizer. It was fried well, the plum sauce was delicious, and, again the portions were impressive. It was something neither of us had had before, and we both agreed we would definitely come here to get it again. The chinese food menu seems stronger than the sushi menu. The General Tsos was delicious, as was the fried rice. Our sushi was fine, good quality for the price. I saw a couple of interesting special roles I'll probably try next time. I was also impressed by the fact that, upon leaving, we were followed out to the parking lot by a waitress-- she realized my friend had dropped his pack of gum, and wanted to return it to him. I have to think most people would definitely not have bothered, and that was just a nice thing to do. Overall, good experience, solid food, and I'd go back.

I've known this place under its many incarnations, and it is at its best as Metro North.  My mother, a family friend, and I went for an early dinner last night and had a perfect dinner.  Joanne was our server and was attentive and patient, even though we can be a bit high-maintenance.  She was very knowledgeable about the menu and the wine list! I started with the French Onion soup, and it was so good that I can taste it now just thinking of it. I notice that a lot of other reviewers have said the same thing, so they're consistent!  My mother's friend and I both had the Chicken Marsala, and not only did I love it, but my mother's friend said that it was the best Marsala sauce she'd had in 20 years! Joanne topped the evening off by keenly recognizing my martini needs and addressing the issue by recommending the delicious Chocolate Martini.  Everything was lovely!  The only criticism I have for the restaurant is that while the appearance is cozy and intimate, the acoustics are oddly balanced, so communication was a little difficult, especially with an 85-year-old at the table.  Otherwise, a new favorite! Thank you, Metro North and Joanne!

Nice restaurant. We went there twice already. On second time, we brought our friends and they like it too. The food is good. I like the grilled Sea bass. I don't know the name. The environment and atmosphere is really nice. The price range is reasonable. Most importantly, service is good.
Great atmosphere... Food has gone down. Sake list still one of the best in the World.

This place has the best, freshest, tastiest food ever.   You do not need to be a vegan to go here. It is delicious. We went last Saturday night. Great food and service.  Second time here. We don't think we will be going anywhere else in Montclair now that Mundo vegan is here. Well worth a try!

Love this place...LOVE IT!! If you care a whit about NYC and its people and are in any way attracted to watching the world amble by while enjoying a perfect, well-priced meal, this is your place. As an East Village veteran we have all found those perfect spots where you could hang and drink in the vibe while drinking the vino, and then had to figure out the next one as the last one lost its lease or its vibe. Maybe this will happen to Contrada too but I'm glad to have gotten in on the ground floor. My only complaint is that in less than six months the kitchen has taken true winners off the menu and replaced them with new, mostly delicious items. I only wish they'd give their winners a little more run time. And, yes, file the above complaint in the bin labelled "First World Problems."
do not order from grubhub. my order never came and when i called they said the fax machine was busy.

I went on a first date here for dinner this past Saturday night and it definitely earned it's place as "No. 2 best new restaurant of 2014 in the United States" by Bon Appétit magazine.   We did the "Leave it to Us" menu, asking specifically that they include the Green Tea Garganelli and the Angry Crab Spaghetti and they did not disappoint. One side-note though... make sure you tell them several times if you have any serious allergies.  My date had an allergy to nuts and, despite telling the waiter about this at the beginning of the meal, he kept delivering things with nuts in it without warning her.  When dessert came, it was one of their house-made ice creams piled high with nuts.  When we reminded him of the nut issue, he apologized... and took the dessert away.  It would have been a nice gesture on the part of a restaurant of that distinction to have at least have come back with a replacement dish of ice cream, without the nuts.  But apparently, that wasn't part of the "Leave it to Us" menu.   Other than that, a top-notch restaurant.

I attended their lobster buffet for a friend's family birthday celebration. There were over 10 of us and it was amazing! The buffet was superb! They had a variety of great options. I really enjoyed their lobster bisque as a starter. The Lobster was delicious and there was an abundant amount to go-round. I had zero issues with food poisoning as other guests stated; however, I did not attend a wedding function but rather the buffet. I heard the Al La Carte dinner is great as well.

Did not get as far as the food When entered foyer smelled of cigarette smoke thought someone lit up before got outside I was seated as the odor of cigarettes was do strong I could not stand it Left and went a few doors up to the mule bar. Here I found fresh air great IPA and oh so fabulous food

Great Place! The staff was friendly, especially the bartenders! They're fun to talk to when sitting at the bar. The food, I tried the cream pasta. It was so good, my friend ordered one for himself! (because I didn't want to share it!) The dumpling was a delight. Right texture and the portions are good for bar munchies. great bar food over all. Must try!

My boyfriend and I were looking forward to doing restaurant week and to our surprise this restaurant was apart of it. From the moment we stepped in the restaurant we were greeted by this polite host who offered us a table in the dining room but, we wanted to do happy hour so he suggested the bar area. Which was perfect because we enjoyed the booth we choose directly across from the flat screen tv's. The Writing Room is really cozy, happy hour was 20% off drinks and the prix-fixe dinner was $38 of amazing food. I had the fava bean hummus as an appetizer and my boyfriend had the sweet corn soup, fried chicken and biscuits we both had because our waitress sold us with her mouth watering description on how it was made, and for dessert I had the hazelnut chocolate cake and he had creme brulee. I give five stars because from the service to the food it was a great experience!! Perfect place for a date, I will be returning:)

OMG the signature ward III cocktails is out of this world... It was like when a mad scientist comes up with an instant love potion and gave to me. A must have! Must must must have. I didn't eat here but them cocktails, ambiance and cool vibe will get me coming back every Monday!!! I used to go to school around there and know the area very well. Its definitely an addendum to the community. Love love love!!! Rock n roll baby!

I have no idea how the food was because yesterday we waited for over an hour for a table for 4.  The guy standing outside who was responsible for seating people was very charismatic and funny but he totally left us hanging.   Again, We waited for over an hour outside,  we watched as other people,  table for two,  table for three were seated, people who came after us. After an hour, we walked away and the guy didn't seem to care.   I'll never try again.

Highly recommended when it is nice out in the spring, summer & fall months. Sit outside- the patio has a great atmosphere! My friend and I went for dinner and drinks and got a pitcher of something fruity - I don't remember what it was called, but there was red wine, limoncello & blueberries in it. That was ok but very lemon-y. For dinner, I ordered the 3 meatballs, my friend ordered a side salad, and then we split a pasta with crab meat and spicy sauce (I believe there was chile in it). The meatballs were good, but there are raisins in them and I wasn't a huge fan of that. As for the pasta - SO GOOD. It was small though (especially for $19), so if you're going to split it with someone, make sure to get something else as well. But seriously.... that pasta was well worth the price.
This little gem of a restaurant has a wonderful garden/patio area where we ate a late dinner. wonderful food, reasonably priced, and excellent house pinot grigio. Would recommend this place!

for those that want below par food or can be classified under the category of tourists, this is your place to go.  they are experienced with non asian speakers. also, long waits for a table equal high quality food, right? i mean come on! everyone is going there! almost everytime i pass by this place, i see a line out the door with people holding their zagat guides waiting to get a seat during dinner time. i use to come here when i was a kid, when chinatown was less crowded, when tourists didnt even know what a soup dumpling was.... but now with shanghai cuisines popping up all over the city, there are much better places to go if youre a local. a hole in the wall usually is best.... goodluck on your search!

I had the pork belly tacos and the refried beans. They were very good. I also had the chocolate cake with banana ice cream. Which was delicious. The only negative was the ice cream which had some ice crystals (possibly frozen chunks of bananas) that were not very appealing.
I loved this place. The food was really good, but if you go for brunch make sure you are there early because there is a lot of people! The atmosphere is pretty great.

Sorely disappointed! Saw a feature on Diners, drive-ins and dives and couldn't wait to stop on for a burger and duck poutine. Instead, I got a server/hostess that told me  it would have been better to make a reservation.  We sat at the bar instead of waiting for a table. The bartender was sweet - but clearly new and the waiter on shift yelled at her over and over. Total ass - never smiled - should not be working in customer service. Again, excited for the food so we ignored the obnoxiousness! Ordered burgers with bacon med and med well, no duck on the brunch menu.  Burgers came out rare and med rare, no bacon.  Disappointed by the whole experience, didn't bother sending it back. The bartender was being tortured enough my her co-worker....didn't want to meek her shift worse!  Terrible experience, with just an ok burger. Love Guy but this is 1 triple D spot I will avoid in the future. Don't waste your time.
rad sushi in bk

The Good: - This place has some fun decor. - The outdoor area looked great. - Good variety of drinks offered. The Bad: - This place was DEAD on a Saturday around 10-11PM. Though they had pop music blaring, it almost added to the sad, sad vibe. -The bartenders and manager were drinking booze the entire night. Maybe this is somewhat normal in the industry but damn, they weren't even trying to hide it. All I know is I'd rather the waitstaff be a little more attentive and a little less drunk on the job. * A tip for you: Their "Happy Hour" specials start at 10PM, strangely enough, but there are some nice deals such a $4 beers, shots, etc. *

I checked out Pitaziki because I had heard good things, and I was not let down. The atmosphere is very bright and fresh, and the employees are super friendly. The owner, Khaled, and his son are especially kind, and they gave me great service. I ordered the beef shawerma in a pita. I added all sorts of other things and they all mixed together and made a delicious dinner. The baba ganoush was especially tasty. And the pita was so warm and fluffy...I am dreaming of it still. Check out the outdoor seating in the courtyard area, it had a great ambiance.

Love the craft cocktails and apps. This is my go to place for after work drinks out of the downtown hustle. The entrees are a bit pricy for me though I have been to the Mother's Day brunch. Ok for the first time but expected more from a brunch. Ask the bartenders to make you something special! Great Vermont liquors!
Average vietnamese, but over priced and over rated catering to the hipster crowd. Save your money and stick to places that are not hipster hyped.

I didn't know how great this restaurant is but my aunt suggested going to it and a free meal won't ever be turned down. Taverna Kyclades has a great location, only a couple of blocks from the train. We sat on the patio on a nice day and it was definitely crowded and bustling. We ordered as appetizers their trio of dips and their greek salad. The dips are absolutely delicious with their oiled bread. My favorite is still the cucumber dip but their red dip that's a little bit sweeter is also very delicious. The greek salad literally comes with slabs of feta. The dresses for their salad is also refreshing and balances out the richness of the bread. I ordered the grilled calamari and my aunt ordered the fried whiting. The grilled calamari was cooked perfectly and not chewy at all. My only complaint is that there were a lot of black crusts from the grilling that wasn't so tasty. The fried whiting was definitely better than the calamari. It had a great breading that was crispy but not too thick. It came off the bones easily and had the perfect level of salt to it. I would definitely come again and try all of the different dishes. There's a reason why so many people come and the reviews are so great. I can't wait to try the rest of their menu.

Hosted my office fantasy football draft party at fish market.  Went in expecting cheap beer, wings and a chill place to draft and goof off.  Fishmarket exceeded my expectations with a friendly waitstaff, great food (wings were ok and chicken fingers were good but the fried rice, chicken curry and pork belly blew us away) and the Jameson flowed like wine.  Would def come back for dinner or for a place to watch football on the weekend.

Very spacious, beautifully appointed room. This is a large restaurant. Tables are well spaced, and so not noisy - what a lovely change. The table settings very upscale and nicely done. The dishes are presented on large white china flat bowls. The service was superb. 100% recommend this restaurant. Would be good for dinner too - as it is also in good proximity to Grand Central.
Such a great night at this neighborhood gem. Great ambiance, excellent service, outstanding food, seasoned perfectly. Duck confit was spot on!  Can't wait to return!
The China Pavilion serves the BEST Sesame Chicken ever! I have been going there for at least 20 years and it's never disappointing.

BT receives a full 5star review even thought they have gone "all fancy-smancy" with waiter service. The self-serve worked just fine for me.  Mark was cool and he resembles the character Lt.Dangle from Reno 911, so I guess it will grow on me.  You do what you have to do to enjoy the bona fide best brisket in all of NYC. Two buddies had never been to BT and one had (with me in 2013). They were utterly floored.  On several occasions this crew has canvased LIC and Astoria for BBQ. BristketTown was the ace up my sleeve.  They could not believe the brisket could be so moist and  tender - but still have the right amount of char on the end and smokiness.  They each enjoyed their side dish, as well as the quality of the pickled accompaniments that came with the platter.  I skipped on the sides -   a slice of potato bread and a cold-one are enough for me. We will all be back, though I suspect my buds will tell other people - dang!
great place
I love hunan dishes, there are only limited places cooked it. The food I tried here is almost as good as original hunan taste. Love the pickled beans and Chinese bacon here.
Beautiful restaurant in a great location. Food was excellent, service even better. Not too noisy-able to hold and hear our conversation.

Best sushi in montclair. Hands down. Only place in town I will eat. Their sweetheart salad is amazing.  Samba roll and temptation roll would be the two that I would recommend.   The family that owns this restaurant all work there. The sushi chef/owner is always behind the sushi bar. You will never leave unhappy
excellent place to take time enjoy  a meal with someone special ...  BYOB works well...

I ordered food from this place from seamless web. I called after a hour because seamless said delivery time would be between 30-45 minutes. The gentlemen on the phone said it would be another 20-30 minutes. No apology. Terrible customer service. Never ordering from you again.

We had the calamari and the spinach pizza, and it was amazing. There was a long line ahead of us, and we were still seated in no time. The food came out really quickly, and the servers were delightful. The calamari was really light and delicious, and the pizza was thin crust and perfect authentic New York. So glad we discovered it.
The combinations Of food Rocco puts together are fantastic.The mascarpone cheese and fish was deliscious.I'm still thinking about the soft shell crabs with tarregon and a little hint of Anise flavor.

Awful experience, really rude personell and wet, saggy sandwiches. They were absolutely not interested in service and were more busy speaking spanish to each other. Positively they gave me a full refund when I didn't want the wet, saggy sandwich.

This place is amazing even in the land of hip and cool restaurants with pedigreed chefs. We started the evening with a cocktail at the chic bar...a delicious elixir over a giant ice block. Then on to our table...our server was friendly and very knowledgable. I started with the braised beef ribs over risotto-this I'm sure is what is served in heaven. My entrée of beet ravioli with pistachio creme was an incredible, creative combination of flavors.

I wish that I can give more stars to this place! Not only they have the special interior decoration, but also they have the best soup dumpling in town.  I'm definitely the one who has qualification to say this because I'm from China where the soup dumpling comes from! My favorite to The Bao is also their creativity on soup dumpling! I must to give the credit to their wasabi soup dumpling and chocolate soup dumpling ! Good try!
Maybe I am being too harsh on this place, however for the price you pay, it's overpriced. Even though the food was very good, the decor is outdated. Sorry.
Delicious hoagies for super cheap! Got lunch meat hoagies, everything was really fresh, especially the roll. A small was huge! Will def be coming back here again!

As a bunch of college kids, we were heading to Phebes and B bar on a weekend night but typical weekend fashion, the lines for both were massively long. We rounded the corner and found Scratcher. You might miss it the first time because it's below ground level but once you enter it's definitely a comfortable bar where you and your friends can just grab a nice drink and talk. There are wooden benches (not single chairs so be aware when you want to readjust) and tables. Some of the tables were a little loop sided but it wasn't that big of a deal since we just had our drinks on the table. The drinks additionally were very cheap, even on a weekend night so I can't imagine how much of a steal they would be during the day/ happy hours. A beer was about $7 and mixed drink around the same. The light was dim but not so much that you had to squint and the bartenders were very nice and attentive.

Nothing but good things to say. The ambience is awesome and the service is excellent. We had the pleasure of meeting the owner and chef at lunch. He is clearly devoted to his food and his restaurant and it shows. We had the pork belly sliders and the morning after sandwich. Both amazing. The sliders are the best take on pork belly I have had in a long long time. Melt in your mouth deliciousness. The sandwich? Equally amazing. For dessert the shortbread and chocolate with salted caramel. Seriously delicious. Highly recommend for drinks and food.

Pick your way across the menu, sampling bits here and there. Everything is packed with flavor. The Escalor crudo was oustanding, and the meal never let down from there. L'Artusi is small, has a lively environment, and doesn't lack for noise. Don't expect an intimate environment, but they won't let you down on the food.
Attentive and fast service and food was great.  Huaraches and jamaica juice was great!
One of the BEST Mexican Restaurants not just in Bloomfield but in my searches all around NJ! Great hospitality and they bring that out in the food... Excellent Job!!
I've never had a bad meal here. The food is always so fresh, the staff is always friendly and attentive.

Okay went to this place based on the yelp reviews.  5 Stars all the way food and service.  We brought our own red wine and they opened it a kept refilling our glasses with no corking or glass fees.  You know you are in for a Great dining experience when other patrons in the establishment hear it is your first time and make unsolicited recommendations that you follow and love.  Oh yea, once the staff realizes what dishes you like they make even better recommendations!  Thank God I live a half hour away, if I didn't I seriously would go every day of the week!!!  Get the soup!

I wish I could give this place 6 stars, I love it! Outdoor seating, plenty of parking, and the food is fantastic! I think they found a regular in me and my girlfriend. Oh btw, try their hash browns! Soooo good

I left this restaurant feeling cheated.  To tell you the truth, I left feeling hungry/full.   If you have ever been really hungry before, yet you eat sub-standard food you will know what I mean.  I came here with my family on a Sunday night to a relatively empty restaurant.  You would think that would mean good service/food, but not at all! The food that we ordered is NOT authentic indian food.  They try to spice it up, but they are all wrong!  They have no idea what spices they are using.  I'm not trying to be a snob or anything, but curry is a blend of a different spices.  What I tasted in the dish I ordered was not 'curry' but a heavy hand of just a single spice.  I ordered the Andhra Chicken Curry.  The Andra Chicken Curry was horrible.   Dry bland chicken with too much of a certain spice - cloves.   I'm Indian and I know how South Indian chicken curry should be prepared.  This place left me feeling angry and annoyed.  Don't go here! Avoid at all costs! Always remember sort by date on yelp, not yelp sort. Also mandatory 18 percent tip for a party of 4 for lackluster service.  Place sux!
get a flight of bud

This is, hands down, my favorite place to get bagels. Besides the regular butter or cream cheese option, their taylor ham/egg/cheese bagel sandwich is amazing. A new favorite is their 'salt sticks'- the twisted loaf looking thing on the right side of the counter, covered in sesame seeds, poppy seeds, and salt. Good enough to eat plain, and that's pretty amazing.

I got the eggnog soft serve which was amazing. They had a big variety of flavors to choose from. My mom ordered the cheesecake flavor & my sister had ordered the apple pie flavor. I tasted both and they are both so yummy as well. The only downside to the place was the cashier girl wasn't friendly.

I don't know what to say other than I hope the lunch is as fabulous as they say it is...dinner on the other hand was ridiculously expensive for average Korean fare. "Eundae" fish entre literally had 2 pieces of monk fish costing $36!!!!! Whoa.....

I was so pleasantly surprised by this place!  Our waiter, Jesus, was phenomenal and made it a great experience.  We got several entrees and appetizers, the highlight being the cod cheek tacos and the roasted suckling pig.  I will absolutely come back here.
Loved the chips and drink options as well. And the lady working behind the counter was Absolutely lovely and very nice and hospitable.

This is the worst breakfast that I have ever eaten in my life....   The Wait It took 10 minutes for the waitress to take our order and 50 minutes to receive my food.  My eating companion and I both ordered the same thing... 2 eggs (poached) any style.  Nothing too complicated. I wouldnt of been upset about the wait if the food was good.  The waitresses spent more time on take-out coffee orders then actually attending to the guests that were eating in the restaurant.   The Food When I received my food, it was the worst breakfast I ever ate.  I didnt know that you could mess up a basic egg breakfast but they did.  The poached eggs had a very strong taste of vinegar.  I couldnt even eat them.  The potatoes were very greasy and tasted like they were made the day before.  The waitress didnt even ask if there was anything wrong when she took away our plates that were barely eaten.  I wont be back.

I have never been to such a bad restaurant in all my life!!! I was very surprised at this place and after reading all these reviews i wonder who really is doing the cooking first of all the service was very bad very slow i found myself asking for things like bread, a steak knife, i never got ice for my water but i was offered tap water or sparkling the seats are metal and very uncomfortable i found it funny that a gentleman kept walking around asking how things were and when i said "well not good because " he kept walking not wanting to hear our complaints the food was very salty i still cant figure that out the meat balls were beyond salty, the steak and sausage that we ordered looked beautiful and that's all it looked good the chicken and potatoes was a 1/4 small chicken leg and thigh with to pieces of potato for the price we paid for 5 people i was very shocked, i believe the pics of the food must be from another one of there restaurants its very deceiving,  but than again i should have known that if you see a Greek restaurant  in Astoria with outside seating available on a Sunday at diner time its empty for a reason if you go to MP shame on you i warned you stay home drink your own tap water!!

A colleague, a member of our top brass and I decided to lunch at Antinori. We were seated by the owner who, after offering us a table, came back and reeled of a list of specials with panache, far too many for us to keep track of. All I remembered was something with clams and steaks. Anyway, after speaking about the choices amongst ourselves, when he came back to take our order and saw us dithering he suggested that we have a seafood starter with a bit of everything and steak and veal as our main course. Of course, the bread arrived and was good. What I particularly liked was the fact that unlike most restaurants they had butter knives, which to me epitomizes a great restaurant. Some miscellaneous accompaniments for drinks arrived and were good. They changed our forks and knives after we had had these starters. (I, particularly, hate it when servers put the used forks and knives down on the tablecloth). Then the main seafood starter arrived. There were two clams, each in a different sauce, a giant shrimp in it's own sauce and a calamari. I wish I had taken a photograph because the plate presentation was exquisite. Each item on the starter had been cooked perfectly and was excellent. I thought that I should have made it my main course too. Just as well I didn't. Then they changed our forks and knives again! The veal and a giant T-Bone arrived. The veal was good and might have been great on it's own. However, it paled in comparison to the T-Bone which was fantastic.The server put the T-Bone plate facing away from us and the owner came and corrected the positioning. He proceeded to serve us from the main plate. The steak was cooked to perfection and easily ranked amongst the best steaks I have eaten. Nobody had space for dessert but we decided to have some coffee. By this time the table cloth had lost it's initial pristine look despite the fact that the server had continued to pick up crumbs and debris created during our meal. Rather than letting us drink our coffee on the now grungy tablecloth, they brought a fresh one, rolled it up and then unrolled it onto the old tablecloth making the table look great again! Everything was done with great style and panache and the food was wonderful. Do I plan on going back? Definitely. In fact, I plan to take my family there for my son's birthday next month. Do I recommend this restaurant? Absolutely!

The afternoon lunch specials are cheap, but you get what you pay for. I have walked by this place many times and have never seen someone inside. Despite having good yelp reviews, My better judgement kept me out until today when I decided to try this place out. My chicken and fries combo was not good. The chicken was okay at best and served on soggy fries. Good thing I did not have to wait long. With wawa next door, I know where I'll go next time I'm looking for a quick lunch.

We went because our cousin loves Ramen and she wanted us to try it. We had to wait for a table, which seems to be normal, but we went for a drink locally and they phoned us when the table was ready, so we didn't have to wait around. The ambience is brilliant and so is the Ramen - and that's from someone who's not particularly crazy about brothy soups with noodles. Definitely recommend it.

Came as a group of 6 on a Tuesday evening. Portions ranged from small to just enough. Wine comes in tumblr glasses. Pre-meal bread looked like leftover pieces for crostini--- a bit dry, and some were already ripped apart (!?) --- and came with plain olive oil. Oxtail pappardelle was good, but nothing exciting. Found some bones in the sauce, and surprise pieces of gnocchi. Pasta was fresh, and had a good pasta to sauce ratio. My dining-mate's spicy sausage gnocchi and gorgonzola was very tasty! She thought it was too creamy though. Seemed understaffed, as it'd take awhile before we could get service. Romantic atmosphere.
simple amazing pizza. This is a first time I didn't have to wait to get in I am happy about it. food is great next to Brooklyn Bridge. We had a great time

I've been dragging people here for their first taste of Hungarian food forever, and everyone I've brought has wanted to come back. The owners are friendly, and the restaurant feels, like many other people have said, like you are in your grandmother's kitchen. The dining room consists of country-style kitchen tables and chairs. The walls are decorated with pictures of Budapest and various types of traditional embroidery. The food is delicious, and affordable. At this point I've probably tried everything on the menu. The food always comes out fast. The cucumber salad offers an interesting mix of sweet and garlic flavors to start the meal. The main courses are heavy, filling, and full of flavor. My favorites are the Chicken Paprikas with spaetzle, which my friends and family concur is the best in the area, and the Stuffed Cabbage.  The Hungarian goulash and beef goulash are also frequent selections. The rich, sweet paprika flavor never disappoints. A large bowl of sour cream is always on hand. For dessert, apricot crepes are always a good decision, though I'm usually far too stuffed from the meal to even think about dessert. The staff never hurries you out the door, so it is a great place for a relaxing evening with friends or family.

Living in NY, I have been craving a good cheese steak for a while ever since Carl's closed its locations in the city.  I've had both Pat's & Geno's in the past, but according to memory Pat's was better.  Went there this past Saturday around 3pm, and there was a line of about 60-75 people around the block waiting in line for cheese steaks (in pouring rain nonetheless).  The people behind the counter keep it moving like a well-oiled machine, and it was my turn to order after just a 5-6 minute wait, I got my usual with provologne-mushrooms-onions and it did not dissapoint.  Will definitely be back here next time I'm in town to fulfill my cheese steak quota.   Can't miss if you're in Philly!!! :)
Totto is closed today, so we came here for lunch. It takes about 25 min to wait. The noodle and soup is quite good and delicious, although maybe a little bit salty for me.
They must add crack to these empanadas Top fav Reggaeton/romeo & juliet/cuban.   Yuca with guac is really good too!

So many restaurants and doing the same thing, small plates, new American blah blah blah, local, sustainable, buzzword, buzzword, buzzword. It's like Brooklyn forgot that food can be something else then New Brooklyn Cuisine. Not at Glasserie. The food here is beyond delicious, has a very serious identity and attitude. Incredibly flavorful and interesting. Have been multiple times, and was not sure if the chef change earlier in the year would affect the restaurant. Was nervous about coming again but, the poetry and wonder of the food is STILL there and it's so good. I could go into specifics about each dish I had, but instead, you should go and eat it. Everything, anything. So good. I want to give it 5 stars because the food carries such serious weight, but instead, I'm at 4 because the service could use some more attention.
This place is amazing. They call their hot dog's rippers! It has a slice in he middle. These dogs are amazon. Great place to hangout! I would love to bring my friends here!

Due to traffic we were very late, the Maître 'D could not have been nicer. We were starving also so probably not your average fine dining clientele. The waiter was very helpful, the food sublime and we had a lovely evening.

I eat here everyday for lunch! I also use them to cater all my parties, the food is AMAZING!!!!!!!! The owners are the friendliest people and are so happy to please. Their chicken cutlets are life changing!

I think the food here is great!  I live too far away to frequent but always try to make it there. Just had the vongole clams in red sauce this weekend and it was amazing! The sunday sauce is delicious too!
