(That my friend is not steak and eggs!!!)  My brothers shrimp were frozen baby shrimp you find in the fried rice of a cheap Chinese restaurant. (Another $20+ dish). What an insult to a foodies intelligence. Didn't want to complain as we just wanted to leave. (Waiter nowhere to be found anyway!!). Now, finally the waiter blesses us with his presence with bill in hand. (Wtf hello can we please have more water?!!?). We ask for one more drink before we leave to hopefully drown our horrific experience of a brunch. He informs us that he cannot because they are now closed. CLOSED???? (Had you come around earlier and asked if we needed anything else, we wouldn't be having this conversation!!!)   And besides...It's only 4pm!!!  He tells us they close at 4 and reopen at 6. Newsflash... If you have customers in your restaurant who are willing to spend money, TAKE THE MONEY AND MAKE THE CUSTOMER HAPPY!!  Needless to say, this was the worst experience and restaurant I've ever been to. Considering this is L.I.C. and has tons of great places for brunch, this is one place to avoid at all cost!!!  Don't say I didn't warn you...
Amazing!  Sometimes the pizza is the best, sometimes the calzone is the best and sometimes they both are.  Awesome, quiet spot.  Just put your name down early and go get a drink nearby.
Food is great. Service not quite there yet...
i love the pizza here i think its just as good if not better that robertas! the outside seating is really nice you forget your in brooklyn and its right in my hood love it im a regular
Probably the tastiest barbecue I've ever had, plus the prices are great. All of the food was fantastic and the owner is a great guy. I went on my birthday and he gave my whole group desserts.
Nice place great service better food !  Couldn't get enough of the sweet bread they provided .

My friend and I came to eat here in sort of round-about fashion: I thought there was a Friendly's off the same exit, but we couldn't find it, and we didn't want to eat McDonald's etc. American Steak House (ASH) shares a parking lot with another diner, so we flipped a coin. Chance chose the other diner, but when we got close enough to see in the window, we decided that chance was wrong, and headed into ASH. We were greeted by and ordered from a very friendly counter attendant. We were walked to a table in the dinning room, after which we went back past the counter to the salad bar which occupied an entire room, with a surprisingly large amount of options, including chicken legs, 5 kinds of pasta salad, 4 kinds of pudding, and more. I ordered the steak and shrimp, which wasn't great but wasn't terrible, and my friend had the chicken parmesan. The meal filled me up, but in that way where you're still a bit hungry. At no point were we presented with anything of desirable quality, and both meals did quite a number on our insides for the remainder of the ride, with my bubbleguts lasting well into the night. I wish I could remember our server's name, she had long, dark hair and was absolutely lovely. She brought us to our table, brought our food, made us comfortable, checked on us periodically, and answered our many questions about the inner workings of the establishment. We had to ask about tipping, because we had already paid before being seated, but hadn't left a tip yet because our dining experience had only just begun. Our server informed us that most people either leave cash on the table after their meal, or return to the front counter to leave a tip with a card. If you want to leave a $5 tip via credit card, you are actually purchasing your server a $5 gift card to the restaurant they work at, which seems like a terrible, shameful, and questionably legal business practice. Can you imagine having a family, and instead of being able to provide for them, forcing them to come to your place of work to eat food that makes them feel like they'll have diarrhea? I'd recommend tipping in cash. Overall I can't say I'd return to ASH unless I really wanted to punish my insides again, or it happened that every other restaurant on 95 disappeared. But 3 stars for the service and the story to tell the kids..

This review is for a private event! We just celebrated our son's bar mitzvah and we could not be more pleased with the outcome.  We loved working with Melissa from start to finish.  The food and atmosphere were also great!  Thank you!

The tacos are good.. but as a vegetarian, I found the potato mixture to be bland.  It tasted like boiled potatoes with no flavor.  I wouldn't go out of my way to come here, but if you are in the neighborhood, you can check it out.

Located in the historic Vermont House, The Gryphon surpasses expectations.  We've eaten here several times already in the short time they've been open.  Haven't had a bad meal yet.  The Vineyard Chowder is the best soup in Town, hands down.  The Bison Hangar is very high quality, though the side cabbage could be a bit bolder in flavor.  The burgers are great and cooked exactly as ordered.  The salmon dish was worth going back for.  The beer selection is good, and the drink specials are imaginative and prepared with great care.  The desserts are special, save room!  The owners are on premises and take great care to see to a satisfying experience.  The lunch menu is very attractive in content as well as pricing.  Just a short one block walk on Main from the foot of Church Street, this is a restaurant and bar that is worthy of regular visits.
The Pizza is great but this place it's a litte bit overrated, specially the prices are a little high for the quality of the food, and waiting for a table can last hours.

Went here with my family a few years ago for lunch on one of our trips to NYC and loved the food here! The Grilled Chicken Skewers were amazing and the Dark Chocolate "Bag" is an immediate staple to have for dessert on the menu.

My boyfriend and I got a small feast to share. It was yummy but some of the meat was dry. They have a nice selection of BBQ sauce to use at the table. A little pricey but overall not bad food and the host and waitress were very polite. The decor is fun to look at and they have funny and old vintage signs
Second time this year!! We love it here! This time got the mushroom smothered chicken biscuit! We live in Florida and make sure to stop by while in NYC. Great prices, food, and coffee!

We were invited for this restaurant by friends who described themselves as very picky and were really excited going to this restaurant. When we entered to the main sitting area this place was packed and very noisy almost like entering a bar. The food and the wine were very good but miniature quantities. I understand that you want to be exclusive but to give a soup size less than a cup? This all could be fine except for the high price for the food and we stayed hungry. Even this I could forgive but not that night that followed both my husband and me had a problem all night and had to run to the bathroom so I do not get more descriptive. I know that everyone is saying that this is a great restaurant but unfortunately this has been our experience. I am wondering if anyone else had the same.

Not like the original. I mean not only did you get my order wrong. You told me I had to tell you to chop the meat! To think I drove from DC here for the dole purpose of showing my wife a great cheesesteak and left with a poor facsimile of an original great. I'll go to Jim's next time or back to the original.

If you were walking by 46 eldridge st. You would do just that walk by. This hole in the wall walk up joint has a limited menu and a hectic pace. I was showing two friends around New York and I had found this place and marked it on google. For $7 we were all three full and we agreed it may have been one of the best tasting meals we had. We had the fried Pork and Green onion dumplings and we shared a slice of the fryed sesame bread. If I lived in New York I would take the subway here at least once a week.
Very good place especially on Sunday's with the NFL ticket! Food is good and service is surprisingly good! Would come back and recommend this place for family and friends!

The farm stand salad was filling and amazing. The vegan scrapple was delicious. The coffee was great too. The staff are super friendly. And I love the decor and atmosphere. I like this place. I am looking forward to returning and trying out more items on the menu. The food did take while to arrive. But they just opened. I'll let it slide. The staff was hustling. It was just pretty crowded when I was there.
Homemade Roti Canai is amazing!!  Thin, light, crispy pancake with curry with chicken and potato.  Prawn Mee Soup was a little too rich and shrimpy for me, but it was great none the less.

This place cannot even get one star from me. There's false advertisement. The man behind the counter? His attitude was horrendous! Customer service skills were at an ALL TIME LOW! He was so darn RUDE. I REFUSE to come here EVER AGAIN. YOU GUYS GET 2 THUMBS DOWN FROM ME!  NEVER AGAIN!!!!

Excellent excellent excellent. The short ribs are not to be missed. We had the deviled eggs-- pretty good; the arugula salad-- stellar; the short ribs (mind blowing) and pumpkin cheesecake. So good. Highly recommend
Great experience.. Dan Dan Noodles and Dry Lamb Pot were the best at a 5 for spicy. Food was good, a little too spicy (peppers extra hot), plenty to eat and price was awesome for five people
Used to be great food and service has been going down hill past 3_4 months food not as tasteful and food takes forever to get

After taking my order, they realized I was out of their delivery area.  Instead of calling me back, they delivered my dinner (the owner nonetheless) and then called to let me know next time I'll have to pick up.  Now THAT'S customer service.  And the food is amazing.   Love these guys!!
Waffle bowl the is perfect hangover remedy. Go early and sit at the counter, people watch and wake up slowly before the crowds come.
All i can say is THIS IS THE BEST DINER EVER!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! I highly recommend this place to everybody!!!!!!!!!!
Excellent Restaurant. Food was great! wait staff were fantastic. Definitely recommend this to friends and family.

The Ramen is delicious!! I went there few night ago with my girlfriend, she ate there few times already and said its a must to try. Although we waited at the bar for about an hour - it was worth it! Real authentic Japanese cuisine, the soup is amazing!! p.s for the appetizer don't forget to try the chicken buns - so yummy!!!!

Ordered three plates last night, a chicken wrap, penne ala vodka, and chicken francese. My two roommates and I all got food poisoning. This will be the last time we offer from here. This restaurant needs to be more responsible when handling food.

A local gem Lovely atmosphere - excellent hosts and waitstaff - interesting cocktails and outstanding food. Interesting and well executed cuisine as explained by the host as a more British colonial influenced indian style - plates are presented as complete entrees rather than the more traditional pass around family style. Each entree included rice, naan and sauce - complete and satisfying - each interesting and delicious. I can't wait to go back. Highly recommended.

Right when you walk into this "hole in the wall" restaurant you'll realize the atmosphere is immediately unique. It's in a weird spot but DO NOT JUDGE A BOOK BY ITS COVER. Spontaneously, my boyfriend and I were both craving Italian and it was our date night. Yelp reviewers ranted about its delicious entrees. Boy were they right. The moment you open the door countless awards cover the wall between the entrance and hostess area. I had never even heard of this restaurant and honestly, it's quite pricey. From the moment we got there- right up to leaving, the whole experience was romantic, delicious, and the servers knew what they were talking about. Even the bread with olive oil and seasonings was flavorful. Everything was excellent. I ordered the Gnocchi Genovese I believe it was and my boyfriend ordered the Free Range Organic Chicken, both were fabulous.  My dish was cooked to perfection! I didn't even need a knife to cut the meat, it was tender, like butter! With the fresh/ organic ingredients they use, it's worth EVERY penny. We will definitely be returning. If you have any doubts, just go, you won't regret it!

Its hard to miss this place at the corner with lots of people gathered around. I went here on a Wednesday night around 7pm by myself and there was barely any wait. Even for 2 people you would get seated quickly. The menu is very simple: there are four types of pizzas you can order (no slices just pies) of two different sizes. Then you choose additional toppings. I chose a small mozzarella pizza with basil, pepperoni, and sun dried tomatoes. I should've chosen a basil pizza instead. The price here is not worth it and the pizza was moderately okay. I think I would prefer dollar slices over this. Its only known for being a brick oven pizza place. The staff here do not seem friendly but the location is conveniently close to the Brooklyn Heights Promenade park.

I was in the neighborhood on a somewhat busy Friday night with some peeps.  They wisely got Taqueria Diana, but I had that for lunch and wanted something else, so I gave these guys a shot.   After waiting on line for 10 minutes to get to the counter, I paid for my regular fries with especial sauce, after which time they told me there would be another 10 minute wait.  I'm not a big fan of standing on lines, so if they told me there would be a 10 minute wait I'd have just went elsewhere before I even paid.  But the reason for the delay? Someone ordered two trays of fries, and they were going to make the entire two whole batches first.  Again, I'd normally have left already, but my friends were waiting down the block for their food, and I wanted something (different), too. Now I don't know: a) what kind of person thinks two trays of rapidly cooling fries is good for a party, as opposed to some sensible hors d'oeuvre, like cheese and crackers? Or some damn pizzas. b) what kind of establishment will satisfy this one pissant at the expense of 20-30 customers? What's the appeal of this place? That it has a line and must be good? The fries are OK, sure, I've snagged a few from a co-worker before, but over 20 minutes wait for a $5 bag of fries? I gave them their extra 10 minutes, and they were still filling that jerk-off's party order.  I asked for my money back, and they made a pretty weak insult about not taking me seriously on account of my height.  I know they're busy and I'm not sensitive about my height, but his comeback to my very profane words about their awful service was lame. So yeah; these assholes have OK, overpriced fries and shitty/rude service . And they're in a neighborhood lousy with drunk hipsters with too much money, so it doesn't matter what Yelp says, anyway.  You'll find me at Mamoun's, Two Bros., Taqueria Diana, Halal Guys, or *anywhere* else in this neighborhood.

Went here last night with my family due to the positive reviews. I have to agree with everything said before. The staff was attentive and got everything right. The menu is relatively small, but this seems to allow for better dishes all around. We had half the menu items, including the ribs in chocolate sauce (sounds odd, but was delicious), the truffle calamari (didn't taste too much truffle, but I was ok with that and the calamari was cooked well), the charred edamame, and the chicken lollipops for appetizers; the rolling chicken, duck confit, udon with shrimp, chicken fried rice, and pad thai for entrees. Everything was cooked well, and what surprised us most was the flavor combinations, especially in the sauces and sides. We kept going back for more, just to see what the hell the flavor was (whatever it was, it worked really well with the dish). My favorite was the jasmine panna cotta for dessert. Everyone from my parents to my 5-year-old niece enjoyed the food. We will definitely be back.
really good classic brunch

A bit hesitant given the location but the restaurant itself has a nice family vibe. Big portions but the overall quality of the food was just ok. It wasn't bad and I will definitely return again and try other dishes but there was just something missing. It's always busy on the weekends so they must be doing something right.

Delicious in every way. The free wings are spicy and saucy Szechuan. The burger with their aioli is delicious. The fried chicken and cornbread waffle is a must- goes perfectly. The PB&J panna cotta was delicious and I hate PB&J- service was great and price is right.

Been there many times.  But never again, out of anger. My advice: never, never take a group of more than four to Becco before the theater. My wife invited a large family group of our children and grandkids to dinner and the theater in honor of my 70th birthday.  She called Becco a month ahead of time.  Reserved a table for 10.  Specified 6:00.  Specifically asked for the upstairs or the back room.  Specifically asked Becco to note that we had to make a theater curtain: 10 tickets to Matilda to make.  (For us, at least, not a small expense.) Becco called my wife several times during the month to reconfirm.  Each time, she was asked to confirm that we had theater tickets. Finally, the evening arrived.  Our whole party was at reception desk by 5:50.  Told it would be just a few minutes.  Got told it would be just a few minutes 6 more times.  Finally got seated at 6:35.  That is got seated at a crowded table.  In the bar.  With one of our party's back up against a narrow crowded corridor of people standing between the bar stools and his back. No waiter, no menus until one of us went up to one of the managers to complain.  Nearly 7:00. The end result: no time for appetizers, no time for desserts, no time for a comfortable family dinner to start the evening. What should Becco have done?  It's pretty simple.  You have a sell-out restaurant.  You have no problems with the number of "turns" you have to make per night.  Don't overbook.  If you can't handle a party, tell your customers instead of taking a reservation. Don't protect your profitability at your customers'  expense.
hate the fact that this place is extremely tiny. the tacos are good, but the breakroom fries are better.

Good wine and a nice atmosphere but the food is very overpriced: tiny portions and more than half of each dish consists of bland, unsalted bread. I feel like this is one of those places people fall over themselves praising and convincing themselves they love because it's a nice space in a cute location and you might find yourself seated next to Julianne Moore or someone like that but if you break the food down, you're really getting almost nothing and it's either not that tasty (the steak tartare had no seasoning at all) or something you could make at home in less than a minute for about 35 cents (the $10 anchovy tartine). Our dessert (the chocolate mousse) was the only tasty thing we had, out of eight dishes (and, funnily enough, the only one with any salt). In any case, I'm not trying to scare anyone away. It's a cute spot and nothing was terrible. But I'd recommend it for drinks and one plate at the most and not for dinner.

What can I say about the best place ever? We shared the double bacon burger, the bacon hot dog, the grilled cheese, and burger with fried shallots. We also feasted on cheesy french fries with hot red peppers. Frogs Leap wine and Yard beer was perfect seeing that we were visiting from the Napa area. The crowning glory was the pumpkin custard. Cheers to Patricia and Derrick the manager for making our first experience at Shake Shack a delicious and fun evening.

Craving some real good beef brisket for the last few days, i yelped this place out since i was in nearby Dumbo. Having had spectacular brisket from a food truck a few weeks before, my bar was set high.Out of several in-a-row mediocre eating experiences, i was really hoping this Red Hook hipster eatery would get my thumbs up, unfortunately i was again disappointed. The few quick reviews i read (very positive) didn't prepare me for the huge Saturday evening line out the door to the order window (about a 45 minute wait) , or the lack of table service. It took us about 5 minutes to get oriented, and figure out how this weird place worked (just get on line like cattle to slaughter). While waiting on line, one nervously looks around the establishment trying to eyeball a seat, there were four of us, and the long beer festival hall tables didn't make the task easy. Once at the order "window" the "butcher" asks you what you want, and cuts off pieces of it, and weighs it right on the spot. The meat prices average $25-$30 a pound. Some things were cheaper, like the sausage, which they ran out of . The beef ribs are $25 a pound, bone and all (are you f*cking kidding me?!?) were too rich for my blood to even try. Though I suspect if its like everything else I tried, good thing I didn't waste my money. So we ordered we ordered the beef brisket, dark Chipotle chicken, lamb & pork belly, and a side of Mac n Cheese ($8 for large). Out of all those things, the cheesy mac was the best tasting, garnering a 7/10 on my subjective taste scale. The Brisket was just ok, at a 6/10. Not even close to the cheaper and much better brisket I had from the food truck. I hate myself for not remembering what it was called. The lamb belly was very dry, and had no taste (though it had a spicy rub) 3/10 The pork belly was dry and tasteless too 2/10 The chipotle chicken was spicy and decent tasting, but super dry 3/10 My friends pulled pork had no taste, and a weird mushy consistency 2/10 Their potato salad (is that what it was??) had a weird tangy-mixed with coleslaw type formula. I kinda liked it, but it was weird nonetheless 4/10 Other notes... The cashier didnt say thank you when I was done ordering and gave this kidults their due tip. The banjo playing band from Flyoverlandia, sucked. Parking took a little time to find (Saturday night, and lots of other establishments in the area). On the plus side, the beer was good. All in all I spent close to a C note and was very disappointed. Though I've never had Dallas BBQ's brisket, their Beef ribs are AWESOME, and you get a huge rack (like 3-4 pounds) for 15 bucks, with a bunch of sides. How these hometown a-holes can charge $25 a pound (thats like 1-2 ribs) for beef, is beyond me. Tommy says skip it.

I went here tonight with my family because I've heard it was so great from multiple people, and I'm sad to to say I was very disappointed! The food portions were actually surprisingly small, and the food itself was OK at best.  The food took forever, and my waitress didn't seem to care one way or another.  Overall I will not be coming back. 1-10 I give it a 3.

Cozy little placed with a  (hopefully on purpose) distressed look throughout. It actually kind of gives the place a dirty vibe. The floor is unfinished and even had a few cracks, the table had chips of paint missing. You can't really tell if it's on purpose or they just didn't have the budget to make the place look nice. We shared the Chips & Guacamole, pork tacos, and salsa verde chicken enchiladas. The Chip and guac was good and there was plenty of guac. Chicken enchiladas were very good and more flavorful than typical. The pork tacos weren't very good, and in fact lacked flavor. There just wasn't much too them at all. Service was decent, not great but not terrible. They seemed as if they're not used to being as busy as they were as the place was full and there were even people waiting outside. Plenty of waiters but not really fully attentive. Guess that's what receiving a Michelin star does for business. The star was part of the reason we decided to go, and to be honest we prefer the Mexican food at Skinny's just a few blocks away. The spicy margarita was good and very different.

Being from Maryland, I don't just get to go to White Castle when I want. Friends and I were in Edison one night and just knew we would have to make a pit stop here for late night eats. The roads confused us, but the adventure was worth the while. Yum! Sliders! Yum! Fried starches! Happy bellies for all of us. :)

A must try when in NYC.  We went for the lunch tasting and it was so good!  I would fly to New York just to go to this restaurant again. The lunch tasting came with 5 courses, all very delicious.  The added bread cart with its fancy breads (e.g. pistachio saffron) was a nice touch. The restaurant was beautiful.  Walking in you are greeted with a wall of fresh apples from floor to ceiling, a nice sweet smell. Trust me and try it.
What a selection of whiskey! Very cool place! Very knowledgable staff, let them pick!

I've been coming here for years now and sad to say my  most recent experience was horrific. My mother and I made 7:45 reservations for a Sunday night. We started with the octopus special, unfortunately it was extremely salty. My mom had a pasta seafood dish and I had the scallops, both dishes were extremely salty. I don't know if it was a different chef that night or what but i was very disappointed in the food and the service. During our dessert the bus boys started cleaning up all the tables, includings ours! We were in the middle of eating when he took away our water. When he asked him to leave the water, he gave us a nasty attitude and threw some other water glasses on the table. We ignored him and continued to eat dessert and have a funny conversation. I guess he thought we were laughing at him because he approached us aggressively and yelled "What is so funny, i like to laugh to". I was in such a state of shock and said "it was a private conversation". He then proceeded to ask us what our nationality was, if we were Hispanic. I asked him what did it matter to him and tried to ignore him. He asked us several more times what was so funny. The manager was not in that night or else I would have asked to speak to him. Needless to say we finished our dessert and left immediately. I will def not be returning and no longer recommend it to anyone. Terrible dining experience, waste of money, the food was horrible and the service was terrible.
this place is cute good drinks and great fries also the avocado toast is my fav great place to stop if your walking along the highline
Love this place!  Bartenders so cute and soooo funny!!! Great music.....and way better than that bitch on Jay Street!!

I've eaten here recently.   It was really good.  Had the crab sandwich and shrimp steam pot.  Was really full and satiated.   Friendly staff.  And a laid back atmosphere.   A breath of fresh air from the pretentious restaurants that are popping up all over my native Harlem

If you want to eat at Halal Guys - you better like spicy.  A little bit of hot sauce goes a LONG way here.  And they really don't know what "just a little" means.  The lines are super long - and the quality of food has really gone down in recent years.  There are better ways to spend $6.
love this place, love Halal food... I recommend this place very much!!!!!!
Food tastes great, line can be long but moves really quickly, had the mix over rice and lots of the white sauce, only paid $6.

The food here was superb!   The fresh bread is warm and fresh, so delicious.  We started with the mussels.   The portion was enough to share with two people.  It was made with tomatoes and crumbled sausage, I wanted to keep dunking my bread.  I had the veal with mushrooms and artichokes , it was to die for served with mashed potatoes and finely shredded vegetables.  My date had chicken dish with peppers and it was perfectly spiced for him.  We arrived late, however they treated us with the best service ever.  Even the gentleman who worked as car valet was so very nice.  We skipped dessert because we felt bad we arrived so late.  We are definately  going back.  I feel the atmosphere was romantic and very peaceful.  Cannot wait to try the other dishes.  Bravo to the owners, the wait staff and the kitchen!  You must try this place!

My husband and I both love le Virtu, so we were eagerly anticipating the opening of Brigantessa. The first floor smells delicious because of the pizza oven. We sat upstairs and I was surprised about how big it was. The space was beautiful with natural light, wood floors, and Italian photos on the wall. Our waiter seemed nervous and kept apolozing for everything, which was completely unnecessary since he was really attentive and nice. We ordered the artichokes and octopus appetizers, both of which were really good. I could have used another artichoke in the portion, but I'm greedy. When we first ordered, I was a little disappointed that the Clam Pizza wasn't on the menu, since I read good things online and had a similar pizza when I lived in Italy, but was told that they were having a problem with the clams in the oven. So, I ordered the Pizza Zucca, which had squash and cipollini onions on it. I don't eat dairy and was worried getting it without cheese would be a problem, but our waiter checked with the chef and it was fine.  Despite my earlier disappointment over the lack of clam pizza, I was really happy I got it and loved it. I would order it again. My husband got the Pizza cannolo- with smoked mozzarella, pork sausage, and porcini mushrooms. It was so pretty and had such a fun shape. Since we were in a carb coma, we didn't get dessert, but a lot of the things sounded amazing. One of the the best, if not the best, pizza I've had since italy. We definitely will be back.

My boyfriend and I came in for the first time last Friday. It was very busy and the service was great. We sat at the bar with Caroline who was extremely helpful and knowledgable when we asked about cocktails. I had the coquito passion and my boyfriend had the smoky room. They both were out of this world! Caroline is a true mixologist, and very friendly. My bf and I shared the salmon brûlée and the brazilian seafood stew. Best Latin food I've had since Brazil. We were impressed with the food, drinks, service and atmosphere and will definitely be back.

I wanted to love this place but just didn't. I liked the location, view was nice and the restaurant itself was nice.  There were 4 of us and we were excitied for the experience.  And then it started to fall apart.  The bartender was pretentious and almost mean in her delivery.  Same for the waiter who was frustrated to have to deal with a vegan patron.  The food portions were small which would be ok with if they were filling but mine was not. I got the scallops- they were delicious, but there were only 4.  The bottom line was that everything was just good and nothing blew us away like we were hoping.  Then the bill came:   Drinks at the bar, wine & drinks at the table, 2 apps 4 entrees 2 coffees & 2 desserts came out to be $500.  Granted, most of our money was spent in alcohol but we walked away feeling it was so not worth it.

Came here with my boyfriend on a Friday night not realizing they don't actually have a lot of seating compared to how big the place is. The hostess was super sweet and let us sit down even though we didn't have reservations and they were going to be packed in an hour. We ordered the Mac n cheese, salmon, watermelon/goat cheese salad, and lemon Parmesan cauliflower. Everything on the menu sounded fun and vibrant, but we were very disappointed. Everything was bland. Except the salmon, it tasted like they seasoned it. The ratio of watermelon and goat cheese compared to arugula in the salad was completely off. Couldn't taste lemon or Parmesan on the cauliflower. The Mac n cheese was decent. Had to call the waiter over for bread. For the price, I wouldn't go back. But it was nice for a date night :)
i love this place! first time i had brunch there this past weekend. just as good as dinner fish tacos are so good!!! sangria also thumbs up

The food here is not NYC quality but, it is very good for our area. My complaint is the manager.  Over the past year this woman has been nothing but rude, rude and incredibly rude. I usually get my food to go so that I don't have to deal with her. If I want a pleasant dining experience, I go with a Chinese speaking friend. They need to find someone, ANYONE, who can greet customers with a smile and be pleasant and welcoming. Food quality and service has improved over the past year and overall the food is a delight. The manager totally leaves a bad taste at the end of the meal when I walk out the door though.
yum always great to eat a philly cheesesteak here!  a famous place & even if there is a line they are on the ball & wait on everyone quickly.
Awesome atmosphere! So chic and fun and the drinks are AMAZING. Try the Twizzle.

Talk about incredibly large portions.. The food was definitely filling, but I honestly was hoping for quite a lot more in terms of taste. The "famous" chicken was notably dry, and there really wasn't much substance to their fries. The only thing they had on point was their pasta. The food definitely isn't bad, but at the same time doesn't live up to the hype.
Very good but too much overprice. There many other sushi around that are just as good or bettr but they don't cost so much.

I've eaten at bareburger before in NYC and I like them a lot. The food was as good as usual but we had subpar service at the Philadelphia location. It wasn't crowded but it took them a long time to get to us even though there were a lot of employees passing us and we put our menus aside. One guy also tried to clear our fries when we still had half of them left and were actively eating them.
I just had the BEST French onion I've ever experienced in a restaurant!!! The Buffalo chicken sandwich was great too and the service was very charming!!! I will be back at Pauline's Cafe!!!!

This place is absolutely wonderful. Great food, great prices, and, most importantly, fantastic coffee. Service is fast and polite. And the food is great. If you want a good, fast meal at a good price, this is the place to get it.
The pizza was delicious and so tasty. For a thin crust pizza, it's honestly great. It's a must try if you haven't been here.

Went here on Saturday night with a few friends that live in the area.  Food was GREAT!! 1.  Chicken wings, healthy and crispy, baked in the oven with rosemary, you could eat a lot of them and not feel like your cheating on your diet!! 2.  Prosciutto  and Mozz.....enough said, I'm a sucker for prosciutto! 3. PIZZA PIZZA PIZZA!  We got a sampling with extras to spare to take home, ---white   pizza with truffle and mushroom THIS is a must, AMAZING!  ----margarita (I like the sauce) -----pesto with fresh tomatoes.  Pizza was crispy and a good ratio of sauce/cheese.  You can ask for well done for extra crispy too!! Lots of drink choices, I had a cucumber martini, very good.  And good wine list! Everyone was very nice and welcoming when I first arrived.  Being from New York and loving Grimaldis pizza I was excited to try the new restaurant.  I was surprised at how big the restaurant was, and liked that there was a separate bar area, will be good if you needed to bring kids and didn't want to be near others drinking!   In the main dining room I loved the mural of New York, it really made me reminisce about the area and where the original Grimaldis is! I will certainly be back!!!

I have wanted to try Grimaldis for a while and we will be coming back. We dined for lunch today. The pizza was crispy, the toppings were fresh, the service was good, I really liked it! The cocktail menu looks great. I will be back. Is there a happy hour or late night menu?

Tried it out of curiosity and I was hooked. The Loffa changed my life with the amount of food you could fit into it and not feel like you just eat all of it. The decor is a cool place to sit, relax, and enjoy.
I'm not normally one for seafood but their Captain's Cakes are amazing!! It's been a while since I've been but will be in very soon for some more great food and drinks!!

Dis is where I want to go if I feel like hitting up a house party where I know no one. Its small, crowded, and packed with an eclectic group of downtown intelligentsia. Every time I go, I feel like I've been transported to Paris in the 20's. It feels old school, but in an exciting way. I always seem to get caught up in conversation with someone I've never met before. Besides the excellent mingling environment, the cocktails are DELICIOUS. Pass on your usual G+T and get weird with whatever they put on the menu that week. The great spot for after dinner cocktails or post-movie snacks (Reuben Croquettes? Yes please!). If you're going to eat, call ahead and get a table. I like to get to this place around 9:30 or 10. Any time after, you'll likely be turned away at the door because its reached capacity. Also, you'll be required to respect the dress code. No flip flops. Go beyond casual. Show them you care, because they certainly do. Hands UP!

The sandwich was good but nothing to rave about. I was not a fan of the bread. Too tough for me but I could tell it was fresh. When it's hard to bite through you just make a mess. And what sandwich place in Philly doesn't have a cheesesteak on the menu?

Delicious! I'd recommend the Barbecue De Maiale. We ordered the Vongole and Funghi as well. I'm told the Fughi was the best, but I'm not a mushroom person so I did not try. Service was excellent. Our waitress was assertive and the restaurant was accommodating to our party of 4 considering we decided to dine late.

Miya's is a dream, I grew up in Florida on the Gulf of Mexico where fresh local fish was a daily part of life. I went to college in New England where seafood could more easily be categorized a religion than a protein. Miya's-though admittedly boldly experimental- features a menu featuring all sustainable local fish, fresh farmed cheeses and vegetables that come together in a way that's unique and delightful. Go in with an open mind and let the staff take you through a meal that doubles as a history lesson on sushi and sustainable food practices. Yes the menu is long, no you won't be out fast. If you're looking for a spicy tuna roll and miso soup go somewhere else...though their miso is infused with pumpkin and incredible. This is a place where any seasoned foodie will be happy guaranteed.
AMAZING FOOD!!! and you can't beat the unlimited mixed drinks for 1 1/2 options a must go and eat staff was very nice and above all the drinks were NOT watered down!
sheep's milk ricotta & Uovo pizza & garlic pork loin & salted caramel budino for two!!! Can't be more satisfied and full!!!

I couldn't figure out if the salmon was supposed to be chewy. I had to google it to see it was overlooked. I ate it anyway, chew, chew , chew. I got salmon teriyaki. The salad and soup were good though.

This place is the closest thing you can possibly get to a speakeasy. Such an awesome ambiance and atmosphere. The waiters/waitresses are fully dressed and in character as if in the 1930's. They have a fantastic bar which is pretty expensive but worth it. I haven't tried the food but i heard good things. Live instrumental bands that play jazz.

WORST service I have ever encountered.... I'm new here from Miami looking for a yummy Chinese spot I order out 3-4x a week...I have ordered a few times. First time they delivered and refused to bring it up to my door. Mind you I have a 90 y/o grandmother I take care of... When I told then to please bring it up the guy rudely huffed and complained. Next time I ordered for pick up. Fast service... Now today I call for delivery again and the guy says "I have to come down to get the food". I tell him my situation again then he hangs up on me. I called back several times and finally got him on the phone and told him I would come downstairs and he rudely said "NO, NO delivery for you now" when I asked if he was the owner or manager he said he was neither of those but he didn't care no delivery and hung up on me again. I called back again and told him I would pick it up and he said if I'm only ordering one thing then don't bother to order..... I was in shock at how rude they could be. I will never give this business my money again they are rude and nasty ill mannered people... They should change workers might get more business. Disgusting person answering the phone he should be FIRED!!!!!!!!!!

I did my birthday dinner here. They had so many great options for private parties and our waiter was awesome. I come here all the time and just snag a seat at the bar. My ultimate favorite thing in the world is the Truffle oil Mac and cheese. You won't regret it!!!

I was really excited to try this new place as it is right around the corner from where I live. I have also spent a great deal of time living in Sydney and was hoping for a great cappuccino or flat white. No matter how good the coffee may be, or how pretty the granola and yogurt is arranged, or how beautifully smashed that avocado is on the 7-grain-whole-wheat-rye-raw toast, right off I rolled my eyes to see that they don't serve skim milk. But they DO serve almond and soy. Why? It's certainly not "Australian" to do that...every cafe in Sydney serves skim milk. Its snobby. It is also ignorant because no one drinks full fat MILK anymore...its 2014 guys....fat, skinny, healthy, or not, NO adult in modern day America drinks whole milk. CHILDREN drink whole milk. So if you open up a cafe (in Nolita of all places), just make your clients happy and offer skim milk. All the skinny pretty girls you're serving? They want skim too! (Oh and guess what...its even cheaper than the soy and almond you're either buying or hand-making)

We went for the pig's head.  Turns out, they only make 1 per day, and someone had ordered it before we got there.  Would have been nice if they mentioned that on their website, or on the menu. We decided to stick around anyway and got several items. Broccoli rabe - it tasted like floor cleaner.  Far too astringent.  The parmesan cream on the bottom was tasty, however. Lamb pate - Mint jelly sauce was a nice touch but it was overly salty.  Not the worst thing I had but it was mediocre for what it was. Bone marrow - easily the best thing we had.  Sadly there wasn't a lot of it.  But it was very very tasty.   Lamb shoulder for two - this, however, was the worst thing we had.  I was very excited for it as everything had been kind of meh to that point.  It was completely overcooked - I like my lamb rare to medium rare and this thing was well-done, tough and quite dry.  They also didn't deliver our dish with the sauce it so desperately needed, and we had to wait a good 10 minutes before it came after we requested it, so by the time we tucked back into the lamb with the sauce it was cold and even dryer.  I was very disappointed as this was the most expensive thing we ordered and it was awful. The other thing that my date did not mention to me until after we had left is that in the yard area, there is a small garden growing behind the tables, and there were mice constantly running back and forth across it as we ate.  That's seriously disgusting, as the mice obviously can easily get into the restaurant from there and into the kitchen.  For what we ended up paying (over $140) the meal was absolutely not worth it and the ambiance sucked.  I almost fell off the bench I was sitting on several times because they are wobbly and parked on top of uneven cobblestones.  I will definitely not be returning, even for the pig's head.

I love this place. Their portions are beyond huge and they're delicious. I had a huge seafood pasta and it was like an entire pot worth of pasta and all kinds of yummy delicious seafood. The customer service is good. Everyone is super friendly. My family and I typically go here for birthdays etc. and they offer coupons which is always a plus.
Loved the spinach and artichoke dip its a must try ! We also had the toasted almond cake for desert ! Also delish !
I can wait to visit awesome pls two weeks from now!
Service was great but the paella was very soggy, the sausage was really hard and the taste wasn't the same.
Best breakfast we've had in New York. Tasted just as spectacular as it looked! Would return to New York just for this Breakfast!

I die and go to brunch heaven every Sunday I have been there! Food is amazing. Presentation is spot on! They may make slight variations to the brunch menu and it never disappoints. And please, order a mimosa!

Simple perfecto !, made with love, great service.... Had brunch, came back later to eat again. Always a nice crowd, people laughing, having a great time. Sit at the bar if Chris is bartending, Teresa is also a great server... Just good people with great hearts, an eye for detail, and amazing charisma. All around an excellent experience. Try the Dutch baby pancakes.... The burger... And work through the drink menu... All of it Very good place for group parties,Hands UP!
great burger.. simply the best in the west village
I love the creative and delicious flavor combinations of all the dishes here.  The wait staff is super friendly and attentive.

AMAZING FOOD!!! I am in the area frequently and always dining-in however tonight I took a whirl at delivery- I highly suggest Friedman's! I got the turkey burger which is handmade (packed with spices and flavor), Rosemary fries- delish, and the brussels which were to die for! If you're in the neighborhood stop by- it's a must!!!!

Food and Drinks are amazing! However the seating and bar set up are terrible. The place has no space and is always crowded. The bar takes up too much room even though it only has 10 or so seats. This place would be a 5 star if it had more room. However the one cook named pauly is a ****

This place sucked tonight. Calamari was bad (dry), the waitress was forgetful.  My favorite part is when she came out of the kitchen with a mouthful of food.  Sausage was uneatable. Glasses were dirty.  I'm telling you it really sucked tonight.  Oh, and it wasn't busy.  Will update next visit.

This is my first ever review.  I was compelled to write because of the exceptional attitude of the service we receive.  Doing a good job is not hard, but how you deal with a situation when something goes wrong really shows who you are.  There were two of us, ordering sandwiches #22 & #23, one with a roll and one with a wrap.  When they arrived, I must have made a little noise due to my disappointment that the wrong bread went on my sandwich.  I'm not one to complain, and would have eaten it as is, but our waitress said, "What's wrong, tell me."  She whisked our sandwiches away immediately to correct the situation.  She brought our sandwiches back with a smile, and let me tell you, not only was the service exceptional, those sandwiches and fries were DELICIOUS!
My wife and I really enjoyed the food and the service was great. My wife had the ROTISSERIE LEG OF LAMB and I had the BEEF BOURGUIGNON. Both were excellent.
Good food.. Average service.. Hate that they serve water in plastic glasses with straws..

Great service. Great food. Nice drink selection. Would have been 5 stars had the only other party sitting in the back room NOT been seated at the table next to us! Can't understand the seating etiquette when the rest of the back room was wide open (and there were still tables open when we left). We heard them talking about having to wear sandles due to a toe infection. I'll be back but will insist on being moved if that happens again!
It's a great place to take the kids, but most adults will find the decor a bit over the top. The burgers are decent. But it is their customizable milkshakes that keep me coming back.

Piss poor customer service.  I ordered the baked grouper to go.  I waited 40 minutes before I had to ask how much longer; and mind you no servers came to me to let me know how much longer it would be or anything prior. I was just ignored at the counter. Plus, no smiles or no apologies for my long wait!  Never again will I come here!  Very disappointed!!!

My friend recommended we dine at this restaurant. I checked out the menu online and it looked great. I was shocked when I walked in to find a modern diner. It definitely was not what I was expecting! Maybe I'm too old and/or expected something a little more sophisticated. The service was great and the food was pretty good. The best dish was the grilled octopus. The crispy brussels sprouts were good, but too greasy and friend for me. The steak frites was another good dish as the meat was perfectly cooked and the fries were delicious. Probably a good bet for those in their 20's or 30's; anyone older might be better off dining elsewhere.
Very small, but great tasting food! Prefect when on the go and wanting something fresh!
Authentic Chinese food very similar to what I had in china Try the spicy cumin lamb noodles with the tiger vegetables salad

Not sure why so many people are giving Nora's Deli bad reviews. I always have a good experience here. Nora knows me by order because I always order her grilled chicken wrap and I always request that she put honey mustard in it as well (it's delicious!) Also, her Italian hot dog is SO good. My husband and I order it for dinner and it feeds both of us! And there's typically left overs! She piles on the fries to every dish so you really get your money's worth. Prices aren't even super high to begin with AND you get a lot of food. Nora is always nice to me and I've never had an issue with rude customer service. I'd give her another chance even if she was rude, her food is really good and the portions are super large. I'll have to upload a pic soon.

If you want to find a Chinese restaurant in University City, SangKee may be a good choice. The food here may not be absolutely great but totally acceptable. Its location, service and ambiance may promote you to have the Chinese style meal.   Location: SangKee has a special location, at the first floor of the Sheraton Hotel. This location may give itself a chance to have more customers. Nevertheless, unlike most of the restaurants in the hotel, this restaurant has relatively more delicious food with a passable prices. Service: The workers of this restaurant are totally friendly and helpful. Several workers in the restaurant can speak Chinese. When I first communicated with them in Chinese, I just feel I'm back to my hometown. When I had meals in this restaurant, I also saw 20% to 30% non-Chinese customers. Waiters could also communicate with them in fluent English. They could also give accurate descriptions of the food and some constructive suggestions to customers. SangKee's service may attract more customers to the restaurant. However, their service is not completely perfect, because, sometimes, customers need to wait for their seats while the restaurant is crowded. Food: One customer claimed on Yelp that "Sang Kee Noodle House provides passable Chinese food -- it's generally okay, but not great" (C.Sen). I think although the "Chinese food" here is not absolutely traditional Chinese style, it is much better than the food I have tried in some other Chinese restaurants in Philadelphia. One of the dishes I want to recommend in SangKee is the "Spicy Stir-fry Pot". This one is extremely attractive to those people who are keen on Chinese spicy food. Since I'm from Sichuan Province, I have a high requirement for spicy food. This dish almost meets my requirement. It holds different spicy contents, like shrimp, pork, cabbage, tofu which make it not only spicy but also full of various flavor. Its taste is similar to our hometown's chili pot "Taiwanese Beef Noodle Soup" is also tasty. One bowl of noodles hold about 30% to 40% beef meat over noodle. This would make the dish so attractive to those carnivorous customers, like me. The taste of the soup is also very delicious. Despite trying this specific noodle, people can also try noodle with chicken, pork, shrimp or seafood. However, one thing the restaurant need improve is to add diverse flavor of soup in different kinds of noodle. This can make multiple styles noodles taste differently. The taste of all the dishes in SangKee is similar to Hong Kong style taste. This may be attractive to those people from Hong Kong or Guangzhou province. Most of the restaurants in the hotel always sell dishes with high price and small quantity of meat. Unlike them, you should try SangKee because holding enough meat is the common characteristic of all the dishes here. For all the dishes, there are three main special types. They are "SangKee Favorites", like Beijing Roast Duck, Crispy Garlic Fried Chicken, Steamed Fresh Stripe Bass, "Asia Rice Bowl", like Bulgogi Rice, Hot Pepper Beef Rice Bowl and "Big Bowl Noodle Soup" which I mentioned previously. Different desserts, drinks are also available. One thing great is that I can even enjoy the Chinese traditional hot tea. Ambiance: There are both outside and inside seats for customers. The chairs and desks are brown and the light inside room makes customers feel comfortable to enjoy their meal. There is no music inside the restaurant, but the atmosphere still let customers feel comfortable. There is a bar-like table near the door of the restaurant. Customers who prefer to have meal with themselves often seat at these tables. There are different tables with sizes for 2 to 10 people in the restaurant, too. One thing I think SangKee should improve is to offer more chairs for customers in the waiting room.

This review is based on my idea and personal experience. I have been found a fancy and affordable Chinese restaurant, and this was the only restaurant which I was recommended by my academic advisor. He said that there is 50% discount for new student, but you should talk to waiter that you are a new college student and show your student ID card. Because I sent a lot of money for buy school stuff, I needed to save money. The name of restaurant is Sang Kee Noodle House, and it located at 3549 Chestnut St Philadelphia, PA 19104. Based on the name, I thought this restaurant is not Chinese restaurant. There is parking building next to the store, so do not worry about parking, but it was not a problem at all. The setting of store was lovely because the setting was fusion of classic and modern Chinese culture which I like, and it played classic Chinese music. Since it has large windows, you can see wonderful view.  The quality of food and presentation were outstanding. The ambience was unique. I went there with my friends at night to eat dinner, and we ordered varieties of food that were recommended. The menu has a lot going on, but I ordered the wonton egg noodle soup which was too flavorful. Personally, I worried about food. I did not like oily food, but most Chinese foods are oily. However, it was meaningless concern, the meal was not oily at all which it was fit into me. We decided to share the food. The pork dim sum was boring in taste. I was not entirely impressed with the dim sum sampler. I found the dumplings to be a little bland and sweaty. The udon noodle and tofu sitr fry were just incredible. One of my friends ate roasted duck with vegetables rice bowl; it was attractive, but not as fabulous as my meal. You may worry about flavors and quality. I believe that it is the best Asian restaurant which I know in Philadelphia. I will definitely go back without one. It was a enjoyable experience.    However, service was not fit into my mind. Service was fast, but waiter was little bit rude. Most waiters are Chinese. When I went there, waiter thought that I am Chinese, so she kept saying Chinese to me. I told I am not Chinese, but still she kept asking in Chinese. Also after ate meal, we wanted separated check, but she did not separate even though we told her. Hence we sent ten minutes to pay after dinner. However, not every person did not like service. According to Robert B.'s review in Yelp, " I ordered two dishes (mixed sauteed seafood w/ vegetables; and stuffed eggplant) and both came out of the kitchen fast, hot and tasted excellent.  The service was courteous and attentive from beginning to end, and the restaurant is big, quiet and beautifully appointed."  Overall the quality and presentation of food was excellent, and price was suitable. Restaurant's interior design was a fusion of classic and modern styles of Chinese culture. I am guarantee that you will love this restaurant.

Have you ever looked forward to something so much that the real thing couldn't possibly be as good as you thought? As much as I hate to say it, that's what Sushi Yasuda was for me. Mistake #1: Not requesting the sushi bar. We were seated in the very back at a stuffy, dimly lit table in-between two bougie couples. Mistake #2 (I apologize to my ancestors): Ordering the omakase. Maybe we just didn't get the best selection, but the platter of sashimi, nine nigiri each, plus a hand roll wasn't, in my honest opinion worth $250+. Don't get me wrong, the fish was fresh, the rice was the perfect cook and temperature, and whatever that hand roll was was BOMB, but the only way I can think to describe how I felt after the meal was that feeling you get when someone holds up a high five, then pulls their hand away the moment you reach out to slap it; like a complete and utter idiot. On another note, our waitress--though I will say she was meticulously diligent about making sure my tea was piping hot and ensuring the soy sauce my boyfriend spilled was wiped up--was borderline rude. Bottom line: If you have a tree the grows wads of cash, go for it. If not, be prepared to get slapped in the face with your own hand.

A great place owned by a wonderful lady.  The food was fantastic and the servings abundant. We had a Souvlaki wrap and the picture on this site is a great example.  I wish we could eat here more often but it is a long drive from Texas.  Elaini made us feel like family or at least a local.  Be sure to save room for the Baklava, it was some of the best we have ever eaten.  All of the food is made fresh but without much of a wait.

As someone with a zillion food allergies I am very hesitant to dine out but happy assured me that he'd take care of me. I never had Indian food but now I'm hooked!!!!amazing food and amazing service!! highly recommended

Perfect late night diner that doesn't feel like a diner at all. Food is great and fresh at all times. Can feel safe ordering any type of food even though its a diner. Fish? Lobster? crab? oysters? Good to Go! Ambiance is very inviting and calm. Great place all around!
I think that was the best panini and lasagna I've ever had. And at those prices. I would eat there all the time if I lived closer.
wow.   wonderful crust.    this is "almost" better than Pepes.
Five stars and worth every star,food, service  and decor a real friendly  tavern you must go

Pizza is fantastic! Ambiance is awesome and trendy, location is perfect with an indoor and outdoor seating option. the only reason it doesn't have a 5 star is because theres always a 2+ hour wait. But if you just want the food without the service, theres a take out option right next door! Sick spot!

We went to PJs for breakfast on a Tuesday. I didn't have enough change to fees the meters so I figured I could get change in the restaurant. They have a change machine for that task but it was out if order. I asked the wait staff if they some change for a dollar , this was after we were seated, not one of the servers had any change.  I said we can't eat here if I can't get any change.  The reply was no one had any change.  You can have the best pancakes in the world but if you don't have customer service who cares?   By the way we went to Panera Bread and got breakfast and change!!!

The ferry departures are timed events that take place every half hour.  The train and buses normally drop off commuters 10-15 minutes before the ferry departure.   However, without fail there is only one person at the register at this time.   I have often seen the manager doing some menial task and have to ask him to refill milk that is never filled.   He could jump on the register! My point is that once the boat leaves there has to be at least 20 minutes of slow time before more commuters come.   Why cant this place just be more organized?  It is very dissapointing.

For around $5, you get a nice sized bahn mi, stuffed with really great meats, nice pickled carrots and good sauces. And all of these things are perfectly portioned so it's not like too much bread or an overwhelming amount of carrot. Jussttt rightttt and  the flavor is soooo good. Also I must say, they're bahn mi/kimchee fries are excellent. Now those are a bit overpriced (I think also around $5) but they're so so yummy and addicting!! Technically I consider this a fast good place, and I suppose that's something to keep in mind. Yeah it's gonna be kinda cramped, sometimes it can get hot, and the service is quick and not very personal, but it's not rude or unbearable at all. Overall, the sandwiches are really good here, and I'm really looking forward to tasting them all at some point!

Portions are very good and the chicken is moist - not overlooked. The rice is fluffy with small amt of brown rice mixed in. Served as Gyro but no pita bread which is a negative. Svc is brisk and pleasant and the staff are attentive. There are only 6 tables but with quick svc they turn over easily. While it is a bit of a hole in the wall, it's definitely the good kind. Really worth a visit

Without a doubt this is one of my favorite places for Brunch.  You can pretty much get the brunch menu 7 days per week, and at all hours.   Best items on the menu?   Mac and cheese, but be sure to order it with the mushrooms... the smaller side dish is not nearly as flavorful.   Even if you don't care for mushrooms, they are large enough that you can easily take them out.   It's also a huge portion, so order, eat, and take the rest home.  Another favorite is the French Toast Biscuits.... I mean, WOW!!! great buttermilk biscuits prepared like french toast and strawberries piled sky high.   If there are 4 of you dining, get one order and share. Another reason to love this place is the owner.  Jacob is ALWAYS there and he takes care of his guests.  Because the place is so popular you can sometimes wait a good long time for a table.  They use a texting system to let you know when your table is ready so you don't have to stand there waiting.  One time when the estimated wait time was way off, Jacob bought my friends and I a round of drinks for the inconvenience.  He earned our loyalty for life with that gesture.  We had a chance to talk with him for a bit as well... He's super nice and listened intently as we are not big fans of the Tap sparkling wine they serve (in all honesty, this place is not a place to enjoy fine wines).   We aren't big beer or pickle eaters, but trust me this place has all the right stuff to keep us coming back again and again. Tip:  Go before 11:30am on weekends if you want to avoid a 1-2 hour wait for your table.
Great chicken kabobs. Friendly cool staff.

My boyfriend and I always frequent Teresa Caffe! The food is amazing, the prices are reasonable and the atmosphere is the icing on the cake. Not to mention that the proportions are perfect, especially for being an italian restaurant; typically you get 10x more than the average person can eat or not nearly enough, however at Teresa's the meals are a perfect amount! I will continue to drive the 25+ minutes to eat here, LOVE IT!

We went to breakfast at Tartine this morning and we are not happy with the service. Restaurant was empty this morning around 9:15 am. We tried to sit down and the waitress told us that it was a table for 4. So we find moved to a smaller table for 2. Tartine is a very small and cramped restaurant. Their table for 2 is really a table for one in most other restaurant. So it is relatively uncomfortable place for 2 people. Mid way through our meal, another couple came in and they sat in the table for 4 and the waitress said nothing??? There are at least 4 other small tables available. So why are these couple got special treatment? Never asked and will not come back. The good case to be made here is the waitress is not competent, the bad case to be made here is the waitress is racist (we are Asian and the other couple s white).  Food are not special enough for their $16.50 prix fix menu price since we don't drink orange juice (and according to the waitress, there is no sub and only one coffee per customer). And it is cash only (????). Starbucks coffee is much better than the coffee I had this morning.. It is a place that try to be special but fail miserably for us this morning..
I actually like this place and come often. However, I am not happy with one of my experience here, which sort of pissed me off so that I think it would take me a while to come back again.

SOOOO happy this place opened. Great staff, great food and great atmosphere. What a wonderful addition to our neighborhood! Congrats on nailing it! Cant wait for their breakfast and lunch to be extended to dinner!!!!!

This place is magic. Manny is so friendly and funny; he knows all the regulars and makes your visit fun right off the bat. The case of pastries look AMAZING - every single one of them. Ordered a cappuccino, which was really nice, not too strong or bitter, and Manny drew a 'hipster heart' on it, ha! I didn't even want to add sugar, it was a lovely blend. The food was great, too, and very reasonable prices. There's a lovely little back patio, as well as the cozy interior. Very stylish and they were playing old jazz - my favorite. Seems like the locals really love this place! This was my last stop before heading off to JFK, but I will gladly be back when I'm in NYC again!

Hello there. Off the start, it used to be my favorite Thai restaurant for a long time.I live in Woodside myself. Recently, something has gone awry in this dining place.The last time in the restaurant, i ordered Chicken Tom Yum, and my wife ordered Papaya salad. We had been waiting for more than half hour for a salad to arrive (it usually takes 5-10 mins to cut that salad and start eating, in Thailand). The food tasted nothing like in Thailand,more like Chinese take out. Second, waitresses DON"T pay attention to the customers ( it took me 10 mins to find a waitress to order a different dish and 15 mins to ask for a check. Just wanted to add that the waitresses don't smile and aren't  polite as in Thailand. Well, make your own decision upon visiting this restaurant.

While visiting my bf in NYC, she insisted that we have pizza at this place. She talked it up for days and I was concerned that I'd be disappointed because of all the hype leading up to the meal. As stated in all the other reviews, the place is a hole in the wall. Rather dumpy to be honest. But the pie did not disappoint. It was delicious. Fresh, fresh, fresh ingredients. Hand made dough. Hand grated fresh mozzarella and parmesan. Chunky tomato sauce and topped with fresh cut basil. The master behind the pizza, Dom, made every pizza himself from start to finish. Do yourself a favor and check this place out if you're ever in Brooklyn. I'd highly recommend topping the pizza with the fresh red peppers (not the dried flakes, but red pepper soaked in olive oil). Cons- be prepared to wait. Also, it's pricey- an original cheese pizza is $32.00.

What should have been a happy birthday celebration was ruined because of the manager of Bridget Foys. My 30 year old daughter drove down from New York to take her sister to dinner for her birthday. The manager told my 30 year old daughter that her New York State drivers license was a fake and took it away from her. After much arguing he finally gave it back. What a jerk.

My husband and I went to this cafe for Sunday brunch after reading exceptional reviews on yelp, and we were not disappointed. Yes, there were a lot of people, but the wait was no more than 20 minutes. We especially loved the quaint and cozy feeling of the place. We looked through the extensive menu while waiting so when we were seated, knew exactly what we wanted. The coffee was amazing! Nice and strong and of course, fresh. One of the best I've had in a cafe/diner. I ordered an Omlette and my husband a waffle with bananas, both delicious. The reason I'm giving 4 stars instead of 5 is because of lack of good service. We got the food quickly but there was no cutlery to eat it with. Even after asking for it twice, nobody seemed to respond until finally my husband got up to get it himself. Also there was no jam/jelly on our table for the toast and neither there was there syrup, salt and pepper on the adjacent table. They kept borrowing ours, which sort of disrupted our conversation. Despite a few flaws, I highly recommend the cafe for its delicious food. We are definitely going back soon!!

I have been to Chattime several times, and I have to say that Chattime is a really good choice for you if you seek some delicious Japanese food with lower prices. Chattime is located at 3608 Chestnut Street, University City. It is really convenient for the students in Drexel University and University of Pennsylvania. If you are sick of the food in the dining hall, go to Chattime and enjoy delicious Japanese food is a good decision.       Food:       First of all, I really like the food in Chattime, and there are four things you need to try when you go there. The first one is Chicken Fried Rice. It not only has a good look, but also tastes delicious. The chicken is very fragrant and appetizing, and you can't even wait to try it. When you put the chicken into your mouth, you will find it is soft and juicy. The chicken is surrounded by some broccoli and carrot, so the chicken has a little bit sweet taste from the vegetables, and the vegetables become succulencier. This is a great combination to make the food have different flavor. Also, one thing I need to mention is that the fried rice is separate from the chicken, so the fried rice has no chicken's juice. Maybe you may think fried rice must be plain without juice. However, the truth is the fried rice has its own flavor and it could really make you fall in love with it. I cannot eat so much rice usually, but at that time, when I ate the Chicken Fried Rice, I just ate whole bowl of rice. Also, Shrimp Fired Rice is delicious too. The shrimp is really fresh and it tastes good.      The second dish I recommend is Eel Sushi. I love to eat Eel and I think the Eel Sushi in Chattime is pretty good and well-season. If I really need to say some deficiency, I will say the rice of sushi is not good enough. When I ate the sushi, the rice could not stick together, and it was too scattered to drop down. Also, I think each sushi is too big to eat the whole sushi at one time. The third dish I believe is worth to try is Beef Noodle. The soup of Beef Noodle is aromatic and tasty, especially; it is very good for us to drink a hot soup in the winter. The noodles are very chewable and with some beef fragrance. As for me, I am a person from Guangdong, so I love to drink Bubble Tea and I almost drank everyday when I was in my hometown. My friends told me that the Bubble Tea in Chattime is quite good, so I tried it and I think it is the most authentic Bubble Tea around University City.      Service and Ambience:       The service in Chattime is pretty good. All of the waiter are very enthusiastic and they will recommend some famous dishes if you ask. In addition, I would like to talk about the environment and atmosphere in Chattime. It is a traditional Asian style restaurant with some bamboo to decorate. This restaurant is very clean and you can see the chief is making sushi while you are eating. I like to go there with friends in the afternoon, we can chat and enjoy the Bubble Tea. However, if you go there during the rush hour, there will be lots of people and you may feel noisy.      I hope I can go there and try some new food next time.

Came here for my birthday dinner, random and later on in the evening on a Tuesday night. Well we were not given any kind of attitude for walking in 35 minutes before they closed. Our waiter was very courteous and helped us with any questions we had. We all ordered probably a bit more than we should have but being hungry and knowing that the dishes were on the smaller side we kind of went crazy. I think we didn't have a complaint about a single dish we ordered. I ordered a shrimp dish which was great but the real stand out were the short ribs and the pork belly. They were both so delicious and perfectly seasoned. The serving size had me wanting a little more but was the perfect amount to not fill us for our other courses. My sister in law had a crab dish that she said was her favorite. The waiter was super nice about it being my birthday, bought out dessert and even a glass of champagne for me. It was a sweet touch to complete the meal and the champagne was on the house. I haven't gotten the chance to return yet but my brother and sister- in- law have frequented numerous times again and love it. I'm going to make it back here sooner than later to have another delicious meal!

Prosperity Dumpling is literally a hole in the wall.  It is small and very dirty and hard to find.  Perhaps that is why it is so popular.  That is called slumming.  It is very authentic in way that people with means confuse poverty and dirt with an authentic experience. First of all there is almost no seating, five stools against very narrow counters.  On our visit there were no napkins in the dispenser and the counter was greasy with food and oily spots and no napkins. To order there is a counter and the order taker is rushed and rushing.  Dumplings are fried, steamed and cooked in soup.  The dumplings are quite tasty and very cheap.  The fried dumplings were the tastiest followed in defending order by the steamed and soup dumplings.  The fried dumplings were what is known as pot stickers in some places.  It is really hard to sit and get comfortable given the limited space on the shallow counter and the small and uncomfortable stools.  The soup is served on a deep plastic container and the dumplings are served in styroform takeout containers.  There are chopsticks available as well as cheap flimsy white plastic forks and spoons.  The napkin dispenser was empty, so I had to find the  napkins where they we stored behind the cashier. It is hard for the first timer to know exactly what he or she is getting because of the time pressure to order quickly with the line at one's back and the limited communications skills of the order taker/manager.  In the back of the kitchen there are perhaps a dozen or so kitchen works preparing the dumplings in a dimly lit medieval setting, with the sound of chopping and steam rising. There was no trash container in the hole in the wall, but the one outside the door was overflowing and smelly.   There are other affordable dumpling stores in Chinatown with "authentic" and tasty dumplings without the naively defined Middle Class "authentic" defined  experience.

I am so happy this place opened up for lunch in my neighborhood.  To say they are busy is an absolute understatement - I think they were not prepared for the terrific outpouring of support from the South Street West community.  It gives another terrific option for lunch, dinner and brunch in the neighborhood.  The food is great and the service was good.
Very friendly even though I came in close to closing. Sandwiches were made fresh and tasted great! Thank you again you guys! 10/10 would eat here again!

I love French food and this review is to speak about the takeout only - we paid 54 for the below meal and it was ok for 30 but definitely not worth the final bill. I suggest a takeout special be created and perhaps the "in restaurant" option is a better value since it's all you can eat crepes for brunch. We weren't satisfied by value and the restaurant didn't have anything that special. I would prefer a Maison Keyser unless you have time to stay all day.
Ruullllzzzzzz, I would make out with Honest Tom if he'd let me. I love his burritos in my mouth!

The service was abysmal. They took half an hour to get us the plantain chips and guacamole. The empanadas were cold and soggy, and the pollo guisado had undercooked chicken, which definitely did not fall off the bone. Yelp, I live by you, but this was a big big big big let down. Terrible place. Terrible ambience. Definitely would not recommend it.
Amazing chines! Try the dandan nudles and the garlic eggplant!

The food here is really amazing for the price. You get what you pay for in terms of portion size. Casually walked in and was surprised at the small complimentary gestures given. Thought not much, I was given edamame with my wait.
always crowded, food is ok, kind of expensive for what you get. The drinks were "ok"
Traditional Japanese tea and snacks with a modern twist. I love everything on the menu. The teas are must-try: the roasted rice tea was the best I've ever had:3

We were on a wait and then got asked if it was okay to be seated in the bar area to lessen our wait time. When seated, numerous servers, captains, and a manager walked by our table frequently and not one person acknowledged us. After seeing the same servers walk by, Not even a "we will be right with you" was said. After 15 minutes of waiting we walked out. No one ever said a word to us. very disappointed because I enjoyed the food there previously. Will not return.

Cramped in elbow to elbow in a small, low-ceillinged very noisy room.. Impossible to have pleasant dinner conversation without screaming at your dining mates. Service was rushed beyond belief. Food, although good, was not spectacular. would not go back there again. May be okay for some folks, but was okay experiennce overall .

A good place for take out. The pizza is pretty good. Ordered sub sandwiches once and got the wrong thing. The take out driver is usually on his cell phone gabbing away, so not so professional. So average overall. But a decent local pizza to go place.
I enjoy the food here and their service is great always. The waiters or waitresses are always good with answering questions on the menu. The prices on the menu is okay.  Great place e to dine.

I have ordered from many different Chinese places near Montclair State University and this one is by far the best! The boneless spare ribs are amazing!!! The delivery is FAST! As a student I have to say the prices compared to other Chinese places are a little higher. It would be nice to see a special deal for college students like the other Chinese delivery places.

Best indian food you will find! I have tried many, many different restaurants in NJ and NY and none can beat them. The food is very delicious but beware it is spicy as it should be, because its authentic indian. Also everything is cooked to order so no frozen food, you will notice just by the taste of the food. I'd recommend the lamb roganjosh, chicken tikka masala, chicken vindaloo, lamb chops, chicken tikka, chicken 69....those are my favs

The view is stunningm The staff so friendly and helpful. Day three of celebrating my boyfriend birthday. Denise was very personable. The pizza so tasty. The the Apple cider with Jameson...superb. It does get chilly..it is a rooftop...but they have heaters and offer blankets. Very romantic ....
Horrible service and I agree with another review that the kids running around this place is just unprofessional.
Great BBQ food. Kind of like a sit down fast food but leagues better in quality and service. Fantastic authentic BBQ
