Tiff is who cooks all the food and not only is she an awesome person but her food is just as great. She is super friendly and willing to adjust to any food allergies! Chelsea and Riley are THE BEST bartenders there! They always know what drink I want and get it for me as soon as I walk in! They are always super friendly and make me feel welcome. Not to mention prices are unbeatable! A must go to bar!!!! Try the food!!!
Excellent sangria! Been there long time ago with my girlfriend who lives in Philly. She didn't like it but i love Mediterranean food. I greatly enjoyed the rustic atmosphere and the food.

So I didn't try the sushi.  But I had the teriyaki chicken and beef combo, and the seaweed salad.  The teriyaki beef tasted like pepper steak crossed with some sort of bastardized cheese steak.  The seaweed salad was a little bit of seaweed on top of a mess of iceberg lettuce.  I've never seen a seaweed salad with anything other than seaweed.  I paid $5 for a bunch of cheap rabbit food.  I won't be going back to this joint.

Food is decent. Seated us pretty fast even on a crowded night wait was no longer than 10 mins. The seating is a little crowded but they were more than happy to accommodate groups, server and staff was attentive speedy. The food was okay not the best could've been a bit hotter but overall not too bad.
Love this place so much can't wait to bring my parents to meet her

This is one of those great little finds in the middle of Little Italy/Chinatown.  I'm a local and love a good breakfast place that I can eat at once or twice a week. The food is excellent and reasonably priced for the area. The reason why am not giving it five stars is that the service was so painful this morning that it nearly ruined my appetite.   I walked up to the counter to order and the gentleman standing there, a blonde Australian guy,  said to me "can you hold on a second."  I said "sure." ...And then to my surprise right in front of me on the counter he was pulling his one dollar tips from the jar.   Five one dollar bills at a time and replacing it with a five dollar bill.  Then he did it again and again till there was 4 five dollar bills at the top of the tip jar.  I found it a bit strange or shall say I poor taste, but I thought okay.... maybe finally has a chance to do that.   I sat down and waited for my breakfast and notice three or four tables were piled high with dirty empty plates. One of them even had a tip on the table.  I did see the sign "bus your own table" but not everybody follows that and the sign is ONLY in the back.  Meanwhile the entire restaurant has dirty tables all over the place.  Customers we're coming in and wanting to sit down but there was dirty tables everywhere.  Even the table I was at was super sticky.   Then when my amazing food showed up and the same blonde Ozzie said "do you need anything else"?  I looked in the little silver bucket on the table and said "there's no fork here" and he said "oh you can get it over there."   I cannot believe how lazy this person is!   Half the tables are missing them.   It's a service business and he works for tips!  What a joke! It put a bad taste in my mouth.  Then I asked the guy across the table from me "is it just me or is the service here really bad."   He said, "I had the same experience with silverware."   I walked up to the counter and said "the knife table in the bucket is dirty."  Response he got was "you can get a new knife over there."  I've waitress for 10 years.  My response would've been "oh my gosh I'm so sorry " and walked 3 feet to hand a new knife. Now I'm willing to come back here because I'm a local and love Two Hands food.  Maybe the manager or the owner had a talk with the staff or got a new staff.  I hate to blame one or two bad experiences cause of one or two poorly hired choices.  One more time Two Hands And if I have another bad experience service I'll bring my breakfast appetite elsewhere.

My First successful trip to a place using the Maps app OMG. I ordered a "the best bloody Mary" and scrambled eggs with ham. Strangely it comes w a side of mixed greens. The bloody Mary was banging! It's was hot n spicy just the way I like it and the eggs were very tasty. The waitress kept refilling our waters.. that important. I enjoyed the mixed greens and the conversation. Only con was our table was too close to our neighbors.. it's like we went to brunch with strangers! I would def recommend this place!
Adobada taco on a fresh, warm homemade corn tortilla will become that thing you crave whenever you're hungry.

I am utterly disgusted with this place. I ordered the buffalo mac and cheese, which sounds amazing, but I was sadly mistaken. After a few bites, I felt queasy to the point where I thought I was going to vomit... I thought MAYBE the burger bomb wrap can make up for the repugnant buffalo mac and cheese...NOPE. Wrong again. I felt as if eating rat poison would have been a better option than eating this garbage. The wrap was soggy and it fell apart before I could put it in my mouth. The end result was me hugging the toilet for the rest of the night. It made me feel like the queen of the porcelain throne....... It's safe to say I will never order again, even if someone were to pay me.. Seriously not worth your money or time. ALL ABOARD THE NOPE TRAIN??? Nope nope nope nope nope........
Cool ambiance, great food, awesome service. Tomato soup was best I've ever had. Ever had. I shall return.  Make reservations via Open Table.
Typical Italian menu. Food was only fair eventho it was crowed in the restaurant.

Shout out to Mohammed and Ahab. Two great members of the team that bring me my favorite falafel, consistent and delicious every time. Can't beat the price, under $4, and right next to the train. Line moves quick, we all get served, and I can usually get a seat. Great place, happy they finally came to Greenpoint. I haven't been to that one yet but I am looking forward to it. I have been to this place like a hundred times and never have I had a bad experience.  Thanks guys and keep it up

Carnivores unite! Wowzers this place was great. On a recent boys night, we attacked this menu. Without reservations we were lucky enough to dine at the bar without a wait. Our bartender and now server was amazing. We started with the Black Label burger divided three ways with the Roasted Marrow. And we could have stopped there. That's how good it was. The dry aged beef combined with the succulent marrow is killer. Next we shared the Filet Mignon, Veal Porterhouse and the Pied de Porc. Sides included the Aligot and the Macaroni Gras. All perfection. Meats cooked perfectly. All notes hit. Perfect 10. Minetta Tavern is an institution. Period. #oldguysyelptoo

Not sure what any of the one star reviews are talking about- this is by far the best pizza I've ever had- perfect crust- and delicious toppings. Try the melanzana or the margarita! Also excellent Pinot Noir! Highly recommended. Great service and all around atmosphere. Will definitely be back!

At the bartender's suggestion, I had the burger, which, despite the bacon and the dollop of sauce, was one of the blandest burgers I've eaten. It took forever to arrive and the unfriendly bartender (I was at the bar) didn't make the wait go any faster. With all of the great eating options steps away, I regretted going to this place.

Just ordered take out from here--plain pie, spaghetti with marinara sauce, and a side of meatballs. I was thoroughly underwhelmed. I ordered the spaghetti, but received angel hair. The pasta was overcooked and very soft. The marinara sauce was rather bland and on the sour side. Maybe some people like that, but it's definitely not my style. I had to add my own spices and was still disappointed. The meatballs were a decent size, but the price seemed a bit much for just two. You could tell the meatballs were homemade, but lacked flavor. Again, under seasoned. I didn't try the pizza, but was told it was good. Actually I was told "the crust would be too thin for you." Honestly, I probably would not order from here again just based off their dishes.

This restaurant has good reviews but for us was disappointing. Very crowded, we were sited at the center communal table. When the couple seated to our left side left the water glasses were not taken off the table and table not cleaned properly. The appetizers and main course tasted ok (nothing to remember) and were pricy (only cash accepted) for what is being offered. We ordered desert (I love sweets and I never miss deserts). Two puddings that were worse we ever tasted: thick bread with syrup.
This is a okay place to have burgers, however, I think their burgers are a little bit overpriced. I spent $15 on the burger and fries and I was not that happy about it.
This place is one of the better restaurants in W.H. Its is very fairly priced for it location and has a wide selection of affordable wine.  Highly recommend this spot!!!

Great spot in Brooklyn to go for brunch. The food was amazing. I had the pulled pork grits and my girlfriend had the all walks of toast (french toast). Couldn't have been happier or more stuffed. The beer and wine menu is full of variety and their lack of liquor has given way to a very inventive custom cocktail menu. Will definitely be going again. Reasonably priced food and drinks with a great atmosphere and wonderful service.
Best ribs ever! Don't forget to get the salmon!

Felt like years since I last came here. Maybe 2 years lol. Either way it has been so long that I forgot I wasn't a fan of the crab and pork soup dumplings, note to self, stick to pork only. My mother in law has heard about this place from us for years and she tried to make her own soup dumpling but failed. She too liked pork over crab and pork. Until next time Joe!
Solid spot.  A tad bit overrated, so I wouldn't consider this a "destination", but I used to live in Nolita and came here about once a week.

A very good place when you have a strong appetite for middle eastern food, particularly shawarma! I had a wrap of chicken shawarma with everything in it. It was absolutely rich, well-seasoned, and delicious. I also had dolma (stuffed grape leaves) for appetizer, which was (and as a middle eastern) perfectly made. I would definitely have that again. For those looking for a Halal place, this is not just the one, but the good one. Probably not very good place for large groups, but for a couple or few people or just to have a meal to go as I did.

i have been goin here since 2010 i love the food the fresh pizza is like going to a ny house of pizza shop right here in vt there steak an chesse wow if you can save enough room try there fresh baked.brownies

My Chinese friend highly recommended this place so I went there to give it a try. I ordered the beef noodle soup and it turned out amazingly good! Noodle is chewy and properly flavored. Soup is thick and material. Only flaw is the environment, not very pleasant, probably due to their self-service policy so no waiters around to clean up tables.

Consistently the best place to dine near Parc Restaurant, Bistro & Cafe. Have been there several times and the food is always fresh, creative, delicious and well presented. Once the daily specials are presented, it is difficult to decide what to order. If you sit in a booth, the dining experience is significantly enhanced. Individual tables are much too close together. Wines by the glass are excellent, elegantly served, and at the right temperature. The staff could not be pleasanter with one exception - the lead hostess. She has an Upstairs/Downstairs attitude - she's Upstairs and her guests are Ddownstairs. Her attitude and demeanor are so bad and ungracious (rumor has it the staff agrees), my husband and I always debate returning.

This was a wonderful experience.even better than the reviews.it was a very personable experience.the staff was marvelous to everyone.the food was absolutely wonderful ambiance great.it was packed but the acoustics are marvelous all around one of the best in a long time.I cannot wait to go back again.

This place is among the best deals in Princeton! $25 for all you can eat sushi is an amazing deal here, especially when all the kitchen appetizers and entrees are included in that deal. This is especially great when your family is made up of meat eaters and vegetarians- Masa Sushi truly has it all!! This place is a can't miss!! Dishes I would highly recommend include: Vegetable hibachi, miso eggplant, vegetable gyoza and the tofu teriyaki.

Made an order for delivery tonight that was supposed to be here at 7:25 so when 7:45 rolled around I called to see where my order was. After putting me on hold they came back on to say they are not delivering and I can cancel my order or pick it up. Not only did I have to call them to find that out (they had my number), when I asked to speak to the manager they put me on hold and then hung up on me. I called back multiple times to get an answering machine. Not only can I not cancel my order, but after waiting for almost an hour I have to reorder dinner now somewhere else. Terrible customer service here...who knows what happens behind those counters... First time trying this place. Won't be trying again.

I went there with family and we all ordered different things. The portions are great. The food was awesome and the service. Totally not what you would expect from a pizza place..  I would recommend it to anyone that wants more out of a pizza place.

Just call me fat now! LOL Just came here with some friends for breakfast and it was delicious. I got so much food eggs, home fries, toast and a waffle. YUP I can eat all that by myself. My waiter was super nice and friendly checking up on us every minute. The pricing is very cheap also. I got everything for like $7. Our wait was a little long but that happens when it comes to breakfast especially in new york city. I would def come back

this is a little spot, that is a good healthy pick for a bite. please order online or by phone, then just go pick it up, or other wise you will be on an line that sometimes extends outside. place is small to eat inside. the sandwiches and salads very tasty. the soups and side bites also very good. the hot pressed sandwich are a crowd fave. the tunisian style tuna with egg whites and the pastrami wraps are my fave.check the menu for all items available, and online or on phone for daily soup lineup .as for regular style sandwiches,go with the crunchy tuna or chimi chicken. for sides the baked sweet potato pieces or the courgette(fresh zucchini strips with olive oil are good choices. also hot and cold drinks available. the lemonades are above average as well as the hot drinks. just check out menu online , you will find something   GOOD to MUNCH ON.

I'm so sad to be writing a negative review for a place that I want to love so badly...the staff is super sweet and the food is awesome... ...but this is my second time coming here for food, and it's the second time that my order has been lost! both times ended up waiting over 30 minutes for a basic menu item.  Maybe it's an issue of being understaffed and therefore overwhelmed?

Ate here once and thought it was ok so I ordered delivery from seamless but the lasagna was horrible not fresh, the cauliflower was old and browning, and the bread was stale. Absolutely awful never again.

Loved blend on the water . Their frozen sangrias are the best . I had the chx and sweet plantians dinner  the taste was amazing . my server Alexis was so pleasant and sweet , she made my experience here so welcoming . also the view is amazing check it out .

We recently held to a gathering on a Friday night to celebrate the beginning of the 40th class reunion weekend. The owner and his staff couldn't of been more helpful with the accommodations, the drinks, the food and friendly atmosphere! Thank you Ivy Inn and staff, we had a real blast!

Been coming here for years, due to the fact my mom came here when she was growing up in the area. I am not from Jersey, but have been raised on Star Tavern pizza. The best THIN crust pizza in North Jersey.
Very good pho - first time was a good time. I will definitely go back to try their non-pho dishes.

Stumbled upon this place at Broadway bites by Urban Spoon on Saturday and it was so good that we had to try the original spot while in Brooklyn. Weird neighborhood but wonderful pizza! The pork sausage and Calabrian peppers were a great combo!
Went here for a large group birthday brunch. We were quite the group and with many requests but everyone was so so helpful and accommodating! It was a great brunch!
Always excellent.  The pulpo with grapefruit is to die for.  Yes, it is usually packed, and hard to get a table, but isn't that what NYC is all about?

This place just opened a week ago so we decided to give it a try. There's been a few different business owners at this location over the years so we weren't expecting anything great. But let me tell you that the food we received was excellent! The onion rings had the right amount of crunch and the sauce was amazing. The burgers were seasoned perfectly and a nice big bun to get with them. Next time we'll have to check out the bar and try the pizza. Hope this place is here to stay. We will be back!

Love the lounge here, Jeff the bartender is awesome and knows how to make a perfect margarita! My wife always gets the rigatoni bolognese and then has the leftovers for two days! I try to mix it up and have had just about everything, the pasta is always ridiculously good, but I really love the half chicken. The flavors are just incredible.
Omg.  Great meal.  Amazing food. The cheese plate was too die for.   Our waiter wade was amazing.
The cheese steak is really the best cheese steak in New York and it could pass for Philly try it out and the Samson to the left is delicious

Food was decent but it was absolutely appalling when I received my bill for $18+ dollars for an egg-white omelette with a side of bacon. They charged extra for: Ham Egg whites (expected) Broccoli Swiss Cheese Bacon and English muffin instead of toast. Waiter did not mention one additional charges to me but who would ever think that an  omelette with bacon would be 18+ dollars before the tip! RIDICULOUS!

I grew up here in the NYC area, with many great pizzerias, but Di Fara outshines them all. Every ingredient is the absolute best you can get. The crust is thin and well-cooked. The sauce is incredibly delicious. They use a couple of different cheeses that are so flavorful. Once the pizza comes out of the oven, the owner (who makes every pie), drizzles some high quality olive oil on top, and cuts fresh basil and puts that on top too. When you taste it, it somehow is a flavor explosion and melts in your mouth all at the same time. The toppings are amazing, but my favorite is the plain, round pie...you can really taste the ingredients more without anything covering them up too much. Well worth waiting on line, but if that wasn't enough, they have private parties right in the pizzeria! I've been there for two parties already with my soccer team, and we were all treated like family. They will make any pies you want with any toppings right there on the spot. We have another party reserved in a few months, can't wait!
Great place! So good and the chefs were so friendly! Will for sure go back and try the rest! Make sure you have cash since they don't take cards!

best oriental breakfast and soups in the NYC area. don't be mistaken by the looks of the place. its not fancy and actually they only hace a. ounter for 4 maybe 6 people to eat on the site. but dumplis, soup, breakfast are just amazing
Food is excellent every time I go.The decor is basic but clean.The service is good but a little slower then I'd like.

SOOOOOOOOO GOOD!  We waited a little to get our tables even though we had reservations but the manager was very apologetic and ended up taking care of us. ABSOLUTELY WORTH THE WAIT! I'm very picky about Italian food because nobody beats mom's Italian cooking but this definitely tops the charts! Can't wait to go back next time I visit Philly.
Food is so delicious!!!! The best pizza I had in a very very long time!!!! Highly recommended!!!!

This place is so good. I went on Saturday around 8 and the wait time was around 10mins which is convenient because you can figure out what your going to order in that time. There drinks are really really good and strong but so tasty. I ordered the steak and collard greens which were so delicious like the fact I ate collard greens means it was amazing. The customer service was excellent and very quick. The lighting is pretty dim. They had sinks outside the bathroom which were really cute and they used natural soap which I appreciated. Overall this place is fantastic! Perfect date restaurant.

ATROCIOUS, disgusting food, and inexcusably POOR customer "service."  BEWARE and AVOID. This is heartless, tasteless food, and we had an ABSURD and BAFFLINGLY AWFUL experience here (elaborated below).  Bottom line: eat ELSEWHERE!!!!!!!!!   We ordered seafood curry soup after clarifying that this dish was pescatarian-friendly (seafood only, including broth, NO MEAT). When I brought the food home, we discovered a hunk of BEEF in the coconut curry broth (which looked suspiciously like a beef stock, given its dark brown color), so I returned to the restaurant to replace the broth (as it was packaged separately, such that the remainder might be salvaged). Instead of apologizing or expressing concern, the cashier RUDELY challenged me to prove that there was beef in the stock, claiming there was none while swirling a spoon around.  "No beef, coconut only, show me where is the beef?" I told her, "you find the beef, it's right there," resulting in her removing the piece from the broth, brandishing it on a spoon and boldly claiming, "That's not beef!" I said, "What is it then?," prompting her to confer with her colleague in Chinese, before telling me: "Tomato!" (It was quite evidently NOT a tomato and distinctly a piece of beef). I insisted that the dish be changed, maintaining that the beef was beef, ordering a Tilapia curry as a replacement. Upon returning home a second time, my daughter opened the bag to discover a half-full container of "sauce" (looking a lot like the beef curry from earlier (!) except a lesser quantity and minus the piece of beef). There was NO FISH in our fish curry. And the container was partially full (of what was most likely the dish I had "returned"). I called to say there was no fish in our fish curry and was told "it's blended in with the sauce" (even though the dish pictured online shows fish). UNACCEPTABLE. Expect more ONE STAR reviews to follow. I hope this restaurant FAILS miserably. UNETHICAL and LUDICROUS.

Mindblowing ramen. Maybe I have been craving for ramen for far too long, but I would never forget my first sip of that akamaru ramen after a personal ramen drought of a month. The tonkotsu broth was deep and tasty, certainly on par with those that I had in Hakata, Japan and even better than the ones served at ippudo back home. One thing that could have been better was the egg. Pity that the egg charges extra. Also, it was cut across the width, not length-wise that I am used to. It could also be marinated more to match the depth of the ramen broth.

this is by far the best pizza in NY, well Brooklyn! Well worth the wait, although we got lucky and waitied 20 min. the pizza was Hella Good. i would definatly recommend coming here. i would love to come back here and eat again on my next visit. Im a thick crust lover myself, but the thin was very Good. Two thumbs Up!!

My husband and I came here for Brunch this past weekend and absolutely loved the food here. Firstly, they take reservations which was awesome because we didn't have to wait in a ridiculous line. The food was very unique and delicious. The biscuits are incredible. We had the Almond hash and ricotta pancakes - both must haves!
One of my favorite places for brunch, always great service too!

Very homie place, We went on a week night and had a very nice dinner. We share the Steamed mussels delicious! As mains we had the salmon which I really like,  though the couscous was overcooked. The cocktails were superr good! tequila, mint grapefruit juice!! that our waiter recommended.. service and ambience was great .. Ill definetily wanna try your brunch, the menu looks fantastic !
This is an updated review as the situation has been handled by the owner and the employee is no longer with this establishment.
So happy we found this hole in the wall Mexican place. Doesn't look like much from outside, but the food is brilliant and the service friendly. The pork belly tacos are a highlight.

Made a reservation one month in advance for 11 people traveling from NYC to Philly and the day off the reservation was nowhere to be found. The person on the phone was rude and unapologetic, he literally told us he could not serve us. Tip: make sure you call them at least 5 times before making the trip.

Loved everything about it! Been twice and looking to go back... The pizza gets the buzz (and well worth it) but the apps and entrees are why I've gone back - the pasta is hand crafted, lamb meatballs superb. Cocktails are innovative and D-lish, service is friendly and professional. The feel is casual and comfortable -

I bought a sandwich platter for my daughter's birthday.  My sister-in-law is a vegan and I wanted to make sure she had something to eat other than fruit.  Lisa came to me and told me there had been a mistake; that the sandwiches were not vegan.  I ran to the table thinking someone had screwed up labeling the food on the table.  They had not.  I assured Lisa the sandwiches were vegan.  On three separate occasions during the party, she repeated that the sandwiches were delicious and couldn't believe they were vegan.  She removed the "Vegan" sign from the table so other people would eat them.  No one knew.  I tried them too and they were yummy. The next day, Lisa called to ask me where I had gotten them.  Thanks, HipCityVeg, for making me a hero!

I got tipsy, I ate tacos and I had fun. It was my first time here, and I had a lovely time. All I had to do was strike up a conversation with the staff and they made me feel right at home. Suuuper nice. At the very least, I'll be there every Tuesday night.

This place was terrible from the moment I walked in. The restaurant had just opened and we were the first customers. As soon as we sat down the manager or person behind the register was on the phone the whole time yelling and fighting with the person on the other line.  The restaurant was absolutely silent and all you could hear was her conversation on the phone. It was so distracting and disruptive to our meal that I had to tell the waitress. The service was also incredibly slow...which I don't understand since there was no one else in the restaurant.  The menu was also incredibly limited and over priced.  I did not enjoy the meal at all and am surprised that it got such good reviews.  I completely disagree and would not recommend it to anyone!

Great tasting sandwiches, and made with really fresh ingredients. You can taste the difference between Chopping Block sandwiches and sandwiches made from anywhere else. If I lived closer to FiDi, I'd be eating here every day. Nevertheless, still worth the travel.

I used to eat at Chipotle every day until I discovered Chopping Block down the block from where I work. They seemed like a east village type restaurant, but in FiDi. As it turns out, it was one of the coolest places to eat in this area of NYC. They offer great food at great prices, and the portions were HUGE! The food usually comes with a few treats, making it even better. Their coffee is the best in the neighborhood though, great tasting beans and great espresso.

Hands down best sandwiches in NEW YORK CITY! I am not exaggerating! I don't usually write reviews, but holy cow! Their sandwiches are far from the typical sandwiches you get from anywhere else in the city. They offer a great selection and also great coffee! It's one of the chillest spots in lower Manhattan. If you haven't been yet, you've definitely got to go!

Having worked in FiDi for almost a decade now, I never actually realized that there were no options for good food, or even real food. Upon being introduced to Chopping Block, I had only wished that they had moved here sooner. Their sandwiches are delicious, unique, fresh, and organic. Best of all, their prices aren't high and is generally cheaper than most restaurants around here that offer crappy food. We have been ordering from Chopping Block for months until they closed down for renovation. We hear that they are reopening this month and are very excited to be able to eat their sandwiches again.

Absolutely the best restaurant I've been to in the Financial District and arguably even New York City! Their sandwiches are top notch, unlike what you get in other nearby sandwich shops. They use fresh ingredients and offer a variety of very tasty sandwiches and for a great price. We definitely love the popcorn side that each meal comes with. I hear they will be re-opening soon, and look forward to eating there once again.

I have been going here for darn close to 40 years. They closed for a little bit , but now they are reopen. Since the reopening their food is even better then it was before. The have many varieties of burgers and it's quality beef. They also have various seafood & subs and things to tickle the kids fancy too. The help is and has always been friendly and you couldn't ask for better ownership.
Killer wings here. The beer selection is the best in town....the staff is friendly and so are the patrons. One of the owner/managers Fran is one of the most helpful and sweetest people around!
small little crepe store, serve pretty quick and great selection to choose from! really love their valentine crepe!
Flies all over this place. Rude owner or guy making pizza. Pizza sits out for the whole day, you can tell by looking at it. Don't bother with this place. You will not be pleased.
Great food and customer service! This is a staple of mine. Love the sandwich and salad!
Simple, delicious, inexpensive. What else do you expect from a food cart?
I literally will drive an hour just for their curry chicken , Mac and cheese and collard greens. My favorite Jamaican restaurant in NJ hands down!!!

We were so excited to dine here as we love Le Virtu and we love Pizza. Have had it all over the world. However we were disappointed the prices were ridiculous. We had the stuffed pepper appetizer. It was one stuffed long hot cut in half and stuffed. It was good, but it was one stuffed long hot for $12! We ordered 2 pizzas. The Marinara and the other with the special tomatoes. I was super excited to get this, but it was terribly disappointing. It was soggy. Not just soft and chewy, but actually soggy from the tomatoes and very little taste to it. It's interesting to see the notes going around about the Neapolitan style pizza. I've had this before from the same style of oven from Napoli (Cane Rosso in Dallas) and it was soft and chewy and incredible, but it wasn't soggy. And the prices were expensive. 1 appetizer, 2 pizzas and a lower end bottle of wine was $120 with tip.

I love this place!  I have been going to Tavern on Jane with various friends for a number of years, and we are never disappointed.  It's quiet, low-key, and has a wonderful ambience enhanced by the old wood and unique fireplace.  The staff is always friendly and outgoing--and they provide some of the best service I have ever had in NY.  I was there recently with a friend who was celebrating a major birthday, and our server was accommodating in every way--to the point that she remembered our names throughout the evening, was always there at exactly the right time to refill our champagne glasses, and she provided excellent commentary on the menu offerings.  When the server brought the birthday dessert to my friend, she even sang "Happy Birthday" in key!  (Not that off-key, monotone junk that so many restaurant servers dump on their customers).  Since my friend is a professional singer, we appreciated our server's gesture VERY much.  Anyway, this was my most recent of many fantastic experiences at Tavern on Jane, and it goes without saying that my friends and I will all be going back regularly for many years to come.  If I could give them 10 stars, I would do it.

The nutella stuffed french toast was pretty great and couple with the coffee made for a great rainy day brunch with friends! I would definitely recommend if you're looking for a nice and a little different brunch place that's not too expense.

I've been here twice, and each time was very good, especially for a place on a college campus, so I owe them a good review.  After living in Baltimore for three years in the 60's, you'd think that the best oysters and crabs in my life experience had come from there and then.   Not so!  Magrogans holds that distinction now.  The food, service and drinks can't be beat, even by the downtown Philadelphia restaurants, many of which are quite good.  It does get a little crowded, and some areas in the building are noisy, so discuss with the hostess where to sit if you want a quiet table, and have some oysters in the Oyster Bar while you wait for a table of your choice.

This place is very reliable which is what is best.  The ability to order a sandwich and drink at decent quality at all hours of the day is so clutch. I just wish the sandwiches were a tad bit better and they'd be a 5 but rest assured, I love Sunny and Annie's

I always have a great experience here.   The beer selection is great.   They carry my favorite German on tap!    The oysters always taste super fresh and tasty.  Dinner platters aren't huge but quite good too from the burgers to the salmon.    The only thing here is it's pretty pricey compared to some other restaurants with similar fare.   But to not have to travel to Manhattan and stay close to home is also priceless.   If you don't mind spending a little extra $ then don't hesitate.  Also, on Sunday's the brunch menu is good too.   I'm a fan of the salmon benedict.

Food here is amazing and fresh! It's family owned and operated! Yes the service tends to be slow, but imagine your Mom serving food in her own house and trust me it won't bother you. Dinah is incredibly friendly and sweet.
Great  food in a upscale setting! Hearty food in large portions make this a winner! Close to Convention Center, Infinity Hall and across from movie theatre make this a great weekend spot.

My boyfriend and I tried this place the other day, the food is really good. The pasta was perfect and the price is very reasonable. We had bruschette with the wild mushroom and ricotta cheese and truffle honey, they taste amazing. Mini veal meatball was so good too, especially the bread stick that come with it, sooo delicious.  We had the red sauce seafood pasta, that was really good too. The best is their Gnocchi!!! They are so soft and yummy, best Gnocchi we had in NYC. Place is very cozy, we love the ambiance. Definitely recommend couples to come here for dinner on a date night.

We came there yesterday and were agreably surprised. The place is very nice and the food and the wene were just perfect for us, french! If you want to have a clear overview of french cuisine, you should totally go there. The brie with black truffle and the foie gras were delicious! Good chat with the chief-cook/owner who took time at the end of our dinner to tell us the history of his restaurant!

Although it looks gross from the outside, the interior is gorgeous. Our party of three was more than full after two sushi rolls and one 20 dollar bowl of spicy rice cakes with all - and I mean all - the fixings. We will back if we are in the area again!

The tacos...the burritos...the nachos I don't even know where to start and quite frankly it really doesn't matter. We looked up the best nachos place in NYC and this was the answer so why not start there. As you can imagine by now these nachos are friggin delicious! We got the chicken nachos and everything tasted ridiculously fresh and amazing. On one trip it was followed up with two tacos which were equally delicious and filled with chicken/beef, did not hesitate to fill those bad boys up at all. The other trip the nachos were with a chicken burrito and it was also amazing. 5 stars, I will be back many times.
This place has a great vibe. Great people, homemade fresh goodies and tunes :) I love it!
Worst 4 person feast ever. Portions are so small it's really only for one person. Will never order from here again. Also bad service and the food took so long to be delivered.

This is the second time I was there the food is good but not for the price. They were not very friendly the last time and this time they were the same. I will not be going back and would not recommend this place to anyone.

Hit or miss service. Sometimes forgetting to bring things that we have ordered. Probably because they forgot to enter the order. Barely anyone writes anything down and then we have to suffer and watch our friend's eat while we are waiting for our meal. You forget a beer, ok not bad, forget a steak ??? Bad ! Or bring out a well done steak when you asked for it medium... just as bad because now I am stuck eating something cooked in a way in which I do not like and thus did not order, or I will be watching everyone eat while I wait for a new steak. Plus it's always cold in the dining room between the bar and the front of the building.
Sad. I love this place but the cashier pays more attention to people calling to place orders than the people standing there waiting patiently forever. Disappointed. Had to walk out.

I went here today for lunch and was so surprised that they've been here for over a year. How did I not know this? My super Mexican food powers must be failing me somehow. But alas I was most definitely recharged once I left. I had a pork taco and a few appetizers (guacamole, taquito's). My friend had the fish taco and was very pleased and energized as well! Do go here if you love Mexican / Cuban food. Everyone was nice the place was clean, Just Do It!!!

Just had the deep fried tofu with simmered beef. The tofu was not fried and had only the texture of creamy soft tofu. When I asked if it was fried the chef and waiter were insistent that it was. I am far more offended by being castigated than I am that they still charged me for half eaten bowl of nothing special.  Maybe I ordered wrong because other reviews are good?  Not for me and if you like the more traditional Japanese stewed dishes you won't enjoy it either.  Arigato gozai mashuta

Very nice place with attentive service, good food for sit down Chinese. ***The waiter told us that they had complaints that the Kung pow chicken was "too spicy and too many veggies" so they make it bland and with only chicken, peanuts and water chestnuts.*** they will make it the right way if you ask.

I met my close friend for brunch here and I was very disappointed. We love to try new places, and this promised southern comfort food. The biscuits were very dense and thick. Not light and fluffy. The shrimp and grits were over seasoned. I got the omelet and it was also over seasoned with a dry piece of bread. The drinks were flat and the service only so-so.

The picture on their website looks better than what it is but their food is solid. Waiters are very attentive. I had lobster salad and thought it was pretty fresh. My father had 1-pound lobster and it was pretty fresh and cooked in a right way. Some restaurants cook lobsters too buttery but this restaurant enhanced what lobster taste like. I liked it. But I would say this restaurant is good for a big group. Not suitable for a intimate conversation as I felt it was rather loud.

I walked past Heritage House after a massage at the Woodhouse. Loved their décor, so I grabbed a menu and decided to come back for lunch with my girlfriends this past weekend. When we walked in we were the only table in the place, by the end of our meal three other couples had come in. We ordered the brussel sprouts (which we loved!),  two orders of chili (spicy and good, however the menu stated it came with "dipping bread" which was never brought out. When I questioned the waitress she said it did not come with bread but brought out two hard rolls upon checking the menu), mac and cheese bites (that would have been perfect, except they were topped with a lot of mayonnaise which was not listed on the menu. super weird paring choice), cheddar grits (decent but overall pretty bland), and a black bean burger (it was okay). We also ordered hummus, but it was never brought out. Overall, we left feeling pretty unsatisfied. Perhaps we would give it a second chance after some fine tuning, as their menu was diverse and their location was close to parking and church street.

We loved every minute of our experience at David Burke fabrick. We were seated right away, at a nice corner booth; the hostesses were friendly and smiling. Our server, Mark, was charming and attentive without being overbearing. The ambiance was interesting to look at (but not distracting) and it was quiet enough to have a conversation without straining to be heard while still feeling vibrant and exciting. Everything we ate was delicious. The drinks were wonderful (I had the Manhattan while my friend tried a couple of yummy lemony vodka concoctions), and we devoured the Avacado Panna Cotta, which was incredibly delicious and flavorful. We almost ordered a second one. :-) Every bite of our entrees (the burger and the mushroom pasta) was wonderful, and we had the incredible Burke-in bag hazelnut dessert... wow. (And clever name.) I don't usually eat sweets, but I tend to make exceptions at restaurants like this because they're usually exceptional... this proved me very, very right. After dessert we paid and headed upstairs to Spyglass, which was a true gem! Tiny but solid, with an exceptional view. It was the bartender's last night working there, so I'll opt not to judge this place by his less-than-stellar service; I would definitely come back for a future night of cocktails before or after dinner, as the view of the Empire State Building was stunningly great, even on a cold and rainy night. (Sunset there would probably be gorgeous, as the patio faces south and would give you great contrast in the sky.) Overall I was extremely happy with this recommendation and will absolutely come back the next time I'm in the city.
Love this place!....the wings and clam strips are amazing. The staff is courteous and the prices are very reasonable. Great place for seafood lovers!
One of my favorite Fish & Chips spots, I live in BK, but anytime i pass through i have to stop here.
Excellent little nugget in the LES.  Worth the trip.  Delicious food cooked by chefs who care about what they are doing.  Fun, comfortable atmosphere.  Great service.  Great sausages & Awesome Ruben

Outstanding! The culinary skill in the kitchen is matched by the courteous and prompt attention of the staff and management. This is one of the best restaurants in town without the pretentiousness of its peers. It is a dress up restaurant and it can get expensive.

The food is top notch. I gave it 4 stars because I just can't justify the black label burger price tag.. or some of the others bone marrow , for 6 pieces, is like $20-30 The service is excellent, decor is excellent

After wandering around in circles for about 25 minutes with my somewhat-significant other (and my feet were killing me) he said "let's just go in and eat here". "Fine", I said.  I just wanted a burger, and wanted it fast.  The burgers were OK, best part was the fries, actually.  My burger was still a bit too raw for me, but I was so damn hungry that I just dumped on some more ketchup and wolfed down the fries.   The somewhat-significant other ordered the French onion soup and he said it was awful (and he will usually eat anything), so I would say avoid that.
Great dinner as always! Everything is shareable and highly recommended! Service always good!
Atmosphere is nice.  Restaurant is located in a great location, love to walk around there.  The service was ok at first but then waitress eased up which made it more pleasant.  Meal was pretty good.
The place is really simple, old style, I think a new decor would be really inviting, but I still go there when I'm near by for a slice.  They really do make great pizza!

Came to this place after my friends recommended it to me. I'm really not that much of a foodie, but even for me this place fell short of expectations. The chicken was dry, and I even left some pieces of it untouched as I felt they were undercooked. I did get some of their Mac & Cheese, and while it was okay, it wasn't amazing as I would have hoped considering how pricey it was. My friends can come here if they want, but count me out.
One of my all time favorite places in NYC...get the burger!

I came here for lunch with some friends food was a little greasy but not bad. Beer selection was great, a lot to choose from. Service wasn't bad but it wasn't the best either. Hostess was nice greeted us right away!

I really can't recommend this place enough. Pita Ziki is straight up amazing. It is a must visit. It's open until 11pm and is perfect for a 2nd dinner or late meal. I had the rice bowl with chicken shawarma and falafel. The meat was cooked to perfection and the countless number of additional things you could add to the rice bowl made for a great variety of flavors. All the ingredients tasted fresh. An overall great and healthy meal. The restaurant is clean and the music playing is upbeat and fun. An overall great environment. I highly recommend coming with friends whether it is for lunch or a late night snack. The staff are nice, funny, and seem to genuinely care about pleasing the customer.

My wife and I were there last night and really enjoyed the experience. The place is quiet, so we could actually have a conversation. The food was wonderful and the service attentive and unobtrusive. We had the meatball, pretzel nugs, scallops, and the pork large dish. We shared everything and were more than full. Check came in at under $60, but we had nothing to drink but water and no dessert. Everything was delicious. The pretzel nugs were my favorite along with the meatball. The pork was also good, but our least favorite (the cut was rather fatty). We would go back!
Best Pizza!

This joint is hopping almost every night of the week. From early-birds to the late night crowd, this place almost always has a wait, but the food, service and atmosphere make up for any waiting you may do. Great wine selection, seafood is always amazingly fresh and their pasta is to die for! Can't go wrong here!
This is the place this Fall/Winter season. Best soup broths in town. Organic Chicken is rich and deep in flavor. Beef with Ginger is incredible. A must daily stop for sure.

Great place for ramen! It's a little different from "standard" ramen places, but by no means is it worse. All the appetizers are also very good. I've been going there since they first opened and the only bad thing is the wait - as it's become more popular it's become more annoying. But still worth it!

THE WORST CUSTOMER SERVICE EVER!!!!! I've been ordering from Picnic Basket for over a year now and today was the last straw. I've put up with them messing up my orders, I've put up with the obnoxious guy on the phone...all because their food is actually pretty good. But today I waited over an hour and no food - I called to check on the status and the rude guy acted like he could care less. His first response was "oh it hasn't gone out yet. So you want to cancel?" Then he proceedes to tell me that he doesn't know what to tell me - has no explanation as to why it hasn't even left yet. And again says "so cancel, right?". Sorry but this is NYC - plenty of restaurants to order from. I'm done with Picnic Basket forever. They just lost a customer. And I order literally 3-5 times a week for multiple people in my office. NEXT!

I went to Tuome as part of a self-guided tour of "what's new and up-and-coming" in NYC this fall. I wasn't disappointed, but nor was I really amazed. (Note - I just read the NY Times Review today and I'm a little surprised by the enthusiasm for things that I've seen a lot of before, but my complaints are the same, so maybe there's something there) Service - just fine, attentive but not overly so and quite friendly and enthusiastic about what they are serving Ambiance - spare and industrial/cabin hybrid. Not overly fussy but clearly on trend. Restaurant designers just can't seem to get enough of all those Edison bulbs these days... Wine - short but interesting by-the-glass list. Props for diversity. Food - we had a few small plates, sides and one main between two people... Deviled Egg: If there's one thing I'm absolutely going back for, it's this! LOVED IT Scallops: Perfectly cooked, like butter, but the veggie puree with it is too sweet and really distracts Octopus: I came specifically for this dish and found it was neither here nor there. Really well cooked, but both my dining partner agreed that the bacon distracted from the octopus and was too salty to compete with the delicate flavor of the foam Corn: Too sweet, a bit too liquidy, and nothing particularly special Sticky rice: Yummy comfort food, but nothing I haven't had before Conclusion: I'd go back to have those Deviled Eggs, and maybe try some of the other things the Times raved about... always worth a second shot, if it's even possibly to get in!
I love everything!

My absolute favorite place to go when I'm home in Jersey! I don't go as often as I want to, though, because of the wait. I find that if you go for an early/late lunch or early dinner, the wait is manageable. Otherwise, expect to hang outside or at the bar for about an hour. As for the food-- more often than not I get the swordfish tacos. I have not seen swordfish in any other restaurant in the area.. for the price you get a hefty portion and a happy stomach! It also comes with half an avocado and other sides. Swordfish can be very flavorless and dry if not prepared correctly, but what comes in their tacos gives it the punch it needs without being overly spicy or greasy. The margaritas here are huge and aren't skimpy on the alcohol. The burgers are also very good, for only $6-$8 a pop. The complimentary chips and salsa are always a plus. It's not exactly a great place if you want to catch up with friends as you will probably have a hard time hearing them. Still, 5 stars for the food, drinks, and ambiance!
Had a beautiful brunch here.  The eggs Benedict were perfection.  The restaurant was gorgeous and the service was wonderful.
Beautiful place, amazing food, honest price and the owner Gaia is very kind and sweet
The food is very good and seasoned nicely. Great Place to stop in  and the portions are good for $$.
This makes me want to move to the neighborhood! Adorable and café con leche was flawless. Love!
omg this place was so good. best mexican food so far. not pricey either. Great mole burrito i had. Cant wait to go back. wish they had longer hours

as a Middle Eastern, nothing beats home cooked Middle Eastern food. That kind of changed when i had my first meal at Unclo Momo's .. which had me back the following week for breakfast, then lunch then dinner. i've tried almost 90% of what's on their menu. the owners are extremely nice and hard working people. i admire their passion for cooking and providing excellent service. i would defintely try the combination mezza to get a taste of their hummus, rahib (which means awesome in Arabic and it tastes unbelievably AMAZING), babagannouj, etc.. anything they cook in that oven tastes wonderful. ANYTHING! Ouzi, Lamb chops and Moussaka are my fav. entrees. as for dessert Mouhalabieh and their fruit salad. you can never go wrong when your at Uncle Momo
beesting!

Absolutely awful. My two cousins from Italy were in town so we brought them here and I was thoroughly embarrassed by the end of the meal. First things first, we had a 8:30 reservation and didn't sit down until 9:00. We ordered a bottle of wine and we were ID'ed (we are all pushing 30 or over) and the waitress didn't understand how to read a Euro license so she took it down to her manager (this took about 4-5 minutes). We ordered appetizers (a flatbread and calamari) and it was mediocre, that is being generous. We all ordered steak for dinner and it was smothered in A1 steak sauce. The only reason you smother a steak in A1 steak sauce is because it is bad quality meat. And it was...bad quality meat. Water was almost never filled up unless we asked for it. Service overall was just atrocious for what I expect at a relatively high priced NYC restaurant on the Upper West Side. I would never come back here again.

The soup dumplings are to die for. Food is all round outstanding. Bring your own bottle is a nice option. Service can be hit or miss - but the food more than makes up for it. Ahhhhhh those soup dumplings!
Lam Zhou is absoutely the best noodle shop in NYC , they taste great and have probably the best tasting handmade noodles in North America.  try them you love them
first time coming to this place the food is amazing the bartender cindy is nice friendly and beautiful I will definitely be back time and time again

Like many others, a 'used to be a good place' review. I've lived in Princeton for many years, and enjoyed Teresa often. Many family dinners, including meals with just me and my daughter, enjoying pretty good food. However, our last two visits - I wasn't willing to let one bad one rule out a restaurant - have torn it for our family and Teresa. Portions: Much, much smaller. A supposed dinner shrimp salad seemed to be made up of a slightly larger than normal side salad and two - two - shrimp. Bread:Carefully allotted out. And the Momo's have a GREAT bakery across the street that sells bread at very reasonable prices. Prices: Higher than ever. Waits: Longer than ever. Noise: Loud as ever. Why the decline? Boredom? One of the lesser family members running the place? Cynicism about a cash cow? If in town, go to their bakery or their other restaurants, which are more expensive but a reasonable proposition. At Teresa's, you no longer get what you pay for.
My go to for ramen in the west village.
Best pancakes ever!!!! (evil laugh).

Randomly walked into this place because my boyfriend and I were going to a nearby haunted hayride and wanted to eat dinner beforehand. This place doesn't have much of an atmosphere. It kind of reminded me of places you would see in Paterson. The food was awesome and plentiful. I ate everything! Also glad that our waitress spoke English fluently, but I don't think everyone there does.
Originally a mixed Japanese family from the Bay Area.  Moved out to Connecticut and discovered Feng. Some of the best sushi around, it is always our choice for dinner when we are in Hartford.

FOND is the best restaurant I have been to in Philadelphia.  Each and every course was outstanding, even the amuse bouche (divine cream of mushroom soup).   Pork rillettes app is my "go to" and the short-rib stroganoff was inspired.  Our waiter, "G", was funny, personable and always on point.  G will take care of you!

Avoid this hole if possible. Visited with a group before a UConn hockey game at the XL Center. I will not blame the place for being packed. I will, however, blame them for not checking in on our table after my friend and I joined our party. After 20 minutes of waiting, one of us was finally able to get the attention of the server who took our order. After 15 minutes, we got our beers. Another 30 minutes later (that's a 45-minute ticket time), our buffalo chicken sliders came out without the advertised bleu cheese dressing. They were dry and somewhat bland. Also, during the whole time we were there, the server checked in on us only once. I'm not local so I don't know how this place compares to others in the area, but I will certainly never return to The Tavern Downtown.

This place is a gem! The Italian food here is one of the best around. Every dish you order is so authentic. The baked clams are the best id ever had. The spaghetti with white clam sauce is out of this world. The veal don Pepe is a must along with the shrimp louciano. If ur in the neighborhood it's truly a must go!
I love this place especially their pork buns hahaha  oh there is a cutie here who dressed up as a Sailor Mars on halloween, i thought he was a actual girl wow lol

Interesting cocktails, great service and welcoming environment Cocktails were interesting and served in vintage looking stemware. Bartender was very efficient.  Loved that they served hard boiled eggs instead of mixed nuts.  Worth the trip.
Great food, service and atmosphere!

Been going to Pat's for 20+ years , when ever we go up for the Ball or The Penn or to visit friends, Pat's is consistent and always tasty. I grew up in Delaware and Center City as I got older into my late teens early 20s. When you come for the first time its a must see/do.( I always get one for there and one for the road home)
As good as it gets!

Wonderful experience! Had a business dinner there, in the small private room downstairs. Service was good, food was exquisite! The fact that they customized the menu for the occasion was a nice added touch. Made the trip from Long Island worth it!
Great food and drinks.  I'm looking forward to coming back.
3 basic offerings .All are superb!!!
Guess 3rd times a charm,, barmaid was very friendly nice crowd and good vibe.i guess the weekend is too busy for my taste..

My wife and I recently had dinner at Cielo at the Mayfair and it was amazing!! Everything from the food to the service was impeccable!! I had the rigatoni with sausage and my wife had one of their pizzas which were delicious. Our server was a lovely young woman named Megan who was fantastic. She was on top of everything and we never had empty drinks or plates!! She also made my wife the best manhattan she had ever had. Everything was great and we will definitely be back!!

Great bar, great vibe. I always try to force my friends to come uptown to this place instead of our normal LES Thursday hangouts, and it's definitely worth it. The rock and roll music, the friendly bartenders and waitresses, and the great beer and drinks make it a must-go. My friend tried the sangria and said it was randomly one of the best she's ever had, so that's got to say something. It's super casual and has some spacious outside seating, which is prime for late-night people watching.

I always have a good time here. I love the cozy feel, affordable menu and good food. The bartenders are always a bit to relaxed but they are quite pleasant and get things right. You can watch a game but its not a loud sports bar. I happily voted for it as "best bar" for Philly Mag's Best of list.

Absolutely amazing, a splurge that was totally worth it! Came here on a rainy Saturday with the boyfriend. The ambiance is nice - the restaurant is lit well enough to see the food, the music is just the right volume where you can hear your date talk but not necessarily every other word being said at the other tables, and the décor is charming. This is not a party atmosphere, nor is it super overtly romantic, but the room has a definite warm glow-y buzz as the clientele seemed to be all couples and everyone seemed really into the food. The food is unbelievable - some dishes are mindblowing in their flavor combinations, others are for their high level of execution. I have never had better octopus or ice cream in my life, and the butternut squash tea soup with husk cherries blew my mind. The care in which both the chef and front of the house take in explaining the dish to each table shows how much pride they take in their craft. The service toes that perfect line between attentive and unobtrusive. The playlist rocks. The wine list is great as well, plenty of reasonable options. We will be back for another special occasion, if we can even score another reservation. Tip: We got there exactly at 8, but felt like we were a little behind as other tables had drinks and snacks. In the future, I'd try to get there around 7:45. Also, the neighborhood is charming and good for a post-meal walk!

Wow! What a find and what a surprise. Adorable little restaurant attached to the Hotel Monaco (Kimpton property). A small yet unique menu. The free-range chicken served over creamy grits and roasted asparagus was scrumptious. And the house wine (chardonnay) was delish! The Caesar salad wedge had large chucks of freshly grated parm and was so good. Some cute little tables mixed with interesting things to look at while dining. Definitely worth it.
Top, top, top!!! Great Food like in Thailand! I can highly recommended this restaurant!
Awful customer service! To make matters worst it was a manager who barked at me to give him my order as we was really busy!
The best street food in NYC!
Great food. Friendly and attentive staff. Highly recommend. It's our go to for Indian since it opened, and love the ambiance for dining.

Hands down best Chinese takeout I've ever had. I used to work in Hartford and pick it up on my way home - now that I'm in Simsbury, I make the drive from Berlin to West Hartford to pick it up and it's STILL hot and delicious when I get home! Sonny is awesome and everyone there is so nice. And there's free green tea while you wait for your order :)

This place is a must if your passing thru. The sandwich takes the cake over having a cheese steak at pat or Gino's. The roast pork With broclirabe is the way to go. Throw some cheese on it and your all set. The flavor of this sandwich explodes in your mouth.

My friend and I came to Burger Baby because we were going to Paint Nite and this was the venue. First, I'll say that the food is mediocre and the selections uninspired. For a place called "Burger Baby," I was expecting to be blown away with their creations. I've seen more creative burgers at Red Robin, and I dislike chains. I ordered the sliders because they were the cheapest thing on the menu- at $9- and "sliders" they were... in that I mean plural, there were two. I found it strange, and somewhat unappealing, that the sliders were served on a hotdog bun sliced in half, but this may be part of their allure. I ordered the duck fat fries because they sounded delectable. They were not. OVER SEASONED, probably to hide the fact that they were not, in fact, fried in duck fat. All you could taste was the garlic salt. Second, there are a lot of flies, probably because they have the door wide open. My friend got two of them in her wine, and had to exchange it for a new glass...they graciously replaced the glass of wine and would have given them a decent review if that had been the end of it. It wasn't. Our bill came towards the end of our painting. We were still in the midst of talking and painting so we kind of ignored it. The waitress came around, I kid you not, five different times over the span of twenty minutes and tried to take the bill when it obviously hadn't moved from the spot she dropped it on. Finally, out of irritation, I told my friend we should pay the bill to get her off our back. My friend, nice girl that she is, offered to pay for us both since I paid for the Paint Nite, and the waitress came and collected the bill. Upon running the bill (it was a $47 tab), she came back, stood in the middle of a room of people with a live card, and called my friend's name, since she couldn't remember which one of the Paint Nite patrons had given her the card, which (after working at a bank for many years) I feel is completely irresponsible. We left a standard 15% tip, signed, and went on our way. Two days later, my friend calls me and asks me how much she charged at Burger Baby. I told her $54. The amount that came through on her bill was $78. When she called to give them the chance to resolve the issue, she got the same annoying waitress that had taken her card, who argued with my friend (with my friend having her receipt in hand) about the amount charged. She brought up several times that my friend had only tipped her $7 on a $70 tab- which my friend explained was a good tip for the $47 tab we actually had. She then changed her story and told my friend that she could "pay her back out of her pocket" or "give her a few glasses of free wine." Shady? I think so. I wouldn't recommend Burger Baby to anyone- in fact I have gone out of my way to warn people now that I've had this experience. If you do go, be sure not to use your card. My friend has decided to take the issue up with her credit card company to resolve it for her, and we're thinking about taking it to the Better Business Bureau (Burger Baby is not accredited, I wonder why), and advising Paint Nite about our experience. Shame on you, Burger Baby.
Terrific restaurant.  Good service and Food.  Both the seafood stew and the blackened salmon were the best I have ever tasted.  Try it you will not be disappointed.

Great little corner tavern-looking entrance and a local, homey feel inside. Food and drinks are delicious, staff is friendly and the menu changes so I can always order something new. Always a favorite meet up spot of mine.

If you like crepes, you GOTTA go here!! This is the most freshest food you will ever have, they make each dish to order. Yes, you will take a little longer to receive your food, but it's worth the wait! Trust me

Came here for brunch on a Saturday with my boyfriend. They weren't very busy and had several open tables. Despite that, it was very clear the one server in the restaurant couldn't handle her tables. It took nearly 10 minutes before we were greeted and asked about drinks. Another long wait before our order was taken. She didn't write it down, which is probably why she got my order wrong. When the food runner brought out our food and I pointed out I had ordered apple pancakes, not potato pancakes, she tried to protest and seemed very displeased as she took the plate back. She also neglected to bring any silverware, and I tried to raid the host stand for silverware but they were out. It took over 10 minutes before we could wave down the server for silverware. By then his food was cold, and mine was still nowhere to be seen. It took her another 5 minutes before she brought out silverware and napkins and began rolling at the host stand. Clearly they need more servers to help out. The food was fine. The pancakes were good, but overpriced. My boyfriend liked his eggs and salad, but again, they were overpriced. We weren't the only ones displeased with the service. The table next to us asked for coffee multiple times and no one ever brought any. They brought their food over, but forgot the coffee, so that table actually got up, grabbed the coffee pot and two mugs, and poured their own coffee!! Probably won't be back. The service was too much to deal with.

I've eaten soooo many burgers in my time. This is clearly the best one I've ever had. Something about the flavor of the meat is just unbelievable. Of course, I can't forget about the Truffle Fries, also unbelievable. Even better with their different dipping sauces. I haven't had one thing to eat here that wasn't 100% delicious. Been twice and neither time did I have a crazy wait. This has to be one if not the best lunches in NYC.

I don't get to enjoy it as much as I've recently moved slightly further away, but I love the food at this place. Good portions, great staff, and fair prices. I use to always get the wings here as well as the spagetti and a few other dishes. Good stuff and my experience here has always been pleasant. Recommended to anyone, especially if you have a taste for italian pastas!

Ok somebody has to say it. Those who gave this Thai restaurant anything more than 2 stars apparently has never been to Thailand nor tried authentic Thai food (or were just piss drunk when they ate the food). I am of the opinion that if you never traveled to a foreign country and tasted their food, you really shouldn't share your views on Yelp. You guys are just skewing the ratings system. Really, the food here is at best mediocre. Service, well, they managed to screw up my order every time I go. So at least they are consistent. I know, there are so many garbage Asian "restaurants" in Manhattan it is hard for those who has never been to Asia to tell the good ones from the bad. So I am going to help you guys out a bit since so many of you can't tell the difference between good and bad Asian food. Often, these restaurants' food has the same quality as McDonald's, but these "restaurants" have better furniture and are much more overpriced. I don't know why but you Manhattanites somehow love that combination (ie crappy food, nice decor, and an overpriced menu). As a general rule, you can tell an Asian restaurant has terrible food and is just trying to sell you an image (and not the quality of their food) when you see one or more of the below: 1) Hip, trendy music playing at the restaurant. 2) No (or very few) Asian patrons. Maybe one of two who are just mostly hanging out with their unfortunate non-Asian friends who are about to get ripped off with overpriced and mediocre food, but no groups of Asians (and come on, guys. This is a dead give away. If you haven't figure this one out already then god help you. As a general rule we Asians have a better idea where good Asian food is so you might want to follow us on this one instead of Tom and Dick from Ohio). 3) Food served on over-sized square plates. 4) Over-the-top Buddhism/Hinduism decor. 5) Strong smell of garlic (chef can't cook so he drenched everything in garlic, oil, and MSG and just fried it). For better and authentic Thai food try Jaiya (was there many yrs ago not sure how good they are now) or that little Thai restaurant in Woodside, Queens (right off the 7 train line). Totally forgot the name. Think it starts with an "S". Or befriend someone from Thailand and ask them where they go to get good Thai food. And stop messing up Yelp's rating system.
Waiter took so long that gave me time to really analyze menu and realize how pricey dishes were based on ingredients (Food Bazaar buy 6 plantains for $2) .... waited more....walked out.
Delicious. Been here many times before for just drinks but had dinner tonight... Amazing. Dessert- also amazing. Will return.

This place has the best Thai food I have ever had!! It is a must!! The sticky wings are to die for and try anything that has pork belly as the main. Anything on the menu is delicious!! It's a little out of the way but it certainly is well worth the trek. There could also be a ridiculous line but again it is well worth the wait.

My food came late, and wrong. I ordered a turkey bacon sub, it came with no bacon. This was the first time I've ordered so I am willing to give them the benefit of the doubt, but looks like other yelpers had the same problems. Leaving off the bacon is a sin. My dumb plain turkey sandwich was ok. I originally gave this 2 stars, but the restaurant refunded me, which was nice. I think 3 stars is the max for a place that brings the wrong food late, though.

we had a reservation for 7:30 p.m.  we walked in and the place was packed with people so our reservation person told us that we were going to be running 15 minutes late. we didn't have to wait too long before we were seated and the place being so crowded was a good sign that the food we should be good for such a new place. the thing that made us choose this places that we saw the menu online and it was pretty intriguing we got there we ordered the flatbread pizza with the goat cheesethe goat cheese and mushroom ravioli and also the season vegetables tasting. sometimes our waiter would walk away before I could even finish my sentence which was an appealing but it was okay he was pretty much there the whole time and he always came back and asked us if we needed anything else. they did a really nice dessert presentation and I thought that the desserts would be very expensive and that's the reason why they were doing presentation but actually it turned out really well the desserts are only $3 for each shot glass. only thing we didn't like about the food for the portion sizes really didn't fill us up we wish there was more on the plate it for the price that we paid and also the quinoa salad had an orange citrus dressing in the vegetables tasting and we were just werent a fan. the drinks are absolutely amazing I got the cranberry sage and also the pear something. my husband enjoyed his drink that was on the ginger beer side. overall the experience is great and will definitely be coming back for the onion and new menu for every other season. again my onlywish was that there was more food on the plate!

After I wrote a review saying that Bartaco was good for apps/drinks, not really a dinner place, one of the managers sent me a message asking to give them another chance and they would send me a gift card for dinner.  I appreciated the offer and agreed to give it another try.  I gave the manager my address, and he never sent the gift card....

This is my favorite indian place in Princeton! They're a little on the pricey side, but the food is great as is the service. If you decide to dine-in it is BYOB, which is a big plus for me. Most dishes range from $10-$16 dollars. We get take out or dine in at Cross Culture once every week or two. I would highly re conned the paneer masala and the palak paneer.

This weekend was my first time at Balthazar and i'm so disappointed with our service. I'm still shocked with the treatment we received  from our waitress.   I made a reservation for 3:30pm for my husband and I and a group of friends. We were seated at 4:00pm which i completely understand since it was super busy.  My friends were seated 5 minutes before i entered. When i arrived to our table and started to greet my friends the waitress tapped me on my shoulder shoved the menu in my face and told me in a really rude way that i needed to order NOW because the kitchen was closing until 6pm. I had not even taken off my coat  nor sat down. She then decided to slam the menu on the table and said "everyone needs to order NOW" ( almost yelling). I asked her if there was a smaller menu i can order from after 4pm i was okay ordering an appetizer i'm not picky. She again proceeded to tell me VERY RUDE that NO i could not order from any other menu until 6pm.  At this point she was being so rude and i was getting so upset that i decided not to order anything from the menu at all. My husband also decided not to order anything from the menu.  We did not leave the restaurant because my friends were starving and finding another place in the area was going to take forever. After my friends placed their rush orders she then proceeded to tell our table " now you can relax". What type of service is this? She then came to me and brought me a small menu and told me if i wanted i can order from this small menu. At this point i was too irate to even look at her. In conclusion i did not even taste the food. It was the worse service i have ever received at a restaurant. But i understand that sometimes people have an off day and maybe our waitress was having a bad day. I will try  the restaurant one more time because everyone gives it very good reviews. I just don't want to be seated at her table ever again. She should not even be a waitress at such a high rated restaurant. P.S - she never even bothered to apologize to our table.

Alice's Arbor = fresh, wholesome tasty food!  Visited twice and will be back for more.  Portion size is smaller than average BUT was sufficient to satisfy my appetite.  Great one-of-a-kind decor was a "vacation away from new york city" in itself -- you'd quickly forget that you're in Brooklyn once you step inside.  A mini store where you can purchase some of the products that they use in their edible creations!  Very friendly wait staff, great ambience, famiy-friendly, great variety of music... very reasonable prices!  Highly recommended!

We stumbled into this place by accident while on a business trip in Philly. The roof top area was very quaint and cozy. The service was great, but I was surprised to find that the food was excellent! Being from the South you don't expect to find good Southern food this far away. The fried catfish was great, but the grits, holy cow! Grits are a Southern staple and the cheesy grits here are the best I have ever had! Cooked to perfection with lots of delicious, bubbly, cheesiness, you have to try them!  An added bonus was that the bar made a perfect "Old Fashion".
The best sushi ever. Unusual and delicious. Can't wait to go back. Took my son there for his 16th birthday and he loved it. Fantastic.

If you love Cuban food and are looking for a quick and inexpensive fix, you should definitely swing by this place! I came here with a friend after reading reviews here and was definitely not disappointed. Yes, the portions are huge and the prices are great for the Times Square area. The place is narrow and seating is limited, you could always take your order to go. I tried their oxtail with the rice and beans, and unlike a lot of other Cuban restaurants I've been to, they didn't skimp on the oxtail and each piece had quite a bit of meat. They offer various combos and have daily specials on the wall that are usually cheaper than if you order it on a different day, so definitely take advantage of the specials if you're in the mood to try something new.

The cassava cake is my all time favorite and their coffee taste great! I stop here whenever I am in the neighborhood. The employees are super friendly and it's always a pleasure to stop by their for a quick coffee and cake/muffin on the go.
Simply put: awesome service and people, and even better food. The chicken satay tacos are off the chain
It a very nice place. There product is very inviting you can't go there once and stop, best place to chill out.
Neighborhood gem. Quality. Service. Great price. Please don't change .

My favorite NYC restaurant/ Single diners catered to I have been going to GT since about a year after its opening. I read that single diners are welcome at Danny Meyer's restaurants and so I tried four of them. It is absolutely wonderful for the single diner. There are two dining areas. One is the tasting menu in the back, for which you need reservations. I did it once with friends and it was unbelievably great. What I love is the tavern, no reservations (though VIPS do get a table sooner). There is a wait at popular times so I go at unpopular times, including right at noon for lunch. For years I went on my birthday, alone (not as pathetic as it sounds!!). One time I was given a prime window table for three, unhesitatingly. And I'm not a cute young thing--restaurants often put beautiful people at the window. It was a generosity that I have not forgotten. Actually two friends showed up and I joined them at the bar after my lunch. I have eaten at tables in recent years and at the bar in previous years. If there are others alone at the bar, I often have really nice conversations with strangers. There is NO snobbery or attitude. I have had friends come from out of town, go to a famous restaurant, and be treated like crap. One group of 10 lawyers at a VERY famous restaurant asked to have the French entrees translated and the waiter refused. Can you even imagine.
