Authentic!!  Ironically on my bf's first night in town visiting from Nola (I grew up here) we stumbled here because they had a late kitchen on a Tuesday night.  He got the BBQ shrimp and I was worried bc he is very picky, he loved it!!  I tried some and it was really good, flavorful and the real deal.  I got a Pimms Cup (it was called something different) it was awesome.  The staff was super friendly and very good.  I will recommend to my family and friends here in Philly
Great food.  Fun place. Our server was a bit rude. We had to ask for bread and drink refills .  He paid us very little attention.

This place was not bad - the service was definitely struggling (there were only three other tables and we had to chase the waitress down). But, they did let me order off the lunch menu when it was clearly dinner time. The food was not terrible, the ribs were not the best. The wings and nachos were good I would definitely recommend them!! The mashed potatoes were excellent!  And the burgers were OK. Overall, the place was meh.
Great food and really friendly service. My wife and I are just moving to the area and I am pretty sure this place will be in heavy rotation.
The Original burger....that it is.  No frills good burger.  Have it their way or no way.  I respect that!  On my way to tasting the best burgers in the USA and beyond.

the food and service here is consistently fantastic! I got the garlic rice with sunny side up egg and pork sausage with cucumber salad on the side. It is divine and I can say its my favorite brunch spot and I've even been to Clinton Street. I also tried the chicken and waffles and that is also top notch. Chicken is tender and moist and the syrup they provide for the waffles knocks it out of the park. Would def recommend!

Literally the best pizza I have ever had. i would honestly fly to new York just for dinner here if it wasnt so cost prohibative. the owner (Patsy) is awsome and his wifes cannolis should be enjoyed with someone you love. I wish yelp had a 6th star to give this family run business.
Delicious sushi!!  I'm writing this after my first takeout order and am happy to report that the rolls were awesome.  I highly recommend the Washington Square Roll!

Best Japanese in the neighborhood. Not quite authentic (there's hardly any in this area) but the food is very tasty and the price is decent. i usually get beef negimaki or chicken katsu bento box, it comes with miso soup, salad, california roll,  gyoza and tempura. I can easily eat one order for two, sometimes three, meals.

The food and service were both excellent. I got the cabbage rolls and am already craving them again. If you check in on Yelp, you get a free shot of any flavor of their house-made infused vodkas. Also, when my group of 7 left, they gave all the women Russian cookies, the men newspapers, and everyone another shot of vodka. Great experience.

Umm...yes, yes, yes and more yes. We first ran into the owners of Emily when they co-opened Brooklyn Central in Park Slope. A few months of weekly (and sometimes daily) attendance followed, but we fell off the BC wagon during Hurricane Sandy (work was a bit hectic). Much to our sadness, when we returned, we discovered the owners had parted ways, and while we loved the food, much of what we enjoyed about BC was the atmosphere created by Emily as manager/hostess. Happily, the party's just moved a little uptown! Emily continues to serve most excellent pizza, and the cocktails aren't too shabby either! After our triumphal reunion with this fabulous food, we vowed to bring a group of friends with us...and we did! I'm happy to say they were all very pleased, too, and we are planning more trips to Emily. I could go through the list of pizzas and tell you about each one, but what a waste. If you've read this far, you hardly need to hear me go on even more. What I will say is that my partner and I have had, between us, 4 pizzas and our friends had 3 others, and no one said anything beyond variations of "yum" or "I want more."

This is a nice addition to the block. The space is beautiful, really nice open air, art on the walls for purchase. I love the green life throughout the shop. Really cool bathroom. Nice staff, even though are Australian ;) The coffee is great, nice selection of teas, sameies, snacks. Basically it's a nice spot to hang out and have a bevy. Double thumbs up, I'm a fan

Give these guys a TON of credit - walked in 90 minutes after they opened their doors for the first time ever and they already got their act together! Amazing service, food and a great vibe. What a welcome addition to Wayne. This is gonna be the new hot spot for sure. Meatballs were EXCELLENT and pizza was well cooked with delicious toppings. Waitress was bubbly and management was really on top of it all. Pleeeeease stay great! Hooked already.
I've bern going here for many years and I love the good. The people are nice too. The crust is firm and they use a coal oven. They also make good garlic bread

GREAT new restaurant in Cobble Hill! Great outside and inside decor - Cool gatstropub restaurant vibe with an amazing craft beer selection. Good place for everything- a date, meeting friends, even a family dinner (i was there with my hubby and baby). The owner, manager, hostess, and waitress were extremely warm and accommodated my pouty 15month old. They came over to make sure everything was okay multiple times-not in an annoying way; just a "is everything cool and can we do anything more for u way". We shared the pork belly and sweet corn fritters as an appetizer. Comes with a mango(?) jalepeno same that is not hot at all.  Weird sounding combo but very yummy. A perfect guy appetizer for your hungry date (who happened to be my husband , in this case!) . He had the chicken and waffle and liked it a lot. A little different from your typical soul food menu item- a bit crispier and maybe need some powdered sugar (?) for presentation. But still good.   I had the ugly duckling burger-needed the ketchup for a sauce addition. But was cooked to my medium well perfection and yummy. The chips were a hit with my son. Handmade thin potato chips with sea salt with sliced pickles on the side. Overall, a great addition to the neighborhood. Will definitely come back and have already recommended to fellow Brooklynite foodies.

Cold pizza? Wrong toppings? Order from here!  After a really long wait (1 1/4 hours vs 45 minutes I was told) they delivered the wrong pizza, charging us $5 more for toppings they didn't deliver. Skip it, they don't care, at all.
Pretty good and authentic Chinese food. I regularly order their spicy pot.
First time here for celebrating my mom's late birthday. The food was very good especially the steak !! Every taste is heaven :) !! Will come back again for sure   yum yum

Eh.. their burgers only come with 2 add ons that are 50 cents each.. the burger doesnt include lettuces, tomato and onion so you pretty much get a dry burger and are expected to be okay with that. Their breakfast food is awesome! But come on if you are selling burgers make a damn burger! Too expensive.

On july 19th I held a surprise wedding engagement dinner for my girlfriend. The staff at Mediterra was EXCELLENT and soo helpful in the whole process! They were able to provide us with a private room for our 35-40 guests, were extremely helpful in the decoration set-up, and even provided some staff members to help distract my girlfriend and throw her off from the surprise. We were supposed to have the room from 2-5 but they let us come in 2 hours early and helped set up, and since it started late let us have the room for almost an extra hour! I ordered the steak to eat and it was one of the best steaks I've had in a long time! The seafood pasta needed just a little bit more seasoning, but was still very good. Their wine selection was excellent, and service was awesome. I want to truly thank the staff members and Mediterra for playing a huge role in making one of the best days of my life a success!

Went here for the first time after reading some good reviews The burger was good not to big just right but the Peanut butter shake was outrageous I would say probably the best so far I would DEFENITELY be coming back almost forgot the fried pickles very very good

I have worked in the restaurant/hospitality industry for over 10 years, and am a frequent customer of Woodrow's. I have had nothing but great experiences at this bar. The food is always good, paint night is so much fun and the staff has always been genuinely hospitable to me and every other patron I have encountered. The waitstaff and owners know all their regulars' names and make a sincere effort to make sure all their guests are taken care of and have a good time. This is a great spot to watch a game, hang with coworkers or throw a private party (the downstairs room is amazing!). If you are grateful for the amazing, eclectic restaurant industry NYC has, and respectful of the hard working people that keep it running, you will love Woodrows too!
We met some friends for some oysters and sliders at happy hour but were asked to leave because we had a baby with us. It was 4 in the afternoon! Horrible customer service. Never going back.

Came in for dinner and the music.  Ribs were fantastic!!  The "Other orchestra" played great music.  It is pretty loud in the main dining area when the band plays.  There is room to dance if you have a partner.
Pho: the soup is too bland, not hot enough, the beef is too soft, overcooked. The beef balls have no taste, the tendons are too hard, not edible.

I like to come to this place often with my friends and family. There is a relaxed vibe and friendly environment. Good food and strong drinks make it special.The fried chicken basket and slushy infused cucumber whiskey drink is my favorite. So awesome and a must try;) The staff are very friendly.

If Tikaway Grill and Mamoun's had a drunk crazy night together, Pitaziki Mediterranean Grill would be their delicious offspring. Like Chipotle and Tikaway, you select a meat (or falafel) and choose wrap, pita, salad, or rice bowl. There is an excellent selection of toppings: baba ganouj (sp?), lettuce, red onions, eggplant, chick peas, and sauces (the tahini sauce is yummy). This place is run by the guys that used to run Aladdin Pizza in the same spot. They used to be an average pizza place. Good but nothing notable. After shutting down and reopening as Pitaziki Mediterranean Grill, they now offer something unique yet familiar, and it's fantastic. This is the kind of place you want to tell your friends about. Places like this make me glad that I live in New Haven.
great burritos, good price and the burritos are very filling...nice place to go if you enjoy mexican cuisine.
Beautiful Gem in Brooklyn, Long established but recently has stepped it up to another level. The decor is inviting food is amazing, classic french but  throws many surprises.  Will be back.
Made my co-worker sick from tuna at lunch. Decor is average, bathrooms were messy.

Had high hopes for this place after reading all the reviews.  First, my gf and I were greeted by an unpleasant, almost rude hostess.  Stone faced and pretty much snapped at us when asking indoor or outdoor seating.  Waitress was friendly, at least!  Omelet was mediocre with a side salad with stale looking lettuce, and my gf's croque madame was nowhere near how it's supposed to look and taste.  It came with an enormous/disproportionate size of bread!  Only thing somewhat ok is the Belgium waffle with berries.   Later I went home with stomach problems from the salad!!!   Horrible, will not go back!

Good donuts, sub-par breakfast. The coffee is average, the tea is Lipton. The scrambled eggs were flat and slightly browned. Bacon was over-cooked. Sausage links were decent, though the menu said patties. Service was adequate, though the waitress seemed distracted and there was a delivery through the front door.  Go to Bella's, The Pantry, or Lena's. Even Ikea has a better breakfast for the money. And you won't have to pay for parking. If you're in the area, do grab a square donut. That's what they're know for.

Been here a few times now. I have to say my favorite dish is the fried chicken with waffles and collard greens. The service is cool, wait time is always short. I will say I tend to go late afternoon and it's not really busy. I would recommend this place to a friend, enjoy:)

Seabra's Marisqueira is a Portuguese restaurant that has character. Every time I go, the food is consistently well cooked, well priced and very good. Traditional Portuguese cooking and steaks and seafood are cooked to perfection. It's a type of place where their own would be seen eating, if something doesn't come out right, words are said, corrections made. The servers are a little older but....sorry to say the Portuguese (mostly older generation) may be teensy bit ornery but so would anyone if you are undecided and fluctuate back and forth with indecision, if there is anything you don't about the menu or food, ask. The knowledgeable servers work hard and I'm always amazed at the tiny kitchen fulfilling several orders in a timely manner. You hear sizzling food as the cooks are cooking, chopping of the knives as they prepare food, the guys WORK and the plates that come out, makes you want to sneak a piece as the servers deliver to the guests... If you are asking if I would recommend this restaurant...100% yes!
Fantastic meal at a good price. Friendly staff. Great random find when staying at the nearby hotel.

This place is amazing. Great coffee and service. I loved my experience here. The atmosphere is super chill and soothing. The Hunter hotdog was to die for and they have a large variety of iced teas that will make you feel as if you are in heaven. I highly recommend the 90s candy flavor one. The staff is really helpful and sweet. Overall, I give this place an A++.
What a change, and not a good one.  Staff is practically invisible, spaghetti under cooked and watery meatballs. Would not eat in again.  Stick to take out pizza.

Very friendly atmosphere. Attentive wait staff as well. The chef just asked if i enjoyed my meal which i did. I ordered the turkey burger with fries combo meal. Fries My  were hand cut and not in chip shape as others mentioned guess i they listened  to the other yelp review. My  friend and I inquired about this place last night and since i was getting my car repaired around the corner, i stopped by. My only complaint would be the bun. It was kinda crumbly and fell apart a little as i ate. I dont like that. No other complaints though.

Good late night option in Tribeca.  They have cold press juice 24 7 which is impressive.  They have amazing friend chicken.  They cut down the late night menu in half but still gabby the classics minus the chicken tacos

After reading so many negative reviews, i had my radar up but my good friend made reservations for my birthday and since it was for a Monday evening i figured, whats the worst that could happen. Service: pretty friendly and relaxed. We were late for our reservation but they did not give us any problem. Our biggest issue was it appeared as though they were VERY understaffed. Our waiter was very nice but did not check on us and i had to look for him. Food:  good tasting. Nothing extraordinary but definitely not bland. The appetizers were amazing. I tried the skirt steak medium well with cilantro mash. steak was great. mash was okay. It was happy hour all night btw and you'd think they would be watered down but they had some delicious and strong drinks for the specials. Overall: It was only 4 of us and it appeared its the spot to go for your birthday. A bit over hyped but We didn't feel rushed and had a great time. I just may go again and just stick to the weekdays then.
One word amazing. I come every Sunday!
the lobster bisque is the best!! and if you like a mature crowd friday is reggae and mondays are soul open mic poetry

I like this place and I'll order from here again. The main selling point is how convenient it is. Its definitely not the best hoagies I've ever had, but they are super cheap and were willing to deliver my 11 dollar meal. The last two times I ordered I got the buffalo chicken cheesesteak that everyone is always commenting on. It was good, but I wish they put a little more filling into my sub. It would be great if they gave you an option to add toppings like lettuce or tomato. Also the bread was cold and a little stale. I like my subs hot and crispy. Besides that, I def recommend the crab fries! They are seasoned with old bay spice which makes them extra tasty. They give you a generous amount too.

One of my favorite restaurants in new haven. Located at the top of the omni hotel, the view is spectacular. I visited for dinner on a Tuesday night and it was fairly slow so we were seated right away. The waitress was lovely very warm and laid back. I had a filet.. Like buttah. Used a restaurant.com gift certificate which helped with the bill. The waitress welcomed it without fuss; she told us it's been great for attracting new diners. Parking is convenient down in the hotel garage. Overall, excellent food at a premium price.

This is my first yelp review, been using it for a year or so to always find a pretty good meal so I figured it's time to chip in.  I have been to hinge cafe 3 times now, the first two times for lunch and now yesterday for breakfast, and it has been great every time.  For breakfast I went with the Super Spicy Burrito, eggs, chorizo sausage, pa blank peppers, corn (and I went with no black beans), and I ordered a sesame seed bagel, which, after the burrito came out, I knew I wasn't gonna need.  It was excellent, though I wouldn't call it super spicy, it had it's punch.  Burrito was perfectly put together, big enough to need a fork and knife but held together very well.  Side of salsa and sour cream made for a fantastic breakfast.  Wife had the challah French toast Bananas Foster, and I will be getting it the next time we go for breakfast.  It was like a candy breakfast, just delicious.   Had the pulled pork sandwich for lunch previously, and although it could be on a stronger roll then the ciabatta, which didn't hold up well, I just pulled out my fork and finished it up that way.  Moist pork, nice taste to it, with some cheese, spinach, and roasted peppers.  Definitely worth a shot, and the French fries were excellent Will definitely be back many times, so many more interesting menu items to choose from.  And the price seems about right for the quality of food

Definitely  my favorite Indian restaurant. its pretty consistent and has a good selection of vegetarian and non veg options. I especially love their dosas and kathi rolls . Sambhar and sauces are delicious and have great samosas . Their mango lassi was awsome , would definitely visit again .

Awesome place! Saw a write-up in the local paper, and it's only a 5 minute drive from my house, so thought I would check it out. Not disappointed! The servers were very personable- shout outs to Sebastian and Judd. The focaccia bread that was brought to the table was fantastic. Our food was great as well- I had a southwest chicken wrap and the Mrs. had a chicken panini. Looking forward to going back to try out some of the more traditional Italian fare! Also, can't forget the delicious gelato that came with strawberry and a lemony biscotti which was a nice compliment to it. The presentation was also quite nice!
Everything you could want and more from a cafeteria style BBQ joint. I really enjoyed the pulled pork sandwich!

My boyfriend and I popped in here to enjoy a late lunch on a Friday afternoon while meandering around SOHO. At first glance we weren't too sure about this place as there was only one table sat. Since it was a chilly weekend, we chose to eat indoors next to the windowed doors. I ordered minestrone soup with the Insalata Mista, and my boyfriend ordered the Napolitano pizza. Both were really large and I don't recommend unless you split one or the other with another person. The waiters were a little slow after we mentioned we were in a little hurry. But I can give them the benefit of the doubt here as it was not busy. I would go back dinner if ever given the chance as it seems to have good menu items.

Put in time and effort choosing a place for Sunday brunch, but ended up disappointed: 1) Waitress seemed to be on edge or nervous which in and of itself would have been fine if it weren't for her short attitude with us after we ordered. The menu we were given listed Eggs Benedict with a side of potato hash but was served with a side of wilted, unappetizing greens. When we asked the waitress, she said the menu had changed that day due to a new chef but asked if we would like the potato hash. We said yes, and she went to tell the chef, returning moments later with a different menu and pointing out that this particular menu was different, and telling us that we could pay for a side of potato hash. Rude, poor service. 2) No coffee refills were offered 3) Cornflake French toast was not bad, but didn't come with a side like the other entrees. 4) French fries served with sandwich were undercooked and soft. Overall impression was that they were unprepared for Sunday brunch rush, but that is unacceptable for an established restaurant. Will not be returning.

Just went here for New Years and this place surprised me!  I have always been skeptical of catering halls because they have known to be very generic, with reheated food and bitter waiters who rather be celebrating then serving, but not here.  My family and I were worried about sharing our new years celebrations in such a public way, but the Staaten truly made it special. The price was right fro almost 7 hours of food, drinks, dancing and festivities.  The food was just right with a buffet cocktail hour ranging from fresh seafood to hot rissotto.  Then the sit down dinner with a choice of steak and lobster tail, cooked to you preference, veal and chicken.  The servers were friendly and the ambiance was just right for the perfect new years festivities!

Noooooooo!!!!!! I'm holding a MAJOR grudge!! Only three stars because the old place was worth a five star review! So upset they closed and moved.... Planned to meet my sister here (as we always have over the past few years as a go to place). I ended up being early and very confused because I had no clue they closed and moved and reopened in a few months time. I know, I know, if I like this place so much how did I not know they closed up? I haven't been around since the winter and needed my fix only to be devastated!  Anyway, the new place was..well..new. I sat at the bar waiting for my sister and I was asking the bartender what the hell happened. She told me they had to close because the building got sold or something. They lost a lot of their bartenders/staff because of the move. This is the WORST part!!!! Nooooooooooooo. Where is that awesome Irish bartender with the long hair that always remembered you???? He looked like a sexy Jesus! Where the hell did he go??? Seriously, if you know, message me because he was one of the reasons we (my sister and I) loved this place so much. The food is the same, thank god because the food was always great!  To be honest I probably won't be back, I'll be searching for my bartender friend. On a side note, I saw him about a year ago near the west 4th subway stop and he waved and asked how I was doing. He knew exactly who I was, that's how great this place was. Oh well, my search continues for a comfortable pub with dim lighting, good food/beer and a one of a kind bartender!!!

I have been to scarpetta thrice now and the restaurant consistently keeps getting worse.   The trouble tonight started by the host arguing with me that my opentable reservation was for 8:00 when we checked in at 8:30.  He told me that it was originally at 8:30 but got moved to 8:00 day of. He seemed to get nicer after I insisted on showing him the opentable confirmation email stating 8:30. The service was quite slow and while I understand that being the case for the entrees given how full the place was, even getting our water seemed to take quite some time. And finally the food, rather bland and underwhelming.  We got the spaghetti and a calamari and vegetable dish to start.  The veggies were quite tasty but I cannot say the same about the spaghetti.  Now this spaghetti's sauce has been the golden standard in my kitchen ever since Anthony Bourdain prepared Scott Contant's recipe on one of his television shows. The sauce you get at scarpetta now is a phantom of that glorious sauce: you might as well make it home yourself. Others: - the cavitelli was okay and the lamb neck although was barely there, it was flavorful. - dinner mate barely touched her steak as it "just did not taste good" - the bass was blan - as for desserts, the olive oil cake was so incredibly tasteless and lacking in that richness one seeks I. Such a cake.  The salted caramel gelato accompanying the chocolate cake was so intensely salted that it was unpleasant to eat. In short, service is terrible and slow and the food is bland and underwhelming.  Find another fine Italian establishment which would be more worthy of your hard-earned monies.

I like Lincoln Station a lot. I spend a lot of money there. They see me often. It's near the train, the Brooklyn Museum, and the Botanical Gardens. Great place to have a meeting, do work, eat brunch, grab a snack, have dinner, get takeout. LS serves so many purposes and is an all around great joint. Here are things I love about it (reasons for the 4 stars): 1. The braised kale sandwich. Where the hell else are you going to get a sandwich filled to the gills with kale? That's right. Nowhere. And with the fava bean spread and focaccia this is perhaps the best sandwich I've ever had. 2. Iced Americanos. Perfection every time. 3. $3 Beer. 4. Computer users have to sit at the communal table. And I do so for some of my own work. There are plugs at each seat and coat hooks under the table. Keeps home-workers away from choice window seating. Totally logical. 5. Lots of veggie salad options. The fact is there are just too few cafes that have non-bread-based options. I'm not vegan, not even gluten-free, but I like to get in my 4-6 servings of veggies a day and don't always like to cook. These are great for a snack or a meal. 6. Friendly register people. 7. The soups are bangin'. And to keep it real here are a few criticisms in case the owners/managers read all of the reviews (why it is not 5 stars): 1. French fries are over-cooked. Lighten up dudes! Fries don't gotta be so crispy. Also please cut them a little bigger. 2. Bfast sandwich is good but could use some tweaking/is sometimes too greasy. Maybe add something crunchy like lettuce or tomato. Lighten up on what seems to be mayonnaise-based red sauce. 3. Fried chicken usually too salty/has been brined too long--this is also the case with the chicken at the sister restaurant, Bar Corvo. Brining is good, but not to be overdone. I love salt, so if something is too salty, then it really is too salty. To be fair, I've had some great fried chicken here. It's just hit or miss with the salt thing. 4. Cookies can be too hard. Make softer cookies! 5. Wifi can be spotty.

Great Sunday brunch!  The selection is extensive, the Western omelette and Corned Beef Hash were great, the apple turnover was fresh and they have fruit for dessert.  Three people with coffee and coke was about 33 bucks and worth every penny!
The combo of my sandwich with basil and his special spices was so simple yet so delicious! Wish I could try them all.
My favorite bagels ever! Just like NY bagels and they are always the perfect consistency and taste. A toasted egg bagel with scallion cream cheese is the way to go!
We loved this small restaurant right next to Broadway. Around 100$ for a couple with a main course and a glas of wine, cheap and delicious.
Had a fantastic bowl of Ramen here last night. My only complaint was that the portion was slightly too small; I wish I had ordered more chashu.

Love this place! This is my second time coming to Wayback in a while and I was blown away by the change in service and the quality of the food. The burgers never seise to impress. With a wide range of choices on the menu Jakes Wayback is the place to go for a great meal. Prices may seem a little steep for a burger but the quality pays off.

Thai-licious. We started our epic thai meal with the Papaya Salad and BBQ beef. The papaya was super fresh, a little heavy on the peanuts for my liking but overall a good. The beef was excellent, the mint is a nice touch. Since I'm a sucker for thai noodle dishes our next course was all noodle. We went with the Drunken noodle, which was good but not as good as the Northern Style Curry noodles. I think this dish made our meal. Our gluttony continued with Soft Shell crabs and an order of the Fried Fish with basil sauce. Nothing beats an entire fish, head included, delivered to your table! Everyone knows how reliable and great the food is here. But the service just isn't up to par. It's a little off putting the disinterest the wait staff has. Like others, it's not enough to keep me away though.

We didn't actually get to eat here, but I thought our experience might be useful to others. We arrived at 6:30 on a Monday night and although only one table was occupied (we didn't know there were additional tables in the garden), we were told we'd have to wait or eat at the bar. I pointed out that the place was practically empty, and was told the other tables had reservations later. How much later? Around eight o'clock. We promised we would be finished before then, so finally the hoity-toity hostess showed us to a tiny table crammed against the wall next to the bathrooms. She told us it would be quiet there. Except for the toilets flushing, I suppose. Anyway, when I opened the menu and saw the prices I told my wife there was no way we're going to pay $11-$18 for hummus and $15-$18 for "small plates," and so forth, while I'm sitting in a dark corridor by the bathrooms. We left. Fortunately there are many good restaurants on this stretch of Amsterdam, and we found a place that wanted our business only two doors down.

Awesome new place around the neighborhood. Great ambiance and awesome hostesses. I love that there's no need to ask for water. They provide you with your own jug. Lol. I love water. Overall a great clean restaurant. New favorite spot in my neighborhood.

If I had to eat one pizza for the rest of my life, it would be a Di Fara square pepperoni slice.The ingredients work in concert to form the best pizza I have ever had. It has a crispy crust with a soft airy center. The sauce is well balance and loaded with cheese. Topping it with basil and flavorful pepperoni takes it to another level. The complimentary red peppers added a nice kick. Definitely one of the best things I ate in NYC. The wait the pizza is long. I came in on a Thursday afternoon and still waited about 1.5 hours. There is only one man making the pizza and there's only one oven. The wait is worth it though. I prefer the square pizza a lot over the slice. I recommend calling in your order or having a free afternoon because of the wait. The place is also small with only a couple of tables and there is no AC.
favorite pizza in new york hands down. Nothing else comes close
GREAT!
Best pizza ever

I came here for breakfast on a few occasions. The pancakes are absolutely MARVELOUS here. The omelettes are to die for as well. One downside: There is always a line when I go here, so waiting is required. I guess everybody wants to eat the best pancakes in the world!

Sadly 3.5 stars is not an option, but that's exactly how I would rate the food here. Given the small menu, you get the impression that what they do, they do exceptionally well.. However I found my meal to be a little under-whelming. While the beef pho had good quality meat, I just wished there would be more of it (esp for the price). Noodles were perfectly cooked but the broth was way too sweet for my taste. Mango salad and raw apps were very well prepared... But if you're only going to offer one dessert I suggest it be something a little more memorable and not one I could easily replicate at home. Nevertheless, I'll probably be back to try the few dishes I missed.

Ordered from Fuel for the first time tonight, and I was very pleased! I wasn't expecting the food to be as fresh and delicious as it was, especially for being healthy. This is now my "go to" delivery place. Cant wait to try more of their menu, especially the smoothies!

I am very shocked at the reviews of this restaurant. I was extremely happy with my visit here. I ate here on a Thursday night with a girlfriend of mine. We were seated immediately in the bar section right by the windows which was great because it was a beautiful cool night. The restaurant is clean and has a nice interior. The bar area was pretty packed and they had live music. I personally liked the music it was a lot of 90s grungish cover. The crowd unfortunately left a lot to be desired. A lot of gawking men and several loud groups of women. The food was amazing though. we ordered the Spinach and artichoke dip appetizer - da bomb.  The drinks were awesome and strong (if you like that sort if thing) I personally tried the Vanilla Martini something.  I ordered the Pork chops and my friend ordered the Short ribs both came with a vegetable and potato.  All the food was well seasoned and had great presentation. Our service was from a younger waitress I thought she did a nice job.  Just attentive and friendly enough. No overkill or lack of attention. Price that's the only other downfall it's extremely expensive for NJ. Even know it is  South Orange. It's definitely a splurge meal.   Overall great food and interior. Pricy and slightly sketchy crowd.  Worth trying out.

Good value - decent food. But they never have enough sushi and rolls out on display. The plates on the buffet are constantly empty with people standing around waiting for more to be made. Maybe that's their ploy to give less and profit more but its very frustrating! Might never go back.

My husband and I were celebrating our wedding anniversary. When I mentioned this to Asha, Rizzuto's hostess, she showed us to a very private table near the windows. Asha was so friendly. She checked back with us numerous times during the meal to make sure we were pleased with the service and the food. The service was outstanding. Henry, our waiter, was at our beck and call. He anticipated our needs and was always there to check back with us. Leigh Ann, one of the waitresses, overheard me wonder aloud what appetizer to get. She suggested the tortellini. It was so delicious--succulent and spicy.  Ashley, another of the waitresses, overheard my dilemna about what to order for the main course. She recommended the sweet potato pasta. It was FABULOUS!  I usually leave food on my plate but I ate every bit of that pasta! Both waitresses were friendly and they seemed to smile all the time. John, the manager, stopped by our table several times to make sure all was well. He explained how my main entree was also his favorite. He was charming. Tyler also served us water. He has a wide, easy smile and made sure we had everything we needed. When we left,  Gianna escorted us to the door. What a memorable meal. It was outstanding and the service could not have been better. I highly recommend Rizzuto's in Blue Back Square.
Just came into town from boston for work, and found this gem next to my airbnb. The sandwich was pretty darn good the sesame bun was fresh, and the local beer worth trying (even for a work lunch) :)

The food is ok (absolutely nothing special, but not disgusting), but the problem is the really amateurish, rude waiters who ignore customers and just don't provide any level of service. Overall, very blah.

I have to give this place zero stars. By far the worst dining experience I've ever had. I went in for lunch this week and was greeted by the most pretentious hostess and was beyond rude to us. Once we were sat, our server took forever to even greet us and we still hadn't gotten menus. After we ordered we did not see our server till he came to check on our food which took about 40 minutes. The server told us that our order was stuck behind a larger party, which is no excuse to me. I expected a manager to come to speak to us but never did. The food is severely overpriced ($18 for 3 shrimp!!!) and our experience was not worth it. I would not recommend this place to anyone and definitely never go back here.

This place is owned by terrible management. I order from here very frequently, despite the fact that 30% of the time the kale in the salad is practically rotten. There aren't too many vegetarian options in the area and so I liked supporting it anyway. FORGET THAT! Today, I ordered a salad with spinach and kale chips. My delivery comes and it's a salad with tofu, no spinach, and I'm allergic to soy. Also, no kale chips!! No problem. I'm a reasonable person. I call them to inform them of this. The woman says they will send out another salad and the kale chips. When the delivery guy gets to our office, he did not bring his ID and was not able to come to my floor. This is an inconvenience as I'm in the middle of a call with a client but I run downstairs so that he doesn't have to wait. I did not remember to bring back the other salad with ingredients that I am ALLERGIC to. I apologized for forgetting and the deliveryman said it's ok. Sure enough, the manager calls me 20 minutes later to inform me that they will be charging me for that additional salad. This is terrible, terrible business practice. I tell her I am a loyal customer and order all the time. She said, "I know that", so clearly it doesn't matter? There are plenty of other places I can order from with nice people, good management, and fresh kale. That's the last time I order from this place now that I know the unfriendly, enterprising management that's behind it.

The pork belly buns are great. It goes down hill from there. First, they do not take reservations. The wait can be up to 3 hours. Is it worth it? Probably not. Momofuku and Gonzo in Brooklyn have better ramen. They do not let you take home leftovers, the hostess is impatient (can't blame her...she deals with angry mobs all evening) the wait staff is sometimes great, sometimes super slow. I have eaten there many, many times and it just isn't worth it anymore. I think maybe their ramen recipe changed...
great place but long wait... worth waiting for!
the broth man, the broth

Overhyped is one word for this restaurant. Usually a long wait to get in -not sure it is worth the wait. You could go much better elsewhere. Also, the service was below par. I would say refrain and stay away from the hype.

The food at Jeepney was actually delicious however I have never had a more insulting or unprofessional dining experience in my life.  The manager of the restaurant is beyond rude.  We had a reservation for 10 and upped it to 12.  Which they were happy to do.  When we tried adding one more person they changed the price from $700 to $1,160.  First we tried cancelling the reservation with more than 24 hours from the time of our reservation but they still were charging us the cancellation fee which is not what their policy says. Since the cancellation fee was so high we decided to still go and asked one of our friends not to attend dinner.  12 of us came to dinner and one friend showed up once the food was done to have a drink with us.  The manager tried charging us $1,600!!!! When trying to discuss with him how this is not what we agreed upon he was extremely argumentative.  We had emails from him stating $1,160 if it was 13 and tried showing these to him and he did not care.  We had to discuss with him for over 20 minutes and completely ruined my friend's bday celebration.  I worked in the restaurant industry for 8 years and I have never seen such poor customer service in my life!  None of us will ever go back to any of their restaurants after this experience.  My one friend is Filipino and actually a regular at the restaurant.  The manager should be fired!!
the atmosphere is nice! the waitress was distance but not freindly! the food and drinks are good. i can reccommend
Right under the bridge! Line out the door, but we (3) were seated within 20 minutes. Pizza was fantastic and very reasonably priced.

I don't understand the hype.  A sub-par Cheese Steak, at best.  my son and I had better Cheese Steaks at two other restaurants while in Philly.  It may be worth a try to rate for yourself.......I believe many people will not be back a second time.

You have to be patient, because you will wait for your food quite a long time. But once the food is there, you know it was worth waiting for! And the atmosphere of the place is unique and the ladies who cook the food absolutely lovely!!! Thank you, we had great time and we definitely will be back.
this place is very classy! i absoultely reccommend. a date night or just happy hour with freinds. (martini's) the food is great. i will be back

I was in New Jersey for one night on a quick work trip.  If you are staying at the Hampton property it is a great place to spend an hour or so for dinner.  They have a great happy hour here from 3 pm - 6 pm.  Half off drinks, appetizers, and sushi.  If you are coming just for the drinks, they have 3 TV's on each side of the bar so you could catch a late afternoon baseball game here and be perfectly happy ;) I showed up just in time to miss the happy hour deal, but settled in at the bar anyway. The bartender was quick to wait on me.  Within 5 minutes I had my Guinness and was ordering my meal.  I decided to order sushi and it ended up being a good choice.  I went with the spicy tuna roll and the white tuna nigiri.  It was a good meal.  The only reason I went with 4 stars is because I felt the prices were a bit higher than necessary, but the atmosphere was pretty nice so I wouldn't feel bad about coming here again on another visit to the area. Thanks to yelp I was able to get a free vanilla cheesecake desert for checking in.  It was almost like fried ice cream only the cheesecake was fried and the ice cream was on the side.  It was very good and best of all, FREE!
Bad food for a high price - choose another place! There are plenty of other restaurants along the street...
Excellent food, environment and music/video.

Hands down, my favorite bar! The complaint often received at most microbreweries is that the beer is solid but the food leaves something to be desired...not here! I have tried countless items on their menu (my favorites being the hickory burger, mac & cheese and cheddar chicken sandwich) and plan on continuing to sample other offerings. The variety of beers range from English Pale Ales to IPA's, Pilsners, Wheat Lagers and well, the list goes on and on. I have been a proud member of the Mug Club since 2012 and will bear the lack of parking at least once or twice a week to get my fix with some work friends who share my love for this "cheers" of sorts. To top it off, the Brew Ha-Ha Comedy Club provides some amazing acts that I only wish I could have seen more of in recent years. This downtown Hartford staple has consistently attentive service and the atmosphere pays homage to Hartford's history utilizing the beautiful design of the Cheney Building with tables on multiple levels. Strongly recommended!
nice décor and environment.... good concept too. but the food wasn't super

My favorite place ever. Great staff, family owned italian place.  Literally the best margarita pizza i've ever had. Lived in fairmount for 3 years, and had their margarita pizza most fridays...it will never get old. I dont know what it is about their sauce, it's just perfectly sweet and the right amount. YUM. Also great cheesesteak and fries.  Delicious sicilian and tomato pie. ALSO they have THE BEST thick crust square pizza. to die for.  I can't emphasize enough how much we love Luigi's Pizza fresca.

Really disappointed on the food and service. The famed beef wonton noodle soup was nothing to write home about and moreover, the staff was the opposite of charming. Not speaking a lick of understandable English makes the ordering process a nightmare and  frustrating, not what you look for in dining out. Having a little dialog with your waiter is sorta important; gotta be able to order ya know. These glum faced servers looked unhappy to be at work. Little Italy is right across Canal Street. Go there. This was poor.

I came here for a quick lunch during the work day and the buffet set up was perfect.  I also got a side of steamed pork dumplings which were super tasty.  The food is reasonable priced and definitely authentic.  I would recommend this place to anyone looking for a quick and tasty Korean lunch fix.

Recently went to Sunday brunch here with a large large group.  OUr server was excellent and very attentive for such a large crowd, food was delicious and there was a great atmosphere.  He was also very patient with us, which I appreciated a lot.  Looking forward to taking my group back there again sometime soon.

Best Italian food in NYC in the best neighborhood in NYC.  Reasonably priced, good service, and a great ambiance.  Only negative is that they don't take reservations and sometimes it requires some patience to get a table.

Our experience at Bank & Bourbon was perfect! We had a reservation for 8pm on a Monday evening and were seated immediately at a table with a street view (great for people watching). It's a large space and the decor is very stylish - classy, yet comfortable. It's a place that you can dress up for a nice date, but there were also families from the hotel there in casual attire and didn't seem out of place. The service was excellent; the staff is very knowledgeable and attentive. Our drinks were never empty! For starters we had the fois gras-chicken liver parfait with brioche toast and cherries (amazing, and so rich) and the beef short ribs were cooked perfectly. My husband had the custom Knob Creek to drink and I had an Overnighter, which was delicious. Our entrees were impressive: I had the lamb plate with lamb loin cooked to perfection, crispy lamb belly that melts in your mouth, and house made lamb sausage. My husband had the 8 oz steak (again, perfectly cooked) and parmesan rosemary fries which were tasty but I personally found them a little too salty. We were each given a free glass of champagne in honor of our anniversary, and for dessert we had the German chocolate cake and the cream-filled donut holes, which were both delightful. Our experience was really wonderful from start to finish, and we will definitely be back!

I have had several meals at Fogo de Chao with consistent results. Carnivores paradise, with an extensive winelist. The salad bar presents a deep variety of salads, vegetables and charcuterie, but focus for most is the variety of roasted meats. Like most, my favorite is the picanha, it is sirloin steak prepared in such a way that it shines when compared to the ribeye or filet. Not a fan of the 'garlic lamb' or 'garlic filet' - although I love garlic, these are over the top, i could not taste anything for a half hour or more after eating these. Great for a group.

I came in looking for seco de rez but they only serve that as a special dish on the weekends so I went for the combo with my family.  We were not disappointed. Quite the opposite, we were very satisfied. I agree with everyone pio pio has nothing on this place. I stopped going there years ago.

I love Denino's.   Don't expect fancy bright decor, it's a basic old school joint packed with people who enjoy great pizza. I've visited the place over a dozen times so far and have always left more than satisfied.   We visit the place with co-workers during lunch time to celebrate other employee's birthdays.  I love the thin crust and the ton of stuff on the garbage pie.  Fried calamari is the best I've had to date; nothing chewy, just melts in your mouth. I've taken my parent's and family there on occasions too.  They enjoyed themselves always leaving stuffed. I recommend this place. They should accept credit cards! Who carries cash around these days.

My quest for the best cheesesteak is officially over now. This place here is hell!! The meat they put on your cheesesteak is outrageous!! I needed a fork to help me eat it. The flavor was there and everything is on point. I've found out something. North Philly and South Philly has a different variation. South Philly is on the cheez whiz kick and North Philly isn't on that as they like to give you the choice of real cheese on your sandwich. I'll head back over here before I leave to go back home. After eating this, I don't even want anybody else's cheesesteak, REAL TALK!!! This is MY SPOT now!!!
Excellent food!! My husband and I came after reading reviews from fellow yelpers. Everything is clearly made fresh at the restaurant and the portions are very large. Worth the money!
Only my second time but again my food is almost cold. I'd rather let my food cool than get a close to warm dish

So a local friend from New York highly recommended me to this place and he told me their stories, like from a small food truck to now more than one across the streets. It was actually amazing to see how long the line is even past midnight on a weekday, that tells something for sure. The portion was big and I like the barbecue sauce a lot. We just ordered the classic rice bowl with mixing meats. They are really tasty, however, I don't think I would go back to there just for having this. It was good to try once, but I could not imagine eating it every single day. The owners are passionate, loving what they are serving to people and I appreciate that a lot as you can sense it in the food. I believe some people will love it so much but I am still not there yet.
so legit. just go get it, don't ask questions

I had to try the declared "Best Sandwich in America".  The Roast Pork was very good but not the best I've ever had. We attempted to get a sandwich late in the afternoon but the line was way too long.  I went back early the next day and was able to get a seat at the counter.  I thoroughly enjoyed the sandwich and would order again.
Awesome food and service, Marigold was our server and she was great! The food was amazing and fast!

Been here many times. My husband threw me an amazing bday party here as well. Great food and excellent service. Wish I could eat here everyday! Favorite items are the Brussel sprouts and warm eggplant. Super vegetarian friendly but great for meat eaters as well
Always a great meal and good drinks. Staff is nice and the prices are good. The spicy chicken is an absolute must! This place has become a regular for us even though we don't live that close.

I love the VPB. I always order the pulled pork pie and sweet potato fries. I'm finding less and less items I can eat now that I've been relegated to the gluten free penalty box. I'm assuming the fries are off limits for me (but I've never asked actually. The issue would be the fryer and being fried with non-gluten-free items in case people are wondering.) I have had the pulled pork since my diagnosis, and haven't had any ill effects (though I have since found out I can't have vinegar either. Sometimes you just don't realize what you can and can't have when the diet is a new thing to you.) However, regardless of my restrictions, I love the food.I love the onion rings and the calamari. The only dish I've ever had there that I didn't like was the meatloaf, and that was because it had onions and some other veggie chunks. I personally like a smooth meatloaf. I don't drink beer, but I do love the blackberry seltzer. All of the seltzers are delicious, and one of my favorite drinks is their seltzer with vodka on the rocks. So good!

Any person or persons who do not like Nurenberg must evaluate their life or lives. From 2 independent German nationals, they've complemented this food as the best outside of Germany. One man was 85 years old. He was finally satisfied. I have yet to order anything off the menu that I disliked. The all German Beer taps are fresh and delicious with many beers by the bottle. The staff are VERY knowledgeable about the beer and food available. Don't know what to get? Get the Muscles. Get the Jagerschnitzle. Get any desert. You will NOT be sorry. Been going here for 4 years and I never leave unhappy. Cozy and welcoming. Simply delicious.

The steak was ok, but the slightly cooked, under-seasoned onions really kill the joy. I've had vastly better cheesesteaks in South Jersey, but I'm sure Philly has lots of good ones, too. Also, I find the "speak English" bigotry at the window to be pretty annoying. It's just not friendly and is pretty offensive to the masses of non-English-speaking tourists who come here.

Went here for the boyfriend's birthday dinner on a recommendation from a friend. The layout is cozy and though we were originally put in a high traffic spot, our server moved us to a more private table by request. We got guacamole and mole sauce along with our salsa and chips to start out. The chips tasted a little stale and the guac was just average but I really enjoyed the salsa and the mole sauce was some of the best I've ever had: creamy and sweet! For entrees I got the vegetarian enchiladas and my boyfriend got enchiladas in mole sauce. I am vegetarian and he has a gluten allergy: the menu was accommodating for both dietary restrictions and our server was helpful. My vegetarian enchiladas were fine and the green sauce they came in was delicious. The enchiladas in mole sauce were to die for! We also got two margaritas that were tasty, generous, and very authentic. This spot is expensive, $46 for two of us without dessert, but a good dining experience. Great service and good food but not fantastic enough for the the price.
Just had lunch here for the first time. Amazing sandwiches, great prices, friendly staff and fun atmosphere. All around great experience. Can't wait to come back!

After having eaten here several times and meeting the owners, I really want Beehive Oven to succeed.  The owners seem like good people .... BUT..... the restaurant has a few issues.  First of all the location s*cks.  It may not be there fault (do to budget etc.) but THAT corner, in THAT building...it has a really negative vibe.  Could go into more detail here but I'll refrain.  They are trying to spruce it up but ultimately the location has a lot to be desired.  As far as the food.  Its good.  Its decent.  But one cant help comparing it to Pie's & Thigh's 2 blocks over.  My take is that they (Beehive) shouldn't have to tried to do the fancy/southern food thing.  Williamsburg has tons (too many) nice, fine dining, fusion establishments already.  If people want that there are plenty of places to go.  But if they want good ole fashioned southern food, home cooking (however you categorize it) there are very few options.  So therefore they (Beehive) should STICK TO THAT!  Don't try to make if fancy, just DO IT RIGHT!  Keep it simple.  That's why Pie's & Thigh's is so successful because they serve up what its meant to be.  Not something that's obviously trying too hard to be a new and contemporary take on southern fare etc.  Btw, the biscuits are kinda small. And like I mentioned before, the entrees are trying way too hard to be something different.  Also they don't transfer well into a takeout meal.  Did that once and it was a cold mess.  As far as atmosphere, its a little bright (at night) for my taste.  And the hours are posted outside the door in front but they don't seem to be accurate...or at least not yet.  ANYWAY, I feel bad for writing a lot of this because I like them and I want them to succeed.  I just figured I should be honest and hope that it helps them in the long run.

Every night we walk by Vite and we see how packed it is. We finally decided to try it out. It did not disappoint! We had the pork sausages and mozzarella appetizers, and the lamb ragu with pasta. All the dishes were delicious, but the lamb ragu stole the show. Not only was the sauce rich and flavorful, but the lamb was so tender that it melted in our mouths. Also, you could tell that the pasta was made in house and not from a box. I took advantage of their happy hour drink special, which were mojitos, and I was so glad I did because they were amazing.

Wow this is one of my new favorite spots now!...Outstanding. Great ambiance! This is THE BEST Italian dining in Astoria now !!... I felt like I was actually in Italy! The servers were all very nice, the owners speak in Italians, service was fantastic and I loved how laid back they were, never once felt pressure to pay the bill and leave. The place is small, but very busy, which it's okay to wait a little bit, (coz the crowd is really cool ) as the food was fantastic!..Very cool Bar/Crowd to ..!!..nice Prosecco !! All the pastas are cooked perfectly.Quality, old-school Italian! The seating is comfortable and the tables are not on top of each other. Great location, the vibe and atmosphere were amazing!. Worth checking it out. I definitely recommend Vite Vinosteria for a taste of real Italy. I would definitely come back and recommend this place to anyone looking for good food and great atmosphere  that doesn't get sticker shock. Tiramisu' Vite & Mousse di Popcorn with Brandy-sorbetto were out of this world !! I love the Bar ambience !...and their bartenders : very friendly and gorgeous !! Read this review on : "ASTORIA POST " Two former Cipriani employees open Italian restaurant in Astoria astoriapost.com/2014/07/…

So when I went  there I noticed the "cash only" sign, I was quite disappointed but the servers informed me that they will have they're Computer system running within the next week, so I let it slide. I couldn't even tell the place just opened, their were so many people and the ambiance was very perfectly rustic and cozy. We had polenta with mushrooms and goganzola cheese, it was so amazing, then the pasta with lamb meat was so tender and the pasta seemed super fresh. The servers were very personable and welcoming,they spoke to us like we were friends from way back in italy!!! It wasnt until later we found out they were the owners running everything themselves.  The food was good,the owners were cool, I hated the cash only thing but Besides that I would definitely return with more friends!!!

My boyfriend and I love this place. It's a little bit of a pain to get to but the food is so good. The people there are super friendly, especially the older lady. I'm pretty adventurous when I come here, but my favorites are the tortas (mexican sandwich), fish tacos, and burritos. While I'm waiting, I get to munch on some housemade tortilla chips. Recommended!
Came here for my birthday, was perfect!  The rodizio was scrumptious, the service was great!  Huge portions, and with the sangria to boot, we were feeling full and fine.

So delicious! Great service, great atmosphere, and good people. The food was excellent, margaritas were delicious and great quality. Highly recommend the vegetable burrito and chicken quesadilla. Guacamole and salsa excellent as well.

The salads are great here you build your own many options. Everything is super fresh and fast here. The line goes quickly in case your in a rush to get back to work. I get my lunch here all the time it's clean and it's new hopefully it stays that way.

My first thought was ... Urban Outfitters restaurant? Not. But the food won me over. Really innovative flavors, presented beautifully in a gorgeous space. Loved the open kitchen and we watched the staff like a performance. I went with 3 other friends and we tried a bunch of things. Bacon wrapped matzoh balls, GLT sandwich, Pea salad (my favorite) and sweet breads coated in falafel (amazing). The chewy carrots were outstanding, so was the Banh Mi Poutine. We also loved the upstairs roof bar- so chill. On the negative, not quite up to speed on the service but they just opened. I will def go back.

I'm disappointed. Nice atmosphere, and much anticipation waiting for this spot to open. Unfortunately, the $17 Porgy was a letdown. Small portion, definitely needed a side to accompany the tiny fish on my plate - That, and it was a really unattractive cut of meat with a bloody vein at it's center. Then, there was the schnitzel. I mean, gravy or a nice jam would be the appropriate accompaniment, but instead - you get the 'claw.' I'm all for a bit of theatre with my dinner - but not when it replaces basic attention to dinner flavor detail. I don't like to hate, but this was not a great experience. That said, the service was AWESOME and so was the wine. I think there is still hope...but the kinks need attention.

OMGEEEEE!!!!  Finally, a Thai restaurant close by that I love!!!  The pad Thai was great and the side salad was a nice surprise!  Not expensive either.  Would recommend to anyone looking for authentic Thai food!

This review is for the coffee and pastry side store. The coffee and deserts are wonderful and I go here a couple times a week but I have not had the best quality service like I have had I the dining side. I have had coffee spilled on me and have witnessed altercations of rusts and service workers. Not good.

It was my first time coming here a week or two ago. I came inside I ordered a sausage pizza. I go to sit down on the little bar strip they have and there is leftover food sitting there. the waitress finally cleaned it up after she got off her phone. The pizza was so oily I had to wipe it off. Overall I was not impressed by this place.
Had a birthday dinner here and it was incredible. The staff was awesome and the food was fantastic.
Had dinner here for my wife on her birthday. Excellent food and very friendly service

Heres the thing, when it comes to food everyone will have their own taste & standard. I can that I have never been disappointed. But its more than just the food, parking is great, free wifi is a plus, & i live that they offer healthier alternatives for your sides instead of just french fries. They have great freshly brewed tea which is just not something is offered for this area. For someone who works in the area I always feel guiltless in having a healthy wholesome lunch instead of a typical slice or regular sandwich. Do wish they delivered that would be sweet!

had dinner here the other night and so glad we did! the food was very tasty and fresh. for an entree we had the panang curry with beef- it was perfection! the decor is super unique and when you sit down you do not feel like you are in nyc! only complaints- the girls in the front are unorganized- we were quoted 30 mins for a table so we went to a near by bar for drinks. after we got our drinks (probably 5 mins after having left the restaurant) we got a call that our table was ready. Basically we had to down our drinks and head over. Also, i got  the UPtini- infused vodka with basil and lemongrass. When the martini arrived it was already a little bit warm, so within 15 minutes it was room temperature and very hard to drink- it was basically straight vodka! It should have been ice cold when it came to the table. But- those issues are only minor and i will def be going back!!

Yelp let me down.  I don't understand how this place has 4 stars,  and with so many reviews. There were some good things to mention, for example, the water had ice in it.  The chefs were also visible cooking, and also, real live Japanese staff!  Sugoi!  They could even be heard speaking to each other in their native language.  Fascinating. Anyway, the basic yakitori was alright.  Also ordered the hotate (scallops) which was pretty sad.  Not much else to say.  Won't be going back.  Makes me question other totto restaurants as well...

It's a dollar slice, and its good.  Service is fast and there is a philanthropic component to the business, what more can you want?  I saw some complaints on Yelp about this and that, look if you are looking for a slice that satisfies your wallet, your tastebuds and your soul, this is the place.  It is just that simple.

Since this place was introduced in the Dining Section of recent New York Times, I stopped by yesterday to buy take-home fresh pasta.  The fun part to try different kind of pasta is to learn about it and cook with suggested sauce.  I bought Reginette, Squid Ink Sitrozzapreti and Saffron Shell Pasta.  They didn't have box with the information of each pasta ready (they did but all of them were wet on the counter) and put all of them in a box with the information of Paccheri.  I asked for the information for each pasta, knowing the cooking time for each pasta was different.  Well, everyone of them, including three male managers who came later was quite incompetent and one girl told me the cooking time for every pasta was the same, reading the level of Paccheri, which I didn't buy.  When I still asked for the information of each past, one manager told me he just placed the order for the level.  Hello!  I cannot wait for the level delivered.  During these  conversation, NO one apologized.  So, I took the wet box with the information, paid and left.  I haven[t cooked the pasta yet. I hope they are good.  If you go there, be ready to deal with these extremely unqualified salespeople.

I ordered from here for the first time after reading some of the amazing reviews. I decided to get the chicken wing platter with candied yams, macaroni and cheese and macaroni salad lol one of them nights. I decided to get delivery and I'm only about 7 mins away so shouldn't take too long...after about an hour I decided to call them, they said the order was sent out. After another half hour a man finally arrived to my home. He was very polite and apologized for the wait. Upon inspection everything looked great, except my macaroni salad. It had an odor like something wasn't right. I can't put my finger on it but it did not smell fresh, AT ALL. Everything else was OK nothing mind blowing. Mac and cheese was bland I would've swapped for anything else. Now the cornbread was AMAZING, next to warm daddy's and relish some of the best cornbread I've ever had. Sweet and moist, taste like cake. Overall, ok spot nothing more

I work a lot with the food industry and have  had the opportunity to interview some of the top American chefs (Batali, Carmellini, Bobby Flay and many others) and I've filmed in some of the top restaurants  in the USA. The one thing I've learnt through my experience is that the two key ingredients for a GREAT restaurant are great food (obvious) and great service. If one is missing it  doesn't matter how good the other is, the restaurant should not be in business. Which brings me to St Anselm. Yes, it has very good food (not mind blowing) but due to the reasonable prices for NY it is extremely popular... BUT when it comes to service I don't think the staff at this establishment even know how to spell the word "service", never mind understand what it means and how important it is. This was my second time there, although this time I didn't even get the opportunity to to be seated after an hour and half wait. I understand this establishment has long wait times and that wasn't the issue; it was how the staff managed the situation and how I was treated during that time.  I could go into a longer description of how awful my experience was but instead I'll simply say this to the staff at St Anselm: You work at a busy restaurant with long wait times. Understand that if you actually try and make the wait time pleasant rather than being rude, obnoxious and downright mean, it would make everyone's experience at your restaurant so much better. Your people skills leave a lot to be desired and maybe you should consider another profession, preferably not nursing. To the management: please send your staff for proper training and understand that the only reason your restaurant exists is because of the patrons, so treat them with the respect they deserve.
I like this place. Laid back atmosphere, good cocktails and the food is good too. It's my first time here and I will come back.

Had brunch reservations for my cousin's birthday. I was really looking forward to coming here. The food was delicious as I expected, but if you're looking for mom's traditional home cooking, then you're better off going home to visit mom. We enjoyed our experience and the staff was super friendly and knowledgeable. I would definitely recommend coming here to experience what they have to offer!

Came here for only one time on a sudden night and fell in love with this place because of its goodness and faster job for me they have done. They impressd me with careful, fresh and attentive service. They have plenty but I took only a dish of meat which was tasty enough to come for that in future
Gorgeous ambiance, delicious food, and exceptional service. This place truly has it all. I'm coming back with my wife this weekend!

Went for happy hour and dinner with friends on a Friday night. Wasn't too packed when we first showed up so we quickly got a seat. The one negative is that I wasn't told by the bartender that the happy hour only included wine on tap and not by the glass... But no big deal. The food was fantastic! Loved the deviled eggs and the bacon wrapped dates. Our server was fantastic! Very friendly and attentive- which unfortunately can be a rarity in the city especially on a Friday the more packed out a place gets. The manager came by to check on us and how satisfied we were with our meal. I will totally go back again!

I went to the Risotteria because of its gluten free options. I bought the black and white gluten free cookie and the orio cake.I was surprised the food was tightly packaged, probably to make sure it doesn't come in contact with other products. The cake was quite dry but works well with a glass of milk. I would not recommend it if you are looking for a gluten free pastery place but it's good enough for a quick snack in soho.

Went here for the first time yesterday. Good seafood and reasonable prices.  But it was the excellent customer service that really stood out! I will definitely be back when I  am in the area again.   Definitely try their cole slaw as one of your sides.  It is delish!

This place was perfection for one anything semi-intimate where you want good for, an aesthetically pleasing atmosphere, but no monetary or time commitment. Two hands was absolutely charming; a hidden gem in the streets near Little Italy. I ordered an almond milk cappuccino (out of curiosity) and my friend ordered an iced latte- both "for here." I know at a lot of these scene-y coffee shops, patrons are really interested in presentation. By this I mean, people tend to get very particular about the white foam caps on their "to go" cups and be very excited about coffee served in mason jars. There is no shame in this, and Two Hands really tailors to that interest. Everything looks like it is straight off of some very trendy person's Instagram... or at least that is how it appeared to me. The coffee was delicious; I am a huge coffee person, and I have sort of sipped my way across Manhattan in search of the best cup, and Two Hands is amongst the top few. The place was unique, too, which is one of its main draws. For one thing, the menu is interesting. Acai bowls are offered (although I can't really comment on these because I just had a chocolate croissant and a bite of my friend's avocado toast) and Young Coconuts are sliced open and punctured with straws, to be enjoyed on site. I thought it was all very refreshing, no pun intended. The avocado toast was somewhere above Little Collins/ Jack's Wife Freda, but below Cafe Gitane; regardless, it was yummy. Magazines like the New Yorker and Kinfolk are offered to patrons, hanging up invitingly on the beautiful, exposed-brick wall. I poked through Kinfolk while waiting for my sweet little drink to be brought to me. As I mentioned, the crowd is "scene-y" but nothing repulsive or overtly pretentious. All in all, this place harbors very good vibes, and serves excellent food. If you have the chance/are near by, I recommend trying it!
Great price and the eye can't behind the bar is amazing!  Stayed for karaoke but would have been better off if I did not!

Been here twice already. Tried the organic soup, masitas, pico de gallo, ropa vieja, lasagna, and ice cream -- everything was FANTASTIC. Service is phenomenal, fast and friendly. The perfect place for vegans, lactose intolerant, and/or people allergic to gluten. However, I took a non-vegan here and they were raving about the food. Reasonable prices for gourmet organic, non-gmo food. They make almost everything in-house. I also appreciate the transparency of the food they make -- the kitchen is open and right next to the dining area and they are very honest about all their ingredients and where they're sourced from. Their hours are a bit limited; I asked why that is and they said that they are still experimenting with the menu. Will be back here again and again.

I love grilled cheese. I've actually even thought about opening my own grilled cheese truck - don't worry whey station, not in ct! When I saw them in bushnell park I had to try them and they did not disappoint. I ordered the avo melt which was described as cheddar, bacon, I think chipotle mayo and truck made guacamole. Wow. Just wow.  It was a little greasy but that's going to happen when you have cheese and I'm sure butter on the bread. I think it was sourdough bread? I dunno it was just wonderful. And the cheese that got on the griddle and turned into heavenly cheese chips was a lovely addition. The sandwiches are a good size. I could have easily shared it but I had no one to share it with today so I nursed it for an hour because there was no way I was going to waste something that good. I'm sure I'll regret it later but it was so good I don't care right now! Definitely check these guys out!
Positives: Wow best pizza I've ever had in the whole wide world. Negatives: The staff can be total rude a-holes.

Night staff was friendly enough, but please avoid this place during the day!  You have been warned.  I get that this is an airport hotel restaurant.  I didn't have very high standards coming in or anything, but the service here is just terrible.  I sat down at a table and they promptly asked if i wanted anything to drink and i said just iced tea for now.  Which they brought.  They didn't check up on me again for maybe 30-45 minutes so i went up to the bar and put in an order for ceviche.  Maybe 15 minutes later someone finally came to my table to ask if i would like any food.  I told her I already put an order in for ceviche with one of the other servers.  Maybe another 10-15 minutes go by, and another server comes around and asks if he can take my order.  I tell him the same thing.  Finally, my server comes out to me with.... tomato soup... *womp womp*.  The waitstaff goes silent again and my bf goes to remind them that i am still waiting on my food.  And finally! I get my ceviche.  It came in a little martini glass with NO CHIPS...  What?  Am I supposed to eat ceviche with a spoon???  So i asked for chips or crackers, just something and he told me it would be an additional $5.  $5!!! Are you kidding me.  You shall get no more of my money!  Especially since not once did any of the three of them apologize for any of it--not the wait time, not the wrong order, nothing!  I mean, you are in the hospitality industry!  Be a little more hospitable!
Servers are a little slow but the music is always on point! The burger's my favorite and you can substitute the fries for a little kale salad! Bed-Stuy gem!
Was nice

It is an amazing place where you may find a wide range of cuisine. There are not only common cheese steaks but also French crepes, Vietnamese soups and a lot of sweets and fruits. After a trip, when you don't know what to eat, reading market is worth to visit. If is a magic spot with delicious plates, not so much expensive.

No doubt about it: ROIA would be my go-to spot if I lived in New Haven. The staff and space have charm to burn, and the food is dreamy: I started with a superlative chicken liver mousse topped with a thin layer of duck fat and red onion marmalade. Preparations this good at restaurants in my area are half the size and twice the price. Another favorite was the sensational tuna crudo with housemade potato chips. I'm feeling a little guilty that I didn't offer to share any bites of this particular dish with my dining companions. I'll be trying to duplicate the flavor combinations in the crudo at home, no question. Other highlights: a generously sized salad of perfectly fresh local lettuces and a beautiful burrata with fresh peas and mint. Others in my group ordered and loved: pappardelle with hen ragu, the eggplant entree, duck alla diavolo, and the burger & fries. I was so focused on my meal, and on making sure everyone tried the crazy-good chicken liver, that I didn't get too many details about the other dishes--but I know everyone walked out very, very happy with their choices and planning to squeeze in another visit before leaving town. Another note: if you like a well-curated bar, this is your place! The bar manager is friendly, knows her stuff, and was very thoughtful in helping with whiskey and wine selections. You won't be disappointed.

I ordered for delivery and boy was I disappointed! The pizza was cold and seemed old! I also ordered a Nutella cake and it was a whole bunch of scraps thrown together which I payed 6 dollars for! I had ordered from here before and was very happy! something must be going on, new management or something. Highly disappointed! I should of known not to order, my friend recently said he went there and got treated poorly! DONT ORDER HERE! If you want to have a good experience.

My husband and I were visiting New York from MA for a few days, and unfortunately decided to grab dinner at this restaurant. They market themselves as an Irish restaurant but they were far from it. They didn't even have the #1 Irish meal on the menu, shepherd's pie. Above our table was a speaker blasting the radio into our ears. Throughout the first 10 minutes of us sitting down, one of the staff members kept playing around with the stereo volume....up, down, up down, and so on. It was so annoying. When we got our food, the hamburger (ordered well done) was raw inside. I mean RED raw, it was disgusting. The cheese quesadillas were mediocre at best. The only good food were the onion rings. Then thank goodness I checked our bill because of our waitress had added another table's drinks to our tab. We ended up paying $70 for a meal that sucked. Would never recommend this place, ever.
The coffee is amazing, and the tea is really good, but not quite the same. Also, it's a great place for brunch. The flatbreads are probably the best brunch item in my opinion.

Best Chinese food ever. Great food and great service. Always packed with people. Salt-and-pepper shrimp is the best dish there. Make sure to go to location on pell St. Try the scallion pancake it was amazing

Hadn't been back in over a year and was disappointed by the quality of the food. Pretty bland. They've let the quality slip. And the place is extremely noisy. I'd rather pay the extra bucks and eat amazing pasta at Perla.
Wow. The Laura Pizza. The Fresco calzone. Amazing. Food is fresh and comes out quick.
