Really no reason to eat here. I give this place my lowest rating of any restaurant since moving to Glastonbury.
It's a little place but the flavors are HUGE!! Great place!

I went to Kafe Neo yesterday, and I was really disappointed with both the service and the food. Service wasn't good. The waitress came 5 mins after I sat and when I asked for couple more minutes, she returned 15 mins later. The pastry I ordered was too greasy , didn't even taste fresh and the coffee was average. My expectations for this place was higher, now I regret wasted my time and money there. I definitely won't go back.

The food is good.  My mother had a soft shell crab special.  Came with a side of mesclun salad, nothing more.  For $26, a bit stiff.  My mussels came as a plate, maybe 25 in all, with absolutely no side.  For $21 I'll never go again.  I'll head over to Bxl Zoute on 22nd btw 5/6 Ave, where I can have a whole pot of steaming mussels *and* a beer for less. The desserts were ok, but definitely not worth the price.  The tiramisu is all right, the toro is not super fresh but passable, but my baba au rhum was dry as a pound cake, a real disappointment!  Head over to Maison Kayser on broadway and 22nd, or to La Maison du Macaron on 23rd btw 6/7 Ave. All in all, it's wayy overpriced and touristy.  Moreover, you get to choose seafood but then no pasta (it's a different place within Eataly, and pizza is yet a different place, etc.).  They don't cross plates.  A bit limiting.  There's the Scuola where I guess you can have a mix of dishes (more like a restaurant, it's their culinary school).  I haven't tried, but after this experience, I'm not likely to.
there's a blonde who works here (bartender ) who could be the most attractive woman in America- food and beer is ok (she's that good)

The chef carlos Swepson has done it again with this Classic American menu . The food is really good and it's made fresh daily , these recepies are from carlos and his missippi family over the years . The bistro is small and quaint , the decor is modern and up to date so for all the hipsters this is the new spot to eat in Harlem . I've watched chef Swepson from his humble beginnins to create a uptown hotspot that caters to all . I'm going to end on this note ..,, the food is banging
Simply the best. Thin crust, very tasty.

Alex the manager answered the phone to take my delivery order. Before placing my order I politely told him that my last order was incorrect and that we had paid extra for grilled chicken that we never received. I told him that I just wanted to make sure it was right this time and that I wouldn't have to pay the fee a second time considering the error in the previous order. Simple enough. He responded to this by telling me that it was "strange" since that fee should have never been charged and accusing me of lying then putting me on hold for 2 minutes while he fact checked my story. When he returned, he was even more offensive and rude, telling me that he had other customers waiting and asking whether I wanted to place the order or not. Since he told me he was proud of his customer service skills and would want someone to respond similarly to him or his family, I thought it best to leave it up to you. I'm a Texan who knows good Mexican Food and good customer service. Try the food, sure- it's ok for NJ Mexican food. You might get lucky and avoid a run in with this manager, Alex. But his "customer service" skills just lost them a loyal customer of the past 3 years. Had I had the displeasure of speaking with him before, I would have never wasted my money in a place that makes up fees then faults the customer for actually paying it and having the nerve to call back and attempt to spend more money. Guess I learned today...Thanks Alex.

Unbelievable thai food tucked into a delightful hole in the wall. The mango salad changed my life. I live in Boston, and I crave this salad on a weekly basis but have never been able to find anything remotely similar. Rodgee's ability to please each and every customer is clear in every interaction he has with his public. When my Bloomfield friend told Rodgee she was meeting me at Tanglewood this past weekend and she'd like to pick up some mango salad for our picnic, not only did he prepare it for us, but he de-constructed it and packaged the components separately so we could assemble the salad at the time we were eating it. He wanted to be sure we experienced his food the way he prepares it and took the extra steps to make that possible. Do not pass up the opportunity to eat at this amazing restaurant! And Thank You Rodgee for the always amazing mango salad, which I will now proceed to finish ;o)

The food is consistently good and the place is charming! Best gluten free food I have tried in the city so far and a romantic atmosphere. The prices are very reasonable and you can even buy some gluten free groceries there. They don't accept reservations however. The neighborhood around it is lovely so it isn't really an issue waiting for a table. We would just walk around and check out the stores nearby.
Its was very nice evening. The food is so nice and service too good I like everything here ,good luck

I really like this burger place, the burgers are all great, with so many unique burger choices you will never get bored. If this place had a fancy dining room and wait staff we would be paying triple for these awesome burgers. Go for the burgers not the atmosphere and you won't be disappointed.

I been here a handful of times and i would say the review is always mixed. I have sat outside and had sushi with some friends and sangria and the sushi is always delicious and so are the drinks.   The only downfall is that i once waited an hour and a half for my sushi. The service is kinda of iffy, but it is a really nice spot to grab a drink and hang out on a summer night. They always have a band or live music playing upstairs.

I'm astounded that this restaurant gets 4 stars from Yelpers, b/c it is a two-star deal all the way: edible, clean, but zzzzzzzzzzzz my GAWD how pedestrian and boring is this place?! First of all, let's get this out of the way: this restaurant is absolutely NOT at 1515 Broadway. It is ON 45th btwn 7th & 8th, so know that much if you're going to eat there despite my and the other two-star reviews. Second, while it's nice to be asked on a humid morning whether you'd like to be seated indoors or out, it's pretty much a fail to be seated inside (as requested) at the open doorway directly beneath the blowing Arctic A/C but near enough to the great outdoors to have your hair frizz out like Roseann Roseannadanna's. Finally, a compliment to Deanna, our waitress, who was polite and nice, but had the misfortune to serve us our undercooked bacon with dry, overcooked pancakes, my so so fluffy omelet that was only half-done (despite having been ordered well-done), greasy homefries, and cold rye toast. Junior's might have a great bakeshop next door, but this restaurant barely rates a Meh. Skip it, save up your money, and go to Norma's or Michael's. Heck, I've had a dozen better breakfasts at the Bagel Maven on 7th & 31st -- go there!
Excellent strong Melbourne type coffee, amazing "Paris like" croissants, Chocolate recommended. No doubt one of the best in NY.

I really tried liking this place but the food was overpriced, they were unable to give me what I ordered (from their menu) for each course - dessert, drinks, dinner, and apps. My waitress was great but I don't think I'll return.

Excellent food, excellent service. I think this restaurant is in competition with Tulsi for being the best Indian restaurant in the city. I've had the duck, the Bihari Ghost, chicken, Jaipur kofta...all outstanding. Service was warm and solicitous without being intrusive. Highly, highly recommend. And I should know...I grew up eating Indian food almost  every day of my life!

Haven't got the food yet but already loosing faith. Being the only client waiting for food, I've waited 10 minutes up to this point watching EVERY employee standing outside of what appears to be the kitchen (which is right next to the restroom, FYI). I was counting quite much on their efficiency. Seems like we'd have to wait for he crepe place for that. Update: food tastes fine... And that's about how far it goes.

We have lived in Wayne for many years and have seen a number of restaurants come and go. I think we finally have an outstanding Chinese and Japanese restaurant literally almost in our backyard. For many years my wife and I have been frequent visitors to China Kitchen for take out. While China Kitchen was good it does not compare to this new restaurant KOI. KOI's Japanese and Chinese food are equally excellent. We have now been to this restaurant at least 10 times either to eat there or take food out and the quality is consistently terrific.   We must have sampled by now at least 20 to 30 dishes from both Japanese and Chinese items.  All of our culinary experiences have been wonderful there!
Delicious food! Everytime I go there I'm wowed! The service is good, the drinks could be better but the food is amazing!!!
Very quaint and a cute little place! I love the food here and I'm never disappointed with whatever I order.

Very deserving of my first 5 star review. We've had our company Holiday parties there for the past few years and I've never had a second of bad service, a sip of bad drink or a bit of bad food. I want to go there more often, if I only I could afford it!

i love the pizza here!  the  best pizza i have had in NJ and i grew up in Brooklyn, NY so that's saying a lot!  Garlic knots are awesome but best not to get them toward the end of the day because they will be a bit on the hard side.

This is my favorite restaurant in Philadelphia, where I lived for two years before moving to NYC.  Even after moving to NYC, I think this is my favorite restaurant out there, especially when combined with the Graffiti Bar out back.  I love this spot and couldn't recommend it more.   I would LOVE if Sampan/Graffiti would come to NYC.  I think it would do great in the Lower East Side.

AVOID: I WAS SHAKEN DOWN FOR MORE MONEY WHEN LEAVING THE RESTAURANT! I happened to be shopping next door at a large do-it-yourself home improvement retailer, the one in blue - not orange, when I decided to grab a quick lunch.  Gino's was next door and advertised lunch specials; I figured, "Who wouldn't want a deal on pizza?"  I went in and bought the $5 slice and soda special. Here is Rocky's SAFE review: SERVICE Horrible!  I literally told to pay another dollar as I was walking out the door by the lady who took my order.  I inquired about their lunch specials, and the "$5 pizza/soda" deal sounded great.  I ordered, paid, and was told "grab soda from cooler".  Never was I told a "can of soda" - but that became irrelevant.   After ordering, the same lady comes over to me - soda bottle in my hand - and tells me to sit down, they will bring my food.  Again, she makes no mention of me taking the wrong soda.   The cook brings my food and places it right next to the soda bottle - and again - nobody makes mention to me of the fact I have a bottle of soda, not a can.  It was still unopened at this point.   As I leave, I throw my trash away and am stopped by the counter lady.  She runs around, gets in front of me, and tells me she has to charge me more!!!  I asked why, and she says the special is for a can only.   When I asked why she didn't tell me a can earlier - and did not correct me before I got my food - she says I owe her a $1 because it's $1 more.  I looked on the menu, and a bottle is $.75 more.  I paid her, laughed, and left. ATMOSPHERE It is a typical strip mall establishment.  Prices are cheap enough and it reflects in the décor. FOOD A decent slice of pizza may have had me forget about the war of words earlier.  However, most of the other Yelppers hit the nail on the head.  It has that hard, hard crust that makes me think it was born a frozen pizza.   Additionally, the cheese lacked any elasticity what so ever and is reminiscent of an article I read last year about lab created beef.  This could be test-tube cheese, no doubt. ENCOUNTER Overall, this was a total disappointment.  Disgusting food, and even worse customer service, had me thinking I should have done Boston Market next door.  I have no problem paying whatever the accurate price of the soda was, but the manner it went down was tacky.   I had flashbacks to a time when I was traveling in Eastern Europe and was shaken down by the local police: escorted to an ATM to pay my "fine" for stepping on the other side of an invisible line.  But hey, they clearly need the money more than I do.  So, fellow Yelppers, consider yourselves warned! ~ Rocky Waddell

I stopped in for lunch wanting something on the healthier side. I ordered the hummus asked for them to substitute pita bread for cucumbers it was no problem at all. I caved and ordered the zuchinnii balls which were delicious. I ordered the chef stix the meat was so juicy and tender was tempted to order another one, but was full.

This is a great place to go when you want to get a late dinner. The servers and owner were very nice, although maybe not the most attentive. It didn't take too long for food to arrive though. We got fried pickles to start which were very good, with delicious ranch and chipotle mayo. The burger was juicy, filling, and delicious. It has a hint of sweetness since it has pineapple on it.. but it really is just the perfect amount of sweet, not over powering at all. We also got the fried catfish sandwich which was huge and delicious.
Great sandwiches that deliver!

This review is for two different visits. I stay-cationed at the hotel when a friend was in town back in March and had an excellent time--we visited the Library on the last day in the hotel and were seated promptly (also willing to seat my friend while I was on my way over from my office, which is always great!). The drinks were excellent and worth the price, and the service was swift. Five stars for that visit, especially since no one told me off when i started pulling out books and flipping through them! I made plans to grab a drink at the NoMad again this week, thinking we could try to get a seat in the Library since it was a Monday, or perhaps at the bar next to it/behind the restaurant seating section (unaware that the new bar had opened). When we walked up to the Library we were told it was for hotel guests only, but we could check out the new bar, The NoMad Bar, next door (also connected through a passageway). I understand giving priority to hotel guests, but to close it off completely is disappointing. I hope there was a misunderstanding, because I'd really like to visit again!

It took me a couple of times before I actually fell in love with their Sicilian pizza slice ... I just had it for lunch today and I must say it's the tastiest Slice of pizza I ever had. The sauce was perfect the bread was soft and doughy and I love the fresh grated Parmesan  cheese they put on top it was perfect I ate three slices. Even my coworker ask me for a piece she couldn't resist how tasteful it looked. So I must say Maybe it various from day to day but I def give it 5 stars for quality and taste. Overall 4 for not being consistent Hands down best Sicilian pizza !
The food is consistently good from brunch to dinner. Street parking is a little difficult in this area (only to be expected). The tapas style is wonderful for trying different dishes!

Pretty good sandwich with a SIDE OF THE WORST SERVICE I HAVE EVER HAD.  The girl behind the counter actually seemed annoyed that I was there and I ended up apologizing more than 5 times and, even though I am quite a doormat of a human, that feels like way too many times to feel guilty for ordering food.  I asked if I could have a bag because I wanted to take it to-go instead (after finding out that the outdoor seating was for Trestle only) and, to her credit, she did supply this.  She didn't, however, wrap anything I had ordered in the to-go "packaging" (literally just a sandwich bag please put my sandwich in a sandwich bag) so I just had a plastic bag to shove all of my sandwiches in: SANDWICH FREE FOR ALL.  On the plus side, I COULD HAVE JUST PUT THE BAG OVER MY HEAD AND CUT MY LOSSES.  After realizing that to-go wasn't going to work out well, I just decided to stand there and eat it with my new best friend, Counter Girl.  I probably would have gotten over it if a waiter from Trestle didn't come in and start talking about how he "hate[s] the rich douche bags" of Chelsea that he is waiting on and if she had not completely agreed with him.  IMPOSSIBLE NOT TO COMPLETELY HEAR YOU I AM THE ONLY ONE HERE.  SORRY!!!!  It is a good sandwich though so if you don't want to feel like you are completely ruining people's lives by existing and wanting a sandwich, I highly suggest you order it and have it delivered (Monday-Friday).  STILL FEELING SORRY Y'ALL.

My boyfriend and I came here and loved it! The meat was juicy and cooked to perfection. The service was normal, no rush and they allowed us to talk and enjoy our dinner as long as we pleased. The warmed up apple pie with Ice cream on the side totally hit the spot!

This is a really cool joint, with great and very afordable food! This is a true diner experience! The place is tiny and there often is a wait, but the food is great. I went for breakfast two times and they will make anything you want! Check it out, great for when you are on the run and want fast service!

Great Korean food here, so fresh and enjoyable a great place. Great Korean restaurant, I like soy pickled radish  cucumbers here is some good staff who are so attentive and fast to the customer.I love the Korean food . the price here is not high but affordable

I just happened to be in from out of town and decided to try this place. I had a chicken and pasta dish that was pretty good, I think its the best Ive had in a long while. The chicken was tender and not stringy and the pasta was cooked and seasoned just right. The service was pretty good, I did have to wait for a refil but other than that it was great. The place was clean and tidy. If I was in the area again, I would visit again.

Gross, the place was dark, flies galore, staff was horrible. The girl at the counter was so unfriendly, they didn't have corn, the pork was fatty, and I had to ask for bbq sauce for my to go order. Who gets pulled pork without sauce?!  She didn't even tell me my total and just took my card. I will never return. I threw my food out.
I have never gone wrong at Sally's , for me it has always been worth the wait . My fav: egg plant + hot cherry peppers
Incredibly delicious. Savory, comforting food. Large portions. Good Vietnamese iced coffee. Cheap as hell. Can't ask for much else.

I love this bar. the food, the staff, the fish, it's all good. I like that the music is always cool, but different depending on which bartender is working. I also really like the french fries. The backyard is one of the most pleasant in Brooklyn.

This place is the bomb diggty. I came here with my fanily and we ordered different dishes. I being a pancake connoisseur of sorts ordered the banana pancakes.  Now these banana pancakes are like no other I have ever had: 3 pancakes the size of my head,  1 inch of thickness galore, the perfect amount of cakey and pan, and so much banana you'd have thought they used an entire banana tree. Seriously some of the best pancakes I have ever had the pleasure of masticating. Unlike some other places I have been to they actually incorporated the banana into the pancake instead of just throwing it on top. All in all these pancakes blew my mind. My mother ordered a single cinnamon roll pancake and, quoting her, "It was freakin' awesome!". My sister happily asked for the eggs benedict and man did they deliver. She begrudgingly fed me a bite and it my taste buds rejoiced! My father ordered an omelet which looked to be very satisfying. We also ordered coffee which was good. The ambiance was nice and it was perfect for families as well as business (there were some super professional looking gents eating). Décor is awesome with jazz posters covering the walls. The only issue I saw with this quaint place was I was somewhat squished up against the wall but I am also tall and like to spread out. ALSO, THIS PLACE IS CASH ONLY!!!! All in all, stop in for some delish food!

The amount of food reduced drastically- I'm very disappointed. the food is good, but the amount is much less than 9 months ago when I ordered the same menu dishes and the amount has diminished about 30%. I would love to go back to eat, but because of the amount of food vs. Price, I might need to  find yet another good halal food restaurant that carries decent desi food and a decent price...

really good xiao long bao--smaller than I've had before but very good! rice cake was also deliciously squishy. scallion pancake with beef also good. very modern trendy decor; kind of makes you think it would be bad or inauthentic but not the case!

Let me start off by saying that I have been patronizing this business for over 4 years. Just about every morning I would go to Bills Breakfast and Lunch to place my order. My order became so common place that often times I would only need to leave my name, and Bill (the owner, proprietor and chef) would know exactly what I wanted because I WAS such a loyal patron (until this mornings turn of events) However, after going to this establishment for so long, I can tell you with certainty why you should not frequent this establishment. First, the lines are ridiculous. Its not because the food is great, it's only for convenience. I call and place my order just about every morning, and between the 30 minute commute to work, sometimes my order is still not ready. Secondly, the women behind the counter border from being friendly to manic. Thirdly, and this is why I am choosing to never go here again, my prices are never consistent! Yesterday, and the day before that, and the day before that I paid $2.70 for my meal, and today they informed me that I wasn't being charged enough. My total was supposed to be $4.57. WHAT! That's double the price. I understand inflation but these people are crooks. I will not frequent this place again. Sincerely, A loyal customer lost
Favorite place in the WV hands down! Sit at the bar and watch the cooks make art!

Great little place on the edge of town! The fish tacos were fresh and delicious, we shared them as an app. The lobster Mac and cheese was rich, creamy, and loaded with lobster, definitely recommend it! They do have Hopewell valley wine by the bottle, but we brought our own wine. The menu was eclectic and offered something for everyone, from tacos to mushroom mac and cheese to bacon wrapped scallops. The wait staff was very friendly and attentive. And the free, private parking lot was a definite plus-tough to find downtown. This is a perfect place for a casual date night or a dinner with friends!

Let me just start off by saying that I hate to do this. I work in the neighborhood, as well as being born and raised here. I have been ordering delivery from this place since they opened and being that I work in the hood, I have recommended this place to numerous people because I loved it so much. I just don't know what happened. There were times that I ordered delivery EVERY DAY and spent a lot of my money here. Now I'm almost scared to call. The people answering the phones are always rude and always put me on hold, (I get it, I worked in my dads restaurant for many years), but 15 minutes? One time they must have completely forgot I was on hold and I heard someone pick up the phone and then hang up on me! Called back and waited another 20 minutes to finally order my lunch special, which I was finally told rudely by the girl that delivery requires a $15 minimum. Huh? I've been ordering the same exact thing for 2 years. When did this happen? I'm a simple Brooklyn girl, don't care about decor or whatever else others worry about, I just want my food that I love! After getting treated badly again today, I will have to take my business elsewhere.
Cheap and delicious food

After a long day roaming Prospect Park, I Yelped for "fish tacos" and was directed to Citrico. Needless to say, I was not disappointed! After having a little trouble finding the place (there was no sign outside or in the window with their name!), we were seated in the window by the extremely friendly waitress. Based on Yelp and her suggestions, we ordered the guacamole (yum), the camarones al ajillo (holy smokes), and the fish tacos (yesssss). The garlic shrimp were some of the best I've had, and we soaked up the rest of the garlicky butter with the bread provided. The fish tacos are probably what they serve in heaven. Great staff, killer food, decent prices, and a cute vibe. I'll definitely be back!
Stopped by for drinks and not disappointed. Jesus has become my favorite bartender! Next time we'll plan to have dinner.

Pleasant mistake.  I walked out of my company (new to the area) and went the wrong direction looking for burritos...(World Burritos or some such)...anyways landed here and had a great Roast Beef with roasted red peppers, horseradish mayo, provolone and sliced onion on a sesame bagel...great sandwich...not to mention a nice sunny day walk.  I would do it again in a pinch.

Wow @ some of these reviews! We must have gone on a good day (yay for us). We went on Sunday afternoon on the way back from Canada. It was not busy at all. We picked our table and the waiter came over right away. He was pleasant. Food came out right away. We had a meat & veggie personal pizza, a cheeseburger, hotdog, steak quesadilla and fries. Everything tasted fresh, seasoned well. We were satisfied. Maybe we came on the right day? With these other reviews I don't know if I would chance it again though.
Love the 3 for $20 deal, cheese, meat, veggies...can't beat that. Nice glass of wine for the lady, Peroni for myself. The s'more desert was amazing. Always a great meal at Rizzuto's.

Had the pork buns, Akamaru Modern, and the green tea. Pork buns came out first, they're like 3 bites each but very good. Akamaru Modern was great. Thick and hearty soup base, kitchen made noodles, and pork belly. The green tea was very good, tasted very herbal, but it was placed in a thin glass with 3/4 ice for $4. A few problems with this place: the communal seating can be awkward, service can be mediocre at times, wait can be very long (at no fault to the restaurant), prices seem a little high, and the white servers speaking broken Japanese feels artificial can get quite annoying if you've ever heard proper spoken Japanese. I'm guessing for most people, it adds to the authentic experience.
I did not eat there food but I have to say the person i spoke to on the phone was so rude and unpleasant i will defiantly not ever eat at there restaurants.
Simply put...incredible!

What a find!  As a single person -- to be welcomed as an old friend -- is a place to be treasured.  With a simple but carefully crafted menu, every selection is a gastronomic delight!  I have been here often enough to know.  Tibo, one of the owners, is an erudite fellow, who can charmingly hold his own in any conversation.  On a lovely summer day, come in in the late afternoon and watch this establishment come alive as it enters into evening.  You will not be disappointed.  Bon appetite!
most amazing sandwich shop ever. Never disappoints. I hope this place exists forever!

I love the atmosphere here! They have so many food options - and theyre very inventive! I wouldnt get an omlette again because even though it was an egg-white omlette it was swimming in oil - I could barely eat it. Other than that experience, I've been here 5 times. They're mini sweet potato tater tots are AMAZING. They have great salads and they even star the healthy options!
I threw up on someone. Never going there again.

Went there with my friend on a Saturday afternoon. When we walked in, waitress are all moving very fast and you can't even make eye contacts with any of them. No one even paid a slight attention to us. No host No greeting. We stood there for 5 more minutes and still had no one to greet us. Then my friend took out a pen and write down our name on the waiting list! We waited for another 20 minutes and then finally caught a waitress's attention. She shown us our seat and menu then no where to find. We waited another 10 minutes and finally someone came to our table to take order. WHAT IS STILL MISSING HERE???....WATER!!! We didn't get our water until our food comes. I know this is a tea house but severing a cup of water is the BASIC etiquette!!!  So is to greet your customer!!! What happened to this Japanese restaurant? It is supposed to have good customer service. Then the food....it is waaaaay below an average Japanese restaurant's standard. I know most of the pictures from this restaurant look pretty nice. Don't be fooled by that. Tasteless food. Super duper sweet dessert. Not to mention "only cash" ??!! Definitely not going back and definitely won't recommend this place!
I am from Texas and grew up eating BBQ. This is by far the best BBQ in the state of Ct. Went during lunch and service was quick and good which is not easy to do. Planning on going back for more.

I went here a couple of times and i have tried some of the items Breakroom has to offer. My favorite items are the Pork Belly Sandwich, Breakroom Fries, and the Mint Lemonade. The Pork Belly Sandwich is awesome, i like the fatty pork belly and it tastes great withe the runny egg. The Breakroom fries is the epitome of happiness, it has bacon, pork belly, jalapenos, cheese and a runny egg, It tastes great with everything in it.The Mint Lemonade is very very refreshing, especially for the summer. Will definitely being coming back to try more items on the menu. the staff was awesome and pretty chill, the food takes awhile but its worth the wait.
Totally nice!   Live piano player. Quick service and great foods!
Amazing every time!  If you are in New Haven and like pizza, this is a can't miss stop!

What can I say? Food is great come on down to Brooklyn to experience BBQ meat at it's finest. The Mac and cheese as well as the coleslaw are amazing. Perfect for groups and kid friendly my son loved it!! Other parents come and enjoy food and drinks here so I felt at home with my 18 month old!!!

I'm updatin to four stars as this place has corrected the most serious problems with their menu, but the menu is still over-sweet and over-rich, really there is so much sugar flowing out of this place from the menu to the taps it's a diabetes factory, but it's up to you to handle your nutrition - local saturated fats and simpe sugars are still those things, local doesn't automatically mean healthy. Putting a couple of pieces of kale next to 1100 calories of saturated fats doesn't make it healthy. But still, in the tiny market of Burlington your options for actually good tasting food on an actually nutritious menu is very limited and when found as expensive as this place. These are ownership/mgmt problems. The people who work there and the service is about the best you'lll find in any college town, and the staff are super super friendly. Extra star for you!

All five of us had the chef's surprise tasting menu.  It was a great surprise.  We had some New York and French wines we never saw before that were very delicious and good values.  Service was paced very  comfortably.  The restaurant is very quaint and not to loud or to dark.

From the minute we walked through the front door of this restaurant, I knew I was in for a good time. The atmosphere is incredible...very Manhattan like decor...modern, sleek. We went to the bar and were fortunate enough to catch the last hour of happy hour. The deal is half off of ANYTHING behind the bar. Being a tequila drinker and only enjoying more top shelf liquors, this was incredible for us.  Top Shelf Grand Marnier margarita's at half off...It doesn't get any better. My friend was drinking some crazy good single malt scotch at half price...The bartender Jon was awesome. He told us that on Wednesday nights all bottles of wine are half off all night long. So we got an incredible bottle of wine for dinner (Half off)...The dining room was pretty busy, energetic and fun. Our server was incredible. We both had the $50.00 chef's tasting. I am new to Indian flavors and spices but the dishes ranged from infusion type small plates to some traditional items in the final course. Truly the funnest dinner out night I've had in a long time. Bravo Tashan. We'll be back!

I work near El Fuego, so I generally hit them up a couple of times a month for lunch.  Today I was feeling especially ravenous, so I splurged and tacked on an order of chips and guac for an extra $4 to my usual burrito.  Grande-sized regrets after the fact. The chips here are TERRIBLE!!  Brittle, dry, saltless, completely uninspired.  It's as if Gweneth Paltrow herself baked them up...  (refer to article here if you don't get the reference: jezebel.com/everything-i…).  Do yourself a favor & skip the chips if you're contemplating an extra lunch perk -  NOT WORTH IT!!

You can't get a better Italian sub for the money!  It's awesome, so tasty, I'm addicted! Great pizza and dinners too.  Glad they survived the economy, tasty homemade authentic Italian cooking, only bad thing.....they don't deliver....but take out service is very quick.

Adorable, delicious, well priced. My fiance and I went here during a recent visit to NYC. This was among the top 2 or 3 places we ate. We had a savory crepe each and split a sweet one--a full meal for the 2 of us. The crepes were great and some were Scandinavian recipes, a first for me. The service was fast and friendly, though it was a weeknight and they weren't packed. All told, about $30 (before tip, we drank water) for a full delicious meal for 2. If I lived in NYC, I'd eat here often!
Two glasses of wine, two appetizers, a bowl of soup, two sandwiches and a slice of cake for $55 - what a great deal. Enjoyed the food immensely and would recommend for parties of 2-6!
pleasantly surprised by this place. cool nautical decor...great service, good food although MP was a little high. very good overall!

I have to agree with a lot of the other reviews about the service, or rather the lack of it.  We were here on Thursday night and the restaurant was not all that busy; there were four of us--two with a groupon ordered the paella and the other two ordered off the menu.  We also ordered a couple of appetizers; in all, not that difficult of an order for an experienced staff to handle, yet when the meals came the paella came first (after about an hour), the second order off the menu came 10 minutes later, and mine never came.  When I complained to the waiter (about 5 minutes later), I was told it would only be a few minutes more; 20 minutes later he showed up with a dish that presumed to be a tapa that had nothing to do with my order (ironically, my order was one of their daily specials, so I can't imagine it was that hard to convey to the kitchen staff).  At that time it was nearly 40 minutes since the paella came, so I told him to forget it; 10 minutes later (now nearly an hour after the first entrée was served), the manager came by the table and asked if something was wrong.  When I told him, he said that he could have my dish for me in 10 minutes (where was this speedy prep when it was ordered or after I asked for it again), but didn't buy it and told him to forget it, everyone had already finished eating.  We ordered the dessert (I needed to get something in my stomach after the wine) and were not charged for it (although I don't know if that was intentional or a waiter error), and the waiter also apologized and said he was removing the mandatory 20% gratuity (of course, I still tipped on what we received). My guess is that the waiter was new and didn't understand English well enough to take the order (although we took pains to point out everything on the menu), but the way it was handled was pretty ridiculous, culminating in the manager offering to get me my dinner after everyone finished.  Even on a busy night this would be unforgivable, but on a Thursday when many tables were empty (and perhaps rightfully so) it was unbelievable. The food, from what I tasted (a little paella and some appetizers) was pretty good, but certainly no better than many of the other restaurants in the area.  Parking is on the street, but generally available within a couple of blocks. All in all, if you are planning a dinner in Newark, try one of the many other Portuguese restaurants along Ferry and the adjoining streets.  Even with a groupon, this place is no bargain and is not worth the trip.
best halal food in NYC, the price is cheap and the amount is great! everytime i visit the city i pick myself up 1, its the BOMB!

Great food but poorly managed and highly understaffed. Spoke to the manager and told him I don't get treated poorly at his competition. He immediately put down the competition which shows how unprofessional this company is. They're not the only game in town, eat elsewhere.

We really wanted to like this place because it close to our house.  The service was very poor.  After initial check-in, it was 10 minutes to come back and take our order.  Once we ordered, another 15 to get our drinks!  We went for taco Tuesday (first time there, figured it was worth a try).  My wife, son daughter and I all ordered 3 tacos.  They came out in groups and we had to pass tacos around the table!  Really?!?!  Server NEVER came back for a quality check.  Finally I had to ask for our bill. 10 minutes after dropping off the bill I had to go look for someone to pay. After bringing it to the attention of the server that one of the drinks wasn't rang up at the happy hour price, she had the audacity to tell us that happy hour was over...... This was after waiting all of this time.  Seriously something as simple as two drinks and a round of tacos you should be able deliver at least a decent experience.  Too many good places,to eat around here to deal with that!

I waited weeks for this place to open and it didn't disappoint!  My mother lives at Stonebridge just up the road and we dine out locally once or twice a week on average. Here you can expect high quality seafood with a very cozy beach-like atmosphere. I started with clam chowder soup and had the crab cakes for my entree. Both were terrific. We also brought a bottle of wine which the owner opened for us herself! Highly recommend.
So happy this business moved in to the East Village. Super nice people, high quality, eco and animal friendly meat, affordable and totally unintimidating.
great place! very accommodating to my food allergies! Tasty food too!

Love these cheesesteaks!! I have been to Pat's (across the street) and also Jim's. Geno's is by far much tastier and juicier. I like how the meat is cut into thinner slices than most other Philly cheesesteaks. I also prefer Geno's bread than any of the other cheesesteaks. I see people complaining about the service, but you know what you are getting yourself into: an establishment that has been around since 1966, quick service, and a bang for your buck. For the price that the cheesesteaks cost, I don't think we need 5 star service. It's all about how delicious it is!

Bringing shame to the delivery game, since (at least) 2014! Morgan's does not know what they have available, which, as it turns out, is very little. It took them 20 minutes after my delivery order before they called to tell me that the 1st of 2 entrees we ordered - pork ribs - was not available . Ok, what about beef ribs? No? What about fatty brisket? No? Fine, I'll settle for the lean brisket (which I know from previous experience to be bland, but figured I'd drown it in bbq sauce). Then another 10 minutes before they call to tell me that the 2nd of 2 entrees we ordered - chicken - was unavailable. Giggles and a tepid apology from the other end of the phone. I'll probably go back because I'm weak willed and unprincipled. I may even order delivery again, because I make mistakes in my life. But it's not too late for you!
Best creemees in Burlington! Hands down.

Me and my friends decided to check out this pio pio in the city and I will never be back.   The customer service at this place was really poor.   We arrived at 6pm and asked for a table for 6, when they finally found a table for us at 7,they told us we asked for a table for 4.   We then had to wait another 45 minutes to be seated.   Then we head to our table and as we proceed through the restaurant there were many empty big tables available.   We got to our table and we looked at it and it was in the back corner of the restaurant and it was two little tables of two pushed together that could only seat 4 trying to accommodate 6 (4 guys 2 females).   Our elbows were rubbing against each other practically and there would have been no place to put the entrees.   We asked to speak to a manager and proceeded to ask if this looks like a table for 6, he agreed with us that it does not and told us he would switch it but we would have to wait another hour or more.   We ended up walking out and taking our money elsewhere.

Obsessed with this place! Best Chicken Teriyaki bowl in NYC! The menu is amazing - super easy to mix, match, create your own dish. The space is super clean, modern, and inviting. Young crowd looking for good food at good prices. Great addition to the neighborhood. My buddy had a burger and was raving about it.

I went to Benvenuti for a corporate lunch and it was a fantastic experience. The staff was very nice and the food was great. I had the Chicken Marsala lunch special which came with a choice of soup or salad, included your choice of pasta, great bread, and coffee or tea. All of this for only $11/$12. I would recommend Benvenuti to anyone interested in a great meal at a great price. Plus it's BYOB!!!

I braved the negative yelp reviews and decided to take my family here when they visited me this past weekend.  It was my Uncle's birthday.  We were sooo pleasantly surprised that the restaurant exceeded our expectations!! My Mom and I each ordered the special, which was 1 lb lobster with snow crab legs and a side.  She got the mac and cheese, I got the baked potato.  The meal was SO GOOD, we seriously couldn't stop talking about it all night.  Also, it was for a great price; our meals were $19 each.   My uncle and father ordered the swordfish, which they both really enjoyed, and my boyfriend ordered the Maple Salmon.  Everyone had a great meal.  The dessert that we had them bring out for my uncle's birthday was also very tasty.  I'm not sure what it was called but it was some sort of cream pie. The service was good, and I love the style of both the interior and exterior.   I'm sure I'll be back here for more lobster!  Yum!

My first visit to this location. Spacious and clean. Ordered the chole kathi roll. Food was tasty but a bit too oily for me. Could have been prepared with less oil so that when I open the wrapping at work it would not be messy.
Awesome place!  Great coffee by Cafe Grumpy.  Great atmosphere and food!
Perfect

Free jazz daily (at least I think it is daily) Great happy Hour Specials A pretty good menu for what is really a bar.  (food nothing special, but it seems thought really went into menu) Bartenders professional Mixed drinks good. Good as a destination or as a stop while drifting among the other (rather good) places within one block of Sassafras. Just for balance, bathroom kind of lame. Service just OK, can get a bit stuffy.  They have a deer over the bar childishly defiled with sunglasses, hat etc. - So what! (I said it was just for balance) All things equal, Sassafras a great place. I would go anytime.
Their cheesesteaks are simply amazing. There were several customers waiting in line but their service was fast. I most definitely will be back.

Solid Thai restaurant with a lot of space in the back room. Reasonably priced for the city and I they were able to accommodate me on two separate big group dinners that I had there. Very good Pad Kee Mao and Curry.
I had the chicken eggplant basil, the best I've had! Compliment to the chef!! Great service, place is spotless, food is great..highly recommend to everyone!!
Great bistro with fun service and good food, can be very noisy at times , bread is some of the best I have had!!

Had their PBLT and was not expecting at all how amazing it would be! The pork belly was tender and even the bread was amazing. Had their Roasted Kale & Corn to complete the combo. It was simple yet packed with very nice flavors. Hope many people give it a try and continue to come back.
Hands down BEST BRUNCH IN PHILLY! All you can drink mimosas are served fast an very tasty with many types of juice! We love coming here!

A cure to the "Crown Heights Blues"! My friend told me about this place so I decided to give it a try. Everyone was very friendly (which was nice since you don't normally experience anything like that around here) and the guy at the front counter recommended the a few sandwiches so I went with the Cuban. I was NOT disappointed. Although not a traditional Cuban sandwich, Chop Chop's Cuban was a perfect, flavor-filled blend of roasted pork and ham with mozzarella and garlic. It came pressed on a pretzel roll which was a perfect touch. I'll definitely be back for more.

AMAZING AMAZING AMAZING! I loved this place so much. Just went there today for the first time and I felt like I was in London again with their amazing Indian cuisine. Very high quality, amazing flavor, great price. I loved it! I really wish I knew about this place earlier! I ordered their Tikka Masala lunch special, next time I will try the Vindaloo I think.

Gave this place another shot recently.  I was VERY satisfied with their service.  My tapas came out two at a time and they were as delicious as ever.  The waiter was attentive and helpful.  The lobster quesadilla is my favorite!

Had to go to the Yellow Plum for lunch today due to "Restaurant Week in Bloomfield." Glad we got there around 12:15 because they started to fill up. We got both the regular menu and the restaurant week menu. I loved the choice of ordering from either but the restaurant week menu was 3 courses for $20. How could we say no to that? And, the restaurant week menu is lower in price than the regular menu.....love it !!! We both had the salad, mac n cheese and the hamburger. Needless to say.....hands down the "BEST" mac n cheese ever !!!!!!!!. The flavor from the short ribs is just amazing and had my mother not taught me manners, I think I would have licked the dish. Our waiter Sam was attentive and also informed us that the Chef changes the menu each season. No wonder I couldn't find the Watermelon Salad. But, that's just another reason to keep coming back..... restaurant week or not.
Best Pizza in New Haven hands down!
yumm, vegan

the king crab and snow crab bags were incredibly good.  The flavors are too good to describe with words.   However servers could be a little friendlier.  They couldn't let us in 5 minutes earlier before they open when they saw we had two obviously pregnant ladies with us.    I wanted to give them 3 star for this, but the food made up for it.

I think I needed to read more reviews before venturing off of the highway JUST for this particular Indian food.  The decor and cleanliness factor here are both low about a 4/10. The service was the same, our server albeit friendly was way too busy to handle an the entire dining room hisself with just one food runner. The dull plastic pitcher of water that sits on the table would have been a non-issue but the water literally tasted of metal, not faint but really strong. Ok now the food. The crispy onion app was tasty (that's pretty hard to screw up though) and they were still a bit too oily. The other app we ordered (Veg Manchurian) was tasty.  Our entrees: Bhindi Masala: tasted of low budget tomato sauce and old okra it wasn't fresh at all.  My entree the Noelle (sp) fish curry was also made with some low budget version of a canned tasting tomato sauce and was NOT fresh.  We just had almost identical dishes in MD exactly one week ago and they were fantastic.  We left most of this food behind, it was THAT bad...beware.

Moonshine is a neighborhood gem! The staff is always friendly, the cocktails are amazing, and the food is awesome! If you go here often, you can get a frequent diner card and earn points, which you can redeem for free things! The veggie grilled cheese is awesome, as is the spanish arincini! Try one of their Moonshine cocktails! You wont be disappointed. Overall, Moonshine is a breath of fresh air in a neighborhood full of corner bars, and awkward stares from 2 Street-ers. Keep doing what you're doing Moonshine, and I will continue to bring my friends and family!
Awesome place for take out!

Pizza. Real pizza. Best sauce. Very cheesy. This is the pizza I crave. It's not fancy, just good pizza. Been there a few times. The salad is basic but exactly what you want on the side. Love that they have the part pizza but order in advance. The ziti was not my favorite but still worth ordering if you wanted something besides pizza.  I've gone for pizza lunch then ordered ziti and salad to go so dinner was done!

This place is a few small changes away from being a best of Philly and super popular meeting spot. Sto's has all the pieces to the puzzle- incredible Market Street location, outdoor and indoor seating, a cool bar, premium drinks and inexpensive daily specials, decent menu selection, professional staff, flat screen TV's  and video games (X-box etc). All this, yet Sto's is seldom crowded, much less overcrowded. Why not more popular? My guess is consistency and state of cleanliness. I always feel a need to shower after going to Sto's. I really do not doubt is a clean place from the point of germs, but every surface is sticky and napkins are both cheap (junk) and hard to come by. Staff keeps surfaces wiped down, but with dirty bar rags.  Because of stickiness and lack of napkins, I really hate touching anything here. Management simply not on top of this.   Bathroom- Come on, make sure everything is clean and in good working order. It may just be my bad luck, but the bathrooms are neglected. Paper towel dispensers broken, surfaces wet and dirty, always an out of order urinal or toilet or sink or something. Inadequate ventilation. Food- I have had a couple items (wings , burger) and they are just OK and because of the sticky surfaces I described, it is not enjoyable eating here. This means I end up having a reason to leave (if hungry) or going somewhere else altogether. Drink - They have a great selection of beers and mixed drinks. I am a draft beer drinker. Same brand of draft beer from day to day will vary widely. One day, I will try a bartender suggested craft beer and REALLY enjoy it- just perfect. The next day, that same beer will be some combination of flat, skunky and warm. I do not mind too much as servers are professional, super apologetic and accommodating about making things right. I am no worse for the wear , so I return. Though I have been specific and tedious about describing them, these are overall small complaints. My suspicion is that other people are finding them too small to really complain about, too. Though, taken together, these little complaints are enough to cause someone to choose elsewhere- holding Sto's back from being a far more popular place. This reads like a dissatisfied customer review, I love Sto's. It is really a guess at why this pretty darned great place is not very popular. I like Sto's, am a regular, and would say to give it a try to anyone.

I use to go to the Lee's in Clifton. Love the place and then it burned down. Turns out, the cooks ended up here. The Hawaiian foods is great, but I love the Cantonese food. Best shrimp and lobster sauce around. Over pork fried rice? Incredible. Kinda hard to get there now, but I save this for father's day and my B-day

Was ok - the owners were in the process of having some work done on the décor and were distracted by everyone there having to discuss how it was going. - One of the 'supervisors' was walking around the restaurant barking instructions to someone on his cellphone. - made it less than a pleasant environment.
Really, really bland kangaroo meat. Pretty good lamb lollies. Decent beer. Nice waitress but really slow.
big portions good lunch specials
Mexican food was ok... Didn't have guacamole... Lame. Waitress was rude and had no suggestion for the unavailable guacamole! Go to other Mexican venues in Burlington!!!

After reading some of the reviews on Yelp, I want to add my comments of what I consider the most comfortable Italian restaurant in New York On my first visit to Piacere,I felt I was in Tuscany @ a local restaurant where everybody knew each other and greeted you as an old friend, like an Italian Cheers, where everybody knows your name Lots of community tables so you can sit where you want, for the more intimate inclined, you can sit at an individual tables, although I like sitting outside looking at the Broome Street traffic, observing downtown life.   The owners, Marco (Tall) and Marco (short) are what makes this restaurant fantastic if you're lucky you might meet Amanda, the Brazilian wife of Marco S,who adds more glamour then one needs in a given day. I consider this the friendliest restaurant in the city The food and wine ... Excellent, I'm trying to work my way through the entire menu and still haven't found fault in any of the dishes I noticed someone mentioned they spent 3 hours over hors d'oeuvres and several  glasses of wine and questioned why no one paid attention to them, i guess they prefer a waiter hovering over them with the check, rather than a relaxing time at Piacere also said person, wondered why the ATM machine located in the bathroom? Why not? i must have bought 20 people here ,now i walk in and everyone knows my name, "Yves"

I stopped by The Industry this weekend with my 10 month old and the rest of the family. They were very accommodating with my little one and we sat outside and ate. I had  fried chicken and waffles, but wasn't aware that it was super spicy regardless the food was good and I will return to try out other things on the menu. Oh yeah I also had the Mac N Cheese with kimchi definitely worth a try and my little one loved it too.
Overrated, better pizza all over NY, overly salted salad, stupidly skimpy entree portions, too noisy. Once was plenty.

I've been here a couple of times and i declare myself to be a regular there bc i live so close but they don't see me that way.  The wife is a little rude and she could careless if i go in twice a week or not.  But i go there for the fresh sushi and not the service and they do have  one of the best sushi in town.  Their signature rolls are really delicious (Million dollar rolls, Dragon rolls, Spicy girl roll, rainbow roll) but there are only 2 sushi chefs working so there could be a long wait on weekends or evening.  The restaurant is very small and seatings are so tight that you can't have a private conversation w/ your guest.  You can hear everything someone in the corner is saying and i don't like the fact that you have no privacy.  All in all, they do have fresh sushi and love the ginger salad dressing and miso soup, but the service needs to be worked on and the parking is horrible.  You can't hardly see the cars coming while you back out! Therefore, i give them 3 stars.

I've only ever had (amazing) breakfast there, to which I thought was a little pricey. But the decor and view of the river is well worth it. Staff is always friendly and accommodating, and the music is very hip, supporting local bands. Will have to make to dinner one od these nights.

Great food, great atmosphere, great location. This new location is very well decorated and with that and the music you really feel like you are in a authentic Greek restaurant!! The food is always hot and fresh and reasonably priced. The staff is very accommodating and helpful with the menu. They are always on top of everything and make sure that you are having a good time and enjoying the food.
Unexpected treat we found while walking along Flushing Avenue! Great host, great adult beverages and yummie wood-fired pizza. Highly recommend!

If you are hungry, leave Manhattan and come to LIC!!! As a LIC local, I couldn't be more thrilled to see the opening of this new restaurant that adds a new dimension to the LIC restaurant scene. This is a different kind of Latin restaurant that sets itself apart from the taco and burrito take-outs. I am very impressed by the chic decor and the upbeat energy. Besides, the drinks and food are fantastic. We ordered pisco sour and urubamba, two classic peruvian drinks. They made it to perfection. There food menu is small. I think they were going for quality over quantity. However, I hope to see them rotate their menu periodically to keep the returning customers excited. For appetizer, we had Pulpo al Olivo, which is thinly sliced octopus. I love octopus cooked the italian ways and greek ways. Although the sauce they put on the top is an acquired taste, it grew on me after a few bites. Plus the dish is in generous portion and the octopus is cooked to perfect tender and has a delightful taste of salty ocean water. For entree we had grilled skirt steak cooked medium rare. From the steak to the fried plantain to the rice and beans, nothing wasn't mouth-wateringly tasty.   Overall, I loved this place and can't wait to come back. Selfishly, I hope to see more and more restaurants like Jora opening up in LIC that push the boundary of LIC food scene.
you better make your reservation ahead of time, otherwise good luck getting here :). the food is amazing, and the staff is extremely friendly. Must go if you are in Phili.

We went here for my girlfriend's birthday dinner, and it was absolutely worth it. They placed us in a nice nook table that was both beautiful and romantic. Our waitress was also incredibly fun and engaging, and helped us make all the right choices. We started off with a cocktail and a few appetizers, all of which were good. Then, we did the cheese plate, which is not to be missed. Afterwards, we moved on to wine and our main course. She accidentally brought out a version of the chicken with nuts in it (an allergen we had warned her about) but she quickly corrected her mistake and brought out a new plate within 5 minutes. Anyway, I got the steak tartare, she got the chicken; both were fabulous. For dessert, they brought out our order with a candle in it, which was nice. The bill came out to about $100, and we left feeling very satisfied. Overall, it's a place I would highly recommend checking out; we'll definitely be returning here in the near future. Happy eating!
The food was fantastic (get the NY strip steak, it's seasoned perfectly!), the service was good, and the prix fixe menu is reasonably priced for a delicious and filling meal. Excellent wine menu!
Great selection of quality shops and food vendors under one roof. Does not feel particularly clean. Crowded. Pricing fair
Went for a prix fix a while back and got a few extras to try. Everything was good. Would like to go back and sample some more.

Some reviewers wrongly compare this to a NY style deli where the sandwiches are piled so high, they need to eaten open faced with a fork and knife. It is a slightly better than average regular jewish deli sandwich shop and aspires for little more. This review speaks specifically for the Reuben, but I saw many other sandwiched being served, everything fits this pattern: The meat- Better than good, not quite great. Somehow my pastrami was a bit dry even though there was a nice edge of fat and glistening of grease. Flavorful, but not memorably so.   Bread- A great match to the meat and the volume of meat.  The assembled sandwich was finished in a panini press rather than grilled. Nothing particularly wrong with this, but I did expect and would have preferred classic grilled. Sauerkraut - Good.  Could have used more. I suppose my fault for not asking. Russian Dressing - Perfect amount and not overpowering. Swiss - Kind of got lost. It was visible, but no flavor hint. I am not sure if it is the brand or maybe the type of swiss chesse or maybe they could put more on.   Price - $11.50, I think. Value- Dead on fair.  In a sit-down restaurant with table service, this would be a $15 sandwich. It is ala-carte, coming only with a pickle spear. Potato salad / cole slaw extra. Size- As commented at beginning of review,this is not a Fred Flintstone sized serving.  It is a generous sized serving of somewhat better than average pastrami. A light eater will have leftovers, a regular appetite will be satisfied, a super hungry appetite will take more than a sandwich. For an $11 take - out order, this is appropriate. Minuses- Communication - They are no very good with making menu available.  No take out menus, no online  menus. Just medium sized low contrast (difficult to read) menu board to read when ordering and greasy laminated menus (need to clean them!) at the eat-in counter. I work nearby and would probably enjoy this as take out periodically.  Lack of menu makes this a pipe dream unless you have a craving for a specific item. The menu (selection) was not very big.  A few meat types, a few bread types a few toppings. No dessert, whatever sides they have are a mystery to me.  I think they had a sign for motzoh ball soup. Maybe they think the menu is so small a person should memorize it. Needs cleaning.  Overall grungy. I assume passes health department, but crud on walls, stainless steel surfaces etc. Supposedly clean pots and pans hung and stacked for next use all had grease slicks and boogers of the last food cooked in them. Would not pass a moderately stringent inspection for cleanliness or hygiene. Nothing overwhelming, but not up to par if this was a sit-down eatery. Pluses- This is a no nonsense place that really does deliver what you order. Portion is generous, ingredients are all better than average. With all these components in place, Hershel's then pays attention to the finished product.  Food was tasty, well-presented and fairly priced.

This is my favorite Mexican place in Jersey, hands down.  It is authentic Southwestern/Mexican food that is prepared very well.  What's good? -Quesadillas, a must every time -Chimechongas, eschew the steak and ask for ground beef, though the menu doesn't offer it - the ground beef here is really savory -Enchiladas, you eat every bite -Salsa, their house salsa is basically my favorite restaurant salsa anywhere I don't have a wide Mexican palate so I haven't tried many things, but you should sample whatever your favorite is, it is sure to be great.   p.s. my baby LOVES the chicken inside the chicken quesadillas - the only meat/protein she'll eat usually, and other parents have told me the same.

I have lived in town for over a year and local people recommended Village. Not only is the staff incredibly rude there food is terrible. I have tried it several times now, thinking maybe it was an off night. Nope, it's how they are rude and have no sense of customer service. Lucky Lou's across the street is phenomenal and I would much rather go there.

This is a great restaurant for groups, I went with three other friends (so 4 in total) and we all split everything (it was a good amount for all of us to be full). We ordered the Pumpkin Ravioli, Linguine with cream sauce, chicken Parmesan, and chicken Francesca. Great service, the server stepped in with the specials of the day, such as the Pumpkin Ravioli. Seems like a strange combo but it works! The filling brought out this sweetness that regular raviolis do not have. I think it was topped off with some goat cheese. We chose the Linguini (which were fresh for the day) with cream sauce, and the Chicken Parm because a lot of Yelp reviews praised this dish. These were perfect and really complimented each other. Our meal totaled up to approx. ~$80 (with tips/tax), which they subtracted $40 from the voucher, leading to us chipping in around $15 dollars each. Not bad for a meal of authentic Italian cuisine! The deal sold me in coming to this place, and I'm glad I tried it! My name is Shelly, and I also keep a amateur food blog-- Check it out here! alreadyhungry.wordpress.…
Great food, I love it. So many kinds of delicious pizza !  Latest restaurant open in new haven and delivery !

Best South Indian chettinad food in USA. Period! Chicken Lollypop, Mutton Sukka varuval, Parota, Keema Parota, Chicken Chettinad are  excellent choices! Have dined here many times (1 hour from my house).. Worth the trip everytime! Costly.. yes.. but worth it! Edison (when they had the branch there) and NYC (service is really bad)!!  No complaints about North Brunswick though. it is the place to be! -Prabu
Had the grilled salmon very crispy on the outside and succulent on the inside melts in your mouth a perfectly grilled salmon...
Came here twice and both times the food was amazing. Definitely will go back again!
This is IT. Perfect for lunch and dinner. The different choices in pasta and sauces are awesome! Plus, Everyone is so nice. It's definitely a hidden gem in the Gramercy area. Yum!

I go to NYC a lot - sometimes for work, sometimes for fun. NYC is arguably the best food city in the U.S. There are great places as far as the eye can see. For a place to distinguish itself to the point that I consider it a must-visit spot says something. Bubby's is exactly that place. If I'm in NYC, no matter where I am staying, I'm going to make it to Bubby's on that trip. Everything about this place is great. The farm to table concept would seem incredibly difficult to pull off in a city like NYC, but Bubby's pulls it off better than any other place I've been to. As far as the food goes, you can't go wrong, but I prefer the brunch menu. If they have their omelet that has bacon, cheese, onions, and apples on the day of your visit, get it. Tip: even if there is a line to get a table, there is usually a seat at the bar. The bartenders are awesome, and friendly, and they like to have the company. They make all of their juices in house, so the cocktails are fantastic, and they have Stone IPA (one of my favorites) on draft.

I went here on a Saturday night. This place is great for people in their 30s and it has a pretty attractive, laid back crowd for the most part. I had one of the ciders (the name is failing me) and it was probably one of the best beers I've ever had. Definitely a place to go if you're a beer drinker and want to hang out with some friends without drama.

Came here for Easter with the family and it was a great experience. The food is made to perfection and they have a great menu. The restaurant is very traditional and it makes you feel as if you really are in a restaurant in Greece. The atmosphere is great and the staff is beyond helpful. They are accommodating and make sure that your meal is made the way you like it.
Excellent food, very hospitable, lots of team work with refilling water, bread, etc... Not to expensive, depending on how much you order of course. I'll go back in a heart beat!
Descent breakfast.  What you would normally find a diner. Prices were reasonable as well. Nothing stood out as spectacular,  but you can get in and out quick and for a good price.
Manager greets you at the door...... Great service very professional......the food was excellent.... It was my first time at the restaurant I would 100% go back......

My husband and I tried their fried chicken and wings two days ago and since then we wanted so much to reward the owner's and the team work of this restaurant by writing a good review that they deserve. You'll be impressed by the way the chicken is clean. The food is super delicious.  The restaurant is modern, they use up to date technology when taking your orders and during the payment method. People are very friendly, prices are very reasonable and the amount of food is just perfect. I would recommend it to anyone.

Another northern libs restaurant with decent food , but apathetic hipster servers.    There is nothing wrong with showing you care about your job.    If you can't remember an order for a party of 2, then maybe you should write it down.

when we saw they serve fake syrup, and charge an extra $2.50 for real syrup...we left! hello, this IS a pancake house, right? just not right!  Why come here then when you can have the wonderful pancakes at Perkins right up the road in E. Windsor?

My favorite breakfast spot. 222 2 eggs over easy. 2 sausage, 2 pancakes or French toast. Always hits the spot. Hubs always gets an omelette. The berry pancakes are awesome! Great staff. Gotten basic sandwiches to go too. Haven't tried the other hot lunches c

I'm glad this place reopened and is still great for a good meal. I haven't had a problem with service, though I don't usually go during peak hours. The one time we had to wait to be seated, the funny waiter (should catch his name next time) explained that it was due to the weather (rain = beach plans ruined = everyone goes to the diner) and even warned us that ordering certain things would take longer in case we did not want to stay long. He also suggests when we should stop ordering so we don't feel gross and full at the end of the meal. I typically go for pancakes which are a generous serving portion and delicious. The sausage or bacon on the side are tasty and fruits inside are not mush. I love their fries! Other meals are good too and I'll definitely go back.

Ordered take out. Food was delivered hot and quickly however it was not good. The Mac and cheese was absolutely nothing special at all, very bland and not creamy but it was a large portion. Also, the butter that everyone raves about didn't come in our takeout. It was very basic and was completely melted when it arrived. Maybe if you eat at the restaurant you will have a better experience.

I went in w/ my mother to get a platter of sashimi take-out but they didn't have any party platters so ended up buying sashimi deluxe instead.  The wait was what i expected to be and while waiting, the lady brought water for us to drink (tasted like tap water)..and gave us an extra miso soup.  (I guess Sashimi Deluxe is for one person since there were total of 2 soups and 1salad.)  I thought all that was nice until we got home w/ the Sashimi and when we opened the container, we could tell the fish was not fresh and of low quality.  I had went there previously, and did not notice it (i went during 1/2 price Wednesday w/ a friend) since we ordered a lot of rolls but Sashimi's had a fishy taste to it and you were able to tell the fish was not fresh at all.  Needless to say, I wanted my money back but decided never to go back there again.  The most important thing about sushi is that they're fresh and it did not meet our expectation.  Now i know, 1/2 price or not (or whether it's rolls or sashimi), i'll never go there again.  I give one star for their service, which wasn't superb either.  I guess i'm being generous.
stop by while going to City to just try it out very good malaysian food. definatly will come back again

they literally have any crepe imaginable here; whether sweet or savory, lunch or breakfast! plus the service was very good. I got the Vermont apple crispy on a gluten free crepe, which was absolutely amaaaazing. I love how they use local ingredients here!

very mediocre "Mexican" food.  I understand there are limited choices in Princeton which explains the relatively high user ratings. The first test for any good Mexican restaurant is their house salsa, and unfortunately, Tortuga's is borderline awful. Second, the jalapeno peppers I asked for on the side, were CANNED, just like at a 7/11- really? As for the food, all I can say is their cheese bill from Sysco or wherever, must be astronomical. Our waitress was not interested in anything but taking our order, it was as if it was physically impossible for her to act like a real human being. I don't actually remember her saying much of anything, a "thank you" or smile would have been a major hurdle for this woman. Enough said. I'll give them two stars for cleanliness and reasonable prices, but take another away for having to use the usury ATM to pay my bill.

After wanting to hit this place up for the last couple of years, today was the day. We waited an hour & a half for a square pie & I was prepared to be wowed. Unfortunately the crust was seriously burnt & Mr. D. had to really work the pizza cutter to get through it. No napkins, no fan, and seriously, God Bless Mr. D. because the back story & amount of time he put in is commendable, but he should hire someone & take a break. I saw nary a smile. I wanted to love the pizza but burnt & crunchy is not how I like my pizza. I enjoyed watching him grate the cheese & cut the basil but an hour & a half wait for a pie & $32.00 to boot? Glad I tried it but I won't be going back (I saw him poke at a burnt spot in my pie..maybe he knew...)
I go here all the time - delicious pizza. Order sausage with mushrooms. My fav!

So I am really picky when it comes down to the dough. I would have to say that this is not the dough i preferred, but it is one of the best tasting ones. The toppings were cooked well. The cheese was at the right crisp, and the sauce was just fine. I love italian food and if you are trying to find some thing new. Try out lombardi's pizza

Terrific restaurant, the hype is justified. Totto was the last of the Big 3 NYC ramen houses that I visited (other two of course being Momofuku and Ippudo), and I'd have to day Totto was top dog. Food: Spicy Ramen was amazing, not way too spicy but not bland. The pork is perfectly cooked, and the egg add-on is a must-have for a proper experience. Service / Interior: the restaurant is cozy for sure, but service is great and the food makes up for the run-down look. Wait: I showed up about 15 minutes before opening so we were in the first round of people who went in once the restaurant opened. That said, by the time we left the wait for 2 people was about 45 min to an hour - this was on a Wednesday during the summer, imagine it can be worse during the weekends.
This is one of the best places in New York City. The waiters are so friendly and fast. The food is delicious. The taste is just like Italy

Wow what a great experience!!! Came in this weekend for the first time with my gf, we liked it so much we went back last night We were greeted outside by the host Rob, he took the time to explain to us the menu which was posted outside, he then walked us in to show us the inside and were wowed by the beauty of the restaurant, he told us the wait was about 20 min and than brought us wine outside as we waited for a table, thanks Bud i had a great feeling about the place from there on ..we sat in a beautiful booth and had Arnold as are waiter, he was a really nice guy too and took care of us.....We had the Meatballs and Calamari for apps...hit the spot....the pizza was also amazing ,so thin and crisp..i love the coal taste Came in again last night and had another wonder evening saw Rob again who i found out was also the manager which explains why he was so caring towards us , had another glass of wine outside while i waited...waiting never felt so good as me and my girl sipped wine on the corner of 99th on a beautiful brooklyn night, got a booth again and had another great waiter sorry i could remember your name bud...food was great again had baked clams and the eggplant parm and it knocked socks off I could seriously eat here every night i will def be back this weekend. Great Food Great service P.s. can't believe people wrote bad reviews about this place

I was shocked at how good Sora's sushi was! Seriously fresh ingredients made the Sora Special Roll and the Great Lake Roll delicious. Plentiful electrical outlets and free WiFi make Sora a great stop at EWR.

Do not ever order take out over the phone. They require a credit card to "Hold your food, and insure that you come to pick it up" Then LOOK AT YOUR RECEIPTS PEOPLE!!! They charged me a $1.10 take out fee!!! What complete crap! I've never experienced that before from ANY restaurant of MUCH Greater quality!! I've been here several times in the past, but I will not be there again in the future. That's a promise. It's a shame because I live right around the corner from them.
Wonderful food, wonderful service. The chef is super cool and they've got their priorities straight. Love this place!

I can't vouch for the rest of the menu but the pizza is hands down the best in the area and actually would rank very high among some of the better pizza joints in NJ.  I've ordered from them a bunch of times before when I was living in North Brunswick a few years back and they were always "good". Yesterday I was in Franklin Park at a friends house (I live a few towns over) and wanted to treat everyone to a quick meal so I ordered 4 large pies. Side note: I could be wrong but I feel as if this place may be under new management. The person who answered the phone and the person who took my order (a little dry but nice) both had accents as well as the delivery guy, but I remember the owner and everyone working there sounding to be native Jerzian. Pizza this time around, fantastic! The pizza was delivered fairly quickly. Pizzas were huge compared to the personal sized pies offered by the other establishments in the neighborhood. Crust was thin, crispy and not salty. Toppings were fresh and very generous. The white pizza which seems hard for some shops to nail was executed very well. Prices were fairly reasonable as well. To top it all off, I looked like a hero...everyone asked where I ordered them from because they enjoyed their slices so much.  I think Brunswick Grill needs to bump up their advertising strategy a bit to get the word out because they really have a great product but even my friends and their families who live 2 min up the road have never heard of them. I only knew they were still around because I frequent the liquor store next door. Bottom line: If you want a really good Jersey style thin crust pie that will fill your stomach and not empty your wallet, try these guys out.

I found the meal here to be excellent but none of us had any seafood and we passed on dessert. The meat tended to be slightly undercooked, medium look more like medium rare. I had the roast pork special that came with roast fresh peaches, yes peaches! An excellent dish and my wife had the eggplant stacked thingie, which was also exceptionally good. The have 2 covered decks that offer an excellent protect view of the lake, as well as plenty of indoor seating.

This place was so bad it was kind of funny. The sangria is free, but did not seem to contain any alcohol. The service was unbelievably slow, and the waitress was acting very oddly. We asked for an ice bucket for our wine, and she told us that they were all being used. She then left, and came back to assure us that she had found a temporary ice bucket that she would be bringing over. We pointed out that the table next to us had just handed her their check and no longer had anything in their ice bucket, but she said she could not give it to us until the other party left. She then walked away, returned with a jug full of water and some ice, and attempted to dunk our wine bottle into it. The wine bottle bobbed awkwardly around the top of the water.
