Finally the other table left and she brought us the actual ice bucket. Meanwhile, our dinner took over an hour to arrive at the table, even though there were only about four other parties. The pasta was overcooked and the sauces were nothing special.

The food was great. I am not a fan of pasta but the food was seasoned great. I had the ribeye and for the price the size was great. I couldn't finish it. The service was spectacular and if you order the fish from the godfather you are in for a treat. Worth it. Price was less than expected. Well worth every penny.
Amazing food. Right on, no faulities

Wow, it's just crazy packed all the time!! If I was a woman I would've given birth already waiting to be sat! I had the akamaru modern ramen..and it was awesome! The broth was rich in flavor and I probably burned my tongue twice like an idiot because I rushed into eating it.   I also had an extra piece of chashu in my ramen.  Very tender and flavorful. The lady m mille crepe cake was awesome too. My girlfriend ordered it I never really order desserts.  But really soft and creamy.  That what she said.
porkbunss rock

Great ramen! Just a bit pricey. But this is probably the closet thing you can get to the traditional Japanese ramen. It's ALWAYS packed so if you want to go I say go at an off time or call a head. They have a very fun spin on the traditional ramen as well.
Great food :)

My son and I had lunch here yesterday and it was great!  I love the energy and atmosphere of this place, the wait staff was very attentive and I had one of the best veggie burgers I have ever had!  The fries are cooked to perfection!  We will be going back.
Excellent atmosphere. Unique and flavorful menu. Wonderful open air dining. Live music and exotic cocktails.

Was concerned that this place was just a total tourist trap since the line was so long but was happy when a couple folks in front of us were natives & raved that this is actually really great pizza & worth the wait. Didn't wait too long for a table (about 1/2 hour). Been told the line at night during the weekends could be over an hour. Anyway, we sat down all happy & excited but waited for more than 10 for any one to come over & even acknowledge we were there. (Come on Grimaldi's so far you've lost 1 star for the even longer, unnecessary wait.) The pizza is truly delicious. Nice thin crust, high quality cheese, basil, & great sauce. It's really authentic brick oven pizza. My main problem with this place is the service. It's slow & honestly not nice at all. Also make sure you check out your bill. They add the tip to it & not tell you. Service this bad doesn't deserve even $1. Checking out Juliana's next door the next time. From the reviews on here, not only is the service better but they also accept credit cards & it's the same recipe since it's the original owner.

Still thinking about the bluefish entree I had last night, served on just the right amount of green curry, fresh with snow peas and small chunks of eggplant. The curry stood up to the bluefish without overwhelming or masking it. The service was great - as ever - I always look forward to coming here. The Wellfleet oysters are highly recommended also: nothing hidden about them either... salt, ocean, perfectly opened by the pros. This place is one of Philadelphia's pearls.

What a gem! The waitresses were as sweet as pie! When mom is in the kitchen of a restaurant using grandmother's recipes you can't miss.  We had green curry with brown rice and chicken, udon noodles with pork, and pineapple fried rice. My favorite part was figuring out how spicy to make everything with the waitress. We decided on 5 out of 10 because she didn't want to hurt us, but next time bring on a 10. TOM YUM soup is a must have.

If visiting Philadelphia and you want to get the Philadelphia local vibe, Pat's (and Italian Market) is really a great place. As it is not categorized as a yelp tourist point of interest, but a restaurant, I will base the balance of my review on Pat's as a place to eat. It's popularity and fame are based on the past. There are many places to get really great cheese steaks in Philadelphia. Different businesses will often have a specific reason theirs is best (the meat, the bread, the cheeses, etc).  Pat's reason to visit is the history. Once upon a time this was indeed the definitive place for a great steak sandwich. The competition is pretty tough in Philly and Pat's has not really kept pace. Nothing wrong with sticking with the original or classic, but the sub you will actually eat from Pat's will not live up to the great sub you hope you will get and could get elsewhere. They try to pawn off their abrupt and rude service as Philly charming.  No, it is just out of touch customer service. The serving size is lower end of average compared to what you get throughout the city. Meat is pretty good, not phenomenal. The cheese is towards the bottom of the list. The roll is decent. Overall, that adds up to a 2 star "Meh, I've experienced better" review. They make decent steak hoagies / subs here. They just do not belong on a foodie's Best of Philadelphia lists. It is an old recipe that has not kept pace with changes in the market. Depending on what you think most important in a steak sandwich, you will find better. If you have no single item that is most important and just want an overall great steak sandwich, you can do better in that way, too. Pat's best is really the entry level steak sandwich standard nowadays. Most every decent place serving steak sandwiches offer a quality comparable to, or better than, Pat's.

The crab roll will blow your mind. This isn't one of those crab rolls that's 90 percent mayo. This is incredible. Even the bread on it is warm and garlicky! Also had the steamed crabs. Delicious. The staff couldn't be nicer.

Good lunch spot. Easy place to get take out too. I like it because there are so many different cuisines that everyone can get what flavor profile they want. At one table we had American, Thai, Italian,  comfort.

Wesley ecker is the best manger such a people person great great customer service, goes around and make sure customers are ok ! Helping out when needed at the bar the floor bringing out food he's a all around great awesome manger keep up hiring great people for your brand

I got teary when I found this place. My son is gfcfef. Gluten casein egg free. I am not a baker but thank goodness Dee is!!!!  He had his first muffin recently and you should have seen his face light up. I got cookies that we haven't tried yet but looking forward to it the bread is great. The breadsticks aren't egg free but they are a hit too as my son can rotate on and off w a bit of egg in his diet. The brownie is soo good. Let me tell you there is no missing gluten and the rest of it when you can eat Dees food. It's a blessing and worth any bit of a drive. Found you through Max et Mia restaurant.

We have been here twice, The sad part, we live upstairs. The waitstaff or those few we have had the unfortunate consequence in meeting are surly and clearly on their way to splitting the atom or some such, because they have no interest in being waitstaff.the food is ordinary, it is bacon but not BACON! And the prices!!! Its ninth ave people!!! I looked so forward to this place opening because of its proximity to our apt. .What a disappointment , we all miss Ned Kelleys, former occupant of the place.

Great burger.  Big patty that has great flavor to it.  The fries were ok, but that's my personal preference.  they're coated fries which i didn't like as much as regular ones.  a little on the pricey end as far as burgers go, but they are really good so you pay for what you get.
Wonderful dinner/ lunch spot!  BBQ Cuban is amazing.  This a staple restaurant.  Prices are reasonable, at staff is welcoming.

Very clean interior. Typical bar menu. Ordered the bleu cheese burger med rare. Temp was good and the burger was good. Came w fries, slaw and pickle. Had Brooklyn Summer on tap so I was happy. Had about 8 beers on tap. Would come back for a casual night out.

I have been to the Four Aces Diner a handful of times before and always had good service and great tasting food. This trip was entirely different. I went with my father around 11 am on a weekday and we sat ourselves (as is customary) but our table was covered in the food from the previous diners. The place wasn't busy so I don't know how this table got missed during cleaning. I had to wipe the table down but that was no big deal. We ordered and our waitress asked my father if he wanted hash browns with his breakfast sandwich. He specifically said that he didn't want them, while I wasn't asked if I wanted hash browns. Our food came out promptly but there on both of our plates were hash brown potato wedges. The food overall was nothing special, especially the hash browns which were basically a potato sliced in half and grilled with salt and pepper added. An extra $1 for two pieces of thin, stringy bacon seemed a bit pricey to add to a breakfast sandwich. After taking our order, our waitress never once came back to check on us. Not to offer more coffee or to check how the food was or to ask if we needed anything else. We finished eating and sat there for over 10 minutes waiting for her to come by so we could ask for a take home box and the bill. Our waitress was nowhere to be found anywhere in the restaurant. Finally she emerged from the back and gave us the bill and box, and when I looked over the bill I saw that the water I ordered was charged as a soda. At that point I was so sick of the terrible service and I knew that trying to argue with our waitress (if I could ever find her again) would be another half-hour process. I just paid it and we left. Other Tripadvisors have said that the Four Aces is under new management and have complained that it seems to be going downhill. I wholeheartedly agree, and won't be going back.
Very cool place. A little off the beaten path but worth the trip. My date and I had the $50.00 chef's tasting and it was very good. I'm new to Indian food but after that meal, I'm hooked.

Ambience - OK Server/customer service - Excellent South Indian Food - Very Good I live only a mile away from this place and have had food many times. My all time favorite is the Chicken Kodi Vepudu, Chicken Dum Briyani and Chicken Pepper masala..  I am from South India and these items are really authentic.. I am not a big fan of the indo-chinese (or) north indian curries here.. Parotta is also good. Rajesh - the supervisor is very friendly and they do have good service.. Definitely a good place for south Indian food.. Cheers Prabu!
AMAZING HUMMUS! great service, kind staff!

the gluten free bread was very good and tasty, but it was a little crumbly in my vegan delight sandwich. maybe it was just all the weight of the fillings that made it that way, though. even though i'm not a vegan i was a big fan of the vegetable combinations they used (avacado, hummus, eggplant, tofu, to name a few).

This place is amazing. Their crepes are the best. They look exactly like the pictures. The crepes are really good. The place is small but it's really clean. The employs are really nice too. They would help you if you don't know what to pick. So make sure to check this place out.

Server was very nice.... Won't be back though. They try very hard to be upscale, but the food doesn't match the atmosphere. The place sets you up for failure--immediately creates an atmosphere as posh, but doesn't deliver with the quality of food. Too bad, though. It has potential.
Food is great. No matter what time of day there is always a long line BUT it moves FAST, and every time I been there is was great.

Just moved to Philly from Texas, as much as I hate the Chinatown here, this place is awesome. Authentic Chinese food, good portion and reasonable price. I have tried a couple appetizers and the beef noodle soup, they are all very delicious and enough to feed me for two meals. A bit crowded, so try not to go on the weekend.

What a nice surprise!! Great wines, really tasty selection of appetizers topped by friendly crowd. Certainly a night to remember. My favorite dishes: Tomato Raynado, Roasted half eggplant and the Tuna Tartar; Sounds basic but you'll notice the creativity and tastefulness on your first bite.
Great brunch food (lunch too). The only reason for 4 stars instead of 5 was the long wait (much longer than quotes) and no way to do a reservation. Other than that, great service and great food!
Eat breakfast here really nice place.  I ordered the french toast it was very good I would definitely go back for breakfast!!

Yum. Want some now I had a white pizza which I loved. Others had a more traditional and I took a few bites and it was good too. Like thin crust and the sauce is good. Had the Italian wings and I and the kids gobbled them right up We had it delivered so can't comment on dine in service.

First visit notes, the pizza area should be called self service. Service looked much better in the dining room. Pizza had way to much cheese, yes it is possible to say that. I'd give it a second try and order an entree in the main dining room because the staff seemed nice and it was very crowded with locals.

I had been to this place for getting some take out orders. It's been twice times, but i never get disappointed and never get enough of having their sushi. The sushi was super delicious, especially egg sushi! To be honest, I could not even find any Japanese place that can make as the delicious egg sushi like this before. They made me feel like  i had the original egg sushi from Japan. The staff is so attentive to get my order through the phone. The price is reasonable.

Who doesn't like pastry? Especially French pastry!  Lemon tart. Croissant. Baguette with Ham. Coffee. So easy to pop into and get lunch and a treat. Also good place to go when you have to bring a dessert to a party.
Great product, great service, courteous staff, clean environment. They obviously care a lot about their business. Oh, and the subs are great :)
yummm..love their cheese steaks!! best in philly
not good
One of my favorite spots. Great for dates, celebrations, or even just a night out with family or friends.

A tasty café, with an array of vegan sandwiches for lunch. We had an "ELT" whose secret ingredient is delicious "eggplant bacon," thin slices of deep-fried eggplant skin. Their French toast, with bananas, strawberries and a special "butter" made fm Earth Balance and crystallized ginger to go with the Vermont maple syrup, was delightful. All their baked goods, including cinnamon rolls, choc chip cookies and macaroons were fresh and full of flavor. Lots of salad/sandwich choices. Not much seating room, but they do have a few outdoor tables overlooking an old mill on the Winooski river. Great place for a casual lunch.

Algarve restaurant has a nice ambience and amazing service!! Our waiter Abel was so considerate and provided such amazing service. The bread comes out warm and toasted, and our appetizer, the octopus salad, was a perfect combination of tangy and savory and generous servings of octopus. Then came our delicious main course, the Picadihno, which was generously portioned (my friend and I shared it and still was unable to finish it), and seasoned so well. The only thing that would have made it better would be if the pork was more tender, but everything else was fantastic. And again I have to stress how amazing the service was. That really gave this place the 5 stars!
Good food , the only place I eat cheesesteak from. Great service, great people. Nice place

The lamb neck and lamb ribs were OUTSTANDING.  I would have given this place 5 stars if I were judging this place just on those two items. However, there was a huge mishap.  I was there with 4 other people and we all ordered a mix of the appetizers, all vegetarian based, and all good.  Nothing as good as the lamb that would follow, but good nonetheless. We were told the Pig's Head takes an hour to prepare, so we skipped that.  Sort of feel that should be on the menu so you know ahead of time that it's something you need to call in advance for. So, I ordered the Lamb Neck.  A Lamb Neck was brought to the table about 2 minutes after placing the order.  We were told that it was complementary (not sure why) and it had nothing to do with the Lamb Neck that I ordered.  So my 4 other friends shared that one.   After that, everyone got their entrees, except for me.  We were later told that WAS my lamb neck and there was miscommunication somehow.  My friends all shared that - I barely had any because I was told mine was still coming. So, ultimately, everyone finished their dinners and I'd say that I waited about 30 to 45 minutes AFTER everyone else was done eating.  Yes, when it finally came, it was delicious - I'll give it that - but my friends were on coffee and dessert.   What bothered me about this - and I NEVER complain, is that after this entire debacle, I expected them to give me the Lamb Neck free of charge.  I mean, I could've Ordered the Pig's Head by the time it came out.  But no, they still charged me for the Lamb Neck that I waited literally 30 to 45 minutes BEYOND the time that my friends were all FINISHED eating. So, while all the food was very good, I thought that they just didn't do "the right thing" which would have been an apology in the form of comping my entire meal... I never never never EVER complain about service - but this one really was one for the books. I would definitely go back - because the food was GREAT and I doubt this would ever happen again... but this was quite a mishap.

Still going here frequently for breakfast -- their coffee is so good! Recently I've started picking up lunch as well the avocado dream is the best veggie sandwich in town piled high with perfectly grilled vegetables and big slices of ripe avacado- it's a little easy so sometimes I sub the multigrain for a whole wheat ciabatta helps keep everything in

The food is amazing. They have the best vegan burger in Philadelphia. That being said, the service has truly declined. We have been eating here since it's opening and were always happy with the service. Recently, we attempted to eat here on a Friday. We attempted to call ahead and order food. They would not allow us to order. We arrived and it was crowded. A very rude and abrupt cashier with blue hair asked us if we were eating in or carrying out. We answered eating in as she walked away from us she muttered 35 minutes. She then did not return to the counter. I had to yell across to her to ask if we could carry out. She then told us 45 minutes to carry out. I could understand her lack of manning the counter if she was helping out in the kitchen, but she was not. She was rude and brusque.

Delightful drinks menu, cool atmosphere if you're looking to chill for a while. Edgy menu meets Bedford American comfort. Food was fantastic, recommend the fawn-tons, the flank steak, and the pork! Will be back.
Food is good. Fast delivery.
Pros: Veggie and vegan food, desserts from vegan treats, ice cream, service seems more efficient from previous years.   Cons: staff turnover, a good amount of processed food

Great spot to take friends on a Tuesday night for their happy hour and deal for 1/2 off items. Love to take some friends out of town here bc it's laid back, good inside space along with outdoor space and they easily and always have been kind to fit our stroller.

I've been a customer here since they opened and I have to say they've never disappointed!! Malcolm and his staff are warm and inviting as well as professional. he's a truly talented chef! I've lived in the neighborhood for the past 3 and a half years and this place is truly a breath of fresh air! My favorite dishes are the rib eye steak with parmesan cauliflower, and the Cajun club with perfectly seasoned fries! Had brunch with my mom on mother's day and we had the lobster omelette which she was thoroughly impressed with. All around great service, food and atmosphere! I plan to be a regular for many years to come! Oh and definitely say YES to the NoBurger! you'll be glad you did :-)

The food is fair. It is what it is...likes Panda Express in an airport. The service is terrible however. I don't expect a whole lot when eating at airports, but a little courtesy would be nice. Food grade = C Service grade = F
Solid tacos and margaritas, i like the fish tacos the best.
Hands down the worst, most (un)flavorful Thai food I've ever had. Woof!!!! If I could give it 0 stars, I would gladly do so.

I had heard a lot of great things about EO, so I decided to come in after work on a random Wednesday night with my girlfriend and we had a blast. Great service by our waitress Elyse, who was the sweetest. She guided us perfectly throughout the meal to make sure we had the best possible dining experience. Her recommendations were impeccable from start to finish. The steak tar tar is a must have. They mix all the ingredients right in front of you, and customize it according to your personal taste. The chocolate pudding was really good too. Really original. Will definitely return soon!

My boyfriend and I went to Sabrina's and waited more than an hour to just get in.  When we got in, we had to wait another 20 minutes to be served.  Although the wait was long, the food was very good. I could understand why a lot of people stand and wait to have a brunch here. I don't know if the long waiting time made me more hungry, but their omelette was thick, juicy, and warm.  Their poached eggs were excellent.
Love it here !! Definitely a neighborhood fav. Food is always amazing - fav salad in New York to date

First and only bar on Staten Island! I was pleasantly surprised. Definitely a dive, and cash only. However it is what I consider cheap. My buddy and I were drinking Coors Light pints and they were $3 normal price, $2 for happy hour. The bartender was friendly and made conversation with us. She was about 40 I'd say and seemed to be an "islander." The crowd seemed, um, eclectic. Lots of interesting people, I'll put it that way, but everyone seemed nice and we chatted a bit with the gentleman seated next to us. We didn't eat but we did see they have food, which is good to know. Overall a good experience that rests almost completely on our bartender and the cheap beers. Side note: I struggle a bit with reviewing dive bars because really they're all 1 or 2 stars. However, most of what makes me like a bar is the people, and we had a nice time here. The service was good, the beer was cold and cheap. Four stars and I'd come back if I was in the area.

I had a curry dish with roti from Hawker Stall at the ArtsRiot truck stop a week or two ago. The people there were very friendly and the roti was pretty good, however the curry was just a yellow watery brother, pretty flavor- and substance-less. Hopefully it was just that batch, because the other dishes looked fantastic.

We love this place. Cindy and her husband are great. We eat here quit a bit and although it has appeared a little dingy, they are fixing the place up to look nice and to accomodate more eat-in customers. They make a lot of dishes that are not on the menu and can do lots of great things with Tofu. It's definately worth a try!

Went here today for the first time and was very pleased! The owner is super friendly and the pizza is both dirt cheap and delicious! The crust is thin and the sauce is on the sweeter side. It's perfect for when you're craving a good ol' slice of pizza, nothing fancy. If that wasn't enough to make you want to go, the owner donates pizza to the homeless and has hundreds of sticky notes around the shop to prove it. Good pizza with a good cause, I'll definitely be back again!

This place is nice since it is the only Korean restaurant in my area but it has been hit or miss the few times I went.  Their stone bowl dishes always taste great, and the seafood pancake was loaded with seafood.  Definitely a highlight on their menu. The misses come from anything noodle based.  The noodles are not fresh and if I didn't know any better, I would say they are run of the mill instant ramen.  I would stay away from anything noodle based on the menu, but dive into the stone bowls as they are great.  The service is so-so.  Not super friendly or helpful.  The interior is nice and clean, though it is small.  The prices are good and the menu is decent.
NO NO! $11 for one piece of eggplant as an appetizer!!!!!! I am so sorry, you made a big mistake here and lost my business and anyone else I would have taken to LEA.

We hit this place all the time, good pizza and great garlic knots, the best eggplant parm ever, very thin sliced and good sauce. My kids love this place. It's a pizza joint not a restaurant. Good stuff, I wish they delivered
Broccoli with the oyster sauce was heaven!! Food was great.. Drinks were even better. My top recommendations are love potion and zombies. Staff seems a little weird.

Freaking amazing. A burger place that gets it right when I ask for my burger 'bloody as hell'! Good, varied, rotating beer selection... coupled with knowledgeable servers that actually sound like they drink what they recommend. I personally recommend the Philly Steak burger, and the portabella fries.

On my first time here during a busy Philadelphia Thursday evening, Lolita was very welcoming and quick to seat us; we avoided the long waits to sit outside or inside compared to other restaurants. They quickly took our orders and were generous with their margarita pitchers. The vibe is clean, casual and relaxed. I recommend the fish tacos! The staff is accommodating and quick to help you as well.

I never tried bubble tea before today was my first try. I liked it i did not love it. This has nothing to do with the way it was made. The woman making it did it an excellent job and also did an excellent job of explaining to me the various types of teas and which ones i should get. The place is clean and and the staff is helpful. Im going back tomorrow to try something off of their food menu. I will be back for a second review If you like Bubble tea then you should definitley go here and get one. I gave mine to a coworker and she loved it.

The best cheesecake ever made. The cheesecake is so creamy and does not require liquid to finish it. W0W. Having their homemade cheesecake during national cheesecake day in NYC cannot not get any better. Try their traditional cheesecake with a side of strawberries. Very good!!

Such a cheerful, authentic and well priced place.  The food is delicious and nicely presented.  Can't wait to go back.  Only reservation is that the music is a tad loud and repetitive (just a little).

Awesome, but more importantly... The BEST dining experience I've ever had with a waiter/waitress. Linda was an absolute godsend. She not only turned our whole night around, but provided great insight and suggestions personalized for what my date and I needed. I work in the service industry and have been to many luxury restaurants in the city, this lady not only captivated our hearts but captivated our experience and made it the best one we've had yet in New York. Take it from a born and raised NYer. She is an invaluable asset for the Cafeteria!!

We went on Sunday night and had a great time. Our bartender, Steve, was a very charming host. The beer selection is quite good, particularly the draft offerings. The Left Hand Brewing Milk Stout was absolutely delicious.
I ordered a latte. It was quite small for the price but it was high quality. Of I go again I'll make sure to ask them to go easy on the ice to maximize the amount of coffee.

My husband and I have been coming here for over ten years and we have never had a bad meal. Remy, Andy and Jose are extremely attentive. The setting is very quiet for two or more than relaxed enough for a larger party. The wine list is extensive and the desserts (if you have room) are the perfect ending to a delightful meal. Try anything with veal and you won't be disappointed.
Best chicken in town good service fast  little pricey but it's worth it definitely will be back

We were told this was the favorite of the Burlington townsfolk by one of the pedicab drivers. It did not disappoint. The outdoor seating gave a great view of all the street performers. The waitress was quick to come and check on the table and made her recommendations. The chowder had chunks of red potato and bacon and was thick as it should be. The ordered entrees were the buttermilk fried chicken which was cooked perfectly, the black bean burger which my mom enjoyed and fish and chips which we all sampled and were pleased with. They were dog friendly with the outdoor dining and Fido at the next table wouldn't shut up. There has to be a limit to how much is too much though and someone should have said something to the owners.  Great food and service and any of the entrees we tried are highly recommended, I'd be back in a heartbeat when I'm in the area again.

Great romantic atmosphere. If you are looking for oysters and ala carte food, here is the place, its a little pricey, but very high end, so it makes sense. I highly recommend it for relationship anniversaries.
Great place, relaxed atmosphere. Prices are reasonable. As they say... this place IS the original neighborhood bar and grille. Try the spanish garlic shrimp or chicken over rice, yum!
Simply delicious! Noodle bowl was amazing and the banana cream pie was incredible. Definitely get some sangria as well!

Very sophisticated food, ambiance, and people.  It's a great date place for young classy couples. Many different drink options, very good wines and beers, and the servers are very professional to match the food for the drinks.

I went back to PNH yesterday and ordered peirogi's and potato pancakes. The potato pancakes were very good they were not greasy at all and were cooked perfectly. In the last review I stated that the pierogi's were bland, upon having them again I will say that they are not bland but I will say that I have had pierogies that have more flavor. The weird thing about the way they have their pierogis listed on the menu is that you don't have the option of ordering a pierogi plate under the main entrees section like most Polish restaurants would have it, instead they are listed under side dishes at $1.25 or 75 per piece. I will definately be coming back here again.

I went to Rays a couple of days ago and as usual it was buisy , the great thing about waiting a few minutes will be the reward of eating a good meal, well worth coming to that place. Staff is very friendly and helpfull. Even though I feel that they are short staffed they do their best to serve the customers as much as they can. The Belly buster is amazing and the cheese steaks still the best! It's been a while since I've been back, but again I left with a smile.

This is one of my favorite places in the city.   It has more eating places than food stands, but thats OK.    I usually go on a Saturday morning before it gets too crowded or sold out.  Perfect time. I love Martin's Meats for the sausage.  Tons of variety and fresh.   The produce my Iovine is inexpensive and local, which is a plus.  Some of the fruit can't sit too long, so make sure to consume soon after buying. I love the Amish stands and there are a few.  Beilers Bakery is one of the best Amish Bakeries, definitely don't pass up a donut! Lots of good cheese from Valley Shepard Creamery and be sure to try a grill cheese. The best gyro I have had in the city is at Olympia Gyro.   I could go on and on.   It definitely gets touristy, but once you get past that and get used to it, it makes dealing with the crowds a lot easier.  Also, if there is a convention in town on the weekends, it will be super packed.
Good food, good prices, very nice employees, around here one of my favorite places to eat rice, beans and pernil.
Probably the worst food I have eaten. However all is not lost - just walk across the road and go to Empellon Taqueria!

We enjoy murder mystery dinner's.  It was a nice summer evening.  Yes it is a limited menu, but it had plenty on it for us and we are picky eaters.  My husband had the Chicken Rosa and I had the Penne Vodka.  We both had the vanilla gelato for dessert.  The whole meal was wonderful.  The murder mystery show was very interactive.  If you choose to participate it was quite entertaining.  There was a cast of 5 actors.  They built their characters based on answer cards from the audience.  One of the actors, was the victim, who died very early in the evening. The other actors were the suspects and the audience had to ask questions to determine which actor killed the victim.  That was followed by a newlywed show for 2 couples.  One couple had been married over 40 years and the other couple were married less than 2 months.  A fun time was had by all.
Bobby Flay at his best. Loved EVERYthing! Esp lamb sausage pizza, scrambled egg appetizer and tarragon chicken. My wife loved the octopus. Yum. Highly recommend

Pros: One of my favorite vegetarian places in the city. I take omnivores and vegetarians here and they all love it.  Awesome food. Favorite is the bean sprout rolls, and as you wish. Cons: There is one waitress that is a little on the cold side. I've gotten used to her over the years but I do wish she was friendly.

I LOVE their pork soup dumplings. A must experience for all the friends who come to visit me in the city. Also try the Sesame Chicken and the scallion pancake. Service is only OK but the food is worth it.
cheap drinks, neighborhood joint, really good wings

I went to this place few times and I could not resist leaving a review although I don't do this a lot but anyway here we go: the restaurant staff is very friendly especially the Indian girl, she's always smiling and polite as well professional. the food taste great they have got too many vegetarian choices to choose from which Is a big plus for a Mediterranean restaurant. I personally think this place is hundred times better than Tikka way or Chipotle.  with so many options you'll never be burned out eating there. I'll personally recommend this place to anyone.
Man I love this place.  I do wish every location had more seating but the food is great and quick service makes this a place worth visiting.

I really can't believe we just ate at the same restaurant as anyone here who gave this place more than 1 star! My girlfriend wanted to take me out to eat and we decided on a local Italian place which was closed and finally settled on trying this place out. Upon entering the atmosphere was strange and there was some strange lighting situation going on. Anyway we ordered gnocchi for appetizer, spinach pasta with porcini mushrooms and the veal medallions. Bread came out with oil and salt and pepper, which should have been a sign, no herbs or anything, salt and pepper?! Really?! The gnocchi was fairly decent except for seeing mice running around while eating it. Yes mice running all over the dining room. The porcini pasta was disgusting, the mushrooms seemed unclean with actual dirt  or sand still on them. Tasted gross, my GF could not eat it and we said something, decided to be nice and pick another dish. Veal medallions were gross, no where near a $20-$30 plate restaurant, mice, spoiled mushrooms, bland veal just bad bad bad all around! Before the new dish came out we saw more mice running around the dining room and heard they chitting making mice noises, we had enough and told the waitress we were leaving, we don't want the new dish and that our experience has been horrible. When we arrived it seemed like another party was having some words with the waitress also. One if them walked out and another approached the counter and was mentioning something to the waitress. We gave this place many chances while we were there but it failed miserably. Finally we left without paying as the waitress said "just go, just leave".....horrible experience

Just a note of caution here based on our experience.  Obviously, your experience may be different, but my family tried this place for an early weekday lunch after an overnight in NYC recently for a show and were extremely disappointed. We grew up and long lived in the city and so have many options for dining, but figured we'd give this restaurant a try in its new form.  What a disappointment.  The greeter rushed us to a table inches from her perch and by the door.  When we suggested a booth, she insisted they were all reserved despite a "Reserved" placard on only one.  She then announced a forty-minute wait (It was 12noon and the place was maybe a third filled) and turned her back on us to use the phone.  We left immediately and had a wonderful lunch elsewhere right nearby.  Too bad!

Being a staple of the Brooklyn pizza scene, I expected better from the all around menu. I love the square pizza but the other food I had left much to be desired.  The wait for the food was extensive.The potato croquettes were dry, the calamari had no flavor and tasted stale, the marinara sauce tasted like it came from can to plate (like tomato sauce, again, no flavor), and subsequently all the dishes that had that sauce (chik parm, spaghetti, etc) had no flavor. The penne a la vodka was different from a traditional kind and had little sauce.  The one dish with adequate flavor was the chicken Marsala. Also, the Bellini frozen drink was delicious and refreshing.

Went there for lunch today, it was awful.  There was only one other table in the restaurant. Ordered the spring mix salad with chicken.  Chicken was 1/2 raw and rubbery, server didn't even come to check on us or offer to refill our drinks.  We had to get up and ask for our check, when the server saw that I didn't even touch the chicken, didn't even ask if everything was ok.

My boyfriend lives in Philly and he took me out for a dinner at Amada.  This dinner was the most romantic,memorable, and tasty one I've ever had.  Ambiance was amazing.  The music was hip. All these small plates had their own unique, distinct flavors that were pleasant in my mouth.  Yes, the plates were pricey but they serve those prices.  I'm definitely coming back with my boyfriend next year.

I went to Upstate for the first time yesterday with my boyfriend for happy hour and it was totally worth it. The 6 oysters + 1 craft beer for $12 dollars special is awesome. We also got the Sea Scallops and Salmon & Tuna Tartar, which were both spot-on. Great ambience for a cute date night. I can't wait to go back and try their other dishes.

My wife and I were walking down Bleecker Street on our way to Little Italy during a weekend visit to NYC when we noticed a "sandwich board" picturing what looked like a bread bowl filled with melted cheese and topped with an egg.  Two women were outside looking at the menu, and I asked if they knew the name of the dish.  One of the women said it was "Ajaruli," a Georgian specialty.  (I looked it up at home and some recipes refer to it as "Acharuli.")  First things first, if you ever stumble into Old Tbilisi, order this!  It is possibly the best thing that I have ever eaten.  We sat at the bar.  While waiting for our food, I asked the bartender, Giorgi, to pick out a glass of semi-sweet wine.  His pick was an "Ojaleshi," also from Georgia.  I had never had a wine from Georgia before.  It had a sweet front and a refreshingly dry finish.  (So did the next two glasses.)  It paired very well with the Ajaruli which one of the owners, David, came by to show us how it is traditionally eaten.  He also had us try some therapeutic mineral.  We were also introduced to Vasil, his brother and co-owner.  Everyone was extremely friendly and proud of their culture.  Next time we are in New York, we are heading right to Old Tbilisi.

My first trip to Burlington and what do I find?  Absolutely delicious homemade dumplings being sold from a street vendor! For $10 I got five huge chicken & pork dumplings and a load of veggie rice.  If I lived anywhere near Burlington I'd be a regular customer. By the way, the owner makes the dumplings right in front of you so you know they are as fresh as can be.  Don't miss out!

Thank god for the location and alcohol this place would never survive.  I gave this place 3 chances and all 3 failed. Food is bad one of my times their the best thing on the table was my kids box mac n cheese. I waited 1 year to go back and went for lunch 7/16 waited 20 mins for a waitress to come over but that never happen so I got up and left. One day they will learn how to run a restaurant till then they will never see me again. I hope they sell it so I can give the new owner a shot. I really love the location.
Great view. Comfy atmosphere. Martinis on point. Food is fresh and delicious. Highly recommend

T & N was one of the first restaurants I ate at in Philadelphia. I was shocked at the incredible variety that was laid out upon the pages of their menu. A wonderful combination of family favorites & innovative cuisine at affordable prices is why I keep coming back. The staff could not be friendlier. The service is stellar. The food is always fast & fresh. It is for all of these reasons that I believe T & N is the crown jewel of south philadelphia eateries. Dish Recommendation: The Old Fashioned Italian

I am astounded by the number of 5 stars this place has gotten.  Does not give me confidence in Yelpers' food judgment.  I admit to being a foodie, and a snob, but I live in Queens and my husband is a huge fan of Italian food.  He'd driven past this place several times and because it got such great reviews, we decided to try it.  The only reservation we could get at the last minute (on a Saturday night) was for 6:30, so we grabbed it. The "specials" were announced to us (without prices, btw) and a special gnocchi dish was described: home-made gnocchi with wild game sausage, cherry tomatoes and a pesto  sauce.  Well, I love good gnocchi, and wild game; cherry tomatoes sounded ok but a pesto sauce on top sounded bizarre.  So, being a bit of a contrarian, I ordered it, just to see what they could do with those ingredients.  Answer: tasted just the way it sounded, too much and downright wrong.  The gnocchi would have been lovely by themselves: light and airy and perfect.  The sausage might have been good, but everything was thoroughly overpowered by the pesto sauce (a basic cooking fact that anyone who has spent any time in the kitchen should know).   My husband had the house specialty: a chicken cutlet with Grappa reduction and grapes.  He said it was ok.  That's not a great recommendation, coming from him. Desserts were just ok as well: creme brulee, which didn't quite make it though I'm not sure why (custard was cold enough; burnt sugar hot enough--perhaps it was that the custard was a bit too soupy).  Fruit tart for my husband was ok as well.  Esperesso was fine.  Home-made bread was disappointing for home-made bread.  It is apparently impossible to get good bread in Queens. Will not return; too much effort for too little result.  If less is more, this place was definitely more is less.  There's a Yiddish term, "ongepatshket", which roughly describes the food: loose translation--cluttered, sloppy, muddled, overly-done.

I have not a single bad thing to say about this place. Their stuffed Arepas are to die for ! I always get the mami which is a pork arepa with avacado and cheese  their green sauce is so good I put it on everything and finish half the bottle to myself. The passion fruit sangria is sooo good and strong . Def try the cachapas something like that .

I really wish I could give more, was hoping for a good BBQ restaurant in this area. Food is ok, nothing to travel for... The problem is they always screw up something. I've tried a catering order and two dinners. Catering order was ready 2 hours late, and both times for dinner my order has been wrong. They said they would make me the right order, a pulled pork sandwich, and it took 18 minutes... To put pork on a bun, when the restaurant was 1/4 full. Not to mention it's pretty overpriced for what you get. High hopes, but this place falls short
Just got home from coming to this place, I liked the ambiance in here the food was excellent. Presentation with everything matters here and I will be coming back.
Breakfast and dinner are both killer here. Its one of the only places that makes food the way I would make them at home...but they do all the work!
Don't waste your time here. They say 45min 2.5 hours later they were still telling us 45min. For something you could get pretty much anywhere in New York.
Best mexican food around. I've never been disappointed here. Always super busy and it's a long wait- worth it though!
Good food, friendly service, and they have a recycling bin in house.

The food and service is good however the menu is deceiving. I ordered two plates of the braised pork with gargonelli pasta which was delicious but there was no pork to be seen. This dish should be listed as vegetarian. The bean salad with squid also had only 3 peices of squid. The plates are small so dont expect much if you are hungry. The grilled vegetable salad had fried pieces on top which I could not identify. I recommend removing this from the salad and replacing with crutons. Also if one dish takes longer to prepare such as the fried chicken, they should inform the customer in advance.

Hands down the best meal I've ever had in my life. No question, not even close. A culinary experience worth every cent. This is a meal best done with a party of no more than three total. Sitting anywhere else besides the sushi bar defeats the purpose of going to a place like this- you need to communicate with your sushi chef. Do yourself a favor and come here one day, but do it without restraint. It's not going to be cheap. Leave the money thing that at the door, then eat whatever your chef puts in front of you until you are stuffed.
Food was not good at all. Fed the leftovers to my dog and she got sick too. Its hard to find good bbq in NY but this is definitely not it.
The best sandwiches in the world... No better where you are in Manhattan, its worth to come to this p lace just for a bite. Excellent customer service. Keep it up!!!

Ate here a week ago and the food was decent but the service ruined the experience. It's a good looking restaurant with a good looking menu. The apps were very delicious (brussle sprouts, croquettes) as were the unwanted desserts. Post-appetizers is when it all went terribly. There was a 20 minute gap between when the first and last entree came out, with no forewarning from the server. No apology either for that matter, the server simply said "you have to wait 15 minutes until it the last dish will be ready". When it still hadn't arrived after 15 minutes, they offered to comp desserts, which appeared to be a nice gesture. However, immediately after ordering two desserts, they quickly brought out a miniature version of a third, unrequested item. It may seem petty to say over yelp, but it played out in a very misleading and unprofessional manner by the server and Bao herself. We ended up being charged for the two desserts we ordered, even though it was stated they would be complementary. They claimed bringing out a third unwanted dessert was their compensating gesture although they never gave us an option to chose the item they brought us. After all of this, we had another issue where one of our ordered desserts was brought well in advance of the other. When the latter dessert finally arrived, it was the wrong item. Again, no apologies. We asked to cancel the order and they said it was too late to do. Still ended up being charged for it. This place could be a great gem, but its poorly managed and poorly executed. I don't like to be harsh, especially when a place is new or shows promise, but there seems to be zero care for the customer at this establishment.
The food menu is short and weird and with so many other bars in philly, there is nothing impressive about this one at all
Very nice here, good for a date, prices are decent based in the course of what is being served. Definitely will come back again
Best meal I've had all year. Since Eli Kulp took over the kitchen this restaurant has been transformed. Loved every single dish that came to our table. Go here! Trust me.
Very nice seafood spot with nice decor and great food. It can get a little loud in there but I don't mind it much. Tuna tartar and oysters where amazing.
Delicious burgers- turkey, Kobe and prime. I had the turkey burger with grilled onions.
LOVE this place!! Great place to grab good food and good drinks! The bartenders are night and the atmosphere is perfect. Hidden gem in the middle of a tourist trap!

My girlfriend, best friend and I went to Traif last week and we all were huge fans! We order the tasting menu which was a great deal at $50 a person. We had 13 courses (3 of them were desserts) and all were fantastic. The star item for me was the strawberry-cinnamon glazed ribs. It was the right balance of flavour and the ribs were so tender and the meat fell right off the bone. Definitely an A+ joint with great service!

Grilled meats and chicken hearts. Eat to your hearts content (chicken or until satisfied). I've been to the expensive rodizio's around and then I have this place. It's been my favorite so far. The salad bar is amazing with fresh selections. That Brazilian drink is delicious and strong, tv's all over, and pleasant service and affordable price.
Excellent, the lamb chops are just the best thing you could eat on earth. Came here twice already and I love it. Plus on happy hour the wine is at 4$ !

In town for work I checked out what is now called Sunny Buffet. The sun was no longer shining on me after having eaten there. I like to keep my expectations realistic when going to a buffet style Chinese restaurant. However, this place failed to meet, let alone exceed those expectations. The food wasn't horrible or inedible, it just wasn't good, well actually it was rather bad. That being said, I was able to eat slightly more than one plate and live to complain about it. The "best" part of all, the utensils are plastic. What the hell is that? Not compliant with steamed broccoli. Don't waste your time, go elsewhere.
The shredded chicken Tostada is incredibly tasty and the fish taco is very good.  I also like the Ensalada Luna (very fresh). I live in the neighborhood and eat here a couple of times a week.

More of a tourist destination than anything with folks trying to catch a glimpse of the cast, but the crab mac and cheese and the aioli sauce for the fries will keep you coming back even without "mac or dee" there, a bit pricey but totally worth it if you have a taste for good bar food

Best thai food in area. Always fresh and well prepared.  Curry is always a great way.  Masaman is my favorite.  Also the tamarind duck special will blow your mind.  Save room for the sticky rice mango!

Charged my 11 year old son as an adult. Boring food, selection never changes. Half assed prepared hibachi.... Mediocre sushi ugh I'm just do bored of this place! I hope my son finds another favorite spot! He just likes the buffet bc it's close and he doesn't have to wait. BLEH
Black eyed pea soup is vegan and delicious. The staff is super friendly and fast. I'll be back for more!
One of my favorites.  Broth is nice, noodles are great, meats are good - all around a great meal every time.
The food is great!  I always go for the swordfish entrée and the sampler of Mediterranean dipping sauces.  The service is ok.

WOW!   Visiting New York and was dragged to this place by my brother on a Friday night --  who wanted to impress his recent flame -- a tall attractive Indian girl.   We ate at the new Toa the previous night and had a blast.  So, even though Yelp reviews highly recommended this place, our expectations were muted. We got there around 10pm. Place was packed.  We sat on the cozy bench outside, next to a big monkey.  Selfies with the monkey were in order.  We got seated and our drinks arrived.   Good presentation of the cocktails and the metal straw they use  just makes the drinks taste better.   We did not have that at Tao. +1 Food was outstanding.  Not too spicy and the lively atmosphere gives it a very french (read: home)  feel.   The lamb chops were one of the best I've had.   We kept ordering the okra side dish.   Our Indian friend who initially did not seem thrilled about going to an Indian restaurant, could not stop raving and rewarded my brother later *wink*.     Okay, so this was our best outing in New York. Spectacular. I'll be back!

After reading the long list of Yelp! reviews & food network accolades, we went to Paesano's located at Italian market, 9th street, Philadelphia, PA. First off, this is a really small eatery located in an old neighborhood. So, if you are looking for ambience, this is not the place for you. Secondly, the food is OK but is not great. We had panelle and Gustaio sandwiches. They  were ready in 15 minutes or so .  Both sandwiches were wrapped in a thin tortilla type thin crisp bread and came packed with ingredients & sauce. Because of the heavy ingredients, the think bread was falling apart and this made a  messy eating.  Panelle was kind of spicy due to the hot sauce but was otherwise ok. All in all, we wouldn't go here again as it is not worth the long drive. If you live in the area, it is probably good place for a quick take-out.
This place is supposed to be healthy but is just gross. Too oily, deep fried, and nowhere close to healthy.
Banh Mi = French Vietnamese food, ergo French bread, not the wonder-bread they serve. Interesting place though, but service is awful at lunch. Guy at the register is mentally out to lunch.

I've never had worse service in a bar in NYC (and that's saying a lot).  We sat outside in an area with table service for 20 minutes -- nothing happened. They weren't particularly busy, either.  A dumpy guy shows up at the table and says "hey we're closing, move inside now." Geez, well, ok. So we move inside at another table and wait for an additional ten minutes.  The dumpy guy returns says "so, you're ordering?"  We say yes, would like to. He replies: "Well, now we're bar service only, so go up there."  Why couldn't you have told us that when you were barking at us outside? Two of us dutifully head to the bar to fetch drinks. He refuses to serve the entire party because her license is expired by one month and was even ruder about it -- if that's possible. For the record, we were sober young professionals coming in for a quiet after-dinner drink to celebrate a friend's birthday,all between the ages of 28-35 -- not loud, douchey or drunk.
Delicious! Just had the 3 cheese grilled sandwich and the tomato spinach soup. The side salad has an incredible citrus honey vinegrette. The staff were super nice!
mmm authentic Philly cheesesteaks
love el vez!!! awesome mexican food, guacamole, and margaritas!

This is a hidden gem! I am a huge diner fan .. This one is excellent! Everything in home made on the premises and the food tastes like it. Portions are generous and you get a lot of extras, like a cup of home made soup or a fresh salad. Service is friendly and fast. Prices are very reasonable. I highly recommend the detour on your way to or from Princeton or if you are in the area. The apple pie is worth it alone!

What a great place to go.  Fun loving home like feel. Momma is awesome. Makes everone feel like they are eating at their momma's house. food is very good. Greak Salad is the best I have ever had. Highly recommend it. More salad than you can eat in one sitting. Thank you

It's a local place with an old school charm.  I don't think anything has been updated for about 30 years. My order is 2 rippers, relish, gravy fries and a birch beer.  The dogs are flavorful and unique.  The relish is sweet and tangy and compliments the dog nicely.  The cracked deep fried skin of the dog is also good.
Love the pizza here, every time I visit my grandma I come here! My mom loves the subs and my grandma loves the calzones!

Kona Grill is a great place for a gathering whether after work or just with a group of friends. The drinks are always flowing and food is great. The sushi is always a winner and  I love the Kona Chopped salad. However I tried the fries off my wifes plate. Way too salty, therefore the 4 stars but other than that, I'm there a lot with good friends for good food, drinks and conversation
Good varity of sweet and savory crepes also there paninis are osm. Cant forget the latte it was osm.

Since I got there the waiter had such a nasty attitude, then there was a peace of plastic in my dumpling soup and when I told him about it he got mad... I thought I was being part of a joke, unfortunately not, this place is just terrible!!!

I came in to visit this restaurant today and was delightfully surprised. It's rare to find a bar that is busy and the bartenders still engage and give great service(especially if you're one for the friendly bar banter). Did I mention the drinks!?!? Me and my coworkers will definitely be coming back soon

My favorite burger place.  I've had In N Out as well but I feel like Shake Shack is more upscale.  So warm and juicy.  I ordered their seasonal beer but I think their ShackMeister goes well with their burgers more.  Price seems a bit high for a size of burger but I always pick quality over quantity.  However, parking was an issue though.  I've heard that they also have one in KOP so maybe I should try there next time.   When I brought my friend who were all first time to Shake Shack, were very impressed with taste.

I've been to Five Guys, In N Out, Elevation, etc.  Shake Shack has the best burger for the juiciness, temperature, and texture you feel in your mouth.  I'm actually thinking of applying a job there to just to find out how they can make it.

The food here is just absolutely amazing! You have to stop by! This is really a hidden gem. They have great specials for both lunch and dinner, and the food is amazing!! The sandwiches are just to die for as well. All the sandwiches I've had have been delicious. The prosciutto sandwich is my favorite! If you want great homemade Italian food you need to visit this place!
So good!  Family friendly, fast service, EXCELLENT pizza.

This is the best Brazilian Grille Restaurant in Philadelphia.  Ambiance is great and the servers are very friendly.  The meats are great especially Filet Mignon and Picanha.  I always eat with horseradish and seeded mustard and they were prepared immediately.  The free breads were nice and warm. I wish the salad bar had more variety considering the price we pay; however, whatever they had at the bar all tasted very good.  Parking was an issue for me so my boyfriend just valeted.

Pros: best freaking veggie cheese steaks in the city! (I do min minus the ketchup) Green smoothies, desserts, lots of seating, fast service, friendly staff, earthy-industrial atmosphere. Pros: although the desserts are tasty, I wish they came from vegan treats.

The food here was overcooked, dry and over sauced. I ordered the home made hot sausage, and not only was there no heat, it had no flavor. The dino poutine had soggy fries, little cheese and way too much sauce. Their brisket was dry, the ribs were dry and tough and the brisket over cooked and over sauced. The mac and cheese side was way too salty, the potato salad had too much black pepper and the coleslaw was partly decent but tasted too much of lemon juice. The only thing I can say was good was the unsweetened ice tea. I am not a professional bbq'er, but I know what good Q should taste like, and this was not it. I should have taken the hint when most of the tables were ordering burgers and fries.

I went to Tashan last Saturday and I had a good time there. The food was delicious and restaurant environment was really nice. The servers were really courteous and cooperative. Overall I had great experience and looking to go back again.

One of the best lunches I have ever had in New York City. We took our Mother there for her Birthday and it was an amazing experience. Although an expensive restaurant, the "Lunch Menu" is actually quite reasonable considering the quality. Make sure you dress nice - jacket and tie men!

This place is phenomenal, great food selection its really was just OK. I went here once a while back with a group of friends had the pork belly and green beans salad thing and a green tea vodka. We were seated in the back of the restaurant where there was more space and TV. The service is pretty fast, though i did see some people wait a while for their food.Their ochazuke with spicy cod roe was alright. Nothing spectacular either. Definitely recommend this place if you're looking for a late night dinner!!

This is a Restaurant in identity crisis, mediocre food, and poor service.  We went there for a lunch break from work and it took 20 minutes from when we sat down for the waitress to take our order, the appetizer came out cold and it was evident all it was prefab frozen to deepfryer quality, and another 25 minutes after that to get our food so lunch took well over an hour even though there were only 4 other tables filled. The food had very little flavor and nothing was fresh.  Too many items on the menu all over the place and video games in part of the seating area below is confusing, but luckily no kids were playing them that would have made the experience even more painful. Only redemption I may see is that they look like they have allot of beer options so might be ok for late night drinks and perhaps the food may even be edible after a few beers. I would suggest saving your money and appetite for somewhere else.

Just visited men at wok for the first time. The food was ok, with very large portions. However, if you are looking for the best Chinese food in the upper valley you must try china station in Lebanon, blows men at wok out of the water, consistently great food.

This is my first time here at this restaurant and i have to say that it was okay and i would probably won't be returning. I started off with the buffalo wings and the alligator bites. the wings were amazing by the alligator bites were a little dry and flavorless. For my main course i had the jumbo crab cakes served on a bed of rice. Again these were pretty flavorless but all in all tolerable. Overall, i would not go here again and this place did not meet my expectations in any way shape or form

I'm a steak guy simply put. I have been to numerous steakhouses and Ruth's Chris is my favorite by far. The staff is always attentive and food is great. I usually go in about 30 minutes before my reservations and grab a couple drinks at the bar. Once we are seated, I always get a steak, usually a NY Strip cooked mid rare and side of whipped potatoes. It always comes out in a timely manner and again always come out juicy and flavorful. I would have to say the same about all the Ruth's Chris I have visited. I always know what I am getting no matter which one I go to

I have to say, before starting this, I really should have known better.  As a vegetarian, I should know my limits.  But as my friend had heard of the famed Halal Guys, we made a trip to stand in the line that seems to be as famous as the food: unceasing, largely homogeneous, and filled with grease-balls.   The draw of the Halal Guys is simple: basic, tasty food at heaping portions and low price.      How this has been confused with some epic, life changing experience is beyond me.  Meals over rice are hefty and cost only $6, but it left me wondering how much I would have paid to get moments spent in line back so I could do literally anything else with my time.  Something worthwhile, no doubt, like writing Yelp reviews on my phone. As stated previously, I am vegetarian, so I cannot speak on the meat, which is obviously the draw.  Piles of minced chicken and lamb piled on the grill did not look particularly appetizing, but who am I to say?   Nevertheless, from an aesthetic perspective, the score is a definite 0.   I ordered falafel over rice, and somewhat predictably, it was absolutely disgusting.  It is entirely obvious that falafel is a complete after thought for Halal Guys.  But more than I expected.  Bad falafel can be dry and brittle, and have little taste other than chalkiness.  I have to say though, this is the WORST falafel I have ever had.  After less than 2 minutes, my meal was ready (others may take 5).   Maybe 4 deep fried lumps sat in my rice, and after attempting and failing to pierce them with a (metal) fork, I tried a bite to find they are completely inedible. They taste like deep fried rocks.   2 stars and not 1 because I feel I have to give them credit for knowing their client base well enough to not bother even giving one iota of a sh*t about vegetarians.  That almost takes guts.

BOOM!!!! Before The Halal Guys I never ate from those kind of food carts but the moment I tasted The Halal Guys chicken & lamb platter with the white sauce and the hot ass red sauce it was game over. The BEST...You cannot come to NYC and not have that.
best "after drinking at a bar/club" spot
The owner is often there and stand up guy, the food is delicious, and its great if you want to grab a quick, really, really tasty meal. Its rather top-notch for being a quick pick-up spot.

Nan Zhou is one of my favorite places in this city. I really love the kelp and cucumber and especially the Aromatic Mixed Platter - pig ear, beef and tendon cut very thin with a nice vinegary light sauce and pickled cabbage underneath.   Their noodles have perfect texture, shaved noodles are out preference.   The coconut chicken dumplings are one of the greatest things I think I've ever eaten.   They have a small menu, very focused on what they do well. If you've not tried this place, do yourself a favor and go.

I go here when I want to grab brunch/lunch with friends and have a simple but good meal.  The prices aren't expensive and the food is better than average.  The place can get packed on Saturday and Sunday morning so expect to wait at least 20 minutes. The location is walking distance from train stations and buses if you need to travel to get there.  The staff is awesome, attentive and friendly. Perfect pick for brunch on a weekend with friends, even before the night's activities.

I agree with the person who said going to this place will make you happier.  The gentleman who took my order was so helpful and willing to explain how the menu is set up. He also offered me a sample of the frozen yogurt flavor of the day, rum raisin (they also have vanilla every day).  It was absolutely delicious, and it's a flavor I never would have tried without the sample.  The customer behind me in line was redeeming the free juice/smoothie/fro-yo at the end of his punch card, and I witnessed him get upgraded to a medium size.   I was also told they can customize any of the juices and smoothies, so you are not bound to the combinations listed on the menu.  I would assume that extends to the wraps and salads, but I did not ask since the listed items looked good to me as is. I ordered the Magic Pink wrap, which is one of the most expensive menu items at $7.95, but it includes 4.5 oz of wild Alaskan salmon.  This store really does deliver on the "healthy" promise.  Sure, we're supposed to eat more fatty fish, like salmon.  It's good for us.  But farmed Atlantic salmon is a lot less healthy (and maybe even harmful) than wild Pacific salmon.  Any place will serve you farmed salmon and call it a healthy menu item, but this store does it right! I agree that that the atmosphere is austere, and I'm usually one to be swayed a bit by nice ambiance since I REALLY enjoy eating out.  However, the food here is so good and varied and healthy that I can overlook any qualms I have about the decor.  Besides, it's primarily a week day lunch place, and I don't really have time for leisurely lunches in my work day anyway.  I much prefer to "grab 'n' go", so it's great to have an option that is actually healthy.  If you really dislike the interior, there is outdoor seating on scenic Audubon Street you can use on nice days, or you can take the meal to go and find a nicer place to eat it. I thought about this place all afternoon after I ate my delicious wrap.  I literally started planning my next meals there and which menu items I would try next.  I highly recommend this place.  The great food aside, you really can't go wrong with a place that has consistent visibility and involvement of the owner on a daily basis.  Places like that really care about their customer base and reputation and are constantly looking for ways to improve.  Another nearby delicious lunch eatery like that is Zoi's on Orange St.
Great gourmet Pizza! Everything looks wonderful and taste good. They also have a great selection of cocktails and wine! The only thing is that is a little pricey.

Pretty good food, great waitress, dreadful hostess. I came for a birthday dinner with 7 of my friends.  I made reservations for 7pm.  At 7:02pm the waitress calls me and asks where I am.  I told her I was down the block.  When I got to the restaurant, there was literally 2 people in the restaurant.  I didn't understand the urgency on her part to get me and my party to the restaurant.  My friends were late and for 20 minutes, she kept pestering me.  Basically, she rushed us during our meal because she had booked another party after us.  We spent over $400 there, and if she can't do her job to schedule reservations, don't blame us.   I will never come here again and will tell my friends again.  Disgusting hostess.

We love iMunch. Typically we get the herby chicken sandwich and the chicken panini.  Both are excellent and, in my own mind,  these are among the better sandwiches in Philly.   Coffee is great too, they use coffee ice cubes.  Thinking they don't want to dilute their coffee and I thank them for that.  Thanks iMunch! They made a very comfortable eating area upstairs so like a nice mix of eat in and take out.

Once in a while a restaurant will come along and change your perception of a whole category of food.   Not only is the place clean with a great family atmosphere; their version of "traditional recipes" is amazing.  I'm sure that judging by all of the other positive reviews on here no one would object to my calling it "The Best Grill in Town."
Impressed with: -architecture decor/ atmosphere 7/10 -food presentation 10/10 -customer service 8/10 May return. Thanks for a pleasant time!

Food was ok. A little bit too salty. And price is more expensive compare with other Thai restaurants nearby. The waiter was rude. When we were talking to him asking to have a box  to pack our food, he just walked away in the middle of our question without explaining anything. Few min later, he walked back asking us what do we need. Can't believe such service can survive in this area.

Food was too salty. waitress brought wrong dish. We ordered 65 but they brought 66, and blamed on us not pointing the right one. Also, they refused to change our dish. Owner is very rude and food become very salty and overcooked compared with other Thai food around this area. I wouldn't give it a star at all.
We were promised a reservation only to be turned away, saying reservations were not on weekends.  Not recommended.

BEST THAI FOOD EVER!!! I am half Thai and it's so hard to find a place that taste like my moms cooking or better! The ambiance was perfect and low key. The prices was great! I had 2 martinis and an entree for $24.00 dollars. For NYC that was great pricing! Service was amazing too!

My favorite Italian in New York.  I've been coming here for years.  They usually know my order even if it's been a year since my last visit.  The lobster cannelloni is def. the dish to have and do yourself a favor and order a bottle of the house red.  A true classic NYC dining experience.  However MAKE A RESERVATION!!!!!

The Bistro continues to be a sure bet whenever I'm in Soho. They've made a few changes to the menu- which had me nervous (I am a creature of habit) But I have to say I'm mostly delighted. The salmon is even better than before. And the watermelon gazpacho- wow. Still a great place to have a relaxing meal- and watch the world go be. Everything in that neighborhood seems to be turning over- I hope this place sticks around!

I use to come here all the time about 2 years ago, and boy have things changed! My rolls had absolutely no flavor and were very dry. I think they forgot to put in the sauce maybe? Despite the bland boring flavor which was definitely not worth the extra calories, the service was poor. When I first came in the gentleman behind the counter was on his cell phone and pacing back and forth cursing at whoever he was on the phone with. There was no one else in line and I was standing there waiting to order. The gentleman did not acknowledge me once and continued to go about shuffling through receipts is what it looked like. Another person was working at the register and also did not acknowledge me whatsoever. I politely said "excuse me I have been waiting to order." He then pointed at the other guy who fooling around with receipts and abruptly said "he's not taking orders" -- so then I move over about 10 inches where I guess I should have been standing in order to be acknowledged and placed my order. Had the place been busy and hectic I would totally understand and would not be making a fuss, but I was the ONLY one in line and was just flat out ignored until I spoke up. Once I got my order, the guy gave it to me and said "I can't give you a bag for this" when there were clearly a stack of plastic bags sitting right next to him. Was my order too small? I have no idea and these rude people had no intention on explaining. -All that topped off with bland, dry food = 1 star for me.

Definetly one of the best French restaurants in NYC. The food is amazing, the atmosphere is very upper class and chic ! Didn't like their foie gras too much though, the added salt was a major let down.

Best wing spot ever!!! You know it's a true wing spot when they serve you wings and they don't give you a fork and knife.  Who eats wings with cutlery?!?!? Try the dragon wings and the honey ginger garlic wings. Delish!!!
Service is great there! The bartenders do a great job and they work hard to get there food & drinks on the table.

Dined here the other night. Food was very good, but the overall prices and portion sizes of both food and drinks were comical. $90 after tax and tip, and we left hungry. I feel for what we got, a $55-$65 total with tax and tip made more sense to us. We'll wait awhile to see what they do moving forward. For now, we can wait. We can get a full dinner at many Park Slope neighborhood places  (this is in Windsor Terrace) all with farm to table style food at $90.  But to literally feel like we just had a few snacks and still be hungry, it was a bit unacceptable.

Best pizza in New Haven--hands down. Don't be over-zealous with the toppings because the crust will get soggy. BAR brews their own beer and it is damn fine. Their signature salad is worth ordering as well. Very pleasant for a lunchtime meal and BAR turns into a fun spot at night -- quite loud and busy, though, if you want something more mellow come in the daytime. "Authentic" hipster waitstaff but nice enough to get the job done.
We had really good service for dinner at the bar. Drinks were great and got good recs from the bartender on dinner. Def will be back!

La Boca is a welcome addition to the North End. Everything is prepared fresh and there are a TON of local options. The food was awesome. The chef knows how to mix amazing flavors together. The Saltimbocca is so flavorful. Our waitress recommended the perfect local brew to accompany our meal. It was impossible to decide among all of the incredible flavor combos. The ham and artichoke was fabulous. Who knew you could enjoy pizza without sauce or cheese??  A wonderful local place and I pray they are successful!  Try it, you'll love it!!

I love to try gourmet burgers and Bobby Flay's has a lot of them.  Obviously, they use a lot of high end cheese and ingredients.  Considering the ingredients going in, I think Bobby's Burgers are higher quality than In N Out or Shake Shack.  However, taste wise, I think Shake Shack tastes better to me.  However, if you pick uniqueness over taste, I recommend this place to you.

Have eaten here over 10 times, from birthdays,to anniversary dinners, the food is amazing and it will always be, sad to say, what will make me never go back is the lack service I had my last time there, when I was there the girl who care of us was ok, we got our food the food it was perfect, the drinks were great my wife and I were 2 of the only 4 ppl in the restaurant which is fine,we asked for the chk,once the bill came we told the young lady that we have a Groupon deal we found on line, her face and attitude change completely, we gave her the check once she told her manager the youger guy behind the bar the situation he yelled out loud "I knew it, I knew it"i turn head and looked in there direction, they've seen we heard what they have said, so now the entire place becomes a awkward silence, we payed for the chk left a 30$ tip and walk out,what I dont understand is why do businesses sign up with online sites, like Groupon, or living social, and once you attempt to redeem what you payed for the service and attitude changes, I always tip good and I felt that 30$, was more then enuff between my wife and I our bill wasn't even 60$, so for that I will take business elsewhere, what they have to remember is Bayonne has sososo many other restaurants in the area, you can just walk down the block, and go to a different place.

Bustling Italian marketplace with amazing food and people!  We had the calamari salad and took it to go across the street to the scenic outdoor seating area. Wonderful atmosphere and many good food choices and restaurants... And of course coffee and wine! A favorite stop in NYC!
Not bad. Good price.

A fun place to go based on the original & charming atmosphere. Waitstaff will not disappoint with quirky personality, jokes, & fun "attitude". Burgers are cooked in a vertical cast-iron grill, they come on white toast with the option of: cheese, onion, tomato and are served on a paper plate. House-made potato salad and small bags of chips available for sides. Connecticut's own Foxon Park sodas are available in bottles and other big name sodas in cans. You may not have any ketchup. The Library of Congress recognizes Louis' Lunch as "the birthplace of the hamburger sandwich".

Im writing this review a little bit late... well very late haha.
