This is possibly my favorite restaurant. The food is very high quality and absolutely delicious. Everything is prepared to a meticulous standard. The setting is on the formal side. You don't need to wear a suit or evening gown, but slacks and a shirt (business casual) would be fine. That makes it dressy enough to take someone out for a special occasion. Service is very good. It's friendly and professional, and they cater to you to make sure your visit is pleasant

Easily THE best burger I have ever had. Next time I am back in New York (I'm from Texas) I will totally go back. Usually I am not a big burger person but this burger was nothing short of amazing. The fries were also very good as well. If you are in Brooklyn, go. You will not regret it.

This place is pretty disgusting. The salad bar hardly has anything in it and what it does have is not fresh at all. When it came with my meal I could only find cucumbers that looked edible and ended up eating half of one and leaving the rest. I ordered something I thought would be fool proof and couldn't eat it at all: linguine with garlic and oil.  The pasta was so over cooked it was like mush and the garlic were huge slices all over the top that not only were burnt but tasted like maybe they'd been sitting in the refrigerator for a week or two. My meal also came with chicken noodle soup which appeared to be one of those bags you add water too, with maybe 1 piece of chicken. When the waitress saw I didn't like my meal she did have the pasta taken off our bill but charged me $10 for the salad bar and soup...most expensive half a cucumber and half eaten cup of soup I ever had! This was our last attempt and will continue going to the nutley diner which is always fantastic with much better atmosphere and fantastic wait staff. It's worth the extra few minutes it takes to get there.

The perfect way to. Spend a Saturday night .. Clean and cozy perfect atmosphere for an intimate night with your significant other..delicious wings. & Henry makes a mean drink.. So happy to have found a local spot we can enjoy

This is my favorite go-to spot in the neighborhood for happy hour or late night cocktails as well as a casual dinner.  The happy hour is fabulous with great wines as well as fantastic cocktails (2 for 1!).   And I know I can never go wrong with the sumac chicken or the double-cut pork chop (if that's available on special). I do have to give a special shout-out to my favorite bartender, Henry.  He made sure to reach out to me one of the first times I sat in the restaurant.  The second time I arrived, he remembered not only my ams, but the type of drink I liked.  He has a way of making people feel special, therefor making the bar/restaurant feel special.

It's about what I expected. Greasy meat and onions on a great piece of bread but it's part of the Philly experience. We got there right before a huge lunch rush which lasted the rest of the time we were there. I'd venture to say that a Whiz wit would be awesome at 2am on the way home from the bar though. I'll try Pat's next to compare, then I've gotta get a roast pork that people rave about. I love sandwiches!
The tostones were amazing... the rotisserie chicken was flavorful, pork was cooked perfectly, service was quick, and the cafe con leche was to die for.

Had lunch there today, food was not good at all and spent $80.00 should have just thrown out car window. Calamari  was over cooked , ox tail was not  right meat tasted  off.. Good  Luck  but I told  u all

My husband & our daughters went to Brooklyn Crab to celebrate his birthday. We ordered fried calamari, 2 orders of King crabs and beer battered cod fish with French fries. Everything was delicious & worth every penny. I ordered a piña colada which was delicious as well but the birthday boy drank it all lol and I had to order another which turned out to be even better! The staff & management are the BEST and were very attentive to us even though it was busy. The best part of our evening at Brooklyn crab was having the manager send over a banana split to say happy birthday (on the house).

Amazing place! Very busy for breakfast so I recommend calling ahead! I had blueberry pancakes and my family had a sandwich and omelet. All of the food was absolutely delicious! Fun atmosphere and fun people! We went at the very beginning of January and it was nice to get out of the stereotypical New York Times Square hustle and bustle restaurants!

One of the few coffee places in Upper East serving genuine Italian espresso and the derivatives. Excellent quality coffee in chilled atmosphere with friendly Italian baristas. Additional pluses are the shady courtyard and the spacious, clean bathroom with the NYT on the rack.

I came here for a romantic dinner with my boyfriend for a special occasion. It is somewhat new york-sized restaurant with decent food. More than anything the decor was top notch. Service was attentive and the staff was extra friendly For the two of us with non-alcoholic beverages, it came to about 105$ including tip.

Food: very good - 8/10 Service: below average - 4/10 Decor: below average - 4/10 Cleanliness: below average - 4/10: I saw manager bringing jug of water with his finger touching water. He runs around the place clueless - he forgot my order and on another table he said I don't know what cook puts in a dish. But surprisingly cook knows what he is putting in the food. So my thali was very good, each of the three curries, rasam, and even dal makhani was nice and buttery.
great food, but horrible attitude.  If you enjoy abuse from a seriously bitchy host and waiters, then this place is for you.
I am giving it 4 stars because the food was good... But you would think when you order $24 poached eggs you would think they would be runny not hard boiled inside

love love love this place! I have tried the tom yum soup and the noodle soup in the picture (some sort of beef noodle soup) and both are delicious! My favorite dish here is the Kwaytiew Neur Sub, a beef noodle bowl.This particular dish is so tasty and is especially nice on a cold winter day.  I love that they bring you the spice tray (their version of it) without you having to ask.  I love spicing my dish up with the crushed red pepper and adding some flavor with the picked jalapenos. I LOVED EVERY THING ABOUT THIS PLACE !!!    a must !!!   if your in HK !!  wo- hoo !

The food is fresh. A gourmet variety of pizza available and local beer! A great casual hangout and doesn't feel touristy. Also, really great service. Everything was very timely and they always made sure that we were well taken care of. Nothing else I can ask for.

Our Order: Stuffed Mushrooms Mixed Pickles Oysters Apple Crisp Molten Lava Cake Coffee Stuffed Mushrooms: They were ICE cold. When I say this, i mean it tasted like it was microwaved then left to sit for 25 minutes. My group absolutely hated them. Mixed Pickles:This was interesting to me, because last time I was here they served us 3 different kinds of normal pickles. 1 Small kerby, 1 bigger normal style pickle, and 1 other half-sour pickle. This time we got something completely different. 2 pieces of pickled cauliflower, 4 pickled string beans, 1 normal pickle. Really nothing special this time around, mainly because i was expecting different. (and there is no description?) Oysters: These were served with a small side of pickled onion. Honestly we didn't even get a spoon to put it ON the oysters! I asked for cocktail sauce....they don't have it. Apple Crisp: For those who have never eaten apple crisp, it is sliced, baked apples with a cinnamon crisp topping served warm, with a healthy scoop of vanilla ice cream. Sounds delicious, right?.....This was served cold, with a teaspoon of ice cream on top. Edges of the topping were burnt. Was jut poorly done. Very upset with the way it turned out. Molten Lava Cake: My sister ordered this, and was complaining that the "lava" was cold and the edges were also burnt. Coffee: we ordered 2 coffees. One of the members in my group asked for a small refill. Turned out they were totally out of drip coffee. (and didn't seem to be willing to put another pot on. They close at 1AM. Why not?) I will never return here.

To be honest, I have no idea how this place is so highly rated. I waited over a half hour now for my food and the coffee is absolutely terrible. There are people who came in after me -like 20 minutes after me- who were served before me. I ordered the creamed chipped beef. I was surprised to see it was not served on the toast. That would be ok, except the toast was heavily buttered. The result is, of course, that the dish becomes to salty from the butter. And that is ignoring the fact that I am now eating cream with butter. The home fries were pretty good, but I wish there were more. I was never offered water.  The whole experience was just disappointing. There is really no reason for me to come back, not with better options right on Main Street.

I'm sorry to say my meal wasn't very good. I ordered the swordfish on a bed of angel hair pasta with pesto sauce but, the entire meal was drowning in pesto sauce. It looked like they just dumped 3 cups of pesto on top of my meal. The fish was also a little under-cooked. I didn't go there for sushi. The appetizers we ordered were very good! I like the atmosphere and the friendly staff and sitting on the rooftop! Sadly our waiter  is not included in the friendly staff category he didn't really seem to like his job very much. When he asked how our meals were I told him ( in a very nice way) there is too much pesto sauce on my meal, he kind of shrugged & just looked at me for a bit  then asked if I wanted to return it. Of course we all know you don't ever send any meal back to the kitchen! Well, at least I don't.  I would go there again but I would only order the appetizers which are a meal in it's self.
My choice would be the mash potato pizza!
The chili paste was not very spicy, too sweet and overpowering in the pad led moo krob.

My wife and i went to Dominic's for the first time yesterday after receiving a promotional menu from then in the mail a few weeks ago. We walked in and were greeted and seated immediately by the hostess.  This is the only reason for the one start. It was all downhill after that.  Unfriendly waiters, mediocre food, cobwebs and dead flies on the wall and 20 minute wait between finishing desert and getting the check so we could leave.  We will not be returning and will, stick to our regular Italian restaurant Venezia in Woodbridge.

I applaud the pizza and beer concept. 5 stars for the beer, 1 for the pizza. I grew up on NY style pizza and this does not come close. If you're from the south or out west you might like it, but I would personally stick to the wine.

Monday, August 4th, My friend and I decided to enjoy the summer weather and so chose to eat at the Rooftop Birreria at Eataly located at Fifth Ave & 23rd, NYC.  We got a great table location as the scenery was fantastic.  The Flatiron Building was "smack" in front of us.  We had a nice breeze and the ambiance was lovely and very summery.  When the waiter (Daniel) came to the table, he recommended we order a particular drink on the menu.  We really didn't have a chance to look at the menu but took his suggestion as it sounded refreshing.   When he came with the beverages to take our order, we told him what we wanted...ONE appetizer to share and TWO chicken dishes from the small menu, one for each of us.  We were presented with two menus and wanted to order off the smaller menu.  But it now appeared to us that he was pushing the chicken entrée off the larger menu, which we thought was odd.  We made it clear we wanted the chicken from the smaller menu.  He tried to explain that the chicken on the small menu chicken was the same thing as the chicken entrée on the larger menu. We thought this was strange having two menus with one being obsolete.  We gave in and ordered what he told us to order form the larger menu.  It was becoming ridiculous, and after all, we were hungry and just wanted to order lunch. We were perplexed as to why Daniel was insisting we order off the larger menu because the chicken entrée had a different description than the chicken we wanted on the smaller menu.  We agreed that it should not be this hard to order a simple lunch.  It seemed as though the waiter was just not listening to us as it seemed a struggle to get our point across...one asparagus appetizer to share and one chicken entrée for each of us.  The fact we told him we wanted to share the appetizer stuck in his mind because he apparently presumed that we also wanted to share the chicken because when a server presented our lunch, it was not what we had ordered...only ONE chicken dish was served, not TWO which is what we ordered. We told the server when he came with the food, we ordered TWO chicken dishes, one for each of us...NOT ONE and that we ordered ONE appetizer to share.  So, he took the food away, and a few minutes later, a woman named Rebecca came to our table asking what the problem was with our order.  We explained the mixup to her...the two different menus and the fact that we only received one chicken entrée when we ordered two.  Her attitude was not nice as we sensed she didn't want to really know what the issue was...she was condescending and seemed as though she just did not want to understand.  Also she did not clarify the reason for using two menus. Ultimately we did get our lunch (the chicken entrée that we really did not order, but at this point..."what the heck.").  Although the food was very good, the workers Daniel and Rebecca made the simple task of ordering from a menu that was presented to us a very difficult task.   Bottom line:  The service was horrendous, but the food and the ambiance was great.  In spite of this confusion, we did enjoy the rooftop scenery, the food, and the order debacle turned into a scene from a comedy show, which provided us with  a bit of laughter.

I am new to the area and this restaurant.  I took out a combination dish of Shrimp with vegetables fried rice egg roll and mixed egg drop wonton soup. Also had a small BBQ spare ribs on the bone.  The food was fresh and delicious. Two people ate this food so there's plenty of value here.  I only gave four stars because it's my first time and I would have to try it again to raise it to five stars.
Liked the food, But disappointed with the price it's expensive for what I got.

Great sandwiches! This family run 'jewel of Main Street' is always fresh and the service is always friendly. Taylor Ham, Egg & Cheese is the simply the best! Kudos to one of the last of the true old school delis left. The only down side is that sometimes you have to wait for the best...but the conversation is always good.
Great place, and generous portions. Grapefruit with sea salt and honey was really good!

Heres the bottom line , im ALWAYS right and will never steer you wrong , if I say it sucks , it SUCKS , if i say its awesome its AWESOME ............ bottom line , take a date here sit near window , enjoy the best priced wine bottle list ive seen anywhere and have some ridiculously awesome pasta especially the Gnocchi , After that walk back to Manhattan over the bridge at night , great spot........romantic and 10 ft from the restaurant , and then enjoy getting laid  , you are welcome
Just had a fabulous meal here. Super delicious upscale Mexican. I had the pork shoulder platter. Korean beef tacos were awesome too! Highly recommend this place.
This place is really good and very great prices. The burgers were money, and the cheese fries were awesome.

From the moment they started construction on this place, I was eager to check it out. Two Hands has that specific hipster vibe where you just know from looking at it that good coffee is to be found inside. Finally got my chance to check it out yesterday, and while the coffee did not disappoint, everything else did. During my 15-minute wait in line, I decided on an iced coffee and the baked egg roll, only to be told they were sold out of the latter. At 10am. On a Saturday. At a breakfast establishment. I settled for the avo toast. As a lifelong New Yorker, "NYC prices" rarely faze me, but $7 for mashed avocado on a piece of bread the size of an iPhone is ridiculous. They can probably get away with charging these prices since there's nothing else like this place in the neighborhood, but I prefer not to feel like I've been robbed first thing in the morning. Next time I'm in the neighborhood, I'll hit up Baz or Nolita Mart instead. Their decor and coffee is on par with Two Hands', but blessedly come without such a pretentious crowd.

Try the Lamb Balti(Balti Ghosht). Restaurant is not expensive and food is really good. Not like other restaurant where very dish tastes the same. Biriyani is also good and not overrun with spices. And the staff is awesomeee. Very courteous and helpful, never had a bad experience. (I have visited the restaurant around 10times). They also have a grocery store attached to the restaurant.

YaHOO! Texas Roadhouse! We let the host know it was our first time at Texas Roadhouse! We were seated immediately this Sunday night around 6:00 p.m. and welcomed by the owner, "Mike." He put an American Flag in our pail of peanuts (which we loved!) and then, "Joe" our waiter welcomed us, too! Wow! Warm, friendly staff! The peanuts are great, although it's not in our genetic code to toss the shells on the floor! The bread, fresh baked steaming wonderful rolls served with maple butter were superb! "Joe" recommended the New York strip steaks, and we both had house salads with bleu cheese dressing, he had the baked sweet potato, I had the steak fries! The steaks were cooked to perfection, "rare" and seasoned so well we never had to add anything! He had the 22 ounce frosted mug of Blue Moon beer, I had a wine spritzer and the total tab was under $55.00! Wow! It was a great experience, fun, family atmosphere, country music, rustic, wood "Texas style" interior and we came HUNGRY and left HAPPY!
Excellent Eggs Benedict - got the special with prime rib. Other half had baked Eggs - also good. Will go again!

4 out 5 because I carried out so the wait staff was not involved. That said, we really have enjoyed the Tap House pizza and the speed at which my take out was complete was very helpful. Have dined in in the past and that to was a pleasant experience.

I grew up in San Diego, so I'd like to think I know a thing or 2 about Mexican food! Nothing on the east coast can compare to SD or Texas Mex, but Los Tacos is pretty dang amazing. I had the cactus taco and chicken. So Yumm. Their drinks are pretty amazing too. I was stoked to see Tamarindo  (water infused with tamarind), a San Diego taco shack staple.
awesome food, good people!

Their food was OK. For the price it was decent. However, for a self proclaimed Greek restaurant,  the food was a little safe and bland. Spices are absent and made for the non Greek eating customer. The service was very proactive to the point where we thought they wanted us to finish quickly and leave, but there was no line of people waiting. I would probably go back for a simple wrap or cheap salad, but with low expectations. To put it in perspective, my lady friend just told me that if I bring her here again, she will not go. But I would go with the boys. This could be a five if the food was more ambitious and closer to their Greek roots. It's like a kids menu for Greek food. (And I usually don't give poor reviews)
I have never been to a place that had excellent dinner and mouth-watering dessert. Not to mention a lovely atmosphere and great customer service. Felt like royalty. Make a trip here!!!!

Tuk Tuk... I am clearly obsessed with this place.  Even when I move out of the neighborhood, I KNOW I will come back here. Really good food. Everything we ordered was tasty and the portions were filling. The wait staff was attentive and helpful. My only complaint is that they charge a $10/bottle corking fee. I thought it was excessive. Totally looking forward to coming back to try out the other stuff on the menu in the future.

Amazing place. I was there with my two other friends and one of my friend is actually a chef so he was really amazed with the food he told the waiter that he would like to meet the chef so 10 mins later this amazing dish comes to table actually the chef sent it over . After the dish the chef came to table and met us very nice person Overall definitly the best place in philadelphia
Came here for my second time and food is great! Sometimes the wait might be loooooong but def worth waiting! Staffs were friendly and came 2 times to refill my drink! Overall great experience!

This was our first time here and I love this place! It was a little overwhelming at first, with so much to see and eat. You should definitely try the Brisket at Tommy DiNic's, Pastrami at Hershel's, and a desert  from Termini Bros.

Decent burgers and fries! Got the Bullseye BBQ Burger, which comes with onion straws, bacon, BBQ sauce, lettuce, tomatoes, mayo, and cheddar cheese on an onion bun - was really good and cooked accurately like I had requested. Fries were cut medium-thick and were firm and potato-y without being too greasy. The menu is pretty diverse, and you can also get chicken burgers, paninis, wings, and hot dogs, amongst other sides and milkshakes. My only (metaphorical) beef about the whole experience is that I placed my order on the phone, and when I went to pick up my food there was a bit of confusion since the worker had misspelled my last name pretty badly. It's 3 letters long yo. Plus I had spelled it out multiple times doing the whole "D as in David" thing. But whatevs.
Good food, Lahori chicken and Beef Bihari Kabab were good.  Small place and not that clean, but owner is very friendly and nice.

Went here for a late breakfast 8/10/14. I got a two egg platter that had 2 over easy eggs, home fries, sausage, and toast. Also ordered coffee. I can honestly say that the only thing that was enjoyable were the eggs. They were cooked over easy as ordered, and the yokes were suitably runny. Now, for the rest... The "home fries" were nothing more than plain, unseasoned potatoes that were obviously sitting on the side of the grill all morning. There was no flavor and no texture. The outside was hard and crusted, the inside mushy and a little cold. The sausage was bland as could be. Even the whole wheat toast left something to be desired. It was limp and partially buttered. The coffee was unremarkable. This diner was once a go-to spot in the area. Now it's worth driving past to get elsewhere. They are renovating the outside, but what really needs fixing is the food.

Fabulous!!! Tight quarters inside - unbelievable food ensures you don't care.  Guacamole Fresh, Fresh, Fresh. I had a amazing dinner at this place. Drink: floor y luna - vodka ,st Germain , lemon juice , mint and blackberry purée . Is one of the best cocktails I ever had!!!  Dinner: ceviche - ref snapper , mole line juice,avocado,and jalapeño. Delicioso!!!! Entree: chilpodito jarocho. Is a sea food stew( the best in the menu). And no price at all!! We skip desert.  But am sure they r great!!  Service is awesome!! And friendly !!! Next visit will be brunch. !!!  And soon!!!
VK  Dumplings are A1 Beef on a stick also a nice value When I feel a cold coming on I ask for Chicken broth with Fresh Ginger and scallions amazing.     JohnnyR

I consider myself a Ramen Connoisseur and I have to say that to me this is some of the best Ramen Soup out there.  The broth is so rich and full of flavor, the Pork is so tender and delectable and their noodles are perfectly firm...Their Gyoza is homemade and absolutely delicious and their Radish Salad with Sesame Dressing is so refreshing and tasty.  Although I have not tried every single Ramen house in this City, so far they outshine all the ones I have tried.  Minca is a MUST TRY...It is my go-to and I think you will not be disappointed with not only the food, but the hospitality as well.  The only complaints I have is 1) they don't deliver (very sad about that), and 2) their restaurant is a little too small, but truthfully...I really don't care...I will sit on a rock if I had to in order to eat a bowl of this stuff!  Hope you enjoy!

Last night was my first time going to Toro Loco.   First off the reviewer that said the food isn't authentic is clueless.   The food is authentic and its really good.  This is coming from a guy that grew eating at the best mexican restaurants in Arizona and New Mexico  The guacamole is excellent. The chicken in my chimichanga was juicy and not dry and blend like many other Mexican joints in the area.   My wife's shredded beef on her California Burrito Loco was so moist and flavorful I was very impressed.   Last but definitely not least important, our waiter was super helpful and was kind.   I only wish he would've checked on us a bit more.   I had to wait a bit to refil my margarita on rocks.   I know right,  first world problems.   All in all we will definitely be going back and by far the best Mexican I've found in NJ.

Consistently fresh, consistently fast and always friendly. Don's always makes a great sandwich, on fresh bread with the freshest ingredients. The hand sliced red onions are absolutely amazing! A must stop on Main Street in Boonton.

Decent food, but the kitchen was slllooooooowwww.  Clearly a problem as the waitstaff was clustered at the pass through and nothing was coming out for ages.  The waitstaff was EXCELLENT in keeping the patrons patient.

This place is hit or miss. Since my boyfriend lives in QPN we have tried it few a times. Although the staff is awesome the food is inconsistent.  The same dish can be perfectly seasoned one time and the next time not.  Kitchen inconsistencies  are understandable in a new restaurant but after several months the experience has not changed. Drinks are well prepared but the prices are a bit over the top.  (They forget they are in Queens not Manhattan). The final straw was when we realized we had been tipping in addition to the 18% gratuity already added to the check without letting us know.  (This amounts to stealing) The LAST time  there we asked about the added gratuity since we were only a table of 3.  We were told it was MANDATORY.  (Googled it and found that NYC law states restaurants are allowed to add gratuity  to table of 6 or more).   M. Wells here we come.
Been coming here for decades.  Great pizza, heros, Italian ices, ice cream, spumoni, atmosphere and prices.  The inside sitdown restaurant is good too.  A Brooklyn Tradition!

I went there last week with some friends. It's on the pricey side as you would expect from a good restaurant but I have to say it is well worth it! The food was amazing, delicious and fantastic, cannot praise it high.. Service was bit slow.

Very disappointing from a bbq place where bbq meat has no flavor whatsoever. I had half order of chicken with rice and beans, chicken was not seasoned, dry and hard to swallow, didn't even have that yummy bbq brownish color to it. Rice was parboiled, not my favorite, no salt in it, black beans straight out of a can, accompanied with its own black liquid, again, not seasoned with anything :( my husband had beef ribs he said they were delicious, but he also disliked the rice amd beans. Chicken tenders for the kids were cooked nicely though

I've been here at least 10 times so far and it always gets better, service is fantastic!! If you love southern style BBQ where the chef butchers his own beef each morning, this is the place. I've sampled almost everything on the menu and is one of my favorite spots. They have a mean apple pie with vanilla bean ice cream.

I tried Pepe on Friday (8/8). Small hole in the wall place - very charming. I ordered Panini with Proscuitto Di Parma, Tomato, Mozzarella, Arugola. It was totally awesome! The price $7.95. Perfect - great value, great food, in a charming hole in the wall New York style place. Loved it. Definitely coming back.
The atmosphere was nice and the gumbo and blackened chicken were very good. The seafood enchilada had way too much cheese (even for an enchilada) which completely killed the flavor.

We had a wonderful dinner at the Orange Squirrel during Restaurant Week. We had studied the special menu in advance, but were pleased to see that we could order from the main menu as well. Francesco Palmieri is not only a creative chef full of surprises, he is the most charming host, and even had the honor of delivering an engagement ring under glass. She said YES and we all applauded, some of us tearing up. It is a small, intimate but hip and colorful space, and we felt like we were sharing our dining experience with everyone there under Francesco's infectious joie de vivre. Highlights from our group of 7: veal meatballs were firm and full of flavor that stood up to the melted goat cheese on top ( I hate it when they are all bread-y and soft--these were not); pork chops were a tiny bit salty but melted in our mouth; the braised fennel and tomato was absolutely outrageous; the chicken pot pie had a great flavor and delicious crust but was served a bit too hot; the duck breast was cooked to perfection, not at all fatty, and a new quinoa-lover was born. We were treated to delightful breaded squash blossoms that had been picked from the garden that morning. For dessert, we loved all the flavors in the Three Dirt Tasting, especially the s'mores, and the German chocolate soufflé was very good. For cocktails, we had Pink Squirrels and Orange Popsicles--I tasted both and couldn't decide which I liked better, the tangy Pink Squirrel or the not-too-sweet Orange Popsicle. This was my second time at the Orange Squirrel, and it won't be my last. Next time I'm going to try the squirrel nuts, the hand-rolled pasta and the vegan BLT soup. And more of the vegetable sides that we didn't have room for. I am still dreaming of the mustard sauce I had on my first visit. A few weeks ago we couldn't get a reservation at the time we needed--I wish they would expand or move to a larger space. While I'm dreaming let me add that my mother wishes they had an outdoor dining space.

I've never had a bad meal here, including today! In fact, this was one of the best meals I've had in a long time. The server took time to ask about my preferences and recommended a beverage which was perfect. For the starter, I ordered a farmhouse salad which included yellow and red organic tomatoes, basil and watermelon sitting on a thin spread of hummus...yum! For the entree I ordered the diver scallops. A perfect meal for a smaller appetite but with a good ratio of savory seafood protein to veggies (asparagus and corn.).  Looking forward to my next meal here!

So I went to this restaurant with my friends. There were six of us and we all dressed somewhat casually. I think that is the reason why I didn't feel like being treated well. The waiters were dressed really well and the environment was great! One more thing about it - I didn't think the food was worth the price. I ordered the entree that had beef and it didn't have any kind of taste and cost me 42 dollars. Anyway I don't think it is a good restaurant if you want to eat good food.

Finally an authentic chinese restaurant in the area! I tried the xiao long bao and it was better than any I've ordered in chinatown! The restaurant itself had a great ambiance with a clean modern design. The staff was very friendly and attentive. I will definitely visit again!

The Bao is at a great location (right above  Spot dessert bar)! Compared to typical Shanghai food that you'd find in Chinatown, this restaurant is a mix between traditional and exotic foods, with their Wasabi Xiao Long Bao and Super Spicy Xiao Long bao, which you can't find anywhere else! Really great decor and just an overall awesome atmosphere.

Just opened! I came in today and coming back over the weekend to indulge in my love for the xiao long baos. Really reminds me of my childhood - the meat is firm, the soup is amazingly light, and the skin is just thick enough to keep it all together. I need to try the other main dishes, but I can literally eat 2 dozen of these. The Bao is a welcomed addition to the neighborhood full of food and will become a mainstay in my weekly diet for sure.

The XLB is great.  The skin is very thin yet strong enough to hold all the soup and the very moist juicy meat.  Very creative with their wasabi, very spicy and chocolate XLB.  They have a great selection of some authentic Chinese dishes.  I love the salty egg with bitter melon and the eggplant with lots of spicy hot peppers. An awesome place.  I often go to chinatown or Flushing for XLB, but I would much prefer coming here because the ambience is nice and the restaurant is much cleaner.  I often judge the restaurant's cleaniness by their bathroom.

I really wanted to like this place.  My first impression when I walked in was oh oh this place is empty and it's dinner time not a good sign. Then the host coldly asked me "Can I help you?" No smile, no warmth, nothing.  Like I was interrupting him or something. The coldness didn't stop there,  the staff in general seemed like they didn't want to be there.  I ordered the shrimp special appetizer which was so bland.   I am so upset that I paid $12 for 3 shrimps and wilted spinach. Very expensive and definitely not worth it.  My entree was a little bit better but it was bland as well. I had to ask the bus girl to get me some salt and pepper and red pepper flakes to add flavor. On the positive, it's a very nice establishment,  good ambiance and if sitting outside, romantic. I'm really glad I used a voucher to try out this place. They really need to work on their customer service skills.  Try smiling and making your customers feel welcomed.
First time here, really great fries and green tea infusion drinks. The BBQ pork was good.

My wife and I like funky, unique places.  We searched yelp and came across this one.  Skeptical on a "sandwich place", we went while we were in town and left with the best memory.  A very airy, fresh, intricate, delicious sandwiches.  I honestly can't picture the quality of sandwiches getting better than this.  Keep up the great work! The only reason that this does not get a 5, is because we did not see any description of the sandwiches.  They all had great names, and I was curious on all of them.  The owner and staff will graciously help you out if you ask, but I am just someone who would like to see every single option to feel confident I am spoiling exactly what my taste buds are craving at that time.
Good fried seafood. Not fancy...huge portions, great place to enjoy soft shell crab and the seaside.

We've tried their Chinese and Thai food as well as their sushi and it is all delicious. It's hard to find a place that specializes in as large of a menu as golden chef, but every time we eat their food we are further impressed. We have eaten there as well as had them deliver, delivery is always very quick

Ate at Talula's Saturday night, we got there just as it opened for dinner so garden seating (which is first come, first serve) was not a problem. Server was efficient and friendly, it was our first time there and she explained everything wonderfully. We started with the domestic cheese plate which was delicious, I even ate the goat cheese and I normally hate goat cheese. One of the cheeses (my fave) was made by the Von Trapps, of Sound of Music fame, in Vermont. They also brought excellent brioche rolls with basil butter to the table (so warm and flaky). Since it is a bit pricey I got an appetizer portion of the ribbon pasta with truffles and ricotta, it was amazing. Very flavorful and not overly filling, plus the zucchini and summer squash tasted like they were just plucked from the garden. We also got some crispy Yukon Gold potatoes with ricotta and lemon zest for the table, so good as well. My friend got the bluefish with sweet and sour eggplant and kale. I am not exaggerating when I say the eggplant and kale was the best I have EVER eaten in my life. I didn't even think I liked eggplant much until eating Talula's. His bluefish was also perfectly cooked and really fresh tasting. Finally we finished with the ricotta donuts which are served with plum jam and covered with cinnamon. DELICIOUS, it is so worth getting dessert here. Highly recommend this  place, the best food I've eaten in Philly in awhile, fast service and beautiful atmosphere. Talula's is definitely a MUST. Can't wait to try their brunch!

This place is where Arunee used to be and it blows Arunee out of the water. They did a great job with the modern/chic decor and the food is fantastic!! We've been there twice in the past week and it's definitely my new favorite spot. The roti appetizer is delicious and the wild boar entree is as well. It's BYOB for now but I saw a tap at the bar so you know the liquor license is coming soon.

There is an oasis on 66th street and second ave. A restaurant you walk into, are warmly greeted by a pleasant & accommodating hostess. My friend and i were seeking refuge  from the heat and  noise generated because of the second avenue subway construction, when we entered  Mediterraneo. On to the food, we each had different , delicious cold crisp summer salads. and a coconut sorbet. The wait staff were pleasant , efficient and made our summer lunch a delightful experience on a hot noisy day in Manhattan. Prices are moderate.
Absolutely stellar pizza -- this is why I came to the Big Apple! Lombardi's is worth coming to NYC for, and that's not something I say lightly. You'll be thanking yourself for many years to come

So I'm sitting at my office desk in NYC, clearly unsatisfied with my chinese takeout order and remembering how good China Cafe is. I've been going here for the last 15 or so years when I lived around the area and it's definitely the best chinese takeout place I've been to. For some reason, I'm convinced the quality of food is just better than your average random chinese takeout place and feels "cleaner". I've noticed the prices have increased over the years but demand still stays high (especially during lunch and dinner times) which is a clear testament to the food. The workers there have always been nothing but friendly/professional and I am surprised that some of them even recognize me from 10 years ago. Living in NYC now, its mind boggling how terrible some of the chinese takeout places are here and wish there could even be one place that makes food as good as China Cafe.
I ate here for the first time last night  and I was very impressed ! the Peking pork chops were AMAZINGG ! Also had roast pork , duck and chicken with fries rice and all were great !
Incredibly fast, ridiculously cheap, and absurdly delicious. What more could you want? Go for the boiled pork and chive dumplings.
Chicken 4/5.  Donuts 5/5!  Nuf' said.
Completely contrived decor--looks like a "cool" NYC bar from a bad action movie. Makes Houston Street even more disgusting than it has already become.
Delicious crab cakes, both the appetizer and the sandwich! Happy hour until 6:30 means all appetizers are just $6, so I couldn't pass them up! Bar staff were friendly, and kept my glasses full.

Going for the AYCE sashimi during dinner service? think again........... After 2 visits I would have given this place 4.5 stars for the price paid, and the ever expanding list of new food they add every week. But my most recent visit was a disappointment. The sushi chef started hiding some of the sashimi slices of salmon in the fridge. When we asked for more slices of salmon sashimi, the chef would point to a frozen piece of whole salmon and told us that it was frozen and we would have to wait. But what he didn't know was we saw him cut and hide the already prepared and thawed salmon sashimi from our group. For a buffet to hide one of their highlighted items from dinner service to customers is sad and we were all displeased.

I have never written a Yelp review but feel compelled to after receiving the worst service and treatment at this restaurant that I have ever received.  The food here is good and I know people that love this place, but the waiter that served us was obnoxious and rude.  He was passive aggressive and made inappropriate comments to our table.  I will never go back to this restaurant, despite my love of interesting Korean food.  Management should consider giving their servers a course on professionalism and what it means to work in the hospitality industry.

I was looking for a local place to go for dinner and reading ALL reviews selected Catas. I went on a Saturday evening around 8pm before the crowd started to roll in. Quaint setting, beautiful ambiance. Bartender (short young woman w/black hair) made me feel comfortable, offered sitting inside or outside. Additionally, when explain our first time here she offers specials and her personal recommendations: shrimp croquettes-FABULOUS. The lobster mac and cheese was flavorless, 98% full of pasta and lobster no where to be found. When expressed my feeling my waiter comp the lobster mac and cheese. I loved the bacon wrapped stuffed dates. My waiter was attentive, courteous and recommend drinks which we ordered and liked. Menu was broad so plus cause my date doesnt eat seafood or pork. The only reason we rated it a 3 cause it was our first time... will change if we revisit.

Had a great lunch at Drunken Munkey. Excellent food, great ambience and great service. We ordered Lamb Biryani, Cheese toast, saag paneer, sheekh kababs, and Kathi rolls. All were consistently good. Overall great experience. Great for kids too during lunch. We'll be back very soon.

We tried to get a table for 5 on a Sunday evening.  They didn't have the table space for our party.  Waiting for a table, the manger asked us to step away so he could speak to his staff, leaving us to step outside.  We felt so unwelcome we ended up going somewhere else.

No exaggeration, this establishment probably provided me the best service I have ever had at a restaurant. Food was delicious, everything brought out on time and in order. Service, in my experience, has never been so amazing. They treated me like I was long lost family. I was surprised and shocked on how good it was. I will see you soon Salute!
We went last night for the first time and was very impressed with the service and comedy show.  I would differently recommended this place to my friends.

I've been here twice now and if you're into fusion indo-Chinese, this place is great. The spices they use must be locally imported or homemade as you can taste the bold flavors with ease and gratitude (we shared some chili and garlic flavored meat and fish). The bar is also stacked with all the usual culprits, including the full range of Macallans, Johnny and Chivas. I will definitely be back!

Not a good night for them when we went to try it out, it took over 1.5 hours for our entrees to come out (they weren't busy as far as I could tell?) Husbands clam half shell app was (smelly kind of bad) sour-his words. My salmon entree came out wrong but since we waited so long, I didn't say a word (not like the server came back for a bit either). So we had the entrees wrapped after a bite (thank you food runner!) and left. My husband orders his steaks rare.  His steak came out well done, no joke, it was a way over-well done steak...  The only reason I could think of for this expensive error was waitstaff leaving food to cook under the hea tlamp in the kitchen for over an hour, or cooks error or just no management going on in that time? ...but since my salmon was well done and dry...and the wait for food after our apps was long, but I wouldn't have minded so much if the food was good.  Oh well, we wanted to like it based on a Yelp review.  Perhaps it's just inconsistent.  Either way, my husband was not liking his steak and won't ever go back (how can you ruin a steak a rare to a well, well done?)  I tipped over 20% as the server looked really frazzled.  They have a patio, and a bar...I think are the only things that are enticing to me after the experience and in NJ.  I'd try it again, but my husband won't because the food was in it's simplest, dirty, unkept seafood and was sour.  Hope that was just a bad week. Sorry for the poor review, it wasn't good though.
Friendly staff. Delicious crepes with a variety of fillings and combination. Definitely recommended!

Good service.. GREAT FOOD... best buffalo chicken pizza in NJ... Nice decor and environment... only downside is that it is a bit expensive as it is $2.75 for a slice of the buffalo chicken pizza but the slice is worth it and more...

Was very excited to try this place. but it was quite disappointing experience. I have been to shabu-zen in boston (which is only shabu shabu place I have been to) and loved it. however, in my opinion this place is definitely NOT comparable to shabu-zen, especially THE SERVICE. after viewing all the positive reviews, I figured this place could be full on sunday night. but when I went in with a reservation, the place was pretty empty. the waitress seated us right away but never came back to us for about 10 minutes. and never asked if we wanted anything to drink besides water. isnt this the very first thing they should ask after having the customers seated? we even had to call them over to place order! although the food was fine, I dont think Ill be traveling more than 30minutes again to have that kind of service. save your time and make your own shabu shabu at home!!!!

I came here for brunch/lunch recently on a Sunday. It was a party of 6, we ordered 3 appetizers and brunch/lunch entrées along with a bottle of wine. Let me start off by saying the food was absolutely wonderful! (Plates were a little too small) did not walk out full. However food was still amazing. I would give this restaurant 3.5 stars. I ordered the bottle of wine & paid for it in advance because I wanted to treat the table and not have it on the end of the food bill. I gave the waiter my card, I paid, I signed. When we were done enjoying our meal. We got the check for the food. We gave the waiter our credit cards, we paid, we signed, we said thank you and left. As I was walking the waiter asked me to wait he wanted to tell me something. I kindly waited while he was taking another parties order. He came up to me and said that I didn't leave a tip for the wine bill. In my head I was confused because we left a generous tip at the end of our meal and it was all the same table so what did it matter? I said oh I'm sorry. He said it's not about the money it's the principle. I kindly left him ANOTHER tip, however I was so embarrassed and ashamed that this man pulled me to the side and demanded another tip from me. Corrected me if I'm wrong but that was straight out rude. For that I will never come back or recommend anyone else to go there!
That's tiramasu. Also Denise is Versace. Also Tiramasu. Also Versace. This place is great. Denise made my day. Also Versace.

In my opinion, this place should be re-named The Unusually Slow Times.   Pretty much my only criteria for a decent airport restaurant is that service be quick -- people are stopping in for a meal while waiting to board their planes. Based on this criteria alone, the place failed miserably -- my daughter and I ordered a simple breakfast sandwich from the menu, and then sat waiting for 45 minutes.  Once or twice I went up to the bar to ask (politely) whether my order was almost ready.  I was told (with attitude) that it would be out soon.   Finally, with our plane about to board, we had to get up and leave the restaurant and run over to a kiosk to buy a muffin to take with us.  Our order never did arrive (at least not before we boarded the plane).

I came in for brunch on a Saturday, we were seated in the back outdoor seating. I browsed at the menu and figured out what we wanted to order within 10 minutes. However, no server came to take our order and no water was served for a while after we were ready. The restaurant was not busy at the time so I don't understand what would take so long. Our waitress finally came with our waters, chips and salsa and took our order. We ordered the breakfast burrito with no beans, the huevos dos secundos and two corn on the cobs. The breakfast burrito had absolutely no taste and the huevos was super oily and dissatisfying. The corn was probably the best part of the meal. I would not recommend either of those two breakfast entrees. Maybe other foods are better, but I wouldn't come back to try it a second time.

Wow!  Mind is officially blown. This place should not be in business. Bar, food, vibe, service, all positively atrocious. I keep giving this spot a chance because it's so convenient to my apt. But never. Ever. Again. I got a breakfast sandwich and hash browns with a mimosa. Both glasses (I needed two) were dirty. The bar was tacky as if it had never been washed. The people working there look like they have no running water at home....and this might actually BE their home. A potato, any style, is easy and among my favorite things and these hash browns tasted as if  braised in tasteless, old grease for days and a waste of a fresh red onion and red pepper. Eggs were burned, flat and rubbery. The bread was a bread imposter...allegedly Ciabatta...soggy, and just gross. They messed up bacon and cheese in the vicinity of potatoes!   AND in spite of all that, it needed salt.   Just as I'd finished picking through this culinary disaster perfection, cutting it with a seriously half a**ed mimosa....searching desperately for a decent chunk of bacon, a hiking hipster couple entered and sits with dog after being told no dogs.   They may as well have dogs here; and let them eat this slop.   Never again.  I'd give negative starts if possible.

Tashan was really great. I went there for Happy Hour and had drink. I later tried the Chef's tasting menu. I really like their selection of wine. Not your typical Indian restaurant as it serves beef. Try the Waygu beef. I think I could eat that everyday!

Surprised this place isn't too busy. The food is quite good for a very reasonable price. Got a beef cutlet that was as good as any other South End place. Guys working were friendly and quick with the order. My new number one choice for Hartford grinders
Fun drink menu, reasonable prices, fast service, excellent food (cheesesteak wit moonshine & lightening burger)

Having been a little over a year ago with my friend and loving the seafood Fra diavolo and Palmtini , I had wanted to go back. This time my meal was nothing to write home about. Having gone back this time with my boyfriend. We started with fried artichoke and mozz stuffed zucchini blossoms. We had wanted to try something neither of us had either had and the only good thing about em was the peppered mozzarella in the zucchini blossoms- but how can you go wrong with cheese?  So not worth the $13 they were asking for them. He got the lasagna bolognese and I the Veal two ways. His was to have veal in the lasagna and it ended up being a tasteless portion of lasagna accompanied by a veal cutlet layered with vinaigrette marinated field greens and red onions topped with soggy croutons. Mine a perfectly fall off the bone tender osso bucco that tasted like nothing- I mean nothing- I kept adding fresh black pepper hoping for some magic, telling him we should probably just stick to eating at home. Veal#2 was supposed to be Saltimbocca yet where was my prosciutto? It was only grilled pieces of veal tenderloin in Marsala wine sauce... Did the waitress get hungry on her way over to the table? It was all very bland, luckily we had a groupon and the Cucumber Collins the bartender made was delicious. One thing they are consistent on is their cocktails- yummy.

Racist:  I was so disappointed. I heard some good reviews and was very hungry. That is, until the host (who I've been told us the owner and manager) had a 15 minute conversation with a friend while I waited to be seated. I told the lady at the register that I wanted to be seated and she told me that I had to continue to wait for the unresponsive host. Only after a line started to form (maybe bc there were now white people waiting) did he see if I wanted to be seated. I tried to have a conversation with him but he seemed drunk! I am African American, and feel as though he didn't care to seat us bc of that. Maybe it wasn't about race as I saw some customers walk out without paying because they were waiting so long. Maybe everybody there is inattentive. The lady at the register seemed to agree with him as she didn't even ask him to attend to us. Never again. As a show of support for equality or good service, please choose another place to eat.

I have to say that I was very unimpressed with this place. I want to give them the benefit of the doubt and say maybe they were having an off day. I overheard one of the staff members say they were understaffed so maybe that was the source of the problem but our overall experience was pretty rough. Although we were seated quite promptly, our waitress took forever to take our order and then it took almost an hour to get our food. And the restaurant was never THAT full. The bar tender and the waitress were running around very anxiously and whispering stressed things under their breath. Not exactly the nicest environment for a Sunday brunch. The food was decent, at best. Our table got two burgers and two breakfast burritos. The burgers were much better than the burritos. No one who got the burrito was pleased. I hope this place just had an off day but I'm not sure I'm willing to give it a second try.
I came here for brunch on a Sunday and it was packed! I got Audrey's egg sandwich and an oj. Both were delicious. Service was simple but friendly. It was a really cute spot in a nice area.

A cute coffee and crepe shop with a shabby, mismatched charm. Coffee is fairly good. Food is non-greasy and light tasting but not particularly flavorful. Service is friendly and polite. Overall no significant negatives but nothing to write home about.

We did not like this place at all. The staff was unfriendly and also not very knowledgable. Just because you don't like a certain dish, you should be able to tell your guest something about it! We also waited quite a long time for our food and drinks. The food and drinks were also not very good :( Prices are mostly ok.

Food is great, atmosphere is great, drinks are great.  Place is so modestly pricced that it is always packed though so there can be a wait for a table and sometimes, they sort of bring out stuff all at once and not in some order but I love this place. Food could be twice the price in this city and seem reasonable.
Had the cinnamon pancakes, with Bacon. Very very good food, not the best but very fulfilling.  The butters are amazing.

This space is gorgeous and really unique for the city.  Reading the other reviews, you understand that you come for the atmosphere not the food.  Everything at a more reasonable price (breakfasts and cold plates) tastes fair, and the sad truth is you have to spend a lot to have anything decent.  We finally discovered this after spending over $120 on dinner for 2. Hungarian Goulash is delish, but we'll keep returning for the coffee and torte.

Of the Orange Street Markets, this is my go-to for any kind of last minute meat. This is what makes P&M four stars. WAY better meat selection that the other two. For everything else, I prefer the others since they are a bit cheaper with more selection. Especially the fruits and veggies - I find that the selection isfresher with more options at Nica's/Romeo and Ceasers

Good food Reasonable price Good customer service Great ambiance Loud but fun Expect to wait on weekends Bring red wine or rum Bring your friends or family Parking behind the place or at Fullerton for $5

We were really excited for Pok Pok and were happy to see there was no wait on a Sunday afternoon for a late lunch. Unfortunately, we left extremely disappointed and still hungry. I will say I loved the notes on the menu, and everything sounded absolutely wonderful in the descriptions. The atmosphere was lovely and comfortable as well. We ordered 2 dishes and 2 sides of rice, one jasmine and one sticky. The first dish, Yam Makheua Yao ($15), was a mix of smoky eggplant salad with pork and prawns (among other ingredients of course). I am always open minded and make an effort to appreciate flavor before writing something off, but this honestly tasted like a stale ashtray. Everything was dry aside from a slight garlicky-limeyness on the shrimp. We tried to enjoy it, but we left about $10 worth of this dish on the plate. Next we had the Muu Paa Kham Waan ($16), the boar collar. Our sever warned us about the spice which was nice, and it was definitely spicy but tolerable with rice and some Thai tea to wash it down. This dish was much better than the first; we wrapped the meat up in the greens with some sticky rice inside. The portion was very small, and we quickly finished it and began mopping up what was left of the sauce with sticky rice. The rice portion was also minuscule, so we quickly ran out of that as well. I can understand small portions when food is delicious and each bite can be savored, but unfortunately this was not the case. Our server was friendly enough although not overly helpful. She either didn't notice we left the first dish mostly untouched or just didn't ask if there was an issue since we didn't mention it. The best part was the Thai tea with evaporated milk, but you don't need to go to Pok Pok to get that. The rice flavored water was a nice surprise as well. In the end, we wished we would have just gone to Shmorgasberg a couple blocks away, to get something with a lot more flavor for a fraction of the price. I would only go back to Pok Pok with a diehard fan who could show me the best of the menu, but only if everyone promised not to order the cigarette smoke eggplant.
Best pizza around! There's a large bar up front & a nice size restaurant in the back. Have never been disappointed with anything I've gotten there. Price is good for the area.

The food gets 5 stars. Seriously delicious stuff that I crave if I've gone too long without it. If you like New Orleans eating, you'll find a happy home here. The bar service gets 2 stars. I haven't experienced a whiff of hospitality on any visit.

I appreciate the ethics of this place. In a lot of ways its right on. But every time Ive come Ive been grossly underwhelmed with the food. Todays breakfast bacon was so overcooked and cold it lost all the amazing deliciousness of the happy pigs it was made from. What a waste! They should put more effort into the taste of the food than marketing. With such great ingredients it shouldn't be hard to make yummy fabulous food.
Came all the way from Alaska. This place was yummy!!!! Try it out you won't be disappointed. The staff is friendly, a little short on seating, but overall great food!

I ordered delivery and when the pizza arrived it looked and smelled amazing. As I began digging in, I realized there was not just 1 hair, but a chunk of hairs in my pizza. If I hadn't been picking out the large pieces of garlic I probably would have eaten it. Yuck!
Food is ok BUT THEY TAKE FOR EVER!!! Had to walk out without my lunch after waiting a half an hour for my sandwich
Excellent authentic Italian food. Great atmosphere. Feels like home. Service is casual and friendly and superb. Just cannot say enough good things about L'Angolo Ristorante. Buon Appetito!
I was pleasantly surprised.  Food was very good pasta was home made and delicious.. I got the gnocchi Gorgonzola and loved it.

Had a really good time on Saturday night. Kitchen was opened late and the ginger wings were great. Music was a mix of old school hip hop and top 40's.  Lychee martini was good just a little too sweet. Might come back during the week instead of the weekend to actually be able to sit and eat at a table.

Mint Thai Cuisine is now my favorite new Thai Restaurant. Went in one day, had the Chicken Satay and the Massaman Curry, both excellent. My first experience was so good, that I went back a second and 3rd, fourth and now 5 times. It's been great. Nice friendly service and tranquil ambiance. I've been to Thailand twice so I knwo my Thai Food, and Mint Thai ranks high, and as far as Connecticut goes, Mint Thai is the best I've food in the state. They have an awesome team in the kitchen. Those guys really know what they're doing. I went there with a group fo 5 other people one day and got to try a lot of the dishes that I hadn't tried before, all really good, and full of the wonderful flavors of Thailand. These guys excel in Fish and Curry Cookery. Get and Curry  or Fish dish and you can't go wrong. You've got to try the Green Papaya Salad, really refreshing. Most people don't know, but in Thailand they make some of the best BBQ Chikcen & Fried Chicken on Earth, and at Mint Thai, thier BBQ Chicken is out of this world good. ANd you've just got to try the BBQ Pork! Awesome. I love this place, it's my new favorite Thai  Restaurant. Try it, you're sure to Love it too.

Fell in love with this place my first time going in. The food is good and the beer is better. Vegetarian friendly which is always a plus. The atmosphere is nice if you just want to hang out and don't feel like being bothered with typical bar shenanigans. Definitely going back

I am an ardent fan of Chop Chop Grub Shop. The food is divine and the atmosphere is welcoming. It is a real pleasure to get such interesting and quality food on Nostrand Avenue. The real treats are the sandwiches, which are large and filled with generous portions of meat, fish and vegetables, and you get both a salad AND fries, served on a china plate with real silverware. The other nice things is that the restaurant is frequented by people from the neighborhood, both new residents and longtime residents.

We were staying in the Ludlow area from out of town and found ourselves at the Pizza Stone. After trudging through mediocre reviews of other places in the area (and landing on basically only this place that offered vegetarian options) our low expectations were pleasantly met with a fantastic experience. We ordered the starter with mozzarella, basil, and capers and then the VT homegrown pizza. My husband and I could honestly say that it was the best pizza we've ever had. Waitstaff was good, food came out timely. The atmosphere was also great with live local music! Going back again tonight.

If I could give this place no stars I would! Went in yesterday with a group of 3 people after a long day of shopping in NJ, thought I'd stop in before heading back to Manhattan. I had my little 3 lb Pomeranian puppy with me in a bag hidden and put away. It was a Sunday and not crowded at all maybe 5 people in the whole diner. The waitress who has HUGE holes in her ear called "gages" sees my puppy and even makes a comment on how it's cute he is. We order drinks and food. 15 mins later the waitress comes back and says "you can't have dogs in here", I was like are you kidding me you saw 15 mins ago that I had this dog with me. She then got a manager. This basically Jersey looking housewife nasty women who has no idea how to run a business came up to me and said "you can't have dogs in here it's a health hazard, you can leave him in the car! Mind you that is is 90 degrees outside so my in car temperature would be well over 120 degrees if not more. I bring this to her attention and she suggests that I am wrong and the dog would be just fine in the car. I tell her then that I would just like to pay for my drinks and leave. The owner/manager then basically says "NO, you have to pay for your food and you can take it to go"! I tell her "no no no" that's not how it works, I should only pay for it if I have actually received my food and started eating it. She then walks away and has the waitress bring me the full bill of like $40 bucks and the waitress who obviously doesn't want to deal with any confrontation slams the bill on the table and runs away. I leave cash for only the drinks and extra for a tip and leave. The owners son then runs outside as I am in my car about to pull away and starts writing down my plates!!!! ARE YOU KIDDING ME? He even stands behind my car not wanting me to leave. I slam my hand on my horn and he moves just a little bit out of the way while he takes pictures of my car as I pull away. All in all, I will never return. It was by far the worst dining experience I have ever had! I was threatened, treated like crap and harassed. If there are any animal lovers out there I would skip this place or just anyone who wants to go to a place and be treated fairly. Why give your business to a place that treats people like this. The owner is unprofessional and unapologetic. This all could have been fixed by her coming up to me and letting me know that she was sorry I was seated when I shouldn't have had a dog with me. And I would have paid for my drinks like I did and went on my way, but for her to FORCE me to pay for food I never got was beyond me and then to take it to the  extreme of having me followed out to the parking lot and having someone stand behind my car took it to a whole other level! WILL NEVER BE BACK!
Simple and fun. Nice beer, simple food and a great atmosphere. Don't expect cocktails here. Awesome fun for an afternoons drinking.

Actually, more like 2 1/2 stars. I really wanted to support this place since our dining options in the NNE are so limited, so we went last night despite the lukewarm reviews I've heard from several neighbors. Our service was very good and our pizza arrived quickly. Apparently, a little too quickly - the crust was doughy and underdone, and therefore soggy, and the cheese could've used more time in the oven as well. If I'd been alone, I would've sent it back for more cooking. We ordered a marinara and cheese pizza, but there wasn't enough sauce, and it didn't extend far enough out from the center. However, the toppings (mushrooms, sausage, and black olives) were fresh, plentiful and good. The weather was beautiful, so I was a little disappointed that the big garage doors weren't open - maybe next time. We may give this place another try, because we really want them to succeed - I just hope they improve the pizza with longer baking, more sauce.

Go go curry is amazing! We love the food there. And imagine this kind of restaurant near time square - it's affordable and tasty. My friend, who never enjoyed curry before, liked the curry here. I ordered Grand Slam, which contained five kinds of meat and it was amazing and the portion was enough for me. Anyway we loved it!

Let me say that i am a tourist to nyc and know nothing of nyc cuisine but i will try not to sound like a tourist. Anyway, first of all i will say this place is a share food place, so its huge portions, which depends on who you are eating with could be good or bad, whatever. So my girlfriend and i ordered the lobster fra diavolo, which is not something we usually get but it sounded good and we said why not. We both got sodas and found out that no free refills means that youre paying $6.50 for a few sips of soda which kinda pissed me off. The food itself was amazing. My only concern is that the claws were in the marinara sauce as well which i dont know if thats normal for that dish but i found it to be odd to have hands covered with sauce in such a nice place. Its right near time square and really big, so this place is worth it to try. A few concerns is that on the menu, it says it feeds 2-3 yet my girlfriend and i arent huge eaters yet we left only shells on the plate with ease, so keep that in mind. Also the soda thing is what makes my review drop to like 4 and a half stars. Oh well. Its probably not the best italian place in nyc but well worth a try.
Awesome place, awesome food, awesome service. Great for anyone who wants a great chill place to eat.

MENU: delivery.com/#!/cities/v… PROS: The sicilian pizza is out of this world. Super saucy, and just the right balance of fluffy dough - to sauce - to crust ratio. They're very generous with their antipasto, too. CONS: Wouldn't recommend the penne vodka sauce pizza. Too cheesy and not as much sauce. *Still worth the 5-stars for their sandwiches and plain or sicilian pizza.
Two words... TACO TUESDAY (they are white boy tacos but so so good)!
Went there Friday night with friends Food, Drinks and Service was excellent The Mojitos are strong and tasty Will be back again soon

Pretty disappointing. Pretty average tasting, there's definitely better places around here. Came here with a group of 7 and everyone agreed it was nothing special. Service & staff are very cold. They put about 2 pieces of basil on our margherita pizza & when we asked for extra basil on the side, they said they can't give us any for whatever odd reason. So we ordered extra basil on the next pizza & they put about 3 pieces. Maybe basil is a rare item around here? Wouldn't really come here again.

DISGUSTING FOOD! over priced food...has no flavor and there was nothing good that we ate....my sister found a hair in her fries so they took it off the bill but really??? the soda was watered down the clams casino werent even all the way cooked...spend 200.00 in a disappointing meal with my family. none of us even bothered eating our whole meals because it tasted gross.

After attempting to go to Bacchanal for a pre dinner drink and being treated horribly, we decided to go to Piacere instead. I'm glad we did, I cannot speak about the food, but will say that without a doubt we were treated exceptionally well, and were given the royal treatment. Based on the service and the food that I saw being delivered to other tables, I look forward to going back for dinner.
Solid place great experience great service Would recommend everyone try at least once!
Came here for lunch and got 3 rolls combo as well as the tuna dumplings. Everything was fresh and delicious, but particularly the tuna dumplings - a must if you come here!

Any rating less than 5 stars wouldn't justify this place. Food tastes really great. Cooked to absolute perfection. Trust me on this, you really don't have Togo trough an exhaustive list of reviews on this place. Just step in and try any food, u'd be glad 4 u tried this place. Don't forget to try their desserts before leaving.

Came here for the first time with my kids and my sister in law who lives in Brooklyn...I am a queens girl lol but am I glad I came here....first let me start off by saying that the mushroom ravioli is amazing!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! we had 3 types of pies the Brunch pizza, fig pizza and the Bufalina....Awesome!! I am definitely going back again....this is a gem of a place.
It's vegan. Don't be fooled by the big burger in front.

Went here based on the good reputation and overall positive yelp reviews. On a Sunday night, it was pretty quiet and we were quickly seated. The restaurant interior is beautiful, built to replicate the inside of a Mediterranean home. Service was efficient and timely. But unfortunately the food did not live up to expectations. While nothing was particularly bad, for the prices we paid, we felt it should have been much better. We found it irritating that some of the appetizers were almost as expensive as the entrees, with half the amount of food on the plate. I think that you can find better or at least food that is equally good with more reasonable prices somewhere else. We will probably not return.
Not a lot of options for vegetarians, but I've never been disappointed with their build-your-own salad option.

I never understood places that claim to be steakhouses and proceed to cover their steak with flavors that entirely mask the perfect flavor that is steak. I came here with my whole family and ordered a 14oz rib eye. It was cooked to order but was covered in rosemary to the point that I was unable to taste the steak. If spices must be added to steak it should be a very conservative addition. I scraped off the rosemary ( along with the mushrooms that absorbed the rosemary flavor ) and finished my steak. However i was unable to finish the asparagus as it was burnt to the point where the spears were pure black. Wont be back.

As Burlington VT goes this place is not the place to go for dinner. A steakhouse should know how to cook good steak. Salt, pepper, and maybe butter. But not drenched in rosemary sauce. Too much. Sides should compliment the steak. Service is aloof and not really accommodating. Unfortunately this place was not good. Just wait in line for something better. Its worth it.

We ordered a couple of dishes including a Mutton Biriyani. The Mutton in the Biriyani was horrible. It was so damn rubbery that we simply didn't eat more than a bite. The furniture looks horrible. They probably got it from a dumpster.
I'm crazy for the pizza here!So cheesy and creamy :p this place really popular and one slice is enough to fill your stomach and make you feel good.

Can't wait to come back!!! I was there with a group of 8 people and we all loved it!!! Food is AMAZING!!! Gotta try the lomo saltado, the arroz con pollo, the salmon a lo macho... It's just delicious. Everything we ordered was perfect. Only by trying the appetizers you are able to know that the main courses are going to be great. The drinks are also really good. Joey and Jessi... Great bartenders. All the staff is friendly and willing to help you. I highly recommend this place. Great spot to spend a night with family and friends.
Great service, good food, great atmosphere

A French restaurant with Mexican and Mediterranean decor always frightens me. And I was right. We ordered the steak tartar and the baby octopus. The octopus dish was good but not classic French. The steak tartar was flavorless and unappealing - stay away. They did have a nice wine list and cute atmosphere. However I do not recommend.

Amazing. All round a fantastic experience. Service was impeccable. It was packed on a Saturday night; we waited maybe about 15 minutes to get seated for our reservation. The host was very apologetic even though we weren't in a rush to be seated. We had the magical Bihari Gohst, the meat just fell off the bone, such a medley of beautiful flavors. The Baingan Ka Salan was also mind-blowing. Desserts were spectacular. Fabulous. We will certainly be back!
There is no better place to experience Philly
Wasn't impressed. Attended bridal shower lunch. Food was mediocre at best but service was horrible/ wait staff clueless.
Warm, friendly owner.  Great sandwiches.  Fresh food.  A great local deli.

I do not care what negative reviews you might read or might have read, this place is legit and it could not get any better than the $29 it cost for dinner. 2 glasses of wine, 2 desserts which we selected tiramisu and ice cream.  Dinner could not have been better. Atlantic salmon covered in a lemon garlic sauce with zucchini and mashed potatoes, and chicken cutlet parmigiana was to die for. For a small local restaurant & café on Avenue B I give it 10s across the board.

I order from this place at least once a week from work in Princeton. I try to get something new every time, and I haven't been disappointed yet. No delivery fee, great staff, and when I was doing Keto, they were very accomodating. I wish I could give them 6 stars, haha.
If you enjoy eating steak, this is the place to go! The skirt steak was absolutely delicious and the shoestring fries were just the perfect addition to the meal.

This is the most amazing bakery i have ever been to in my entire life! They are la bomba!!! Blanca & Yandrel make you feel like you are at home and part of the family. Hope this place expands in the future. As people begin to discover this treasure in belleville its beginning to get more packed and packed
VIP treatment with my son knowing the owner topped off the evening with great food, dessert and wines! I shall return!!!

Bring your sweatpants and loosen your belt because they are very generous here. I've had a couple dishes: steamed buns, pork noodle soup, beef noodle soup and spicy beef soup and of course, their signature dumplings! It's very casual, mostly Chinese customers which is always a good sign. The decor or atmosphere isn't 5 star quality but the food makes up for it. For the beef and pork noodle soups, they give you a TON of noodles. Like the amount of carbs one would eat pre-marathon. All homemade. The beef one was ok- not too generous with the beef. The pork, however, they were very generous with. The broth is decent. The steamed buns are cheap and delicious, nothing extraordinary by typical bun standards. The spicy beef soup was vegetable laden, filling and SPICY. They are very generous with the meat but skimped on the noodles (which isn't bad, you'll struggle to finish it). I wish this place was open later- their fried dumplings are perfect drunk food. Greasy, savory and fresh! They're also very affordable. Seating is limited so it's best you don't come at peak lunch and dinner hours. This isn't a date spot by any means, simply a place to get some AMAZING food. I always end up waddling out cursing your small stomach. Cash only.

My husband and I live right around the corner from this restaurant.  This location was the  previous location of our favorite restaurant in Caldwell and we felt weird going.   We finally went about 2 months ago and we were not that impressed.   We had 2 artisan pizzas and an appetizer as well as 2 soft drinks and our bill was $60.00!  60.00!!!!.  Way Way overpriced.   So we can say we went but not again.  I'll stick to my Boboli.

A friend of mine wanted to try something different and new, Pitaziki nails it--simple, good food that appeals to the gourmet foodie or the guy next door. Awesome, awesome, and more awesome. Just tried Pitaziki,  for the first time...will be going back for full lunch or dinner...or both

DO NOT EAT HERE. I happened to know of  the "chef" at this dump. His name is Steve and I dont think he has bathed in weeks if not months. He is preparing your food. We odered a pizza and a pasta dish, and I happened to see this guy I only knew as "steve the dirtbag". I asked the waitress what is that guy doing in the kitchen? She replied that he was the chef. We left before our food arrived, no way in hell I was eating that.
good spot

We saw a TV show that featured this place.  We liked the idea of different Italian grandmothers cooking the meals from their home towns in Italy.  It was not a disappointment.  The food we had was delicious and it was such a nice change of pace from Manhattan. The service was top-notch as well.  They were always checking to see if we needed anything and were always refilling our water glasses.  If you want out of the grind of Manhattan, this is the place!

More like a 3.5 Yes they are a bit pricey but I love the fact that their food has quality ingredients and it's not a long wait. I always get the chicken lo mein. The only downside other then their pricing and parking situation is that occasionally the lo mein is a bit oily from them not draining it properly when putting it in the take out container. I'm always shocked they are still in business because it always seems like I am their only customer but maybe I'm just lucky. p.s. stop being stingy with the duck sauce please lol

I was deciding between 3 and a 4 stars, and decided to round up and give Thelma 4 stars, and then switched it back to 3 stars after writing out the full review.
