However half the menu seems to be unavailable (no lamb burger, no skewers, no reuben ... Wth?) 2.  The servers and bartenders are all knowledgeable.  Especially impressive service considering the bartender looked pretty uncomfortable rolling off the laundry list of things that weren't available ... ... However the staff always seems to completely change and the food seems to come out of the kitchen REALLY slow. 3.  The whiskey list was impressive! ... Again though, a good deal of what's listed is unavailable and some selections are a bit overpriced. To be fair, it was explained the whiskey list was changing extensively soon 4. The draft list is the best reason to go! ... Not so much for the cocktail menu though which is uncreative, pretentious, and overpriced With a spot this good, with the servers trying as hard as they are, I can't help but walk away with the impression that this place SHOULD be better than it is. It just can't seem to stop tripping over itself.  I prefer Growlers (about two or three blocks away). Selection isn't quite as good as The Barrel House's (should be), but they definitely have their act together when it comes to running their business ...

Amazing! My husband and I celebrated our anniversary here recently. Great atmosphere, great drinks, and the food is phenomenal! For drinks, I recommend the Rosa Margarita, it's delicious. For food, try the Queso De Mariscos and the Molcajete de Pollo. You won't be disappointed!

I went for the first time with a couple of friends and we all thought the food was fantastic!! I got the chicken and shrimp hibachi dinner. Both the chicken and shrimp had great flavor and the chicken was not dry, which I have experienced in many other hibachi restaurants. The fried rice was a little bit different (they seem to use a different sauce) but was excellent!! However, the menu does not clearly state in all hibachi dinner sections that the fried rice is $2 extra. I have never seen an extra fee for fried rice at any other hibachi place I have been to, but the rice was definitely the best I have ever had!! The restaurant was clean and there is ample parking. There is no designated waiting area which caused some confusion. We sit an area with tables and chairs we assumed to be the waiting area (others had done the same) but then a waitress from the bar area came over and asked if we wanted anything, so it was actually the bar area.  The service here is adequate. The hostesses were not rude but were definitely not too friendly. We were brought our drinks and our order was taken but the waiters did not come back once during the meal to see if we needed anything or to see if everything was okay. The chef was pretty good but definitely not as enthusiastic as I have seen elsewhere. We are definitely all coming here again!!!
The best crab I have ever had! Their crab legs and crab rolls are to die for! Great atmosphere and friendly service. I love this place!  You need to check it out!

Had dinner one night and split the tacos for two. Good sized portion, but they failed to tell us that they add an adobe sauce which in our opinion was super spicy. So much that it killed all flavor. The next night we were walking by after dinner and decided to sit outside for a quick drink and try the nachos. After waiting over 30 minutes, the nachos arrived. The delay was due to a banquet that was going on inside. Would have been nice if our waitress would have told us. Once again, the adobe sauce was added heavily...we couldn't eat the nachos. Shame, it's a nice looking restaurant with outdoor seating and good ambiance. But if you don't have a palate for hot food, save your money and go elsewhere.

stellar cocktails, cheese board is wonderful.  I haven't eaten dinner there yet but I plan too.  The staff knows their product, so important for a restaurant.  I enjoy their patio area except for when the dumpster is full behind the building and it smells.

Service was a bit on the slow side despite not being very busy. 14 Dollar burger was incorrectly cooked both tries- ordered medium rare and got a hockey puck. My friend's bizarre fish and pasta dish was rather tasteless. Wouldn't go back again.

We were in the area and celebrating our 25th wedding anniversary and found this restaurant on Yelp! We were pleasantly surprised with not only the food but also the atmosphere. Our waitress Beth was excellent, attentive and personable. If we are in the area again we will return!!

This is some good stuff. You can't get food like this everywhere. I love the authenticity of this joint. Every time I go I get something different and I haven't been let down yet. Get their carne asada tacos! You can't go wrong! Worth every penny!

The food was good, not great. The restaurant is crowded and very noisy.  A waiter (not ours) removed our  half full wine bottle from the cooler in the middle of our meal and it had to be retrieved from the kitchen. In all, we were somewhat disappointed.
amazing cappuccinos  ... the black & white crêpe is amazing with yummy fresh berries ... very cute place to sit over coffee with a date or a friend :) i'll definitely be back soon
If you have not been it is a must, excellent meal and nice Borolo wine with dinner. Make it a point to go there if you have not.

Very good pizza and we love the rock shrimp. If they don't have the pizza combination you are looking for, they are willing to do a special pie for you (we love olives and artichokes on a white pie). The inside is a little dated, but the staff is very friendly and it's good for a large group.

So I live in Mass, but my fiancé brought me here (multiple times now) claiming it was the best pizza in the world. Now I don't know about the best pizza in the world, but I have to admit it is some of the best pizza I have ever had. We love the margarita and the simple, yet delicious, original tomato. The pizza is extra crispy and is always served up fast. We also love getting the liters of soda here because its made at a local beverage co nearby! It is also in a great location in downtown New Haven which makes it great for a night out or to get dessert at Libby's right next door! Cons: It is ALWAYS mobbed here, unless you go right at open (11) or randomly during the week. This may seem picky, but the napkins here are horrible lol They basically have no purpose. Also, parking is usually very difficult on a busy night night like Friday or Saturday.
Don't waste your time on this place the staff is rude and very slow service. The BBQ is just ok there are better places in Brooklyn to go.
Good food. At a decent price.  They even made us a request for food. The food also came pretty quickly
Food is fantastic. Exceptional service. Great for afterwork drinks or with a group. Will be back very soon. A+ all around!

The T-bone steak was very nice. It is  seasoned very well and cooked perfectly. The only downside for me is the overwhelming amount of butter. It is a bit heavy. Also, the service is not quite on par. We waited for quite a while just to get salt and pepper.
finally found out why the line here is always so long! place was amazing, especially when you're starving at 3am! lol
Great plate of food!
This is my favorite wraps spot in NYC... Love The Howling.... pumpkin seed & date dough was a unique twist...

After eating the traditional whiz and onion cheesesteak for a couple days around Philly, my friends and I wanted to get something slightly different so we headed to Tommy DiNic's. It was 1pm on a Monday and there was a decently long line but we got through it really fast. The girl taking orders and getting sodas was hustling for sure. I ordered the roasted pork with provalone and hot peppers. This might have been the best sandwich I found in Philadelphia. The meat was unbelievable, it went really well with provalone, and the peppers were blistering hot. Its really nice to order hot peppers at a sandwich shop and get an actual HOT pepper instead of cherry peppers. The rest of the market was really cool too but it would be hard for me to try anything else when I know I can get that sandwich again.

I had been dying to go here the entire time I lived in the area but the brunch line was always ridiculously long! Finally on my last day I got a table and I was blown away. I had the chicken pesto sandwich and it was melt in your mouth good. The pesto was so delicious I asked the server (we sat at the bar) if I could get some to take home with me to make some pesto pasta for friends the next day. He went and asked the chef and she was more than happy to give me a cup for $6 which is way less than most gourmet pesto out there. I used it for the next few days in basically everything. Perfection. Four stars only because I wish it were bigger or took reservations for brunch.
This place is great. My favorite bar and I have been there since the day they opened. Great beer selection. Always something new. Servers are the best and really know there stuff.  Love the burgers!

Can't say I agree with the negative reviews below. This location is consistent with all other Jersey Mikes I've been to. They've never been too busy, even during lunch, and  quite friendly and familiar for a chain. We've always enjoyed their food and consider the "mini" to be large enough for a lunch sized portion.

I got to Peaches Hothouse on a Saturday at 8pm. We had a party of 6 and the place is really small so we had a wait of almost 2 hours. The good thing is they let us order drinks and sip them outside on the bench. We finally got to eat i order the fried green tomatoes- delicious!. I got the fried chicken hot- it wasn't spicy to me. and the mac and cheese which was also really good. Ill be back just won't go on a sat. night with a  large party.

This would probably be OK to good pizza in some place, but in New Haven, with so many great pizzerias, this is just a mediocre pizza fare with mediocre service to boot. I came to pick up my pizza and decided to eat eat there, but regretted it quickly- the place is tiny and people constantly struggle to squeeze past my seat, when I asked for a cup of water I was handed a tiny flimsy plastic cup that the guy filled with lukewarm water from the faucet.  I thought about buyingt a drink from the fridge selection but then noticed they have no recycling bin for plastics or cans, so I decided to pass. Too many places with better service and food in this area to come back here again.
Absolutely terrible. Unclean, and the food is just terrible. Do yourself a favor and steer clear of this place.

I came here when visiting Hartford, Conn. Firstly, the service was very slow until we had a waiter come over to our table.  Secondly, I thought the cuisine was not what was expected. My boyfriend and I ordered a tomato pie and a caesar salad. The tomato pie was very small for $18 and this should be an appetizer plate instead of under the entrees section. The salad for $9 was not fresh! The lettuce was brown, which should of not! It was loaded with caesar dressing to hide the color as well. Also, our waiter was not very helpful and was very disrespectful as I explained that I was unhappy with the meal. Usually a waiter would be happy to make the customer feel at home and try to resolve any issues. This was not the case! I will not return.

I recently found myself hanging in Brooklyn for the day, and my friend Toni and I wound up at Bijan's at the recommendation of a colleague.  While I usually follow my own favorites, I'm glad I listened this time. The space has a creative vibe and being an artist, I loved that they had abstract impressionism on display.  Didn't even pick up a menu yet and I was like "yessss, like that".   The specialty cocktails are inventive (and tasty).  I don't usually go for a second drink (lightweight!) but I indulged this time, haha. I had the Lime Sumac Chicken and it was amazing, just right. For dessert, I had the Tiramisu, which I was told is a family recipe.  Verdict: To. Die. For. The service was great and how I like it: casual, efficient and not overbearing.  Also bonus was the music selection: eclectic yet fun.   I'll definitely be back!!

that place Outdoor seating available The place is big so you can seat there chat and chill for hours The food is delicious The Mac and cheese is delicious you must try it It's enough to share And try the peel shrimp I didn't care much for the drinks but the food was delicious Affordable for 2 we spend $110 but we had 2 drinks 2 meals 2 starters and the staff is very friendly Parking is available around  we literally spend 4 hours there chatting

If you are going for Henry's, you should definitely get a delicious homestyle breakfast sandwich served on a bagel with your choice of toppings, any time of day. Usually very busy and you will never be surprised to spot a familiar face when picking up your sandwich. Calling ahead is your best bet!

I loveeeee it here! Ropa Veja & coconut shrimp are the best! Bring your own that can be mixed into a sangria or mojito! Street & meter parking. The owner is a doll and always accommodating! Fun lively Saturday night out kind of place !

The best rodizio! My family and I have been coming here forever. Everyone has their birthday here! The sangria is amazing. The menu is huge so it can fit anyone's appetite. Iv tried a few places in the area and Fernandez is for sure the best!

I was surprised to see how high this was rated! Went in shortly after what i'm assuming was a re-opening. My boyfriend and I stopped in a few days after we noticed the place. The staff was friendly, but a bit slow. I have a feeling they were all new. The place was pretty empty early on a Wednesday night and we were sat at a table RIGHT by the door. I didn't think of it until other people started coming in and could just stare at me eating. You could also see the line for Fudruckers at our table. The manager came to greet us with homemade chips. THEY WERE DELICIOUS. Boyfriend ordered a beer and ordered a Sangria. Sangria was actually pretty good, a bit too sweet. Waiter took our order. We both ordered burgers. My first sign to run away was when my waiter didn't ask how I wanted my burger cooked. Food came out at a reasonable pace and was ABSOLUTELY DISGUSTING!!!!!!!!! Considering how pricey this place is i was APPALLED. The menu advertises 100% fresh and homemade ingredients. COMPLETE AND TOTAL LIE. The "kobe" burgers seemed like frozen patties that had marinated in the dirt of the stove-top. It was rubbery and there were charred parts around the edges that I actually thought I chipped my tooth on. Nothing on my burger was fresh. The fries were stale. And gross. I'm usually willing to give things a second chance....not this place.
After going here for many years, I had a really disappointing few experiences.  Ownership didn't seem to care.  I won't be going back, bummer
Great atmosphere, and good Mexican food. The drinks are pretty surprising. A nice place for a fun lunch or dinner.
I go about twice a week for my coffee... Besides the coffee always being so fresh it is great to be greeted at 630 am with a smile... Makes the start of your day even better

It's okay....came here weeknight with friends for dinner and couple drinks. Wed was karaoke night which was mildly entertaining but was still not too crowded with the most random group of customers. Place has two entrances, one for bar and one for restaurant which I didn't really get since they brought you to the same place. Food was average. We ordered salads and wings. I would only come here for beer and bar food for drinks after work. Nothing special. They do have specials each night and coupons going around in papers. We stayed for two hours and had four different waitresses. None of them seemed to care. Don't get me wrong, they did their job and were not rude but again...nothing special. We had to flag them down if wanted something and they brought us check before asking if we were done.

Charming place. Good tasting food, although very small portions that add up VERY quickly. Small wine pours that make a regular glass of wine 1 & 1/2 times the price of every other place. They claim they're 4 oz pours, but more like 2-2 & 1/2. But wine pours should be 6 oz. not 4 oz to begin with.

I do not get the good reviews- Dry ribs Bland brisket The worst German potato salad ever--- Food sucked! The lighting was so bright I swear I left with a sunburn Beers were cold and they did have a great selection Wine they offered two- One was out So...Merlot only Idk- I'll be back for a beer but definitely not for dinner I really was hoping this place would be great It could be Needs a whole new concept as the BBQ thing simply isn't workin!

I finally got  a chance to come to craft house...if you are looking for some really good comfort food like  beef brisket...chicken&waffles.. mac& cheese etc..you definitely need to try it out. I don't drink but the company I was with said they was very happy with their drinks/ top beer selections.The place is amazing in/out with a nice ambience to it.
Thai girl on UES seeking Thai food. Finds Up. Takes parents. Parents raaaaave, Thai girl scores big. The end. Get: Grilled chicken plus sticky rice Minced chicken basil rice plus egg Crispy pork

By surprise we were there on Taco Tuesday. Five tacos for $4.99. What a treat! We had five tacos de carnitas and five tacos al pastor. They were both scrumptious. A small bag of homemade crispy chips for each was a freebie. Also included were various sauces-- the fiery pickled onion was great. We know where we will be next Tuesday!
The food was great and they gave huge portions of food.  The decor was super sexy and they played fantastic music. My favorite are the stuffed shells, Amazing!!! : )
All the food is solid here, however it's their brazilian/american style burgers that keep me coming back. Check out their desserts as well. And the acai shake!
OMG these are so yummy! I had two vanilla, two strawberry poppy, and two rose petal. At first I was skeptical but after the first bite I was HOOKED!!!! Yum
Really funny how Honest Tom's tacos is down the road from here, but between the two, Cucina has my vote. Best truck in the world, hands down, would definitely recommend.

I give this place one brown star because it sucks sh*t ! It's Dirty and the ADT alarm beeped loud the entire time no waitress or waiters were around we asked was the chef Mexican in their advertised authentic Mexican cuisine and she said he was American the homemade guacamole was bought out of a store tasted like plastic waitress was a b*^ch was mad that we asked if they had Mexican soda acted like she didn't have time to answer question mean while we were the only ones in there we ordered a bunch of food waited 30 minutes no one was around to say it's coming or u want more to drink so we walked out Thumbs down for this place and the pizza place down the way we ate at was fuckkng gross as well dirty and run by junkies it's obvious here in Wilmington or lake placid New York bring ur own food or go to the most expensive restaurants they have so u know u will get a good meal but shop around for ur restaurants walk in inspect ask questions look at menu and wait staff if looks clean and wait staff looks clean give it a whirl! Oh yeah and it's owned and operated by Asians sushi or Mexican same place two menus bahahaha
So good!!

This is a little cozy deli, the food r amazing the bread they use is light and has a slight sweet taste and the tuna salad is divine. Everything is done with care and passion, customer service r friendly and warm welcoming. Definitely recommend to friends and family...

I am only in philly for the second time, so I had never heard of Burgerfi before. However being from New York I am well acquainted with this type of classy burger joint. They have been a new trendy thing popping up everywhere in the NYC area for a few years now. However Burgerfi exceeded my expectations. I was with a group that had food restrictions so we could only order the onion rings and french fries (largest sizes of each) and it was more than enough for the 5 of us to snack on. To make it a little more interesting I asked Shandae (I got the name of the lady at the register because she was that good) for a bunch of the sauces too. Many restaurant workers get annoyed with this kind of request, especially with customers who are just snacking. However not only was Shandae totally cool about it, but I got little sides of alllllll their fry toppings- all the sauces/seasonings, the melted cheese and chilli! After such an amazing experience I cannot wait to return when I can order burgers too. While the food being well above average was part of why my dining experience was so great, it is even more because of how amazing Shandae's service was- the perfect blend of friendly, professional, and understanding!
Nice place great service good food Kind of expensive Had the beef burger on gluten free bun w/ sweet potato fries & a side of the house mustard.

Although it's a bit pricey it's so worth every penny.  I go often and have never had a bad meal or bland anything.  Always 3+ vegan baked goods in my experience.  Love the atmosphere.  My kids love it here, too... 8&5.  Highly recommend supporting this local joint

We like this for delivery- food is good, but the few times we've eaten at the restaurant the service was lacking. The thin crust pizza and house salad are tasty (tip- must ask for the dressing mixed in for the salad ). The cheesy garlic bread is a good value when getting delivery for the family.
Great stop! Perfect coffee, delicious baked goods, clean restroom, ve

Went to cafeteria at 10:40pm on a Wednesday night with a table of 5, walked in and there were about 5-7 empty tables in the restaurant and told by the hostess that it was a 20 minute wait.  When I questioned him he said that they only had two tables for large parties because the plates were too big and didn't fit on other tables. We decided to wait anyway and while we waited the manager continuously told us to move out of the entry way. When I questioned him about why we couldn't be seated he said that they were a high volume restaurant and couldn't move tables together for us because their drunk inebriated customers who were going to come in in an hour were more valuable. Extremely disappointed and will not return.

Yelp, please change the price to "$$$".  There is no way that this is "$$", that and indication of cheap, but this place isn't cheap at all.  I order 10 piece of sushi, and ended up with a $35 bill.  That's $7 for an order of 2 piece, may be Sushi at Newark is expensive.  I live in SF, even SFO sushi bar is not this pricy.

The lack of competition in the area really allows this place to shine: a medium sized fish in a small pond. The food is delicious, if salty and overpriced.  The beers are cold, if manhattan-priced. The proximity to the train station may explain this, but looking at rent in the area they definitely must be bringing home a lot of money. Average to above average in all aspects: food, service, decor. Waaay above average in terms of price, and I usually don't place a premium on quantity over everything else.

This has got to be the best pizza I have ever tasted in my life. The spinach artichoke pizza has a great crust with so much flavors. I'm from Boston and I dream of this pizza! The wait staff is super friendly and the ambience is a real chill spot. The beer I remembered was very cheap for a large size.

FINALLY!!!!! GOOD latin food in this area!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Visited this spot with the hubby on Friday night and I was very impressed with the service and food. This establishment just opened, so I know it will just keep getting better in time. I appreciate wait staff that are attentive and food plates that are big enough to get you full! Thank you Jora, we will be back!!
Chicken cutlets are great and awesome catering trays. It is on the expensive side, but you get what you pay for. The fresh mozzarella is great

Best prices for lunch! They have set menus everyday of the week from 12-3pm that is $7.50 for a soup or salad, an entree and a drink. How can you go wrong with the deal! I have come here a million times especially for the chicken it is the best! Oh and the Lomo Saltado too definitely can't forget about that. Will continue to come back for a long time!
I had the fish n chips and was probably the best I ever had...different choices of tarter sauce too.

This review is long overdue. My husband and I love this place. Mostly because we love the escargot appetizer. They have other wonderful dishes as well like the seared filet mignon topped with foie gras and the seafood linguini. This restaurant is BYOB which is a also a plus. But I'm hearing that they have started their own wine menu recently. Only thing is that its very noisy inside and can be a bit crowded at times. Its also better to make a reservation.
The turkey samich place is mmmm....drool worthy!

Came here with my wife for dinner shortly after arriving in Hartford with the train from NYC. We were promptly seated outside which was enjoyable. She ordered a salad which was drenched in dressing and otherwise rather tasteless. I had the meatloaf, which was terrible. The food was too cold, the meatloaf was bland and lacked spices, and the beans were unsatisfying. Mashed potatoes alone did not cut it for me .... Next time I would try another place before coming here again. We left disappointed.

Family and I stopped in and ordered a bit of everything.   The scallion pancakes are excellent as are the fried dumplings.    We shared a table with a mother and daughter from England,  so if you enjoy a social aspect to dinning this is a great place.    As a reminder bring cash.
Owner is awesome. Food is delicious. Ambience is solid. All good in the hood.
Awesome food!

Cute BYOB with a hidden little patio in the back. The pizza is very good- interesting combinations and we've loved them all. The sausage fontina pie was our favorite so far, and the special pie with corn was delicious. The meatballs are excellent and the special salads are always really fresh and out of the ordinary.
The best pizza and Spumoni ice cream know to MAN! Such a Brooklyn Staple and with good reason! Love this place!
Funnel Cake good!

Just had lunch today with a friend. I have visited Georgia, and the quality of the dishes is absolutely on par with the local cuisine. We had some eggplant salad, the khinkali (small dumplings) and a khachapuri (like a pizza filled with cheese and eggs on top). Reasonable pricing, great service and a good atmosphere, with a back garden that would be great for taking someone on a date. They have a wine menu, very important on a restaurant from a country that claims to have invented wine. It's a shame they don't have Georgian beers, but maybe that is asking too much. Even though they could have had a more traditional decoration, I highly recommend this place.
Mushroom Swiss Cheese Burger with GoldBurger's special sauce DEEEELISH!!! Perfectly done!

It is always a great thing to see the red Hong's cart on church street. Fresh and extremely delicious dumplings made right in front of you. This can mean a line and a wait, but if your hungry and in the mood for these yummy dumplings definitely worth your time.

Wow- has this place gone downhill! My family has been going to the Townhouse since before I was born and they were originally located in New Haven. As a child we would always grab quick family meals at their old location in Branford. The food was great (especially the seafood dishes) and all of the staff, including the members of the family who own the restaurant, were always so warm and friendly. We were heartbroken when they were forced to suddenly close at their old location, but were beyond excited when they re-opened at their current spot. Unfortunately that amazing service that was previously offered at their old location did not transfer to the new one. Although their food has remained pretty good, the service has seriously gone downhill. Due to the poor customer service, i.e. some of the waitresses were very impatient and stand-offish when taking our orders and would be snide when pointing out when our meals had come out wrong, we decided to stop going in for meals and resorted to doing take-out. But tonight was the "straw that broke the camels back" moment. I placed an order for two hot-opened faced turkey sandwiches, but when we sat down at home to eat we realized we had been given pot roast instead of turkey. I called the Townhouse to let them know of the mistake. The father of the family who owns the restaurant answered (someone I have become a familiar with as a loyal customer since childhood) and he had remembered taking my order but repeatedly insisted that I had told him roast beef- which isn't what we had gotten anyways. When I told him that I was certain I ordered turkey he became quite hostile and kept saying to me "Well, what do you want me to do about?"Realizing that he was not a believer in the "customer is always right" motto I let him know of my family's disappointment in the direction his business has been heading and that I would no longer be ordering from them. And while I do not think the Parthenon's food is quite as good as the Townhouse-sigh-I will be ordering my turkey sandwiches and all other diner food cravings from them from here on out, just to avoid having to fight with someone to get what I originally ordered.

I went in for brunch and had the pork roll sandwich with an avocado on it, and it was delicious. It also came with home fries that were great. The service was also prompt and not overwhelming. I also got a coffee and a wheat beer to accompany the meal. Would go back.

Went here for the first time and I gotta say the food was very good and the view of the city was amazing..  Our waitress was very nice and made sure we had everything we wanted and more..  I will be returning in the near future for sure.

Now Il Falco is open in LIC.  WOW!  The atmosphere is crisp and clean...old world Italian elegance.  The food, service, staff and atmosphere was top notch!  High-end Italian food with a loving flare!  It is a must if you are in Queens!

My friends and I went to The Happy Rooster for dinner last Thursday night and had a great experience. We were greeted with nothing but kindness and our food was PHENOMENAL! I had the veal chop which was the best I have ever had, my friends had the lobster rolls and fish tacos - all three meals were outstanding. We moved to the bar after dinner to enjoy some cocktails and our bartender Diane was so sweet and attentive. I cannot say enough good things about the service and the food at this place. I will definitely be going back.

My family of 5 ate at this restaurant last night.  The atmosphere was cool.  Sports bar all the way.  Beer menu was good.  Make sure you get the 16oz of beer for $1 more.  The food...well....three of us ordered the corned beef dinner with cabbage and potato.  We were all VERY disappointed!  The corned beef was shredded (not sliced) and not moist.  It was basically a small shredded pile along with a few very wilted pieces of cabbage and 1 small potato (hard) cut up set in a bowl of hot water.  The price was $9.99 which was reasonable but I would have rather they charge a bit more and give you a better meal!  My husband ordered the Reuben with slaw and loved it. My daughter ordered a pulled pork sandwich which was just okay.  Overall the place was just okay but a disappointment.  Stick to the beer/bar thought process and forget the restaurant for the supposed Irish dinner.  Shame!

Slow to serve and only decent food. We had the Brazilian steak, calamari, chorizo, and one of their special pork plates. They were good but I've had better. The chorizo appetizer was huge! It was salty but nice and smokey. The service was nice but the food took forever to come out. This place is better as a bar than a restaurant, considering the clientele and how quick it took for drinks to arrive compared to food.

I went back to Taim last night and it was as delicious as ever! All of the falafel flavors are vibrant, the bread is soft but absorbent, and the sauces are incredible. The prices can't be beat either. It's very cramped inside, but grab a falafel and eat on the street.
I had the chicken bacon ranch wrap and it was very tasty. There is minimal seating and no facilities, but a great place to stop while wandering church st.
Maybe the best pizza in New Haven. Best sauce at the very least. Always makes me happy in my fat belly.
best pizza in brooklyn!!!  ...(enough said!!!)

Great food! ~ The largest, juiciest buffalo wings I have ever bitten into! The tastiest bruchetta and pizza! Great Service ~ Unfortunately not enough staff to cover the busy times....but...Jud is great. Deserves a raise. One of the best personalities I have ever come across in a waiter/server. He cares for all his customers and treats them as if they are family. Great Atmosphere ~ The bar has a family feel to it...like Cheers!
great patio, the friendlist owner, and some tremendous beers. christy's makes me a happy, fat baby.

We went to On20 with friends at the end of August to help them celebrate an anniversary. I had been there for lunch with a friend before and at that time the experience could not have been more perfect. This time it was far less so. The food was excellent and well portioned. I got the fish and everything was cooked to perfection. They also took care of my gluten restrictions so gracefully. But my friends ordered the pork and reported later that it was surprisingly tough. The real problem was the pacing of the meal was off. Though we mentioned we wanted wine with dinner, perhaps because we ordered from the Prix Fixe menu, the food came out and we were never offered another chance to order wine. The server was young and seemed very inexperienced. The dinner felt rushed when earlier it had been leisurely, with time between courses. The worst part - the cocktails were terrible. Worst Cosmo I've ever had. And yep - I'm kicking myself for not sending it back.  I've run into this recently where it seems that young bartenders don't tend to drink what they serve. My friends Margarita was terrible as well. Martinis are a pretty simple thing to make and make well. (I confess my husband is a former bartender from the old school.) But I didn't think it was a lot to expect a good one in a place that prides itself on excellence. As with any dining experience I think you have to balance cost and what is possible. So here's the grade for the other night. Drinks -F, Food - A/B+, Service-C, Atmosphere - A+. Don't get me wrong - I will try this place again -because the food is terrific - but if it do I may not do the Prix Fixe. I think the experience may improve. And next time - I'll tell them how to make the drinks. :)

Loved the service and the food. I had my bday dinner here with 20 people (they actually stuck the multiple tables to make a single long one) and we all had a great time with very delicious food. The Xiao Long Baos were the best I have had in Manhattan. Actually, I would say that it is on par with those I ate in Shanghai, China. All the food we ordered were very 'clean', making it high quailty and appetizing.   The staff were very accomodating and friendly, which made the experience just so much better. Everyone should definitely try this place out!
healthy and tasty.

When I have worked a twelve hour day, having to listen to the wretched person behind the bar where I sat because even though there were plenty of empty tables that remained empty during my brief visit to this place that embodies all that is wrong in the new york dining scene, tell me that she did not get me the glass of water I asked for three times because she had "17 other things to do." Whatever, I get it, but it's not like I hadn't already ordered a bottle of wine. But even if I hadn't - it's your job.  Just do it.  Don't complain.  I am not the cause of the 17 other things you have to do - which given how slow the restaurant was, well, it's just completely laughable.  Her glacial pace may have actually led to her having 17 things to do, but when I ask for a glass of water for the third time, just please give it to me, and spare me the behind the scenes BS. Was so upset because when I challenged this 17 task juggler, she made me feel like I was wrong, that I gave my friend with whom I was dining my credit card, left my meal and wine on the bar and went home. So, brava, you won.   And, if the best thing a place has going for it is a burger, bearnaise, toast, wtf, they really need to step up the service.

My husband and I went there on Sunday night because we were already on the area. The food was delicious and the service was very friendly. I recommend the kale salad, sweet potato au gratin and the chicken, although they said there menu changes frequently bases on what's in season.  Restaurant is small and tables are close together.
Great food great people great all around. Highly recommend this place. Never had anything I didn't like!!!

Check out my blog at whatsaachisays.blogspot.…! Now on to the review, I'm not sure if this is a hidden gem, but Galli was amazing! Located on Mercer street in Soho,a perfect comfort Italian meal to end or start of your day. I would say end just because the vibe at this restaurant is really cool. As you enter, a narrow path with dim lights some even red, comes a bar and then a huge space for seating in the back. Brick walls, accommodations for large parties and small, and plenty of hip hop R&B  music in the back to go along with the meal, could that be a more ideal dinner place? The menu is simple and not full of a hundred different dishes, You have your basic appetisers, salads, a speciality in calamari and parm, mains, and then pastas which looks like a pretty balanced menu if you ask me! OH and don't forget the dessert. Here is what we ordered: FREE BREAD- and it refills... Mozz Chips $11- This may sound super typical and you may ask the question of why we ordered greasy mozzarella sticks at a nice restaurant? They were SO heavenly. WOW. the cheese was melted perfectly, breaded to perfection it did not even feel oily or greasy. The pomodoro sauce was the perfect compliment, made it feel more elegant. Penne Vodka- This was by far my favourite dish, and solely the reason I would recommend this restaurant to other people. Sometimes you get pasta and the restaurant is greedy with their sauce leaving your pasta to dry, but this had plenty of sauce, plenty of flavor, and the perfect vodka sauce I was looking for. Fussilli Pollo- Garlicky, Chickeny (is that a word?) with a little bit of greens, this dish also looked super appetising. Everything was sweeped clean. My friend said the chicken was moist and great and the pasta oozed of garlic which she loves! NOTE: The portions are really big! One pasta can definitely feed three people so be cautious of when you order! We unfortunately were too full to try the dessert but the tiramisu sounded great! also NOTE: the restaurant is noisy, so if you want a quiet dinner this is not the place for you! One thing I need to complain about is the bathroom, it was not very sanitary. The servers were very attentive, sometimes a little too attentive, but always asking us if we wanted something more, they refilled our bread immediately and got us any toppings as soon as we asked. Nonetheless, Great meal on an average Tuesday night!

Review for service only....DiFaro's I've heard so much about you, but sadly it wasn't meant to be. I ordered and didn't mind the hour the lady at the front said it would take to get my pie. An hour came and went, I was told a half hour more. I don't care how good it's supposed to be, I was getting impatient. The last straw was when I asked if the pizza had even gone into the oven, an hour and 45 minutes into it, and she snapped at me for being impatient. Don't tell customers 1 hour when you mean 2+, just lemme know what I'm getting myself into! Terrible system and customer service. Not to say I didn't gain anything, I got bit by Mosquitos or bed bug or idk what those crawly things were. HORRIBLE SERVICE!
Whoops wrong place. My bad :-/

So love this place.. I came here by myself around 2 pm and got sitted right away while people are still waiting in couples or group outside. I didn't know what to order so I ask the service for recommends so she said take the spicy miso with pork, ok done due.. After tasting the first sip of the soup I felt like I was in heaven the soup was so rich and flaverful and the noodles were perfect aldente.. I definitely recommend this place if you love ramen.

I made a reservation via Open Table, and the restaurant called to confirm my reservation on the day that we were to come. I showed up at the appointed reservation time, and there was nobody to greet us at the door. Someone shouted from across the room that they would be right with us. Then, a waiter came over and greeted us, and I informed them of our reservation. He went to check on it, but the table was not free yet. I was invited to sit at the bar, and we had a cocktail while waiting for our table. It seemed that we were forgotten, and after we almost finished our drinks, the bar tender (or another waiter) asked us if we were waiting for a table. I informed him that we were waiting for our table that we had made a reservation for. He went to check on it and another different waiter came back and told us the table was now ready "for whenever we wanted to move" and got ready to disappear again, we had to practically hold on to him to get to our table which we were more than ready for. I will take a moment here to state that there were a total of three waiters and they each seemed to be serving, bar tending, and greeting people as they came in the restaurant. Once at the table, we looked at our menus and decided what we each wanted to eat. We ordered the camembert alongside the duck breast and prosciutto di parma charcuteries to start. This was presented nicely on a wooden board with cornichons, mustard, a fig jam and pickled veggies, with some cut up baguette. With that we also ordered the baked figs stuffed with blue cheese and wrapped with bacon. The charcuterie board was very tasty, the baked figs were OK, nothing to write home about (the bacon was thick cut and overpowered the rest of the simple ingredients). After we finished our appetisers, one of the waiters asked us if we were (and I quote) "still waiting for food", not realising that we had already ordered mains. This seemed to be the main problem with the restaurant: there was no good communication between the waiters and the service was a bit slow and disorganised. For our mains we had the filet mignon and the duck leg confit. The beef was cooked perfectly and the sauce was stunning. My husband liked my dish better than his duck and he started to run his duck through the beef sauce because it was so good. I also tried the duck. It was a little on the drier side, but not terribly overcooked. During all of this, nobody seemed to bother too much about asking us if we wanted more drinks (the table was so small that we had to have our glasses on a shelf right next to the server station, so lack of visibility was not the problem here) or a refill of our water glasses. Apparently we looked stuffed because asking if we wanted dessert was also completely omitted. Overall the food and ambience was great, but the service was mediocre. Every person we dealt with was friendly, but again they were very disorganised and inattentive. If the service was better, I would have given this restaurant 4 stars easily.

We went for the "deal" and ended up spending a lot more - more than I normally pay for a dinner out. But it was because everything was so good! Get the Happy Hour special. And the salads. And mussels. Great food.
Great food, excelent service...a quiet place if  you are tired of the crowded timesquare!

Went to Omar's today for lunch. Found a parking spot right out front.  The neighborhood felt safe and I liked being able to see my car from inside the restaurant. The guy behind the counter was friendly and quick to take my order.  After thinking about getting a fresh juice I ended up ordering a Cuban sandwich and a cappuccino instead. Oh Good Grief - they were both DELICIOUS. The cappuccino came while I was waiting for the Cuban and it was ridiculously good - topped with whipped cream and a dusting of cinnamon. Tasted like they put something extra in it to make it extra delicious but I'm not sure what (evaporated milk maybe?).  Then the Cuban sandwich came. They were premade so it really only took a few minutes. It was crispy and buttery and flavorful to the max. The meat was obviously seasoned for a while before going into the sandwich and the cuts of meat were thin and tender. I'm not a big meat eater - not a fan ethically and also because I don't particularly like the taste - but this was melt in your mouth deliciousness.   I'll be going back and trying other things - can't wait!

Every time I think they've thought of it all they amaze me again.  I just had a focaccia pizza sandwich from pizza one and it was absolutely incredible.  I will never go to another pizza place as long as pizza one is around.  Everything from their menu to staff is excellent but their creativity with pizza is absolutely phenomenal.  If you haven't tried it I feel really bad for you.

There are not enough words to formulate to express how wonderful this restaurant is and how helpful they were with my party.  The library/dining room upstairs is intimate, cozy and rustic and combined with the delicious food and attention to detail, I could not have picked a better place to have a family gathering. Jessica, the restaurant's Events Manager was gracious and so lovely to deal with throughout this whole experience.  When my party had to be suddenly canceled, they were so helpful in rescheduling. The food is rustic, fabulous, plentiful and presented beautifully. I recommend everything but the meatballs, the fried artichokes and the CHEESECAKE were big hits! Thank you again Palma for making such a lovely party!

FOH Staff = Excellent. Probably best in town. our water glasses were refilled many times. our server checked in on us appropriately. the hostesses did not forget about us while we were waiting and notified us as the status of our table a couple of times. First impressions - The salsa they give you is the smallest portion of salsa ever... my guess is its 1-2 tablesppons at most. I definitely don't mind a long wait if the food is worth it (like at Sushihana) however, the food at villalobos was lack luster at best.  I ordered 3 tacos - al pastor, tinga, and camarones.  the chicken in the tinga taco tasted like it was simmered in Campbell's tomato soup and was weirdly dry.  all of the tacos were dry. perhaps if they gave you a tiny bit more salsa we could have used that to. I wont be back. Casa Piquin blows this place out of the water (even with that strange smell).

Disappointment at best... both service & food were sub par. Service: slow waitstaff, confused about who was our waitress because many people came to our table, they didn't refill our water glasses or chips, waitress brought out wrong food and on top of that it was cold. Food: We ordered the traditional guacamole which was the highlight of our meal. Along with this we also ordered the chicharrones (crispy pork skin) which was incredibly hard to even bite into, it tasted stale and my friend couldn't even take a bite it was that hard... we sent those back to the kitchen and they took it off our bill. The time in between the appetizer and our mains (we ordered taco) was ridiculously long. I don't mind waiting in a restaurant for food, but when it comes out less than lukewarm and tastes like it was cooked the day before I get upset. We had the chicken, pork, fish, and shrimp tacos which were all unmemorable. Overall the staff looked confused and were not prepared, good idea for a restaurant but the menu was not executed well. I feel bad because it's the opening week, hopefully the staff are able to sort out these issues.

Love this place! A wonderful addition to the neighborhood - casual, affordable, and really delicious, fresh food and great staff and service to boot. We've both eaten in and gotten delivery - I always get the fish taco and the garlic shrimp - YUM! The chicken tostada is great too. Guacamole and torta milanesa are other favorites. My kids love this place too. A family owned business that I'm happy to support!

I went back to McLadden's to see if my first good experience could be repeated. This is a fun place and has a great atmosphere. I've read lots of the positive and less than positive reviews. I can understand the criticisms but I think those writers are unrealistic. This is a place that is really trying. The staff are all smiling and helpful and look pretty busy. The beer selection is great and the food is good. The French onion soup is delicious and the sandwiches were really good. (Once I had fish and chips that I wasn't crazy about - too soggy) The personality of a restaurant is important for me - even more than the food. (The kitchen is the lowest point in this pub.) This feels like an Irish pub where families, singles, and couples are all welcome and comfortable. Whenever I am in the area, I am going to go here.

Went there last night for a friend's birthday.  There were four of us and we arrived at 6:30 and were seated immediately.  Young woman who sat us was all smiles and very welcoming. We looked through menu and decided on roti canai and crispy wontons for our appys.  There were both hot and delicious.  We shared four entrees , Pad Thai with Seafood, Black Pepper Beef, Pattaya Ginger Chicken, and Crispy Basil Chicken.  Each had a unique flavor and was prepared and presented nicely.  The seafood in the Pad Thai was not plentiful but the noodles were delicious.  I would order with chicken next time.  The Pattaya Ginger Chicken was fresh and light. We all enjoyed passing and sharing!  We finished with the mango coconut flan for the group to taste.  Pretty presentation and very tasty.  Prices are reasonable.  Our bill was 85.00 for all the above which I consider a bargain.  It is a BYOB so we all enjoyed our favorite wine with dinner.  I would definitely return again!!

I am sure I will never go to Outpost again.  These guys are a much better experience.  I visited here three times during my recent trip to Brooklyn.  Every sandwich was excellent, every cup of coffee superb.  The husband/wife team really make you feel welcome, they engage you in conversation, they make a serious effort to get to know you.  I felt like I was with friends while I was in Lunitas.  The Fulton sandwich is excellent, you must try it.  The caprese sandwich was delicious.  They cook to order, so its always fresh and warm.  The coffee is hand pressed throughout the day and I really loved their coffee.  Cannot wait to come back to Brooklyn to visit with them and try some more of their wonderful coffee and food offerings.  You must walk past Outpost and cross the street to try this place.  You will not be sorry.

It takes a special kind of finesse, skill, & attention to even the most minute details to be able to realize an authentic Italian dining experience here in the U.S. Rizzuto's does this...flawlessly. Having grown up in Italy, where authenticity is the fundamental ingredient in the creation of all meals whether made in a modest country farm house or in a Michelin-rated Milanese restaurant, I'd like to think I have a penchant for all things Italian...especially when it comes to food. (In other words, if I might suggest, modestly, that I'm a credible source- which is dubious in the case of many yelpers!) The beginning of this summer was my first introduction to rizzutos. I was invited for pre-drinks at a nearby venue, and we then carried on into rizzutos to take advantage of their happy hour menu.  First impressions are everything. The GM, a very hands-on, articulate guy, John, ushered us into the bar area and introduced us to a bartender, Jen, and told us she would accommodate us in any way. Excellent first impression. The aroma from the wood fire was intoxicatingly delicious. Just. Like. Italy. The wine selection spoke to the owner's (Bill I believe his name is whom I have yet to meet and would love to hear his story!) awareness of Italian fine wines...with some very fine Barolos. The open, limitless feeling of the interior space was reminiscent of a roman restaurant...vibrant, colorful and full of energy. The happy hour bites were extremely reasonable and were absolutely delicious...the little savory dishes abided by American happy hour conventions, but maintained an Italian flare...which my guests and I appreciated. I've been back a few times for dinner, and wi continue to do so. It's a place I now insist in taking all my foodie friends and family. The cheese plate was also indicative of the well informed chef & owner. Sourcing not only Italian delicacies like the dreamy burrata, but also an homage to local artisans like Cato corner right here in colchester ct. For dinner...one must try the braised veal osso buco which is heavenly adorned with goat cheese infused polenta and (my favorite!) kale! The pastas, in particular the pappardelle are made in house, and are terribly authentic. I rarely take the time to expend this amount of effort to extol the virtues of something...but this place is most certainly deserved of it.

The service was very good and the drinks were excellent. The place had a nice vibe. The food was OK; nothing great and it was overpriced. I wanted to try the Mac and cheese with my main entre since I had read so much about it and I was very disappointed. It had way too much garlic and was not very cheesy. As far as the chicken and waffle I ordered, the chicken didn't taste as good as the chicken at my grocery deli and the waffle lacked flavor. My friend had the short ribs which I tasted. It was a generous portion of food but I disliked the Asiatic barbeque sauce. The experience was a letdown.

Great service, great food and drinks, and the inside of the restaurant is beautiful! The prices for tapa and drinks is very reasonable and great quality, especially compared to other tapas places in the ironbound. Great if you want to catch a game at the bar or have a romantic dinner in the back restaurant.

Brought my family here for dinner and we were thoroughly stuffed before our entrees arrived. The servings for their appetizers were actually enough to be a considered a meal. They also served us a generous amount of bread. I tried their ribs with sweet and spicy tomato sauce and it was so delicious. It was actually a new taste I have never had before. I usually do not deviate from the more familiar tastes, but this was a great new discovery for me. I am eager to return here for this same treat or perhaps go on another adventure with their menu. We arrive at the restaurant at seven in the evening on a Friday and we were able to get a table for four without any wait. The other popular Greek restaurant across the street appeared to have a much longer wait. This place is certainly worth trying if you appreciate Mediterranean foo.

Get the sticky buns, you wont regret it. I don't understand all the negative reviews for waiting time, I'm a frequent here (as I work down the block), and all hours of the day I never see any lines, or when I do, everyone is served quickly. Really good on the wallet as well, when it came time to assess the damage done to me, came out to $15 for a really filling meal. Would definitely recommend.

Pork dumplings and the peppers.. Obviously show up early as it's always packed. If you like Raamen, definitely a great choice. I also recommend hitting up the small bar in the front of the house, great bar tenders! HOLLER WITH A DOLLAR, pW

A local hangout with good food and a great selection of draft beers, where you are likely to meet your friends and be served by your next door neighbor's son or daughter, who probably played in the marching band or sang in choir with your kids.  It's that kind of place. .

Real Italian food and better yet: great service! House wine was delicious and very affordable and we did not feel rushed (didn't get the bill shoved under our nose after 20 min, something that can happen a lot in NYC).

My wife and I had a NJ Transit layover in Rahway, so we decided to find a local spot to eat. We discovered the Rail House, which is across the street from the train station.  Food was excellent. The only flaw was the service, a little slow.

Excellent ramen + great atmosphere. The restaurant is usually crowed with a long wait if you have a group larger than 2. The chicken buns were a little spicy but tasty. And since I was in a chicken mood, ordered the ramen with chicken (add the egg for $2 more). This was some of the best flavorful ramen I've had in a long time. Highly recommended.

I was excited to try The Eddy for dinner after I saw the review on Tasting Table.  The service/ atmosphere/ food itself was great.  Nevertheless, I cannot recommend eating dinner here due to the price to portion value.  I finished my dinner plate with 4 forks full of food.  This is not the restaurant to go hungry to.  My friend and I had to go to another restaurant after to get a more fulfilling meal.

The food was OK but should have been better.  I also felt that we were nickel and dimed on some items, which at these prices should not happen.  Monkey Bread was good BUT with $30 plus entrees there should be some bread that you don't have to pay for (Colicchio and Sons at the same prices has the same type of fresh baked bread for free as an example).  Also, we were grossly overcharged for gin and tonics $15 per gin and then $5 EXTRA for tonic (which was cheapo Seagram's tonic) - $20 for a gin and tonic is not cool ever especially when its flat and nothing special.  The lamb I ordered as an entree was cold.  It did not say it was a cold dish.  The veggies were hot on the plate, but the lamb had obviously not been made fresh.  I told the waiter that the lamb was cold.  It came back lukewarm and the plate was burning hot, obviously they just stuck it in the oven.  It was inedible.  So while some may have a great meal here, beware that they may cut some corners and they to charge you more than they should.

Let me start out by admitting a bias.  I don't like more West Hartford eateries.  Most are pretentious, and are over-priced for 2nd-rate food and drink. Noodles & Co. breaks that mold.  The service is down to Earth.  Extremely polite.   The food is excellent.  I usually get the noodles with vegetables, and/or soup.  The veggies are always fresh and delicious, the noodles always cooked just right.  The soup is equally excellent.   The beverages: their coffee is excellent, as are their bottled cold drinks.  If there's one thing I can fault Noodles & Co. on, it's their cold drinks machine.  It's one of those you see at more and more establishments now, where you can mix and match dozens of varieties of sodas, waters, flavors.  It's not awful, but it's not as good as the actual products are if purchased from dedicated machines or in bottles or cans.   Outdoor dining is on a nice little patio, with some cool gas-fired torches that add not only ambiance, but light and warmth.  Thank God there's no TV anywhere to be found. I'd also rate Noodles & Co. an excellent value.  So we have down-to-Earth, friendly, professional personnel... excellent food... excellent coffee... an excellent value... what's THIS place doing in West Hartford?  (Answer: being special.) Phil

This is my first time here. I had the special: Chipotle bacon cheeseburger with crispy onions. It was delicious, cooked just right. And the hand-cut fries were perfect. The service was friendly and attentive. My son had the Apple-brie burger,  and while he's not great with descriptions, he devoured it. This is a great place in a convenient location. And the prices were extremely reasonable, especially considering the quality and size of the portions.
Affordable healthy gourmet food. Excellent!
The food is fantastic. Nice service.

This lunch was mediocre at best. I went with my boyfriend and simply got a burger and beer each. When the beer first came out the glasses they were in were extremely dirty, but they switched it out for us nicely. My boyfriend got the avocado burger and I got Ryan's burger. We both ordered medium and they we're both waaaaay over done. On top of it, the avocado on the avocado burger was a small wedge that was hard and browned. They only saving grace of this place is that the waitress was super sweet and they allow dogs on the patio. I would not suggest it for food though.
One of the best restaurants in nyc.  Get there early and stay late.

Great American style food with fresh ingredients from around the Colchester area along with nice homey environment. I believe that the cooks and other employees are very professional but also very fun and nice.
Fine dining experience, excellent service - portions are adequate (not too much or too less), can get a bit pricey when combined with starter, drunk and  a dessert. But overall a good experience.

I really love The Monk Room. The Caesar salad is heavenly with the whole anchovies and the maple dessert is super tasty. I've sampled a few of their other dishes with nothing but happiness and indulged in a few yummy Snowbird cocktails.  It's probably the closest place I've found in Newark that's hipster (IPA's on tap!) - which I sort of like :-) My only suggestion/concern: the prices are a bit high. If this was in Hoboken or on Grove Street the prices would be fine. And the place is inexpensive compared to NYC. But for downtown Newark, where there's a lot of gov't and non-profit workers, it's a bit much. The price definitely limits how often I go - especially with other places in the immediate area offering $2 drink specials and much cheaper salads. Maybe have a half price lunch or dinner? Or offer happy hour specials that include  food?

I've been to this pizzeria 4 times now. The pizza is fantastic!!! The reason that it gets such a low rating is the guy in the back doing all the other cooking is horrible. Every time I try to order buffalo wings I always get something different. Sometimes it BBQ sometimes it's just fried wings with nothing on it... The last two times I made my order there was a hair in it somewhere. Once in the pizza and once in the wings... My opinion, fire the fry cook and buy some hair nets.
The mood is very chic and welcoming. The food is delicious but the portions are soooo small! It is a great spot if you are in the area and want to enjoy a meal with friends.
Highly recommend this place food was excellent. We had the lamb sand which and chicken pasta both were fresh and the prices were awesome between 9-16$ per meal
If you want chicken and rice you have to go Halal Guys or risk becoming an old man, filled with regret, waiting to die alone. Also, beware the hot sauce is really hot!
No introduction is necessary. The lamb over rice is my poison and have never been dissapointed.

Thought this was a cool looking pub from the street, so we decided to come  in and have a few drinks and supper. It wasn't particularly busy, so it was surprising that there was no hostess or staff to greet the four of us. We just sat ourselves down at an open table and went to the bar to order our own drinks. Eventually the waitress came over with menus.  We had burgers, buffalo wings, and a chicken caesar. Sadly, I had to send one of the burgess back because it was overcooked and then had to wait a long time to get a replacement. Bummer. The fries were pretty good, admittedly, but on the whole, the meal and service was average. They seemed indifferent to us being there. I don't get it.
The wait was ridiculous but got in for a great brunch. $18 for a nice brunch item + drink. Cute little restaurant.

Ordered the veal marsala. The veal was a little tough and the pasta overcooked. Called it in as a to go order and arrived 25 minutes later and still had to wait 15 minutes. I could see if it was packed but it was 8:00 on a Tuesday night.

Absolute favorite neighborhood place to go for great tapas.  The menu is very creative and every plate tastes delicious.  I love coming here with a group of 5-6 people and sharing a whole bunch of different tapas dishes.  HIGH RECOMMEND!
The hibachi was on the salty side for me but the sushi is some of the best I've had! Definitely coming back for the sushi!!

Ehhhhh the cheesesteak is forgettable, definitely tourist trappy. I didn't try Pat's so I can't compare but I probably won't go back to try them either. Also not a huge fan of the over the top ~patriotism~ theme going on here but to each his own.

This was my first time trying Jahan Kabob & grill and it was amazing!!! I had the falafel pita with French fries (the lunch special) it is the best falafel I have ever had!! The combination of flavors from the hummus and tzatziki plus the fresh vegetables was perfect!! The fries were even amazing. I will definitely be  going back again and would recommend this place to anyone. The restaurant itself is very clean and looks nice.

After reading these reviews, we figured this place would be a great place to go for a bite. We walked in and the place was empty and the woman was reading a book at one of the booths. She had us seat ourselves in the dark dining room. All the tables were dirty and sticky but at this point it was too late to turn around and leave. The food was edible but was not very great. I got the chicken francese and the sauce was way too creamy and thick. The older man and woman were arguing in the front during our entire meal. Horrible experience, bad food, won't go back.

Wow wow wow, best place in town was very lucky to get in as we didn't have a reservation and luckily enough some crazy people didn't show, straight away service was amazing we knew our cheeses but was schooled by our server, everything was amazing, we were all eating off each other's plates great time, just don't forget to pay your parking they wait for your car to expire as we set a time for exact and not a min before
10/10! Great food, great service, affordable! Quick! A Cuban sandwich a day will keep my hangover at bay! Go check it out! So worth it! The meat melts in your mouth. And that garlic sauce

We don't go to NYC often anymore, so when we do, we look for a good place to eat. Based on what I read about Hu Kitchen, this was our choice for lunch today. It was a HUge mistake. And not an inexpensive one. I had what was reviewed as this amazing vegan lasagna - the Grandmaster Veg - that was supposed to have eggplant, carrot, green cabbage, cashew, marinara, garlic and chili flake. What I had was a lasagna look alike thing that had a ton of shredded carrots, onions, what I suspect was a vegan cashew cheese substitute, some traces of marinara, and whatever made up the dark tasteless topping. I had some curried cauliflower on the side which was tasty but cold. My wife and son both had rotisserie chicken that was no different than what we can make at home with a side of mixed veggies that were simply sauteed mixed veggies. Both bland and everyday. A huge place where you order like a cafeteria and hope to find a seat because the place is packed. Mostly younger professionals who get upset and roll their eyes when you ask them to move their large, expensive leather bags so you can sit down and then proceed to occasionally glance at you, roll their eyes, and move their bag closer to them while you eat. (O.K., that's pretty much descriptive of most places in NY now.) The staff were neither friendly nor unfriendly. They just put the stuff on the plate. Its impossible to really get any questions about the product answered since they're in a rush to serve the next person like any cafeteria. Oh, well. Live and learn. There are probably 15 other vegetarian / vegan places in the same neighborhood. They don't have to worry.

Obao is a bustling little kitchen that has provocative style with spicy dishes to entertain everyone. The interior of the space features raw elements: wood logs line the walls with monolithic panels of mirror and linear lacquer paneling. Its a contemporary aesthetic that looks to be a reinterpretation of the 5 classical elements. My boyfriend and I visited Obao, he looked into exotic flavors and found Obao to be tantalizing based on their offerings. He ordered Lak Sa, a colorful mildly-spiced soup with large fresh noodles and whole chunks of shrimp. I took a taste, it was amazing. A sharp flavor with a warm touch. It was delicious. I ordered the Vietnamese Pork Chop which featured white rice, veggies and a vinegar based sauce that complemented the softer flavors wonderfully. The pork was cooked to perfection with colorful grill marks and just the right amount of moisture for a succulent dish. Our only qualm was about service turnaround. The waitstaff are well informed, polite, and very friendly. However the time it took to receive our check and my card back was a little long. Long enough to casually finish our drinks. So in conclusion, if you're looking for an exotic escape in flavor, Obao is just what you're looking for.

Had brunch and lunch here. Good food. Come with an appetite,or you'll be so stuffed. Fast service. Awesome Bloody Mary menu.
14 for slice pork? 17 for chicken? No no Go get something else. Not recommend ! Not come back

Food is great service is great they have an awesome beef tips and caprese salad the fried brussel sprouts are unbelievable the bacon and blue mussels were amazing. They make a great makers mark Manhattan.

WOW!!!!!! I have dined in and ordered out at Spumoni Gardens. The pizza is always superb.

My girlfriend and I went to Tuome on opening night last night for our anniversary. I had flowers with me and the staff was very accommodating, offering to store them in a cool spot in the back. The decor is rustic with much of the paneling, fixtures, and decorations coming from old Philadelphia factories (our server was kind enough to educate us on the wall of wool spools behind us). Tuome's ambiance is not dissimilar to a West Village wine bar: candle-lit, chock-full of well-heeled 30-something couples, and long on exposed brick and reclaimed wood. Perhaps in ironic acknowledgement that it is very squarely in grungy hipster territory and far from Greenwich's angular cobblestone streets and $10mm lofts, Tuome's playlist ran the gamut of 80's high school dance classics - from Asia's 'Heat of the Moment' to Abba's Dancing Queen. Somehow it worked marvelously. The wine list is well-considered with relatively affordable selections and a token rose for girls' night groups that couldn't get a reservation in Midtown. In our own irony, we ordered beer ($7, from a short, but remarkably well-curated selection) and the Mexican Coca Cola ($4). The chef's amuse was delightful - a well-balanced, subtle offering of pickled vegetables with an Asian touch. Restaurants that resemble any relation to the bygone fusion era are always at risk of producing flavors that conjure memories of some panko-breaded slider with teriyaki dipping sauce gone awry. Luckily Tuome avoids this gracefully. The ginger-scallion sauce is just right. Our next dishes - watermelon with farro and chrysanthemum ($12) and chicken liver with milk toast, sunflower seeds, and local maple syrup ($13) are marvelous. They embody the inventive yet harmonious combination of familiar flavors in crisp, bright, unique preparations that is the greatest hallmark of modern cooking. After a long lull (a bizarre pause to an otherwise good tempo of service), we received our mains: scallops with carrot puree and maitake ($25) and beef short-rib with sweet potato puree and grilled shishito peppers ($28). Diners have long come to expect a standard of perfect or near-perfect protein preparation and Chen does not disappoint here. The beautiful sear on the scallops does not come at the expense of its smooth, tender flesh. Likewise, the braised short-rib maintains its form long enough to stand upright on the plate but absolutely melts in your mouth. Chen tends toward the sweeter end of flavors on the proteins but this is a minor shortcoming and easy to forgive. Where Chen excels is his obsessive attention to texture - our side of snap peas ($8) was crisp yet tender with peanuts for additional crunch, and the sweet lotus root chips perched atop the delicate scallops provide the perfect contrast. We were disappointed to learn that dessert was not on the menu for the evening, but after such a wonderful first experience, we'll surely be back for more.
Great flavor, wonderful service.  Crust is a bit hard, could be because it was a reheated slice.

Ok, went BACK to Blend and... Had another good 'ol time. For after work, just want some drinks and good food; very good. Alexis (again) was attentive (as usual) and fun (as usual). This time, spoke with both managers, Carlos and ... I forgot his name (eep). Very gracious and courteous. If you work or live nearby, go around 6 during the week. Wow, worth traveling from Manhattan for the delicious food. I live near Il Mulino, but its generally out of my price range when looking for a place to eat. Il Falco has an excellent selection of meats and pastas, along with a tasty Nero D'Avola that I thoroughly enjoyed.

Not sure if the management/bar owners are aware that the in-house live music walks around with a 'tip bucket' asking for money in-between sets. My favorite little cafe! Their service is fast and their presentation is impeccable. You must try the chai tea! I have made the 20 minute trip down multiple times just to grab a cup! They even sell bags so you can make it at home. What a great place!

The three stars are for the atmosphere. I doubt I would go again.

I really love this place.  The food is good, very fairly priced and it's BYOB.  I come with my boyfriend and we usually order a burrito, a quesadilla, rice and beans, some tacos and cokes with real sugar.  Only thing I don't like is pickled onions, but some people do.  If you want a chill place to get some good mexican food and not break a 20$ bill this is the place.  Awesome mole sauce, and really nice guys behind the register.  I always tip because they are so pleasant but technically  I don't think they are servers, you grab your food and bring it to a table yourself.  love it
Best soup dumplings I've had in awhile!
It's always a good place. Not a long wait & they ave no problem with picky orders.  The manager has been there a long time & it shows.  Its well run & food is fresh

Went with my mom and sis to the Firebox to have some catch up time with the girls and some good food. We were not let down! The waitress was so friendly and did not rush us. We spent about 3 hours there (by choice!) just talking and enjoying the fantastic food, ambiance, and service. I ordered the cheese plate for an appetizer which was very elegant and creative. My sister teased me for ordering the french fries but put her foot in her mouth (as well as half the bowl of fries) after trying them. By far the BEST fries I have ever had! The duck was delectable, so juicy and cooked medium to perfection just as I requested. My family and I will be returning and we just love how the Firebox is "Farm-to-Table" using only fresh local ingredients. Definitely worth the money and drive.

This place is no joke.  Worth every penny.  Shrimp and grits, gravy smothered chicken, biscuits, AND matzoball soup?! all of which I have tried, and each have blown my tastebuds to southern heaven.  I recently tried the turkey leg dinner.  Delicious.  The cocktails are dangerous too.  I've had most of them, my favorites are definitely the apple pie moonshine which tastes like apple pie and the jam jar.  Downside is they are almost always packed with a 30 minute wait.  A must try, if you're willing to get addicted.

There are many things to pick from, with various levels of "spicy" which I found very nice. I got chicken with cashews and noodles which I found delicious. The servers were very nice and the restaurant had a nice atmosphere to it. I also got the fried ice cream which was out of this world.

What is so great about this place. I went way out of my way to come here last Sunday afternoon. You have to order brunch which I didn't feel like so I went with the steak and eggs. The table next to us ordered after us. By the time they had eaten and were paying there bill I asked where our food was. When it came the waiter said the steak takes a long time causing the delay. My steak was very rare in the first place but I did say rare. But it was also cold so if that's what held up the meal it should come to me hot right. Other than that the food was OK but it was outweighed by snobby pretentious lousy service. See ya. Oh and way overpriced.
Si quieren probar comida mexicana, deben ir a este lugar, RIQUÍSIMO, el mejor sabor mexicano que he probado en EU.

WOW! Hands Up The BEST Thai Restaurant Outside Of Bangkok! Prices Are Very Reasonable (Cash Only), And The Food Portions Are Bangkokin!  What's Really Cool About This Place Besides The Authentically Delicious Food Is That The Restaurant Is Literally (4) Restaurants In One! A Beautiful Outdoor Seating Area With A Fountain Completely Helps The Ambiance.  Definitely (2) Thumbs Up!
amazing white.

Best ramen in NYC - but expect to WAIT at least an hour unless you visit during "off" hours. I always order the vegetarian ramen with extra avocado. The pork buns are delicious as well. I like to sit at the counter and watch the chefs. Be ware, it's no frills. Not fancy. And it's a tiny joint. But the food is great.
Bubble TEA is out of this world highly recommend this place.  Their food is really good too. I'm glad I work  near by so I can come here frequently.

We have been here more than 5 times already, so short version of my review: it's very good quality and taste! The pho is amazingly good, absolutely a perfect balance of rich and clean tasting broth and quality of the beef (even noodles taste good too)! Besides pho there are salads which are good as well as bahn mi. Every time we come here we are surprised by the new items on the menu. Today was a delicious pineapple desert dish. So we will back again and again.

This isn't a normal traditional sand which shop. Its something a lot different. Instead of subway where they toast the bread and put maybe 3 slices of turkey they put a lot of meat and toppings. They stream tge meat and cheese! What other sand which shop does that? This is the best sand which shop. I recommend the club on a sub or the turkey bacon ranch.
Great bang for the buck. Excellent tacos and the sauce is amaaaazzzing!!!! Keep up the good work!!!
wonderful Chelsea neighborhood brunch/lunch spot. food was deliciousness, service was impeccable.
Horrible everything.

Salt alert! My wife and I dined at the Astoria location. We were seated across from the bar. Very noisy. At times could not hear the server. But the main complaint was the over salting of everything. From the veggies, fish, salad. We ordered dover sole "for two". The price was for two but not the portion. I have visited many other Greek rest. for fish and have had a satisfying portion of fish. I don't know what all the praise is for this place. It is more of a scene. If you want a serious meal search elsewhere.
mmm...pork buns.
