The service here is top-notch.  The guys who served us were awesome; super down to earth, reliable, friendly, and at our every request.  Among the best service I have ever gotten anywhere. Every dish we ordered was good - I have salad every day, and yet I found the arugula different and perfectly seasoned. The mixed seafood with lobster came in a huge portion and everything was delicious and flavorful. For dessert, we shared the family style strawberry shortcake which was more than enough to feed 6 of us, especially after a meal here. This place offers great value for large groups and I would definitely come back to try some of the other dishes! I would strongly recommend reservations. It was so nice to walk in and here, "come this way, your table is ready"

Once again Tony's made me look like a star.  I sent yet another freind and his family to "my favorite italian restuarant in all of NYC" and got rave reviews back.  Even a thank you card signed by the husband, wife and all the kids.. Ciro, Jimmy and Dreni, managers all,  were all on this night and they made a point of welcoming my friends. Their server Jordana, did a fantastic job, thanks sweetie... The report I got was the food, oh the food...they couldnt beleive how much, how good and how reasonable.  And they added the sangria (which they want the recipe for....) This is one of the absolute best places to send out of towners to when they are in need of a great place to eat.  Especially family style.  Just a wonderful restuarant, super managers and staff and oh the food, the food.....FANTASTIC.... Thanks all....Ron

I truly enjoyed my experience at BLVD Bistro... They offer a nice menu with fresh produce which produces a great combination. The owners are hands on, and will greet you at the door. More importantly, the owners have true Harlem roots, and they offer a menu which echoes the history of Harlem. Personally, the Mac & Cheese, shrimp & watermelon salad, Shrimp & grits, and the simple steak were great... Lastly, I was impressed w/ their baked goods, and their homemade German Chocolate cake (made the right way)... Its a great Brunch spot, and an amazing place to have dinner... BLVD is my new dinner spot... and I believe it offers the best meal in Harlem...
Just a wonderful place. Great food. Made us feel welcome.
This place only takes cards! I went today and they don't take cash. Nonetheless the food is delicious!

I'm not much for sharing reviews, in fact this is my first one, but I felt compel to share the experience I had today at Labebe.  The food was delicious, the menu was full of  wonderful choices that made even a novice to Mediterranean cuisine feel comfortable ordering anything.  The space was beautifully appointed...elegant, stylish, not stuffy...very comfortable and warm.  But I'm not writing just to say the food was great and the ambiance was spot on, I'm writing to share my experience with the staff and particularly the owner, Pierre.  He was gracious, generous with his time and his charming spirit.  He was a pleasure to meet and helped make our meal memorable and special.  We will be back again and again to learn more about the food and culture of the Mediterranean region through the inspiration of Pierre and his team at Labebe.  Thanks Pierre!

In town traveling. So glad the husband and I agreed on BBQ. The setting is great as was our server Katie, very welcoming. The ribs were some of the best I have ever had, the BBQ sauce made it!!!! If we come back to Philly, definitely coming back!
Can't go wrong with dessert here!

I went here for drinks with a friend and had a wonderful time. The staff is very friendly and the owner even made an effort to talk with everyone at the bar. Prices are typical for a NY bar. Overall fun but laid back ambiance. Will definitely be back.

Ate here on a work lunch and found the service extremely accommodating to ne as a vegan. I ate the cauliflower steak followed by an americano. The service was fast and we didn't wait for much except for the coffee.

I love NY pizza. Not so much this pizza. The crust, the sauce, the cheese... so many things distinguish NY pizza from the sad pie I get to eat in Seattle, but this place... it stands alone... but for the wrong reasons. I don't enjoy pizza swimming in grease. I don't like the avalanche of scalding, oily cheese cascading towards my face as I tip the pizza to eat... Don't take a good thing like cheese and ruin it by drowning it in grease. If I wanted to take a good thing and ruin it with excess, I'd watch Mean Tweets Read by Celebrities then watch endless hours of interviews by Jimmy Kimmel. Seriously, why?

This is a decent pizza place with a pizza bar around the pizza oven/hearth where you can see them make pizza right in front of you. The service is pretty quick. The only downside is that it is a small place and is always crowded so you should expect wait times.

i am a regular at this place for years ( always got the falafel sandwich ) and they do have good falafels.Hence i crave for  it . But charging a dollar per falafel is absurd!     I was shocked to pay almost 7 dollars for 6 small falafels.

Last night me and my wife and 2 friends went to eat at dabuscos it was horrible. When we first walked in we notices a young lady sitting at a table across from the counter wearing short , shorts and she had both legs up on the chair with her crotch sticking out that the workers didn't have the sense to tell her she's at a restaurant and sit like a lady. When we sat down no one came over to ask us if we would like anything to drink and give us our menu's I had to call out to get someone's attention . Finally we asked the waitor for fried calamari they said they had none than they said they had no stuffed shells which both items were on their menu. I asked for the pasta fagioli soup and they brought me minestrone soup and the waiter argued with me what kind of soup it was and I told him I know what pasta fagioli soup is. That's what happens when u go to al Italian pizzeria and the waiter is not Italian . I asked for baked raviolis and all they did was melt cheese on top of the              ravioli and called it baked. The sauce taste like tomato soup. Like a lot of other pizzerias and restaurants when they first open up the food is good than once they get their customers they don't cook as good and they use cheaper products. I asked to speak to the owner and of course he wasn't there. Like the saying when the cats away the mouse will play.
I am not sure if I got the same lamb shank. It didn't taste that good. I expect the lamb to be chewy but it turn out to be loose and simple.
Awesome Jersey pizza. Huge slices, lots of variety, a and their Sicilian is bangarang. Prices are greattt! Lunch special was 2 extra large slices and a large soda for $5.

I will definitely seek elsewhere next. This one of the most disgusting restaurants I have ever been in this city . I have enjoyed pizza from most ever known pizza place here,NYC,Rome,Florence, Chicago,Boston, Providence. I had very low expectations, but this was unreal. The crust was doughy,pasty white, even after fully cooking the color was beige at best.All te topping were tasteless and useless, the cheese was that industrial ultra white cheese that one hopes never to encounter. I have no idea how this place stays in business, but be the later hours. The kitchen was filthy, there was a B on the card out front and under no circumstances will I have be hungry enough to go back there.
Great beer, wine & cocktails but wow the food is awesome! Loves the people and the artwork.  What a great hang.  Make sure you try the crabcakes!!

This place is awesome! The food is great, it's inexpensive, and the employees are all extremely friendly and helpful. The felafel is fried to order, and the pitas are super fresh. Also, the best thing is that they are one of the few New Haven food establishments that stays open late. Way to go, Pitaziki!

I just tried this place for the first time... I was in the mood for something fast filling inexpensive and relatively healthy.  I ordered a Chicken Burrito and it was delicious as well as fitting all my criteria.  I was so pleased that I also posted a review on Yelp for the first time.  It was simple and satisfying with fast and friendly service.  No complaints here :)

Would eat here ALL DAY EVERY DAY! Best kept secret in VT. Have dined at many of the much-hyped local eateries and cannot recall last time that I had a meal that even compared. Had the Seafood Stew, Sweet & Spicy Meatloaf Sandwich, Stuffed Mushrooms a la Gallega, Pinxto Pork Encobijados, and the Potatas Bravas. Each and every single item was outstanding. Impressive beer, cider, wine, and liquor selection as well!
Best milkshakes in Brooklyn!
Much improved restaurant since new chef has taken over.  We will certainly revisit.  Homemade gnocchi were a little gummy (minus 1 star) but overall a very delicious meal.  Desserts were lacking.
Best biscuits and gravy ever! And I really like biscuits and gravy.

Their bacon sliders a like a little piece of heaven. Perfectly cooked burger with little bits of bacon and onion on them. The service was pretty good. Nice and quick and very polite, but I could tell us having her go back and forth for water refills annoyed her a bit haha. I don't know what type of cheese they use on the cheese fries but it's not my type. It's too smoky for the fries imo. All in all this is a good place to stop by for relatively cheap food.
Very bad experience. The waiters always chatting with each other, never refill my water. I also found a bug inside my steam seafood pot. This is the worse Korean restaurant ever! Don't go !!!

I realize airports are not the destination for gourmet refinery ,peace, or value. However: Newark international Airport has many choices in food, from convenience-type granola or snacks to McDonalds or Qdoba, pizza, up to a steakhouse near Terminal A that looks very nice (but too high for what I wanted to spend on dinner.) When travelling with a decent layover (over 1 hour)  I like to relax and therefore pay more to sit down and enjoy a table to myself. The value in paying more for your meal at a sit-down at an airport is peace and privacy, which is a commodity at a busy airport. I ordered the BBQ Bacon burger with fries and an iced tea. The food came out quickly, within 8-10 minutes. The burger tasted good, but was too large to eat so I waited a few minutes for a fork and knife. The onion rings on the burger were shrivled/soggy and the bread was really basic and cold. (They could have grilled the bread too). My biggest issue is this: not even halfway through eating my burger the waiter asked if I wanted anything else and then proceeded to hand me the check. I was really annoyed! He was friendly, but this is rude and bad policy in my opinion. I was not playing on my phone etc- just eating- and yet I felt like I was being rushed out. The other customer service complaint I have is that another server was standing behind the counter, rolling napkins or something, and talking really loudly with a friend sitting at the counter. It was very loud and went on throughout my entire meal (under 25 mins). The manager (who corrected an employee for greeted me while wearing gloves) was sitting nearby at a counter and didn't seem to care about this. Really disappointed and regretted my choice to spend $21.00 (food,tax and tip) on a burger and iced tea with awful service.   If I have to go through this airport again I will eat at one of their food court areas, so I can grab some food and a table. As a resident of Northern Liberties for the past 4 years, I've been here numerous times and can say the food quality and customer service has degraded significantly since PYT's menu items started gaining publicity/fame for their shock factor.  Years ago, this was a fun place to come in the neighborhood for a guilty/cheat meal.  Over time, it has lost its charm, the dishes are sloppily composed and served, and the food doesn't stand up to the quality of other restaurants you can go to in the area and around Philadelphia.   Beyond the overstated opinions about the customer service (which I can confirm has  been slow and lacking), the crowd here now seems extremely rowdy and immature, and it's impossible to sit in either their indoor or outdoor dining areas without being disrupted or annoyed.  Not that I expect a burger joint to be a classy dining spot, but I think an average level of professionalism should be upheld so you don't attract the wrong type of clientele. As someone who used to brag about this place to non-Philadelphians, I will no longer be bringing my friends here.  PYT has left a bad taste in my mouth and I'm not a proponent of what it's transformed to stand for.

What a great spot! I love the vibe here and there is something for everyone: the lively bar area, the more intimate dining room to the side with the secret entrance to gin den Madame Geneva, and the darker sexier downstairs area. We just ordered entrees and asked them to fill in the rest and boy did them! Seafood platter was fresh and so good that it was sweet. Reposting my review! When my parents from out of state wanted to throw us an engagement party, I was having a hard time finding somewhere that could accomodate a group, was affordable, and didn't want us to start at 12 in the afternoon. After doing some research, I stumbled upon Terre a Terre via Yelp and we decided to check it out. We went for brunch on a Sunday, and were presently surprised by not only the atmosphere of the restaurant, but the food! The steak and eggs was delicious, with flavorful sides of fruit salad and potatoes. I usually go for the sweeter side of breakfast, but was beyond pleased with my savory choice. We booked the party on the spot! In between then and the party we went back for my fiance's birthday dinner - all 6 of us enjoyed each course of our meal and there were zero complaints. Our party was this past weekend - chef Todd and staff were great from start to end. The planning process was smooth and easy; Todd is always very responsive to emails with questions. We had a group of about 25 adults and 4 kids. They even offered a kids menu for the little ones which was fantastic (and greatly appreciated by their parents). A bonus of Terre a Terre is that they are BYOB - perfect for our group of celebratory drinkers. I was able to drop off the beer and wine the night before which minimized the stress of having to remember everything the day of. Given that everyone was traveling to NJ for the party and the monsoon-like rain on Saturday, we had a few late-comers. The staff was very understanding and we were able to get the order in without feeling rushed. Everyone raved about the food throughout the party. The carrot-ginger soup was the winner - even my dad who doesn't eat carrot-ginger anything loved it and wanted more! They offered a choice of 4 entrees which everyone was pleased with. I had the steak and it was cooked to rare perfection. Three of my guests are pregnant and have dietary restrictions, and Todd was more than understanding when they sent their steaks back to the kitchen to be cooked well-done. A culinary sin in my opinion, but they were happy with the outcome and went on to enjoy their meals. Everyone also raved about the dessert. My only regret of the day is that I wasn't able to eat any because I was too busy mingling! Overall, we had a great experience and that staff made us feel welcomed and comfortable. I hope they weren't too frustrated with us as it was hard to get everyone to leave since people were catching up, chatting, and drinking. I tried to get the process moving but it took a little longer than expected. I would definitely recommend Terre a Terre and chef Todd for an event. We will definitely be back!!

When you enter you find yourself in a delightful outdoor patio area. I chose to sit inside at the bar and was pleasantly surprised with the friendly attitude of the entire staff and especially by the bartender Grace, I took her suggestion and had a cocktail she called the Lila Jane. What a delight! I started with a salad, burrata cheese and followed that with a snap pea appetizer which was delicious. At the suggestion of Grace I tried the ribeye steak which was fabulous. My surprise was that I could find absolutely nothing to complain about! Everything was cooked perfectly! To conclude this meal I had the berry shortcake, wow! Price was average everything else was above average!

I wanted a place where I could bring my own liquor and I remember Mexicali rose was BYOB. I did not know however that Mexicali rose was closed for buisness. The new name was la cucina Italiana. We said why not let's just give it a try. What an awesome choice for us to eat at this restaurant first off the service is amazing complete attention to detail the waiter took my bottle and made some delicious mixed drinks for me and my wife. I was having a little trouble looking at the menu because most of it was in Italian however the waiter was able to recite all the specials per Batum and let me tell you they all sounded good . The food was absolutely amazing fresh perfectly cooked and delicious. The prices are great I will definitely be coming back to this place everyone should definitely give it a try.

The mutton curry and biryani are authentic in taste and my favorite dishes in the restaurant. The best way to wrap up the meal is to order some saviyan which are covered in chocolate. I have made multiple visits to the place in order to try everything on the menu and have been delighted with the flavors and presentation each time. Their cocktails are great as well although they make them quite strong which may be good for some folks. All in all I would keep going back to them whenever I have a craving for good Indian food which can happen even late in the night as drunken munkey is open till 4 am.

I had an excellent latte here a couple weeks ago. I like that there are multiple seating areas so it's easy to find a spot that suits one's needs (reading vs. studying vs. people-watching). nice staff, didn't have the music too loud, good drinks, great mango and avocado salad.
Great meal the chicken and orzo dish is amazing ... Penne ALA vodka is one of the best I ever had ... My only complaint is the bread sucks and for an Italian restaurant that's a big thing for me
I was a bit disappointed to find out this is the not the traditional dim sum where they push carts around. However, it was still decent. The soup dumpling is the specialty there.
The best pizza i've had in the states. Loving the hot honey on .... well everything.

It's football season and what pairs better with football than barbecue?  So on Saturday when my wife and I were preparing for the Notre Dame v Michigan game we thought that take out from Uncle Willie's BBQ in West Haven would be a great fit.  For those who know me or who have followed my reviews, you know that I am brutally honest. I review a restaurant based on my perception and experience cooking. Now I am a trained chef and my passion is good food, so my rule of thumb has always been that a restaurants food needs to be better than, if not equal to what I can do at home. Unfortunately during this game, Uncle Willie (like Michigan) never made it into the end zone. I will start off by saying that this was not my first time at Uncle Willie's. A few weeks back my wife and I stopped in on a Sunday afternoon to test the food. During that visit all we ordered was ¼ pound of burnt ends and a sweet tea. I was surprised at how long it took them to serve the burnt ends and to be honest I didn't pay much attention until we sat outside to eat.  At first glance I noticed that the serving was not all brisket, to which burnt ends come from. There was a small about of pulled pork in there as well. It really didn't matter at the time, we wanted to taste the BBQ.  I will say the meat had a really nice smoke flavor that wasn't overpowering yet lingered on your taste buds leaving you wanting more. On Saturday we called ahead and ordered two BBQ Dinners with 2 sides. My wife stuck with the burnt ends with  mashed potatoes and  mac n' cheese. I ordered the brisket with  collard greens and the black-eyed peas and rice.  When my wife arrived to pick up our dinner it was ready, so I would say service was quick and without incident, as it should be with a takeout order. However, let's talk about the food itself: Side Dishes:  1 Star out of 5 We had to throw two of them in the garbage. The mashed potatoes were overcooked and the potatoes had broken down and turned into mush, however the chef chose to mix them up and serve them anyway. They lacked any flavor or seasoning, the texture was really unappealing, certainly not the fluffy, creamy, buttery texture you expect from mashed potatoes. The mac n' cheese..... the macaroni was cooked properly but the cheese sauce didn't appear to be house made. I would compare it to one of the canned or jarred sauces you can heat up in the microwave; one that becomes overly creamy when warm, but solidifies like jello when it cools down.  I ate my side dishes, however the collard greens were undercooked and therefore lacked the deep flavors that develop when braising greens. I also found myself searching for the acidity that often accompanies a good southern style collard green, but loved the level of heat that they offered. I enjoyed the black-eyed peas and rice offered as they had a nice flavor and the rice leant texture to the dish, my only concern would be the peas. They were slightly mushy as if they sat in the steam table too long and had begun to overcook or come from a can. Overall a horrible display of quality control and lack of standards, yet if Uncle Willy takes my review to heart, this is an easy fix. Meat: 4 Stars out of 5 I loved the meat.  Uncle Willie knows how to smoke meats, I will give him that. The only reason I didn't give them 5 stars was because of the test experience. I almost feel insulted that the chef that day didn't think anyone would notice the difference between burnt ends and pulled pork and that shows inconsistency. Again, this could be another quick fix. On Saturday. both dishes had an incredible depth of flavor that you can only find in real BBQ. The brisket was tender and fell apart in your mouth, I even had a couple pieces where the fat was not completely rendered down or trimmed away and for me it offered yet another layer of flavor. Just Delicious. My mouth is watering just thinking about it. Pricing: 2 Stars out of 5 I know Uncle Willie is living the American dream and in this for the money, but brother slow down. You're a BBQ shack and I meant that will all due respect. You're not a Michelin rated restaurant offering table service dinner and you don't have expensive china plates. So why charge your customers more than $38 for two takeout boxes??  The simple answer here is, you're overpriced. The restaurant business in NOT a get rich quick opportunity. It's about sharing your passion for food with the people and being able to live off of it. If done successfully, you will find the pot of gold at the end of the rainbow. However $38 for two styrofoam containers with  1/2 pound of meat in them, you won't be seeing this Irish fan on gameday every week.  Maybe to celebrate if we can make the playoffs. Overall - 2 Stars out of 5
Food here very average. Wings r the best that's about it. Beer n patio only plus.  Wraps not that good and nachos dish will make u shart. Owner big dbag

Eaten here twice now. SHS is a warm, welcoming space, with a really nice vintage vibe and a lovely bar. It does a great job of seeming very classy without being stuffy -- a surprisingly local-feeling place considering its location. I've had fish, scallops, deviled egg, chicken and waffles, and an asparagus thing on toast -- all of it was delicious. The food seems to vary between comfort food and more haute cuisine ambition. Servers take good care of you and do a fine job of talking about the dishes without seeming to be laying it on too thick. I can also recommend the Liberal Arts Degree from the cocktail list, if you like whiskey-based cocktails (which I do). A very nice place for a good, casual dinner and a nice drink or two. I live across town, but if I were in this area I'm sure SHS would be my go-to choice.

OK but was not quite as good as we had expected from recommendations. Queued to get in (not unusual), tables too close to each other, overt attempts to up-sell us by waiter, omelettes very odd texture. However, lovely blueberry pancakes!
I can vouch for what everyone else is saying here, that the experience here is superlative in every way.  I don't know why it's not busier.  This place should be packed every night!!!

Reservations are a must at this trendy local, which if you know to ask, is friendly to vegetarians -- just ask for the special menu. Booth and communal seating is available along with service with a smile. The location is a little in the middle of nowhere, but its worth the effort.
A small group of friends met for brunch here. The food was excellent and the staff was super friendly. Even though I had never been here before I was treated like I was one of the regulars.
Great homemade ice cream and great burgers and sandwiches!!

one of my fave restaurants in nyc.  Whatever negative things people say about this place, they are crazy.  The only problem is it's too good and too many people want to eat here, thus during the dinner rush (i.e. 7:00-9:00 time frame) be prepared for an hour to hour 45 min. wait at least. BUT it is totally worth the wait. This place hands down has the best jalapeno margs in the city.  As a resident of nyc for over 10 years and a mexican food addict and moreover someone who loves spicy food/drinks, I can confidently say that this place has some of the best drinks and food you are going to find in nyc.  my husband and I have never had a poor meal there, and we have now tried everything on the menu, including the desserts, everything is great and pretty well priced too.  If you like lamb, the lamb stew is incredible, and the chile relleno is really great.  Tacos are all delicious, my fave is the al pastor ones.  The guacamole is always fresh and delicious and never those big chunks of avocado that you find in some restaurants.  The tortilla soup is great too.  love love love everything about this place.
Stopped here for a family breakfast the service and food were both excellent. Only downside was a slightly limited menu if you want something without eggs.

A bunch of us shared starters and everyone of them was delicious from the Sweet Corn & Red Pepper Fritters to the Mixed Market Melon Salad. The Spiced Vermont Lamb Meatloaf was also very yummy with an interesting mix of organic bulgar wheat, walnuts, currants and chile aioli. I would definitely recommend this restaurant to all.

The guacamole and chips are a great starter, but be fair warned, the chip shape is a little obscure. If you like to drink (and lets be honest, who doesn't?) I'd highly recommend getting pitchers of your favorite adult beverage for the whole table! Hank's Personal Pick: Baja Fish Tacos with an endless flow of margaritas to wash them down.

I love this place!  The food and drinks are great, really reasonably priced, and they are KID FRIENDLY!  I love that I can take my boys here, get great food and not feel like I'm inconveniencing them by having kids.  They bring over coloring books and crayons, have cups with lids and straws, and a great kids menu! So happy to have found a fantastic family restaurant that I actually like to eat at and enjoy myself!

The food is uniquely presented: like the fish & chips-the fish is the whole fish, upright on the plate with a bright orange fish roe mohawk :) Its so good!!- the pop of the sweet roe with the succulent fish- YUM!! We loved the interesting food combinations: like foie gras & grape jelly inside a doughnut!! And best of all, every thing we ate was melt in your mouth delicious!!! That doughnut? i could have eaten several- the doughnut is slightly crispy on the outside with puffy yummy doughnut on the inside & the combo of the creamy foie gras with the jelly? HEAVEN!!! i also highly recommend the fried deviled eggs- i want to try making them for my next party!!! and the fatty lamb with fried eggs over easy & greens with vinaigrette dressing -perfect!!! Will definitely go back!!
Love this place. Food is always plentiful and on point. Been eating here for probably the last 10 years always solid and reliable all the time.

We went out for a girls night dinner with a new baby and were expecting a long wait.  However, we kept getting passed up it seemed and waited a LONG time.  Finally the owner realized we had been waiting for a long time and recognized that we kept getting skipped, and had a new baby (who was very well behaved).  He made it right for us by automatically bringing us free appetizers and providing us a table immediately.   The food was awesome and I would most definitely return because the experience ended positively for us.
If you're drunk and want somewhere fun and chill to go to this is a good place. Good crowd and funny bouncers

Best pizza in the city. This place is great for a date or very small group. The wine list is impressive and there is something for everyone. Zavinos is a place I will always go to when I want pizza. Always fresh ingredients

The food and atmosphere is great but the best of all is the cocktails. I could hang out a t Geronimo's every night if my schedule would allow it. The service is always top notch also! Nothing bad to say about this place.

This truck is fantastic!  They pay great attention to detail and it shows.  I've had their specials each time I've gone. Food consumed:   1. Oxtail soup- Amazing! Came in a smaller cup than expected, but was delightfully filling and came with bread. 2. Tomato Bisque- Delish!  Came with bonus fresh mushrooms! 3. Watermelon Salad- Had mozzarella, basil, and vinaigrette.  Creative, pretty, and super tasty. I really need to try their regular menu items, but it has been so hot lately that I've been going for lighter items. I also want to mention that their customer service is outstanding.  The owner really cares about his product and it shows.  He is highly energetic and very engaging.  Pleasant truck to visit.
They have some strong choices for healthy, dairy-free food options.
Delicious food and nice portion sizes. Rooftop is beautiful and our waiter was very attentive.
Absolutely love this restaurant. My husband and I go often for date night. Friendly staff and great service. Great small plate menu! You must try the mac n cheese!!
Amazing pizza.  Get the mash potato bacon, it doesn't disappoint.

I've now been to La Boca about 5 times and am yet to have an experience that was anything short of amazing. Each pizza has been cooked perfectly, at least in my opinion. The chipotle honey with chicken has already become my personal favorite. The beer selection is purely local, including a selection from Simple Roots (a home-based operation in the NNE). I'd recommend La Boca to anyone and everyone. Great pizza!

So far tried a few different things in Eataly. Most impressed by the seafood section. The razor clams special was a phenomenal experience! Other fish dishes came out good. even the salad there the flavors are spectacular. oysters was so so though.... Another time I tried the vegetarian section. the risotto was one of the best I have ever tried. Other time I bought a loaf of bread from there. Was very expensive but the best bread I have eaten in USA!

Horrible service, the only good server is the little Ecuadorian girl the others including in the front they are not nice and they don't care about the customers. They never put our order and they didn't even apologized for their mistakes.

Neighborhood kinda place - fresh, flavorful, fast, and inexpensive.  You're there for the food, not the atmosphere.  Definite win in my book. Ordered the grilled squid app and it was cooked PERFECTLY, soo tender.  The dressing was a bit acidic, but full of flavor.  Main was the grilled lemon grass shrimp salad or their version of bun tom heo nuong. Pleased it was fresh greens with plenty of shrimp and a bit of noodles.  Solid dish. So, I sat at the bar and observed the cooks.  A takeout dish was being prepared that had cooked bean sprouts and what looked like beef, anyway, the cook placed the meat on the dish and wasn't happy with the look of the sprouts.  Showed it to the other cooks and tossed it. They grabbed a fresh bin of sprouts and remade the dish.  Got the feeling that it had nothing to do with me being there - we'll done guys!

Selection was mediocre.  My steak was cooked perfectly however grossly under seasoned.  Actually every aspect of the meal was under seasoned.  Ironically the salt mill did not work however the wait staff seemed to be cognizant of this and thoughtfully brought me a salt shaker.  The foie gras is a nice and unusual addition to the add-on menu however again could have used some salt.  This place suffers from poor location.  The pricing was what I would expect from most fine dining restaurants.  App, salad, entree, tip, and two drinks brought the total to $106.  Overall disappointed but not a terrible meal.

The food was good and had very nice flavor. I ordered the bbq beef bowl. The problem was the portion was tiny, the price was good but it was literally half of what it should have been. For the type of ingredients and the style of restaurant (mostly take out) they should be giving you twice what they do. I left and went to a pizza joint.
The pizza with prosciutto and arugula was delicious.
One of my favorite places in the neighborhood. The staff is always friendly, there is an amazing beer selection, and it is one of the few bars that has Wi-Fi. The staff is also very friendly as well.

I'll start by saying that I like this place and that I'm sorry that I can't give it the excellent rating. The menu is small and seasonal and yet they seem to run out of things - regularly and this can be quite frustrating. Add to that service is a little spotty - OK, more than a little, and it loses that fifth star. On the flip side, the menu and food are very good and not unreasonably priced. They have a nice, albeit somewhat crowded, back yard and the interior is fairly typical nouveau-Brooklyn and nicely done.

My wife and I have been there about 6 times.  We've always enjoyed the food and the service has been fine.  Sure, it's touristy but so what.  It's a local place that delivers.  They started off small and because they were successful opened up the theater district spot. P.S. My wife and I went to Katz's Deli because it's the oldest and so forth.  It's dirty, they herd you through like cattle, and the staff are completely disinterested in their customers.  Trust me when I say do yourself a favor and avoid the place.

I went there for desert the other night and I was pleasantly surprised.   You can find them right off of time square and the atmosphere is eclectic. I elected for their cheesecake and it was delicious. Weill definitely be making this a regular spot if my thighs can handle it LOL
Best fish and kebab place in the City. Friendly stuff-Ali and Yasin. Fast delivery. The delivery guy is very handsome too.

I'm a vegetarian so burrito box is one of the best places in the city that makes great food that anyone would love.However, recently the service has been really bad.Ive been a patron of this place for years and the simple things like chips and salsa while you wait seems to be a thing of the past..the food is still delicious, but the attitude of the workers behind the counter,service and little things that make this place what it is seem to be gone.

Like the atmosphere here, the halal menu is pretty good and great to choices on it. Pastas were good, I think over the years they've changed portion sizing, not saying that's a bad thing. Go for the more complex items on the menu, pastas are fairly normal. Haven't gone in a while but hope to go back soon.

Not sure why this place has such high reviews... It was average in most aspects. Food is good, but not good enough to ever come back, which is common thing to say in New York: "Yeah, it was good--I mean I'll never go back, but yeah it was solid."

Great selection that goes beyond your typical brunch staples. I had the shrimp hue is rancheros and it was awesome. It's a cute place with plenty of space, you're not too crowded. And on a Sunday at 11:30 we only had to wait about 15 minutes for a table! Good coffee too!
AMAZING!!! Was visiting from out of town and unfortunately was still full from breakfast. Still managed to eat the pork tacos. Definitely a must when in NY

Holy prices are high, I'm not sure why. 10-15 for a glass of beer - I guess if you want to try different ones. Food is meh. Sliced ham and cheese wasn't much better than trader joes. Portions are small. They kept me waiting for an hour which happens, but it's still annoying. Bring cash, split a dish with friends, look around, and split.

We luckily arrived before the big crowds came for brunch. The menu has Mediterranean overtones and the whole menu is offered all day which is a nice perk. Feel like a burger at 9am? Go for it! The house cured duck bacon should not be missed. It's definitely worth a shot if you're in the neighborhood. They offer some really unique items not on your standard eggs and toast menus that you can find elsewhere for brunch.

Love this place! Perfect for brunch and after work dinner and drinks. The owner Dean is my favorite and I love how he always greets his guests when they arrive. The food is delicious and I always come here when I'm in the neighbourhood.

with a name like La Sirene and setting like a restaurant, although there is a bar too, the setting could be compared to a railroad car type diner except with posh seats and comfy atmosphere. Quiet enough to hear a conversation, food titled appropriately, ex: "Frenchy burger" its unpretentiousness puts it in the luxury category and the food was delicious

Best Pizza in Nutley, along with Queen Margherita. There's just something very unique yet authentic about their pizza. Love it with olives or eggplant. I don't think they deliver, though. Limited seating, so good to bring just one or two friends, not a large group.

From the joke-telling doorman to the unique dishes, this is the place for brunch. I had the spinach and mushroom omelette...wonderful. My friends had several of the eggs benedict combos. If you want great food in a casual, friendly place, go to Queens Comfort.

A favorite spot of mine and my wife's.  Features some really delicious food and at decent prices.  Check out their Crab Mac & Cheese.  They get a bit busy though, and finding a table is difficult.  Outdoor seating is very nice. I would skip on their brunch, however.

The service was above average and the calamari was out of this world that is where the heart of my review is coming from. I have been there for lunch a few times and always go with the bourbon burger, the bbq sauce on that has my mouth watering while writing this review.

Great food and service. The restaurant is located in the East Village, away from the tourist sites. We walked around 10 min after getting off the closest subway from the restaurant. The neighborhood is quiet but price is right compare to those overpriced restaurant in Manhattan. Would recommend this restaurant to everyone.

Went here on a date night with my husband. We usually share a bottle of wine, but my husband insisted on starting with a mixed drink. My waiter rudely joked asking if I was planning on drinking he entire bottle. That was the beginning of the problems. We were not offered bread, our waiter did not refill our water glasses until they had been empty for a while, and he didn't offer us dessert. All this while being very attentive to nearby tables. I ordered a medium well steak, but was served a steak that was medium rare. After sending it back for more cooking the manager showed up at our table with the cooked steak and ask us how we are doing. I recognized this as an opportunity to complain, but I was trying to have a nice time with my husband so we said everything was fine. The food was ok, but the service tainted our experience. I would not return.

Food was excellent and reasonably priced.  The meat (at least the Corned Beef, Pastrami, and Roast Beef) were kosher, usually the turkey is too but they did not have it kosher that day.  If you only eat meat that's kosher and will eat at non-kosher certified establishments, this place is definitely for you as I recommend it to everyone, as I had good (but not as great) kosher meat at Hamifgash and Burger.org with bad service, this place is quick and helpful.   .
I enjoy the food, but every time I leave I find myself running to the bathroom for days.  Maybe I am just not accustomed to all the grease in German cuisine...

In Philadelphia for the week-end with my husband from Seattle.  We both grew up eating Jewish food in New York and was lucky enough to get a reservation Saturday night.  This is by far one of the most enjoyable and unique eating experiences we've had.  The server was knowledgeable and  all of the were friendly and very efficient.  The drink combinations including the Manischevitz wine (known in the Jewish community as cough syrup) somehow was turned into an incredible drink.  The food  was absolutely delicious.  The restaurant manager was very personable, interested getting feedback and spent time talking with us.  Only wish we had an Abe Fisher in Seattle!

Hands down the best happy hour in the Hartford/West Hartford area. You can't beat their half price apps and $2 beers. If you're stopping by you have to try the wings, these guys know BBQ! I'd also recommend stopping by on a Friday or Saturday night for great live blues music and an all around festive environment. Hanks Hot Pick: Jambalaya with any of the endless beers that you will always find on tap.
I did not love this place :(

Best Plain thin crust pizza.  Nothing fancy, but so good.  If I am back in the area and craving a slice (or a thin crust cheese pie) I go no where else.  For everything else pizza, I go elsewhere but these guys are plain cheese thin crust savants!

There appeared to be a lot of good brunch food on the menu & we each tried something different. Everything was delicious; I thought the spinach & feta on a croissant was the best. The waitperson was very attentive to our needs.

I went with a group of friends to this exclusive Spanish restaurant. The decor was fun with ample room and a Tuscan atmosphere. The food was subpar to average. The croquettes in particular were disappointing, tasting like they were from a stouffers box. This was on the restaurant week menu. Overall the experience was frustrating each time a course would arrive the initial excitement of what was coming would be met with the eventual sigh of over Americanized Spanish favorites. If you are looking for authentic Spanish flavors, this is not the place to go!
Casual place with great burgers.
Really good food, but the service tonight was terrible

I've been going to Jimmies since I was a little girl. I enjoy the food, but I have measured expectations. The serve can vary from good to lousy, and the fries are usually soggy, but the nostalgia bring me back nonetheless. It is also settled right on the beach, so a long stroll with the smell of freshly cooked seafood wafting through the air usually draws us in.

Amazing restaurant.  It seems like to I am in Korea. Especially seafood is very fresh and delicious. It was great time for me. I would llke tell thansk to sik gaek!! Handsome waiter, has good body. And cute waitress.
Great food, great prices!!  It doesn't look like it from the outside, but you'll be surprised!
I do not recommend this place if you're going for a quick bite because they are stingy and will not give you good service.

Disappointing!!! I've been coming here for quite some time and their customer service keeps getting worse. Sushi is a little over priced and only greet and serve soup and salad to "certain people". They are also ungrateful when you put money in their tip jar. They act like you didn't put money in the jar, or they just don't say thank you.

I've been here a few times with family and friends since this restaurant open.  The service is excellent, the waiter and waitress are very attentive and always asking if there is anything else we need.  Pho Vietnam 78 décor is very nice compare to other Vietnamese restaurants in the city.  They actually have a train and tracks in the restaurant which looks pretty awesome.  We ordered different dishes to share (family style).  For appetizers, we ordered the fried eggrolls, fried squid (calamari) and the salt & pepper soft-shell crab.  All three appetizers were extremely yummy!  For entrees, we ordered the sweet/sour/spicy soup with shrimp, grilled pork chops, clay-pot satay fish, and an order of grilled beef roll wrapped in some kind of leaf with rice on the side.  Everything was very tasty and gooood!  This restaurant has just became my go to place for Vietnamese food.  Would recommend it to everyone.

I came here a few weeks ago with a friend, and we had a great experience. We both had steak with blue cheese on top and it was delicious. My steak was cooked perfectly, however my friend had to send hers back because it was a little more rare than she had ordered. I had the brussell sprouts with crumbled bacon on the side, which were also very tasty. I was displeased that the sides were a la carte, but I guess that should have been expected with a fancy restaurant. I had a sort of iced cream cake for dessert and it was the perfect ending to our meal. I think what really set our experience over the top was our waiter. I believe his name was Chris. He was super attentive to our needs, courteous, friendly, and even made a point to have my dessert dish decorated with "happy half birthday,' because I had told him that's what I was celebrating. My one disappointment were the drink specials. I usually love Max's for their cocktails, as that the tavern has some of the best in my opinion, but theirs were sub par. I would definitely come back here, but I might have to win the lottery first with the NYC prices they have.
We had a mimosa brunch here and it was excellent, the eggs benedict were wonderful. The selection was great, the service was really good and pricing not too bad. Recommended.

Great surprise at the end of an alley! Waiters were really nice, delicious drinks and food (the fish of the day I had, served full but without any fishbone was scrumptious!), great ambiance... A place to go definitely, the only drawback being that you cannot always reserve a table.
This place is tucked below the sidewalk and is small, but service is fast, food is filling and delicious, and the price is affordable. I got an arugula pesto salad and lasagna pesto (I love pesto)!

I love this place. We come here for special occasions the food is always amazing. The food is wonderful. Standouts are the prosciutto e burrata, the mezza Luna (ravioli stuffed with mascarpone cheese and pesto), and the osso buco. (I don't eat veal...or marrow, for that matter...but my boyfriend swears this was the best he's had outside of Italy.) Not only is the food amazing, the service is excellent, as well. Very attentive, knowledgeable and no BS.   The best part is that dinner at L'Incontro is a night out. Unlike most restaurants, where you are given the check the moment you get your dessert, you are expected to spend an hour or two at your table. You are never rushed and never ignored. I'd definitely recommend Trattoria L'incontoro if you're ever in Astoria; and I'll definitely head back, if I'm ever in Astoria again.

Most driest burgers in town... Not to mention the dead flies on the windowsill. I would expect a restaurant to be more aware of health codes. Ohh and I forgot.. The bartender was putting ice into my drink with his bare hands. Is that even legal?

This restaurant has average burgers at best.    The service would maybe rate 2 stars.    With the great positive publicity they receive they definitely should rate no higher than one or two stars.   Stay away and save yourself some heartburn and heartache.
Terrible place to eat. Poor service, lazy staff. I went to eat a burger for lunch and it took a 45mins to get a bacon cheese burger. Unacceptable. I do not recommend and will not return.

The service was terrible and the burger was comparable to a McDonald's hamburger.  It was dry and overcooked.  The fries were plain, nothing special.  Took forever to receive the food after ordered.  Didn't receive a whole lot of attention from waitress, she may have been too busy.

I'm a business traveler who comes to Philly every other month.  My team and I have dined at this place several times (at least four) in the past year, solely because of its location relative to where we work and stay. The staff has never been friendly to us, as a group of black males, requesting to be seated.  Not hostile, just not friendly either.  The food has been average at best and not edible at its worst. The service has never been anything above average, but then it's never been below average. After seeing a customer full credit card receipt posted for the world see and reading the comments by the owner I can say that I will never set foot in the place again and it has been added to the non-reimbursable list for the use of company charge cards so doubt that anyone from my company will either. The management of this company has shown a complete disregard for their customer's privacy and payment information.  I have advised VISA International of this violations of their merchant agreement. Best of luck in the future, you'll need it to stay in business.

I have been here several times. The food has never been an issue. However, the service simply LACKS. Unfriendly, bickering, slow, forgetting things, etc. I give the 3 stars b/c as I said the food is decent even though service LACKS. Middle of the road is as fair as I can give. At some point the poor service will come back on the establishment good food or not and this place will suffer.
I went here with my girlfriend and we had a great time. They have a ton of different alcoholic milkshakes, and the burgers are great.
Awesome food, very good service, would highly recommend to all my friends.

This place is FANTASTIC!! I first heard of them re the D'Oh Nut Burger which my son HAD to try. They have great food, and even a veggie burger (excellent!) And one thing we recently also learned: the owner stands up for his employees in a way rarely seen today! Best place hands down all around!

Found this little gem quite by chance and we can't wait to go back!  My wife got the Vegetarian Mediterranean with delicious variety of olive salad etc.  When the owner brought out the dish he had overcooked the initial set of falafel and brought them out along with an extra set of perfectly cooked falafel.  I ordered the Bean Wrap with cheese etc and had all I could do not to order another it was soooo delicious.  Every place I've ever been will bring you a "glass" of chi.  The owner brought us a small pot that we had to share.  If vegan always tasted this good everyone would walk away from meat.  This is a destination!

My husband and I went here for a double date with my sister and brother-in-law. I also came back with a friend for lunch. I love the chopped salad, so I had that for lunch a second time around. In terms of dinner, We had the late night menu and ordered a bunch of things to share. We enjoyed all of them.
Awesomeness

After a few experiences, I've taking them off my list of local places to grab a bite.  Its a good establishment, and friendly atmosphere, but had a few disappointing (cajun) meals in a row to want to go back.  We enjoy their brunch however.
When I'm in NY, I make it a point to dine good. So on my last trip I came here and yes the hanger steak was amazing + wine selection was something else. Thank you!

I've tried a romantic brunch with my girfriend but it is too crowded for anything romantic. The waitress asked us to change tables in order to acommodate a large group in our table. We ended in a bad spot and the waitress refused to change us for another one, offering it to new clients. Also, it can be noisy because it is small. People told me that the food is great, but we felt so disrespected that we left before the food arrive.
Visited from Chicago and went with local friends.  Wonderful atmosphere, creative and wide menu and knowledgeable service.  A thoroughly enjoyable evening. miker

What kind of place is this? This place charged me 3 times for refill of regular ice tea. I didn't even like their pizza and when they charged me 3 times for refill of regular ice tea made my day. Come on. What is this.  They should have tell me if they were to charge me every time. I don't know why this place is famous. Pizza wasn't that good. Don't go there.

Great menu  , the ambience was great , the food was terrific , the service was very good as well. It was my first time there and I really liked pretty much everything about it. there was a lot of tables open when we went there so I believe reservations aren't necessary. Over all great place.
This is one of my favorite restaurants! I am never disappointed with my food or service. The food is so mouthwateringly delicious, and the menu has something for everyone.

Food was great. The tartar and the ribs were my two favorites, and the donuts for dessert are a must. The food did take a little while to come out, however. And it seems like there's only one or two waitresses handling all the tables even on a busy night, so sometimes it'll be hard to grab their attention when you need something. Otherwise, this is a great restaurant.
Best dumplings I've ever eaten in my life. The prices are unbelievably cheap too, especially for New York City. 4 dumplings for a buck, you can't beat that with a bat! Foamie approves.
super nice place, cool atmosphere and awesome place to eat a brunch on a sunday !

I never met a Mexican Restaurant I didn't like. Then I ate at the Black Ant. . . and while the food was okay/good - it wasn't "oh-my-gosh-this-shyt-is-to-die-for" - which is how I like my Mexican Restaurants. Too dark inside, I literally could not read the menu. Too expensive! $23 dollars for a chicken entree - really? Happy Hour drinks would have been nice for five bucks had they had more than a drop of liquor in them. While the food is plated beautifully, "the proof is in the pudding" (so to speak!). The waiter seemed surprised that I knew any thing at all about Mexican cuisine, which I admit I apparently don't know that much since I've never seen ants and grasshoppers on other Mexican menus; I wanted to try this place, and I did. NEXT!

Yerba Buena is an awesome, upscale but unpretentious, delicious Latin restaurant tucked away in the E. Village. In fact, this place is so unsuspecting we could barely find the entrance on the street. I ordered the Tres Arepas.   Though they are smaller than Caracas' arepas and yellow from yellow corn, I liked them better here.  The three arepas contained short rib, pork, and chicken with egg, respectively. The next time I go, I'm going to try the fish tacos! I would highly recommend Yerba Buena to just about anyone and can't wait to go back myself.

Ordered steak medallion Benedict for breakfast. Issues: 1. Hollandaise sauce watery 2. Poached egg was completely cooked through like a hard boiled egg 3. There were eggs shells in the poached egg 4. Food came out way too fast meaning food was precooked 5. Meat over cooked Hire a new chef or continue to not give a crap about your business. What difference does it make, your location is terrific so why give a damn right? Le comptoir my a$$

Absolutely love this place.  The few years I spent in the area, I came to love this place.  The sicilian is the still the best I have had... and I have had a LOT of pizza.  When I go to visit my folks, my wife and I stop here on occasion.  Next time I'll bring the kids so they can have real pizza for once instead of disgusting Philly pizza.
It's southern food minus the grease and prepared with a twist!
Food is terrible, the kitchen staff is obviously very inexperienced which matches the servers.   All inexperienced serving horrible food.

I would just like to say that I was very dissapointed today with lunch.  I ordered skirt steak and they delivered the wrong steak with a side salad and the side Caesar salad was covered with whole pieces of anchovies.  Not only did I have to wait a half hour for my food to be served but the lunch was messed up completely and the bartender didn't ask me once if I was ok or needed anything else.

We were most happy getting a table without any wait tonight. The don't take reservations. The pizza was pretty good and was served in appropriate time. The really bad thing was that they are somehow suffering from a severe form of wrong calculation not able to put it right even in a 2nd try. Beware!
They should just call this place "Better than Genos".  I will say--the service staff there is always courteous and funny.  Keeps me coming back, that's for sure!
I've gone here a few times for late night dining. The food and music are very good here.
This place has the best margaritas in the entire city!!
I had the spicy pork meatball with risotto and mushroom gravy. I absolutely loved the risotto! The meatball and mushroom gravy were okay. It wasn't what I thought it would be.
I've been twice over the past two months. The food is pretty good, a bit on the pricey side.

Went here last weekend with friends who were regulars. The food was good, but not incredible. I had fresh mozzarella with roasted red peppers. The peppers were amongst the best I ever had, and the mozzarella was fine. My wife had salmon for dinner. She said it was salty. I had the veal pizzaola. It was tasty. I did not notice the salt content until later in the evening, when I was parched. The portion was tiny. Dessert was the special chocolate creme brûlée. It was nothing special. Maria was very nice, but the service was incredibly slow and she had to step in to help. That should not happen.

I've gone here twice for late night dining and once for lunch. The late night menu offers a large selection of delicious cuban appetizers. The food is traditional Cuban kicked up several notches. The lunch menu is affordable and offers large portion sizes. Your meal can easily become dinner later on.
Fabulous breakfast,  luscious lunch, lovely setting, wonderful staff. Fresh, Fresh, Fresh. Go, go, go.

This place is excellent! Every single thing on the menu is incredible. The breakfast sandwiches are one of the best in the city! The service is always good and the prices in my opinion are fair. Definitely check it out!!!!!

I have lived in the Hartford area since 1986 and the First & Last Tavern is one of my favorite restaurants in the area.  This is much more than a pizza place.  The mussels marinara are about the best I have had anywhere.  And lets not forget the arugula salad, the baby artichokes, and of course the bread basket is amazing.  I have never had a bad meal or a bad experience here so I was very surprised to see some very negative comments in a few reviews.  For us, the service has always been prompt and the staff has always been friendly.
High quality fresh fish You get lot for the price compared to other Sushi places Highly recommended
It's first rate all the way. Great food, great ambiance, fabulous staff, opens late...perfect spot for a great date.
We loved our brunch here. The portions were large, for us more then enough to share one. Also the brunch cocktail was a good deal. Loved it, would go there again!

Being in NYC, I had to try the Halal Guys.  Lucky for me, there wasn't a long line.  The portion and the price were good.  I can attest that the white sauce was great, and that the red sauce was indeed spicy.  I have a high tolerance for spicy food, so I can tell you that it is SPICY.   Eat at your own risk.
a bit overrated

I came in for a drink a few weeks ago, I was visiting some friends who were in town. I ordered an Old Fashioned, and was rather shocked that an Old Fashioned with Blantons rang up at $21, this isn't Manhattan...but anyway, I ordered another beer and left. A week later checking my back account I had realized that I was charged $450.+ for that transaction. With haste I called my bank and disputed the transaction then went down to the restaurant to inform them and find out what happend. I met with the GM Daniel, who said that one of the bartenders accidentally plugged in the wrong tip, he said he was sorry and that was that. I was offered absolutely nothing for my trouble, this was not just $50, this was a huge chunk of cash. He never took my contact info or even bothered to follow up with me, my bank is still working out this dispute and I still don't have my money. Beware, it seems they have no idea what they are doing.

Had an amazing breakfast, especially enjoyed the homeade tater tots in the breakfast bowl, and although the atmosphere was clearly too cool for me, I never felt uncomfortable. Service was great, coffee was outstanding.

This sandwich was very good. I ordered it with bacon. Lots of bacon on the sandwich. I took most of it off. Also had the peach bellini -really hit the spot! Cute quaint restaurant. Friendly wait staff.
Absolutely amazing, great food, great ambiance, beautiful place, plenty of rest rooms available...I love it.

The pizza is excellent. Truly a good representation of the greatness in pizza that New Haven has established in it's reputation of great cuisines. They deliver in a timely manner. They are in the middle of the price range, spending around 15$ for a large pizza with toppings and the only reason I don't give then 5 stars is because the pizza has been undercooked 2 out of 20 times we have ordered from them and they got our order wrong once. But this is not enough to stop us from ordering from them, great pizza!
Great Location, Love the vibe, food and love the service, highly recommended!!!

I was recently here for dinner and the food is amazing. We had 2 appetizers, the pitakia kaisarias and the meatballs, both are great. Then for the entree I had the pastitsio which was to die for, and my friend had the lamb which was just delectable. Overall I will definitely come back and try other dishes.

This is a 5-star review even though they forgot a candle in my sisters birthday tiramisu - which they comped our wine and desert because of We started off with the baby arugula and fennel salad with lemon dressing as well as the burrata salad, both were light and refreshing as well as fresh and delicious! Great service, ambiance, and most of all, food! HIGHLY recommend.
Love this place!!! Love the location, love the atmosphere and the decor, love the food, just love it! Try the rum bowl for 2.
Had a great time there. The food was very good, the place looks great and the staff was very friendly. Would definitely go back again. The only downside is that it can get pretty noisy.
Delicious organic burger, but a bit overpriced for the size. Sweet potato fries excellent, but also overpriced.  Service is good.

Ordered carryout for first time.  Food was pretty good, albeit sweet. Then I found that there was a dead bug in my soup.  Can't be certain but it looks like a roach. Safe to say I will never eat here again.
my experience at liming cafe,was not very good.The food is overrated by many.The caribbean soft drinks are watered down and the food too salty.

Amazing bar. Have a large choice of wine, wiskie and have a nice workers. can meet with friends and have some meeting there too.
My wife and I love this place. Great food, friendly service and a full bar.  Authentic and very reasonably priced. Nice addition to the neighborhood!

Definitely planning on going back to try the specialty rolls, sweet shrimp, raw scallop and salmon, service was excellent and very friendly!

27 Mix is a happy find, my consistant choice when I am taking friends out to dinner in the neighborhood. It holds its own against very strong competition in the West Village. Excellent food!!  Awesome customer service!!!  Will def come back again!  The fried whiting was the best I ever had
We went on a week day so it was not too busy. Service was good. Wash rooms clean. Food excellent. I never thought that a watermelon salad could be that good.
I totally love this place. Their mac and cheese is the is good and done to perfection. The waiters are really nice. I plan on coming here very often.

One of the best Farm to Table restaurant in NYC with reasonable price (bar). Highly recommended!!

My wife and I have eaten at this restaurant three times now, so I feel comfortable officially pronouncing that it's just not good. Here follows a tedious chronicle of our experiences: The first time we went, we had brunch. It was OK. The second time we went it was to take my in-laws out for brunch. We were just about to order eggs when we were told that the home fries that came with them were cooked in duck fat. My wife is vegetarian, and, while I'm not, the idea of food cooked in duck fat is gross to me. New plan! I love Huevos Rancheros, so I figured we'd get those. Oh, but those come with duck fat fries, too. The waitress was very clear that there was nothing else that could be substituted for the fries. Unpleasant. Finally, we opted for the special-of-the-day breakfast burritos, since those had their ingredients listed on the board. 40 minutes later our burritos arrived (because, you know, that's how long it takes to make a burrito). It was at that point that we learned that whoever wrote the list of ingredients failed to note that they too also contained the same duck-fat home fries. What the hell? So, ok, there are several levels of madness at work here. Let's dissect this: * First, the list of ingredients was incomplete. So they served my wife something cooked in meat, which she had no reason to expect (especially after mentioning that she was a vegetarian). Not cool, bro. * Now, leaving that aside, what is this lunacy that is putting potatoes INSIDE of a burrito? It should surprise no one that the burrito was bland as all get-out. It was like eating a starch blimp. Also, greasy. God, I feel like I can still taste it now even though this was months ago... * ...and thirdly: OK folks. Let's be honest about the kind of neighborhood this is. Spruce Hill / University City is as crunchy and left-leaning as neighborhoods get. Now, 10% of the US population follow a largely vegetarian diet (surprising, right?). If that's the case, in our little utopia of a neighborhood, with its preponderance of college-age youth and well-meaning old hippies, it's got to be at least 30-40%. Typically, brunch is where vegetarians clean up because eggs (sorry, vegans). But not if you cook everything in duck fat. It's just bad business sense to alienate a large percentage of your potential clientele. Also, I tasted those duck fat potatoes. They tasted in no way different from their oil and/or butter cooked counterparts at other brunch places. It's just pretentious, faux-gastropub marketing. And super unhealthy. Still there? I warned you this would be long. OK. Now let's move on to the coup-de-grace. This evening we wandered in like a couple of hungry chumps. We ordered something that was described as "bolognese with cavatappi, and italian vegan sausages" before realizing that it was 16 bucks. Oy! We were the only customers, so it only took them 25 minutes to prepare our food. The waiter, who seemed affable and incompetent, asked us if we wanted salt and pepper. It's never a good sign if a restaurant offers you salt, by the way. I didn't want to be rude, so I just asked for pepper. I expected that he would come back with one of those long-ass pepper grinders, and that he would make a big idiotic spectacle of grinding the pepper for me, you know, like you do. Nope. Not happening. He brought out one of those super classy $1.99 McCormick black pepper grinders that you get from the spice aisle for when your slightly nicer grinder gets all jammed up. OK. Whatever. Now, I'm just being petty. Here's the thing: The food was terrible. The pasta was way overcooked. The vegan sausages were just the same ones you can get from Trader Joe's, the tomato sauce tasted canned, and because the whole thing really did need salt, there was nothing to mask the tinniness. It was cafeteria-quality pasta. The whole thing was very home-cooked tasting (and not my home, by the way). It was so terrible that my wife and I couldn't make eye contact when the waiter came and asked us how everything was. (I told him it was great, obviously. I'm not some sort of crazy madman who would give another human honest feedback except on the internet when it's too late for him to do anything about it. I mean, jeez.) This restaurant looks absolutely charming from the outside. They have a (very loose) "concept" (it's farm-to-table, guys! come on! eh...) and a knack for pretentious gastropub-sounding menu items (along with fancy gastropub logo design and pricing). Their website describes them as a "destination." Unfortunately, this place is writing checks it can't cash. They just aren't able to execute that level of food at all. I feel badly leaving a negative review for this place because everyone who works there seems so young, but after three truly sub-par and not cheap meals, I actually want to save my fellow humans from wasting their time and money.

If anyone reads this review and finds anything I write to be disparaging, it is absolutely not intended that way. We were in town for a week for the Special Olympics National Competition. The opening ceremony was at the New Jersey Devils arena on Sunday June 15th. After the ceremony finished, we had hoped to find a local spot at which to eat nearby before heading back down to the Princeton area where the competition was to be held. We were just wandering about lost kind of following the river and came upon a bridge with a steakhouse restaurant adjacent to it. Restaurant looked ok, but we wanted something a bit more casual, someplace with some local flair, ideally. Crossed the bridge and came upon the Spanish Pavilion which from the outside with its strings of lights in the outdoor seating area looked like a fun beer garden sort of place. We looked at the inside dining area which seemed nice and comfortable (in an old-style vinyl booth kind of way), but opted for the simpler outdoor area since it was a gorgeous night and we could just nibble on their tapas-style menu and relax and take our time amongst the lively local crowd. Boy did this place hit the spot right on the head. It was perfect. The weather was wonderful, there was plenty of room, nice TV's with the world cup soccer game on, and lively groups of locals scattered all about. The prices for the tapas and beer were reasonable. The food was exactly what we were looking for; something a bit different and kind of old-school. It definitely was not nouveau cuisine but tasty -- calamari, ribs, large sardine-type fish, stuffed mushrooms, bread, etc. Definitely food that stuck to your ribs, especially since several seemed to be sauted in butter. However, I love to people watch and I was in heaven; the ambiance couldn't have been more perfect. Watch some soccer, chat with the wife, enjoy a beautiful night, and watch everything going on around me. I felt like I was on the set of the Sopranos. The group next to me of various middle-aged men and women with amazing high hairdos, discussed a number of various topics throughout the evening. One that stood out regarded one of the ladies (who were all in tight dresses which showed off their ample figures) being at a local place where some fellow that the group seemed to know. This fellow was hitting on her. Apparently she was already in a relationship/married (which apparently was also known by aforementioned Don Juan), and the various men all waxed poetic about how they might rough up or disembowel Don if this fine lady had been their significant other (but the language was much more colorful, and the accents (for this local Bay Area guy from West Coast) were to-die-for). Across the courtyard was a sweet couple with a child in a stroller. His white T-shirt was rolled up to hold his pack of cigarettes and they seemed to be enjoying a wonderful evening together. The pretty young hostess who was behind the outdoor counter and took my order, rung me up and poured our first round of beer, warmed up to me after awhile, it seemed -- it was just like old times in school back on the East Coast where people didn't do the "California" fake "friendly, chummy" attitude toward someone they didn't know or weren't friends with. Getting our second beer, I was served by another fellow who, clearly, was old-time staff at the restaurant; he brusquely served me the beers and notably made no effort to clear off the ample frothy head on each beer to fill the glasses any higher with beer. When it was time to leave, we went inside to use the restrooms which were in the bar area at the front of the establishment; the restaurant was emptying out and it was just a few stragglers that seemed to mostly be hanging at the bar. There was all the usual loud banter about the local political/sports-team messes with those great East Coast Jersey/NewYork accents. As usual, wife ran longer in the restroom so I had a few minutes to enjoy this other unique nook in Spanish Pavillion. All in all, Spanish Pavillion was by far the highlight of the day for me and the exact gem of a place that we were looking for. When I looked on Yelp and discovered from other reviews that this place had also been on the Ramsey restaurant reality show, that just added to my feeling of having hit the jackpot. Thanks again for a great night, Spanish Pavillion, and may your future be bright and full of success!

The drinks were pretty terrible and way over priced, the sangria was probably the worst I ever had. The bartender did not seem to know what he was doing. The location is not bad and the decor is pretty interesting but that is all. Nothing to write home about.

Time to either revamp the place or get out so another restaurant can make use of you special location and space. Will not be back Alta!!!

I used to order from them all the time - but since I go to college, I tend to have an issue with drivers telling me to walk to some weird parking lot like 5-10 minutes from my dorm room to pick up the food. Normally, I'll just politely make it clear that it's NOT an apartment building and to please come to the door and they'll do so without incident. It's happened three times now that they'll refuse to and just leave. The first two times, I just called the store and asked what the heck is going on and they send out a new driver with new food and it's okay. Normally they don't sound too happy about it, obviously, but it's their job. Every time, I've been exceedingly polite and patient with them. I used to work in food service (People's Choice Pizza, actually, in Wethersfield) and a few other places, so I ALWAYS tip well and am EXCEEDINGLY polite with them. This past time, however, was different. I ordered my usual online and waited for them to come here. About 40 minutes after I placed the order, I got a phone call from the driver. He asked me to come out, I made it clear that it was NOT an apartment building and to PLEASE come up to my door with the food. He seemed hesitant at first and said he had to call his manager, but after I made it clear that I just wanted him to come to my front door and described where it was he said okay. He said he wasn't sure where he was, but he would be there very soon. I was left waiting for 25 minutes. So I called him again to ask where he was and he didn't pick up. So I called the store to ask what was going on. It turns out that the driver had just LEFT after speaking with me - without so much as a word. Please keep in mind I paid by credit card. So, I complained. How is it okay for a driver to just leave like that without warning? I didn't (and don't) think that I was asking for too much to have the delivery driver come up to my door - rather than making me walk literally 5 minutes to get my food. I ended up somehow getting connected to the absolute rudest manager I have literally EVER spoken to. Possibly one of the rudest human beings - and I've worked in retail/sales for most of my career life. He talked over me - literally refused to listen to what I had to say. He actually told me that I was lying and the driver said I was rude and therefore it was okay for him to just leave without notifying me. He also said that the driver just leaving without letting me know or giving me a chance to walk over (because it's REALLY not that big of a deal - it's annoying, but if he flat out refused I would have done it anyway) was acceptable and he doesn't see why I'm upset. He even expressly told me that he doesn't want my business because I was being rude on the phone with him (at that point, I admit that I was getting pretty short because of what he'd been saying). He also then took it upon himself to cancel my order and hang up on me. I am NOT happy with what happened. Even if I WAS rude (which I KNOW I wasn't - I'm the most quiet, passive person you could ever meet -, but for the sake of argument, say I was), that is NOT acceptable customer service behavior. You do NOT tell the customer they're lying. You do NOT hang up on the customer. You do NOT just LEAVE with the customer's food after telling them you'll be right there. I have the phone conversation recorded, and you can believe I will be doing my best to take this to corporate levels. The food is fantastic here, but this is WILDLY inappropriate and unacceptable. They will NOT be getting any more of my business.
One of my favorite lunch time spots. I've never had a bad experience here. Kabobs and fries are very tasty!

Terrible food. Went for dinner on a Thursday; clearly it's not popular for the cuisine. Ordered about 6 tapas and a burgers with fries. Sent the empanadas, chorizo and chicarones back because they were too salty. By the time they returned, I was just no longer hungry. We got a free drink because we complained about the food, but...

I love ramen. Being a fan of Daikokuya and Orenchi, I wasn't sure how Ippudo would compare, but it blew me away. Went for dinner (around 5pm) and was told the wait would be 30-45min but tt would be faster if we waited inside, so we waited by the bar and the wait ended up only being 20 min! The pork buns were amazing. I wish I ordered five for myself! As for the ramen, the Akamaru Modern was so flavorful and delicious... just writing about it makes me miss it! :9 Slightly pricey for ramen, but hey, it's NYC, and I have to say... you get what you pay for (and it's delicious!) Wish this was on the West Coast...

Bad food, with inattentive if sincere service. Salad - bland. Crab Cakes - no seasoning whatsoever, very little taste of crab. Meatloaf - moderately acceptable, with gravy that had about twice as much salt as proper, served with zucchini that was so undercooked it was crunchy... except for the disks that were so overcooked they were mush. Really, really really bad.  Stay away
