Very disappointed with Papa's. I had heard that it compared to Delorenzo's so we decided to give it a try. The hostess was extremely rude, but we kept going. Pizza was ok, definitely no where near as good or as fresh as Delorenzo's. I actually think it tasted like any old standard pizza place. We also had to ask for clean dishes since ours were filthy when they came out to us. Since then, we know friends of ours (that were 'regulars' there)  got into a bit of an issue with the same hostess and a man who was in the kitchen running the place. Not surprised.  Overall review:  rude staff + mediocre food = won't ever be back. Delorenzo's wins our vote hands down. Fresh ingredients, much friendlier staff, cleaner place, and a much better pie! Another great place in the area you won't be disappointed in is Palermo's on 206 in Bordentown. They are great with their customers and their pie is awesome!! Highly recommend them as well : )
Ordered chicken fried rice. It was flavorless & there was no chicken in it. I usually like this place. Very disappointed! I miss Sesame!

Very good Cuban place.  Some modern twists on Cuban classics while maintaining the true classics like Pernil and Ropa Vieja.  Tapas style works well and the bento main dishes didn't disappoint.  Mojito was excellent.  Decor is nice and subtle, classier and simpler than some other neighborhood places.  Staff is also very nice. Definitely recommend it.

Yikes. The ambiance was dated, the carpet was dirty, it looked like no-one dusted their drapes in years. The bar in the front was deserted and looked like you were entering along side another restaurant as a guy too well dressed for the establishment led you to your table (this is not a professional steakhouse--the man was practically wearing a tux). Upon seating, we (eventually...despite the open tables around, the staff waited until we had cleared the bread basket before deciding to take our order) ordered a few unremarkable appetizers including a soggy breaded/fried/stuffed cheese and prosciutto special which was underwhelming. The salads were wet and wilted.  Whatever dressing was added was just watered down by the residual rinse water on the leaves, leaving a soupy mess where a crisp salad should have been. My peppercorn encrusted steak with a light brandy cream sauce was none of those things. First, overcooked from medium rare to well done, and was either gristly or nervy, depending on where you cut. Second, zero peppercorns. Lastly, smothered in some heavy sauce which might as well have been a vodka sauce, as it was pink, sour, and didn't belong on a steak. I can't recall what the other pasta-based entree we ordered was, but I can tell you when it arrived, it literally looked like refuse. I've never seen a dish so unappetizing. A quick taste confirmed that we wouldn't be eating any of that--bland, watery, rubbery pasta overlaid with some random assortment of 'rustic' elements (ie under cooked vegetables) all drenched in some kind of liquid pretending to be a sauce. Credit to the waitress who did recognize our plight and comped our wine, however. In the end, we still left with a bill completely disproportional to the terrible food we ordered--even if the food was great, the place is overpriced for what they offer, which is poor quality Italian-American masquerading as some sort of fancy eatery. The menu items all listed in Italian that the wait staff had zero knowledge of should have been a tip-off. Unless you said "you know, the pork chops", 'costata di maiale alla valdostana' wouldn't get you very far. There are so many great Italian restaurants in the area there--this one clearly fell through the cracks over the years.
The arepas are equivalent to or possibly better than the Caracas NYC arepas chain.
The sushi was great, but we spent over $300 on LUNCH drinking water. In my opinion there are other great sushi restaurants that are a better value.
The best vietnamese ever! My husband and I had classic pho, my son had fried spring rolls. They were absolutely fantastic!

I've been to plenty if food trucks and I've waited for a pretty long time,  but I have never in my whole life had to stand their for a whole 2 hours!!!!'. To be fair there was a long line but you figured they would be good at their job.  Taqueria Autentica doesn't earn to have a food truck let alone a restaurant.  I wouldn't even bother looking at this food truck.  If you were to take a pile of shit and call that food it would still be 100x  better than the garbage they produce.   Rating:  -5 stars I have never Waited for food from a truck this long and when I did the food was actually worth it.

We all loved it! The service was excellent, and the food was delicious. My braised octopus appetizer was one of the best things I ever ate! The pasta was perfect. My only complaints were the over-priced cocktails and the volume of the noise - the background music made conversation difficult.

Hands down THE best place in this neighborhood. I'm always here and love every single one of the staff members. Brunch on Sat & Sun is phenomenal and the setting is perfect. Huge fan of sporting events being played but not having the sound on because sometimes you just wanna relax and not be swarmed by rowdy patrons n shit. A+'s across the board from this guy. This is my first and probably only Yelp review so it was saved for a prime spot.

Something has changed. I have been to this restaurant many times during my time at UVM and always left full and happy! I even considered Magnolia as my favorite breakfast spot in Burlington. When I came back to visit for the weekend, I couldn't wait to go back! Sadly, this time around, after waiting 40+ minutes for our food, the coffee was weak, the toast was stale and cold, and the food was very greasy. The biggest difference was the potatoes served with the omelet. They used to be tender nice chunks of potato cooked with great seasoning and amazing crispy but not greasy texture. What I saw next to the omelet was bland and unseasoned potato stringy strands swimming in the vegetable oil, like the potatoes you find at the Denny's on route 7. Disappointment is an understatement. Has there been an ownership change? What's going on Magnolia?

What is so great about this place. I went way out of my way to come here last Sunday afternoon. You have to order brunch which I didn't feel like so I went with the steak and eggs. The table next to us ordered after us. By the time they had eaten and were paying there bill I asked where our food was. When it came the waiter said the steak takes a long time causing the delay. My steak was very rare in the first place but I did say rare. But it was also cold so if that's what held up the meal it should come to me hot right. Other than that the food was OK but it was outweighed by snobby pretentious lousy service. See ya. Oh and way overpriced.

The waitstaff are always attentive to patrons needs and very informed which helped us in deciding on the meal. We chose to share a kale salad together to start and for the main course I chose the Colorado lamb while my wife chose the Amish chicken. The dishes were tasteful and beautifully arranged. In between each course the chef would send  out small samples of new tastes that would complement our meal. A very lovely evening was had here.
Yum. Best pizza yet. The mini pepperonis are so delicious on the crispy crust and amazing sauce.
The vegetables are super fresh and crisp and the fried chicken is crispy without being greasy. Service was incredibly friendly and prompt. Lovely atmosphere outside on a warm fall evening.

I went with my family yesterday, and I was not impressed, not only was the wait long but once they seated you it was another two hours to get some food.  It was as if the waiter completely forgot that we were still waiting for our food. Once the food arrived it was cold and not totally impressed.  I won't go there again.  If you don't mind waiting then go ahead give it a shot.

An honor to review one of my hometown favorites! Grew up eating paella marinera here. Just the smell is so nostalgic! The sweetest most friendly staff, lovely ambiance, and the BEST bread and paella. Delicious flavor on the rice and the tender seafood. Also loved the spicy and regular olive oil selection. Didn't have room to get postre, but dessert menu looked very exciting.
Great breakfast & staff was very attentive even with my mom who is visiting and older!

I've been looking for a really good soul food restaurant for my Sundays off and after reading the reviews fir B's I had to give it a try and it was AMAZING!! I had ny favorite meal fried chicken mac and cheese collard greens candied yams and cornbread The chicken is perfectly seasoned and crispy you can tell everything is homemade nothing frozen even though I'm used to greens with some meat in them and theirs had none they were still packed with flavor!! Even the Pepsi was slushed and cold and a glass of crushed ice completed everything I felt like I was at my grandmother's house in north Carolina perfect earning of 5 stars!!

Food was outstanding! The experience was really fun starting with a greeting in Japanese that meant welcome. Noodle Ramen was very flavorful. However we would've like to have the pork to be cut up in the Soup. Edamame with the special salt was outstanding. Cucumber dish was excellent. Green tea sorbet was different. We would return.
very delicious

One of the best sandwiches I've ever had meat is packed on there so it's more than just two slices of bread staff is very friendly and personal... My only complaint and it's so minor I'm not gonna take off a star is that it's cash only but that's it on the negative this place is phenomenal

I loved thier buffet. Biriyani,Baigsn Bharta and mutter panner was super good. They even had kachhi keti sharbat which was super delious. Yummmmm food. Please do try once and ignore all the negative comments.
Craft cocktails and authentic indian cuisine! loved every bite and savored every sip!

Never the judge or a juror, just a foodie .We were not thorough with Geno's critique, because it wasn't worth the memory... to rehash the nightmarish experience naah , but Pat's was better. This will help you greatly, if you trust our experience , We went to 6 spots, Pat's was one of them, of course, considering the hype. Meat, cheese and toppings, bread, and overall sandwich considered.  BREAD: was fresh, and a good texture, on a scale of 1-5 , the bread was a 4........MEAT: the meat had no seasoning, as if it were frozen, then on the grill, the natural steaming process was a problem , on the =15 scale it was a 2.5.....CHEESE AND TOPPINGS: though not a fan of cheese whiz , it did compensate for the lack of flavor of the meat, and the WIT(onions)  was WHAAAT???? enough said, scale 1-5 it was a 2.75. OVERALL SANDWICH: though better than Geno's, that's not saying much, on the 1-5 scale it was a 3, Pat's and Geno's isn't the real Philly battle that's needs the hype, they are close to throwing in the towel, because they know people will come anyway, and that's sad .Give other places not so publicized a chance, and you will be surprised. I'm not wacking Pat's , but, a horse head is in the bed.
As good as I remembered it being 2 years ago (other location). If you like ramen go here it's amazing !

Pretty amazing date place.  Has a good variety of risotto to choose from.  The negative is that it's pretty much just risotto and not a big selection. Other than that great service and pleasant atmosphere.

Good for happy hour but the staff never knows the drink specials and frequent give the wrong pricing on the bill. Check the bill before you pay! They corrected it when highlighted but this is a little frustrating....

Some of the menu is quite good, but as a review of their omakase, my experience was very sore. A friend and I went in hoping for a creative and delicious evening. What we ended up with was standard fair. The chef prepared our entire omakase at the same time and then brought it to us, although we were sitting in front of him at the sushi bar. The arrangement was your basic nigiri lineup. In fact, the chef even asked us if he should add toro. I mean, I confirmed that we were doing an omakase before we started, but it looked like he just prepared something akin to "sushi platter number 1" and tossed it at us. And although the chef had other (albeit at most two) fishes available as specials, they were not presented. Moreover, we wouldn't ask for them,  since what we did receive was...off. The fish was cold (not body temperature) and awkwardly cut (size), the rice was overly firm, and honestly, the experience as a whole was disappointing and lacking. Especially when we saw the bill at the end. What did we pay for? Certainly not the guided tour through beautifully prepared fish we were expecting...

We had fun here. Late Monday night after work shenanigans. Pitchers of beer were good , food was solid (if small on Portion side ) we had a laugh ticking our menus and the server was really pleasant. An intimate, fun place - good beers, big table to accommodate lots of us, an outdoor seating area that's a bonus for those nice fall days and nights we have right now and decent prices too. Well worth a visit. Vegetarians catered for too!

We had heard great things about this restaurant, but were disappointed in the service. We had a party of six, and were only served five pieces of veal for our table. Instead of adding one more piece, we were told we would have to order a whole additional plate. While the quality of the food was good, the poor service made this an unhappy experience.

Foodwise it totally deserves 5 stars Plus! However the service yesterday was not what one would expect for a 4 stars and a half restaurant. I get that on a Saturday night this place gets very busy but it was quite annoying to see the servers literally running to and from the kitchen and arguing with each other. Maybe they need another busboy 'cause the hostess was cleaning the tables which meant that she would "welcome" the clients with hands full with dirty dishes which was pretty uncomfortable. However, the food was awesome. We've been here 3 times already and we love everything we've always had. We always get pasta or risotto and love all of them so far. Our favorites are Papardelle, the black risotto with squid and the goat cheese ravioli. So, a piece of advice, even though they need to improve their service, this place is a MUST in terms on good Italian Food! Let's hope I can upgrade this review soon to 5 stars as it deserves!

Lovely jewel of a restaurant.  Met friend we hadn't seen in over 25 years.  General Tso, fish tacos, hot sour and tom yum soup.  BBQ ribs to die for. Ambiance of elegance, piano music....lovely baby grand with classical beautifully played.  Lovely lighting.  Best Chinese in years

The service was flawless from the time we arrived till the moment we left. Everything was fantastic, I went with my wife and some friends and they gave us a very big and comfortable table. I have to say that the food was really beyond my expectations. I had the Porccini Flan as appetizer and the Lamb as entree. My wife had the shrimp and scallops, I've tried some and it was delightful. I would highly recommend this restaurant.

One of my favorite places in Philly. From the ribs (which you should order dry rubbed) to the brisket sandwich (which you should get as a wrap) to perfectly seasoned fries and chips, there's no end to the great choices at El Camino.

Me: Time to write a review for The Halal Guys! BF: Like they need another review... Me: Hmm, good point. No need to write a long review here. There's a reason why they're so popular and they always have a line and people coming back for more. I have visited NYC at least 5 times and never tried them and decided this was finally the time! Everyone says: chicken & rice w/ the white sauce. However, when I was in line I kept hearing people also ask for barbecue sauce too so I decided I must get that as well and I'm super glad I did! Line seems long (well, it will always be long) but it goes pretty quick and you'll be happy you waited in line! Don't forget to bring your CASH. Now go try some!
Had my first Philly cheesesteak there.  I had the one with the broccoli and I was not impressed. I'm never coming back there.
Hm...I don't see why this place has 4 stars bad food and very slow service. It's better to eat at home.
Awesome!  Love the atmosphere, the grapefruit hefeweizen, spicy sausage and pretzel with dip!
fresh and delicious sushi. and 50% off on certain days! what else can you ask for?
Nice bar, excellent service from Mike the bartender.  I'd definitely go back.  I want all my bourbon and rocks served with ice on the side from now on.   Steak egg rolls were ok.

I was in Philly a few days ago and heard about this place. Iit was very disappointing. These guys seem to be riding their name, the steak was dry and the cheese almost non existent. My girlfriend and I shared one sandwich and had to throw half away... I would definitely NOT recommend.

I go to Cafe 72 multiple times a week. I enjoy both their stand-by menu items as well as their daily specials. I am especially fond of the selection of grilled cheeses. The breakfast options and lunch options are equally strong. Classic breakfasts like Eggs Benedict are expertly prepared. There are also exciting modern takes on classic breakfasts such as the Croissant French Toast (which is AMAZING) or the Fig Waffle with Blueberry Chutney and served with Cannoli Cream. As I said, the lunch options are also very strong. I've tried the burgers, sandwiches, soups, salads, and pretty much every category of food on the menu. I have never been disappointed by any item I've ordered thus far. I especially like the daily lunch specials. Occasionally they have a lamb burger, pork & mango bbq sandwich, or the chicken mango wrap. Recommended for all ages and all palettes.
I order takeout literally three times a week!! My FAVOURITE indian food, by a mile!! I love their extra spicy chicken tika and garlic nan SOOOO GOOD

My fiancé loves this place and brought me here a while back. She said she used to go out the one in Queens when she lived there. The food is awesome and not expensive, which is nice change for this hood. Only thing I gotta say is the hostesses are kind of rude. We've gone there before around 5:30/6pm after work and they've given us a hard time about getting a table inside (during summer) when there were clearly tables inside, the place isn't small. The food made up for it though.

The environment is very romantic, but somehow it's too dark. We have difficulty to look at the menu. The waiter was very polite and provided excellent service.  Our waiter's name is Kike.  He served us professionally.  The food and drinks were delicious.  I'm highly recommended it and I'm definitely will go there again!!

I was visiting Hartford, Ct. from the San Francisco Bay Area and one of the locals suggested I try this Sorella.  The staff was friendly and the food and wine were good.  Nick the bartender can carry a pretty good conversation.  Friendly type of guy.  I would recommend this restaurant and dine her again if I was ever back in the area.
More vegan options than I expected. The collard green wrapped farmstead was hardier than expected.
A great mix of ex pats and locals. Never had a bad night there. Staff are very friendly and food tastes great. Being smokefree and a western toilet would give it a 10/10 but when in china....
it's atypical diner fare but it's pretty good

Meh. Did lunch there with co-workers for Restaurant Week. Service was EXTREMELY SLOW. I myself am a server, and can tell when a server is just busy or just slow! The restaurant was only half-full. Our drinks took fifteen minutes to arrive; we only got wine and beer, so that was way too long.  App was a plate of spicy meatballs.  They were good, but the portion size was really small, even for Restaurant Week. Burger was just a regular old burger, nothing special.  They barely gave us any fries. Lastly, the dessert was a plate of assorted chocolates and a shot of espresso, which, in theory, sounds delightful. But again....MEH

Very small portions, unless you want a quick bite, one kathi roll is not filling. Also it is no where close the original middle eastern/Indian kathi rolls. I like their unda shaami a little, but spending 12$ for a decent filling meal is a big No for me. I think this place is more of a hype than quality.

Seated quickly and with a great spot to watch the passers by but under cover. Ordered soup and salad - i assumed they would come separately but they didn't - that would be my fault but a too would be to mention that to your waiter. French onion soup is great. Beet salad is awesome

Visited the truck at the Manayunk Streat Food fest. The Jagerschnitzel was extremely tasty and it was made very well. The coating was crispy and light and the meat was juicy. I was hesitant to order because it required a fork and knife which makes for difficult to eat street food. But I certainly recommend taking a few minutes to find somewhere to sit if you come across this truck.
Prepare yourself for an absurd wait, but Chuko always is delicious and wonderful.

This place is awesome and totally shocked me! I came in with a group of co-workers we ordered the Max's Pie that was simple and amazing, smoked chicken wings with bbq sauce (that they make in house) and crispy wings there was a live band and we sat outside but the inside was a bit small but overall great space service was great (young kids but helpful) we'll be back!

Happened upon this place on our way out of town. So glad we did. GREAT sandwiches and local beer selection. Comfortable little place to grab a bite with good service. Prices were very reasonable, too. Check it out if you're in town.

I discovered that Yuji Ramen has a pop up on monday and tuesday here at Okonomi. Happy to see they've found a new home since they closed in Whole Foods. After two visits, all of the food I had was excellent. Service was polite and prompt. Wait was manageable, and very professionally handled by the front of the house. Prices were extremely reasonable based on the quality of the ingredients. I'll be returning here as often as I can. Looking forward to having lunch at Okonomi as soon as my schedule allows, I hear its great from a few friends.
The food is good, and the chef is super attentive to preference and allergies, so that's a plus.  The service is always solid and the happy hour cannot be beat.  Solid go-to local place.

This place is great ! My friend and I had to wait about 10 minutes for outdoor seating which was amazing, considering it was a Saturday night in NYC in the middle of Times Square. The food was ok, but the cheesecake was amazing as always !!
Amazing pizza so tasty, this is New York pizza with a true salute to Italy. Service was fast and managed to get a table without reservation. If I lives in New York I'd be back once a week.

It's a shame that Bella's is so slow because their food is fantastic. I am consistently impressed with the creativity and deliciousness of their dishes, but unfortunately I can't recommend going here except at the oddest hours of the day. I am always frustrated and disappointed at how long it takes even when barely half the tables are occupied. I'm generally very easy going and don't mind waiting for good food, but the last four or five times I've gone I've brought friends or family with me. Based on my rave reviews of the food, they've eagerly ordered anticipating a great meal ahead. Every time I've been left embarrassed to have brought them as their stomachs growl and their patience wanes before our food arrives. Every time they have vowed to never come back. All agree that the food is good, great actually, but waiting over an hour for eggs is just not worth it. Apparently I haven't learned my lesson and after a few months go by I return hoping they've figured out a system to move good quicker, but it seems as though that's an optimistic wish. Please Bella's expand your kitchen. We want your food, but not the wait!

The antique menu, long wait times and constantly overturning juvenile staff make this beautiful club not worth joining. Ed, the bartender is the only reason this place even deserves one star, he's fantastic .

I'm a peruvian food fan ; but this restaurant needs to improve a lot: The "chicha morada" was poor ..no taste, ,,the "green" peruvian sauce was really bad,taste like rotten.. and brown-mustard color far away from the real taste it should be,,my wife ordered a "lomo saltado" and couldn't finished it, ,,it was too hard...,,sorry...I can't give better score..,

It's been about a year since my husband and I traveled to Burlington for a wedding. We were enjoying our own self-proclaimed bar crawl on Church St. stopping in for drinks at as many bars and restaurants as we could. The Scuffer Steak and Ale was one of our last stops, and since we'd already eaten dinner a couple hours beforehand, we both decided to get bowls of clam chowder. I still think fondly and dream of this clam chowder. It is the clam chowder against which I judge all other clam chowders. And I am always disappointed. Hands-down, the BEST clam chowder I have ever had the privilege of devouring. It was so clammy, creamy, rich, and well-seasoned. It was somehow more savory than other clam chowders I've had, and everything about it makes me sad that I'm not in Burlington right now. It didn't hurt that our waiter was probably one of the best servers my husband and I can recall in our vast dining-out history. We also enjoyed the restaurant's effortless charm. It was a comfortable, classy place to have a drink or a meal (or both). Or just the clam chowder. If ever we find ourselves in Vermont in the future, Scuffer Steak and Ale will be our first stop.
food was nothing special. i suppose you are paying for the ambiance and the service. this was to be expected at a stephen starr joint

The Manor in West Orange came highly recommended. My brother had his senior prom there and decided to have his wedding there.  When we went for the rehearsal, the chairs outside were soaking wet and we were told they would be cleaned off the next morning, but they were still wet and ruined a few dresses.  The manor was supposed to have a dressing room for the bridal party and also the groomsmen. The morning of the wedding the bridal party ended up in a tiny room and the groomsmen in the men's lounge.  There was another event going on and the dressing rooms were given to them and it was a sweet 16! The pathway to the outside alter was crooked cobblestone with moss on it. There were empty beer bottles and cigarette butts along the guest pathway. The maître d' was rude and obnoxious.  He was really pushy and brought down the mood of the day.  None of staff had smiles on their faces and the plates were cleared too quickly. The food was great, but the overall experience was poor.

I discovered this gem a year after having moved to Astoria. It's BYOB and the food is AMAZE! I ordered the ceviche but my husband did not shy away from the carbs. Besides the food, the quaint tchotchke-filled decor and friendly servers are reason enough to keep coming back.

This place is AMAZING. The food is extremely fresh (it's a farm to table/fork place) and the taste of everything that we had was delish! I forgot the name of the drink that i had but it was a play on a michelada with a spicy twist to it - also terrific and the spiciness was not overbearing. My boyfriend got the Bloody Mary which was probably the best that i ever had, but slightly heavy for dinner (the tomatoes they used are grilled so it tasted WOW and it was topped with a piece of grilled pineapple and kale). We started off with the Grilled Vegetable Taco and the Risotto from the small plates and both were terrific. The taco had a really good flavor given it was vegetarian and it was also filling. Presentation of both were outstanding! We then moved onto the sliders (beware - it's a nice and large slider!) - we wanted the short rib however it was sold out, so we instead picked the Almond Crusted Tilapia slider which was also great and had good flavor - this was probably my favorite items and it comes with a side of calamari fritters which was perfectly cooked - no fishy taste at all! Last, we got the Hawaiian pizza - the grilled pineapple and prosciutto complimented each other perfectly - also there was lots of prosciutto! I was already stuffed from dinner but obviously had to get dessert - we got the White Chocolate Flan Cheesecake. So rich and amazing. It wasn't too big too so just a couple of bites of heaven to satisfy your sweet tooth. I will definitely be back!!! Looking forward to trying the other small plates and desserts. Moderately priced for fresh ingredients too! #foodcoma  Perfect place for DATE NIGHT!

After reading a blog which stated the Spotted Pig was one not to miss, I made plans to visit. It was a Wednesday night and heaving! Best to arrive early and get yourself a table/spot at the bar before the place gets extremely busy. They don't take recommendations so it's a case of pitching up and chancing your luck. I was very lucky the host got me a spot at the bar and made sure I was looked after, I think she took pity on me as I was travelling alone, I ordered the burger which was incredible and a few cocktails, very reasonably priced too! I will definitely visit again when I return to New York.

When I first moved to Fishtown I frequented Lloyd a lot and took my friends who visited me there for their mac and cheese. I went this weekend and the mac and cheese was STONE COLD. Until this time Lloyd had been a 5 star establishment in my book. But this visit I found the deviled eggs very dry and the mac and cheese even after it was warmed up overwhelmingly salty. The visit was really a 1 star rating but given my other positive experiences there I bumped it up to 3 stars. The reason I felt I should leave a review is because I now seriously question whether they just microwave their food. I only ordered two side dishes and the bill came to $16. That would be fine with me if I didn't leave feeling like I was given a microwave ready meal.

So happy that this restaurant has reopened.  It is perfect for a celebration for dinner with my son attending Penn nearby.  Great casual atmosphere and beautiful row house.  The dinner was  creative and far more refined than my last visit about a year ago.  We were served 14 courses.  All were imaginative and intensely flavored. Favorites for our group were french onion soup in a spoon, foie gras, eggs Benedict with dippin dots, duck negamaki, squab,  I didn't love the tofu but others at the table did.  The rice pudding was truly awesome,  I can't wait to come back and try new things.  One problem that kept me from giving 5 stars was the pacing missed. Dinner took 3.5'hours and the lulls between courses were occasional annoying. Go and try the place.  Given the fact that we were there on the third night since the reopening I imagine things will get a bit sharper.

Wonderful, cozy restaurant with great food.  The service was ok, a bit slow at times, but our appetizers and dinners more than made up for it.  The fries are great and they have vegetarian options and will even omit the fish sauce.  The owner and chef was on iron chef!  Try her cooking classes if you have the chance.

I love me some Terry's. I work nearby, so I come here every week. My fave items are their breakfast, sandwiches, and burgers. Food is good and reasonably priced. Great local spot in the neighborhood. Many regulars there, which is a good sign. Staff is always friendly. I definitely recommend them!
I came to Mundo for my friend's rehearsal dinner. The interior was spacious, the food was great and the sound (both live and DJ) turned out great. Would definitely recommend the space for an event.
Sat at counter. Guys behind it were great. Know how to make a cocktail. Food awesome. Get corn on stick.

I'm an Australian visiting NYC, and naturally Australians have high expectations of coffee. I came in here and was pleasantly surprised. The staff were super friendly, the breakfast I had was fast and fresh, and the coffee was extremely good. If I was in NYC longer this would of become my local.

Thanks to a neighbor who recommended it, I've been there three times in 2 weeks. What a wonderfully authentic restaurant. Beautiful decor, great friendly service and food that's marvelous. Am a fan of their shrimp dishes which are cooked to perfection. The best guacamole I've tasted in a long time. The portions are huge, with enough to take home for another meal...or two! They don't rush you through your meal, even if the restaurant is full. I appreciate that. Staff members helpful with food choices and explanations. Even if you're not a fan of Colombian food, they open @ 7 a.m. Stop by there for coffee and a treat. Takeout and delivery available. It's my new fave place in town, just a short walk from home. Best of luck to them, and I hope they stay open for many years.

I just don't get it.  I know tons of people who love the square slices here.  I finally tried it and it's pretty terrible imho...  a piece of bread with a little bland tomato sauce.. bleh. I'll take DiFara or any good thin crust any day..

I have now been here 3 times, and it is consistent, so we can start there. The pizza is good, and worth a trek. The crowd is family oriented, plenty of kids around. You want to go with a group and order whole deep-dish pies. These are brooklyn style old-school sicilian style pizzas and they really hit the spot. Even when the line is long, it won't take long for you to get your food. The spumoni and ices are also incredibly good. BUT there is one major issue here. The LOUDSPEAKER SYSTEM. They just scream into it all day. Its unnecessarily loud. I would easily say they deserve 4 stars otherwise, but it is so distracting, and in some cases, if you sit too close to a speaker, painful to endure, that it ruins everything else this place has going for it. The last thing my group wanted to hear was more of that loud, pushy, nasty-toned voice screaming about tables or orders being ready. Time to upgrade AND turn the volume down. There are better ways to do this.

This is my first time leaving a negative review anywhere, as I'm usually very forgiving of mix ups, especially in the food industry. But our experience was so ridiculous that I have to post it. We placed our order at 5:30 and were told it would be 45 minutes. We were starving, so waited by the phone and window for the delivery guy. At almost 7, I called and was told the driver was out for delivery. After another 20 minutes or so, I got a call from the restaurant saying the driver had returned because he waited at our apartment for 30 minutes and called us several times, but we didn't answer. This was untrue as we were checking the window repeatedly and had the phone by me the whole time. The man I spoke with was rude and angry as soon as I answered the phone. He finally said the guy would try to deliver again, but it would be another 45 minutes. After 55 minutes, we called again and they said the delivery guy was heading out soon. Finally, the food arrived and the delivery guy confessed that he has called the wrong number and the person he spoke to said they did not order food, so he left and went back to the restaurant. Then today, my husband's credit card was charged with $360, instead of $36. Probably an accident, but just adding insult to injury. Jewel of India is now listed in my phone as "NEVER ORDER AGAIN." For the record, the food was ok. But they should have AT LEAST given us a discount, if not given us the order for free.

Love this place. Ordered chicken pakora, salmon bhuna, lamb vindaloo. Yes it's in a weird place and a little hard to spot from the street, but look in the parking lot on the right hand side of the street and there it is. You can't miss the banner. Great service, reasonable prices.
Falafel is very avg, whats good is the hot sauce. Omg i love the hot sauce, so i just buy it from them but the falafels are very average.

I love this place.  I go here often for the Sushi and Pad  Thai.   The staff is always friendly and fast. All items are priced well and fresh! I love the variety of items they have that you cannot get anywhere else in the Temple area! This is my go to spot for any item (forget about the 7-11), I hope in the future they will stay open later and possibly deliver.

I went here with a couple of friends for a girls night out and we had an awesome dinner.  The staff were very welcoming and we were seated promptly.  We had the octupus (well cooked and yummy sauce) and deviled eggs (my fav) for appetizers.  For the main course, we had the Pig out for Two (crunchy and delicious pork with two hefty servings of noodles) and with sides of corn, sticky rice and brussel sprouts (I usually hate brussel sprouts but that dish made me change my mind!) Everything was really delicious and I plan on taking my husband back here for date night!

We ordered the Falafel Sandwich and the Chicken Schwarma, both were really disappointing. The Falafel was made out of bread crumbs and contained no chickpeas at all, unsalted and had no taste. It looked and tasted like a deep fried motza ball. The pita itself was a mess, fell apart and soggy from the hummus oozing out. The Chicken Schwarma was not chicken schwarma, this was the boiled down chicken chunks. Probably what was left after they made the motza ball chicken stock. To call this place "authentic mediterranian" is a disgrace.

Had a great experience coming to this restaurant! Drove from Long Island, to check it out and was impressed. Elizabeth was very nice and helpful, made it a 5 star experience. The food and drinks were good, definitely will recommend to all my friends.

Came to Blend on a Saturday night for a little get together for my best friends B-day Dinner. Had a reservation for eight and lost the table since we arrived a couple of minutes late, so I do assume responsibility for that. We then had to wait quite a while for a table so we got a little impatient, but it was  understandable since Blend is very popular, therefor a very busy restaurant. Carlos, However, one of the restaurant managers (or assistant Manager not very sure) turned our night around. No one went up to him to complain, he simply was very observant and noticed that we looked a little uncomfortable. He greeted us kindly and joked with us a bit, he even got us all light vodka shots while he expedited our wait for the table. After we had our dinner, he came to our table with a big bowl of Sangria and a birthday card for the birthday girl..:D..made her night..Must say Carlos the reason why I give Blend a 5 Star rate because at the end of the day Customer Service & Satisfaction is what's most important and he really outdid himself, both in service and personality. Food: Food was simply amazing, hats off to the kitchen staff and chef. We had the Guacamole, Crispy Arepas (  Must Try), and the Tostones Nachos for appetizers. All very delicious. I had the Pollo a La Plancha as my entre, sounds simple right? It was incredible, perfectly cooked, settles very light on your stomach, and the marinade with the lemon butter sauce gave that melting in your mouth effect. aaannnndddd, the food came to us very fast. Drinks: The shot, the classic mojito, the coconut mojito and the Piña Colada were all very good, yes I tried them all ;} I'm looking forward to visiting Blend again, next time on  a regular night when is not as busy. Till then, I will envision that perfect pollo melting in my mouth. Thank You Carlos!!!

Came here for a dinner with family and ordered the all you can eat special. Seemed like a deal until the rolls came out and the food was sumo sized. They charge $1 per piece left over so they make the rolls and portions so big, you can't finish and end up paying double of the advertised price. If you order a la carte the portion size is noticeably smaller. I'm never coming back here nor recommend even if you have an appetite.  They are schemers.

If you enjoy hanging out with a family of large roaches while enjoying a beer, check out the outside benches! One might even crawl up on to your neck if you're lucky like me. Luckily the windows around the establishment were all open, so if the roaches felt cold they could just hang out inside, right near the open food bar. The beer selection is great here, although their disenchanted and uninterested bartenders would probably rather not tell you about them.

After reading the reviews for this restaurant we decided to try out the food and see just how true the service is.  The reviews are right on. The food is amazing and prices make it even more appealing.  The service is exactly as it was reviewed.  We had a server who abruptly snatched our menus from us just to hand them to the diners in the booth besides us.  We all got a good laugh about that and were expecting something like this from what we read.  Overall, I enjoyed the time spent there, ate well and am looking forward to our next visit.

I stumbled upon this place when I was home visiting my family this summer. I came here almost everyday for a soy cappuccino and it was magical everytime. The staff was always friendly and I wish I got a chance to taste their food, the menu looked awesome. I hope more cafes like this pop up around this area! I am a huge fan!

Arrived 3:30pm and the front door was locked.  Eventually a woman came to the door with a huge dog, to let me in and check me in. One of the reasons I chose this place was for their in house Russian restaurant which sounded perfect...unfortunately they are closed except Friday and Saturday nights. The room was OK...needed some updating and repairs.  The mattress was strange, and the pillows were horrible...did not get much sleep. Came down for breakfast at 8am, and guess what???...nobody was around, no smell of coffee...nobody to even get a receipt from... Will never stay here again, and I suggest that you all do the same.

Straight up, best BBQ I've ever had in NYC. Worth the wait, and that wait can be LONG. Come during off hours or hit up the west side otherwise. It's all good, but hope for pork cheek special or try the dinosaur rib. Epic.
Great food

DONT GO THERE! Horrible service, rude, just take a minute to read.I went to Pio Pio on Amsterdam Ave last Sunday afternoon. It was about 4:00pm First the girl at the front looked bored and not inviting. My friend and I had done quite a bit of shopping and were carrying 4 shopping bags. We were seated right next to another guest although the place was relatively empty. Our packages were pretty close to the next table. When the front door girl (Can't call her a hostess) decides to seat the next two people at the table to my right which was where the packages were. The gentleman asked why do we have to sit so close? Why cant we sit over there? With that the girl rolled her eyes a seated them. They didn't stay! (they were smarter than we were) We ordered our meals and appetizers. after 10 minutes I asked a bus boy if he could bring me water. My waiter MIA. Orders were coming out of the kitchen but ours were not after another ten minutes I asked if they could bring the appetizers. Oh yes they will be right out..... Wait Finally get the appetizers. WAIT......... My friends order comes out. Mine is missing. WHen I asked they said it would be right out.......wait........ My friend was halfway through her meal when my dinner arrived.  Sea Bass... Not cooked! No sides. Get the waiters attention explain, he takes fish back... Still no sides and now my friend is about finished with her meal. I called the waiter over (by now other guests have been served, they've eaten and are paying. Im still waiting. . I tell the waiter to Cancel the meal. 2 minutes later out he comes with the sea bass and sides, I told him I didn't want it he seemed surprised.  REALLY? Ive eaten at the Pio Pio on 10th Ave with a very different Vibe. Friendly,  professional, excellent food.. AMSTERDAM AVE PIO PIO STAY AWAY FROM....

was here for dinner...one of the reviewers hit the nail on the head...great atmosphere, but food is mediocre at best. Our server was a bit cracked out as well. On at least 4 separate trips to our table, we were asked if anyone had allergies. we were also asked if we wanted bread, which never arrived and drinks took forever to arrive. Escargot tasted like a shoe sole and the chicken was way too salty. On a positive note, the space is great.

the delivery has taken 90 minutes still not here-owner could care less I asked her to contact driver she said he was not answering-she was indifferent terrible attitude she lost our family as a customer mitch

Haven't been here in years & won't return in this lifetime. Stale smokey retread from years ago with the worst Lipton onion soup muscles I ever tasted. Served with grocery store bread. A beet salad served with watermelon cubes & bad bottled tarragon dressing. The beer was good & the grilled calamari surprisingly good. How this came to $85/2 people with one beer a piece I'll never know.

What can I say?  If you love great fresh pizza . . . this is THE place to get it.   Small in size.  Big on quality.  Best pizza in New York, according to reviewers who have a more discerning palate than mine.  (I refer to NY Magazine, for one).   Go . . .  buy a pie . . . enjoy.
Worth the 2 hour wait...broth was so tasty and the egg was poached perfectly. Best Ramen in NYC!
This restaurant is so amazing =) I really love the food, the quality  ingredients and the service and atmosphere!
good place for drinks

With so many great reviews, there was no doubt in my mind that this was the place would be a hit.  It was my first visit here and unfortunately my last.  Walking in the receptionist wss very nice and sat us right away.   Unfortunately the table was so small it left me wondering how we would fit any of our plates on it.  The devote was nice and had a rustic feel.  I ordered the fish tacos with a side of rice & beans. My s/o ordered the steak or perhaps the beef tacos ( I cant remember the name). The food presentation was very nice but there was very little food which would have been ok it it was offset by big flavor.   However, the food was bland and needed salt among other spices.  I grew up near the Mexican border and know my Mexican food.  If your looking for an authentic spot or at least food with flavor... this is not it
Didn't expect much from this place...but the food we had was delicious, the wine excellent (a recommendation from an excellent server). Dinner was low-key, scrumptious, with familial, helpful staff.
best dumplings ive ever had!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! the pork dumpings are cooked to perfection!!!!!!

We've been waiting to hop over to Campagnia since it opened. Its great looking from the outside, and nicely re-done inside. The place was hopping when we got there, and we were actually seated quicker than we thought we would be. Service was pleasant and non obtrusive. We ordered what sounded like an interesting -"split"-  salad composed of apples, romaine, bluecheese and walnuts. It came out on one plate-not split- and was something any 10 year old could have made....seemed more like iceberg to us.....it was bland and uninteresting. We tried a Coal oven and Brick oven pizza. The sausage on the brick oven pizza was ruined with too much  salty and garlicky spinach to the point where we couldn't taste anything else. If you closed your eyes, there'd be no way to know if it was a white or red pizza, there was barely a trace of sauce. I removed the meat from it and put it on our tiny 12" coal oven margherita which at least had some minor flavor- compared to next to none from our other pizza. Turned out the sausage also had next to no flavor. And interestingly, the mozzarella was totally different tasting on the seperate pizza choices The crust was okay, but ultimately not all that. I kept waiting for magic.....I'm still waiting. To spend 28 plus dollars for 2 pizzas to get about what a large pizza at any decent pizzeria offers is only ok IF you don't care about -1. what you're eating...and 2. money. To be fair, all we had was salad, pizza, and wine in  water glass- not a wine glass, so maybe there's actually good choices....but when you bill yourself as a specialized pizzeria, and serve mediocre pizza at premium prices, it should be much much better. Bay Ridge , and the surrounding area has amazing pizza, Campagnia sadly doesn't. Go here to blow money and have a good time doing it...its a fun, lively place for that.

Friend and I were there yesterday at 5:15 for dinner before a play.  Beautiful walled garden setting but.....right off the go, there was a list of food items not available.  Ok, go with plan B.  We both had mac and cheese entrees, were told by the server that they were large enough alone, no side needed.  Well, they really weren't, but by the time they arrived we were trying to get out in time for the play.  And the mac, when they arrived, looked nothing like the picture above, no garnish, no parsley, just plopped in the dish.  And it really wasn't "mac", it was large orrchietto noodles. So when done, we ordered the ONLY dessert offered, ice cream truffles.  Well, seems they were suddenly out of them too! And there was no one in the place at that time of day except one other person!  Really, if you cannot provide a full menu on a Sunday, then do not open on Sunday!  And the wines by glass....ONLY generic red and generic pinot grigio...really, a bar that cannot open a bottle of something else?  And not even a decent pour when the wine did arrive.  Sorry, this place might be good for people who don't know better quality or more attentive service, like the Gen Xers living in that 'hood, but those of us with money to spend, won't be doing it there again!

My new favorite Chinatown restaurant!!  Cheap and Delicious!! This place is pretty good compared to the usually shanghai spots that I've been to in city. Very clean, friendly service, feels like a new establishment, takes credit cards, picture menu helps too. The wait here is never long, the Soup Dumplings are juicy, and the Mock Duck, delicious. Overall, a nice restaurant with good food (both their soup dumplings and their dishes) plus service. If you're into Shanghai food you should try it.

Linda's sells chewing tobacco to underage high school students. Ask any Pequannock high school student.  I have.  It's a dangerous and disgusting habit.  My child's friends have told me they go there and purchase with no ID required.

very tasty Japanese ramen noodle soup. Very classic preparation. Personally, I don't believe it's worth the wait since there's nothing particularly over-the-top about the product, plus, it's technically a chain restaurant that just so happened to gain large popularity and following at this very crowded and cramped East-side spot off the Bowery. Go early or don't go.
Really wonderful! Good prices, lots of amazing choices. A bit cramped if you're dining in, but get over it! Staff friendly and welcoming.

Brought my friend in yesterday for brunch. We are brunch-loving divas. A good décor/atmosphere, delish cocktails and food, and anything above mediocre service is what we're looking for. First, this place has outdoor seating and nice big windows that they'll open, weather permitting, so we chose this spot because the weather was really nice. Since there weren't any seats available outside, we opted for a table inside near the windows which was perfect. Service: ehhhh. It was very mediocre. Every time we asked for something we felt like we were annoying our server. My friend and I have both worked in restaurants so we're pretty good about how to behave as patrons but any time we asked him something it made me cringe a little. That was whatever, but what bothered me more was our food took FOREVER. In real life, it was more like a 45 minute wait. For eggs. And the place was hopping but not overwhelmingly packed so something was off in the kitchen. Maybe not enough staff? Anyway, our server did occasionally check on us and kept our drinks coming (even though his attitude was blasé). So all in all: mediocre. The food was okay too; nothing glamorous. I had a personalized veggie omelet, my friend had the eggs benedict. The portions were nice but I just think that after that long wait, our expectations were inflated. Like, if it takes 45 minutes for our food then I hope you're giving it some serious TLC. On the other hand, I LOVED the mimosas. I don't like dinky little mimosas that are served in champagne glasses (aka the traditional way) but these were deliciously served in nice big wine glasses. THANK YOU, Barrel House :) Overall, its a nice option if you're in the neighborhood and the weather is great and you have a good chunk of time to spare. Prices are very reasonable too. But otherwise, if you're looking for show-stopping service and impressive food, there are better options nearby.

My girlfriend and I came here with a few of my family members for a Saturday night dinner.  My brother and his girlfriend (who were also in attendance) recommended the place since they had dined here before.  The restaurant was very nice but after waiting a few minutes to be seated, they place us in the way back of the restaurant, in what seemed to be an unfinished area of the restaurant.  At that point, I was a little skeptical but we ordered a few drinks and decided to make the most of it. We started with some apps, including the spicy calamari and the cheesey garlic bread, which were both abolutely delicious.  Our meals which included a chicken parm dish, tortellini dish and a couple of steak dishes were also extremely tasty and we all very much enjoyed our meals.  Not only was the food good, but the experience was excellent as well. To top it off, the Owner (from what I could gather) was super friendly and checked up on us a couple times to see how we were enjoying our meals.  As we left, he thanked us and we walked to the parking garage to get our car.  Side note, they validate parking in the parking garage right next to the restaurant.  So we grab our car and we're pulling out of the garage when we see the Owner sprinting out of the restaurant towards our car.  My first thought was that we left something behind, but that wasn't the case.  The Owner had run out to meet us and send us home with 2 loaves of pre-made cheesy garlic bread, which we all later enjoyed the next day.  Talk about excellent customer service.  I've never experienced an Owner so friendly and willing to go out of his way like that.  Next time I'm in the hartord area, I will DEFINITELY BE BACK for another awesome experience.
Guacamole was out of this world. Everything about this place was fabulous. Food service drinks. I will be back again

The entire experience was delightful. We arrived a tad early and enjoyed relaxing in comfy chairs on the front porch, sipping our drinks until our table was ready. The yellowtail appetizer was delicious, the salmon was absolute perfection, and the cheeseboard... well it was the ideal way to end the meal. Everything was timed perfectly. And our server (Manny), made the evening that much more entertaining. Looking forward to our next trip to Princeton.

this place is phenomenal! great atmosphere, nice vibes & good music! i love their happy hour specials! their outside scene is fantastic! nicely set up! oh....good music too! great place for sport fanatics!!

I was disappointed that I was told this place would be open, I go the next day and it is closed! I had family visiting and there aren't that many halal options around the area. The management could have been better at this.

Thinking about this place the first thing that comes to our minds and to our mouth is the amazing taste of the burgers as well as the onion rings and the lemonade! The friendly environment only helped to make of our experience a 5* one. We all came from Portugal and to Portugal we will spread the name of this place!
Good BBQ!!! Staff is okay.

Great seafood and extremely well priced!  I love seafood and eat it everywhere I get a chance.  I was passing thru newark for work recently and was very suprise and satisfied w my meal.  Since then, I make it a point to get lunch here,  both locations.  Highly recommended and great place overall!

Avoid the eggs. We stopped in this past beautiful Sunday and I ordered from their Sunday brunch menu - the Classic Breakfast - eggs over easy, bacon, potatoes. Pretty simple right? especially when you offer a specific Sunday brunch menu? Honestly did not even know eggs could go this wrong. Cold, rubbery and just sad. The entire plate was cold. The amount of food sparse. Have never returned a meal in my life, but I did this time. To their credit they offered to re-make it and when I said no, they didn't charge for the meal. Wouldn't go back unless I was already full and just wanted a good Bloody Mary.
Love this place. We always go!!! Small, you can talk and the food is perfect
Delicious!  We had gone to other cheesesteak places, but this one tops them.  :-)

Came here Saturday evening with a few of my friends must say food was not bad however service was terrible we are being rushed from the moment we came in they were due to close at 12 we got there around 10PM we where told that we had to order dessert the second we got there with our food they kept rushing us we did not enjoy our food at all.

They claim to all be the same, but that's not entirely true--at least not the one stationed at 53rd and 6th avenue in Manhattan. This food was so good, we've affectionately nicknamed it "Crack Cart" --  Only drawback to this is that lines are typically half-way down the block, but it's well worth the wait, I assure you. And they often bring you free, sample falafels if you've been waiting for too long. Not bad at all. Once you order, your food is in your hand within seconds, so 30 minutes (on average) isn't that long to wait for a $6- piece of heaven (or wherever your religion goes after death). The food was well spiced, hot, tasty, juicy. Their popularity is well deserved. They should franchise.

Food definitely not worth the wait... My mother, sister and I were excited to try Penelope.  The line outside was promising and we could handle the wait on a Sunday afternoon.  After waiting nearly 2 hours, the host gave away our table.  He did get us in next, but that started off the experience on the wrong foot.  My mother and sister ordered omelettes and I ordered the BBLT.  We also ordered cocktails and the Bloody Mary was great.  My mother was given the wrong dish and asked to take the dish that the other person ordered.  My mother graciously accepted the dish she did not order. My sister very much enjoyed her omelette and potatoes.  I was completely underwhelmed by my meal.  My BBLT showed up with white tomatoes...in Sept nonetheless...my fries were warm and soggy and the bacon was undercooked and flabby...gross!  The server was kind to try to accommodate, but it was hopeless.   Pass up Penelope next time you are looking to have a delicious brunch - try Paradou instead!
I gave Maple Giant grinder  a second chance .

Order was wrong, asked for extra hot sauce and soy sauce, all I got was duck sauce!  Top this - one of the fortune cookies, was pre- ate before it arrived. The taste gets it two stars that's it! Won't be ordering from here again.

The place is really small but they are very accommodating. I came with my family and friends we had a great time till we got attitude from the waiter and waitress. Two people with very bad attitude and BAD CUSTOMER SERVICE. I mean the waiter got smart with my sister, eavesdrop in our conversation and even interject. Dealing with other follow Haitians you think they would be more courteous then that. When we told him we would give him a bad review he countine to go back and forth. I really hope they do better. I would have love to have met the chef and the real manager for the night. Also when in larger group be careful of the bill they over charge you and add extra. If I have a 5 course meal for $32 why did I end up paying almost $50 for the night.....smh NEVER AGAIN

The food is absolutely amazing. Fresh, well-seasoned and simple. I stared with a simple salad, which contained incredibly fresh tomatoes. For entree, I had to try the cioppino with the best parts of a well-cooked lobster. We also had soft shell crabs, very yummy! Dessert was also a little mixed.  Both fruit tarts, a cherry and a mixed fruit, were pretty mediocre. The setting in a cozy converted flower shop, the BYOB policy, the warm and charming service, are what render it so completely memorable. I am looking forward to a return visit because I want to try everything on the menu.

My overall experience was terrible. Not only did the waiter give me the wrong fries, the ketchup bottle was disgustingly dripping in ketchup with a weak pouring spout that fell off and spilled all over my food. Not to mention there was a fly in my water. Disappointed but I guess everyone else has different experiences.
Very good burger (both the Original and the Manly Burger), truffle fries were good but not great.
I am not here to argue with anyone. You are all entitled to your own "opinions". I love Café V and will continue to go there when I can. And to the side commenters: I do not work there, thanks!

We were in the city the day before a race in the Hamptons and were looking for a good gluten-free spot to carb load as my friend is Celiac. We found this spot and couldn't have been happier! It had a lovely little patio, and the gluten free bread, hummus and olive oil were so yummy. We both got flatbreads which were so delicious, you'd never know they were gluten-free. Our server was pleasant and so helpful. I'll definitely go back!
Nice spot for a drink, but very disappointing kitchen. The strip steak, mussels, Caesar salad, and flat bread were all disappointing.

The wait staff was nice but the food was quite bad. It was completely tasteless,  the tomato sauce  tasted like it was out of a can. Seafood was very blend and lacked any seasoning. We had ginger calamari as an appetizer and the calamari was very chewy and the ginger sauce tasted blah... I ordered the risotto with shrimp and scallops, the risotto was ok but the seafood wasn't tasty at all. My husband had the red snapper dish with calamari, shrimp and scallops. It was all covered in tasteless tomato sauce and the seafood was overcooked. Overall a pretty bad experience.

This nicely attired place offers a fairly priced selection of food and drink. The choice between draft and bottled beer is extensive enough to satisfy most beer lovers. The various plates, while being attractively named, were somewhat flat in presentation and taste. Service was somewhat lacking when It came to refilling water glasses and following up on drinking and menu selections.
the oxtail dish is delicious!!
Ordered the #1 omelet with goat cheese and turkey bacon.  Very,  very good.
One of the best brunches in manhattan!!! Order anything! great Service!

Stopped in to have a margarita and a BIG JIM pepper after work! Was really impressed - the pepper was lightly battered in a delicious blend of spices that didn't detract from the actual flavor of the pepper which stands on it's own for hear and taste. Had a margarita of the month which was $7.00 and finished up my meal with an ice cold Tecate. Vinny the bartender was great and personable and the servers were smiling the entire time I was there. I love this place, will return for date night in a few!

Sadly I came back on a Tuesday for their happy hour. Although the food was good, the service was awful. They wouldn't accommodate a large party and the hostess was rude. With so many places and choices in New York City they did very little to help out. Hence we went across the street where they were more than happy to accommodate. Will never come back back here for their happy hour.
Steak and cheese is incredible

You can't ever have a bad meal in here. Always fresh and delicious. I frequently go here with family and friends and we all agree that their meals are top quality. Try their crepes and coffees which are my favorite.
One of my favorites from a little kid to now.  And if you are up all night having fun and you get hungry they are open 24 7. So stop in and get some grub

Hostesses too busy eating steak off of their friends' plates at table next to us to send a waitress over, then when asked to, it's clear they've been drinking the past hour of their shift.  Disgraceful behavior.  As we get up to leave we hear "oh they wasn't feeling us?" - try Morandi, Bluestone Lane, Yerba Buena, Oaxaca, Tartine, Diablo Royale, Empellon, Bar Sardine....anywhere but Extra Virgin.

Neat decor, Nice layout. Taco Tuesday was cool but they shouldn't have only one server on. Took to long for her to come back and when we tried getting her, it felt we were bothering her. One of our tacos was not cooked (the meat was red and cold) and a can beer tasted weird..when telling the waitress that, we got comment that was not necessary from her. Beer is a little overpriced and so is the food for what it is. I would only go if there is a special or happy hour there, but My opinion is there are better places in the city.

I am in the area for one night for work and decided to give this place a try based on the reviews.  Today was 5 for 5 tuesday, 5 tacos for $5!  Pretty good deal for $5.  The tacos had plenty of meat and the other ingredients also looked and tasted fresh.  The hot salsa is HOT!  Exercise caution with this salsa.  I am pretty good with hot stuff, but this salsa is tongue burning hot!  It does taste very good on the tacos, but it is pretty damn HOT!  Overall very good experience at a very reasonable price!

On NFL Sundays this place is as close as it gets to being at the game. Food, drinks, and atmosphere are all great. TVs are everywhere so you can keep an eye on every game going on. If you go on Sunday though for the NFL games get there early because it gets packed!

This is a special place where you can get old school, thin crust bar pies. They are so delicious! The atmosphere and food are great. Try the sausage pizza. Make sure to get a pitcher of beer and sample the garlic pie.
Very good. Reminds me of cocos in Japan and is as close to it as you can get. Great food!
Cassava cake and coffee are fabulous!

This has to be one of the best places to get a great breakfast! The first thing you notice is that it is very, very clean. It makes you feel comfortable when you sit down to eat. Also, you can see the staff preparing the food which is a huge plus in my book. Their menu isn't insanely huge or confusing. It's straight up breakfast with a few kicks and quirks and that's it. Whatever you get, add the Turkish sausage. I saw it mentioned here on a few reviews and for good reason! It's THE thing to try if you're here for the first time.

I am 100% Colombian... Born in a small city where arepas are part of every meal... Im  serious!  All I can say is that these arepas take me BACK in time. My words do no justice but its the best I could do... you have to try for yourself. Simply the best arepas in New York!!!

Came here on a Sunday for the traditional Ichiju Sansai set meal breakfast.  We arrived around 10:30am and there was no wait at all.     We totally enjoyed the heartwarming meals prepared by the passionate cooking team.  They patiently explained their menu of the day, where the seafood were sourced, how the fish will be prepared, and all the hardly resistible add-on options.   We ended up getting black snapper and bluefin collar with the sashimi appetizer and Onsen eggs topped with uni.  The black snapper was light and delectable while the bluefin collar was rich and luscious.  Nothing can beat genuinely prepared food served by passionate good folks.   Would love to come back here again for ramen on a weekday when I am back to NY again. Note:  The storefront sign is "fish" in kanji in a bowl.

For me, a good, gourmet pizza can be so easily messed up with pretension or laziness.  10Devoe does it right, with fresh, creative ingredients like huitlacoche or burratta.  The place itself is both intimate and rustic, and the staff is adorable and awesome.  The pizza is a must, but expect more, I suggest at least starting with the pickles and ending with a banana split!

EXTREMELY OVERPRICED FOR A MEDIOCRE MEAL! I went there for lunch and paid over $20.00 for a tiny dish of pasta with chicken and a small order of fries. Will never return. My recommendation to the restaurant: If you plan on having a lunch menu, make sure the prices are fair and the food is top notch. Especially if you want to retain your customers.

This is a place my friends and I  always come back to. Food was great, as well as the service. Staff is very friendly. My favorite meal is definitely the burger with fries and for dessert, the creme Brule is the best.

I've been to Cafeteria many times before and had nothing but exceptionally tasty food, and dinner last night was no different. If you like full-flavored comfort food, this place is your best friend. My consistent favorites: Smoked Gouda & Bacon Mac n Cheese--rich and creamy and decadent every time Short Rib Tacos--a huge portion and wonderful to the last bite with rich, tender short rib mixed with smooth sweet potato puree and crunchy apple slaw Tomato Basil Soup--I don't know what they're doing there to make tomato soup so amazing, but it's maybe the best I've ever had with its creamy texture, rich flavors, and cute + delicious mini grilled cheese accompaniments I've also tried daily specials from time to time to mix it up a bit beyond my go-to orders, and they never disappoint, either. The other day for lunch, there was an amazing shaved roasted brussel sprouts salad that I added grilled hangar steak to and I hope they offer it again soon. When in Chelsea this is a must try!
Fun and artsy vibe, great food and specialty drinks. My only note would be that its a little over-priced on the drink menu, but still worth going.

I don't usually write reviews, but I honestly hope this place is investigated and shut down. My dad and I went here for dinner recently. A few hours after dinner, my dad started violently throwing up. I'm a reasonable person, and food poisoning can happen anywhere, even if the kitchen is impeccably well-kept. What caused me to write this review is the manager's reaction. I called up the restaurant to politely inform them that one of their dishes may be tainted. I believed it was the pork dish that my dad ate, since we shared all our dishes except that one (I don't eat pork). At this point, the manager inexplicably began yelling at me. First, he said that "PEOPLE THAT OLD JUST GET SICK SOMETIMES". My father is 55, so he's not "that old". Also, he usually has a stomach of steel - this is literally the only time I've seen him get food poisoning (and he was really scarily sick - I almost had to take him to the ER). Next, the manager said "YOU DON'T KNOW IT WAS OUR FOOD THAT CAUSED IT". Well, sure, but I have reason to believe it was - the only other food my dad had eaten that day was his regular breakfast cereal (which he ate again 2 days later and was perfectly fine). And as I said, we shared all dishes except the pork one that night, so I think we'd pinpointed the cause. Finally, he said, "SINCE YOU CAN'T PROVE ANYTHING, WE'RE GOING TO KEEP SERVING IT". I was particularly shocked about this. Who knows how many other people he knowingly sickened that night? I wish I had recorded the conversation, because I was honestly trying to be polite, and yet he was literally screaming at me for the sickness that he had caused. I've warned everyone I know in the Princeton area to stay away from this place. I used to be a regular customer, but never again - what a horrific experience.
Sashimi not particularly fresh or good.  Don't order the cold "soba" - it's actually cold ramen.  House saki was good value for money.  Not impressed.  Won't return.
Food was good.....service was horrible and will not be back anytime soon, as we were majorly dissapointed.

An amazing meal.  Flavors and textures I have never experienced before.  I would go back the next time I am in the area and recommend anyone visiting not miss the opportunity.   I enjoyed the lamb (signature dish), amazing cheeses and special coconut cake which is only offered on special occasions.   Also, they offer a top notch list of foreign beers from Europe that can keep you entertained for a while.
Delicious. We had the eight course dinner menu and really enjoyed the variety of dishes--they kept coming. Good cocktails, good wine. We'll be back for brunch.
I think this is the best Thai food! Everything is wonderful!
This is a nice bar great place to come with friends. I love how the exposed brick gave it an old fashion look. The drinks were good and I enjoyed the pizza.
If you want great cajun food, go back to New Orleans. If you just need a jambalya fix, this place will get you by for a little while. The service was excellent.

Positively delighted with this addition to the LIC dining scene. I've eaten here twice and this place is definitely the most interesting menu in the neighborhood. Food is outstanding and the cocktails are well thought out and consistently prepared. Love the vibe - very chic but casual - and the service is great! Looking forward to trying the entire menu!! Great job Jora!

Reading Terminal has locally grown Veggies at a fraction of the price of wholefoods and other local groceries.  The peppers i get from there are fresh and delicious.  I love the variety of fresh foods from fish to pig.  The hardest part is deciding what you want to eat while you are there!

I have been here a few times and have always loved it. I have tried burgers, salad with burger toppings :), panini and sweet potato fries... the food is legit and worth the wait. Haven't tried the milk shakes but everyone seems to love them

Where do I even begin?!? Our rude and degrading waitress, the $18 dollar bowl of plain pasta, the fact that you will be sitting basically on top of the table behind or next to you, or the lack of effort on management's behalf to ensure that we visit their restaurant again. Let me start off by saying I appreciate great service and good quality food and am willing to pay the price for these things. There are a lot of places in New York City where I have and will pay a pretty penny for a good meal and great service - I experienced nothing here that here would make me go back or recommend this place to others. Search elsewhere - there is much better in New York City. I will start with our waitress. Just plain rude. From when we sat down and throughout our entire meal she had an attitude that was unwarranted. We were an easy table and did not ask for much. I had a feeling it was because we were a table of young 30 somethings and she made assumptions about us before she even came over. Well it turns out my assumptions were validated when she provided us with the check and made sure to point out and circle the recommended tip based on the amount of our bill. IS SHE KIDDING?! First of all I always tip and I tip well for good service. A tip is something that should be earned not expected. Our table could not believe she would do something like this. I have never in my life had a server do this to me. We paid the bill and when she returned with our change and cards she again RE-CIRCLED - yes she did it AGAIN - the recommended tips and made a comment about giving what is recommended. The audacity to assume a. we were not going to give an appropriate tip and b. that you deserve a tip at all is in my opinion inappropriate and disrespectful to customers. Next up I want to talk about the food. I have a dairy allergy along with a bunch of other foods I can not tolerate. While Italian might not be the best place to dine - I have always been accommodated very well at other restaurants in New York City given the level of awareness and precaution that is used in most kitchens today. This is not that restaurant as the waitress did not help me create something I could eat or offer suggestions. In other restaurants a manager is called over to discuss options and sometimes even the chef. Their lack of attention just turned me off and worried me a great deal. So I went ahead and ordered really safe with a plain (nothing on it at all) bowl of pasta. I received maybe a cup of pasta that was a weird consistency and definitely not the best home made pasta I have ever had. And the kicker - they charged me $18 for it. When we brought the $18 bowl of pasta to the attention of the manager he said there was nothing he could do about it. He also was basically unresponsive to our telling him how we were treated throughout the evening. Nice job making sure we never return to your restaurant or recommend it to anyone. In addition to the above be prepared to sit with people dining at neighboring tables because you will be sitting right on top of them. Bottom line - there are much better places to get a great meal with outstanding service in New York City. Look elsewhere - you will be happy you did.

I like this place for certain things, such as their oysters and clams, and their whole fish.  Also their fried oysters are excellent.  Rest on the menu are hit or miss.  Lobster roll is pretty decent but pricey.  Linguine with clams was way too salty the one time I ordered it.  I recommend whole fish grilled and fried oysters.  Can't go wrong with that. Place is tiny and from time to time you are bumping into other people's elbows.  But servers are friendly and accommodating as much as they can be given the tight space they have.
Food is good, restaurant looks pretty busy, server explain u everything , must try occasionally because little expensive ..

I went for my birthday last week and the food was really good. The staff is friendly and the server was attentive and nice. I ordered there filet mignon medium per the servers request and it was absolutely delicious!
I work in the area  for that last 9 years. Their sesame pancakes are the best!!!!!! .... THE SERVICES HERE SUCK THEY ARE VERY RUDE...  sad

I visited this restaurant last weekend with a group of friends. The food was OK, pretty generic and Americanized, but not bad. Also, our waitress was polite and helpful, though service was a bit slow. That being said, it was really overpriced for the quality. At the end of the meal a friend of mine had a Localvore Deal for the restaurant. The owner refused to honor it as she did not have a printed copy, even though she had the barcode and all numbers needed on her phone. In all fairness, the deal did say they must present a printed copy, but the owner's handling of this situation, with attitude and total dismissal of the fact that the point of the deal is to attract new customers, left a bad taste in my mouth at the end of the meal. Nothing about this place was worth the price and quite frankly I don't want to spend my money to support someone so unmotivated by customer service.
Yea, Ive eaten here. I don't see the big deal. The pizza is Ehh and the place has no parking. Parking for your Caww ;-)

I'm actually mad, son. I've been meaning to start leaving reviews but nothing inspired me to take the time until the overwhelming whateverness that is Sakura filled me such foodie disdain.
