I ate here right before I moved to Chicago.  The office girls threw me a going away party and the wait staff did not disappoint!  They made sure we had a great experience.This place is new, and I wish it had opened years ago so I could have gone more often! First, The atmosphere:  Very cozy and quaint, sophisticated. You smell the food as soon as you are in the door!  Loved the amuse bouche offering. Food;  We split several appetizers and not a one disappointed us.  There is a lot of mushroom on the menu and in the ingredients, and one of my girlfriends is allergic.  The staff was happy to help her choose something suitable.  I had the pasta sampler, which was to die for! I highly recommend this for a nice adult gathering or first date.

Great atmosphere, friendly bar tenders who make great cocktails and seriously brilliant Sangria, which if you are not carefully will torture you the next day. The food Cuban, spicy and very delicious. They have a black bean dip that looks awful but tastes amazing. Their tasting plate is a really good cross section of the menu and is hearty. Very good value for money.

I had a wonderful meal here with a large group of friends last night. The appetizers; calamari Frito with a surprising touch of honey,and a rum glazed shrimp were a great start. The salmon was beautifully done and all of our portions were generous. Service was excellent and we will certainly return.

I went here around 5:30pm and asked for a table for 3. The lady told us it should be 40-45 minutes wait, but it ended up being 1.25 hrs! I ordered the nabeyaki udon. I advise you do not order this. The ratio of noodles and broth was off and the noodles were overcooked. The tempura was already fully soaked in the soup, which made me really sad. There were only a couple of pieces of tiny chicken in it and almost no veggies. Not even close to avg nabeyaki udon. I guess the place is not called Udon-ya afterall!

The seafood here was good, but the meat was very tough. However the strangest part of the meal was the service.  We were served a dish that was brimming with sauce, and our table was not level.  So when the waitress put the dish down, the sauce started to pour out over the edge.  She gave one wipe of the table with her towel, then just left as the sauce continued to pour out!  We scrambled to scoop things out of the dish and had to ask for a pile of napkins to sop up the sauce. ??

This is the only BBQ place that a frequent in NJ. The food is great and matched by the service. The owner is a great guy and very happy to speak with you. Not to mention he also makes the food. Thumbs up!
Very good service and very good Sushi. We had the Star roll,  Red dragon roll, and Sushi Koshi roll. (We requested the rolls be spicy and all with black rice)

What a great place!  Must have eaten here over 50 times and never has there been a glitch in the fast service and perfect food.  Great service, perfect execution, and amazing value explain why the place is always packed.  If you're looking for a quiet dining experience, this isn't the place for you.  But if you're in the area and want a quick, high quality lunch, you're in the right place.  Fajitas, Route 66 Chopped Salad and Salmon San Sebastian are awesome.

Coming to Sushi Yasuda, I had a high expectation, and they definitely didn't live up to it. I thought this place was just average. The service was so not on point. Our server even forget to bring out our order, but claimed she did. The food was fresh but didn't have the flavor that were're looking for. Most of the Sashimi tasted bland and uninviting. The price was high for what I've experienced. I hope they can step up on their game, cause they still have some good sushi. If you have a tree growing wads of cash go for it, otherwise go else where for your taste buds.

Visited with friends and my mum so was quite preoccupied catching up! That said, the pastas we had were good, just a bit pricey for what it was. Good selection of items and seems quite trendy. Bit out the way to find. Probably would not make the effort to go back.
This pizza is not cheap but I think it just might be the best that I have had in NJ. I am not sure what the best way to describe the food. The thin pizza just cannot be missed.

When we first noticed that a pizza place was coming to Towaco we were excited.  Having lived there since 1970 and not having a local pizzeria was something new to the area!  The first day it opened we stopped to order a pizza.  To our surprise there pizza is 12" personal pizza's.  Since we are big eaters I knew 1 would not be enough.  We ordered a Margherita with chicken and a New Yorker.  Both were good but we were disappointed with the toppings.  Love the concept of the wood fired pizza but we are traditional pizza eaters.  Big pie in a big white box!  Plus we thought thirty something dollars for 2 pizza's was very pricey!  The place is geared to attract the so called "yuppy" folk of Towaco and not the old timers that have live in the area for a long time.

This place do live up to the hype. The noodles and the fried dumplings are some of the best I've ever tried. The price is cheap - 11 fried or steamed dumplings for $3. The space is really small, cramped with lots of people and can get loud and obnoxious. You can watch and hear the guy pulling and banging the noodles, fresh right next to where you sit. I have to say it is somewhat a good experience. I was satisfy with the meal, the reason I docked a star is mainly because the place is a little grungy. The food is good enough for me to come back at another time.

Best place ever omg I kept passing but it with a friend but never came in so I decided to give it a try a few months back and omg I LOVE THIS PLACE BEST DRINKS GREAT GOOD GOOD AMBIENCE LOVE THE DECOR SO AMAZING AND THE WAITeres are very nice worth the price for what you get

I really wanted to love Narcissa but unfortunately it fell short at every turn. (Management take note-this would have been a 3 star review were it not for our incredibly impolite server, Ben) What we ordered- mission figs barley risotto potato gnocchi entree lacquered duck breast carrot fries poached pear Food-3/5 The mission figs were good but far too sweet, would benefit from either a balsamic or red wine reduction. Rosemary was incredibly hard and made me fear I might puncture my tongue at any moment. The barley risotto was quite nice and had a balanced flavor. As for the gnocchi entree, the portion as an entree was incredibly small. My date immediately asked me if I wanted to order another entree when he saw the portion size (bear in mind I am a fit 5'2" and a size 2-not a football quarterback), but I was already disenchanted with the food and opted against. The potato gnocchi had a grainy consistency to it which was not helped at all by the minimal amount of incredibly hard butternut squash in the dish. Granted that I don't eat meat I cannot comment on the flavor of his duck breast, but there seemed to be an excessive amount of fat he had to trim from the breast. Nothing at all like the duck breast at Park Avenue Autumn he had last night and could not stop raving about. He remained notably silent throughout this meal. Carrot fries were nothing special, between the two of us we ate 1. The poached pear was absolutely amazing and the only thing I would recommend on the menu. Now, onto the LACK of service that dragged this from a 3 star review to a 1 star review (actually, I would have left no review at all and might have even returned given that I live nearby). At no point did our server check in on us to ask if we were enjoying our meal. I had to ask twice for balsamic vinegar and my date waited 15 minutes for his drink until finally I flagged the waiter down and reminded him. No apology. Complete attitude throughout our meal-we really are the easiest customers imaginable, we always order a substantial amount (including 3-6 drinks) at every meal. If he had told us there was an incredible bottle on the menu or raved about some additional item we should try as we ordered we would happily have ordered it. Not that profiling your customers is ever appropriate, but if he was discriminating based off of our relatively young ages this should have been offset by price insensitivity. Here comes the kicker-I asked him if they can do an iced soy chai tea latte, which he said no to, and which is fine given that it is a more obscure request. I asked for an iced soy latte, to which he responded that they don't make any iced beverages. Fine. I order a soy latte and the poached pear dessert, then innocuously say "I'm sorry, I'll actually change to a skim cappuccino and the poached pear." Soy milk can take on a funny consistency in hot beverages, which took my a split second to remember given my almost exclusive consumption of iced beverages. BEN'S' RESPONSE-"'You know, there is a Starbucks around the corner." He said this with the most patronizing smirk on his face then sauntered away. Not wanting to ruin the lovely evening I was having I spoke with my date and asked him to not tip excessively as is par for the course with him. Context: we had a very sweet server 2 weeks ago who seemed genuinely happy in her job and who was very attentive. We had an appetizer and 4 drinks and the check came to $59. Her tip was $150. I really don't know why Ben was so rude to us throughout our meal, but I assure you we will never return to Narcissa and allow ourselves to be condescended to again. (Disclaimer- The hostess and Maitre'D were absolutely lovely. He really is the only individual who soured our evening)

This was my first time at this place and I was very happy to find this place the food was absolutely delicious my boyfriend and I was coming back from Atlantic city and decided to stop in N.Y. to eat I yelped all kunds of places and found kelos and it was a great stop and well worth it the staff and cook was very nice to us thank you very much I will definitely be back
It was first time visiting. and I didn't know what or how should I order my burger. but the cashier  didn't help me at all. She was so unkind and rude. I will never come back here again!!
It was veeeery delicious))) Were here with friend on lunch and had the daily special, 5 tacos and Agua mirca. Good stuff! Will be back!

If you rate this guy's one star it automatically goes to "not recommended review" check out all the one stars in not recommended section. These are true reviews. I don't know what they did with yelp. This an't no true review.
The food is good but over rated.

I personally hate the wait and think the pizza is over rated and is too oily! But when I am with friends and they suggest to go here I do not argue because this is a Brooklyn Landmark. The old man is an artist and the pizza pie is his canvas. Someone who has never tried it must try it at least once in their lives but I do not know about multiple trips. You will wait at the bare minimum for 45 minutes in a not so clean place but people say it is worth the wait. But once you take off some of the oil the taste is amazing. Please let me know if anyone else feels the same way about it.
Quiet location, came here with a group of friends and had great service.  Food was delicious and not too expensive!

I did a late night service call there and when I was done they gave me a plate of rigatoni and meatballs.  I got in my truck and started to eat. I started driving and placed the plate on the passenger seat. As I was driving I had to make a quick stop and the plate slid off the seat and fell to the ground.  I'm not embarrassed to say it but I still ate the dish. It was that delicious!!!

I went yesterday with some friends and we all had a wonderful food experience. Creativity and their menu proposal, the taste of every plate was just delicious¡¡¡ One of my favorites places in the world¡¡ And dont forget to order the trucha, is MEMORABLE¡¡¡

OFF TO A GREAT START BUT FINISHED POORLY.  I ordered the signature large plain pizza 2 weeks ago.  It's on the small side of what I'm used to eating when ordering a large pizza.  The slices are roughly the size of an Eiilo's frozen pizza.  You get 10 slices in a large pie.  The pizza that was delivered two weeks ago was FANTASTIC!!! Everybody agreed that it was one of the BEST if not the THE BEST PIZZAS we have ever tasted!  UNFORTUNATELY THAT IS NOT THE EXPERIENCE WE HAD THE SECOND TIME AROUND.  We ordered the same pizza, a large square plain pie.  The pizza arrived about 50 minutes from the time it was ordered.  I believed it to be a little long to wait for a plain pizza on a Wednesday night.  As it turned out the pizza agreed with me!!  When I opened the box I was met by a pizza that had dry pizza sauce on top of it as opposed to a wet/fresh pizza sauce that was delivered on our initial order two weeks earlier.   I called the store and spoke to the manager Brett.  He offered to get a fresh pizza out within 15 minutes but would need to pick up the bad pizza.  I told him no thanks as it was getting late and I had other things to do.  Hopefully they can cut that delivery time down to thirty minutes or less.  The jury is still out on this place.  Will the real Santucci's Original Square Pizza ever be delivered to our home again?  We sure hope so, but another experience like our second, and we may just have to opt out for Ellio's frozen pizza.  Ouch!!!

Oh Traif, a restaurant that serves all of my favourite things was always going to be a winner. The food was great, quite a varied menu that is made up of smaller sharing dishes. A nice spread of options that were well done. The food wasn't 'gastronomy' but it was very flavourful and non-pretentious which I prefer. I would say as a warning - the dishes are billed as 'small plates' but they aren't all that small! We ordered 5 at the recommendation of our waiter but we were stuffed at four (might have been what we ordered though as we went for quite heavy rich food). It's not cheap but neither eyewateringly expensive our meal plus quite a few drinks came to $120 (not inc tip). If you like pork and seafood I would definitely recommend Traif.
I was there last night, on party with my friends. I like this place, Great food, not so expensive, good atmosphere ;)

Our first time there --but it wont be the last !! The food is amazing because  Jane, Skip & Chef Chad let NO detail go without their full attention. It's a 25 mile ride for us; but its worth the ride AND well worth the price of a cab just to be able to enjoy the Martinis by Keith !! You would be hard pressed to find a  comparable value in the upper valley. Rich & Gail Scalesse

I went there recently and I have to say this is a great place if you're looking for Penang style hawker/street food. It is very authentic and the food come very close to what you would get in Malaysia especially in Penang Island. Even the waitress is from there. I can't speak for other "types" of dishes since my goal was to get those exact food I mentioned above and for that I was very satisfy with it.
Awesome restaurant with great prices.  You have to try the roti canai and seafood scramble egg chow fun.  Wash it down with watermelon juice or coconut water straight outta the nut.
Pretty good.

This restaurant opened in the old Ino space which I was so sad to see go but what a welcome addition! Great cozy spot! Delicious wine, yummy small plates and pasta. Great, attentive service. I will definitely become a regular.

Pizza was good but really wasn't worth making the trek out for. Toppings are extremely over priced considering the amounts they give you. If you're in the area give it a try, if not, just look in your area.

Once our server helped us with the menu we then enjoyed a fabulous Sunday brunch. We started with Bloody Marys with shrimp and octopus garnish. Our first course was thinly sliced fresh prosciutto, lamb crudo (tartar), served with warm, herbed crostini,and a wonderful arugula salad with toasted hazelnuts and sliced red grapes. Our main course was Branzino (sea bass) with a compote of garbanzo beans and marinated red peppers and a Purgatorio, eggs poached in a homemade tomato sauce topped with light cheese and buttered bread crumbs. I highly recommend this authentic Italian contemporary cuisine, Delicioso!
Geno's is better, but I'd only give that a 3 star. Very meh
TBH I've only ordered take out. The food is amazing every time but I've waited over an hour and a half for delivery to the point where I'm not even hungry anymore. Only go in person.
awesome veggie food prices are a little steep but taste makes up for it!! try the chicken nuggets and salt and pepper chicken strips

Over hyped restaurant in NYC. Chicken & Vegetarian meatballs could've tasted much better. There are restaurants out there who can do awesome job. You have to admit that their prices are more affordable but I wouldn't comprise for the better experience.

Great pernil asado (roast pork).  Great empanadas (tried a beef and a chicken).  I left off a star because the portion of beans was fairly small given 2 entrees purchased.  Next time I'll order an extra side of beans.  Ridiculously inexpensive as well.

Gorgeous food and friendly staff. Hint - don't order individual meals as the portions are huge. There were 4 of us and we ordered 1 starter, 1 Main and 1 desert between us all and even at that there was some left over. We ordered the salad, meatballs and chocolate torte. Could have no complaints about any of it. Cocktails were also delicious. Not pricey either. Our bill came to $98 for l fod and drinks. A perfect restaurant in New York!

Had a great dinner experience here on Tuesday. I was entertaining a friend from out of town and we ordered the chicken wings, short rib sliders and bruschetta. Everything was delicious, reasonably priced and our server was very attentive and friendly. I will definitely be coming back soon :)

I have not dined at Becco in several years. Having had the pleasure of remembering a better dining experience, I was quite disappointed when I visited a few days ago. The waitress seemed to be going through the motions of doing what she was trained to do. Cold and sterile. As it was not busy when we arrived, I expected better.The breads were cold and unappetizing. The 3 choice pasta dishes, which I ordered were fair to good with unlimited helpings. My guest ordered veal picatta which was very tasty. As the restaurant, which is in the Theatre district, filled up, the service got worse. Not a relaxing meal.. Happy to leave.

Came here a couple of days ago during lunch time and wow. My friend warned me about coming here on an empty stomach and I did not listen. The entire time I was looking at their menu and all I could do was hold my grumbling stomach at bay with the thought that my sandwich would arrive on time to curb the grumbling little beast. The meats and cheeses were oh so fresh, I got the Lamazou Favorite and it was mouthwatering from the first bite to the last. The moz's and roasted peppers, oh. I'm dreaming about them now. The only gripe I had was the price to meat proportion. They could have done with a little more "stuff", hopefully next time I come back, I will get more. Here's to hoping.

Great authentic Italian restaurant in the West Village. Great to have a place that has Italian food not drowning in cheese. The service is fantastic, a really great wine list and pastas are to die for! We get there every opportunity we can! Its almost like being in Italy!

Here's a beautiful place! Shehrezads cafe...we ordered some falafel, chicken kabob and the delicious lamb kabob... Which was served with tabouli, hummus and pita bread taste was awesome. The place was beautifully done well maintained by George the owner. Very neat and hospitable place to visit. Can't wait to go back again:)

Enjoyed a happy hour event here. Tasty, quality cocktails for great prices and yummy appetizers. The bartenders and other servers were just great. Clean and bright environment with plenty of parking. Will definitely be back for dinner sometime soon!

Fabulous ambiance. Had the Duck - very good. Prices a bit high but entrees in NYC between $28-$35 are expected. Portions were a bit small - but who wants to get stuffed. Might be nice to lower the prices in recognition of the smaller portions. Service was impeccable. Wine is expensive. If you are looking for a real good restaurant that has the NYC aura and is not on the tourist route - this one will be a good choice. Also there are some interesting trendy shops in the immediate area.

Very rude customer service.  Beer is extremely overpriced (4 bottles for $15-20+).  Also do not accept cards for bills under $10.  Used to go there for convenience, but now try to completely avoid this place at all costs. Do not give them your business!!!

Who would have thought I'd find a nice izakaya in the theater district? Well, it's here. However, if you want a seat, don't come too late. I showed up at 6:30 once and got the last seat in the place (at the bar) because I was by myself. The bartender was great though, and I loved the various yakitori goodies I got, especially the chicken gizzards. The ginkos were very nice, as was the mushroom. The potatoes were the least tasty, but still nice. On another occasion, my mother had a very rich ramen full of seafood and other tasty tidbits, while I enjoyed a luscious piece of grilled miso salmon and codfish pickled in sake lees. The servers are pleasant and fast, so it's a great pre-theater stop.

All around class-act place. Really sharp looking bar and restaurant. We were just in for drinks but the food looked good. Casual modern and upscale place in a historic setting. From the hostess to the concierge everybody was very friendly. The bearded bartender was the star of the show. Nice to find a place with bartenders with personality.

I loved the food on my first visit. I tried their Crepe/dosa and it was delicious. Lip-smacking chutneys and their Mulaga pudi Idli is a delight. I tried their Indo-Chinese fusion fried rice and was not disappointed. We are making it our must visit at least once a week restaurant.

Don't go to this place. The staff are clearly unprofessional, and the food is disgusting.  They have rats and roaches.  The food is cheap but not worth your health.  Take your money and go somewhere else.  If there are roaches and rats, trust me, they are unclean and that stuff is in your food.  There was a dead roach in my potatoes.

On the North-Western edge of Brooklyn, in Green Point, lies a hidden, not-yet-well-known restaurant. The passion and dedication of its owner, Thomaso, a first generation Italian immigrant, is seen, smelled, tasted, and felt in every corner, on every surface, and in every dish. Family recipes, passed down through time, find their way onto the menu and warms the soul with each bite. It's a magical place. With an understated panache Milk and Roses woos you when you first walk in. But it's Thomaso's spirit, embodied in his self-described "decrepit" interior, and infused into the dishes such as the prawn risotto, octopus and shellfish soup, or red-wine poached pear dessert, that leaves you wishing the clock didn't say "closing time." As the jazz playlist fades into the shadow's of Manhattan's lights, and the last few notes of Cynar dance across your tongue, Milk and Roses reminds you that this city is built on the hopes of immigrants and dreamers alike and, once in-a-while, one of their stars shines extra bright.

Solid place. Classic in every sense minus the old school jukebox. Staff is friendly. Service is prompt. Your coffee cup won't stay empty for long no matter what time of day it is. A neighborhood fixture. Expanded the menu some over the last year as well to give more options.

I recently visited Whitman & Bloom this past Saturday night (11/08/14) and was terribly disappointed with my experience there. One of my good friends was celebrating his birthday at the downstairs lower level bar area. I also work in the service industry and understand the need to prioritize especially as the night progresses. Unfortunately, this gentleman behind the bar seemed furious to be at work, slamming glassware as he stocked them for about 10 minutes before he even acknowledged my presence at the center of the bar. Mind you the bar downstairs is tiny compared to the one upstairs, so I find it difficult to believe that he did not see me. This bothered me, however I witnessed this man dressed in a red and black button up sport shirt, leave the bar area and approach what appeared to be a manager. I witnessed the entire conversation and was really disturbed by the content of it. Essentially the bartender was worried about a group of African-American males who in his words were "stoned". If being "stoned" at a bar is grounds for negative attention from the Staff then I'm not sure if this is the establishment I want to ever visit again. What really bothered me is that I saw the group he referred to as "stoned", they were all Black, well dressed and in fact some were socializing with the few people there. I have no choice but to wonder if this is a classic case of discrimination we have here. Employees have to keep in mind that not only do they work for an establishment but they also represent the establishment. This has to be the worst representation of an otherwise fine establishment I have ever witnessed in my life.

I love going to this place. The food is really awesome and the prices are great. Although I have to admit I almost always order the same thing: a bowl of whatever soup they have (always so amazing) and the roast chicken, mozzarella, arugula and spicy mayo panini. I've tried to order other panini's but always go back to this one-its just so good! The beets with baby arugula, goat cheese and toasted walnut isalata is also amazing. When it isn't too cold out, they have a nice (although small) outdoor area to sit.

I love this as to switch it up from the ordinary as for their menu is out of the ordinary in a great way. Oxtail is super delicious and the bavon popcorn is way addicting. Staff really takes good care of you even if its your first time and you act like a deer in headlight when checkin out the menu, but all in all Fantastic place.
Best damn food cart menu of all time.  When I was in new York i must stopped by halal guys every night.  We even brought back 8 orders for friends in California.  Highly recommend!

Came here for lunch and ordered the arugula with chicken meatballs and a side of roasted brussel sprouts. The greens were fresh and brussel sprouts were delicious, but the meatballs were dry and lacked flavor. Overall great meal with quick seating, good service, and a casual (but extremely loud) atmosphere.

Were invited out here for dinner. Would normally not chose Lebanese food but it far exceeded expectations. Fresh and plenty of variety. We shared some small plates of hummus, meatballs and shrimps. I had the lamb shank. Amazingly tasty.

This should have been posted in May but I great food, fun, and venue can never be forgotten. I had my wife's surprise 40th birthday at Palo Santo. From the inception of meeting Palo Santo, it has been nothing but the best. I was able to purchase a total buyout with time to set-up. The staff was super helpful with transitioning the venue. My wife was totally thrilled and enjoyed the cozy space. The food was great. The drinks were great. The staff was great. What more do you need. If you all are looking for a place to have a party, this is the space!

This Aussie place is rather small comparing to a normal restaurant. There are only 4 picnic style tables available. I feel the authenticity for the foreign food because the server carries an Australian accent. For the food, I ordered the Bronte Burger with fried egg. Basically they put together premium ground beef, tomato, lettuce, sweet chili, mayo and cheese. It is simply delicious. The beef was cooked and seasoned perfectly. We also got the pasta dishes and they are also very flavorful. I would probably come back here if I was in the area. I was very satisfied with my meal.

I go to the Wooster Street location for lunch at least once per week and sometimes for for dinner. Of late the lunch service has gone through the floor. What the hell happened there ? From the table service to food prep......the quality has dropped.  This was my go to restaurant.......I'm rethinking that.

I like the food, however, the prices are definitely too high. To order a curry rice dish with garlic naan costs about $15. And that's only for veggies, paneer, or chicken. Add $3+ dollars to that total if you want lamb or shrimp. And some may argue they are a bit skimpy with the meat. I can fork over just a few extra dollars at another place for restaurant ambience and service. Why would I pay this much for a casual, to-go restaurant? The service is also a bit spotty as well. Not exactly rude, but definitely not kind either.
Delicious food and great atmosphere.  Great for a date night.

What a terrific experience! Originally planning to drop by for a beer to check out Beehive Oven, our party of 3 stayed a couple of hours enjoying the great food, drink and company! Delicious food with a Southern flair and cold, cold brewskis were enhanced by the warm atmosphere, original artwork and friendly and attentive owners and staff. No pretension - just fun!

Because the restaurant itself is on the small side, there is always a wait during peak brunch time. If you hate waiting, I suggest you go to brunch at an off-peak time. That said, the service and food at Northern Spy are always excellent no matter how crowded it is. Side note: Tip your server nicely. They really do work non-stop during brunch hours. I highly recommend the sake bloody mary, the buttery biscuits to start and the kale salad with eggs. The menu is a little on the pricey side, but it's worth it if you are looking for something beyond the usual coffee, bacon and eggs.

This place feels like home! The atomosphere is so comfortable,  the staff treats you like family, and the food is as good as a home cooked meal in Italy. Highly recommend for anyone in the area, this place is not to be missed!! I go with friends and on dates with my husband- it can be romantic and intimate or open and friendly- just sit at the bar and you're easily charmed by the bartenders or the company next to you. My fave place in Astoria for sure!!

I've been coming here for years..its definitely one of the best restaurants for rodizio! Also love their sangria and picadinho platter. Waiters and and staff are always friendly too. Love the whole ambience.
Great food and wine! Waitress was super helpful on recommending wine and interpreting dishes. Lovely back area. Would come again.

I had heard good things about Stone Hearth, and we decided to give it a try for dinner.  So glad we did!  Loved the menu, the apps and cheese tray were very good.  Service was excellent!  Each of our entrees were also delicious!  The desserts were on the simple side, but we shared two - the strawberry trifle and the chocolate pot -- outstanding!!  All in all a great experience - will be back soon!

One of my favorite go to places in NYC if your looking for casual and fun atmosphere.  I have been here numerous times over the years.  Always great food and good Mojitos!  Anyone who comes to visit me in NYC always takes the trip down to the LES to experience this place.  Tuesday night - half price apps till 8pm - can't beat this deal!

This place has changed from a decent, reasonably priced Mexican tacqueria into quite possibly the worst Mexican restaurant in the city. They have replaced quality food with a WiFi speaker playing music way too loud and gratuitous servings of bad, unordered margarita pitchers (but apparently "on the house" even though we byo'd that bottle of tequila you took to the kitchen...thanks!). Thur to Sat the only option now is a $20/person family-style meal of dogsh*t taquitos, concession-stand quesadillas, and the most bland burritos I've ever eaten. Never again... Go to Veracruzana for superior food and environment. Happy Birthday Steve. Sorry your birthday dinner sucked, although Jon had fun.

We went on a Sunday evening and set on the bar. The place has great atmosphere and accordingly decorated. The food was great, the best tapas I have ever had. We just kept ordering food until the paella with sea food was just perfect, really the best I had. With two pints of Spanish bear, we had great enjoyable dinner. This place is highly recommended.

Working in NYC,,, we have tried many Sushi restaurants,,,, this place is our Favorite!! Their food is very high quality and beyond delicious.. The service is also excellent. The Hibachi is also great!! We go there once a week if we can. Five Stars!

Hands down the greatest place to shop and eat. Everything from the chocolate to the beer to the pastas to the kitchen goods were beyond amazing. Sat down and had a small afternoon snack, service was great (considering the high traffic of people at 4pm). Will be visiting Eataly every time I'm in New York City. Wish they would open one in Los Angeles!

I was impressed by the vast amount of creative rolls! The pumpkin miso soup was delicious beyond my expectations.Waitstaff was fun and eccentric.Will definently be back to further explore the interesting selections on the menu!

I've been to Samudra over a dozen times and love their food.  I've tried nearly every kind of dosa on their menu and give them excellent reviews.  The staff are always courteous and welcoming.  They are also probably the cleanest Indian restaurant in Jackson Heights. Definitely best dosa experience in Jackson Heights.

Went for a quick lunch and that pasta was very tasty. Small hole in the wall type of restaurant with cute decorations. Plates hanging on the walls make you feel like your in a home style kitchen. The service was good, our waiter was a little annoying but the good food made up for that!
Best Shepard salad I have had... Great lunch spot! I'd recommend the chicken also, it's extremely tender, and the taziki sauce has a great dill flavor. Two thumbs up!
The best "Grimaldi's pizza"around. Love the ambiance and friendly and quick staff. Great pizza.
I love Veggie Heaven! I've been eating from here for years. Lots of unique dishes to choose from. And you can't beat their lunch menu. Love their chicken nuggets!!!
What a great place! As Ukrainian myself, I can assure you this is the best Ukrainian/russian food in the city. Beautiful decor and great service!

I was very excited to have this cozy place fill a spot in the neighborhood.  The menu is small, but varied. The service was as excellent as I've received at top notch restaurants.   I had the quinoa salad which was an amazing vegetarian choice.  I couldn't finish it because it was so filling.  My friend had mac-and-cheese and was not disappointed.  She was stuffed, but couldn't stop eating it. My friend was impressed with the beer selections, and was not disappointed with her choice.  I don't like beer and found the wine list very limited.  I enjoyed the glass I had, but wish there were more choices.   Our server was amazing.  Attentive, but didn't hover.  Answered our questions and made great suggestions. I could do without the TVs in the dining area, but that's nothing unique to this bar.  I don't enjoy football, especially when I'm trying to eat.  Thankfully the volume was down, and we were able to enjoy the music playing in the background.   I'm looking forward to many more meals here.

This is as good as a gets.  And it is all because of their Red Sauce.  You would be a fool not to order a dish that includes that sauce.  It is the money maker for me that separates it from all other surrounding Italian restaurants.  It is so good that I order a few quarts to go after I finish devouring the chicken parm and penne.  It's so darn good that I could take a spoon and dig away like its ice cream and wish it was acceptable to lick my plate, because I would do just that. The bread?  Solid. Warm. Crispy.  Salad?  Solid.  Does have a strong amount of pepper and salt (which I like!) The chicken is normally cooked fine, however I have had an overcooked or "tough" piece every once and while, but there was no problem exchanging it for a brand new dish.   The servers are very accommodating and Sal always welcomes you into the restaurant.  It is extremely nice inside and is great for parties.  I will actually be booking one for next year.  This is a classy place that would be great for a date or meeting.
Great interior, food and service.  I will def go again next time I'm in NY.

This is our third time at the Sea Fire Grill. In one word, AMAZING! From the fantastic Manager... Arron Kraja, to the fantastic wait staff including Donny and Madison; our dining experience was perfect! Our 2nd visit was my wife's birthday and it was exceptional... So much so that we came back the next evening. If you are looking for a perfect blend of both amazing food, drinks and atmosphere; the Sea Fire Grill is a must! As an added bonus, they have the best Oysters to be had from Philadelphia to Manhattan!
I really enjoyed brunch at Jane. The ambiance is great and the food was very good. A bit over priced for what you get, but it's still a good time. Service was very good.

Omg this place is so ahead of its time! A good girlfriend and I went by this place to celebrate a job offer and I must say, the drinks and food were phenomenal. Being a pescataria (with many vegan/vegetarian friends) in NYC, you'd think that there are a plethora of great options as far as restaurants go. But i honestly have to say that I was really impressed by the food quality and the service. Well priced, fresh, clean, delicious! We had the squash and carrots as an appetizer, with an amazing rose as suggested by our bartender, Michael (who was fantastic, knowledgable, and just made the experience really delightful. He's not there anymore tho). The ambiance is wonderful too! Great place for an afternoon brunch or even a rehearsal dinner. Overall I give the place five stars and just wish more people knew about it!

I was not impressed with this place--especially with all the decent reviews.  I suggested that my friend and I go, because I'd read they served Jacques Torres hot chocolate.  I thought it would be wonderful to have a NJ cafe that offered it. We've both had and made our own JT hot chocolate.  It's creamy and rich and quite decadent. It's worth ordering online or going to an NYC location to savor it. What they served us at Le Petit Parisien was a far cry from JT's blend. It was relatively flavorless and very watery.  Perhaps they weren't generous with the mix...or were saving the good stuff for another time. Whatever the reason, it was disappointing to say the least. We also shared the ham and cheese croissant, since we just wanted a snack. We both were expecting a fluffy, puffy buttery croissant. Instead they had put the sandwich in a press and flattened the sh*t out of it, as well as burning it.  How can a French café f**k up serving a croissant??? That's almost sacrilegious! Things that were nice...I did like the miniature Eiffel Tower in the window. Oh and the glass mugs in which the hot chocolate was served were cute.  We didn't try the macarons.  But at $2.75 each, they could keep them.  Like my friend so wryly said, "Were they made in the armpit of an angel? " Lol Don't waste your money.  Skip.

I'm from Miami, FL. And I've been to Chicago and tried there best pizza.  BUT! I was told that Artichoke had the best pizza so I went to NY for vacation in Sept 2014 all I can say is WOW!!! this truly was the best pizza I've had ever and that's hard for me to say Haha.  If you go there you need to try the artichoke pizza that by far was the best.  I wish I could give more stars.  Thank you Artichoke for making my NY experience that much better!

This place has the worst service I have ever had in NYC, and I've lived here since 1996.  I went back a second time thinking it was just an off-night.  BIG MISTAKE.  Both times the wait was endless.  Finding a server nearly impossible.  And the food??--mine literally came out 40 min AFTER my date had FINISHED theirs.  CLOSE THIS PLACE NOW!

Ordered from here off of GrubHub today. Ordered what was written on the menu as "three chicken tacos", and received three small chicken taquitos instead. Would not have paid $6.50 if I knew. Also ordered a Baleada con Carne Asada, had to pick between sour cream or cheese, and picked cheese since sour cream makes me very sick. It arrived with only a little meat and a lot of sour cream, so I couldn't even eat it. When I complained, the staff was friendly and understanding (hence the extra star) and willing to refund me for the $4 baleada or remake it. Didn't really have any interest in getting another, and would prefer to be refunded for the "tacos". Hope they change the descriptions on the menu and adjust the price.
Fun, low-key, relaxed atmosphere.  Great service and tasty food.

Amazing place for grocery shopping, a quick snack, or an interesting way to kill 20 minutes walking around or people watching. Every conceivable type of food, often farm fresh and prepared in front of you. For a tourist, definitely a stop you should make. This one helped rename "Market Street" in honor of the open air markets that crowded it, and Reading Terminal opened as a closed air market in the mid 19th century. Cool place. The Penn. Dutch usually aren't there every day, so don't be surprised.

Actually, the second worst restaurant I've ever eaten in (the first was the now-defunct Leon's on Longwharf in New Haven).  We (my sister and I) both ordered pasta dishes.  If they were not literally inedible, they were the closest thing to it.  Neither of us had much more than a fork full.  The waitress was unfazed when we asked for the check with full dishes of food standing before us, uneaten.  No doubt, this was as common experience for her! PS The whiskey sours we both ordered were fine.
oink..oink...Ok I guess
I agree with all the positive reviews.
Such a wonderful little place with an awsome atmosphere. Great sandwich and finally a good and strong cup if coffee in New York!!! We LIKE!!

Farm to table and local produce mixed with organic items, what could be better. It's Montclair so it's byob which keeps it reasonable.  Seasonal items always keep you guessing. Plus the corn bread medallions and little cookies at the end are superb. Support local and check out this restaurant!
Amazing! Best subs around- and the eggplant parm is fantastic- you gotta try it!
Love this place so much!!! The employees are so sweet and helpful. The front of house is clean and organized and the good is fresh and tasty. I stop by as often as I can!

Great small place, we went there with our class last Friday. Around 15 people ( whole place can feet probable 20 !!! ) Make the reservation popular spot for the weekends. Food taste great, and it's fresh small kitchen friendly atmosphere with great price :-)

My wife and I went to meal last weekend on a recommendation from a friend and boy do I owe my freind a favor... This was by far one of he best meals I have had in a long time (Pun intended), and when I say MEAL that encompasses not only the food but the service, price, and atmosphere as well.. After being sat immediately We were promptly and enthusiastically greeted by a young fellow named Steven who informed us that we were in for quite a treat upon learning this was our first time at the restaurant. All I ask for in a waiter is someone who is nice and genuinely give a hoot about taking care of us, but this server went above and beyond and truly made sure that we were comfortable.  The menu had so many great choices that I didn't know what to pick but once again our sever helped push us in the right direction, after giving us a flawless breakdown of the specials he informed us that MEAL excels in steak dinners and how all the steaks on the menu are  of a specific high quality grade beef and they are cooked at a certain temperature with butter salt and pepper and that no matter how rare we liked our steaks it would still have that nice crispy char on the outside, but when they have special steaks they are usually very high quality.  He made the KC steak (bone in NY strip... Which I had no idea prior) accompanied by a full plate of goods as opposed to the normal ala carte sound so good that I couldn't refuse and let me tell you it was worth every penny, just as thue server said nice and red and juicy on the inside and perfectly charred and crisp on the outside, not to mention everything else was phenomenal as well ( French onion soup with sherry, truffled creamy blue cheese potato chips with bacon bits, tuna tartar, and my wife got the cowboy steak which our server said was his personal favorite from the regular menu, and our sides creamed spinach with almonds and truffle, sautéed mushrooms and beer battered onion rings). I know i have went on a bit of a ramble here but that is how good this place is, but now my fingers are starting to hurt due to my early onset arthritis so I will wrap This up... MY FINAL GRADES: Atmosphere - A Price - A Service - A++ Food - A +++ Bottom line: as soon as you get the chance go have a meal at MEAL( and from what I've heard they have a fabulous Sunday brunch also) you will leave with a smile and a full stomach and you will not regret it!

Superb great greek food. Friendly service. Uge small greek salad. I like grilled dorada and lemon potatoes on the side. Very good also grilled octopus and baked clams. Should say everithing is very very god. I spend the night cloae by to have dinner every time I can.

I lived in this neighborhood over 20 years ago and returned w/ my husband for a vacation. The Hourglass Tavern is still here and the ambience and food are still cozy and delicious. This is a gem of Restaurant Row and they will flip the hourglass if you need to make an 8 pm curtain, so you can get to the show on time. Great meal, great atmosphere- you cant go wrong with this place!

We went there as two newbie oyster enthusiasts and one skeptic and got luckily seated at the last available table. I think even the skeptic is delighted with the oysters. Their beer menu is small but quite varied and of good quality. As Europeans not very accustomed to US brews, we did not have hard time to find favorites. To sum it up, the happy hour deal is amazing. We also tried three dishes with scallions, clams and fish. All were really flavorful and decently priced given the location.
Simple and delicious; Chicken fried rice, California & Atlanta rolls were awesome. Great néw drinks too, loved the Bullet Train.

WARNING this place gave me horrible food poisoning. What's worse is that it was the night before my trip to Amsterdam and I had to cancel my flight I was so sick. I a very reputable doctor and he confirmed I got sick from eating a mushroom Pizza at Adrienne's. I called the restaurant to let them know what had happened and they could have cared less!!!!! They didn't even offer to refund my meal. AND I left a message for the manager and nobody called me back.  I live in the neighborhood and don't appreciate being treated so terribly when I have been a regular customer. You can count on the fact that I will not be eating here again. DO NOT EAT HERE!

I was there in August for my mom's  Birthday, service was Fantastic and the food was delicious. I got a cake for my mom which got destroyed in the cab ride, thankfully the hostess and one of the chefs (I forgot his name) fixed it up for me at no charge. Can't wait to go back... By the way the paella is Perfect!

I've been extremely pleased with almost every single thing I've ever gotten here!  Very fresh ingredients, homemade soups, dangerously delicious cookies, and really friendly lady (owner?) at the counter - she's as sweet as pie!!  This place is a gem!!!!!
Service and food was excellent! Prices were also very reasonable. Atmosphere was excellent as a live, Cuban band played. Overall, I would highly recommend this restaurant and plan on returning soon.

Was not at all impressed with the Floor 19 experience. Was travelling from out of town and just looking for a good dinner with a view of the city. As I was staying in the hotel I thought it easy enough to just head upstairs. Was greeted carelessly by the hostess and informed no room for 1 (even though I could see big empty tables all around (not sure if understaffed or just didn't want to burn a table for 1 person) No biggie, I get it so I preceded to the bar. I sat and ordered a martini (asking if there were blue cheese olives available). You would think that a restaurant of this supposed caliber would be able to whip some up as they had stilton cheese (aged blue) on the menu. Oh well no biggie. Sat at the bar, service was spotty at best the bartender was to busy with her cronies ordering wings and socializing. I was left at the end of the bar wondering if I should eat there. I decided on the lobster appetizer with lemon aoli. It ended up being fried asparagus and 2 small pieces of lobster also deep fried layed on mayonnaise (no hint of lemon). Was greasy and unflavorful. Entire time I was at the bar it was a mess (menus all over, high stacks of napkins on bar and multiple bottles of liquor strewn throughout the bar, in back and on rail. Guess I picked a bad time (stock time) to have dinner. Wouldn't have thought at 7pm that I would see that or have had that kind of experience. I ended having a beer also and left for a different restaurant almost $50s later. Not impressed and if you have the same experience as me you won't be either. Good Luck!

Had the spaghetti Bolognese and my friend had a prosciutto sandwich. Both were excellent and service was quick. Keep in mind: No Diet Coke and no separate checks. Looks like a great dinner menu as well as a nice Lunch Specials selection.

Me and my friends went here for Sunday brunch.  All the food at our table was extremely yumm!! Specially the Spice End platter was so amazing and I would love to eat it again. We also ordered the Mango Lassi and it was my favorite drink. Great experience. I'll definitely be back soon..

We arrived for a dinner on Saturday night and restaurant was so busy even though, they served the best food and service was on time. That's the really a good thing I liked about it.  Definitely some of the best platter and roll I had. The all ingredient in platter speaks for itself.. I kept eating it.. So fresh.. And fair price..

My co-worker recommend this restaurant and Monday afternoon I decided to go with it. I ordered chicken tikka roll, and it was so delicious, but the best part about it that, roll comes with two different dipping sauce which can hit you out of nowhere.. It was sooo delicious, cooked to perfection and their service was outstanding..

Great food,  fun atmosphere and the owner makes you feel like you're family.   The staff is supper friendly.  And it's easy to get to from any borough!   The view of the city is,  well  it's the perfect view of the most incredible city from a great steak house that you don't have to wait 3 months to get a seating at!

For over a year I have been trying to dine here but it's always booked out. I finally got through and I wasn't impress. I thought it was overprice Italian food that's raved as the best restaurant. The service was good,staff was friendly though.

This place is no beauty from the outside. My friend and I walked in and were immediately greeted and seated and served water. It seems like more of a take out place as for the duration of our meal we were the only ones in the restaurant! The food was excellent however. I had the beef dumplings and sha momo (i think!). The broth was delicious and all ingredients tasted very fresh. Although the restaurant is a sit down and waiter service it was very casual.  Our waiter was excellent, bringing my friend a fork without condensation and running to get me a new pair of chopsticks when he saw mine had fallen. I liked it a lot!
Check out my review on my food blog: bigfoodjournal.blogspot.…
excellent pancakes in the mash Browns were very good.coffee was good service was excellent I will be back.
Why did you stop carrying Energy Vitamin Water? :(

Rude staff. DO NOT go here. Attempted to come here after my sister's wedding with a large group of people in their late 20's/early 30's. They let everyone in except my sister, who was still in her wedding dress. Really? We were with a group that was dressed in gowns and tuxes and the wouldn't let the bride in. What a bunch of a-holes.

Sitting in the restaurant right now. Table top iPad - BOLTED to the middle of the table - are an awful idea. iPads replace your menu and serve as a Square-like credit card payment system.  They take up table space and just sit there obnoxiously after you order. You've got to complete and pay for your order (and tip!) before they'll even bring you a pre-dinner beer or drink! So don't even think about ordering a drink while you continue to browse the menu. No sir. At least my glass of Cabernet is good. Entree isn't out yet but at this point I could care less how the overpriced food tastes.... I'm not coming back. Food came. I just raised my ranking from one stars to two. Chicken dish with steamed carrots was very good. Side dish of mashed potatoes was bland. Overall, iPad concept bad, food hit and miss, prices high, wine good, waiter good. Plenty of better choices at EWR.

Basso56 was very crowded with the theatre crowd. The food was great, especially the past with the lighter sauces- cream and butter dishes... the red sauce with bacon on the fusili was just ok.. Would go there again -appetizers and desserts were excellent!
Great food, great ambiance, hostess was super accommodating! Thanks Ryan for the great service!
Been here many times. Great new additions to the menu. Calamari, flatbread, Berkshire pork chop. Great service and management.
The best pizza in the world Period. I Wish they were walking distance from my house in queens.

Really good Ramen. This sums up the place pretty nicely. The broth was extremely flavorful and I enjoyed the pork as well as to add ons of seasoned avocado and fungus mushroom that I added. The chicken base broth was one of the richest I've ever tasted, super smooth and every sip was pure flavor. It is a tiny little place and as expected of New York the later it was the busier it got. The only reason I deduct the star is because the noodles themselves are from packages of noodles and not housemate. Nevertheless they were chewy and good Ramen noodles just not anything out of this world.

I have never written a negative review for a restaurant before in my life. But my experience at this restaurant was so atypical and wretched that I feel compelled to warn people not to go there and waste their money. In addition to poor quality food, what appalled me the most was the arrogant and indifferent attitudeof the manager.  I asked him if I could give him candid feedback and he said he was open to listening to me. He told me his wife was the chef. I very gently pointed out why the food was so poor in quality and quantity and he arrogantly replied that he had never had a complaint before but he would waive my opinion along with all the others he had received and that my opinion had no value because it was the only negative one he had received. My friend and I did not eat one bite of food after tasting the initial bite. Nor did we drink the cocktails. We paid and left. But my fellow New Yorkers and others, I beg you, avoid this place like the plague. What mean-spirited and rotten people and that coupled with bad food makes this place someplace everyone should avoid. I feel bad writing a review like this but I simply cannot lie and say that it's a decent place.
Ok...but not a place I would return to. Expected much more than just mediocre food.

Cheap and delicious Spanish food. The outdoor back area is a little cramped but the service is great. It's like $2 a taco so you can't go wrong. The hotdogs were super tasty as well. Definitely coming back.
Great sushi, especially the Firecracker, crazy, and bagel roll. A little pricey but worth it! Delivers as well and very quick with orders.

Jaysus. This place was rotten. Noodles which had clearly been in the microwave oven. Cheap, fatty pork. Beef which didn't really taste of any meat I've had before.  Very cheap and huge portions but I def won't go again.

One of the Best burgers I've ever had! Period!  And i love burgers and have had many. Fresh Angus beef, corned beef, bacon, blue cheese, lettuce tomatoes, good bun and good sweet potato fries. Reasonable price. 4 stars only because service a little on the slow side. But server was great. Just the cooking took a bit. The beer and liquor menu was enormous...from all over the world. I don't drink...but someone might want to know. Lol!

Been here a few times and I've always had a good time. It's a great place to meet up with friends or grab a table to the side if you want to talk. The beer selection is very large with 80 taps and the new menu is great. Loved the bartender Steve. He was very knowledgeable about the beers and made some good recommendations. My friends and I will be back!

Great place for a late night, drunken slice.  And now they offer buffalo chicken slices.  Awesome. Grinders aren't too bad either. Pizza is a little over priced and a little greasy, but still tasty.   Gyros are surprisingly good.    They get very busy at night, so don't expect quick delivery times.

Ok, I've eaten here and the oyster bar in grand central.  Grand Central is definately better, but given this one is in the Newark airport it's pretty good. Whenever I pass through Newark this is my lunch stop. The food is good, and traveling on business so the price doesn't scare me. I would recommend this for a business traveller looking for a decent me and a cold drink.

Dirty and over rated. I understand that an airport is not expected to have good seafood, however this was well below my expectations. Service was not an issue, although the staff was WAY over worked. One lady, whom I tipped very well, was taking care of the entire bar AND tables in the back. She was amazing. All the seafood, as expected was blah. Stay away from anything not on ice or very cold. The lobster roll meat was warm and had way too much stuff in it (green peppers, onions, seasoning) and was crumbly and dry. I could not finish it. The Oysters were okay, but could not finish them all as they were not cold. The ice on the Oysters was pretty much gone. When I commented to the waiter that they should cover the oysters w/ ice, they all but ignored me. You get what you get with this place. Beer on tap and McDonalds like seafood. Better off grabbing a sandwich at the farm to table place and people watch.
Great (pricey) beer, with a great (affordable) bakery!
Since they changed their head cook they became better than other Turkish restaurants in the city. If you don't want to spent a lot of money  ( PERA-Turkish Kitchen) same quality less price. Enjoy .

The pizza dough is delicious but the service is HORRIBLE. They never came to ask us how anything was. We had to ask for refills on water every time. They are so disorganized that we ordered a tartufo and never got charged for it. Rightfully so we should have gotten free dessert with the level of service. They also do not serve Ricotta on their White Pizza....whats that about?

I placed an order on GrubHub at 7:00 p.m. and got a delivery estimate of 8:15-8:25. At 9:00 I gave them a call asking where my order was. They told me they'd call me back in a few minutes. When they didn't bother to call me back, I called them again. Apparently there was something wrong with their Grubhub setup and they never got the order. They told me they'd refund my money. I was pretty upset at this point, because now it was 9:00 and ordering from somewhere else wasn't even an option anymore. I hadn't eaten since breakfast, I had an early exam the next day, and it was getting harder and harder to focus on anything I was reading because I was so hungry. It was also a shame because I've been looking for a good Indian restaurant in the New Brunswick are for some time, and after this experience I was sure I wouldn't give this place another chance. But the way they handled the situation changed my mind. The next day the manager, Lenny, called me to apologize and make sure my money would be refunded. He also offered to fill the order, free of charge, at a time and date of my choosing. I chose that night (I was still REALLY craving Indian food). Food was all really good, too - we had Paneer Tikka Masala, Palak Paneer, garlic naan, and gulab jamun. Everything was delicious. I might be wary of online delivery (a phone call directly to the restaurant is probably safer), but I would eat here again. And I was impressed by how classy they were in fixing this.

Yikes!!! Never again! My friend and I stopped at this Bar while waiting for my plane home. You have to already realize that it's going to be a bit pricey because it is a bar in the airport, but for the quality and quantity of the food, the prices were outrageous. The customer service was very poor, basically our waitress greeted us with "what do you want" slapped our food and drinks down and didn't come back to check on us. The food was awful! I ordered the popcorn shrimp and ended up getting some kind of sandwich popcorn shrimp and the waitress looked at me and said "that's what you ordered" nowhere on the menu did it was it was a sandwich with 3 pieces of popcorn shrimp in it. The shrimp was also, burnt and tasteless and very chewy! My friend had the claim chowder and she said it was "meh". I wish I would have read the reviews before spending $40 here on water and a meal! Not worth it! Eat in the food court!

I  heard about this  place ,because my coworker told me so, then me and my family decided to give a shot,  unfortunately, it turn out  have to give one star for  them, and a EXTREMELY  HORRIBLE experience in my life .      First of all, we talked about this  place  sanitation . when i were walking  the restaurant with my parents and my babe, i perceiving this place  so  old , older than u thought and also can smelled the rotten and water soaking carpet in the air. My boyfriend and I came her for dinner last week after hearing such great things about the restaurant. We can't disagree. Our food was delicious and the menu was great. Some of the appetizers were overpriced, but what do you expect in the city!

We had such a wonderful Saturday lunch at Giorgio on Pine. Before a show at the Kimmel Center, we walked over to Giorgio's-bringing 7 children with us. We received a warm welcome and delicious food, served thoughtfully and efficiently. The restaurant was very attentive to our concerns about food allergies. They specially prepared two items for my son, who is allergic to tree nuts. He loved the delicious food, and we all appreciated how the staff responded to our requests. Also, our server was masterful about communicating with the children. Thank you for a relaxing Saturday afternoon in the neighborhood. We're coming back for the pasta primavera, the gnocchi and the kale salad!

Madira's is the shining gem of Point Breeze!  This bottle shop + bar combo has one of the greatest beer lists I've seen on this side of Broad Street with 18 TAPS!  The prices were excellent: a PINT of Southern Tier's Pumpking for $7!  I cannot talk up the beer and liquor selection enough, not to mention the food.  Classics like cheesesteaks and wings grace the menu along with some Indian favorites. (The samosas and smoked cheddar saison fries were to die for!)   This is definitely my new go-to spot! In addition, the Wednesday night bartender has an amazing coat.

Most regrettable decision- I had read all of the previous poor reviews about the service and I still attempted to try them out- can't blame anyone else!! I had walked by this restaurant several times and found it to be a quaint looking little place. Yesterday was my one year wedding anniversary and I was looking for the perfect place to celebrate, nothing too big, nothing too bright, something with perfect ambience. So I made reservations at this restaurant and then proceeded to go to it a day or two in advance to check it out. They weren't open when I walked in but I felt that this could be a perfect spot for a romantic dinner and I knew the exact table that I wanted to sit at. Since no one was around I left and then I called them about an hour later- I told them that I had just been in the restaurant and would like to request a specific table for my one year anniversary and I would want to make sure that nothing went wrong. The gal assured me that we were "locked in" for the specific table that I asked for, considering it was for a Wednesday night and in all likelihood,  not busy. We started off we drinks at another location and proceeded to Russet for our reservations. The first thing I noticed upon entering was how bright the place was- they had their chandeliers on, as well as all of their overhead lights, it was brighter in there than mid day outside- lacked any sort of ambiance. Then I noticed, that although only 3 or 4 tables were occupied, one happened to be the one that I was assured of getting. The ignorant hostess then seats us at the least romantic table- large table set for 4 and crammed next to a group of cranky senior citizens. As she is taking us to this lousy table, I mentioned the table issue and my guarantee for the other table and she said she would go talk to her manager. She then disappeared for quite a bit of time- no waiter, no manager, no hostess- just left us sitting at this miserable table so that I could continue to get angrier. We finally got up and started to walk out when Miss Ignorance shows up to tell us that she made a mistake and didn't read the note on our reservations properly, blah, blah, blah.......mind you, there were only 3 or 4 tables occupied and even though a small restaurant, there was plenty of other tables for the other couple that got our table, and even a couple more small 2 person tables that she could have sat us at. I told her that she f'd up our dinner plans and walked out- after so many poor reviews on service, how are they in business?? We walked over to a wonderful restaurant on Walnut, where the mere mention of our anniversary gave them cause to take phenomenal care of us. One star because it won't let me give 0 stars!

Best pizza on Staten Island; has to be one of the best in NYC! Very tasty, with a perfect balance of tastiness in regards to the sauce and cheese! Even the appetizers and toppings are great! Don't forget, cash only, and no single slices.  Also, Ralph's Ices across the street when you're finished makes this a perfect summer treat!

I highly recommend take out or delivery. The service was awful! The waitress made it seem like an inconvenience to have anyone dine in. She yelled loudly at the other staff. Another customer walked in & she asked him if he'd like to move to a smaller table. He said no I'm okay & she told him he needed to move to smaller table. I just don't get how hard it is to be nice if you're going to work in this industry. I give 2 stars because the food came out fast & it was decent taste wise for the price.

Charming, bustling, cozy, neighborhood restaurant. The food is consistently delicious across the board. Wine list is great, drinks are great, desserts are great. Service is warm and inviting. The dining room had original art, but a homey feel to it. Just a very good, pleasant, warm dining experience.

Went to Sharkeys last night.The waitress was very nice so I thought 'great another good night at Sharkeys' I could not have been more wrong. First my daughter found s staple at the bottom of her drink. Then the food came and my burger was way over done and sour. The second one was overdone and the bacon was raw! Decided to try the soup and get wings to go.The soup was ok but when I got home and tried. the wings they were terrible right down to the watered down blue. cheese and the slivers of celery.They did take off one drink and the burger.Generous to a fault. NOT!! Then since everything took longer than I had expected I got a parking ticket!!! So a total of $115 for garbage.Do not spend your hard earned money here. But like I said at the beginning the waitress was nice!

I can't find a fault with this spot. Ambiance is classy and modern without being pretentious. Staff is down to earth, knowledgable and welcoming. The food is as local as possible. Meats from area farms. Delicious! The only reason we discovered this place was because they brought Chef Michael Fox on staff. His passion for food and pleasing customers shines through in his food. We'll continue to eat wherever he is cooking.

I have lived in the area for a few years and found this spot last week. A group of us sat at the bar and we had a great time with the bartenders, a girl and an Irish guy who were so funny and made us laugh all night! We had planned to just go for one drink for happy hour and ended up staying all night! We had a great time with some regulars too, who made us feel very welcomed! Happy Hour goes till 8, which is so great and rare! Get the Nocturnal cocktail! It is a gin and tea martini! Amazing! We had the fried pickles, lamb sliders, and 1.50 oysters. The decor is incredible. I am a designer myself and it is so obvious how well planned out the lighting and decor is. This place is definitely a hidden gem in Murray hill! Can't wait to go back and try their brunch menu out! I think they have live music on Wednesday and Thursday too in their speakeasy.
THREE WORDS. BACON .... INFUSED .... POPCORN. Hell yes. This place is finger lickin' good. No longer need to consume anything with sodium for the next twenty years but totally worth it.

I called today at 2:48 and made a reservation for 6pm - name, phone number provided and confirmed. No record of it when we arrived. Odd. Still, they had a table available and the people who followed us in had an extra 20% off coupon. Grateful for both. It took too long to receive menus, no offer of a drink, no bread when we were seated. My order of two apps instead of a main course was clarified by the waitress 10 minutes after she took it. Still, one app was delivered early - "so other servers wouldn't take it" Really would rather have eaten my meal WITH my husband. Took forever to receive my husband's entree and my other app. Asked for the check when the meal  was dellivered - had to ask again. When it came I asked the waiter to stay so we could give him our card and coupon, get the billl processed and be out quickly - nope, he vanished  before I could finish speaking. We trotted to The Bushnell and BARELY made it to the show on time. Husband's rib eye was on the rare side, but the portion was huge and flavorful so he was satisfied. Truffle fries were great. Lobster app was ok - surprisingly tough texture but tasty. Asparagras salad was lovely. The service really needs to improve. Watching other diner's frustration as curtain time approached added to the nerve wracking experience. Step it up - theater goers seem to be your main customers!
Good for lunches. Nothing exceptional but everything you need from a low maintenance lunch is there. Pizzas are good. Pastas not so much. Service was ok.
Our group waited in the rain for over an hour, without being seated.  The host simply continued to tell us "15 more minutes," until we finally had to leave.

Beautifully cooked and presented dishes with attentive service. Eggs Benedict was yummy and the unusual herb based Brunch cocktail just the ticket for a lazy Sunday holiday morning. Not the cheapest, but justified by combining cost of breakfast and dinner!

Great spot. The food is delicious!  Really well done. They had amazing complimentary bread with one meal I had. The mussels were awesome - delectable Asian inspired broth. Excellent beer selection. Great vibe, fantastic space.

Gross, chewy bread and racism served up hot. How can you have a sign that says, "This is America -  we speak English!" when your staff doesn't understand an order unless it's phrased "2 whiz wit!" Go to Jim's.
My vegetarian friends drag me here every once and a while.  It's a good place we can agree on.  I love the pancakes and assorted butter.  I like the vintage style.  Like walking into a old diner.

It's like a love hate relationship.  One day I love this place next day I hate it .. I totally can't tell you yelper to come or not...Reason being is who is serving me...   Hmmmmm. If you want domincan food come but if your looking for a setting/ambience Don't.......... DJ is great though..

I started ordering delivery from this place (when they delivered). The delivery always took 20 minutes or less.  I really like the chihuahua dog. The chipotle mayo and some kind of cheese topping make the taste perfect. The fries are pretty good too and you can chose from a bunch of dressings they have. You might need atleast 2 hot dogs for a meal as they are kind of small but really good, I have also tried the michigan dog which was fine too.

I have heard so many wonderful things about this place, but my fiancée and I were thoroughly disappointed.  Putting aside the high expectations, there were many issues. First, it took a long time for anyone to come and take a beverage order even though it wasn't busy.  That's fine, but then after we put in our orders the appetizers and entrees came out so fast we didn't have room on the table.  Second, anything that they claim is chimichurri is a half-assed version.  Half the ingredients are missing.  The "crispy pork" is crispy because it's been sitting and drying out.  We won't be coming back.
I love this place the food the atmosphere awesome I especially love the Churrasco  my go to favorite. Its really a special place.

Wow, great burger and Stuffed Burgers! Love the concept ie fast food made with some care and attention and made with real food. Nice ( but a bit scary ) touch adding the calorie values against the good. The fair Stuffed Burgers which has coffee in it is amazing! Hey it's a holiday a small indulgence is OK

This place is great for quick-serve healthy dining. I have been here several times (trying to make my way through the menu) and always leave feeling energized. So far I have tried the fish tacos (favorite) , balkan burger (love the slaw!), mahi curry (curry done right), basque shrimp (tons of flavor) and midtown chicken (excellent, filling salad). The dishes are well thought out and balanced. Highly recommend.
One of the few places you can get a gourmet meal after 11pm & find parking. I come for the salads but their brunch is good too! Try the Bloody Maria's !!!

Just went to Café Matisse for the first eime on recommendation of a friend.  Boy was she right; I took my wife for our anniversary; we both really enjoyed the excellent service and super elegant, well prepared food!  Wanted to sit out in the garden, but was getting chilly this time of year; got to return late next spring.  Portions weren't as big as I might have liked; but what we ate we sure enjoyed. Baked desserts were nicely done up, but didn't taste any better than the fresh baked at my local diner.  Brought our own special bottle of Italian primativo, and they were happy to open and serve it to us; even asked us questions about what we liked about it, and if we'd recommend it to others.  Will definitely return to Café Matisse; but only if I'm not so very hungry !

I'm probably biased because I lived in NY for most of my life & know what good Italian food is like. Bruno's is not it. The food, portions & service have gotten progressively worse in the last 5 years. The owners & adorable waitresses are great; but everything else leaves so much to be desired. The chicken parm hero is served on French bread!! The chicken cutlet is pancake thin & the sauce is worse than Ragu. Adding insult to my chicken parm injury is I actually called back!! The 1st time I was left on hold for 13 minutes. I should've known. Now I know I'll pay the $13 to go through the tunnel. Sorry Bruno's- I miss good Italian food.

Food is very good.....BUT servers are another story....there isn't an host so when you enter --you stand at door at least 5 mins  before someone acknowledges your presence.....girl at counter just does her work and doesn't look up....after being seated a menu is placed on table..no explanation or suggestion....2nd cup of coffee is hard to come by.  Kafe lacks ambiance and courtesy.....
The atmosphere and the food is amazing. The restaurant is decorated with beautiful lanterns and rustic elements. The food is  authentic thai dishes.

OK the food is good, but the service kills this place. The bartender and waitress just do not care or remember anything. It took 3 tries before we got our second round of drinks and I am a very patient person. Also had to literally chase the waitress down any time we needed anything and even then it was a 50 50 chance. This place needs a good staff and a manager that's paying attention immediately.

After hearing and reading rave reviews about the Boil, I had the pleasure of dining there last night and it did NOT disappoint! They seated us promptly although the restaurant was crowded.  They provided us with bibs and plastic gloves, which was a thoughtful gesture on their part because eating the meal can be quite messy. We ordered Catfish basket, Chicken Fingers basket and Southern Fried Chicken Wings appetizers.  They were all good, but the Catfish basket was, "slap yo' mama good!"  They were lightly battered and fried to perfection!  They were light and melted in your mouth!!!  The Catfish basket appetizer was out of this world!  I definitely will order the Catfish basket as an appetizer from now on.  The Southern Fried Chicken Wings were okay.  They were soo hot, they should have come with a caution, "do not handle while hot!"  The fork used to eat the chicken wings with melted, yes you read right melted! I dined on 2 lbs. of the most succulent Snow Crab Legs with an ear of corn and new potatoes served in "the Boil Special" sauce (a combination of garlic butter, Old Bay and Lemon Pepper sauces).  The sauce is thick and quite tasty.  My son dined on the combo of 1 lb. each Crawfish and Shrimp.  He shared some of his meal with me; the Crawfish and Shrimp were excellent! If you are looking for an authentic seafood experience, the Boil is the place to go!  I highly recommend it!

This place is by far one of the best local Chinese restaurants. Their food is fresh and tastes great. None of that sub par food here. I often do pick up and the food is always great. They have been around for decades and it definitely shows by the quality of food.
Delicious!

I see that a lot of people rave about this place. Sadly my experience wasn't so great.  First the surrounding area is a dump, but that can add to the charm... if the food is fabulous. Upon entering the restaurant, the dim lights and outdated decor seemed so gloomy. No tablecloths, cold tables, dated drop ceiling and ugly colored walls. It just didn't feel like an Italian restaurant should. I was hoping for something a bit more cheerful, perhaps some decor from Italy,  classy pictures, some plants & flowers..make it feel like I am in Tuscany.   Moving on, the waiter seem confused and it took him awhile to find himself.
