If, by some crazy chance, you have room for dessert after a freshly prepared lunch or dinner, there are plenty of places for dessert, including the oldest ice cream company in the US, Bassetts. It will be loud and crowded inside, but that offers a new adventure on every visit.

I got a delivery and ordered a large meat lovers, the pizza was very hot and fresh like it was just taken out of the oven, the delivery man was very friendly, the phone girl was also nice... I can't see myself ordering from another steak shop now that I've discovered this place... If your deciding where to order from then look no further cause this place is hands down the best place in the neighborhood !

I can't say enough about it.  From the wonderful, approachable host to the bathroom attendant, Trattoria Dell'Arte exceeded our expectations.  Everything was first class and excellent in quality.  Can't wait to go back to NYC and experience it again.

Went here yesterday and had a great lunch. My friends had the breakfast menu and I went for a main course - both great. Tea and coffee also great with a really helpful busboy who refilled out water glasses and coffee whenever we ran low! Annoyingly, the hostess had told us it was a 30 minute wait, but we actually ended up waiting well over an hour. It was 40 degrees outside so by the time we were eventually given a table we were frozen! A nice man (who I assume was the owner) was very apologetic though and did come out to tell us it wouldn't be long. Next time I'd have appreciated a more accurate time estimate from the beginning, as we probably wouldn't have even bothered had we been told it would be an hour. We only ended up staying because it became a case of 'we've waited so long if we leave now it'll all have been pointless'. Also, they only take cash, so make sure you have enough before you go in. Worst comes to worst, there's a chase ATM in the duane reade across the road.

I will say it's hard to miss this place with all the college kids buzzing by but be sure to stop for a burger. the people that worked there (one who toke my order and one who cooked it) were very friendly. burger came out perfect. I will be going back to try the different burgers on the menu. there are a lot of really good food trucks in that area but this one really stands out
beef pad thai!!! chang mai fries!!!

My brother n sister took us to this wonderful Chinese dumpling house. We tried the pork dumpling, Shanghai noodles, and fried rice. The dumpling reminded me of Din Tai Fung in Bellevue but...twice the size! The Shanghai noodles was delish. If you like spicy, I recommend add a little of the hot chili paste. I would like to come back again and try some of the other dishes.

Nothing appealed to me here. Everything we had on our table didn't taste right- it was either too spicy or flavorless. Wouldn't recommend this restaurant-I've had much better Asian fusion in the city. Staff was nice and the restaurant itself it nice looking but that's about it.

Great place for vegan food and breakfast especially. The service is good most of the time. But the food is a bit of a one trick pony. Think junk food for vegans. The wait is sometimes long for breakfast.

Im a fan of this spot! Great combination of Middle Eastern and Moroccan food, really everything they have is simply delicious. The new location in Williamsburg is amazing, you can see they put a lot of thought into the design- and its working!

This is a tiny restaurant with a big heart. Great food and ambiance with a twist. Spicy ketchup, outdoor seating and enclosed patio. Serves vegetarian and Moroccan specialties but also has wonderful breakfast served all day. Plus at a fair price. Good wait staff. I will go back.

Anyone who says this place is not outstanding is looking for the impossible.  This place time after time proves how genuine and good the food is.  Pizzas are always top notch, meals are great, grinders to die for.  Hit it right and get the Italian Wedding Soup, the best around, hands down.  I wouldn't go anywhere else.  Thanks Artie and John and the whole staff.  You are all the best!!!
Great Food, I tried the Chef's testing in dinner.
beer selection, tasty foods, golden girls or football on the TV's, nice owner...winning for south philly!

Was never impressed with Le Barricou. This place seems to be banking on the table cloths and aprons instead of really good food. I mean, it's not bad. But it's not the upscale dining they're pretending to be.

Had plans to go to dinner in Manhattan, but with all the protesting going me and my girlfriend decided to stay local and we could not be any happier.  The food was absolutely great! To start we ordered two apps, baked clams and the sea food salad.  Both apps were delicious, I only wish I ordered more! For the main course I ordered the Braciole and my girlfriend ordered the Osso Buco.  While my meal was very good, the Osso Buco was absolutely amazing! For dessert we had the Nutella gelato which was homemade and the brownie with fresh cream.  Once again we were impressed! The staff was also great, very friendly and helpful with the menu.  The Chef/Nonna that night even came out and walked around to the tables talking to the customers about their dinner. It was an overall great experience and I would recommend this place to anyone who is looking to enjoy a nice dinner.

We had a group of about 20 and everyone seemed to love it here! The food was delicious,especially the mini shepherds pie! It was a pleasure to work with Eddie who was our bartender/server. Overall we had a great party and we look forward to coming back for dinner and drinks
We didn't stay long enough to eat as our beers were warm and got a weird vibe off the very slow paced Christmas music being played in the bar
Awesome taste in their Good, beautiful presentation, Excellent service.. no needs saying anything else.

I've been working at a pizza shop for 13 years and have a bit of a pizza obsession. After finding Pizza Brain on tumbler, I decided for my birthday weekend to take a road trip down to Philly (from Boston) because this shop is everything I wish my mine was. 100% impressed with the food, service and atmosphere. Upon arrival, the owner asked if we had ever been before, I said, "No, actually, we just drove here from Boston... you're our first stop." He pulls out a megaphone from underneath the counter and announced it to the crowd. I think here may have been some cheering or clapping or laughter... not sure. I was caught off guard and probably turned bright red and awkward. But it was awesome and totally felt welcomed. Then they hooked us up with a variety of slices while we waited for our pie and showed us the lovely mural in the back. We spoke breifly about how he was excited we knew about the place, and how his dream was to make it on the map as a great tourist attraction. The pizza was awesome, better than I expected. I think one was pulled pork, and the other a dessert pie--which I was skeptical on, but ended up being my favorite. I think it had sliced apples and almonds with goat cheese?--SO GOOD. Spot-on ratios and crisp crust. I generally don't order white pizza, I like the sauce, but went with their recommendation and was not dissapointed. My friend, who was more in it for the adventure than the pizza, also agreed it was the best she ever had. Leftovers still good next day. Was kind of cramped inside, but there's also some outdoor seating. A table in a parking spot (I thought was a neat idea--would never fly in Boston). Plus there's a great ice cream shop next door we finished off at (I think they might be buddies), also great atmosphere with an eclectic selection. They seemed to share their dining spaces.   I don't actually remember the pricing... but whatever it was, totally worth it. You can see their excitement/love for pizza in the establisment and in the food. I'd make the trip again.

We had to wait for a table for 15 min but it was worth it. everything was healthy and delicious, I got the quinoa salad and my friend got the artichokes with chicken. The place had a great environment the entire night.

DELICIOUS! But 1st I want to thank FELICIA. Felicia, girl you made my day & hooked us up with a slammin wild salmon salad with your ovens made from God. Thank you for hooking us up & showing us a great time. The whole crew here is super friendly & so nice!!! Love this place. thanks girls. 1st time I've eaten a salad that good.

We've been there three times so far. Honestly, the worst reviews seem to be when Sanford's is PACKED and we haven't been there when it's been slammed. The food has been superlative all three times. Last time we went I had one of their organic burgers which was delicious and a much better value than the nearby Bareburger. High quality and fresh ingredients. The decor is nice, but if it were up to me, I'd have them take down the music a couple of notches, or this would be a five star review
Salads are good. Prices are good. Pesto lasagna was good but a bit too salty. The bread on the panini is hard and thin - more like a cracker.

Quite possibly, among the best pizza anywhere. I have been visiting for the past one decade, and am amazed by the consistently delicious pizza pies at Modern. It is comfortable for sitting in, and quite efficient for take-away as well. Although one cannot go wrong with the cheese and tomato pizza, the vegetarian pie is terrific. All in all, you cannot go wrong with the pizza here. Most highly recommended.

Decent food if you dine in. Order to go, and you're getting subpar quality. Obviously, the wait is crazy long for a table at dinner time, or really any time in the PM. Service is usually ok. Your best bet by far is to head straight to the bar area and eat your food there. Otherwise, you're basically required to get drunk in the backyard until your table is ready an hour later. still, decent pizza if you're dining in.
If you are late for your reservation, be prepared to suck it up and head to the bar and wait up to an hour for another table.
This is my fav in the neighborhood-always a good beat/pulse/vibe-very comfortable -perfect blend of intimate and lively-best staff-always enjoy myself there!

Love this place! Went there for a late breakfast sandwich today, and everything from the service to the sandwich was excellent. Magical moment: I saw their tantalizing treats (cookies and muffins galore!) and asked the owner if the cookies were chewy. He responded "not sure, let's see," took out a fresh cookie and broke off a piece for me! It was divine, so of course I bought a cookie too! It's a bit pricier for the area, and I hate to think of the impact that has on everyone's access to the yums, but it's not super pricey. For the service and quality, I say yes all the way. And for those interested in neighborhood politics, they have a diverse staff. Bam! 5 stars

I feel like I just wasted $15 on lunch. I ordered the lunch red chicken curry, and it came with wonton soup. The wonton soup was great- the broth was flavorful despite being a touch salty, and the wontons were delicious. The red curry chicken- well that's a whole other story. The curry sauce was a really weird consistency- almost gelatinous, and while it was spicy, didn't have a great flavor. The chicken in it was also weird- it had a funky texture, and zero taste. There was also some green peppers, potatoes (very gummy), and eggplant. I wouldn't order Thai here again. Definitely don't get the impression it's authentic. Based on the wonton soup, if I ever gave this place a second try I might stick to the Chinese.
nice food on a rainy lonely day.

Talulas Garden is everything an exceptional restaurant should be and more! We managed to get a last minute reservation for 4 for Sunday brunch and inside the place was buzzing, but in no way felt crowded or rushed. The interior is a polished blend of designer "earthy" elegance. It's interesting, inviting and alluring all at once. The service was superb from the moment we arrived. The brunch menu was inventive, artistic - and WOW was it ever delicious. The flavors jump off the plate to surprise and delight - and without exaggeration - leave you begging for more. The outside courtyard garden is a rare jewel in a vast city, and we look forward to coming back in season to enjoy an al fresco experience Talula style. The valet parking service was an unexpected bonus, and after lunch, as our car was being retrieved we walked next door to 'Talulas Daily' for a peek, but that's a story for another day!!!

Fried calamari was really good there is seating outdoors which I would've loved if it was summer time so I may need to visit again in warmer weather Food is really cheap and still tastes good Waiter was ok

Went here on a Sunday night at 6 pm. There were a few available tables but by the time we left at 8 pm all the seats were taken. We tried 4 appetizers, Ribs, Meatball Sliders, Chicken wings and Mussels. The winner of the group were the Ribs and Mussels, The ribs fell off the bone and the sauce for the mussels was great for dipping. For dinner we had the Steak, Salmon and Linguine with clam sauce. All portions were nice and the food was extremely tasty. Service throughout was attentive and very informative. For desserts we had Skillet brownie (excellent!) flour-less chocolate cake ( decadent) and tray of cookies. Butter cookies were good but chocolate chip cookies were way too hard. Overall ambiance is great, noise level a little high, but prices, portions and variety make this lace a definite repeat

Being from out of town and only in the city for one night, we decided we just HAD to try Lombardi's after carefully researching which pizzeria was THE pizza joint to go to while in New York City we decided on Lombardi's.  & Since it's the first pizzeria in America....we said YES, TO LOMBARDI'S WE WILL TRAVEL. Unfortunately we got there fifteen minutes before closing time and we weren't given the option to dine-in. So reader beware, don't think you can get your late-night pre-game grub on at Lombardi's. We then decided on take-out, but were informed that if we decide on this option we would not be allowed to sit in the restaurant at all to eat the pizza. While this totally understandable, it added to disappointment in our experience. The servers were generally nice and kindly took our pizza order, but I can't say anything beyond that for service. Also, I didn't like that in order to get a pizza from here you had to a buy a whole pizza...so if you just want a slice. No yeah, don't come here unless you're splitting it between friends. When we finally received our pizza and were able to find a nice and relatively warm and dry place to eat it on the streets of New York, we weren't too impressed. While the quality and authenticity of the pizza is definitely present, it's not to die for. It's not something I would go out of my way to get to again. I think that this place is overhyped, but if you follow the food movements (which I won't even lie I do myself) then definitely stop by and see for yourself, but as for me? You probably won't find me coming to Lombardi's next time I'm visiting New York City.
Amanda! It is all about Amanda. All. Of. It. She rules and drools, and spools spaghetti around a fork, and pools wine in your glass. She is an Inhuman superhuman.
Love this place! Great atmosphere great service and awesome food :) authentic Italian food best meatballs I ever had!!! Love this place

My favorite cuisine is Thai -- If I could, I would have Thai food with its richly flavorful variety of curries and noodle dishes every day! A friend introduced me to Bodhi Tree. Happy Hour provided the perfect opportunity to sample the appetizers which were all excellent! It was however, the shrimp drunken noodles and the chicken satay that won me over. The chicken was tender and moist. The drunken noodles are addictive, and I will admit to go through a phase when I visited the restaurant for its drunken noodle dish at least twice weekly! It is a great place to unwind during happy hour or catch up with a friend or two over dinner. Any discerning fan of Thai cuisine will love the food here! Highly recommended. Rating 4.5 stars
Nice ambience, but the food is a total disaster. My grilled cheese looked terrible and tasted worse. The soup was most likely poured from a Campbell coup can. Don't eat at this craphole dump.
I really enjoyed the creative dishes and drinks. This place offered an excellent atmosphere, and I would totally recommend.

My boyfriend and I stumbled upon Cheeky when I was waiting for a bus, and I think we must have had good karma because this place blessed us. I don't think any better biscuits can be found anywhere in New York (or possibly anywhere, period). The service was fantastic - so friendly and quick. I would come all the way down from Harlem just for the egg and muenster biscuit I had this morning, no question. AND THE BEIGNETS. Probably gonna dream about them, to be honest. Appreciated the NOLA vibes being from a half southern fam. We can't wait to come back to try a po boy--or anything else on the menu, really.

Went for dinner last night with my husband and son and everything was DELICIOUS. Service was great. I hope I never run into the rude staff that people talk about in other reviews.. Our waiters were so friendly. Great samosas, chicken makhani and garlic naan was AMAZING.

I went to this restaurant owing to all the positive reviews on yelp. It came out a bit disappointing. The interior decor is well but the food is mediocre comparing to the price. Dan Dan noodle, as everyone comments, tastes authentic and flavorful. But the double cooked pork belly and leek lamb and mushroom bok Choy all swim in black soy sauce and oil, which r quite greasy. If u prefer light-oil Chinese food with reasonable price, pick up a another restaurant..

The ricotta pancakes and the Moroccan scramble looked to be the favorites so I got the scramble. It was light, flavorful, and delicious. The avocado and chick peas were a delicious addition. Although the pancakes looked amazing I rarely saw anyone finish because they were so enormous. I had no problem finishing my entire plate.
Get the skirt steak sandwich.

Please get on Seamless already! This gets 5 stars if you go there, and 2 stars if you order delivery.   The bad:  delivery takes forever and they have at least twice lost the order.  Sad panda face. The good:  the soup dumplings.  The crab and pork soup dumplings.  Happy panda face.  If it's winter, get a table away from the door.  I don't know why, but so many times it seems that the door stays open without closing.

The diner's diner. Tops is what a diner should be. This East Newark restaurant can be a hassle to get to, but if you make it you will be rewarded with a delicious meal as your trophy. Tops diner has a gargantuan  selection of meals. There is something for everyone. Though other diners are a bit cheaper in price, Tops is relatively inexpensive. I recommend the Waldorf salad (if you want to be a good and healthy diner). The Waldorf is a sensual mix of flavours and texture. The mayonnaise dressing that covers the salad is refreshing and zesty. Also, the fruits and vegetables in the Waldorf are ever so fresh. For naughty diners, Tops' Bacon cheeseburger is to die for (ironically, it may kill you due to the plethora of bacon). The ground beef is cooked to perfection and dressed with fresh fixings. The bacon is so savory and crispy that you will squeal for joy when it hits your taste buds. Tops is alway filled to the rafters, so expect to wait for 45 minutes minimum. Also, parking is very challenging. Tops is a must dine dinner!

Stopped in for a quick dinner. We ordered two sandwiches and a smoothie. While the food was very messy, it was also very good! The service was great and fast as well! Definitely a good place if you need a quick bite in the Financial District (they have some ready to go juices and salads as well)!

Great food at great prices but the service is horrible. I return here every now and then only for the food. The food gets 4 stars and service gets 1. If you don't care about service you will enjoy the restaurant, but if service is important to you, steer clear.
Alyssa was amazing ad was the food can't wait to come back.The ultimate bertuccis was great hot and crisp the roasted veggies and bruschetta amazing the 0 I cat a fantastico.
Hands down the best pizza in New York. You also have to try the desserts. The cannoli is the best I've ever had.

If I have -only one week in NYC I'd eat at Ippudo at least 4-5 times out of 7! That's how friken good the ramen is. Westside is a  little tamer than east side. Food is the same :) awesomely amazing!!!

I've been to xiandu twice so far and have really enjoyed it!! It's a great BYOB and the servers are all super friendly. I absolutely love the aesthetic inside. The first time I had the angry beef, done medium, and it was super tasty. The second time I had spicy beef pad Thai and it was fabulous. The price is very reasonable for the friendly service and great food. After dinner my friends and I had some desert. It was delicious creme brûlée  and also fried green tea ice cream. I hope this place sticks around because I'll be back!

ジョルジオ アルマーニアイウェアからブランドサングラス偽物 　　ジョルジオ アルマーニスーパーコピーについてブランド模倣専門店でようこそ。ジョルジオ アルマーニ アイウェアの新作は、完璧なフォルムをもつ木製のアイウェア。激安ブランド通販、カナレットクルミ材を用い­て、職人の技で仕上げられたアイウェアは、クリーンでアイコニックなフロントシェイプを作り上げている。繊­細さが感じられるなので、超軽量といった魅了する。天然のクルミ材を使ったジョルジオ アルマーニサングラスが洗練さをアピールし、コインのエッジのような手彫り装飾がほどこされている。 　　新作のラウンド型ァティカルフレームは、2.6ミリメートルの厚さのフロントや、ネジなしで専用に設計され­たチタンヒンジなど、フレームを15グラムにするまでの軽量化に成功。柔軟性と軽さを両立させている。繊細­で洗練されたシェイプと、リム?レンズやゴールドトリムなどのァ￡ジナルのディテールは、現代的でラグジュ­アリーな雰囲気を醸し出す。 テクノロジーとデザインが見事に融合しながら、そこはかとなく漂うレトロ感に、さらなる偽ジョルジオ アルマーニの可能性を感じる。まさしく、ブランドを象徴するコレクションと言えるだろう。 　　ブランドサングラス偽物を激安でァライン販売している。7hhk----com  大ヒットなジョルジオ アルマーニ偽物、バーバリー偽物などブランドアイウェアも人気通販。

I tried this place for the first time two weeks ago and it was a pleasant surprise. The food was tasty and fresh. The place is well kept as well. There is definitely some room for improvement with the service. I would definitely go there again recommend this place to anyone looking for tasty south Indian food.

I ordered regular pulled pork sandwich, mac and cheese and green beans.   Pros: Service was fast. Cons: Mac and cheese and green beans were bland.  They were out of collard greens, so I got green beans instead. I had an issue with the pulled pork.  It was pinkish inside and had a funny aftertaste, similar to not being fully cooked. I tried my friend's pulled pork from his entree and it tasted better, i.e. the meat wasn't pinkish and no aftertaste.  He took it to the counter to tell them it wasn't fully cooked and was told all their meats are cooked 14 hours.  He came back and traded his pulled pork with mine. I think his pulled pork was fully cooked. Tables weren't wiped down immediately after patrons left.  I noticed this while waiting for another person in our party to arrive, which was about 7 minutes.  There were a few tables in this group which could have used cleaning and had been empty. We took a table in this group and wiped the crumbs off. Wait staff need training on better customer service skills-friendly greeting, eye contact, thank you, problem resolution, etc.  I will perhaps return in the Spring.
Great place,food delicious but portions HUGE. Meals are based on family sharing and we ordered too much.lasagne like huge cake. Food delicious,staff attentive, prices OK atmosphere great.

Love this place. The food the atmosphere. Amazing. Been here a few times. Unfortunately this review is not for he restaurant but for the hostess. She told me that I didn't hear my name called because "Maybe I should open up my ears". After waiting an hour for a table. And continues to wait afterwards. Not ok to talk to your customer that way.
Awesome food but what's more outstanding is their service and attention to detail. My team and I had a great dining experience.
I no longer have to wait for my neighbor to make me Chicken Biryani...Love this place

The food at snack is a selection of popular Greek dishes. The appetizer tray is good as is the Greek salad. We were underwhelmed with the main courses. There are 4-5 tables here so it's sometimes hard to get seated.

Food at Ivy Noodle is quite good. The soup dishes are excellent and the noodle entrees very flavorful and filling. The appetizers are uneven -- some are good but others quite lacking in flavor. All in all, an affordable and reliable casual dining option.

Our second visit with a family group, and the combination of food and service is excellent. Specializing in panini with a wide variety of pork meats, this deli turned restaurant is small but well worth the visit. Good wine and beer list. Access by subway or cab is preferred, as street parking is tight. Highly recommended.

This place is the real deal -- inspired combinations of fillings on perfect panini bread. Add to that excellent salads, a well-curated selection of wines, and best-in-breed coffee-house desserts. And keep your eyes out for the special sandwhiches of the day -- don't pass on any with fresh chicken livers or their tuna. My 1 detraction would be to pass on the meat/cheese plates. the quality is there but the portions seemed small. You're better off splitting the carpaccio salad or losing yourself in the decadently rich tuna-stuffed-tomato before your panini or, better, your crostini. bon appetite.

The food at this place was so so good. I ordered the Steak and Eggs which comes with home fries, multigrain toast, and this amazing spinach cream. The home fries were nicely seasoned and the spinach cream was great to dip the potatoes into. The mimosa was made with fresh orange juice so it was especially good. My only qualm was after we were seated the hostess told us brunch was over and needed to be ordered within the next 10 minutes. No one came to our table to greet us or take our order for about 10 minutes but we were still able to order brunch. Highly recommend this place for brunch!

Inexpensive meal with, quick, friendly service - don't let the line deter you! I had the gyro sandwich and my friend had the chicken/gyro plate over rice. They were both incredibly delicious - flavorful and well-spiced. The white sauce is epic. Cash only.

We had the whole Sea Bass,which I would absolutely recommend. The service was fantastic and the Christmas decorations made it very cozy. Only thing I would change would to be make it a tad brighter, as we had difficulty reading our menus.

t's very small but in a cosy way that was just perfect. Lovely staff and the food was amazing. Hot food, which in a country where the food is mostly cold before it gets to your table says a lot!!! Highly recommend.

We ordered a spinach omelette and a white cream chicken mushroom crepe.(I forgot those names exactly) It was so tasty. The white cream was rich and the omlette was soft. I really recommend it. We didn't order drinks, therefore paid only ＄26 for them including tip. I'd like to go there again.

Literally the best thing I've ever put in my mouth. Oh my god. I got the Battle Royale burger and it was so impressive and delicious, the seasoning was flawless and the sauces on the side were also really really good. The fries were good I just wish they were thicker and I also wish the place wasnt so expensive :( $15 for a burger is so much. The service was also really good, my waiter was super nice and the food was out really quick.
If I'm ever on Death Row and they allow me to choose my last meal, it will be the Truffle Burger.

This review is its first location in Chelsea before they moved. One of my favorite Thai spots in the world. Food is always on point, portions are generous, drinks are creative and delicious, and prices are very reasonable. Definitely recommend and can't wait to check out the new location.

Came here for the first time with my daughter last night looking for an alternative to eating Pho at the Lemongrass. We were greeted by an attentive staff who understood the menu and made positive recommendations. We started with the Spring rolls which included both fresh lettuce leaves and fresh mint which added a nice flavor twist. The Spring rolls were delicious and tasted just like the ones I make at home. Our waiter commented that it is a tedious job, but they make them at the restaurant daily. As a main dish, I had the combination pho while my daughter had the pho tai nam. She wanted to try the grilled pork w vermicelli noodle dish also, but knew having both pho and vermicelli w pork would be too filling. So our waiter recommended that she order a side of the grilled pork. It was an excellent and tasty suggestion. The broth was absolutely amazing! And, as any pho gourmand knows, the main ingredient for any successful pho restaurant is the broth. I've tried pho at restaurants around the country and in Thailand, and this broth ranks at or near the top. At the end of our meal, "T", the owner, joined us to request our comments. T mentioned that he recently hired a new head chef and that the dishes had improved. I couldn't agree more! Although the ambience and decor doesn't meet the standards of the Lemongrass, if your in the mood for great pho, this is the place to go. Oh, and they also serve Vietnamese hot pot which I'll be sure to try the next time I visit!

How I heard of this place: We were up in West Chester, PA, briefly, and decided we had to visit with our good friend Samyar before the long traffic-entrentched road trip back to Arlington. Wanting to sample some good ol' Philly Cheesesteak, Samyar recommended one of the two best in Philly: Geno's. So, we made our way to the bright orange, neon signs that made Geno's easily seen from any direction. Type of cuisine: "Geno's Steaks was started by Joe Vento back in 1966. He figured that if he was going to sell a steak, he had to be where they were already eating them...at the "X" shaped intersection of 9th & Passyunk in South Philadelphia. Joe learned the cheese steak business from his father who in the early 1940's opened "Jim's Steaks". In 1966, Joe started "Geno's" with $6.00 in his pocket, 2 boxes of steaks and some hot dogs." According to their website, "The ingredients are simple, exacting and never greasy thinly sliced rib-eye steak, melted cheese, oven-fresh baked bread and delicately grilled onions. Awaiting your piping hot sandwich on the counter outside are ketchup, mustard, relish and Joe's choice hot sauce." Ambiance: Good thing we were warned while standing in the street, in line for our orders. Samyar let us know that we say, "One with...(fill in the blank with type of cheese between Provolone, American or Cheese Whiz) and with onions (or without)." Writing this, now, I also see that Geno's has also enlighted it's website readers, "Be prepared and know how to order, because the service is fast and the line keeps moving. For example, on a cheese steak with onions, specifiy which kind of cheese you'd like. By the time you have given your order, your money will be taken and your sandwich will e out the window nice and hot! At the next window you can pick up your soda, fries and coffee." This is no joke! Walking up to the eccentric, slightly overboard signage denoting Geno's from blocks away, over the fenced field housing a community garden, one is immediately inundated with orange. The chest-height, glossy, orange-tiled walls with a blue-tiled stripe, the awning overhead noting: "Geno's Welcomes You!" and the orange, plastic picnic tables attached to metallic pillars with an orange cover cannot go unnoticed. While there is no indoor dining, these casual tables find themselves under a canopy on the sidewalk "for those who wish to enjoy sandwiches on the premises rather than drive off with them". The condiment bar, a large, chest-height, metal box with an opening on the side facing the order windows, offers Cherry Peppers, Ketchup, Mustard and Relish. Large, locked, glass display cases include badges which ornamented civil service members throughout the years. Everywhere from the walls above the orange tiles to the ceiling can be seen such memorabilia, including plaques in memory and honor of. A Path of Honor lays the foundation in the brick tile-work that leads to the ordering windows from the street corner, in between orange horse-heads set atop metal pillars chained to one another. As we watch, hawk-eyed for a spot at the orange tables, we find one at the far end, closest to the ordering line, and snag it while no one else is paying attention. At the table, on the table, we see numerous photographs, set like a collage, underneath a thick, plexi-glass table surface. Our sandwiches, wrapped in wax paper with the Geno's logo, immediately in front of us, awaiting the first bite. What I ordered: I ordered "One with Provolone and onions." Chris seconded. Samyar selected "One with American and onions." (Each sandwich: Price $8.33, Tax $0.67, Total: $9.) At the next window, we also placed two orders for Cheese Fries ($4.60 plus $0.40 tax, for a total of $5), a rounded container of thin-cut fries drenched in Cheese Whiz. What I loved: I loved the cherry peppers at the condiment bar, fluffy, juicy and just spicy enough to give a kick, without numbing your taste buds. I also loved the relish, surprisingly. I have never been a fan of relish, especially store-bought, pre-packaged. This relish had larger cut pickles and less of a sweet flavor. I enjoyed the salty, tangy taste of the pickles with the otherwise, slightly dry sandwich. Why I loved it: The bright orange, the casual atmosphere, the large bikers with tattoos the size of my head on each arm working the kitchen line and the scruff woman at the register snapping our orders across the room behind the plexiglass separating us from them, inside. Cost: High ($9 per sandwich, sides extra)
Overpriced. Paid $7 for a small chicken salad sandwich that came with nothing but an under brined pickle.

Don't usually write reviews but I had such a great experience I felt the need to share. I will keep it short since I don't always do this. Service is excellent from all staff. Always friendly and welcoming. I used to live in Miami and this the some of the best Cuban cuisine I've had since going to some of my favorite restaurants on calle ocho. I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for authentic Cuban cuisine and great service.

WAYYY overpriced for what it was... the spot is lovely, very romantic and cute, probably better for a glass of wine and an appetizer. but definitely NOT for a dinner... went with a group of friends for an after work dinner and wine.. the food was terribly mediocre, and the entree portions were way too small for the price. ended up leaving hungry and with a big hole in our pocket! totally NOT worth it...

I've lived on 2nd ave for years and finally came here. I was pleasantly surprised!  The service is good and the food is even better. The  polenta tartufata was great. I would also suggest to order Gnocchi Di Ricotta and Uva's variation of mac n cheese. Also the pizza is very tasty. The prices are moderate and in the summer The poutdoor seating is a perk

Affordable, delicious, and convenient.  I could eat their breakfast sandwiches literally every day for the rest of my life.  They also have great beer selection.  The people who work there are very cool as well.
friendly staff, aaaaawesome food ! there charcuterie plate is very good, and the flatbread pizza is a 10/10 !
This is my go to Mexican spot in the LES. Vegetarians love it here too. Expect a wait, but its worth it.

I say 3.5 stars.  Rocked their brunch; Food-Good, Beer-Good, Service-Horrendous. Sorry to Say, and that is the same feel we as groups received at their sister location Sunswick.  Something left to be desired.

Do it. Great place to take friends or a casual date. Nice and cozy decor, relaxed vibe, tasty food, and surprisingly inexpensive considering the portion sizes. If you live in the area (as I do), this will definitely be one of your go-to neighborhood spots. I recommend the chicken empanadas as an appetizer. Great flavor, nice size, and only $2! As far as the rest of the menu, I've eaten here on several occasions and ordered something different each time...I've yet to be disappointed :)

AMAZING food is delicious, ambiance is young, vibrant, upscale and fund one of my favorite dishes in the world-Dátiles con Beicon 7 Dates stuffed with almonds and Valdeón, wrapped in bacon make a reservation and GO!!!! kitchen closes around 10:30/11 pm
Blows all the diners pancakes out of the water, everything is home made down to the ketchup. A must check out!!!!!!

The staff really needs to work on their attitude and to stop talking French behind customers' back. The whole experience was ruined by the blonde lady that can't stop talking and laughing in French with the other staff while taking our orders. We had to wait for.her laugh to finish to continue ordering. To call it rude is an understatement. I called and talked with the manager and really hope she got disciplined. Definitely not coming back here.
Beet Salad was fresh and wonderful!  Pizza was amazing. They have sandwiches as well and daily specials. The service was really attentive, especially Sean!!  Love local places.

Upon arrival,I was a bit intimidated by the long line that reached all the way to the entry.Quite impressive that our group of five was seated within 10 minutes.This a bustling restaurant with efficient, somewhat hurried service. We ordered french toast, eggs benedict, and a couple of omelets. Everyone was happy with their selections. Even the eggs benedict where "just right". The decor and location is attractive and convenient to Newark. I would return here for breakfast.

We were on the lookout for a good place for breakfast pancakes and Harvest Table didn't disappoint. It's in a popular location for sure, but it's quite big so even mid-morning we got a table without having to queue. Pancakes and orange juice were duly ordered. The service was polite but perhaps a little slower than we'd expect. The food was delicious and we couldn't fault anything else.

A wonderful experience all around! The restaurant has an amazing atmosphere and the food is beyond delicious. I especially recommend the oysters! Loved going for drinks after dinner in the neighborhood but could have stayed at County all night. It is the kind of place where you want to spend your entire evening, taking your time enjoying each dish and the company of the ones you are with.

Would have given this place a 1 if my crab cake wasn't good. THE WINGS ARE HORRIBLE!! By far the driest wings I have ever had in my whole life!!! Boyfriend ordered a buffalo chicken cheese steak and it was just average for what he paid. We got two sandwhiches and no alcohol and paid over $50 bucks for this meal. Save your money- you can get better food at a diner.
The food is good. Waiting time is long. On Sunday the place was packed.  Set of 5 shots of home made vodka is recommended. I'd like to recommend to my friends.

i always love a place that serves eggs benedict on days other than saturday and sunday.  at first i was a little disappointed that they didn't have eggs benedict with a type of meat (canadian bacon, bacon, ham) on the menu, so i settled for the smoked salmon benedict.  i was a little skeptical at first because i've tried smoked salmon benedict and i wasn't really a fan.  however, it was so good, i devoured all of it (i almost never finish my food.) if you love eggs benedict, i suggest you try it here! i've eaten many eggs benedicts from different places and this is one of the best! the only problem i had was that there was a weird stench, it was some type of wet towel smell lingering throughout the restaurant that bothered me. besides that everything else was good!

I almost don't want to write this review so I can have Emily all to myself! It's my happy place. Food: The Colony (red sauce, cheese, pepperoni, pickled chili's and honey) is AMAZING. I could easily eat this everyday. Their other pies are good too, but it's hard not to just get the colony every time. My bf and I get a pizza and then something else (app, pasta, etc) every time and it's a perfect meal. There pastas are great too, they frequently change em up so be sure to check them out. Drinks: Great. Love the goodybags... Some kind of amaretto, bourbon and egg white concoction that is just right. Atmosphere: Perfection. On a Friday night expect to hear our neighborhood boy Biggie and the like. Some nights is indie, equally great. Staff: Totally awesome, everyone's really friendly. Overall: I'm happy to go every weekend and unwind with great food, drinks, music and awesome staff. It's a perfect way to end the hectic work week.

Amazing food! I went with a friend and had one of their daily specials with seafood and red sauce. It was out of this world. The portion lasted me for the next day's lunch. Nice, friendly stuff. Overall good experience. Will go back and would recommend it to friends.

Went there for lunch. Service and decoration is good. Tried one tasting menu. Ingredients is very fresh. Like the dessert with the tasting menu. Also tried a lamb entree and a pasta appetizer. Lamb is perfect, but the pasta is so salty and even worse than some normal restaurant. Pasta is a mess, and shouldn't be on the menu. But overall the food is good and tasty.
Favorite pizza place. Hands down. Price per slice is expensive but one artichoke slice is filling. Their new vodka slice is also damn good.

I had a great time at this cracker barrel! The young man who seated me went out of his way to make sure i was at a nice table. The server christine was delightful, the food was tasty and plentiful, and the atmosphere was welcoming. A very nice place to eat if you are solo. They had a cozy fireplace and coffee that was so good i could drink it black. I misplaced my phone in the giftshop and everyone, including the manager, went out of their way to help me find it. This is a place i would bring my mom to. Thank you for a pleasant lunch!

On our first trip to Philadelphia, we were delighted by the restaurant scene.  There are so many fine small restaurants seemingly scattered around every neighborhood.  After two evenings of delicious meals, we were excited to go to a well known, popular  restaurant-even Anthony Bourdain gave it praise.   Our experience here, to say the least, was extremely disappointing.  Maybe they had an off night but I have my doubts about that-the quality of the cooking was so poor that I can't even see this being acceptable on a good night.  I'm not sure what all the fuss is about-I can see that people do like this place. Here's what we ate: Hummus foul-overwhelmed by salt, drenched in oil.  Perhaps we didn' realize that the foul was an English description rather than middle eastern name. Crispy grape leaves with ground beef, tomato and Harissa. Some nice ingredients in the description.  Some of the grape leaf flavor was detectable, however, the dish was overwhelmed by the oil it was sautéed/fried in. It almost seems like they're reusing the oil for multiple dishes. And like all the dishes, highly salted. Pastilla-Lamb neck, apples, horseradish, walnuts Lamb neck-meat rolled in a flat bread, sautéed/fried and served with hummus.  This is the most disappointing of the dishes I ordered. As with the crispy grape leaves dish, the oil and salt dominated making this a one dimensional dish.  Nice idea, terrible execution. Branzino with apple tzatziki Salty and boring.   Chicken kebab This probably was the worst of the bunch. Rubber consistency, salty, gas grill flavor.

Rude and slow waitress, terrible drinks (4 out of 5 I tried I couldn't take more than one or two sips, the other tasted like a decent Manhattan), so dark a bunch of twenty-somethings needed a flashlight to read the menu, and drinks priced from $14-$16. I would never recommend this place to anyone. Ever.

This market is great and has so much to choose from. I just wish I had a cooler to buy things to bring home with me. I ate a small bite at multiple establishments in the market and was not disappointed. They even h a different a muffletta as good as new Orleans!
Even though I live in Denver now, I never miss an opportunity to visit RTM when I'm home in Philly. It's one of my favorite places in the city - if only there was one here!
Lychee martini's are where its at. Always a great happy hour spot.
Delicious good and great customer service. A must stop for anyone who's hungry and in the area!

Okay so we stumbled across this. Stalled before going in to see a menu (from outside looked rundown). Was impressed with seeing inside. A lot bigger than first thought. Clean and tidy with a dated look. Was offered warm rolls to begin with from a basket. Food was amazing. We had burgers, pasta and chicken pie. We all cleared our plates. We also had deserts, wine and soda. The bill for 4 of us was only about £60! Bargain :)
The staff is incredibly nice, the ambience is cozy and fun, and the guacamole is out of this world. Carino is one of the most consistently delicious restaurants on the south side.
Excellent food

Simple perfection, made with love, great service.... Had brunch, came back later to eat again. Always a nice crowd, people laughing, having a great time. Sit at the bar if Chris is bartending, Teresa is also a great server... Just good people with great hearts, an eye for detail, and amazing charisma. All around an excellent experience. Try the Dutch baby pancakes.... The burger... And work through the drink menu... All of it.

Minca rocks! Order the Minca Charshu ramen and leave satisfied.  Try the radish salad and drink iced tea, not water.  In NYC, Minca is the best ramen house I've tried.  Go for lunch or during off peak dinner hours to avoid a line and a crowd.  When I went today for lunch, it was only half full and the service and ramen was spectacular.
Great food.
Had pepperoni slices and they were extremly greasy.... would not recommend or return to this location

This restaurant was listed under top restaurants with fireplaces. The weather was rainy,cold, and miserable so a warm cozy fire was exactly what we needed.   The atmosphere rocked. Appropriately dim and warm. The seasonal holiday decor was full of spirit and added to the dining experience. The hostess was genuinely welcoming and helpful which I loved, really set the tone for the rest of the meal. My boyfriend got a burger which was huge and filling. I got the open face hot turkey special which was DELICIOUS and hearty. The beer list is extensive, also lots of great drafts. We ordered the holiday beer flight which was perfect. My server ( platinum blonde female, I forget her name sorry :-/ ) was also super awesome, personable, and on point through out service. She even maintained service after we paid which I loved, didn't feel rushed. As a waitress employed at a competing restaurant in the neighborhood, i don't typically yelp because there are so many self Righteous jerks complaining about anything their lame brain can gather--- however praise when praise is due, I will absolutely be back devils den. I tried again to give these guys a chance.. I called to see how late they deliver (because in the past they sometimes don't answer the phone).  Someone answered the phone by coughing.. Pretty good Mexican tacos for NYC standards. The service is pretty fast. But the location is small so there isn't too much room to sit down especially during lunch time..

The food is very similar with my home made ones, the north home made. I like the BBQ lamb and squid, and also the hot pan is very delicious. The people there are warm and friendly. It is a very good place to go.
Hands down best place I have eaten in years.  The food and wine list...the ambiance.  Wow...home run!

We read some reviews and decided this was the place to grab a quick dinner on a lazy night. One said the General Tso's was particularly good and it is our favorite, so we were excited. Royal Palace not so Royal! Where's the flavor? Ordered sweet and sour chicken, sesame chicken, chicken fried rice and egg drop soup. We were informed that nothing came with the main entree. Come to find out white rice came with it. Additionally, we received a side of steamed broccoli. The sweet and sour sauce was thin and less than flavorful. The sesame chicken had no heat to it at all. Got the Hawaiian pizza but had them put BBQ on it, it was quite good. No complaints other then the crust was boring and dry. Noting close to the NY pizza I'm used to but it was a huge step up from Dominos for sure. I also got the bread sticks and they were good, though a bit too salty for me. The marinara dip it came with was great and the delivery of the food was quick and painless. They called upon delivery as I requested, I would give it a 3 1/2 out of 4 stars. The food may be good but the service is HORRENDOUS. I dined here with friends recently and we made a reservation. We showed up to find that making a reservation is useless. They had no table for us and asked if we would mind squeezing onto a two-top with the assurance that they would move us to a larger table as soon as one became available. We agreed, reluctantly. We ordered and before any of our food came out another table emptied. We asked if we were going to be able to move to that table and were told no because they had to save it for an incoming reservation. We reminded them that we were an incoming reservation as well but they said they needed to save that particular table because it was the only one they were able to fit 5 people at. We were once again assured we would be moved when another table became available (yet another lie). Between our apps and the main course another table did become available and when the server went to seat another party there we reminded him that we were still waiting to be moved (as he had promised us we would be). The waiter became belligerent with us. He said you are eating at a place called Nook - what did you expect? It's going to be crowded. We ask people to squeeze into smaller tables all the time. We reminded him that we only agreed to do so because he promised us that he would move us as soon as he could. He said he had no intention of moving us ever cause he needed all the tables he had for incoming reservations (again we reminded him we were one of those incoming reservations). Turns out he was saving the new table for when his buddies arrived for dinner (based on the big hello he gave them when we set them). While all this is going on he continued to take new reservations for tables he knew he could not seat and then the poor people would show up and be told that could not be accommodated. I understand that this is a small space with limited seating but why then take reservations at all. Just have it be first come/first served. Why also would you seat parties who were not all there? During our visit that was a 4-top that had only 2 people sitting at it not ordering anything for almost 45 minutes until the rest of their party arrived. I will never be back to Nook. There are too many other amazing places in this neighborhood to put up with such poor service and disrespect.

This is a sad story all to do with the way Atera is run and how little they seem to value their customers. My partner and I had scheduled and paid for our dinner in advance (per the policy of the restaurant:   We accept cancellations or changes when available, with no charge, up until one week before your reservation. The cancellation and no show fee within one week of your reservation is the full price of dinner $225 and tax $19.97, for a total of $244.97 for every seat cancelled. Reservations made the week of are subject to the same policy.)  Further, we were celebrating a wonderful life event and really looking forward to going to Atera.  Our reservation was for tomorrow Wednesday. I received a call from Jade, today, Tuesday, who informed me that our reservation was no longer available as the restaurant had decided to hold a private event and that took precedence over us.  I let her know that I thought this was very very bad business for a starred restaurant with a policy of taking people's money ahead of serving them.  If I decided today to go tomorrow to a private event, they would have charged me for dinner.  They offered no solution, other than coming in at 6 -- while my partner and I are still at work.  Or shifting our celebratory dinner to another day -- you know during the holiday season -- when you are not fully committed to family, events and other travel. I think this is really terrible business practice and I am really upset about it.  Some restaurants really behave below their class and that is unfortunate.  I get that it's just a dinner -- but to cancel on someone who's money you have taken in advance a day before, when there will be no chance of booking somewhere else, is disgusting.   In short, I hope they shortly go out of business.

How I heard of this place: In February of 2008, on my way to NYC for Fashion Week, someone on the flight from Los Angeles, California mentioned Grimaldi's. He said it's the place to go for pizza in the northeast. It came up again, while looking through a friends pictures (mobile uploads) on Facebook and coming across a steamy, bubbling, thin-crust pizza and learning that it, too, was from Grimaldi's. Type of cuisine: One antipasto, four pizzas (either small or large, regular or white), two calzones (small or large), a limited list of toppings and beverages, including sodas, juice, Snapple, still or sparkling water, beer or wine. And four desserts from which to choose, washing it all down with one of four hot beverages. Simple. Easy. But not mainstream.Ambiance: Their list of don'ts says it all: "No credit cards. No reservations. No slices. No delivery." Apparently less is more at Grimaldi's. Walk through the glass door at the front,only after being invited in by your host, an elderly gentleman wearing a pin-striped, dark grey button-up shirt with charcoal slacks, white suspenders and an almost-black fedora. The doors lead into a small lobby, which immediately opens onto the cramped quarters of what is Grimaldi's Pizzeria under the Brooklyn Bridge. Red- and white-checked tableclothes cover each table, but can hardly be seen among the dozens of patrons, loudly conversing and making ordering decisions. Metallic lamp-shades make their way down, over the tables, from the ceiling, resembling lights you might see in a dark room where mobsters gather to play poker. The white walls are covered in framed photographs of celebrities, politicians and other famous types who have dined at Grimaldi's over the years. Wait staff hustle and bustle through the mini-aisles created between tables and chairs to bring 18-inch pizzas to drooling, hungry patrons. Windows facing street-side at the front of the establishment give way to natural lighting, though the back still feels dimly lit. The wall to your far right and towards the back of the establishment, from where you enter, is full of boxes and supplies on garage-style shelving units. The kitchen, open to the restaurant, is blocked only by a marble-slab counter top and plexiglass, through which one can see the large containers of fresh vegetables, pepperoni and cheese. The coal-fire oven just behind, exude heat and flames, which light up the kitchen, as workers smile and toss pizza dough into the air until it is cardboard-thin. Pizza and calzones are placed on cubed stands  to allow for a bit of dining space, on plates, underneath. Two trays covering the entire table for four.   What I ordered: My husband, good friend from Queens and I decided to meet at Grimaldi's after a weekend in Brooklyn - me, for a conference, my husband, to hang out and take in the street festivals and sites - we could not leave without having finally sampled Grimaldi's pizza. I skipped the afternoon session of my conference to get lost on the subway and wait in a 33-minute line, underneath some construction scaffolding, along Old Fulton, before being called in by the old man wearing a fedora, and pin-striped suit with grey slacks, held together by white suspenders. The simplicity of the menu made it easy to decide: one, large, regular pizza ($14), which comes with fresh mozzarella, crushed tomatoes and basil, and the addition of pepperoni, Italian sausage, sliced onions, mushrooms and fresh garlic (additional $2 each). We also had to sample the large (18-inch) calzone ($16) with tomato sauce, fresh mozzarella, ricotta cheese, pepperoni and onions (additional $2 per topping applied here, too). To sip on, we had one Coke ($2) and two Olde Brooklyn Sodas ($2 each) in the Cream variety. When in Brooklyn...Right? What I loved: I loved the thin crust, the huge size of the calzone, the very fresh ingredients - from the soft and stringy mozzarella to the mushrooms and the basil, from the sausage that looked to have been rolled in house, to the crunchy, transparent onion slices...and, of course, the crunch of fresh chopped garlic, heaped to generous proportions on our pizza. Why I loved it: I love the simplicity of the menu and the bustling feeling of the space. I love the smallness of the interior and the greatness of the food. I love that there are nearly as many employees - from kitchen-staff to wait-staff as there are customers in the establishment. I love that we were squeezed in, between two other tables, and no one seemed to think anything of it. Cost: Average to high ($12-$16 per pizza with tomato sauce, mozzarella cheese and basil or crushed garlic; additional toppings $2 each)

This has never been my favorite store. The cart of products that are past the "best by" date always rubbed me the wrong way, but they aren't perishable items. However, last night, I decided to buy some Haagen Das raspberry sorbet. I dug through the freezer case for the last raspberry one, and took it home. When I got home, I opened peeled off the plastic seal and saw an indentation in the sorbet. That's when I examined the plastic seal and cardboard top: both had a slit in them- probably from a box cutter. So, I instantly stuck the lid back on the container, and walked back to the store to exchange it. I reluctantly opted for strawberry. As I headed back to customer service with my new sorbet, I saw the sorbet I had returned being placed back on the shelf next to the ice cream cakes. Now, I understand needing to keep it cold until it is placed in the back to get credit and whatnot. However, there was NO label on the product or anything to indicate that it was not for sale. So, I reminded him that the seal was REMOVED (though, I stuck it back on in case he needed to see the slit in it). He shrugged it off. Today, after a walk to Shoprite, I decided to stop by Foodtown for some seltzer (it's cheaper, and a shorter walk). When I got there, I saw the same sorbet was still in the freezer- for anyone to purchase. The top had been slit through to the sorbet (probably with a box cutter). The seal had been removed COMPLETELY. The product had left the store and been returned. In no circumstance should this have been back on a shelf. I can never buy another perishable item at this store, which is a shame because this is the only local store that sells the 6 oz. 2% plain Chobani cups. I just can't take that risk anymore. I cannot trust that the food I buy was not returned and placed back on the shelf. That's just disgusting. I cannot believe that happened.

I also tried the moules frites and duck comfit salad. These entrees were amazing as well, something I would get for myself. Expect quality over quantity here. An A+ in my book. I'll def. be back as it's a great all-rounder.

amazing tea. but you always run out of goat cheese croissants. Those goat cheese bundles of heaven are what makes visiting my sister a little less boring. Peace on earth tea and the Sage Woman teas are lovely! the baristas are always friendly and the food is tasty. JUST PLEASE STOCK MORE GOAT CHEESE CROISSANTS!!!

If I had to describe this place it would be "consistent." This place is consistently good and consistently delicious. They don't have good days and bad days. When you go you can know the quality of the food and the distinct and mouth watering flavors will be there just as you remember from your last visit. Been going here for about a year. I brought along some coworkers early on and they love it too. My bosses also go. Now my coworkers and I look forward to it and go every week for chicken, ribs, and rice and beans. The chicken skin is so uniquely flavorful and the ribs are delicious as well. They do have barbecue sauce and hot sauce but I don't think it needs it and never use, except near the end of the meal when it gets a little dry. Very distinctly delicious flavors. And the rice and beans are always good. The service is good and the owners and workers are all very nice. You gotta experience it, there's nothing like it on the island.

After a half dozen visits to the new location (and being regulars in Clark for years) I think we're going to have to strike this place from our list of go-to restaurants. Unfortunately the changes they have made mean that this is no longer the JPD's that we knew and loved. Breakfast outside of breakfast hours is no longer an option. If you want pancakes or omelets for dinner you'll need to head elsewhere. If they want to make a transition from diner to restaurant, then they have a long way to go. You should not have to pay an upcharge for fries with your $11 burger. I can go to The Rail House, The Waiting Room or any number of local restaurants and pay that much (or less) for a burger and have it served with the fries included. I do not expect to go to JPD's and spend $44 on 2 burgers, 2 orders of fries and a couple of sodas - but I did. For that price, again, I can go to The Rail House and get a couple of burgers with fries (or any other side for that matter) and 2 craft beers with money left over. Sad to say, but our last visit there may just be our last visit period.

Park West is your typical NJ diner, but with a little extra quality. This restaurant has a retro flair that blends modern designs with 1950's diner decor. There is plenty of seating, and the dining area is very clean. The service is quick and the wait staff is kind. The food is delicious, and there are a lot of dining options at a good value too! However, parking is terrible, and can be hard at times since the their lot is small. Park was has yummy omelettes and excellent french fries! I recommend the Greek omelette; it was a scrumptious delight of feta, egg and tomato. Also, their pizza burger is surprisingly good! It is a messy treat of sauce, mozzarella and beef (it sounds weird, but it tastes great). Park west is your typical NJ diner, but I feel has better quality food. You will enjoy it.
It is a great eatery just near my shop. The best pizza and service around. I like to take my friends and clients for lunch to this charming place. Food is great and always fresh.

Well well well... this is THE pizza. I'm new in town and I'm a big pizza lover. I'm half Italian and lived in Italy so I'm picky about it, so of course I consulted with my Italian friends and this was their recommendation for the best pizza in Manhattan. I'm not sure and I'll probably never now if they were right, because after trying their Calabrese pizza with spicy sausage and roasted peppers I am not planning to go anywhere else for it. This is it. I'm hooked! Thanks Piacere! Oh, they also have excellent Italian coffee!
Awesome subs!  The very Italian owner and staff seem very friendly and social with their customers.  Reasonable price & BIG portions.

The pizza is delicious, but it's SO loud here, and not particularly friendly/welcoming - I can have a nicer experience across the street, or just get pizza to go if I really want a pie. There are other places to go if I want a great pizza and a nice meal out, I just need to walk a few more blocks. This is the place to go if you're in your 20s and want to impress a date with your "coolness" but otherwise not worth the trouble.

Small small space, but great food and great service. It might be a little more expensive but totally worth it, very unique, fresh ingredients, and thick slices that are super filling! They're also open late at night, so if you're around and need a quick bite, this is the place to be.
Our favorite place to have dinner in Philly.  We've been coming here for years and Buddakan is never disappointing.  Great food and great ambiance.
Great Amish food in the Reading Terminal Market

My go-to for fruit and veggie shopping! Cheap, fresh, ample supply for smaller shops. 99c a pound/bunch isn't uncommon, and $1.99 is "expensive" for them. Always better than triple prices at super markets. Cheese shops are super pricey. Trader Joe's has great and cheaper cheese supply. The sushi bar in the center with the counter and stools, plus the large tabled public seating area is mediocre and overpriced. Dried sushi, expensive, flavorless. DiNic's has good roasted pork, but expensive as well.

A visit to Philly without going to the Reading Terminal Market is not a proper visit. This place is phenomenal with so many excellent choices. This is not a food court where only a handful of vendors are good. Here you will want to eat everything and not have enough stomach space. What to do? Buy some things (like cookies, sandwiches, and chocolates) to go and eat it later. This is a good place to go for lunch or brunch. Even breakfast. You can go to the diner or eat the food of the Amish.

Was walking around with my girlfriend trying to decide on brunch after we saw the line for Green Eggs was too long. Way too long. We happened upon Amis which was very unassuming from the outside, and honestly we didn't even know it was there. Before entering, we googled it to find it was an Italian place, and curious what an Italian place would do for brunch...we decided to stay. We were sat immediately. Didn't love the high top table, but forgot about that once we settled in. Right off the bat, loved the ambiance.  My girl got the sunny up eggs with polenta scrapple and I had a scramble. Both were awesome, and we were brought grilled bread with a ricotta cheese spread for "waiting too long" for our plates. We actually didn't think the wait was long at all, so points for that. the service was a title robotic from both the hostess and the waiter, but no other issues there. Maybe it was just us but there was one thing about the menu we found misleading... The eggs and scrapple specified on the menu that the scrapple was in fact polenta. Under sides, it just said "scrapple." I thought it was traditional scrapple seeing how earlier on the menu it was specified as polenta. No biggie though, I ate it anyway. Kitchen cooks were fun to watch... They looked in tune. Overall a good experience. We will go back.
Great veggie versions of diner favorites! The club was amazing ! Bill for two with coffee was $23 ! Nice!

Amazing place to get Cuban sandwich and Grilled Corn Mexican Style. They have several types of hot sauce which is great. This is the best place to get Cuban and Mexican cuisine at one stop shop. I would definitely go to Cafe Habana again when I am in the area, definitely recommend for lunch on a non-busy day!

What a disappointment- the service was nonexistent, the owner was arrogant, and the food was mediocre.  Explanation? "We're busy"... Guess that's unusual, I understand why now.  Had such high expectations, won't go back.

First time here-Im all about the create your own places so already im happy. The ingredients are indeed fresh and the girl behind the counter was courteous and patiently explained their menu and options t me. I wound up going for a pizza from their menu rather than creating my own (the bronx). The pizza does indeed cook in less than 2 mins! I have to say it was the quickest lunch ive gotten in downtown new haven. I think next time ill ask for a few more mins in the oven but it was good. The sauce i feel like couldve been a little better- kind of tasted like it was just out of can of tomato sauce but the rest of the toppings and cheese were great. I plan on going back and trying the salads and gelato as well.

This. Joint. Is. So. Great. Firstly, get the chili oil dumplings....choose your own spice level. They have this dollop of puréed garlic on top. CHOICE. During happy hour they're only five bucks and my girl and I usually get two orders. I wish they had more beer on tap, there are 3 choices I think. The popcorn shrimp app is a good choice too.   The lo mein noodles are thick, and anything with garlic or black bean sauce is bangin. The decor is a little cheesy but fun. Service has always been on point, both sitting at a table and at the bar. Bartenders are cool and fun to chat with. Highly recommend this place. Lots of variety on the menu. Always leave happy.

Does it get better than their buttermilk biscuits with honey butter? No. No it does not. This is comfort food done to perfection.I particularly recommend the fried chicken sandwich, the mac n cheese, hush puppies, and cheese grits. It's just good y'all.

Good pizza. The old fashioned square kind is definitely the way to go. I haven't had anything in a similar style that's quite as good. The vibe is nice but still casual. If you're downtown it's a nice option for summer since the chairs are always out on stone street.
NEVER AGAIN.  Rudest staff ever. Try Goodfella's: better pizza, nicer people and better food.

First time trying the food here and NOT disappointed.  Did a delivery order for 11 people to our place of employment and everyone loved their food.  A bit spicy for some, but food was A++ for the rest of us and good prices.   Will definitely order again!

Couldn't get zen gardens cause I moved so I decided to get JIN's instead. I waited over an hour and by the time the food got here it was cold. The food was okay but definitely not as good as zen gardens. I know the weather was horrible and I don't blame the delivery guy but I was disappointed and the guy who took my order got my address wrong.

Great place to watch a game and grab some drinks. Had the pot pie which was nice and flaky. Eamon was my bartendor and did a great job all night, very friendly and I always had a full drink. Fun place to hang out for a night.
Walked in to an empty restaurant, 20 minute wait time. Server was rude and mentioned tables were reserved. Ended up leaving. Save your time.

Overpriced for the portions you get.  Got the regular xiao long bao $7.95 along with a lunch menu item, also $7.95 but I only got a bowl of rice and five shrimps! Their fine print said it was the same portion as their dinner menu..so I wouldn't pay full price for such a small amount. My friend got another lunch item. We couldn't split the bill because it's $20 min for credit card. There are better places.
Great food and quite a relaxed atmosphere. Desserts were best part of the meal - basil icecream and pannacotta were delicious! Take a bottle of wine to enjoy with your meal!

My husband and I had a great experience there a few days ago! We were in the area and figured we would give it a try. The food was average, I had the turkey wrap, my husband had the chicken tenders fries and pretzels with cheese. They had a great selection of beer and cocktails. The décor was pretty cool also.. it had a really laid back feel. There were a lot of families, and a lot of people watching football. Our servers name was Kayla and she was great, very attentive and nice. We will be back for sure!

We keep coming back to La Viola for the mussels (white not red sauce). They never disappoint. What can be disappointing is the waitstaff. With the exception of the older guy who is charming and knowledgeable, the other waiters are kinda quick... Even rude, my girlfriend thinks anyway. I get the lobster ravioli every time and like the mussels, it never disappoints. They're my favorite. My girl had an elephant ear pasta dish with sausage and chicken. She dug it well enough....very savory and filling.

I don't doubt the quality of the food but this time I was thoroughly disappointed! After a tiring day, I placed an order for take out - spending 10 minutes explaining my order in detail as I am a vegetarian and do not eat meat. When I start eating, I found chicken and egg in my food- both of which I do not eat and had explicitly told thrice to be removed from the dish! I'm disappointed!

We ordered a pepperoni and cheese pizza. Huge pizza. Great for two to three people. Pizza was great. Thin crust not too doughy. Customer service was great. Drinks were strong and tasty. There is a bit of a wait to be seated. Cash only

Best CUBAN food in NY.  This place has amazing customer service, great atmosphere, and authentic Cuban food/cafe. I am Cuban soo I would know! Everytime I go it's very busy but the wait time isn't bad  at all.  I wish this place was a little bigger but regardless I would def. Recommend going and trying it out.  The staff speaks English for those Americans that would like to try Cuban food without feeling out of place.

Very bland food. Not much flavor. Far over priced for the quality. Wasn't event the correct pizza. They tried to charge me to add onions to a BBQ Chicken Pizza, which is a standard ingredient on BBQ Chicken Pizza. The pizza was literally pizza dough, tomato sauce (NOT BBQ), chicken and cheese. Hardly a specialty pizza (as listed).
really good food.  great staff.  I've been here twice now and I've had DELICIOUS food each time.  Steak is amazing.  Definitely recommend!

Two Petes is 2 blocks from my house. I can't say I love this place. For some reason, when I think about the food, I never think of is it as all that tasty. Some things I've tried have been pretty good: Banana Pancakes included a nice portion and Cream Chipped Beef was mediocre. The overall thing that bothers me is why both Two Peters and The New Ewing Diner on the other side of town exceed what I consider normal diner prices. I understand that the insides are renovated but it surprises me that these diners, located in low to middle class areas, charge 12 dollars for typical breakfast meals. Also, the waitress we had kept calling me "Amish" because I was wearing suspenders and was just annoying throughout the meal. Wish I had a more lovable diner around the corner from my house...

Great place to eat! I took my boyfriend here for his birthday. The place was packed probably because companies were doing there holiday dinners. So we waited by the bar to be seated and had a couple of drinks. It was jazz night so they had a live band playing... great music. The food was to die for, I have the Mac and cheese lobster it was so good! He loved it and it was a perfect birthday dinner.

This is a late review, but HAD to give these guys props. In august, Called half hour early to let them know a party of nine was coming in. They reserved a table, unknowingly committing to the beginning of a bridal party bar hop. Delicious food, great service, Dealt with our silliness and made sure we had a GREAT time. Made my bride sister, who LOVES always sunny the happiest bride in the world. Thanks guys!

we, 4 ladies, drove 40 minutes for lunch here and we loved everything!   the coconut lentil soup, panini, salads w/ flank steak, and quiche were wonderful.   we each ended up buying food to take home for our families.  i just tried thr chicken pot pie and its very good (and i am not a chicken pot pie person). the owners were very nice.  we had about a 10 min wait.   place is very small/ cramped but we were ok after seting in and eating.

This place rocks!  They have amazing food and even better staff.  I love there Wednesday nights they have Latin music and free bachata dance lessons. This is the place to be every Wednesday night. They also have live bands sometimes on Saturdays which is great!

After living in Belgium for three years with my husband, finding this place when we got back home to NYC was a miracle! The menu is basic, as in fries and all fries, but they are so dang good. I recommend going classic as it hits the spot like none other, but my husband always tries their other fun creations and says they are delish. Definitely worth a try!
Very good hookah and food!
great choclete mole sauce big protions love it so good!
i ve been to the place couple yrs ....my fav place ever !!!!! food is fantastic , ppl are nice...clean !!!! nth else to complain !!!!!!

I don't see this place lasting long. 5 pm on Wednesday night and we are not greeted at the door. The place is empty so take time to indulge your customer as it was obviously our first time. The food is cold. Mac is not good. Corn bread is good. I look to the left to see a kid with no HAIR NET making 6 trays of sweet potatoes with his hands. Gross.  Half the staff looks like they just rolled out of bed. What I thought was a homeless man walking in turned out to be an employee. I can go on. Bottom line...don't trust the hygiene so we won't be going back. Hope no one gets sick.
Great place so everybody is welcome to the point where you can get anything done today

Perhaps one of the finest of Diners in NJ (although I do have other favorites in Jersey). Went there twice this past weekend and had lunch one day and breakfast the next.  Lunch was a Chicken Milanese, breakfast of Eggs, Sausage and Pancakes.  Once, Twice, again served up great tasting plates with very generous portions. A "must return" establishment.

Came here to get takeout on a weeknight.  I was greeted with hot tea and the service was fast.  I ordered one of the special rolls and it was great!  Although I was confused by the overwhelming vanilla glade scent when I walked in, I would love to come back and eat in.
This a very good BBQ spot. No pressure, no attitude... Just slow cooked meat. I highly recommend the brisket and the brined slow roasted chicken.

I love this place. Very cozy and not too much crowded and narrow. And server is so kind. You can get nice service at there. The restaurant has high ceilings and the ambiance is great. I've only been here for dinner so it's always lit dimly and there's always a crowd but with reservations (which I highly recommend for dinner) everything usually runs smoothly. We usually order the pri fixe meal with a couple bottles of wine. I've always enjoyed everything I had chosen for my meal. There were times when others found their dish too salty and it would be returned and a new dish served right away. Very happy with this place and very highly recommend it!!!

It was my Mother's 80th B-day, so she had her choice of places and she picked Freddie's.  I was not to happy because last time about 10 years ago, I was not impressed.  We got there early to make sure we were not waiting forever, which we did anyway, but we were not in a rush.  We went into the bar and had a drink.  Service was fine.  We were some of the youngest customers there and I can say I have been coming to Freddie's for 40 years!  When we finally seated and ordered, we got our drinks and salad.  But then we waited for a long time for the main course.  Everyone's food was good and fresh, and my Mom was happy.  I am glad that Freddie's food was better then the last time I was there.  It has been a staple in the area for 80 years, just like my lovely Mom!

The food is just okay but the service is horrible. Our party of 3 stood up to put our coats on, before we even took out our wallets to settle our bill, and were yelled at that we had to leave a tip.
