I told the waiter that obviously we were going to tip but it was not a requirement of customers. He continue to berate me all the way to the register. We have gone there a few times since and every time it has been similar results. Just go to the noodle house and save yourself the rudeness.
My favorite is the Fuego. Great place!

Wouldn't know how good the beer was, since it was too crowded at 6:45PM on a Wednesday to get a seat or to get waited on. After 15 minutes of trying to get service, I gave up.  The beer menu looked pretty decent. Probably won't go back anytime soon.

Splendid ramenya, definitely lives up to the hype. Visited with a small group -- first piece of advice, SMALL GROUPS ONLY -- and had a really delicious meal: Shared: Shishito Peppers UniPo Okonomiyaki Ramen: Mu Ramen (Beef) Tonkatsu 2.0 All the apps were delicious and very delicate. The flavors on the Okonomiyaki blew us away -- salty, sweet, savory all at once. The ramen lived up to the expectations we've had since before the Pete Wells review in March. The Tonkatsu 2.0 that Wells had really could be considered among the best bowls of ramen in the city, but it was the namesake ramen that really blew us away. I can't recommend this place enough, and I can't wait to go back to try the Tebasaki Gyoza and the Spice Miso Ramen.

Great meal for only $6! Lamb and chicken are always fresh due to high turnover unlike others in the area that have meat that's been cooked for hours. Excellent white sauce! I visit the Halal Guys every time I'm in town!

i have been eating here for a few years now. this place is delicious at 3-4am after a long night out with friends. the lamb and chicken combo is what i usually get. not really sure how to describe how good it is but the place is delicious. the only reason i am leaving 4 stars is the wait. they need to find a more efficient way to serve the mobs that show up at 3am.
My go to spot for halal food in the city.

The food was OK.  Not the best Thai food and was disappointed that they take cash only.   The service made me feel uncomfortable as if they were rushing us to eat inorder to seat other people.   And the ambience kind of sucks.
This past weekend, I had my fourth dining experience at Tavern on Jane. It has become my not to be missed place when I am doing a theatre weekend in NYC. Great food and terrific service.
Hole is the wall, but delicious viet sandwiches.

This is a new restaurant in Newark international airport gate C 84. It has iPads to order from which is nice but when you order you must pay with a credit card and include tip. Now wait for the surprise....the food is inedible!  They do fine with bringing you a bottle of beer or a glass of wine but don't get the food!  Run fast as you can! The pictures on the iPad make it look like it's great; what you get is disgusting. Good luck.

I want to like this place but, unfortunately, I think 'Meh' is indeed the most apt description. If you are ok with poor service, an ok but not great (read, over-hyped) burger, then it's worth the low prices, but otherwise I wouldn't recommend.

I am the band leader of one of the bands that was supposed to play last night at North Star Bar. My band plays frequently in Philadelphia and has NEVER dealt with a venue that acted as unprofessionally as this establishment did tonight. The show had been planned for a couple of months, and I know many people were planning on attending. However, according to a rude bartender, since not all of the bands were present EXACTLY at the load in time, they decided to cancel the show. VIA A FACEBOOK NOTIFICATION. Not even a call was made to the headlining band who was there loading in right at 6 pm and briefly left to pick up more equipment. In other words, the people in charge of sound/the show had something better to do with their night and apparently left around 6:30 (2.5 hours before the show even started). North Star Bar made an awful and stupid decision, losing a lot of money and respect from musicians and show-goers alike. I do not recommend this venue to anyone, especially musicians looking for a respectful and dependable venue to share their music with.
This place is awful, they cancelled my friends show tonight and were super rude about it

I had dinner last night wih some of my girlfriends and we really enjoyed it!  The food was great, the wait staff was very attentive and Mario is adorable!  Before we went there, I was a little worried about some of the unfavorable reviews the restaurant got.  One there I realized nothing could be further from the truth.  Everything was delicious and I will definitely be going back with my husband very soon.

I recently visited Zaroka for dinner. The interior design is quite wonderful in its aesthetic. The service is very efficient and courteous. I ordered the samosa chat, chicken vandaloo, aloo palak, and keema paratha (oiled naan bread with spiced minced lamb). The samosa chat was very adequate-- not as good as some of the chat I have had at some of the Indian restaurants in Artesia in Los Angeles or at Royal Place in White Plains, NY, or at Tulsi in Manhattan, or in Pakistan -- but still quite good. For me, a dish like the samosa chat should over-flow with flavors, especially with its multiple layers of different ingredients and food items (stuffed samosa, yogurt, spices, chopped vegetables, tamarind and mint sauces). Samosas also need to be especially crisp to counter the yogurt. That wasn't the case here, and it didn't quite come together. Aloo Palak (Potatoes and Curried Spinach) was palpably spicy, but went down well with the plain naan and also with the rice. It was very well cooked and delicious! In spite of years going to Indian restaurants, I have surprisingly never had vandaloo. This was my first time. Chicken vandaloo, a south Indian specialty, was quite interesting... I tried to guess the aromas coming from the wonderfully aromatic dish but couldn't be sure. Still, I almost had a moment where I thought -- Am I at a Chinese restaurant? Did I order chicken sweet and sour? The aroma had an air of familiarity to it, reminding me of the Chinese staple dish. Unlike the mouth watering sweet and sour, the vandaloo was quite disappointing -- one-note, ordinary and quite under whelming. While it is a very popular "go to dish" for many, I honestly don't get the fuss about it based on my experience here. I really was expecting and hoping for fireworks with this dish, but it just didn't happen... not even close. For me, tikka masala, korma or coconut-based curry sauces are more delectable and flavorful in Indian cuisine than the more spicy but ironically insipid vandaloo. Keema Paratha (bread with stuffed minced lamb meat) is a childhood favorite of mine. Over the years, I have been totally disappointed with parathas at restaurants because they were nothing like the home made parathas that I grew up eating in Pakistan. For me, the best parathas are those that are thin, just slightly crispy, and packed (but not overflowing) with minced meat, or radish, or potato, or cauliflower -- whatever the filling. However, it is the mix of the filling with the spices and fresh ingredients such as cilantro that give the paratha its addictive full bodied taste. It is not for nothing that the paratha is one of the famed comfort foods and holiday staples in Pakistan. It is remarkably versatile -- served at breakfast, lunch, and dinner, and during casual as well as more formal dinners. With this much potential, it is ironic that the naan or the paratha has not been able to transcend its status as a side dish. The paratha from Zaroka, typical of most Indian and Pakistani restaurants, was more Middle Eastern or Italian pizzeria-type doughy, stuffed bread then the Indian or Pakistani paratha. Very disappointing. Based on this visit, I would say the food was quite average -- and did not justify the high prices. To put it this way -- If I am really hungry and the restaurant is right there then I'd probably get dinner there again, but otherwise quite unlikely that I will be visiting. Rating: 2.5 stars

I am a certified beer snob. I lived in San Diego for 8 years, the IPA mecca.  Bay Ridge is not a hipster part of Brooklyn at all which is good but the downside to this is that there are few places in this neighborhood with legitimate IPAs and crafts beers.  The Lockyard answered my prayers. I love all the staff and bartenders, they're all funny bastards and the regulars are an eclectic mix of longtime bay ridgers and hipster transplants.  The back area is great for people with kids like myself and bar is great for bar hoppers. They have an excellent trivia night on Wednesday also.
I've been a regular here for years--the food is on point and the drinks are great! I recommend the mint julep. Jessica is fantastic and can make you anything based on the mood you're in--love it!
This place is the truth. Burgers are juicy and buns are sweet and toasted, the pulled pork is delicious and I recommend subbing bbq sauce on the sammy. Also the the fries the fries are amazing

9am brunch was the only reservation we could get on Black Friday but it was worth waking up for. Service and food was impeccable. My uncle had to run out and feed the meter and they offered to keep his plate warm until he returned. 20min later they ended up making a fresh order for him.

wings and beer. need I say more? happy hour specials are impressive. good place to bring the gang. slider burgers are a must try as well. I wish they offered more beer options but hey we cant have it all.. the excellent wings will suffice.

Omg there food is amazing I would highly recommend the tomato soup! Honestly the best! I love the environment they are very welcoming. My only warning is watch your step when you come in I tripped a couple of times lol

My favorite is the New Mexico burger. I love the peppers on them. The fry sauce is delicious I use it on my burgers as well as fried. The service is pretty good even when its crowded. I do wish there was more seating especially during lunch time.
Le cadre, le service et les produits sont très bon. Un petite salle conviviale pour manger rapido. On peut même demander un code pour le wifi

Someone else on here said it's a must visit if you like Chinese food. I say yes, but also it's a must visit even if you do NOT like Chinese food. For most of my life I've been one of the second kind. Until someone took me here and now I'm a convert. I realized I do, in fact, love this stuff, (at least the fresh, authentic Sichuan stuff). The flavours in the dishes here knock my socks off. Some of the dishes I've had are the fried intestine, ants climbing a tree, beef noodle soup, oxtail and tripe salad appetizer, chicken lettuce wraps, lamb curry, and sea bass stew. Eat here. Do it!
Just okay. Nothing to write home about. Maybe would have been better, if our order had been right.

7 months ago I came to Cafeteria with a friend and had a great experience. The service was good, the food was tasty & I left with a full belly and a smile on my face. HOWEVER today as I sit here I am utterly disgusted with the service I just received. The staff were very enthusiastic as they seated my boyfriend and I and everything went downhill from there. To begin our drink order was never taken, our water glasses were replenished throughout our short stay but who said we wanted to drink water all night?  Our appetizer orders were taken and we received our biscuits (thanks) However after, we were never asked what we wanted to follow up with for our main course nor were we asked how the service or food was. The waiter tended to the couple next to us and provided them with their drinks, their appetizer and next their main course. I cannot believe that nobody ever came back to our table simply to ask if we were satisfied. On one of the waiters trips to the couple next to us, I requested a peach iced tea. I'm convinced that what was in my cup was tap water with brown food coloring and a lemon slice. It tastes filthy and AGAIN I'm completely baffled because this was far from the service I received last summer. I don't plan on ever returning to this establishment and I WILL NOT be recommending it to my friends.

My favourite restaurant in NYC!! You have to try the housemate yogurt with roasted beets, the pretzel-dusted calamari, the burger (forgot the name), the ravioli, and the butternut squash soup!! Everything they have will serve your taste buds in the best way!!!!

Everything is an extra charge. The service is slow even though the place is always empty. There is one lady who was very nasty to us. Too bad because the food is yummy. Maybe that is why they do take out so you don't deal with bad service,  petty policy and may staff members

We went here one night because we heard many good things about it and we were not impressed. The margarita pizza was ok at best. We ordered the famous artichoke pizza and after a few bites it made us sick. It just wasn't for us. Too thick and creamy. There's plenty of pizzerias just as good.

This place is amazing! I recently went when I was in town and I had so much fun there! The bartenders are really friendly, they play great music, free cheese puffs, and decent pricing for alcohol. Definitely a fun place to go to with friends if you're looking for some place chill to hangout. If in live in New York I'd definitely be coming here more often. Will be visiting on my next trip out east.

Impeccable across the board.  A little oasis of warmth and personality tucked away on a somewhat nondescript street -- wonderful service, with an engaging and involved owner who clearly loves his food, his restaurant and his customers.  delicious food -- the tiny ravioli are delicately delectable and just divine.  Hearty goat cheese tart with a wonderful blend of flavors and textures.  entrees and desserts equally well thought out and prepared, all delicious.  Not a misstep in the two times we've been in the past three weeks, and we'll back for many many more to come.  A wonderful find.

I had dinner at V Street last night and today I don't know why I should even eat. Everything will be a disappointment compared to the incredible food we had. We sat at the bar and ordered off the happy hour menu (vegan pierogies!!!! Tofu taco!!) as well as the regular menu. I'm so happy this place exists.

By far the best doughnuts I've ever had. I've tried nearly all of them and go several times a week. The atmosphere is comforting and its run by a lovely couple. Plus they're cheap. Definitely worth it.
What can I say about the Reading Terminal? It's fantastic. Food is fresh and it is all good. It really is a Philadelphi must see.
Pros: GREAT Mac and Cheese; fun and unique menu items Cons: Cash only and operation hrs.
Nice Food The yellow fin Tuna was a good portion size. Restaurant was full yet meal still came without much wait. Good service without being excellent.
Awful service mated with below average food quality equals a complete miss.  This is even bad by airport standards.
Food was exceptional, but of note was the staff who are the most professional I have seen in a while. If you want  good food and  quality service this is the place to go.

After walking the Highline we wandered into West Greenwich and found this great little bar/pub. Have to say this was a bitter pub than many I have visited in UK with good choice of beers & ale. Menu looked great and alll the tables were full
Fantastic! Truly British inspired cuisine done to perfection. Great cocktail, wine and beer selection.

Can I just say... BEST SOUP DUMPLINGS EVER!! First time I was here and I want to come back every time I visit New York. Despite the fact that you might have to sit with people on the round table because it gets busy... I really didn't mind. What I ( I mean my BF and his sister) ordered: *Crab/pork dumpling or just pork dumpling. (Amazing) *there house friend rice *baby bok choy Shared between us three and it was enough. Enjoy! I can't wait to go back :)

The good and the bad. That's what you get at Martha's. Tonight was bad! Great people, friendly people but the food was just off! When we told the waiter that the short ribs tasted old (stale, dry, terrible smelly--like old socks) he said, oh yeah that's what this dish tastes like! Umm...at $26 a plate that's not a great response! Is the chef eating mushrooms back there? No bueno! Plenty better options in the neighborhood. And what's up with the comp when a $200 table is unhappy because of some stinky old meat? I mean, we told the waiter that the meat tastes spoiled and he said "yeah that's what the dish tastes like." Really?

This little cafe is perfect for breakfast and lunch. The baked good are excellent. The sandwiches terrific. The coffee is really good too. The service friendly and delightful. The Pope Francis sandwich in particular is really delicious. Jen, the owner has clearly worked very hard to give this little spot it's own character and she has really succeeded. Highly recommended.

Came in late so there was no waiting and the food was amazing. So tasty I couldn't stop eating even though I was very full! I don't know what they put in the salad dressing but I would love the recipe. I also had the chicken vegi soup and believe me you've never tasted anything so fresh and flavorful! Great experience. Thank you!
This place rules great shows,cheap drink and affordable good food what more can you ask for?
my credit card number was stolen and used at this place.   not cool.  someone on the inside is in on this.

Delicious coffee and pastries.  Belgian chocolate items are wonderful. Including the mocha on the coffee menu.  They use their our chocolate to make the mocha, it's amazingly good. Fantastic place for a pick me up. Lovely place!
The lobster mac and cheese was the best I ever had!!!! They also had so many different lobster rolls to choose from, and the oysters were cheep and fresh!
Consistently amazing, fresh seafood. Never fails.
The chains (paneria fresh and co etc) in the area cannot even hold a flame. hands doen the best in midtown. nom nom.

New American - High End Diner - Great for Groups - No Reservations My favorite restaurant in New York and an absolute staple for lunch. Bubby's combines the best of diner fair with artisanal prep and quality ingredients. The best part is it's ability to work for any occasion from power lunch to date night, even late night tacos (don't forget it's open 24 hours except on Sunday nights). The Tribeca location is much better than the Meatpacking one. I just wish they were still in Dumbo.

Food is decent, drinks are decent.  Nothing I'd go out to specifically, but it's an okay enough place if you're already in the area.  Basic menu with nothing special, but everything on the menu is good, and executed precisely as you'd expect,  No ambitions, but no failures.  The servers are standard servers.  They smile, the bring your food, they come around once or twice and ask how things are going.  Nothing exceptional, nothing bad.  A very standard place to stop being hungry in.

I came in today and got my lunch during what was a busy stretch at the counter. The girls who were helping the customers primarily were super nice, efficient and made what could of been a bottleneck experience really smooth sailing. Also, best tuna in town!

Great place! We saw a comedy show last weekend for a girls' night out and had a great time. We purchased the Groupon, which was 3 admissions for $5, so practically free admission. Drinks were reasonably priced (I think only $6 each--2 drink min.) so it only ended up costing about $15 each for the night out. You can't beat this, especially in NYC. When you walk into the bar the staff is super friendly. The comedians were hilarious and the show was almost 2 hours. A lot of the comedians got the audience involved, which makes the show even more fun. I'd definitely recommend Dark Horse for a girl's night out or a date night.

I hope the owners are reading this: I've lived in the area for 15 years and watched this place change owners many times. The customer service here is at an all time low, forgetting the value of keeping local clientele. On several off-busy-hr occasions, we came in with our daughter and despite the restaurant being nearly empty...we're told the only seat is available next to the cold, windy, drafty front door. Not ideal for a child, and when asked to sit elsewhere, we were told flat out, No.  There is one hosts/manager who is particularly rude and curt we've encountered twice and had to leave. To top it off, the food is meh, so so - having been served cold soup and mussels that were in a thick, bland gravy that was almost impossible to consume.  I will happily watch this place go out of business/change owners again. Watch your staff's attitude, us locals are talking and word is spreading. *As we live next door - I will take the time to walk in when I see him (as it was the same man on both occasions) and ask for his name. Thanks for taking time to reply.
Love the Chili/cheese dogs. Food is usually good...better than the guy in the truck. Would it hurt to say hello, or crack a smile once in a while? Sal was so much nicer.

Awesome place for a catch up dink with friends, after work happy (awesome seasonal bar menu), brunch with the girlfriend or even friendly funky place to take visitors to the big apple.  I will say I planned a group thing here and the events manager was a bit of a tool but the service day of and manager on site more than make up for it.  Plus being a #sandy survivor they get another point and then some. I would definitely go back to this restaurant if I found myself in the neighborhood.
Love it!
Rice pudding was great

Our holiday party was great here! The food was excellent, drinks were even better. The service was awesome. I would certainly come back for drinks with friends & plan another corporate party/event here. Norman and Hannah were the best!
Big fan of this place. Last few times I came I'm Hannah was a huge help and extremely friendly.
I can't write long speeches! so shortly!Before visiting this place I loved fried potatoes,but then,i began to adore potatoes cooked here! Great selection! I recommend for everything!

Was in the area for a business meeting and checked Yelp for a place to get a sandwich. Had the pastrami on rye special with cole slaw and Russian dressing and a cup of chicken soup. It was a good sandwich and the soup wasn't ready so I had to wait for it. 1 pm and the soup wasn't ready seemed weird. I waited and it was ok.

The meal was fine. Had I not had better Indian food in Philly, it would have gotten 3 stars. Hubby and I shared Papdi chaat, lamb korma, and garlic naan. The chaat seemed unusually watery and lacked serious depth of flavor.  Lamb korma was good, though the lamb could have been softer. Naan was not crispy and garlic was undercooked. Friendly service. Idk, the food just seemed to kinda just ... Exist. The rice wasn't floral or anything, and was mushy.  I guess it's in a good location, and is better than Tiffin. But make the travel to the Northeast for tastier Indian food. Won't be back to Ekta.

Fantastic!!! The food, the service (Johnny especially) and the vibe were all on point! They even had live music, which I believe happens every Wednesday night. Definitely try the Jerk Chicken appetizer, Salmon, Tamarind Chicken, Mac & Cheese and Sauteed Spinich! Went for the first time this Wednesday and may be back on Friday!

Let's start by saying I got a free glass of wine. Now let's talk why. Got here, checked in and asked where could I sit. He said: anywhere. Then after 10 m seated, someone (another waiter)  comes and said If I checked in with someone, and I said yes. Then, not at all polite and disregarding the waiter's mistake, he said that I could not seat, that I needed to 'move' to the bar. Rule number 1 of the restaurant and bar industry: you never, ever move a customer from their table and even less with attitude. Staff here needs some serious training. At least the manager is nice.

It's been over 2 years since I went to visit NYC. And I still have dreams about this hole in the wall...literally. Prosperity dumplings has the tastiest, huge homemade dumplings. ONLY FOR $1!!!!! I also had the sesame beef sandwich, fresh out of the frying pan. And oh man that was yummy! I constantly rave about this place to my California friends. I reccommend this place to everyone and anyone! Don't discriminate the small shop.
Their Chicken Biscuit is the best chicken biscuit in the world. 37% better than, dare I say it, Chick-Fil-A's chicken biscuit.

This place is just great! I spent a week at my moms house in Queens, and looked for some nice tacos in Brookyln while visiting a friend, I turned to Yelp and found this nearby and open, it was really a sweet experience , and while it might be a while till I get back to NY this trip has welcomed me to Yelp as it is not really common where im from, and also the great Tacos ElBronco. it was a great ride

Brought my appetizer  after my entree and staff did nothing about the lady playing her kids tv show out loud on her iPad for the whole dining room to hear... Food was alright but probably won't be coming back.
One of the best places in the area. I come here often and every times  an amazing experience. Their milkshakes are life Somethings  are a little pricey but it's worth it

We walked right by the midtown Ippudo as the sign is discreet and in Japanese,, and the restaurant is below street level.. but even the waiting line outside didn't put us off!! FABULOUS RAMEN!! ..like something I have never eaten before. Home made noodles and a sumptuous broth and with totally authentic goodies AND tempting add-ons. It is always a good sign when the establishment in loaded with Japanese!! Don't miss the Pork Buns!!! ..to die for!!! On the down side: a bit noisy, but what place isn't noisy in New York City?? Go!! You will thank me:)

This is my favorite place for ramen. I can't get enough. The wait is always so long but always worth it. I keep coming back for the pork buns, the wasabi taco, and the Akamaru modern ramen. Some of my favorites. Service is wonderful as always!

This is my first ever Yelp review. Just felt like i have to write something coz I/we (party of 11) left that place really upset. We did the Kamayan night. Which is supposed to be $45/person, which is reasonable. But for some reason of we're a party of 12 (just 11 showed up), we have a minimum of $900 food and beverage. (Not including tax and tip). It is hard to consume all that food so we decided to order take out just to reach $900 bucks worth of food. I tried to let the fact go that for a little place "hole in a wall" each of us spent $115.80. The thing that got us was they kicked us out because we've been there for 2 hours. If i wanna get kicked out of a place, then we might as well have eaten somewhere where we only spend 20 bucks each. That not even the kicker. We made us all stand at the side of the bar while we wait for our take out. And they have the nerve to include 20% gratuity? $40 bucks for fried fish! Even Mario Batali doesnt charge that much. So to the management... Its not all about the money. Its ok if your guests leave with nothing good to say but you dont want them leaving with a lot of bad things to say.

Yes I am a fan!! The line was wrapped around the building. Luckliy I was staying at a friends who lived in the building above the place so we were able to call it in and walk down a grab it. I see why people are always in line waiting for what is said to be the best pizza in town. The flavors were so good, the sauce was amazing and they were not greedy with the toppings. If I lived in town I would frequent this place often, even if that means waiting in line!
Epic. Life changing. Exhilarating. Eating a Pat's Cheese Steak with Cheese Wiz is like dying and going to heaven. Why even bother going to Geno's... that would be truly un-American!
Fun place, yummy empanadas!!
Good food, great decor, attractive staff, large TVs to catch the games, decent drinks. On the expensive side for your typical sports bar.

I've been coming here for years and there's a reason--the 3 daily pasta specials. They make something new everyday and it changes seasonally. I love the hummus and antipasti as well. Sometimes I just come in for a $25 bottle of wine or grappa, appetizer and dessert--I recommend the panna cotta. I'm a foodie--and I really enjoy Becco. However the service varies sometimes, which is why I gave 4 stars. Is this the BEST meal I've ever had? No. But it's Italian comfort food and it's one of my favorites go-to resturants.
Love love love this place! Although the venue is on the smaller side and so are the portions it's perfect for lunch with one of your girlfriends or a romantic evening with your man!

Stopped by for lunch midweek. Service was good, had no issues during our visit. I ordered a hamburger, medium well. Meal was good, fries were above average, pickle was fresh (crisp). Would stop by again.

This is a "local" spot in Newark, deep in the Iron Bound. Never the less, it is very welcoming and warm. Every time i have been here, i have been greeted very cheerfully by a member of the staff. The place is always pretty crowded, mainly with a good amount of "regulars" at the bar. There is a typically wide selection of drinks. As for the food, let me just say, I have been around the block a bit, and am a Huge burger guy - THIS IS THE BEST BURGER I'VE EVER HAD. IT is juicy, on a nice bun, and cooked to your liking. The meat is very fresh and NEVER disappoints. Truth is, unless I'm outta town, I'd rarely go anywhere else if I get a craving for a cheeseburger. They also have other good bar food, but i normally go for the Burgers. Bring your appetite, b/c they are huge.

Just Jake's is convenienty located off of Bloomfield ave. in Montclair.  Jake's is a blend of college bar, pub and sports bar all rolled into one. Unfortunately, Jake's identity crisis causes it to fall short at all three. Jake's has a typical bar menu that will satisfy your pangs of hunger. However, if you are looking for a delicious gastro-pub experience this is not the place. Their cheeseburger sliders were undercooked and covered with grease. Jake's does have delicious french fries, and their chicken spring rolls with sweet chili sauce were pretty good. Just Jake's saving grace is their bar and outdoor seating (especially during the summer). Jake's bar specials makes this watering hole a good value; especially with their 3 domestic beers for $5 specials. Unfortunately, with good value comes the college crowd; and with the college crowd comes pounds of body glitter and obnoxious debauchery. If you value cheap drinks over loud noise and food, Jake's is the spot.

This place is quite a gem!  It's quaint, snug, has a good crowd and a polite staff. The drinks were unique (made with their own bitters) and tasty, and food was good.  It's a mix crowd 20-40's, intimately lit, slim walkway with seating at the bar and areas to rest drinks.   Overall a cool place and I'm sure we'll be back.

Without going into too much detail, Russet was a culinary marvel from start to finish. 15 plus ingenious courses of magical and sublime flavors. Attentive, yet friendly service, definitely not stuffy or pushy. A rather demure dining space without embellishments or artwork. The star here is the food. A one off experience for our July 4th weekend getaway. The best meal we have ever had.
I love the Humita de Camerones and several of the ceviches.
Always have to visit at least once when I'm in NYC! Great hidden secret just a few blocks from Rockefeller Center. Prices are cheap so you can try out a bunch of different things.

Waiting outside in the cold. The staff looked on - 10 mins after their opening time on the door still no movement. If they have this attitude before even entering can you imagine the low rent service they will give once inside.

I have not been here in over 10 years but went last weekend based on neighbors recommendation.  In 10 years the interior remains the same. I ordered chicken noodle soup and while it was 4pm the noodles were close to dissolving cook way too long and it was 4pm. I ordered broiled scallop and that's exactly what I got scallops broiled minus ANY seasoning. I have to give credit that the scallops were very fresh. I'll wait another 10 I guess

Amazing food! I was traveling in New Jersey for work and My coworker and I decided to get south indian food. This place came highly recommended from one of my coworker's friends so we thought we'd try it out. We went there on a Wednesday night and it turns out they have "dosa night" every Wednesday eve were you can eat unlimited dosa (different varieties!!) along with some other items in the buffet (biriyani, idly, etc.). They were very courteous and kept the hot sodas coming. The sambhar and chutneys were well balanced and fresh. Overall, we were pleasantly surprised !! Tip - make sure you try the cilantro dosa! It's very tasty. If you like it a bit crispy then try the ghee roast.

I'll admit I'm a bit of a local, but i love Monk Room. The food is very good. Menu is limited, but you can always find something Italian and of top quality ingredients. The bar has a nice selection of beer, every-day stuff, as well as specialty drinks. This place is owned by the same people who own and operate many of the "hip" places in Asbury Park, so Monk Room has a bit of an "artsy" feel. Bar Tenders and wait staff is always very friendly. Vibe is always really cool. Great place for lunch or for dinner, or pre-event hangout/drinks/food. Desserts are amazing and unique. It can get a bit pricey if you explore all options, but its worth it!

GREAT PIZZA! This is authentic brick oven pizza. It was Very good. We walked in and were told to take a seat wherever we would like. I was surprised that they served beer and wine. The Beer selection was not much, but i assume they will get more beer as business continues to increase. We ordered the medium Pie, with Devil's hot sauce and Sausage. The pie was more than enough for 2 people who had a large appetite. There were several TV's set up, and one had the Devils game on, which was appropriate. The ambiance was nice: had the feel of a pizzeria but also a decent place to sit and have a nice dinner. I did not try anything except the Pizza, but that is def. the highlight of Mercato. There was only one waitress working, and several patrons, so service wasn't the fastest, but the waitress was attentive and very nice, and nothing was delayed too long. From reading other people's reviews, I think people are going a bit too crazy over the "price". While there are plenty of "cheap" places all throughout the great city of Newark, this was priced just fine for a downtown establishment with a very nice setting and close to the Prudential Center and NJPAC. We ordered a medium pizza, which was enough to feed probably 3 adults, a few beers, and it came to 43.00 which is about the price of a casual dinner out. There are a few good pizzeria style places in downtown Newark, but most close around 3, and the pizza is not as good or authentically brick over italian as this one. Will be coming back! Try it!
So fresh. So good. So inexpensive. Eat here.

We are loyal customers who have always loved Tavern on Jane, especially for its ability to create an absolutely delicious dinner at anytime of the night. The ambiance, the waitstaff and menu turned us into regular customers who easily visited over 50 times in the past two years. In the last few weeks, the renovation of both the space and the menu have left us bewildered. It appears that Tavern prefers bar patrons to diners and new customers to devoted regulars. I'm not adverse to change, but when the entire menu and wine list is thrown out, we feel unwelcome. And frankly, the waitstaff, who we know well, are equally mystified. Please include your loyal regulars in your future plans. Ask what items kept us coming back (i.e. NO PASTA and several burgers)? Tavern is a place that I loved bringing people to for the first time because it was so welcoming. I look forward to a Tavern once again that combines the best of the old and the new...

I want to share the most wonderful experience I had in the Tavern on Jane. Some days ago I had a great day at work and feel like having a little celebration for myself. Being near the place I decided to stop there and have a good early dinner.Best decision I ever made.Cozy,intimate quiet and welcoming. Mike the bartender made me feel at home as soon as I seated. He has that kind of old fashion service values that are missing nowadays. A true gentleman.Attentive to details and basically focused in providing exceptional service. He deserves an standing ovation. If you want to have a great moment and feel pampered and cared and between friends don't think twice. The food is excellent. The rest is history. Bravo Mike!

This cozy Brooklyn restaurant is for sure a win no matter what, either if you're swinging by for lunch, brunch, Happy Hour or dinner. With one of the most knowledgeable wait staffs in the industry, you will be guided through their delicious menu of delicious meals & divine desserts while you soak up the ambiance. The vibe is unrivaled and on the weekends you can swing by and grab the amazing Bijantini from the bar or enjoy the other great drinks that are available. Bijan's is defiantly a keeper!
Love this place! Food is great AND the service is always good. Best happy hour in Fishtown.

Rude cashiers. When they messed up my order and went back to get it fixed, they got it wrong for the second time. This time one of the cashiers gave me an attitude insinuating that I must have given the wrong instructions.

I like this place and have for years. So consistent and what a classic NYC new american place should be...such a great feel, warm and inviting. Jimmy the bartender is a staple and love the guy. The escargot are sick and crawfish a must. Great wine list. Wish the beer selection was a bit better but I end up getting champagne every time anyways. Classic place, love it.

This is my go to place with my guy. I love the atmosphere and the food. ( low lighting is my fave since I eat like a pig and I get sloppy with a couple drinks) I order the Chaufa every time with chicken chunks. I can't get enough of this rice it's amazing. And with a little of their spicy green sauce on it it's even better. The price is reasonable , the drinks are good. (Try the sangria) A night out here is always fun for me and my friends.

Great neighborhood restaurant. I've been here over 10 times over the years and have never had anything bad. First, the staffs are all very nice and very knowledgeable on the menu. They make great suggestions, so if you are having a hard time choosing off the menu, have them make recommendations! That being said, their buffalo mozzarella with honey & truffle oil and their truffle gnocchi is out of this world, and something you HAVE to try. My friend also had the shrimp scampi and it looked amazing as well. I will definitely be back here!

We went in there on a Friday night and it was dead, that should of been our first clue. The restaurant is pretty inside and almost has this "fine dining" ambiance about it. They had two tvs inside that was on CNN instead of sports or something not as depressing. The bartender came over to take our drink order and I ordered a lemon drop martini. It was really bitter and tasted dirty, I couldn't drink it. The bartender and waitress were both nice though. We placed an order for appetizer mac and cheese and egg roll. We ordered a filet for the entree. While we were waiting for our food they brought out scallops to another table that smelled like rancid rotten fish and instantly made me nauseous. It was the most putrid thing I've ever smelled. Shortly after they brought out our apps. I took one bite of the mac and cheese and almost had to spit it out. The cheese tasted and smelled like sweaty gym socks. I was so disgusted that I cancelled the rest of our order and asked for the check. The waitress asked if we wanted a box for the food and I told her no. They still didn't get that it was because the food was awful. She was really nice so I didn't want to be rude and just paid for what I didn't eat and couldn't get out of there fast enough. I have never had an experience like that before in my life. I got really sick after I left the restaurant from eating 2 bites. I wouldn't wish this restaurant on my worst enemy. Not sure how they passed their health inspection or how it's even possible to charge what they do for that so called food.

Don't bother with this restaurant.  They no longer serve the food that made them good enough to franchise.  They pass it off as not being able to please everyone with menu updates.  The problem is people who eat there on a regular basis have no desire to return as a result of said changes.

Jadis feels like a best kept secret that you've just discovered. Its warm, intimate and has an inviting old-world ambiance that makes you want to stay for awhile. The vibe is perfect for sipping on wine and sampling from the menu to your hearts delight. I come here to relax and unwind. Perfection!

My girlfriend and I were driving up to Vermont and lucked out in finding Cisco's. We were treated to a wonderful breakfast! I had the enchiladas with eggs and my girlfriend had scrambled eggs with chorizo. Both meals were fantastic, and the staff was absolutely wonderful. Would definitely revisit there again.

Pizza Masters has the best pizza is Bayonne hands down. I grew up and still work in NYC and I can't find pizza that beats it there either. (at least not anymore) The delivery is always fast and the workers are friendly. I would definitely recommend this place if your looking for really good pizza.

Nice ambiance, decent food, OK waitstaff, NOT the place to go if you have other plans for the day. Went in for Sunday brunch last weekend and ordered the "Gringo Burrito"; my boyfriend had the nutella/banana/caramel french toast. The food was OK but nothing spectacular and bit overpriced. By the time I got my first cup of coffee it was lukewarm and we waited 40 minutes for our food and about 10 minutes to receive the check after requesting it despite our expressed need to get going. Granted, it was busy and brunch is  typically a leisurely event, however, 40 minutes is a stretch. Definitely not the place to go for unlimited mimosas unless you're looking to consume about 2!

Myself and 5 friends decided to meet here for our holiday dinner. Glad we did. I arrived first and had a drink at the bar. The bartender came right over, even though the place was busy, and served me in less than 2 minutes! Once the rest of our party arrived, we moved to the dining room. Our waitress was great! She came over immediately, took our drink order and got it right the first time. The appetizers we ordered were very good. The Hotsy Totsy Shrimp was excellent as were the Short Rib Tacos (my favorite) and crab cakes. Since this is a steakhouse, all 6 in our party had steak. The Cowboy, New York Strip and the Delmonico were cooked perfectly, juicy and full of flavor. I had the Delmonico and couldn't have been happier. The owner came over twice, once during dinner and then again at the end to make sure we were happy with the service and food. Bottom line: I recommend the Franklin Steakhouse 100%. The service and food were great. I'll be back with the family!

i feel like this place is kind of over hyped, the food is tasty and not too expensive but ive had alot better, i think i could make this kind of food easily at home, not to say i wouldnt ever come here again but its not on the top of my list or my particular favorite to say the least, for south asian food i prefer more typical rice with meat dishes, and kabobs, but to each his own, ps not bad for a late night meal
Got to change a bit, it's still a very good place for general sushi, fish are fresh, but i like better when fish and other materials combine perfectly.Murasaki and sushi red are my favorite now

All the sandwiches are on point... Favorite is PLT. Customer service is above and beyond... When there was an issue with the delivery service, they personally delivered my sandwich at a discount. Thanks guys... Keep up the good work!

Creative Health conscious Vegan friendly Cuisine From a former White House Chef who once crafted custom presidential dishes. You can taste these amazing creations in this Bayonne hidden gem unassuming restaurant. Well worth the trip or visit, especially if you are vegetarian or Vegan! For the carnivores there are many meaty dishes as well.

So, I was brought here by a friend when we needed a place to sit, talk and eat some good food and I've been back every two weeks. The grilled cheese is bomb (you definitely should add bacon) , tater tots to die for and you must get tomato soup to dunk everything in. The atmosphere is very chill. They usually have sports on and change it to the game of your choice if you ask so I was able to watch the Knicks lose again. The staff is extremely friendly and fun to talk to. I like how they change the name of those tip jar. Basically if you are looking to eat good food, chill environment and a couple of laughs, you should check this place out.
You can call it a tourist trap, but coffee is delicious! Lavazza is my absolutely favorite and I have to stop here every time I visit Manhattan. It's even better when you pair it with tiramisu:))

This place is becoming my favorite place to eat in East Village. Amazing food ( stuffed mushrooms and Tunisian tuna sandwich are to die for), great atmosphere and service. Whenever I call for delivery the food is always here in 15-20 min! Give them a try, you will not regret it!

This place was a super cute mom and pops breakfast joint. The owner sat us and was super friendly and you could tell that she was really passionate about her restaurant, which I loved. Our waitress was adorable and made some great recommendations and provided excellent service. I had the goat cheese mushroom quiche and it was really good.
Exactly as advertised. Cheap, simple and delicious.
The best Italian style pizza! The pizza with truffled oil was to die for. Friendly staff with impeccable service! Definitely a regular stop on my visits to NYC! Ask for Marco

Pretty good food and a fun atmosphere.  Not the best Ukrainian food (I personally think the Ukrainian restaurant on 2nd ave and 9th st is better), but the Borsch was excellent.  Also on the touristy side.
One of the best pizza shops in the area. Everything is always fresh and the staff is nice. Very affordable. The chicken Ceasar salad is great! Lots of speciality pizzas to choose from

Shocked to find this place right around the block. Good food. I'm not into sushi but fiancé loves it. He ordered some rolls w mango topping, said they were great. I had hibachi w filet n lobster. Lobster was grilled too long but steak n rice n veggies were great. Would return. We got delivery so I'm sure eating there would have been better but we have a baby so that wasn't possible.

I moved here from new haven connecticut and while vermont outdoes ct in many ways, pizza is certainly not one of them. This is why I was very happy to find a wood fired pizza spot that doesn't add weird stuff like butternut squash. It's no modern pizza but it satisfies my cravings! Best I've had in vermont.
Best tacos I've ever had, period.  I've had them everywhere from Southern California to Chicago.  These are the best.  Get the corn tortillas and enjoy.
Best pizza in Montclair!
Wow what a pizza . Very good taste. Superb
serious. just go.

Although Greek food is 1 of my favorites and I can get greek food at various locations its greek to me in Clifton has to have the worst manager and customer service.  I will never order from there every again I will go out of my way to find a new place just not to eat there.

My wife and I have been regulars at High Street on Market since moving to the area in August - but only for brunch. It became our favorite restaurant from the first meal - a massive pastrami sandwich (easily the best I've ever had) - to the next, when I sampled their richly inventive black bialy with smoked whitefish. The service has always been top-notch as well. I had been wanting to try their dinner menu, especially since I had so enjoyed the pastas at sister restaurant Fork. Last night, we scored an easy mid-week reservation, and hoped for the best. I've never had such high expectations for a dining experience yet been so let down. To start - nothing on the menu really stood out. The waitress kept pushing the shared plates and $50 tasting menu. I've never been convinced the shared plates concept is a good idea - it seems like restaurants are charging a lot of money for very little food. As for the tasting menu, we didn't want to spend over a hundred dollars on dinner. Instead, we went for the bread platter to start, which is very much worth the $4 (+$2 for the spreads) as it is not simply another basket of bread. I'm not great with describing food, so I'll just go ahead and say that if you eat at High Street, you are missing out by not paying a few extra bucks for bread that you will probably not find anywhere else. Seriously, it's delicious. The entrees are were things went wrong. My wife ordered the Cod entree and I ordered the Angry Crab Spaghetti. At $23 it seemed a little pricey for pasta, but it was home made, plus it had crab and scallops, so I figured it would be worth it. When our very small plates came, I quickly realized I was wrong. These were not entrees. These were small plates. Or side dishes. But at main course prices. OK, then maybe the quality of the food warranted the price. Not so much. The cod was bland. My pasta had a nice, mildly spicy tang with a hint of crab flavor (didn't taste any hint of scallop at all). Unfortunately, there wasn't enough for me to really get an overall experience of the dish. I was still hungry when I was finished, though if they hadn't included two delicious slices of bread with the pasta, I would have been much hungrier. While this left us enough room for dessert, we were less than impressed with the Smoky Milk Chocolate that we shared. The final bill, with a glass of white wine, was just under $85 with a tip. Not cheap by any means. If I wanted to spend some money, I would have gone to Fork, where you at least have the option of slightly cheaper and smaller side portions of their pastas. If I'm paying $23 for an entree, I'd rather pay the extra few dollars for something more substantial. The best part of the meal? The nice hostess giving us complementary cookies from a jar when we left. I'm torn. If this was our first meal at High Street, I would be giving them two stars, if only for the friendly, attentive staff. If we'd never come for dinner, at least four stars. Maybe even five. Perhaps if the quality and quantity of the food matched the prices, as they do at brunch, we might not have felt so cheated. Will we be back? For brunch, maybe lunch, I'm sure. For dinner? I'll be at next door, at Fork.

Walked several books to find a breakfast joint. We lucked out when we stumbled into this find! Excellent!  Try the Italian market breakfast - great potatoes with Olde Bay seasoning and the toast was brown rice yum. Even the coffe was just right!

To get a reservation is not very easy. If you have passed this hurdle, you can enjoy this experience only. The ambience is quite economical, but they will be shepherd of mostly bearded men in dark suits. We opted for the accompanying wines, which was a very good decision. The individual dishes are top quality and highest rating level. If you like fine dining, this is the starry sky. For dessert, the chef comes personally, we did not know that he is the chef. He created the dessert on the table, without wasting a word, he disappears again. A great, expensive experience.

Horrible service.  Small portions.  Sub-par for an area with marginal Indian food to start with. We ordered online and was told 45 minutes-1 hour for delivery.  According to the receipt the restaurant completed the food within 25 minutes of ordering.  The delivery then came 1:15 later.  The food was cold.  The best part of waiting 1hour 40 minutes for delivery is a delivery guy that refuses to walk up to the door and instead stands on the sidewalk and waits for the customer to put on shoes and jacket to go outside in 35 degrees and walk up to him for the cold food. The portion size was very small.  After sharing an appetizer and eating two entrees both my wife and I then went scrounging in the fridge for something else to eat.   Highlight of the night: Eat24.com is amazing in their customer service.  When they tried to follow up with the restaurant they were hung up on multiple times but continued to try to resolve the issue.   Will not be ordering from here again.

I came here because it is a popular spot for breakfast/brunch, but it was really packed. We had a larger group, and the wait ended up being around an hour fifteen to a half. When it was our time to sit, they had to squeeze us at a smaller table, so it was an inconvenience to have since it was a tight. I got the green shakshuka, which was okay, and the greek salad, which was good. The food was overall okay, and the place itself was pretty and clean. However, it does take a time commitment to go because it seems the wait times can be unpredictable.

EXTREMELY disappointed with this place. They served at my company and I ordered the grilled chicken dish, which came with 1 base. The amount of food I received for $8 was equivalent to MAYBE an appetizer. I thought it was joke.

A visit to Philly without going to the Reading Terminal Market is not a proper visit. This place is phenomenal with so many excellent choices. This is not a food court where only a handful of vendors are good. Here you will want to eat everything and not have enough stomach space. What to do? Buy some things (like cookies, sandwiches, and chocolates) to go and eat it later. This is a good place to go for lunch or brunch. Even breakfast. You can go to the diner or eat the food of the Amish.

Reading Terminal is a Philly icon for a good reason. Come hungry, because you'll probably leave full. If, by some crazy chance, you have room for dessert after a freshly prepared lunch or dinner, there are plenty of places for dessert, including the oldest ice cream company in the US, Bassetts. It will be loud and crowded inside, but that offers a new adventure on every visit.

love love love!!!  How could you not enjoy this smorgasbord of amazing vendors and foods all under one roof.  Bring your appetite and your wallet (it's not cheap)....oh and wear those comfy jeans one size too big.  You will thank me later.

Been there 5 times, always amazing. Small local place, HUGE menu, with MANY out of this world dishes. Very comfort food, very heavy. The inside is decorated amazingly, with many random things, and always some old movie playing on the wall. If you want to bring people from out of town someplace good, bring them here!!!

Excellent meal, service and prices.  Not really knowing what to expect our first night in NY as we were cold, hungry and tired, we gave it a try and loved it so much we went back the next night!  Service is exceptional.

This place is my favorite after-work bar.  They have a vast selection of beers on tap (including some great seasonal choices), the food is delicious, and the downstairs lounge has an extensive whiskey selection.  However, it's the staff that really make this place top-notch.  Erin, the owner, is very personable and always ensures patrons are enjoying their visit. While Paula, Richie and Erica, are all very professional, and by far the most attentive, knowledgeable and charming bar staff in the neighborhood.  If you're in TriBeCa you won't regret stopping in for a pint.

The space itself is amazing and open. There's so much room to be with a group of people or just find a corner to your Own which is unlike the other places in the area. I'm not keen on their process for mAking the drinks and the sugar/cream space but I'm hoping they'll figure that out with time.

Best Tom yum soup ever! Everything was tasty and fresh. Will definitely be making it my go to Thai spot. Sat in the worst seat in the house but didn't even notice since the food and service was so good. Satisfied.
Great food! Great prices! You could literally feed a family of four for between $12 - $14! Awesome!!!
Really special. Good fresh and creative, ambiance of real class, service supreme. Highly recommended.

This place was all sorts of amazing!!! Loved everything from the food to the people to the decor. Was largely filled with a down to earth crowd - the staff was warm and attentive - the interior has been put together creatively with each piece being wonderfully engaging.  The menu was fun and food was addictive. Highly recommended and I'll be going back again soon! :) yums and yays!

This restaurant is 2nd in my book . 1st del Posto in Manhattan . This restaurant not just good food it is a art . It was a 10 course meal and every meal was taste explosion out of this world . Burst of flavors were unreal . Every bite I was sort of screaming and jumping !!!! God bless the CHEFF and the staff !!! Thank you guys for another memorable evening !!!! HAVE THE TASTING MENU !!! Best decision you will ever make !!!!

It must just be NJ... This place was packed at 1pm when I walked in. Obviously the lunch hour. 2 tables right next to me sat after I did, their order was taken after mine and yet their food came out 10 mins prior to mine. In most cases when I walk into a sushi place, if it smells fishy I tend to leave. Thus place did not until I took a sip of the hot green tea. With a taste of dish water and sea weed, I was not thrilled. The sushi finally came out... Everything looked bland and everything tasted bland. From California tool to spicy tuna to eel... There was no differentiation in flavor. Even the wasabi was mild. I expect spicy tuna to have at least a little kick but it was about as spicy as tapioca pudding! When all was said and done, I didn't even finish the sushi in front of me, nor did I go for a second plate... Which anyone who knows me would be floored, I de ides I needed to wash the tea taste out with some ice water. It took the better part of yet another 10 mins for someone to acknowledge that I was waiting for a bill, tho when the water arrived I was sadly disappointed that the dishy, fishy, tea was erased by heavily chlorinated water! Sorry, but I've had better sushi at a small town Chinese buffet.

This review is for the Shelburne Rd location.  Like others have mentioned, the outside is scary, but the service is great.  The food is typical Chinese take-a-way.  Portions are huge.  Ask for the combination meal - cheaper, comes with egg roll and has plenty for two.  Brown rice or low mein can be substituted for white rice.  I usually get sweet and sour chicken and/or ginger chicken.
Not exactly Chinese, but a pan-Asian style restaurant. Clean and good tastes compared to the other Chinese restaurants in Bayonne. BTW, their delivery is fast!

I was super excited about getting truffle fries but they were out. I would have expected them to have everything in stock and be more consistent with their products. However, what I got was good. Still dissapointed about not getting the truffle fries though.

I love this place. I love the location, the atmosphere, the beers, but most importantly the delicious burgers. Ill stop here on my way to go eat someplace else because I can't walk by without wanting it.
Something good

I've been here a few times, and its been a consistently wonderful experience. I recommend the buttered lobster and grilled octopus. For dessert--I'm not a fan of very sweet treats, but i love their Panna Cotta.

AMAZING!!! Love LOVE Love this place!!! The food was top notch and the service was  perfection. You have to try the meat pies and the grape leaves and don't forget to save room for dessert!!! GO!!! GO!!! GO!!

Once in a lifetime experience - unless you go back for more as we did (provided you can navigate their less than intuitive facebook page to buy tickets) As others stated, this is not just a meal: it's an experience way beyond that, including participating in a performance. The courses add up to a trip: half time travel - half trip inside: into your limbic system. You don't need to follow my advice, but I recommend skipping the wine pairings: they are very good but I enjoyed the trip more fully sober.

I just went for lunch here it was my first time. If you want fresh amazing tasting food Healthy food I highly recommend going here! I was so overwhelmed by the choices!! Luckily Kay Kay helped me out and each step of the way and helped me choose the most delicious plate! I had the pulled pork which had cranberries in it very wonderful fruity flavor and the mac and cheese tastes wonderful! The salad was fresh! I highly recommend going here!
