These days when I go back to NYC to visit, i go here because it is close to the bars on the LES that I like and it is open late.  Also it's slightly a more cleaned up location that can be more appealing to everyone.
This place is decent and the prices are not great but are what is to be expected in that neighborhood.  The banana muffin was pretty good.  Coffee there is too strong but not entirely lousy.

I have many complaints. First of all there is slow service. Second of all we have a low speaking waiter who seems to need a microphone. And third of all the utensils are extremely dirty AND they did not bring any water. We ordered 4 drinks and they only brought us 2 - omg I can't even deal RIGHT NOW!!!!
Family run business, food is presented beautifully and more than that DELICIOUS!!! The shrimp was perfectly cooked, rice was tender & sauces so flavorful!!!
I was there last night and the food was delicious, wait staff was really friendly, and portions were large.

I'm just going to cut to the point: honestly, this place is nothing more than an unconventionality. It's a creative, novel idea that, while innovative, ultimately fizzes and comes up flat. This place needs no introduction or explanation. We all know about the nonnas and the eccentric (and authentic) menu selections. In actuality, people in Italy don't eat dishes such as chicken parmigiana, or eggplant parmigiana, or parmigiana-anything for that matter. That isn't Italian food, no more than the food we typically call "Chinese food" is really Chinese food. These are all twisted, Americanized styles of cuisine that, in truth, often have little to do with the culture it allegedly represents. So, having never been here before, the idea of an actual Italian GRANDMA (not some Mexican named Juan or Pablo) cooking and preparing legitimate, sincere, bona fide Italian dishes was unprecedentedly appealing to me. Unfortunately, for me, the excitement of this originality quickly wore off. As soon as you walk in, be prepared to navigate through a hassling mess of giant, plastic flaps that normally cover freezers or walk-in refrigerators. Why are they there? I have no clue, but they're going to slap you in the face. Subsequently, the place is NOT cheap. On average, most of the menu items range from $25-30 dollars with a few dishes priced at $23-24. This is normal, and to be expected at a fine establishment... except Enoteca Maria is far from a "fine establishment". It felt like a pizzeria or a diner. There were no table clothes on the tables and our utensils were handed to us on a paper napkin. The waitress, who was wearing an Addidas baseball cap, was rather inattentive and on her iPhone behind the counter. (By the way, I'm not trying to call out the waitress, by any means; she was actually very pleasant. I just don't understand how the management of what is supposed to be an upscale restaurant allows its workers to include Addidas apparel/headwear in their uniforms). When she came by to refill our glasses with water, it was always warm and without ice. $25-30 for an entree isn't crazy expensive, although it's certainly not cheap. If I'm paying that much for a meal, I expect some sort of ambiance to be included in the price, and I expect to be catered to. Very unprofessional. Regardless, it'd be extremely bratty and pretentious of me to be bothered by all of this if, in fact, the food was actually good. But it wasn't. The stuffed veal was bland, tasteless and had a leathery texture, and the rabbit had bone fragments all over the plate. Also, I've read a few reviews claiming that the portions here are huge. Please, listen to me: this is false. You will leave Enoteca Maria hungry. The serving sizes are undoubtedly smaller than average at best, and visually meager/unimpressive as far as quantity is concerned (and I've already discussed quality).   The mussles and clams were quite delicious, as was the bread (it's surprising how difficult it can sometimes be to find delicious bread). But I didn't come here for bread. I was expecting to be transported to Naples with every bite I took; but really, I couldn't wait to just get the check and leave. I didn't even bother with desert. Nonetheless, it was a fun and interesting experience. The kitchen is behind glass windows, so you can actually see the nonna preparing your meal. I got a kick out of that. But like I said, the ingenuity quickly wore off and I was highly unimpressed with the service, the atmosphere and (most importantly) the food. Do yourself a favor and pass on Enoteca Maria. You won't be missing much.

This was our second visit to Meal and it was as good as our first.   We both got the Slow Cooked Braised Short Ribs which were outstanding.   Full of flavor and fork ready tender.  Our appetizers of Foie Gras  and Thai style Calamari were equally as good.  Our desserts of Apple Crisp and Fried Banana was a perfect finish to an excellent meal.  Our serving team of Steven and Lauren was also outstanding,  attentive and professional.  Meal is becoming one of our favorite restaurants and we look forward to coming back soon.

I think Yelp's rating of "meh, I've experienced better" captures the experience at TS Ma.  Customer services leaves much to be desired, and the staff members are rude to customers.  Some of their dishes are decent, but they use way too much sodium.  I will go somewhere else for Chinese food that isn't so salty and doesn't take forever for my order to be ready.

I've been coming here with my husband for a while now and we absolutely enjoy this place. We're huge wine lovers, and their list of Spanish wines are our favorite. Not to mention their food is devine! I normally get their Medallions of filet mignon sauteed with onions, garlic, and mushrooms, which is delicious. Really mouth watering just thinking about it. I want to try their scallops next, and take a look at their lunch menu since I've only been here for dinner. I really wish it wasn't so pricey, but it's definitely worth it if you want to go to a really amazing Spanish Tavern.

I grabbed a quick lunch here before catching a flight out of Newark. Service was by far the best I experienced while on the east coast. There was not a moment that passed where someone was not available to help or refill a drink. My coworker ordered a shellfish dish and it seemed like every time he placed a shell in the bowl they would pick it up and replace it with a fresh bowl. Prices were great, almost unbelievable on the lunch menu. It appeared there was a wide selection of food and prices commensurate with the choice. The dinner menu was much more thorough than the lunch.
Overall a pleasant experience. The whole fish was much appreciated yet rather overpriced. A nice neighborhood joint with a cosy vibe and pretty good food.

I'm in town visiting friends and this place came HIGHLY suggested by one of them for a late night run. I wasn't starving so I got a nachos appetizer for $13. The waiter asked if I wanted chicken and I obliged not knowing that this would cost me an additional SEVEN dollars. I don't mind paying the cost for a good meal, but my chips were burnt, there was barely any cheese, and by the time I got it the meal was room temperature. Since someone else in my party was already complaining about their meal I decided to not be "that person" and give them a pass. Only one person in my party (out of 6) enjoyed their food (he had the pulled pork sandwich) but the rest of us experienced a cold, sub-par meal. My friend that suggested the place couldn't believe how bad it was -- as he has only had great meals there before, so we chalked it up as a bad night.... I guess everyone is entitled to one (in spite of the prices =/). Then it was time to pay. 20% gratuity was already added to our bill... No problem. One person was using a card, the rest had cash. The person using the card told our waiter the amount to put on the card and use the cash for the remainder of the balance. The waiter came back to the table, gave the card back to its owner and let us know that we were $20 short. Our bad... We put another twenty bucks on the table... Layered up in our winter coats and proceeded to leave the restaurant. That's when the faux-bouncer came and yelled at us in the most rude manner that we hadn't paid our full bill. We explained to him that part was on a card and the rest was cash. In front of the other customers he continued yelling at us that we needed to resolve the bill. How embarrassing. Apparently our waiter never swiped the card... I get where the misunderstanding happened... But there is a way that you are supposed to deal with your customers. So after a lackluster, overpriced meal and being yelled at and humiliated in this place I can only give them one star and no recommendation. From what I hear they have great food, drinks, and atmosphere... But that wasn't my experience. Too bad.

Clean and friendly place.  We ate at the Deli section of Pierre's.  Great casual atmosphere. There are many choices for breakfast, lunch and Pizza!  The bakery has always been a favorite of ours. You can't go wrong stopping in for a dessert.

A super social spot, the coziest in the winter but also great in the summer when it feels very open air. The beer selection is always interesting and the layout makes it very easy to meet new people. I don't go here for the food so I can't say that it's five star worthy, but the fun vibe of this spot and the fact that I've never had a bad time here is enough for me!

I was really looking forward to this place. However, I was really let down. When I got there it seemed like a really chilled place. The drinks were amazing and the appetizers were delicious. Everything started going down hill when we got our food. I had the pork, it was super dry. I almost chocked. Two of my friends got the lamb and by the time it reached the table it was cold. They sent it back and it was still cold. Also, the waitress seemed to have an attitude. The prices are outrageous, but everything is worth it if it's actually worth the money and I don't think it was worth the money. I gave them 2 stars because the drink, appetizers and desert were great. I don't think I'll be going to this place again. There are other places that have good drinks and great food.

I was visiting my brother in New York for a couple of days and we decided to go out to eat something. As we were driving I asked my brother if he knew a place with a good atmosphere, and he recommended Sanford's. I was not disappointed. As soon as we got there we were greeted by a very friendly and polite staff. I ordered a chicken sandwich, and I have to say, personally it is one of the best I have ever had in my life! Everything was cooked to perfection and I felt like the staff really cared about our experience. I was so overwhelmingly astounded that I decided to make an account on Yelp just to write this review. Go here, you won't regret it! 5/5

So this would be the second time I ordered from this place the first time was amazing I would say best place , but I order a second time and I had a friend over and I told my friend this is a good place to order from so that we did . And I was so embarrassed at what was delivered !! My food was COLD , nasty & it took for ever to deliver . I called and actually gave them feed back on what was delivered and not once did Lisa (her name was) apologize , horrible customer service . I think what I order was extremely to pricey I paid to much for my food to come out that way . And I will never order from here again !

Food is decent but the service is terrible.  The waiter was rude and rolled his eyes at us constantly. Later they said they "couldn't" split a check and put all of the work on the customer.  I would never recommend this place to anyone!

I was extremely disappointed with the quality of food at this establishment.  Not only was the food not tasty it was over priced.  The appetizer sampler was $20 and consisted of 3 coconut shrimp, 1 rellano peeper stuffed with ground meat and potatoes in a Peruvian sauce.  Where on earth does a sampler like that cost $20 in Rutherford, NJ.  My entree special was supposed to be served with beans and rice, all I received was a flat pancake of rice.  My fried shrimp were even tasteless and had to drenched in green sauce.  Drive and extra 5 miles down Rte 3 and head to NYC if you want to spend NYC prices on a Sunday lunch.

I would definitely recommend this place to anybody looking for a good meal with good service. I had the burger and fries and my fiancée had the mushroom ravioli. Both were pretty good. And for appetizers we had the margherita flatbread and one of the soups. All pretty good. For drinks, I liked their bottled beer menu and the one cocktail I tried was also good. Something with gin... I forgot the name. For the dessert I would recommend the warm brownie. It was delicious. The reason for 4 stars and not 5 is just because it was very crowded in there. I don't mind a busy restaurant, but hate sitting at a table for 2 and feel like I'm having dinner with the two other tables next to me. Other than that, definitely try it, if you haven't already.
we love you warren.
Not bad food, but nothing worth the prices. Fast service but as a small restaurant it's too crowded and no privacy. I wouldn't go again

I keep thinking this location just needs more time...they're new. I keep coming back...and it just stays terrible. Let's face it, Chipotle is awesome, pretty much without even trying (or so it seems to me!) but Princeton's disorganization really ruins the experience here. I regularly go to two other locations, Bridgewater and Paramus, and they are amazing. The food at Princeton doesn't even seem as tasty as the other two. Not to mention they are ALWAYS out of stuff. Today, inexplicably, they closed at 6:00. If you were to ask me I would say it's because they were out of everything. As far as I know, today, it was sour cream, forks, white rice, lemons (for iced tea, which was terrible tasting too!) I really hate complaining but today was the last straw for me. Do not mess with Chipotle!!!

Would have given 5 stars if the burrito would not have been so greasy.  The table side guacamole was the best.  Hot salsa was best i've ever had.   Ask to sit in mariana's section as she provided quality service with a smile...the best in CT.  With the exception of the burrito everything was extremely fresh and delicious.
THE BEST. The best hot dog, the best spicy drinks, the best bartenders. its all good. PW
Been here a couple times never disappointed but I haven't really tried to many things.  It had been great so far!
This is my favorite place in the neighborhood. their food is outstanding, everyone is just real nice. it's the warmest spot in south slope. their food though. go look at the menu.
Loved LOVED the pizza here!   The pepperoni and Italian sausage are the best!!  Highly recommend if you want a true taste of NYC!

Had dinner last night - made a reservation and we arrived a little early and waited just a few minutes and we were seated. David showed us to our table upstairs and we loved it. Ariel was our waiter and was very attentive - explained the the specials and favorite dishes in the restaurant. We both had the Squid and black ink pasta with mussels, clams, squid & scallops. It was delicious! We had the soup of the day - also outstanding. The wine list is very extensive. All the wait staff was great to us - they had several large parties yet we were never left without someone making sure we were ok. We were post theater and just wanted a leisurely meal experience and had exactly that. Oh - the deserts - my husband had a canolli and I had fresh berries and creme. They were outstanding - felt the canolli was one of the best I've ever tasted. Prices were more than reasonable especially for NY. next trip to NY - we will return. Loved Trattoria Trecolori!

STAY AWAY!!! FAR FAR AWAY!!! The service is absolutely atrocious and I have two little kids and now my wife sick with food poisoning. What a mistake going here. I don't even know how they stay in business.

This place was heaven !!!! My boyfriend and I went there a few times and it is officially our Sunday brunch spot ! The owner and baristas are so friendly and the place is spotless clean. Crepes and natural juices are  just amazing.

I came here today with my five-year-old daughter. I have been here before but did not want to rush to judge. Last time I was here my experience was outstanding. I can only say that I'm surprised , and pleasantly so, that my experience was even better in this instance. The wait staff is friendly and helpful. The pizza is consistently delicious. Little Falls has been crying out for a wood-fired pizzeria the office. for a place like this for a long time-I hope that they will be here to stay for a long time!
Best service, best food, best show. All around. If you are near by you must stop by!!

He wait staff is politic but the management is awful!  After spending hundred of dollars one of my party was asked to move to a different seat before we got our food so that they could seat more people. She had to sit on her husbands lap before they had a new seat for her.

The "bouncers"... if you could even call those brutish dumbasses bouncers, are the worst humans in the history. As a former resident of Burlington this used to be a favorite haunt but now due to the bouncing staff's inexplicable policies I will never return. Next time I'm told to go eat a slice of pizza, because at 24  I have a different haircut than my 21 year old self, I'm going to take a piece from Mr. Mike's and shove it down their throat. GFY Nectars. That is all.

Ramen noodles. What's the big deal? Nothing till you try it here. Didn't think ramen noodles could taste so good. Prepare to wait during peak hours. Pro tip: get your name on the list and have them call you when your table is almost ready while you bar hop around the area.

This was an absolutely amazing meal. My boyfriend and weren't incredibly hungry so we split the set price menu special, which comes with a starter and an entree. We got the beef tartar. It was so good! Just the right combination of textures. The pork chop was next and it was so tender! I've never had it so tender before. It was well paired with brussel sprouts and an apple mustard. Great service too! Highly recommended.
Probably the best kebabs in ny   It really is a little shack but don't let the appearance fool you. Their house goes good with fries or chicken.
Great place. good food and wonderful service.  Very affordable for the fine dining place in the city

Food is great.  Excellent comfort food (and I mean showing up after a break-up and needing to eat your emotions away excellent).  The problem is they are always short staffed, the wait (not only to be seated, but to get your food AND the check) is really long, and you'll be questioning if it's worth the wait after you've been seated.  Great food, not so great waiting for everything after sitting.
This is the best place in Philadelphia to get a cheesesteak I always go cheese wiz wit onions

Soooo good. Definitely some of the best friend chicken I've had. And that Mac and cheese, ugh, I drool thinking of it. The staff is extremely polite and a pleasant. I've never had to wait more than 5 minutes to get a seat. I love the decor and the vibe. And I always laugh when I use the bathroom because I know how it used to look when the venue was Max Fish haha.

Food is amazing but customer service sucks. The waitresses took my food without asking me if I was done. Very rude service but food was amazing. That was my first and last time there because customer service matters more to me.

Delicious!  Great ambiance and service too! Only things, vegetarian options are a bit of a treasure hunt on the menu and unlike it says on yelp it is in the two dollar sign price range. I will definitely be back!
Great sports bar. Many big screens. Polite and friendly staff. More upscale. Food is excellent. Highly recommend.
Ate there last night.  Indian food there was excellent.  Indo Chinese was pretty okay.  I have had good meals here on several occasions.

By accident I went to Taqueria, and  I can say that was one of the best burritos I ever had. The servers are very helpful and friendly, the food is excellent with an assortment of sauces and lots of taco chips. The fish tacos were excellent,  fresh and delicious. I must return for more. I highly recommend this place!!!
Sat at the bar for cocktails. The bartenders were quick with service and the drinks were delicious! Very cool spot for a extraordinary cocktail.

Run the other way.  FAST!   Horrible iPad ordering system.  A million servers but the slowest service. Food came out cold.  Go to any other place to eat in the airport but do not waste your time here.  Worst food and service I have ever experience in any airport.  You have been warned.

The meatballs are flavorless. The cheese used on the pizza is from a bag (not fresh and/or shredded mozzarella). The owner is always right not the customer. Furthermore, the owner worked for that superior restaurant down the block (Ginos) and tried to ape their recipes. Nice try. Too bad so sad......That's all....

This place was awesome great atmosphere they have a huge front room with a bar in it tables set up and there is a long hallway going to the back which leads to another room with a few tvs and speakers coat hangers on the walls a bunch of tables The whole place also was so very clean and awesome the owner was so nice we sat and talked to her when we got there she was so nice and awesome the whole place was super clean even the bathrooms Drink specials were affordable and great they had a live band garden state radio and they were amazing it felt like we were all at a concert this place is great for large groups we had about 20 people in our party there was only street parking The only thing I didn't like about the place was the girl who served us she seemed a little stupid and she was a bit nasty she gave me a problem at first about not having a card to pay my bill with because she wanted to open a tab and didn't want me to pay cash but I told her I didn't have a card and I was paying cash or I wouldn't get anything she constantly gave me checks after everything I ordered which was annoying and I didn't have the exact amount of the bill I was giving big bills and she wouldn't give me my change she took it all so I didn't leave her a tip because she kept all of my change from all 3 of my bills so I assumed she was just keeping my change as her tip which honestly is wrong and pissed me off I won't get food here again because of it and I will only order beer at the bar I will never get a table here again because of that Also the bouncers at the end of the night were rather rude yelling at us non stop and pushing us out the door telling us we had to leave if we're not part of the band over and over and made us all stand out in the cold to wait for our cabs Other than the server keeping my change and the rude bouncer I loved it here not sure if I would come back because of that but the band was great
Good solid place, cute backyard for patrons
They recycle food from the previous days and the food is SOOOOOO  oily,  greasy and idisgusting. You get what you paid for.

Some people on the staff are friendly.  Others are distant and unhelpful.  The food is good and there's always a great variety of beer available.  It's probably best that you can figure out a rough idea of what you want though.
Finally a legitimate sports bar with great food in Center City/ Graduate Hospital. Awesome interior, views and service.

We love coming here for the HAPPY HOURS (4-6:30) - they are amazing! Half price apps - flat bread, ribs, sliders - and $4 draft beers. Awesome food at half the price. The atmosphere is modern - cozy - intimate all in one. Our waiter Marc was very attentive and friendly ... we split a burger, and Marc thoughtfully had it come out on 2 plates with our own sides of fries -- very convenient! My boyfriend & I have been here over a dozen times and have always had a great experience!
It doesn't get any better. The parking and location are perfect. Prices are in line with portions and  pig wings!!!! I always knew they could fly. Get the plate of meat. It is soooo good.
Never know the texture of pancake could be as minute as this, nice.

There is nothing wrong with a $6 plate/platter or $4 sandwich of chicken over rice or combo(gyro/chicken over rice) with the white and spicy red sauce. There is always a line though. Today, I waited around 30 minutes in the 20 degree weather to get my food and it was well worth it! Even if you are a vegetarian, they do have fallafel over rice too! I would highly recommend this food cart to all tourists and of course, the native New Yorkers know about it already!

If you can stand the lines, or get there when it isn't crowded, the Halal Guys is absolutely delicious! For $6-8, you get a big plate of rice, lettuce, and perfectly cooked schwarma meat or falafel. This is not only how food stands should be done, but how middle eastern food should be done in this city. Not to mention, the guys are very nice, and will make your food any way you want it. Yeah, the lines are long, but the lines are long for a reason.

Have been coming here for years! Can't beat a $6 plate that could feed a medieval village! The guys are always ready for the crowds that approach them each and everyday. Can't see this business ever failing. 1. Will continue eating here 2. Would recommend it to anyone PS. Don't get the hot sauce!    One of the first times I ate there in the early 2000's I burned my mouth so severely I didn't eat the stuff for a year! Maybe don't get as much as me!

I just had a wonderful dinner  last night at Osteria. There were 8 of us and it was packed, however we only waited a few minutes for our table. I had the mozzarella appetizer and it was awesome. I shared the rib eye with another one of our group and it was delicious my only complaint was that there was only about 2 tablespoons of mashed potatoes. This was definitely not enough for two diners.For dessert I had three of the best donuts I have ever had with a vanilla glaze and toffee crunch topping. All in all a tremendous meal. I hope you at Osteria take my suggestion to at least double the potatoes that come with the rib eve. Another couple in our group had the rib eye and they had the same complaint. I recommend this restaurant to all and we look forward to coming back soon.

Awesome service and atmosphere! I've been here quite a few times and that is definitely going to continue. Whether it's lunch or dinner, the prices are very reasonable, compared to all the other restaurants in the Hells Kitchen area. You will definitely leave full. The decor is amazing, you are definitely entering a mysterious, yet beautiful realm. From what I have seen, lunch is usually a quieter time to have a relaxed one-on-one. The lunch specials are a MUST, they include one appetizer and one entree. The portions are definitely good enough to fill a hungry chap. The chicken skewers are just generous and juicy. For lunch, I usually get the Pad Woon Sen. This is stir-fried glass vermicelli mixed with vegetables, egg, and shrimp. Again, the portion is very generous, and the taste is just addicting. Now the good part: dinner. Their squid ink spaghetti is their own specialty. It's a bit spicy, but it is balanced out with the rest of the dish which is filled with calamari, shrimp, and vegetables. The pasta itself with the sauce is just enough on its own. If you are a first-timer at here, I definitely say go all the way and hit up this dish. It might be a little dark at dinner, and the noise level is definitely up there that you will definitely have to talk louder to be heard. But overall, it is a reliable, affordable, and very satisfying place.
Best Pho in Parsippany!  Great food and super friendly service. This place has a new regular customer. You will not be disappointed.

Stopped in for brunch and had the Pork Roll breakfast sandwich.  It was a special so I wanted to try it out.  Several meaty slices on focaccia topped with a fried green tomato, cheese, sunny egg, and honey mustard drizzle.    One of the best breakfast sandwiches in the city.  Please please please put this on the menu!  Staff was great as usual.

More hyped up than it should be. From the beginning: We made a reservation (DO THIS) and arrived a little early but only had to wait for about 5 minutes for our table. We chatted with the hostess who was very sweet and welcoming, poor girl has to stand next to that door that lets in the freezing air which we felt from our table(!!!!)..she weighed about 5lbs she's going to get hypothermia. The tables are very small and close together, my wife was basically cuddling with the woman next to her. The waitress was okay, I think her deep scary voice threw me off but the service was good. She explained all the items on the menu that we had questions about and was a solid server she just lacked a sweet attitude. The wine list is incredibly lacking and overpriced. I got the meatball appetizer and really didn't care for it but my lamb shank was very good. why no baklava on the dessert menu?! i was too disappointed to order anything. The manager or owner came over and spoke to us as we were leaving and he smelled like cigarettes and booze. I just wasn't in love.

This place has gone down hill since the owner sold it to the new person. For example I had the chili from here and lets just say it turned my lower body into the German Luftwaffe during WW2 and the bathroom was Great Britain. Countless innocents were lost on that day as the bombing campaign waged for hours. Butt Rockets!!! All praise to the Grundle Overlords!! G.O. 4 Life!!

Amazing scenery! Perfect place to take someone out on a date!   Tentative staff as well.  Place closes in an hour but it's still packed and customers keep coming in! Get the pitcher of sangria, it's top notch!
had better chicken then this place.

Its a nice spot but they need better management. I went there for my first and last time this summer. It was overly crowded, I put my name on that stupid paper for a table of two. After waiting 30 minutes a couple that just walked in got a seat. Ok whatever no big deal right, so i got the managers attention and I explained the situation. I was told  I had a seat, I followed the waiter and there was still no seat for us. After waiting another 30 mins while standing over people while they ate, we got a table in the old front entrance. I made a scene , I don't care. I didn't wait over an hour to sit at the door. It was clearly the front door, I had an exit sign over my head. I wished I didn't spend my money . There was nothing memorable about the food at all or the drinks.
From the west coast and frustrated by awful NYC Mexican food?  This is THE PLACE that will rescue your lonely taste buds!  Delicious!
good value, but suggest going off peak hours. Otherwise be prepare for long waiting queues.
last three times I dined here, they brought out one person's meal after the rest of the table was done eating.  good food but not worth the aggravation.
Bartender is excellent and knows their beer and wine. Food will leave your tastes buds in a good place without the meal being too heavy. Highly highly recommended
I tried the Kimchi flavor with chicken, it was just amazing!!! Food is served pretty fast and barmaids are nice! I will go back for sure!
Best beef shawarma sandwich! I tried a bunch of places closer to where I work, but I give up. My shawarma cravings have to wait until I can make time to go to Falafel Hut!!
The only thing i will miss when I leave NYC Most awesome restobar/lounge/ in 10 mile area. Try Black Bass  , it will blow your senses !!

I have been to this place for lunch and dinner and have not nada bad meal here. They have a very good selection on their menu. I like their breakfast type selections and went with one of the custom waffle dishes. Very good. Also have had some good sandwiches here. Have not had the coffee but they did look good too.

Craft house! What a place. An awesome environment to kick back and have some refreshing beers. There's a nice selection to choose from and they change the options pretty often so there's always something new and interesting to choose from. The food is delicious and I recommend the pineapple habanero wings. If you can't decide on food or beer because there's just too much greatness going on, ask Dan the man. The guy always  has good recommendations and ain't too bad on the eyes. All in all, I leave here satisfied every time from a quick beer to booze filled night with food. 5 stars! Mmmmmm beer....
By far best BBQ spot on staten island! Doesnt even feel like staten island inside. Hipster and trendy with an extensive beer list.

Food was awesome. Had chicken/waffels. Others had brisket, fried chicken, and a veggie burger. Sides were great service also great. Just can't say enough about craft house. Will definitely add to my "A" list.
The craft house is great!  Came out with freinds and had the best service, food and beer selection on Staten Island.  Really love the place. Love all of us. Place on fleek.

Stopped by on a cold December day for something to warm me up. Amazing location. Staff is great and very friendly. Definitely will return based on my experience with the bartenders. Five stars based solely on those two Irish guys behind the bar. Keep up the good work fellas.
Stella 34 Trattoria has some of the most unique Italian dishes in New York! Great view from the 6th fl of Macy's too.
Good stuff. Simple but tasty. They have all the makings of a nice, quick dining experience.  What were you expecting--Iron Chef?

While this is my first review, and my yelp credibility may be lacking with this being so, I thought it was proper timing to give Da Legna a review. Having grown up in the restaurant industry around New Haven, and being a huge advocate of the city's pizza, it is difficult for me to even consider a pizza establishment with less than a 25 year history under its belt.   That said, Da Legna pizza is worthy of New Haven brick and mortar.  After our traditional Christopher Martins road race this past Sunday, friends and I gave it a shot when we saw Modern was closed. Poised and ready to move on to one of the next NH pizza giants, friends had already been sat. The artisan pies, craft beers, Edison lighting, reggae, and smiling waitress beat my skepticism into enthusiastic acceptance. The bartender delivered the last pitcher of Green Flash West Coast IPA (score!), along with a detailed description of its tap replacement. Dude had some good beer knowledge, which goes a long way with me. Not expecting much from the pies, the margharita, rustica, Clark street and a pork and cheddar were all outrageous. Service, product, and atmosphere are essential to a successful business in the new haven restaurant scene and Da Legna has it figured out.  With a very cool bar room, and it's somewhat outskirt location, I will no doubt be back.

I have lived in Belleville for about 7 years, in New Jersey since 1969. I love diners but have not always been lucky enough to live near one that's consistently good. The Arlington has been a place where I can get a delicious meal and leave feeling better than when I came in. The soup is fantastic (thank Pedro for this - my favorites are the Yankee Bean, Chicken Vegetable and Lentil), the daily specials are fresh and tasty (tend to favor the stuffed cabbage, pot roast or turkey dinner), the breakfast menu is good 24/7 (go for the Florentine Omelet or the whole wheat banana pancakes), and the desserts are "to live for" - especially the cheese cake of course. The staff has always been decent and even delightful at times. I can't speak for the daytime (except for beautiful Barbara who is dearly missed), but I can give feedback on the later afternoon and evening folks: David and Nick have been excellent hosts; servers Janice, Bo, Colleen, Patrice, Mary and others have been efficient, kind, hard working, funny as hell and/or just plain nice; the busboys work hard at cleaning and carrying away. I know we all love to complain and, of course, it's possible to have a bad experience even in a great place (I have had a couple of hamburgers that needed repair). But that can be true anywhere. The thing about the Arlington, for me, is that it has been consistently good and even great in quality of food and service. And on the rare occasion I've had a problem, I can courteously call someone's attention to it and they will do something to make it right and do so without a hassle. If you want a reasonably priced, generous and consistently good place to eat, I enthusiastically recommend the Arlington; it has been that for me.

I had a chilly cheeseburger with fries and my wife had stake fajitas. Food did not taste bad, in fact it didn't have much taste at all and was just bland. The food was also slow in coming.  The waitress was very polite and kept interrupting our conversation every 5 minutes to see if we needed anything.  Environment was run down with cafeteria style tables and chairs.  Urinal did not flush in men's room and the stall was being used to keep cleaning supplies.

I went with my husband and son for Sunday brunch. This is a busy, vibrant place with warm atmosphere and some creative touches to the decor. We took a walk while we waited for a table. There is some interesting architecture in the neighborhood. We ordered Bloody Marys, which were appropriately spicy. (We opted for the "regular" as opposed to the version with shrimp, etc.) I had shrimp and grits -- lots of shrimp and the grits were creamy and good. The boys had eggs with anduoille and bacon -- also great. The beer list looked interesting. The service was friendly and timely. Clearly the staff enjoys working there.

BAD EXPERIENCE.  LIKE I TOLD THEM, I'LL NEVER GO BACK.  The sushi is good but nothing extra special.  For the price, the servings are smaller than most places I go.  And I go to a LOT of sushi places.  The tables are small, and it's dark in there.  I've gone probably five times since they opened.  It was always an OK experience.  We went last night because we bought a Groupon.  That is literally the only reason we went there instead of the many sushi places between here and there.  The Groupon said that you had to have reservations to use it but I've had TONS of Groupons honored where the situation didn't meet all the criteria listed in the small print.  Plus, there was no need for reservations.  When we arrived, only one table had customers in it!  When we left 40 minutes later, there were two other tables with customers.  Still, when I showed the waitress the Groupon, she looked at it for a moment and said "Did you make a reservation?"  I said "No.  That's not usually a problem though."  I probably should have pointed out that the place was empty.  Now she could have just honored the Groupon without even bringing up the small print.  Instead, she took the Groupon (in other words, she took my phone) into the kitchen and returned 35 seconds later saying "You can't use this because you didn't make a reservation."  I said, "Really?"  She said, "Yeah.  I"m sorry."  I said, "Well that's OK but I'll never come back here again."  Her response:  "Oh."  Apparently they don't need the business (despite all the empty tables).  Thing is:  We don't need them either.  There must be several HUNDRED places in Philadelphia to get sushi.  Good sushi can be made quite crappy when served by a restaurant that doesn't care about the customer experience.  So one star.  I'll never go back.  When the restaurant goes out of business, I'll contact Groupon and ask them to refund the price I paid for the deal.  Cest la vie!

WOW today was my first time at Vesta and needless to say I will be a forever returning customer! My experience from top to bottom and from food to service was absolutely flawless..I'm talking even down to the selection of drafts beers to the perfect taste of my coca cola. Our bartender and server Chelsea was amazing, she topped off the experience with a delightful attitude and unmatched professionalism. It all left an impression on me and I will most definitely be referring people I know! If I were you reading this right now I'd be on my way already!!!

Had my first meal here recently and I have to say, I was impressed! The food was quite good, though a little pricey for my taste (but we were aware of that going in). Someone suggested that we try out the Guac, and they weren't kidding, it was delicious! The atmosphere was nice, not trying too hard. Overall we really enjoyed ourselves and are glad we decided to try Lolita out of the strip of restaurants on the same block. Would probably go back again for a special occasion dinner!

Service was disappointing. Food was not as good as we remembered but still ok. But service  was just bad - we were given a table that was too small for our party. We didn't get enough plates or water and had to follow up on the sake we ordered.

Just wanted a chill spot to grab a beer and a quick bite and this was place was great. Super friendly bartender, amazing apps, and great sandwiches. The sweet potato fries are awesome too. Will definitely be back

The pizza here are such big slices and soo cheesy but you will want to share a slice as a few bites will make you feel full/bloated. Good pizza, not your typical NY thin crust pizza but line is usually out the door late nights.

I'm really into this place.  It is as down-to-earth and polite as service and food can get for a neighborhood bar, and the kitchen puts out consistent and delicious food.  In particular their "Hey Stud" sandwich is phenomenal!   Anybody who is going out for a low-key beer and sandwich should pop in to this place and get some tasty stuff.  I cannot stress enough how polite the bartenders and servers are.

Every now and then, through sheer luck, you find an amazing restaurant that you otherwise would never have experienced. Cascalote Latin Bistro is one such restaurant. My girlfriend and I were walking through Spanish Harlem, looking for a place to eat, when we noticed a cute and cozy 20 seat Latin restaurant with a very appealing menu.   I've worked in the restaurant industry for over 12 years and I can honestly say that our first visit produced nothing less than exceptional results. My girlfriend ordered the the jalapeno marinated pork chop with smoked bacon and sauteed onions. The pork chop was perfectly tender with just the right amount of heat. The bacon added a hint of smoke and the carm onions brought out a sweet crunch that brought the whole dish together. I'm normally a gentleman on a date, but I have to admit that I stole an extra piece while she wasn't looking. It was that good. I had the slow roasted short ribs with the crispy potato croqueta topped with a shaved radish salad. The short ribs were flaky and delicious with a hint of beer in the marinade brought out a nutty aftertaste. The croqueta was a perfect addition in that it added body, texture, and crunch to the dish; not to mention that it soaked up the delicious sauce the coated the short ribs. And the crispy radishes were an ideal match with the soft moist short ribs. Unfortunately we had no room left for dessert but we both agreed that, after we told everyone we knew about this place, we would certainly go back. I advice anyone reading this who is looking for unique and perfectly executed Latin cuisine to take a trip up to SpaHa and experience this absolute gem of a restaurant.

I do not like writing I star reviews but this place was TERRIBLE the service was not what I expected of a Cracker Barrel like I ordered a coffee and it took 10 minutes through the PLACE WAS EMPTY the food was HORRIBLE SERVICE and food was awful so I Just left l will never come back

Perfect place to take my wife for her birthday. If you like meat - take the cote de boeuf. If you don't like meat - take the cote de boeuf. You'll like meat afterwards. Sat in the front room and Leslie was a star. Glasses never got close to empty and answers came before the questions.

I love love love this place. I'm from the same home town as the chef and the food is so authentic. A little on the pricey side, but totally worth it. It's byob and you have to try the lamb and the duck, so good.

This market is so awesome. It was my first spot after checking into my hotel and I spent almost two hours exploring this amazing place. Upon entering the market, I was overcome by all the various shops. In every direction, it seemed never-ending. There was soul food, Chinese food, donuts, bakeries, fresh produce, fresh seafood, hoagies, cheesesteaks, crepes, etc. The list goes on! I had the intention of going to Tommy DiNic's for lunch. They're famous for their roast pork sandwich with broccoli rabé. The line wrapped around the entire counter and to the soul food seating area. Many other shops had long lines as well, with eager and hungry folks waiting for a bite to eat. There is something for everyone at this market. It's a blend of Farmers Markets with fresh fruits, vegetables, seafood, and meats to various shops that offer food to eat right there and then. It's enormous and often packed, especially on the weekends. If you wanted to, you could spend all day or all of your vacation at Reading Terminal Market. There's just so much to see and do. Absolutely recommend coming to Reading Market, if not for a bite to eat, at least to see it for yourself.

Why can't this place be in Verona, NJ??? This is exactly  what a town tavern should be. Great Beer, Great Atmosphere, and Great Food. Just try the bar pie, and you'll be hooked. I absolutely love this place.   The bartenders are always happy to see you, and the service in the dining room is just as good. This is one of those places where I could sit back watch a game for a few hours and chill with friends. Cheers to Maggies!

Simple perfection, made with love, great service.... Had brunch, came back later to eat again. Always a nice crowd, people laughing, having a great time. Sit at the bar if Chris is bartending, Teresa is also a great server... Just good people with great hearts, an eye for detail, and amazing charisma. All around an excellent experience. Try the Dutch baby pancakes.... The burger... And work through the drink menu... All of it.

The burger is excellent and I'm glad I went. Excellent beer selection. Also had the deviled eggs which were nice. Place is a bit cramped and a bit worn, still enjoyed it. The waitress was fantastic... great attitude and friendly. Not my every day kind of spot but good once in a while.
Cozy restaurant, get there early for a table or be prepared to wait. Order Devils on Horseback as a starter and the burger, arguably one of the best in NYC.

This is a great hidden spot on Sullivan with fast service. Their portions are great; the people behind the counter are very generous, warm, easy-going. I highly recommend any of their falafel foods. Their grape leaves have great texture and taste. Last time I went their I also tried their beets dishes (they have a beets/eggs sandwich, and a beets/carrots side) both are spectacular with a slight spicy kick going. Can't recommend it enough.

Right off the bat, I have to explain that the star rating I gave is about the overall experience, not about the food and service itself, which was quite good. We bought a groupon for an 8-course omakase sushi meal. The value was supposedly $140, for which we spent $80. $80 is still a considerable sum to spend for a sushi meal (we pay $65 at our local spot for their sushi-for-two which includes soup, salad and tea, and we leave stuffed). Omakase means "I'll leave it to you", so we knew that it would be a chef's choice meal. We were looking forward to it. The only thing we were able to select was one specialty roll per person, which was the final, 8th course. The courses came out at a nice pace, but understand that a "course" really was a taste. For instance, one half of a shrimp, one tablespoon of lump crab with slices of avocado over it, or two slivers of tuna.  I would call each of the "courses" an amuse bouche - a little something to excite the palate. Now, don't get me wrong.... each and every taste set before us was delicious. But, the courses were laughably small. We were hungry at the end of the meal. Not pleasantly sated.... we were hungry. The bill came, and they had already added in 20% for the gratuity, and charged us each $3.50 for the green tea (a tea bag. high quality tea bag, but a tea bag, all the same). I've never been charged for tea at a Japanese or Chinese restaurant. We were surprised. So, we spent $80 on the Groupon, then another $46 and change at the restaurant for gratuity, tea and tax. We could have eaten very well elsewhere for $126. Had we actually PAID $70 per person for the omakase, it would not have been pretty. I don't judge value on how full I am when I leave a restaurant, and I enjoy fine dining. We were happy to spend the $80 for this special 8-course meal for two. But we left feeling totally and utterly ripped off. Food is delicious, value is non existent.
The corn is a MUST!!! The entrees are ok- I recommend getting the corn- to die for.

Ting Wong used to be my go to restaurant in Chinatown.  I would go there at least twice a week and they always knew my order before the words came out of my mouth.  They always got my order correct and I was in and out in a  very timely fashion.  The food tasted wonderful and the portion sizes were plenty.   When Ting Wong reopened, after a much needed renovation, I was beyond excited.  Unfortunately, my experience was very disappointing.  The service was slow, unfriendly and they got my order wrong even after I repeated myself several times.  The person taking orders was very unorganized and seemed not able to handle the stress of the lunch hour. Once getting back to my office, I was hoping for the comforting food that I have had time and time again from Ting Wong.  The portion sizes were smaller and the food lacked the robust flavor from previous visits.  Even the roast pork was dry. With a heavy heart, I have not been back to Ting Wong.  I have spoken with many coworkers who used to frequent Ting Wong as much as myself.  We have all concluded that the stellar customer service that was once there is significantly lacking and that the quality of food that once was served, has greatly diminished.   I miss my lunches from Ting Wong.  What used to be a wonderful gem in Chinatown is now just another restaurant amongst many.
better then the other fast food restaurant that a block away.
This place was excellent. Can't wait to go back for more! Plenty of options (especially for vegetarians like myself) and good service. Calm and inviting atmosphere as well. Recommended for sure.

Love, love love this place!  best BBQ in Queens!  I love their Burnt Ends, and the Sweet Potato wedges and the Mac and cheese are my go to sides!  They just opened up a new space next door with s full liquor bar featuring Bourbons, Whiskeys and Moonshine!  The Apple Moonshine is my favorite!  Can't wait for the summer so I can hang out in their cool backyard!

This place has quickly become my weekend brunch spot. Ate their yesterday with my sister. I had the Fried Chicken on Brioche sandwich, Parmesan truffle fries, Sauteed garlic and Collards and the Blood Orange Lemonade, she had the the Elvis Waffle and Gingerbread Coffee.  I'd have to say that this was the best sandwich I have ever eaten and I've eaten many! The Chef makes your food to order which takes time and I love this. It's intimate and feels as if someone is cooking in your home and last but not least, the staff is really friendly. This is definitely not the place to go to if you want a rushed and forgettable experience.

The decor is beautiful but the entire bar area smells like a deep fryer! It took a long time for my date and I to pick menu items as the large menu was very uninspired. The  plating was unappealing and the food was executed sub par for the price.  Plenty of better choices withing walking distance!
Great value for lunch pastas. Also decent for dinner if you want a quick meal especially if on the go. Great sauce!
Great staff. The manager Carlos makes you feel welcome. Try their sangrias it's the best. Overall great experience
Such a delicious gem in the city! Perfect for a date or a night out with the girls! Highly recommend the vegetarian pasta dish alongside a glass or two of pinot noir!
Such an interesting little place! Great food, great drinks. The confessional wall is fun and interesting to read. Music was excellent was well.

Walking into this restaurant, I was pleasantly surprised by the ambiance and the friendliness of the servers. My friends are from Nepal, so they ordered a variety of dishes for me to try. Every single dish was amazing. Momos were my favorite. The food was quick to arrive, and they were gone from our plates in minutes, because it was so delicious! We also had live music upstairs which we thoroughly enjoyed. Would definitely be back again.

Food is tasty and inexpensive. Waitstaff is attentive and food is served fast. My favorites are the strawberry margarita, Caesar Salad and Chorizo cheese fondue. Great place to go on a budget. will return!

Phenomenal! It is a shame there aren't more Trinidadian Restaurants throughout the state, but this one is worth the HOUR drive for me. The Aloo Pie and the Chana Aloo Roti wrap is worth every mile, and each time as I finish my last bite I want more. Keep up the great work!
Hands down the BEST chicken mahkni FOREVER.  Go to the buffet from 1-5pm !!! it's onlyy $8.99~~~

I have literally Never understood the hype with this pizza.  I could buy a frozen box pizza at 7/11 better than this.... come on guys. Someone made up some hyped rumor years back that this was "The best pizza in NJ" and people have been pretending it is true ever since. But it's not. and this pizza has no flavor. And it is burnt and cooked to the point of shoe leather. It is a frozen stepchild of Celeste and the restaurant is dark and dreary. Sorry. Admit it, people. They make so much money off your make-believe hype that they have no reason to care what I think, though, anyway.

Great job renovating an old landmark in town.  Great atmosphere, great food and great service. Also allow for private parties which is great. Check out the root cellar room. We had our rehearsal dinner there. Awesome job all around.
Best Ramen we've had outside of NYC and Mitsuwa Marketplace. The portions are just right too.

Ok so at first we were a little nervous about this place cause this it is located in a hotel.... But this place is unbelievable! We got the Notali 5 pizza and lasagna. All the pasta is made in house.  Staff is extremely friendly. Must get the wings! Ask about weekly specials. Happy hour everyday. Menu very well described.

we waited in the cold almost 20 minutes but the home fries were worth it.  VERY SMALL place but all of our food was good!  the cinnamon roll pancake thing was really good as well.  we sat at the bar and the door was opened so often, we were cold for most of the time. it was good overall though.
Great place for brunch or lunch. Nice menu that will please anyone with very different tastes.
Get the spaghetti and savor every bite. You will not be disappointed. Also must mention the bread basket is phenom.

We had our wedding reception at Cowgirl Sea Horse this past June, and it was the best time imaginable! Dana was extremely helpful in organizing our big day, and the food and ambience were exactly what we were looking for. We had a casual, fun night with a sit-down dinner, followed by a DJ & dancing for about 80 people. We received rave reviews of the food from our friends and family. We had a bit of a delay on the food service, which was somewhat due to our confusing menu choice identifier. Because of this delay, Dana allowed us to stay a bit later that night which was greatly appreciated! The service staff was accommodating and was always great on every occasion that we visited before the reception, as well as during it. As former food servers for many years of our lives, lack of attitude and prompt service is especially important to us. You should have your wedding reception there too!

I give 5 starts because the service was impeccable, the food was delicious and the ambiance was excellent. We loved the fried pickles and the fried Oreos. Also don't be afraid of the bloody with bacon and a pickled egg, it's amazing!

First time visiting last night. We had a big group so we got lots of food!! Ordered pesto gnocchi malfatti (spelling?), butternut squash ravioli, polenta, and mussels in white sauce all for appetizer. 2 of those are entrees but we passed them around for appetizer. All were incredible. For dinner (like we needed more) we had the Montclair pizza (truffle oil!!!) a margarita pizza we added caramelized onions, mushrooms and spinach to and the butternut squash pizza. Oh my god! What that pizza oven does is something special but the flavors were outstanding. A couple of people also got soup (escarole & beans) and they raved. To top it off was the nutella pizza. It was so light and good! Can't wait to go back
Great beers
Awesome food! Great atmosphere! Smaller portions but the quality makes up for it.
Red Eye is the bomb. The staff are great, coffee is well made and food is tasty. Brunch can be really busy, but overall, a mainstay of Montclair! Plus wifi to do work!

Love love love this place! My friends and I go here probably once a week. The happy hour specials are great (half price margaritas and nachos) and the food is always fantastic! My usual go to is a burrito, but I recently tried the enchiladas, and I have to say my usual might be changing! The tacos are great too (especially if you catch them on dollar taco night) I could eat the chorizo and potato tacos until I explode. The draft list is pretty reasonable too, and they have a nice selection of bottles. The recent expansion of the dining area, and the additional of take out bottles really solidifies Loco Pez as a place I recommend to everyone who hasn't been there before!

Pizza is great!! CASH ONLY!!!! A small cheese pizza cost around $20 and toppings are $4 each... The service was horrible though and ruined the experience! We only saw our server twice (to place our order and to give us our check) . I had to ask a different server for water and a straw. Lastly, we waited for over 10 mins try to pay for our food and ended up getting a different server to process our payment. Sadly it ruined our experience and I will likely not go back.

Everything I've read about this tiny hole in the wall restaurant is true: great food, great prices, great speed at preparing and dishing it up to take home with you. There is no seating/dining as such, unless sitting on the fruit crates out the front n the sidewalk counts! But the fried pork dumplings at a buck a serve (three or four tasty dumplings for that!) are as good as it gets. Lottsa other good food available.

Based on the reviews, I decided to check this place out.  I placed my order, picked up my food, ever so hungry. I get home and just as I'm about to dig in I see a long strand of hair on top of the ginger and wasabi.  Very disappointed and turned off, I just dumped it in the garbage. :-(
I loved everything about this place from the owner to the food and atmosphere. The Cheesecake was excellent. Loving the grilled octopus. The spinach with feta was delicious.

This was the best authentic Mexican food I've had in years. The food was served fresh and delicious, the waitresses were attentive to our needs and always had a smile. The atmosphere was uplifting and friendly and I felt like I was eating at home with one big family. This is a must visit if you like Mexican food. I highly recommend it.

I was there last night. Ordered a beef gyro and chicken combo platter. Instead of beef gyro they gave me chicken gyro then they replaced it with beef gyro. I had to return that too cus it had human hairs in it. I told them I don't need it anymore they charged me for chicken combo platter and I was out. Not going back again.
Great food, great drinks! The duck papardelle was outstanding! Very cool atmosphere

We had our office party here and it was just an AMAZING experience.  Thumbs up on the: 1. Food -  Excellent balance with quality engraved in each aspect of the food.  The food tastes brilliant, and little touches and attention to detail on presentation just makes the food even better. 2. Drinks -  Perfect drinks with a touch of class.  Love the metal/steel straws that come with every drink 3. Service - Even though it was a large party, services were just on the mark.  From the host of the establishment taking out coats, to the servers who were patient, and ensuring that everyone was attended to, and following up to ensure that they had everything they needed. 4. Decor -  I have been to many many indian places but this one just exudes class and you can see how well thought out the everything was.  This is a place I can hang out with friends and family and just relax to good drinks and foof...or have a formal client meeting as well. 5. Attention to detail - Just what it says....embedded into everything that they do. In short, hands down one of the best indian restaurants I have been to!

This place has the absolute worst raviolis I have even tasted. I took one bite and sent them back because they were hard (not cooked all the way) and cold. The "seafood" filling tasted like metal (canned seafood) and it was just all-around awful. I may have considered coming back to try something else on the menu but THEY CHARGED ME for the raviolis that I took ONE BITE OF and sent back. I have never sent food back ever in my life and I am not cheap, but trying to charge me 24$ for 4 raviolis that i took one bite of was just completely absurd. It didn't even come with a salad. Rip off, server has zero personality and horrible food to boot. I would stay FAR AWAY from this horrible restaurant.
Pizza was out 5 min after ordering. It is Monday at 2 pm...  Good but not insane to get the 5th star.
Great experience. Very happy place. Owned by a family, obvious they have passion and love for their business. Definitely recommend "Ajarian khachapuri"  and carrot cake!

Very good cheesesteaks made fresh to order and 100% delicious. Cash only and expect to wait in a small line. We want there and to the place across the street, and Pats won. You will need extra napkins of course, and the seating is only outdoors. Some may say there are better places and maybe so, but I have not found it. We love Pats and we will be returning soon.
Cheesesteak with an attitude.  They win the Pat's vs. Gino's contest. Good greasy food !

Epic. Life changing. Exhilarating. Eating a Pat's Cheese Steak with Cheese Wiz is like dying and going to heaven. Why even bother going to Geno's... that would be truly un-American! Oh, but may avoid Pat's King of Steaks at night. You did watch the intro to Fresh Prince right?

I dropped by while picking my girlfriend up from the train station.  I came straight from work so was still in my Air Force uniform.  Pat's wouldn't take my money and gave me a sandwich and cheese fries on the house.  I tried to give them some money but they wouldn't hear of it.  Thanks for the great food guys!  We always appreciate it!

We really wanted to love this place, turns out we liked it...mostly. I hope the operators read this because they need some help. The food had a great mix of flavors and the variety was impressive. But, Way, Way, Way to much salt. It overpowered the other flavors. And, they need support on the Beer selections. There are beers that could really compliment the foods. On the night we went the beer choices were week and flavorless. They need some robust selections, some hoppier selections would help.
You know I wish they wouldn't keep things hot in plastic but the food is good.
This is my first time to come here , the food look great and the people r kind. The tacos  taste yummy yummy ....

I went here on a Sunday night for dinner. The place was pretty quiet, but that's to be expected of most new restaurants, especially as Los Imperios is not heavily advertised. I'm a huge fan of Peruvian food (Cora Cora, Vista Allegre, etc.) so I decided to give this a shot. The restaurant's location is pretty central. It's on the edge of Blue Back Square (diagonally across the Farmington Ave from Whole Foods) and parking is easily available in their private lot or street parking on Arnold Way. The servers were very courteous. They started us off with roasted corn, green sauce, and bread. The corn is pretty unique and I would love to replicate their recipe at home. For appetizers, we shared Causa De Pollo (mashed potatoes stuffed with chicken), which was pretty good. For the entree, we got the Chicken & Beef Chaufa (a fried rice dish with fried egg, chicken, steak, and vegetables that goes really well with green sauce) and Mixed Saltudo, which came with fried plantains that were very nicely done. As you will find with most Peruvian food, it tasted amazing (and it was not heavy on the salt, which is a general theme in some Peruvian dishes I have tried elsewhere). The portions were big enough to take half of everything home (hence why I didn't have room for dessert) and prices were very reasonable. The whole dinner ended up costing around $40 for 2 people. I was having a quiet night in, so didn't go for any alcohol, though they do have a full bar selection. I also hear they have latin dancing on Thursday nights, although I have never been. If you like Peruvian food, I would highly recommend this place. If you have not tried Peruvian food, you're missing out!
No words to express the perfection of the pies made here.  Casual, quality, classic dining... They need to deliver!!!!!!!!!  Thank you for being there for so many years!

This place has the best food around but their prices slowly but surely got out of hand  for a local place. I remember the first time I got food from here the value was awesome I got a burger and fries for little more than 7$ bucks, buffalo chicken tenders and fries for 6$ and when you bit those fries they bit back. Sadly these days my girlfriend and I are better off grabbing lunch once we're in the city,where prices are absurd, or cooking for ourselves considering the cost. Also their hours are absurd for a coffee place, I need you when I'm headed to work or class bean not at 9am. Can't even count the times I've been headed out early and been disappointed by the late opening hours here.

I come here at least twice a month. When I have the time to. The service is always great except for tonight. My waitress just came to check on my table just once.  My friend wanted another coke and of course she had to wait 10 minutes for the server to pass by. I was never asked if I wanted a refill of coffee.  Only came to my table once and disappeared right after. It might be the night shift people but if the service can get better it'll be great.

This is probably my favorite restaurant in the city. Their happy hour is to die for. 3.50 for rolls and $10 Sapporo pitchers!! Amazing!!! Such fresh sushi, and so consistent, the people that work there are so attentive and sweet. Its really cozy, perfect for date night!

Visiting NYC & thought they would be a good place to grab a bite. Yelp says they're open till 4 am. It's 12:35am and they're already closed. I'm definitely not happy I just made 2 girls walk more than 7 blocks to find out they are not open like they claim.
First slice of pie in NYC. Didn't let me down. Thank you for that
It was fantastic. The broth has incredible depth with a slight muskiness to it. Delicious! Buns are to die for...
I'm a new yorker born and raised but this never gets old. Always worth the trek for drunchies or a sober meal. And one of the few things in NYC that still live up to the hype
Man these guys are so good. Always get a large chicken and rice platter, extra white sauce and two lines of the red hot sauce. It's realllly hot.
Nicely made noodles and great service.  The only place I attend in Chinatown besides the Reading Terminal

I live right by Brigantessa and had been anticipating trying it out.  We sat at the bar, had the duck rillette appetizer, which was different, light and delicious as well as the wood smoked octopus.  Great selection of craft beer on tap.  We ordered the Stella pizza and it was unreal.  The pizza crust was shaped into a star and the crust was just the right thickness/saltiness with best tasting dough.  The sauce definitely made the pizza.  I have been a huge fan of Nomad over the past few years but this pizza takes the place as number 1 in Philadelphia.  We also tried the croquette pizza, but I think anything with the red sauce would be delicious.   The bartender was also super friendly and helpful!
beautiful decor, delicious food and the service was awesome.  will certainly be back.

This place is a foodgasm. So authentic and insanely delicious. Their cheese plate was amazing, as was their beef stew. I loved that the staff was French too! Wasn't a huge fan of the brunchy decor, but it really didn't matter because I was in love with this place. Would give more than 5 stars if I could!

Took my son there today for lunch, What has happened to this place, First the waitress was to busy takeing care of her kid instead of taking care of the customers.I ordered the Chicken with Shiitake mushrooms, "which is on the menu" when she brought it out It was made with button mushrooms. I told her that this was not what I ordered. She went back to the kitchen and then told me they were out. I asked why did you serve me something I did not order. she had no answer. I hope the owner reads this and can explain to me why they served me this

This place is a great bar with live music but not a place to go sit for dinner.  The menu is good as far as bar food goes.  The beers are cold and the staff is excellent.  We stop in on Friday or Saturday to catch a band or a DJ. Not a sports bar not a place to eat, basic bar with some food, bands and beer.
Amazing food! Pollo empanadas, ceviche mixto were so delicious. Highly recommend this restaurant. Make reservations because they fill up quick.
Keep your fingers crossed that there isn't a long wait & you get a seat!

All the food at Nico's looks good and is priced right. I've been a customer for years, being on the road a lot and passing through on South Orange Ave or Sanford Ave. Being on a budget, Nico's is great. A whole 13 inch pizza is always $5. - that's enough for 2-3 people. If I have 3 in the car, I'll pick up 2 for lunch. Bottled beverages in the trunk, everyone is satisfied for $10. I often pick up 4 and bring 'em home. Wife doesn't have to cook, and the kids and they're friends can have at it - $20.  Can't beat it. Note: Nico's is closed Sundays, and every other day opens at 11:30 AM closing at 8:30 PM when the steel shutters come down and crime goes up. It's a busy business area in a low budget community by a main intersection. Consistently excellent!
Came all the way from San Diego and walked 3 miles in Philadelphia whether just to taste this treat. I was not disappointed!

This place is awesome! Went here for the first time today and fell in love with the whole experience. A little piece of Italy made its way to Manhattan! I got a sandwich although it was a little salty it still great but the overall atmosphere was incredible. I'm so ready to go back

I went there for the first time last weekend and had a great time. It would make a great date spot but I would really recommend going with a group. That way you can order a bunch of the menu items because you're going to want to try them all. We tried most of the menu that night. The items that stood out: Tuna tar tar - Super fresh flavor and a healthy dose of wasabi. Fried maitake mushroom - Classic fried-food batter on a really tasty mushroom. The duck liver mousse - Super creamy patte served with crusty bread. The overall experience was top notch. We had a super knowledgeable server and I loved the open kitchen layout. It's really impressive to see the workings of a high caliber restaurant like that. A little tip: We brought our own wine, which saved a few bucks and made us all a little more comfortable springing for some extra menu items. Definitely give this spot a try. I think it embodies the Stephen Starr experience well and offers some really unique dishes.

Not only is this the best Indian vegetarian restaurant at which I've eaten (and I've lived and eaten in Jackson Heights for 14 years, and overseas in a half-Indian country for two years), but it is probably the best vegeatarian restaurant I've encountered, period.  The food is wonderful.  The room has a very pleasant ambience and the staff is gracious and proficient.  And after, or before you eat explore the enticing neighborhood, accessible via 5 different subway lines.

Super yummy! Everyone should try it at least once. They have a really good shrimp/lemongrass soup. The pad Thai and chicken fried rice is also very good. The bar is also fun, too. Everytime family visits us from California, Maryland, or even just friends from NYC, we take them to TOB's and they've all loved it!
Great tasting Margherita pizza, great service.  I was expecting/hoping to get a little more basil on my pizza, but it's not the end of the world. The pizza & crust was delicious!

Wait staff is very attentive. Bar is well stocked, and the teatotaler bar tender served some great pours. Menu is thorough though lacking on vegetarian options but they put something together nicely. Nice room and acoustics so you can talk intimately in such a large venue that counts on my list. Very nice evening out.

LOVE LOVE LOVE! For birthdays, they sing a crazy song and you get to ride the horsey :) This place is a favorite and I go out during the weekends to stop by. There is a lot of food and we always order too much and have to take it home.

Whenever someone asks me to recommend one of my favorite restaurants in NYC for fine dining or just a nice place to eat, this is the place. I originally came here for a nice steak meal but I came during lunch and it was a slightly altered menu so I didn't end up with a succulent steak. Worry not, basically anything you order here is delicious and plated beautifully. I had my first experience eating sweetbreads here and it was a good first time, though had I known what sweetbreads actually was prior to ordering it I probably wouldn't know would taste like and be missing out. Their duck leg was cooked perfectly and the dish was flavorful. P.s. Save room for dessert!! (I'm serious) P.p.s. You can cap your meal off with a coffee to help digest a bit. Their cortado was  well made.
The service was prompt and courteous. I was there with my sister to enjoy a night "on the town". The wine was a bit pricy but we really enjoyed ourselves. I had the salmon and she had the shrimp.

I ordered Vinny's Special Brick Oven Style Pizza and an order of onion rings. The onion rings had absolutely NO flavor and the pizza was HORRIBLE. Soggy, undercooked and the cheese was everywhere except for the pizza. The delivery guy crushed the box, handed it to me that way and when i opened it, half the cheese and toppings were on the box lid. It's so bad I can't tell the difference between the cheese and the soggy pizza crust. AWFUL. Never ordering from here again.

Firstly the GM here I think his name is Arnold ~ always a gentleman always on point . Had dinner last week with friends. Fab atmosphere, and surprisingly crowded early on a Monday evening.  Started with martinis at the bar, which were perfection !!! We always come here for the burger ~ Black Label ******** Yum ! Great service , great food, especially the burger

escargot- excellent. main dishes steaks and veggies - also excellent! service ok. noise level- really bad - shouting customer conversations. . typical tight seating. Too bad noise is affecting my review so badly because the meals are 5-star! But I will only return in off-hours because of inability to converse.

Great restaurant with great food and plenty of variety on the menu. You are sure to find something fantastic for everyone here! My only complaint is the temperature of the dining room, which is WAY too hot. Even in a light sweater I was wishing I had a t-shirt underneath because about half way through my meal I was so hot I could no longer enjoy the food or the company I was in. I could see that other patrons were also uncomfortable as many of them were fanning themselves with menus.

I love this market, particularly when the PA Dutch stalls are open and I can get one of the million donut flavors at Bieler's.  They're all incredible, but the best one I've had so far is their apple fritter.

Owner Donnie has a handle on what people in Astoria love ... Great food at reasonable prices... Today's hit started with their famous "atomic Mac n cheese balls" devastatingly awesome ... Followed by the "bacon bier burger" mmmm. Great food makes you a food connoisseur .. Cause you realize that other places really suck ... Chomp chomp (back to my burger) chomp chomp.  Lol
Worst service and experience ever at an airport.  There was so much confusion by the staff and the require iPad orders just made it worse.  I would never go again.

Just don't I don't even wanna give a star. The menu outside and inside isn't the same then what you see a picture of vs what you get is totally different and the clam linguini I had the clam tastes disgusting and there's like do little pasta do I basically paid $30 for just pasta. Never again.
Coffee and food were good. The barista was really weird. I don't think I will be going back.
Excellent variety of dishes.  Good Service and Decor.

Soooo here is the deal. I know my TEX-MEX (I'm from Texas). Unfortunately most Vermonters don't. And are a bit afraid. I found out from the owners (who happen to have also lived in Texas and still have family there) that it is quite common for new customers to request menu items be prepared more mild before ever trying the dish. So common, that their whole menu now leans towards being far more mild than traditional* and more authentic dishes.* That said, they are only too happy to also spice-it-up (obviously adding flavor/heat is easier than taking it out). Just tell your server you want the real-deal and understand and are prepared - for how it should be prepared.   Madera's (as the best of the lot) has a loyal customer-base  that keep coming back because Madera's can duplicate favorite versions from other Tex-Mex restaurants from across the USA (suffice there are many well established ways to make a taco etc). It'd also be helpful to understand Madrera's menu is Tex-Mex. If you are confused just understand I'm being very liberal with "traditional" and "authentic" - since most items North Americans think of as Mexican are in fact long standing Americanized-versions. What most Americans know as Mexican is pseudo-Mexican fare. And the same is true of what we think of as Chinese food, which are in fact Americanized versions created in the USA - which were never actually originally made in China, hence neither traditional nor truly authentic).
