When our waiter returned to check on the meals I told him they were not sufficiently good to compensate for the time taken to get them, to which he spun around without comment and strode away from the table. He later returned to the table and told me that I should have gone to Angelica's Kitchen (a famous NYC vegan restaurant), making it very clear that vegans are not welcome at Narcissa, and that we should eat with our own kind. The real kicker of the evening, however, was when the bill arrived. I had been charged $29 for four pieces of cauliflower and a tablespoon of lentils - the full price for the entire sea bass main. At that point, I called over someone who appeared to be in charge. He agreed with me that the bill was unfair and said he would deal with it. Then a further manager returned with the revised bill (my meal entirely removed from it), and apologised nicely for the error. He asked how the rest of the evening had been, so I expressed to him how bad it was. He again apologised and then removed the bar tab from the bill as well. While it was too little too late to save the evening, at least management did respond appropriately. The waiter and chef, however, were clearly offended by our veganism and behaved in overtly hostile ways towards us. I reiterate that our friends were previously assured the kitchen could provide perfectly well for vegans, but this was definitely not the case. It was hands down the worst experience of my NY vacation.

Been going here for years. Only like their Hotdogs and Hamburgers. Onions rings are great too. However, was surprised that I have never noticed this but the take out area where the cashier cooks the hot dogs does so without gloves and without washing her hands after touching money, etc. I'll still go there, I may say something eventually.
The calamari and chicken franchise were excellent.  People were very friendly and service was excellent.

What. happened?? Food used to be great, and now it's horrible - the recipes changed? Even the salad is chopped badly with different dressing. Used to be a 2-3x a week go to. After the past two orders arriving messed up, Not bothering to order again.

Campania has redeemed itself! I waited a while before updating this review because I wanted to make sure all the positive changes that I have seen where going to be long lasting. A few weeks after my terrible experience my husband convinced me to give it another chance so I did. He chatted with the manager and it turns out they had actually read the review I had posted and made some major changes in the way they do their staffing and in their management staff. I am happy you say that several months later these changes are still in place and we again enjoy a wonderful dining experience every time we go. The problems with delivery orders have been rectified as well and they never forget to send any of the little extras we request (like the balsamic glaze). The food continues to be of the highest quality and very tasty. I really appreciate the fact that they do read these reviews and work to address issues that are truly a problem. Campania has regained my business and my loyalty and we continue to proudly bring friends from outside the neighborhood there for a tasty quality Italian meal that won't break the bank. The pasta specials are often quite wonderful and their secret recipe sangria is fabulous (if they bottled it and sold it from the restaurant I'd swing by after a tough day at work and buy a jug--it's that good). Well done Campania!

Did not have any issues with service and delivery time was fine. Issue is my entire family who did not all eat one item (meaning multiple items were tainted) came down with violent food poisoning. Completely knocked us out of commission with vomitting, extreme joint pain, weakness, abdominal pain, fever and pretty much every other awful thing that can happen from food poisoning for the next day and a half. Will never eat here again and strongly recommend others do not either.
Friendly owner & workers! Had the fatburger! Note to self you must be really hungry to eat the whole thing!! Very flavorful nonetheless! I'd go back again!

Great looking Mediterranean restaurant  on East village , but for the waiting to be seat take long time, the place is quite and foods all are delicious and absolutely recommend to stopping by again with my group friends ....
#delicious #cozy #had the meat lasagna and the salmon #affordable prices #delicious #goodforhotdates #or good with hanging out with a couple on their date #pannacottababy

Rarely do i comment on a restaurant. .being a San Antonio girl who recently  moved to Vermont I've had a taste of "Vermont " BBQ from another popular spot in Whiteriver Junction  (name rhymes with patties )..so naturally I had my opinions about sampling BBQ from another Vermont place..I stumbled upon this place thinking it was a full restaurant that i had a coupon for..walked in. .its a country store..I said."sorry..thought you were a  restaurant "..he said.."I sell BBQ..would you like  some.. (thinking about my last experience. .i said NO THANKS)..he said. .just try a small  sample of my brisket..again..i said no..about to leave..them turned around and said okay..A SMALL SAMPLE..he went to the back..came back with about 4 slices of brisket. .i tasted a small piece..people when I  tell you this  was one of the BEST brisket I've  EVER tasted (remember. .Texas girl here) this man..who cooks on those precious smokers outside his "country  store " has a GIFT and its BBQ..I  mean a real gift...you know the kind when people CARED about the product they put out...So..after tasting the brisket..he offered a sample of pulled pork..OMG!..melt on ya mouth Tennessee style tender..so of course . what's next..RIBS... (faints )..I FINALLY FOUND THE SPOT FOR BBQ.  Competition quality BBQ..BOY IS GIFTED...I almost don't want to expose my find..cause i know when people get turned on  to this spot..he gonna sell out..quickly. ..daily...but imma become his best friend  so I can always call him to save me a plate..

I love this place! This is the second time I have been here!! I was very lucky to find it again!! They sit you wherever you fit at any table with other people! They give you hot tea and a menu! You have to flag down staff to order because they are so busy! Once you order, the food comes fast! They have roasted ducks hanging in the kitchen! Everything I order is good! Wonton soup with duck, duck with vegetables, spring rolls, soup with shrimp, chicken and vegetables ! It's all good ! They only take cash and I was short six dollars! They said, "okay" ! No argument, no bad feelings! I appreciate that. I will definitely tell my friends and family about this authentic Chinese restaurant! I couldn't even leave a tip but I know when I come back, I will make up for it!
Came here for a date, and was completely amazed by the service, food, and atmosphere. I had 5 courses and all were to perfection!
Good steak pho and I also like the grilled chicken and spring rolls and the grilled pork chops with veggies and rice.
Absolutely the worst food I have ever eaten! They served instant potatoes and rubber roastbeef for $13 !!!!'

My Greek girlfriend and Astoria resident spoke highly of MP taverna after visiting last summer so we decided to go out of our way to return tonight. We arrived at 11:45pm and the host told us that we could be served food at either the bar or a table. We wanted to grab a drink and order a few appetizers and there were only three others sitting at the bar so we opted for that as we thought it would be quicker. After being actively ignored for twenty minutes by the bar tender  (clearly wasn't serving drinks or food, chatting with coworkers, on cell phone, etc), he sauntered over and gave us menus. We attempted to order food but he told us the grill closed at midnight. Normally this wouldn't bother me but we were clearly being ignored for some time and it was particularly frustrating after we specifically told the host we were there to eat. Very much turned off by the service and probably not worth the effort given how many fantastic Greek restaurants there are in the area.

Overpriced. I bought creme brulee, which should have a crystallized top. Instead it was like soft custard.  The tiramisu was just mocha mousse.  The cannoli shells are always stale and hard. We got sandwiches once, and it barely has any meat in it. People rave about this place, probably because its the only bakery around. For great bakery items, make a trip to Gencarelli in Bloomfield,  Brothers Bakery in Kearny (the BEST bread), Calandra's in West Caldwell.
I am unimpressed every time I go.  It's good, just not great, and certainly not worth the hype and hassle.  For this much work, Babbo and Il Mulino are so much better.

Awesome pizza. Basic pizza comes with cheese, sauce and basil, basically a margerita. We asked for a sausage topping. Got our pizza in no time. It was huge and though we ate 2 slices each, we also look 2 home for dinner. The coal fired oven adds to the great taste and service is excellent. We are at the downtown Grimaldis but it is great anywhere. A staple must do if you want the real New York pizza.

I went in for an early lunch, so I missed the rush but I could definitely see a big wait here. I ordered the eggplant and enoki steamed buns not sure if I would like them, but they are one of the most heavenly things I have every tasked, the vegetables are lightly fried and covered in a sticky, spicy, sweet sauce. It has a piece of iceberg lettuce which adds a nice textural component to the softest lightest buns in the shape of a taco you've ever had. Also the ramen was amazing, I topped it with a soft boiled egg. You need to have the ipudo nigori sake, it's an absolute must. This place is fun atmosphere with everyone shouting japanese phrases whenever food is ready or a customer arrives. Will be going back as soon as possible.

Great ramen. Little bit on the hyped up side, but it's delicious. Sitting at the counter is the best. Served HOT, but in the best way. Appetizers are good also. It's a nice big bowl that'll fill you up. Beware there can be quite the wait during the dinner rush.

We were very disappointed with the service. The food was great but the services was horrific. As side from that, we were charged 18% for a party of 4. The manager is also the waiter and he's horrible. We will not visit again just because of the service and the manager being so rude. The bus boy was the next best thing. The girls that work in the cashier are useless. To bad...  I guess you can't have it all.
Had the halibut and truffled mashed potatoes last night.....they were outstanding!!!  Very nice place great atmosphere and staff were very friendly!!!
Delicious mexican food. The taste and quality of the food was really good. Ended up going back to the same place for that reason. Service was good but the music was a little too loud.

Slooooowwwww. Mid day. Light traffic. 35 min waiting for appetizers. The waitress casually goes by  mumbling automatically "is everything ok here?" and moves on without even realizing table is still empty. Yup. So much for training your waiting staff... Food was ok and they did compensate with a cheesecake on the house which was nice. Probably they are better as a late night bar thing.

This is such a cute place!!! The decor is something that you wouldn't normally see in New York City. After walking up the stairs, right before going in, it feels like you have been transported to a small tea place in a small village in Japan. Love it! This restaurant is known for its unique Japanese desserts. There are so many to pick from. There is also a long list if tea that you can order. They also have meal sets in the menu, which is what I ordered the last time I went there. I forgot the name, but it was a dinner set that included soup and a small dessert (it's different every day, depending on what the chef prepared that day). Very authentic home cooked type of meal. Food for the soul :)

Eating at Carmines was one of the worst mistakes I've ever made. We first waited for about an hour, thinking it would taste good with with all the waiting guests and packed tables.  When we finally got our table and ordered, we waited for about another hour and repeatedly asked the waiter for our food. When at last the food came, the spaghetti was undercooked and was all noodles with little sauce. While we were waiting for our check, we had seen another group come in and get seated, we were able to see their food come out a bit less then 30 minutes.We were so dissapointed that we went out after the dinner to eat again.

Let me start by stating that I love all things Jose Garces. I think the man is a genius and we try to go to as many of his restaurants as possible, as often as possible. We were in the city for lunch and decided to check out Village Whiskey. (We've tried to go for dinner and the wait was always pretty long).  We were happily surprised when there was no wait when we arrived.  Everything goes downhill from there though... The hostess put four of us at a high-top for two people.  When we asked if there was another option, she told us no, so we squeezed ourselves in there.  Our server was extremely cold and couldn't have been any less friendly.  She literally was the opposite of almost every Graces experience that I've ever had.  We ordered our food and it was ok-- I think I hyped it up in my head and found myself disappointed with the burger. It was nothing spectacular and really the entire experience was horribly disappointing.  The duck fat fries were okay--again nothing spectacular. I think my biggest disappoint comes from the fact that I have come to love the way that Garces' restaurants have personality and warmth, and this experience was equivalent to going in for a root canal. I will never waste my money there again and am so sad that Jose Garces is associated with this place.

Awful, waited ages for drinks which probably would not arrived if we had not asked for them. I ordered granola and yogurt. The Granola must have been a teaspoon worth so I asked for more and had it returned with what appeared to be broken digestive biscuit. Yogurt was more like thick cream and I noticed someone else had also left theirs.  My husband had a bacon omelette, which he said wasn't bad. No wonder you have to pay a gratuity up front!!!!
They mixed up our order, but made up for it with comp stuff.  Food was good.  Haven't seen a Zapata (so?) on a Mexican menu, but it was good.

Burgers are actually good! The fries are also really good as well. Ordered a medium well burger, and it was flavorful and cooked about right. I find that burgers in this neighborhood are hard to find, but the one here is good.
This food was amazing. I had the pork and I got the mango nacho appetizer. The staff is very friendly, too!

We were waiting in line as walk-in guests before it opened. There were only 4 walking seats available and a couple were waiting ahead of us. As there was no check in system, two girls behind us walked in and just sat down the rest seats without checking other people before them. We questioned the waiter but she just replied: what do you want me to do? Like ask them to give the seats to you? Would you please just provide a checking system to avoid such issues again? and to girls who just sat and might be having dinner right now, I feel bad for you guys as you were quite when we were arguing with the waiter. You took advantage from others and you knew you were wrong.
Friendly staff, good food, lots of choice. The chicken wings were a particular delight!

This quaint little Thai restaurant is very authentic! The place is bright, and music plays throughout the room. Though it is small, the space is used very wisely.  Staff is very kind, and the food came out very, very quickly! It was all delicious! As I am a creature of habit I had the sweet and sour chicken. It was fantastic! The Sweet Thai tea comes in a ceramic porcelain jar. Very cute! Two thumbs up for this hidden Thai treasure! Make sure to check in here on yelp to get 10% your meal if it's your first time. I love it, and the location is not far from the Midtown Marriott and the large post office! Well done.

I would come back to Patzeria over and over again. The pizza is so delicious! Thin crust, tons of toppings, amazing flavors, reasonable prices? What more can you ask for in a pizza? I tried the tomato/basil pizza, the grandma pizza (a square cut, thicker pizza with sweet tomato sauce), and the lasagna pizza (tastes EXACTLY like lasagna, is a bit heavier to eat and very filling. Their garlic knots are also very good (very garlicy, oily on the outside). The only thing I would really say negative about this place is that there isn't a lot of seating areas. People usually sit on stools or stand, crowded inside, or there are a few seats outside. If you wanted to have a big group eat Patzeria pizza, it would be best to do a carry out I think.
Consistently good food!
Great food, nice people, It was not expensive and the place was clean. Great choice for an informal place with great indian food. It is not a pretty restaurant but it is very good

At my first thought of good noodles this is the place I think of first. Fantastic food and service overall. You can get a variety of apps and dishes and still not break the bank. Just remember, cash only at this place unless they have changed payment options.

Such good food!! Went with my boss and we got a Kale Salad. It was AMAZING. I've never had anything like it- pears apples walnuts kale and a delicious dressing- so good, a must try! Service was amazing the staff was so kind and great. Served us soda with a glass bottle and cup of ice, which I love:) And we also got a sausage pizza to split. Broccoli rabe, fresh motz, ugh so good seriously. Everything here was amazing I will be going here for lunch often!!

Breakfast was going good until waitress gave us the bill and said manager HAD to charge $7.35 for 3 hot waters (considered as hot tea order).  Go elsewhere Better brunch at Toast (Montclair) or Raymond's (Montclair) which don't charge $2.45 per cup of hot water.

If I could give zero stars I would.  I walked in the front door to put my name in, was completely ignored by 3 people who worked there.  Finally I caught the eye of the manager, he walked over and in an annoyed tone said, 'yes'?  I said, I just need to put my name in, and he said 'no, I have a line of people', I said 'I can't even put my name in?' And he hastily responds 'no'!  Apparently, you don't put your name in you just wait in line, but he simply could have explained that and I would have got in line, but he basically told me I couldn't even do that because he had an hour worth of people in line.   Needless to say I walked out...won't be trying that place, ever!

Wow, what can I say about this spot.. This is a gem of a restaurant, the food was absolutely stupendous. Our server was a little slow at first, but more than made up for it with the quality of food we ate. I ordered squid ink pasta and arancini. I was a bit nervous about the squid ink pasta since I never had it, but it was delicious.

Wow!! This is my second time eating at Ichiban. Usually with high expectation (1st time experience) it turns out okay, but today I even enjoyed more than 1st time. The waitress is wonderful, food is just great!!! I am a Korean who lives in Boston, and can't compare Ichiban to any Korean restaurant in or near Boston. It is almost 2 hours driving from my house, however I can't already wait to go back!!
Nice and cosy place in West Village. The food is tasty with various mediterranean dishes. Ambiance is calm which is quite appreciable :-)

A GEM of a find. A Saturday late lunch craving for Maman's pho led us to a four-month new Pho Thanh Huong on the convenient corner of New Road and Rt46East. This could not have been a luckier day in this gourmand's tastebud world. We pulled up almost 2p on a Saturday and walked into an empty simply elegant establishment and immediately greeted by a young casually dressed professional. It didn't take us long to put our order in for our pho and for me, the craving for the moment - banh mi (a traditional Vietnamese sandwich). Waters and hot tea were passed out and as the tea warmed me up, I took note of the warm colors that surrounded me that brought comfort to a much anticipated meal. It wasn't long before the large white bowls were passed around with broth that had such splendid depth of smell that I immediately thought - "whoa -- Maman might have some competition for the first time!"  So you see, the traditional pho dish is much about the broth -- the way it's lovingly procured from hours of patient simmering of beef bone and special spices and a few other elements. Although my own dish, the banh mi dac biet, was waiting in front of me, my instinct was to grab a spoon and dip into my husband's not-yet-garnished bowl -- to resist a taste of the broth is like, well, a child turning away from his unopened Christmas presents. It was (pardon my implied obscenity) un-pho-king believable!  Broth PERFECTION. Of course my nasal passages were WIDE open to take in every...single...detail...of the hours of that bone exuding it's illicit flavors into the hot water that slowly danced around it.  And SO well worth the wait....and travel.  Beef...check; thin sliced onions...check; chinese basil...check; bean sprouts...check; limes...check; hoisin...check; sriracha....check; HELLOOOO taste buuuuddss!! Phew!  Ok...back down to earth.  Need say no more re: the pho.  Now to the banh mi - MELT...IN...YOUR...MOUTH.  The planets and stars and all of their moons were in proper alignment LOL for me, the lucky foodie, couldn't have hit it better two-for-two. Just perfect amount of meats and garnishes that literally married the dang sammich to my tongue...bite after bite.   So we only tasted two of the PLENTIFUL menu options and saw many that will be bringing us back for more.  My son seriously said "So, we're coming back for dinner right?" ; )  This is true Vietnamese food. We have gone to Pho Ai (Florham Park) and Lemongrass which have good food as well but this place definitely made a huge first impression that we'll be coming back soon.  The flavors seem more authentic and have much more depth.   Kudos to a great start Pho Thanh Huong and looking forward to our next experience with you.
Jesse is a really awesome, friendly bartender and he makes amazing cocktails that my girlfriend and I enjoy. Killer beer list and I LOVE THE VEGGIE WINGS

Visiting the city and I found great reviews on Pylos.  It didn't disappoint!!!!  It was absolutely amazing!!  The food, ambience and location were wonderful.  The appetizers were more than enough for three.  Highly recommended!

If you want to try some authentic Dosas you've come to the right place. The food is cheap and tastes super fresh. The samosas are also fantastic.I waited almost 20 minutes for the food, which I don't mind at all. The food there are fulfilling. The guy that is making the dosas is so friendly. The sambar is alright, not too crazy about it. Overall, I would come there once in a while to satisfy my cravings.

After being referred here by someone at another nearby restaurant which was packed, we found this place almost empty when we got there. The atmosphere is very nice and the staff were nice. By the time we left, it was packed too and it seemed like they didn't have enough staff to really handle it properly though. We didn't see our waiter for long periods and I had to flag him down when we needed anything. I had the burger which had a "bacon-onion jam" on it but somehow they managed to make it not taste at all like bacon; overall it seemed just like an average burger to me. The dessert I ordered - chocolate cake with pistachio gelato - was no better. The one who brought the plate said it was vanilla ice cream and he may as well have been right since the gelato only had a couple of pistachio pieces and no pistachio flavor at all. The wine is served in glasses with no stem which seems surprising considering it's better to hold wine glasses by the stem so you don't affect the temperature too much (I know to some that may sound picky). The bathroom apparently is inside the hotel down near the gym I believe they said which seems a bit inconvenient for a restaurant which serves drinks.
Everything is served in a plastic container.  This is not green or clean.  WTF is up with the plastic NYC?  From a Portlander.

We happened into Sabor Unido accidentally and could not have been more lucky. Friendly service and authentic deliciously prepared cuisine. The steak picana and the garlic shrimp were amazingly good and flavorful. The side dishes all delicious and authentic. This was the best and most true Brazilian food you can find north of the Equator. We highly recommend this friendly family owned restaurant. Not only that the prices cannot be beat!! Highly recommend!!!vvv

This place never disappoints. Delicious, homemade food at a reasonable price. Much cheaper than surrounding restaurants. Better quality than many places in the Ironbound. Delivery is very quick too, but I only live a few blocks away. The service is also excellent. Highly recommended.q
Great food! Great service! Great wine selection! Perfect for a date! Highly recommended..to the max!

We used to go to Edison just to get Vietnamese pho. But then they moved out. So my wife find out that there's 1 Vietnamese restaurant in linden. We tried it and didn't like it at all. So we googled & found this place. Even closer from us. The food much better than the one in linden, the waiter was very nice. This is our new favorite pho restaurant now. P.S Cash only!!!!
Good food and very friendly and attentive staff. We live so close to this restaurant, and never had a good excuse to try it till tonight. We will absolutely be returning!

Sounds strange I know but a Chinese owned Mexican joint. Serves authentic cuisine.  The cooks are Latinos. I get the shrimp fajita platter with two sides and a drink for under $10. Not much to look at tho. It looks like a renovated fast food place.

Since this place had so many good reviews i decided to give it a shot, but I  was extremely disappointed. We had curry puffs as an appetizer, which were too oily; I've much better elsewhere; my husband ordered Pad Garlic with tofu. Was ok but somewhat bland and not much garlic.  The worst dish however, was mine, "Ants Climbing a Tree'. The description sounded intriguing but what I received did not resemble the description whatsoever. I ended up with a pile of dry, bland, sour tasting noodles with little or none of the ingredients listed in the menu. Bleh! If I had been dining in I would have sent it back, but i had the meal delivered. In fact when I first opened the container i thought they sent me the wrong dish so I called them up and was assured I had the correct order.

We finally went to Geronimo's recently and were quite happy with our meals. First of all, reservations are recommended, especially on weekends as this place seems to always be packed. They have both indoor and outdoor seating. Despite being a cool November evening, the outside seating was full. The outdoor area was mostly enclosed though so you are mostly protected from the elements. Our server was very attentive and provided us with good suggestions. The menu, as one would expect, has a lot of Southwestern and Mexican fare. The menu is fairly extensive, so there is much to choose from. Best of all, if you are a tequila lover, their selection of tequilas was HUGE! For entrees, I ordered the Pork Pibil and my partner ordered the Lobster & Chorizo Mac & Cheese. Both were delicious, nicely seasoned, with the just the right amount of heat. Geronimo's is a busy and bustling place, with a somewhat loud and festive atmosphere. The food is delicious and the prices are surprisingly inexpensive. It's easy to understand why it is always full.

this is the worst soul food restaurant in the newark area the workers are rude and disrespectful,i'm not even sure how they still in business,when you try to support black owned business they give you their ass to kiss but today was the last day i support this business not to mention this is supposed to be a church establishment but again church folk are the worst to

I think the bakers should wear hairnets because I found a long piece of hair in my Mexican wedding cookies, and dirty blonde who I talked to was very rude about it. It's not my fault that a long piece of of brown hair was inside of the cookie....

what the hell am i doing here, ok no college football tonight (damn) and dear friends from west coast here, ok lets go.  old fashion wood decor with an upscale feel, nice spacious place with nice staff , my server was a very pleasant gal. the bar has an old fashion look , which adds style as well as the rest of the place,  very cozy.whom ever designed this place had old charm in mind,across the large bar is a bunch of lounge seating , and the back room with its wall designs and open view room top, which is very cool. the place was crowded but we were able to get a rear booth( hooray). the food is a nice mix of typical american( burgers and fries etc. to more upscale dishes like liver tartar and kale salad. etc. the artichoke dip for app and grilled chicken with fries were excellent, and the server was very nice and always around. this place is a little pricey, but well worth it, my friends and i had a good time. i recommend this place for drinks and or for eating, with food and staff service, that deserves 5 stars.

What can i say about BD that haven't been said already.  There is a reason why this place get soo many high remarks.  I have been coming here for years.  Some people say that it is not authentic.  I say who cares as long as the food is tasty.  The only authentic food you will get is from a home cook meal from your mother.  Going here i would recommend gettting the avocado shake, Vietnamese ice coffee, calamari,  Pho Large (two people can share), and my favorite the fried rice with beef cube and a fried egg.  The only negative thing i would say is that this place has gotten pricey through out the years. I wish they would lower the price on some of their food.
Brunch is awesome here!!!

I like this place for its choices and their affordable prices of a custom made burger. The seating area is cafeteria style with no privacy. It is very loud here with the students. I wish they had combo meals to choose from. Overall, I cannot recommend this place because of the long wait times for "FAST" food and limited awkward seating.
Crowded and not the best service at all. But all and all it's a nice experience with truly original Italian flavors, plus the mix with little shops and the market makes it something unique.
Food was always very good,but I think new owners took over, noticed a big difference in the quality and taste of the food. The fried food is extremely greasy. Not the same food.
Home sweet cooking.  The chicken is amazing in this place.  Great spot for lunch.  Just be sure you take a nap after eating it

Yay, thank you Yelp for leading me to this great tasting pizza amid a lot of Asian food!  I had a Sicilian cheese piece and it literally melted in my mouth.  Plus, the crust was crispy and the cheese was plentiful.

I have been going to il corallo for 15 years and it is far and away one of my favorite restaurants in all of new york. The pasta, especially the black tagliarini with seafood is unbelievable. You also cannot beat rhe price, especially in this part of new york!

My friends and i went here on a Friday night. We were seated immediately even though without reservations. Once inside, i was impressed by the decor. The place wasn't too packed and the server was greeted us with a huge smile. We ordered each item on the menu and the waitress also recommended us a few items. They were all very friendly, knowledgable and attentive. Definitely will be back again soon.

One night, I went on a Tinder date.  After meeting at a bar, where she drank wine, and I drank beer, we spontaneously found our way over to Barbuzzo.  At Barbuzzo, we ordered a cheese plate and a pizza.  First off, the Tinder date was a 1 star who looked much more attractive in the pictures.  Secondly, it's irresponsible to rate a place based on a cheese plate... so that I will not do.  My rating is based on he staff, all of which were sharp.  The guys behind the bar and our server were all well versed on the local sourcing and finer details of the pizza's raw ingredients.  This is usually a good sign.  The pizza was good.  It wasn't great.  I'll take a drunken Lorenzo's slice over that Barbuzzo pizza 7 days a week.  This is the type of place that serves good food, but takes itself relatively too seriously, and that will eventually drift into "just being there" status in Philadelphia's food scene.

There was a party of 6 of us that went to this restaurant. We found good reviews of this place and decided to try it out. The place had nice decor , friendly staff but we waited for 20 minutes to get beverages and even longer to get appetizers. I got a vodka tonic and it was extremely stong, so stong that I had to return it. I got a white sangria later and it was even worse! Later our food came and it was cold! We had mixed kebab platters, whole fish and seared tuna salad. We told the waiter that our food was cold and all he did was bring a bowl of hot rice.. Then we decided to get cappuccinos. And it also came cold. I mean there is something wrong with this restaurants thermometers... Then I ordered a lava cake .. Luckily is was warm but it came over hot melted ice cream?! What?! The cake was floating on top of this liquid puddle of creamed liquid! This place is unbelievable.. Never again will we come here! FYI we spent over $300 here..

This was my first time at BurgerFi. After walking around Reading Terminal Market we just decided to walk across the street to BurgerFi instead. The atmosphere is pretty cool, it's clean and had ample seating for when we went. I ordered the BurgerFi Cheeseburger (double) with onion rings and a drink. Overall, it's more expensive than a fast food joint, but the price is what you'd expect from these new "gourmet" fast food burger establishments. The burger was really good, you could tell the meat patty was high quality and the toppings were fresh. The onion rings were huge and really crisply and tasty. I stole a French fry from a friend and it was tremendous. I may go that route next time. BurgerFi offers free custard to people who post on social media, which is cool. They only had vanilla though. Con: They didn't have any cherry syrup left in their fancy coke machine. Overall, a great burger and fry/onion ring spot and I'd come back again. Five *****.

The taste of real Mexican!! Simple hole in the wall with a soul of good cookin'! Went here because of Cinco De Mayo and wanted to avoid the busy spots where Gringos go to get TexMex slop. BYOB! Great service. Tostadas was amazingly juicy! Flautas was beautifully thick. BIG portions! Great value and very family owned style vibe. Loved it!qq

The taste of real Mexican!! Simple hole in the wall with a soul of good cookin'! Went here because of Cinco De Mayo and wanted to avoid the busy spots where Gringos go to get TexMex slop. BYOB! Great service. Tostadas was amazingly juicy! Flautas was beautifully thick. BIG portions! Great value and very family owned style vibe. Loved it!hh

This was a really lovely, unexpected restaurant.  I ended up in Burlington by surprise and went in search of dinner and we saw Mexican food inside an old-fashioned diner--cool, right?  Unfortunately we were very tired and had to drive, so we couldn't try the drinks, but tacos and water were plenty.  The taco plates are a really great deal--1-3 tacos plus sides (can't go wrong with rice and beans).  The tacos themselves are really quite nice and combine really interesting flavors.  The lengua taco in particular was heavenly, the lengua was prepared really well.  We had the Mexican chocolate brownie for dessert which was really special, just the right amount of spiciness and really rich chocolate.  Highly recommended for good Mexican food and a chill atmosphere, plus really friendly servers.  Would love to go back and try the margaritas.

This was my second visit to the restaurant. I agree with others who said that the atmosphere is attractive, that it can be noisy, that you should have reservations if you try to go on a Friday or Saturday night, that the waitstaff is attentive and that the menu is very creative. Some of the food is excellent, but some is less than desirable. I had the bib salad as a starter course. It was fresh, delicious and beautifully presented. The baked Alaska for dessert was amazing! The Peruvian chicken and beef stroganoff were both nicely prepared and solidly good, but not amazing. I had previously ordered the PEI mussels Asian style and enjoyed the tasty sauce. Tonight, my one of my dining companions order the same, and did not find the sauce to be delicious. I did not sample her dish, so I do not know if her opinion was based on a difference in taste, or if there was  a difference in preparation. However, the truffle mac & cheese with lobster was so salty that it was inedible. Everyone at the table tasted this item and agreed the dish was much too salty. The mac was also overcooked and too soft. We asked the waitress to tell the chef that the dish was oversalted. She apologized, but did nothing more. For a $22 entrée that is inedible, you would expect some reduction in cost or offer to replace the meal.

Love, love, love Mundo Vegan and SO thrilled to have such an amazing vegan option in Montclair! 1. The space... located on the ever-trendy Church Street (street or garage parking). It's exceptionally clean inside, not to mention cozy and definitely has a zen-factor about it! I really like that the kitchen happenings are visible from the dining area--it's nice to know how and with what your food is being prepared, particularly if you are vegan and/or health conscious like I am! 2. The staff... the staff (from waitstaff to cooks to owners) is exceptional. They are friendly (call me by my name and remember my favorite dishes that I typically order!), knowledgable, and great at what they do. They also do a great job of keeping up with social media, and any time I've reached out through Facebook, have answered my questions almost immediately. 3. Most importantly, the FOOD... I've been vegan/gluten-free for nearly 2 years now and have been to almost every vegan restaurant in the NYC metropolitan area. That said, the food here is great-tasting, mostly organic, and completely plant-based, with many gluten-free, nut-free, and/or soy-free options. Their menu changes a bit daily, but rest assured, you'll find something delicious! My favorite dishes are the empanadas, mac and cheese, and amazing dessert pies! I'm excited to watch as they grow with time and at the prospect of what will hopefully be an expanding menu of delicious vegan eats!

Usually I am not motivated to write posts but as I am dependent on Yelp to find new spots and my restaurant experience was superb I decided to help out the public in their restaurant selection. I recommend Jack and Nellie's for Brunch! My friend and I came for brunch. We arrived at 11am on Saturday - when it opened. Several parties were before us waiting as well! We requested and got the seat near the window. As we were catching up, I was blown away by J & N's interior! It's beautiful = neat and nicely decorated. There are tables across the bar on the side and tables toward the front near and next to the windows. In middle of the ceiling, there's a skylight with a crosshatched piece that let down a light ray of light for a wonderful lighting effect. Within 2 hrs, the patrons filled up the place. Overall - it's a lively place, and has an elegant feel to it. A pleasant surprise indeed. Our waitress was Charlotte. She was super nice and answered my questions. We both ordered eggs benedict, since she confirmed it is the most the popular dish. Our food arrived according to how we wanted it. I requested the bacon be replaced with candied bacon. The eggs benedict was divine! I ate the potatoes, english muffins, salad, and eggs and left nothing extra on my plate.  I ordered the bowl of fruit - which had very nicely picked fruits. I did find out  I'm not much of mimosa drinker, though. My friend on the other hand was downing them! Haha. I will be coming here again and suggesting it to all my friends. *edited for grammar and syntax*

Jack & Nellie's is the place to go to when in Forrest Hills- I litteraly feel proud just to have it to when i talk about Forrest Hills. Its good for every occasion I feel, food is great and the deserts are out of this wored. Everyone was very nice- I didnt get to sit at the bar yet since i love the seating area too much- But it really looks great over there.
Excellent banh mi sandwiches for under $5. Large serving sizes and great flavor. A small hole in the wall so there isn't much area to sit.

my family and I just returned from the Taco Truck. We are sorry to say that overall, we were disappointed. My wife liked the fish taco, but still thought it over priced. my kids got the three taco plates, chicken and beef and the taste was very good, but to be honest, the portions--- as per the price, seemed small. We all left still hungry. I think the portions need to be bigger, or the prices reduced, or, the prices could stay the same, but there needs to be more meat. The place was nicely designed, though we can't figure out why there is a free standing wall in the middle of the place, it really divides and closes off what could be an open and more inviting room. We hope the Taco Truck will take these suggestions into consideration, because we would really like the idea of an affordable and still tasty place in the neighborhood. Signed,

For Philadelphia, this is about as good as it gets for authentic Mexican.  To be fair, I've had better in Spanish Harlem.  Mexican in Philadelphia is a relative thing.  Taco Riendo introduced me to Elotes, which is a spiced/seasoned corn on the cob... and it makes you never want traditional corn on the cob ever again.  I've been here 3-4 times now and hands down the most amazing item I've had were the Carne tacos.  The cheese is uniquely stringy and perfectly melted.  The beef is as tender as the tortilla.  I wasn't very impressed with the chicken burrito.  I found it to be dry.  Cash only.
Nice place with a lot of corporate folks at the happy hour time. Giving it 3 stars because it's always too packed to get a seat or even a stand, which also results in a slow service.
Uh, no. Everything there is brown and sad.

A Philadelphia icon.  If you can't find something you love here, then you have no business eating out.  Tommy DiNic's roast pork, in my opinion, is the best in the city.  And yes, I've had the roast pork at John's, which in my opinion is second to Tommy's.  We also had oysters at Pearl's, which in my opinion, was nothing special.  The charm about Reading Terminal, though, is the overall variety of greatness.
love it I went to Dinic's!! Roast pork oh yeah!!! Love line though but really worth it.

Really delicious traditional japanese food ! The place is nice and trendy, service is careful and relaxed. Only defaults : no reservation (so you often have to wait) and cash only (see what I mean...)
Très bien. Très beau restaurant. Le personnel est très gentil et serviable. Nous avons pas regretter notre choix. Manger italien a New York, c'est possible.

Be prepared to wait. Service is slow but the food is delicious. A lot of familiar southern favorites but with a twist. The restaurant is clean, bright, and airy and you're always greeted at the door. I've only eaten here for breakfast/brunch and everything was on point - the cheese grits, ssalmon cakes, hash sliders, fried fish...I'm going to eat my way through the entire menu!kk
My favorite restaurant! Great refried beans. They aren't soupy or grainy like most places and the rice is yummy.
The dumplings were great but the service was very slow. They place needs to expand to handle all the customers. The food also felt very rushed since they are trying to just get customers in and out.

The sauces are really good, and a lot of the savory items. The wait used to be really bad, but now it's in a bigger location with extended hours so that's been much improved. I've found better vegan pancakes and the like and it's a tad pricey, cash only also, but overall I like the menu options here.

My girlfriend and I stopped in at Bombay Grill on a whim, craving Indian food and wanting to try something new in the area. The both of us, being vegetarians, had a lot of options to choose from. The food was made fresh while we waited. I had the Malai Kofta and my girlfriend, the Methi Malai Mutter. Both of these dishes were EXCELLENT! Both dishes were so rich, the flavors robust. The roti was also fresh and perfectly complimented our main dish, soaking up the sauce. The staff was great and helpful too! The atmosphere is lacking but this is mainly a take-out spot. Such a great surprise. I recommend this to any Indian food fan in the Middlesex county area!
Excellent food after long day of skiing. Champ pizza, meat lovers pizza, bbq chicken sandwich and Vermonter sandwich were all great and close to Marriott.

It's been 6-7 months since our visit.  I went with my girlfriend.  We ordered two Sangria pitchers.  She got drunk and made the couple next to us very uncomfortable.  I didn't make a big deal of it because I was in a state of food bliss.  I don't remember the specifics of what we ordered... but we spent a good $125/$150 and I had no regrets.  The best part of tapas is the portions aren't overwhelming, leaving plenty of room to try other items on the menu.  Thank you Jose Garces.

Some of the best sushi in town.  Absolutely the best restaurant in this neighborhood.  The food is great, the atmosphere is cozy, the fish is fresh, and the service is fast and friendly.  Great sake doesn't hurt either.

Not sure how the food is but based on my phone experience they fail.   Mothers 82 birthday with her fraternal twin.  Made reservations for 18 two weeks prior.  Told them we need  handicap access around tables. The morning of the dinner they called me telling me the upstairs may be too tight and if I prefer the basement room.  I asked if they had elevators.  They said no but would use four personnel to carry anyone in a wheel chair down 12 stairs!  Are you kidding me!   I told them we would stay upstairs.  I thought I better ask about bathroom access and yes it was downstairs as well. So much for making my life easy and avoiding trying to find a place for 18 on a Saturday but I prevailed.  I always thought if you want the best Spanish/Portuguese food you need to go to the Iron Bound  of Newark.   Please see my review of Don Pepe 2 in Pine Brook.  It may save you a trip to newark.hht

Well executed American style Chinese food. I appreciate that the chicken in battered dishes like General Tso's is real, not processed mush, and that there are actual caramelized oranges in the Orange Chicken. Almost always get take out here but recently sat there with hubby and toddler, who loved the food--a rarity for her. Pretty chill no-frills atmosphere.

My second brunch at Cafe Renata and I LOVED IT!  The decor is warm and welcoming. The service excellent... I had plenty of water, and refills of coffee. It's clear to me that the Chef is actually a "Chef" and not just a short order cook, because the dishes were plated beautifully and spiced to perfection. I've had a variety of omlettes, french toast, quiche, salad and croissant. Everything was delicious!  Highly recommend - I hope they have great success... great place.

We  loved it lást time ...Now we love it even better... Had a huge Lobster fished out by our friendly and helpful Waiter. They grilled it perfectly added a rice and tomatoes casserole and great bottle of portugese white wine we love it and we were sitting at the counter!  Great service and great lobster was súper fressssh!ds

When you first enter Bluebird, a giant open area with plenty of seating and a pool table greets you. You are then immediately greeted by their fantastic staff, and extremely handsome and friendly manager if you're lucky. Towards the back you'll find a bar, more tables, a warm fireplace and a cozy patio with artwork sprinkled in different areas for purchase! If you want a quick bite to eat, you won't be disappointed by the menu. The presentation of each of the dishes alone are amazing and super affordable--the fancy grilled cheese is a must try! They have a pretty good selection of wine and beer. The waiter even came with samples of different wines when we couldn't make up our minds! The customer service and ambience of this place is superb. They don't push the bill or rush you, and they didn't bombard your table, but they make sure you were well taken care of. If you're looking for a chill and laid back place to spend your Friday or Saturday night, or even a place to rent for a birthday, this is the place!   I will most definitely be frequenting this place!

Six stars.  First team All-Philadelphia foodie.  My favorite chicken cheesesteak in Philadelphia.  Arguably my favorite overall cheesesteak in Philadelphia.  Their pork is amazing, in my opinion second to Tommy DiNic's... but I don't hold that against John.  My advice, if you go with a friend, is order the "small" size of 3-4 different sandwiches and each of you take a half.  Because John's has very exclusive hours (closes at 3pm M-F and 4pm on Saturday) and long lines, it's difficult to find time to keep going back to enjoy everything they do so well.

My favorite pizza in West Hartford. It's nothing fancy and you'd drive by it if you didn't know it was there. The price is right and the pizza is awesome! The crust is crispy and not overloaded with sauce and the pizza is not greasy. They also deliver for a $20 min. I've had the grinders too and they're what you'd expect for a traditional pizza/grinder shop.

I went to Havana Social over the weekend for a friends birthdays for brunch and was pleasantly surprised with how great of a place it is. I usually do not get involved with the Manhattan brunch scene but Havana Social really changed my perspective on that. They were very accommodating with having a large party while taking care of smaller groups that were eating as well. The staff was extremely friendly and attentive the entire time we were there. When it came time to take our order and refill drinks, they were always there to check on us throughout our meal. In addition to the wonderful service, the ambiance of the place was fantastic! The attention to detail was spot on and the decor was awesome. What might be most important to some people was that the food was amazing! Even the plating of the food was quite nice and an added bonus to such a great meal. I ordered the steak and eggs and I was surprised with how great it was. Usually you don't expect to get all of that in one restaurant and I can't wait to go back!

Great Puerto Rican  food. The service was awesome. They make you feel  like family here it was my first time and they took care of  me like they already  knew  me.  The oven chicken  it's so good. Going back next week.
Very decent arepas and prices. Sometimes the wait can be a bit much or the sauces will be out/off, but overall one of my favorite spots.
That fried chicken was the best I've ever had.

So you wouldn't catch me there unless theres a gallery opening or another occasion.  Not because its a bad place, far from it.  It has a great ambiance and a decent selection of drinks.  A little pricey, but always a great hangout at the end of the night!das
Good place to eat and good service. A bit divey for me though. Cash only. No credit cards accepted. There is a pnc bank with drive up ATM in the same parking area.
Great Food Great Service Amazing Drinks BEET SALAD  is very very Good!!  keep the good Job guys !!!!
The Olive Garden of Mexican food.  Below mediocre. Service wasn't bad and the chips were fantastic. Ambience was fine, music is annoying. We had to wait 15 minutes for a table and it was not worth it

I didn't give one star because I thought people might skip over it. The whole reason we chose Galli was because we were on our honeymoon and Yelp reviews said it was a cool spot for date night. Had dinner here tonight. We called ahead to see if we needed reservations, they said they had a large party in the back and to come in an hour and a half. We show up at 8:45 on a Sunday and they put us in a booth next to the kitchen doors. Rap music is blaring and the party in back is so loud we literally cannot hear each other. People from the party are running from the back to the bar, right past our table. After about five minutes, our waiter comes to the table to give us water and take our drink and appetizer orders. The apps come out before our drinks! This party has gotten out of hand, we have stopped trying to have a conversation. The waiter never stops by to see how the apps are, so we can't complain. The mini rice balls are fine, the spicy calamari is terribly average. Our entrees come out and we have finished our cocktails. No waiter. Eventually he passes by the table and we ask him to bring over a manager. The manager says the rap music isn't his cup of tea but the loud crowd are his friends/colleagues and their open bar is ending in ten minutes. He says he will get us a glass of wine. Dinner was pretty middle of the road. We ask for the check. We wait. The loud party is still out of control 40 minutes after their open bar has supposedly ended. We ask for the check a second time. We have just stared at each other for the last hour and a half because speaking was impossible, we told the manager how we were having an awful time, and we were not moved to a quieter table, we didn't receive better service, and then we paid full price at the end of the meal. So much for a romantic dinner.
Awesome Staff and amazing food! I recommend an item not on the "secret menu " nachos K&A style (substitutes waffle fries for nacho chips)
Great sweet spot in New Haven! Old school Italian feel with a very personable staff/owner experience! Large portions and wonderful variety..Definitely will be coming back!

I was excited there was a new restaurant in Montclair with a liquor license.  Our first time was fair, we were told it was a soft opening, so we gave them the benefit of the doubt.  Our next visit was still week, I ordered a Mojito and it arrived an oddly pink color.  When I asked our waiter about it he gladly returned it to the bar, what happened next was a little shocking.  A very young woman who identified herself as the bartender came to the table and  spent I kid you not 5 mins at our table telling us how she made the drink, and that they use a"mix" since mint is hard to find in the winter. (Ha REALLY?  Kings is right across the parking lot, they always seem to have it in stock.)  I ordered a Cosmo in its place,  it was ok.  The meal was just ok too.  It required more seasoning at the table, but we got through it.   The final straw was this past week.  We went for a friends birthday, a party of six, and not one of us could say we enjoyed our meal.  We ordered drinks that were not on the menu, but nothing crazy, bar tending 101 type drinks.  They were all OFF!  So we each had only one.  Which was disappointing since we were there to celebrate our friend.  There were about 6 people behind the bar all of whom looked like they just turned 21, maybe?  They seemed to enjoy each other, the one kid must have watched Cocktails one to many times, he liked to shake and toss his drinks around, another other was a young woman who thought there should have been a pole behind the bar, she would dance when she liked a song.  It was really annoying.  Our waitress tried very hard, but clearly the place is lacking when it comes to mature seasoned staff.   It seemed there was not one grown up among them.  Did I mention this was a Saturday night.  Not a night to have your B team on. Enough about the cocktails and staff, lets talk food.   It is just OK.  The tomatoes on the flat breads we under seasoned and basic.  Tasted like they were straight out of the can.  The same sauce seems to be used on the gnocchi.   The octopus is tender but poorly cleaned the slimy stuff that lines the tentacles was still intact.  The black and white tuna had that fresh out of the freezer texture and color.  The short ribs were dry and under seasoned.    Having been so disappointed with the meal we passed on desert. Sadly if things don't change Denovo will be gone when its lease is up.

Food was great!! If you're planning to eat at this place make sure you come early. It gets packed. The food was delicious although service was not the best. I guess because it gets to be pack that the waiters forget things here and there. Asked for tostados didnt get to recieved it and I have to ask for the reciept since they just handed me back the change without the receipt.  Over all it was a good experience.   Will come back Will recommend

Wow! I was thrilled when I heard the previous owner of Aozora in Montclair, Chef Nelson, opened up another Sushi bar in Newark. I have been trying many different places for the past 2 years since he sold Aozora and no place had the quality, freshness and creativity Nelson's place had. I went to Sushi House 21 today and all I have to say is: I finally had good sushi again! I also tried a new item for me "Steak on the Stone"  it was delicious! As others have said, save room for dessert because you will not find a place to have a cheesecake like Nelson's!q

I love this place! The owners are super awesome and the food is amazing! The sushi is fresh and the service is great! The desserts are homemade and the mango mousse is ridiculously amazing! The cheesecake is great as well! One of the best places around!a

The BEST restaurant I've been to.  Layers upon layers of flavor in each small plate style dish make this the best food.  Service is top notch and has the "get it" factor.  The only restaurant in NYC that I've been to more than twice.

Lovely Malaysian restaurant.  Memorable hainanese chicken over rice.  5 year old daughter looves the coconut rice.  She also surprisingly likes the popular roti appetizers curry sauce, though it is a bit spicy for her normal taste.  If our child likes the food, that gives us more reason to come eat here!

Proof is an interesting place to dine/rest/wait during a layover or waiting to board a flight. The ordering process is electronic so you will not be visited by a server until you order and pay first. Everything is done over individual iPads at your table. The process is easy but you lose out on social interaction. Waiting for a water is not that easy. You have to order all at once or order multiple times. If you're  an individual who doesn't like to talk or be bothered this could be the establishment for you. We paid 38 bucks for two drinks and two glasses of water including 18% tip and tax. Pricy by any standard. The drinks were small but mixed nicely. The ambience is relaxing and upper scale. We later ordered an app where we paid 18 bucks and received three jumbo shrimp. All in all, 60 bucks for two drinks and an app. Not a huge fan of the ordering system and they didn't offer a variety of food on the menu.

Mediocre food and mediocre service. Ordered the meat and cheese platter as an appetizer... was not impressed. Order a whiskey flight and the server did not know how to use a jigger to pour whiskey (at a whiskey bar). Management doesn't seem to care about training their employees. We were offered water once, had to get up and get a server to ask for more.  You use an app via an iPad to order. The app is pretty user friendly but be aware that it defaults to 18% tip when you order.

While visiting Philly, our nephew highly recommended this restaurant.  What a big bummer!  They kill the flavor of the food with too many peppers.  I can handle the heat, but they were overboard.  25+ hot peppers in the meal - really?  I was SO disappointed!  The Dan Dan noodles were awesome and so were the dumplings.  Neither my husband nor I liked our entrees - cut back on the peppers and let us experience other flavors!
HUGE sandwiches, small prices and a really nice staff. Great lunch spot that reminds you of the old neighborhood... where ever your old neighborhood might have been.g

Forever and a day!! Ive been waiting and meaning to go into this deli for ages.... Today was my day and my afternoon already seems delicious. I ordered the "Combo" Corned Beef and Pastrami on Rye toast with Russian Dressing!!!! this was a messy sandwich that I had to grab and hold with both hands, not to let it get away. The meat was tender and just perfectly salted, the juices from both seemed to blend best all over my desk. ( be sure to keep a napkin handy, I used about 7 with this sandy- wich) The décor of this place ... ehh... old world lost-ness... ask other patrons how the ordering/ payment system works (no obvious signs of how to order). Watch as tall sandwich orders go into their large dining area. Hobby's Deli is nostalgic, which can be a little scary in Newark with its eh heem  "eventful" past. This place is warm and inviting and grab yourself a souvenir cap and tee on your way out!!!!o

These guys have great pizza.  I've been going in for slices once a week for over a year and I've NEVER had an issue with the quality of the food or the personality of the staff.  The owner is a young guy who looks like he runs a tight ship and takes a lot of pride in how the place is operated.  If you're looking for an out of the box review, here goes... This place usually has 7-8 specialty pizzas out for slice buying.  At any time, you cannot go wrong with a selection.  The buffalo chicken slice is legit.  The margherita slice is legit.  The sausage and mushroom is legit.  There isn't a knucklehead in the back, trying to reinvent the pizza wheel, wasting our time.  Do you know what I'm talking about, when you walk into a pizza shop, and there are usually 1-2 pizzas that have been sitting there all day, because the guy in charge of making the pies thinks he's a lot smarter than he actually is?  That doesn't happen here.

Sadly, our first and last visit. They were out of numerous menu items, service was terrible and the quality of the food just average. One of our party had to order her vegetarian dish immediately as they were almost out, my wife and I ordered a spinach salad that had no spinach. Long waits for wine delivery and when my wife ordered a second glass, the wrong wine was brought and the server argued with her. Service was so bad, I had to leave my seat, go get a manager and ask him to get someone to our table for service. We have never had such a poor, unprofessional experience. At one point, when I finally flagged down a server, he asked me to wait a minute, helped another table, then walked away and never came back.  Never again...
Went for anniversary dinner.  They went above and beyond.  The food was great the service was awesome.  We would highly recommend.  Great section of Hartford    There is a lot to do there.

This is NOT a place that warrants 4 stars! We were 4 girls walking around the city and trying to get away from the protestors. I don't know how I "checked in" by accident (of all places in NY) but it was not a place I would recommend. First we had someone hovering over us while we ate - and it is really not Vietnamese food. Boo. We went here because of the positive comments - guess we didn't read enough.

Thoroughly enjoyed this restaurant on Christmas Eve. This is my second time here and I can't wait to return and try something else on the menu. The veal Marsala was out of this world. Everyone truly enjoyed their meal and the service is first rate!
The food was amazing. You didn't even need a knife to cut the filet. The price was perfect, as was the service, and a beautiful atmosphere. Really all around great place.

First time eating at uno grill and it's also our last time. The hostess sat us at a table by the door. When we asked to be switch to another table she claimed it was reserved, but yet there were at least 5 other available tables which she didn't bother to sit us there. Out of courtesy we didn't want to trouble the hostess so we just sat down and it turned out to be freezing because there was a draft going through the door. When the food finally arrived the waiter left out one of the order but he didn't explain what happened and just left our table. We waited and waited for the other dish but it never came till my husband stood up to ask the waiter and that's when he said it fell in the kitchen and they were making a new one which will come out in 2 minutes. At this point we didn't want that dish knowing it dropped. You never know if was brushed off or they actually made a new one. The waiter didn't take it well and argue heatedly it would only take a few minutes. In the meanwhile we were very cold and all of us finished with our food except for my husband. We asked to speak with the manager who didn't seem too eager to solve the problem with an attitude of his own. Eventually he apologized and promised us some coupons. We paid for the bill but the manager never came back with the coupon. At this point we had enough with this place and left. This establishment has the most inefficient and unprofessional employees we have ever came in contact with and it just made our family night out unpleasant and memorable - we will remember never to go back again.

I was given about an hour wait for delivery, that was normal. My food showed up an hour an a half later, cold, and with the wrong soda, I ordered 2 cokes, and received 1 diet coke. I called the restaurant to see what can be done about my 30$ that I just wasted on cold take-out.  The person who answered the phone was very nice and polite, and replaced my order.  The new order, got to my house in 20 mins, with the correct amount and kinda of soda.  Not going to order from there again, the food did not taste good, and the "crispy" chicken wings were mush, and drowned in sauce.

Food was ok, if a bit overpriced.  Had the mud pie for desert.  It was rock hard.  Took a few minutes to warm enough to where i could chip it apart with my spoon.   Beer pet peeve:  I asked what was the beers were.  Three on tap: switchback, an IPA (fiddlehead?) and Lost Nation Pitch Black.  I asked what the lost nation was, and I was told it was "an ale".  All three beers are ales.  Switchback's flagship beer is Switchback Ale (people generally just refer to it as "Switchback", so I assume she was referring to this) and the A in IPA stands for ale.  Saying something is an ale means very little other than the way it is brewed.  If a place only has three beers on tap, please have an idea what they are beyond "it's an ale". Fwiw, lost nation pitch black is a black IPA.

There are a bunch of blowhards who run around Philadelphia saying that Pat's is overrated or that they serve stale bread or fatty meat.  The truth is, Pat's has a very good cheesesteak.  Another truth is people like attention, and trashing the local legend accomplishes this.  Also, of all the famous cheesesteak locales, this is where you are most likely to experience the TRUE Philadelphia cheesesteak experience.  Go to Pat's at 11pm, after an Eagles or Phillies game, and stand in line with all of the out-of-towners.  This is the ultimate confluence of steak, cheese, beer, testosterone, Philadelphia pride, honking horns, and cuss words.

I was there last night and got a beer before last call.  The bouncer was extremely rude and disrespectful to the patrons.  He cursed and yelled at us and got in my face and threatened me.  All because it was 2 and he didn't want to wait a minute more.  Horrible horrible service.  The bar tenders wouldn't say anything for or against him, seems like this is an unfortunate regular occurrence.

Ha... what a joke.. the bartenders here are a little too cool for school. By far the most unfriendly staff around... let me guess the snotty chick lives in Flatbush and writes poetry part time haha...if you like rude staff who make 0 effort to be friendly this is your spot!
担担面 红油抄手都是极好的like it so much. it is the restaurant that i must go when going to Philadelphia.

Service is great, atmosphere is cool, wine selection is very good and prices are reasonable. We have enjoyed everything we have eaten there.  Great gluten free selection. The graham gelato is AMAZING!

I had a great dinner experience with some friends. The tacos and drinks were amazing. The energy of the ambiance was great for conversation and a fun time. It's great for groups out on the town or catching up. The decorations are bright and warm. I'll be here next time I'm in town.

The egg sandwiches do the trick and they are friendly. It was great go-to place that remembers your name. Sorry this is so late but wrote this on yelp before They allowed you to post to the mobile app and just saved it as a draft. I'd give it 5 stars but I know savvy yelpers have a slight disbelief with 5 stars haha.

I used to eat here all the time but the last two times I went were disappointing. I am drawn back by the food which I find very tasty but end up irritated by how slow they are. It was not busy when I went yesterday and I did not get food for an hour. Over at the bar area, the chef was slow moving and she was joking around and completely stopped what she was doing. I was starving when I came in but by the time I got my food, I was over it. The waitress did not check in with us to assure us food was coming. I am not sure I will come back again.

Wow! I love this place! Taste the cheese on their pie and you'll get it. If you want dinner, try the eggplant parmigiana. It is totally unique and so good. The owner seems like a great guy, and very committed to quality ingredients. What more can you ask? If you want a bargain, they have a smaller portion dinner as an early bird. It looks like a pizzeria, but there's more to it than that. BYO.

We had a bad experience in this restaurant, the food is not good, at all. They offer in their menu Peruvian food, that not does not taste or have the presentation of what Peruvian food is actually like. Also everything is overpriced for the small portion that they give you. Do not be fooled with those pictures. As a Peruvian I felt insulted.

This is one of the coolest restaurants I've eaten at. The atmosphere is great, amazing music setlist playing in the background, perfect lighting, and a great staff behind it. The food is terrific to top that off. One of my favorite resturants by far.

We ended here at 11pm, glad to see a 4.5 star yelp place still open, but the food was very mediocre, particularly for new york's chinatown. The chicken had way too much dough around it (eg general tso's was 80% dough, 20% chicken) and there was little flavor to any of the dishes we had. One positive point was the broccoli, was quite well steamed

Nice little place I used to live across the street from.  It's got a small menu for food, but most of it is really good.  If you're feeling adventurous and don't mind eating something with a face, I recommend the pig's head.  Make sure you eat it with a friend because it's a huge portion.   Definitely go there for brunch and try the testina hash poutine or the polentu.  And they even have a bar with lots of unique beer choices and a friendly staff.  The prices can range from economical to expensive.  It all depends on your taste.

The lady took me here for soup dumplings, which at the time, was unchartered territory for me.  Good stuff.  Overall, I'll tell you I think there are just too many good sandwiches in this town to spend much time on soup dumplings, but good... worth the money.  We ordered a few other items as well, including chicken feet.  I'm not a chicken feet guy.  I think I cut the inside of my mouth with the claw?  The whole thing might be an acquired taste situation.  Because I'm not banging the door down to go back (5 stars) and I probably wouldn't go back if I was in the neighborhood by myself (4 stars), it gets an "I'd be fine if we ended up here again" (3 stars).

You start with free chips and salsa, if the bartender wants you to.  The house margarita is only $5.  I've tried to get sauced on them before but I could only drink 4 before I was too full.  Overall, it's a decent margarita.  The chicken burrito, if you want my opinion, is dry.  For a while, this was my neighborhood place to go, when I wanted to get out even though no one else was around.  I grew so brutally tired with the female bartender that always seemed to be there, that I just stopped going.  Wait times to be served, in an empty Cantina on a Wednesday night, was about 7-8 minutes.  She would chat incessantly with the other customers about things that were "really cool and stuff," while I suffered the pain of sobriety.  She was the ultimate brainless aimless hipster.

The person on the phone was nice but hard to understand with a thick spanish accent. Ordered  a large pie half plain half pepperoni. THE DELIVERY BOY WALKED TO MY HOUSE but the Pizza still arrived fairly quickly. but when i opened the box it was soaked in grease. The pizza was so soggy i couldnt even pick  up a slice. It was literally a box of pizza soup. The strange part was, it wasn't  even hot. The slices didn't  line up. It was as if they threw a bunch of leftover slices from the day and reheated them. I would have rather had an elio's slice from a school cafeteria. Won't ever order from here again.
Glacially slow line. And the blueberry muffin wasn't that good.
The pizza was really good. However the space seem extremely cramped and the cost was a little high being $4.50 a slice.

Recommended by a friend, so we came here after work to give it a shot. For a corner, hole-in-the-wall type restaurant this place was crowded and it was only 6:30pm.   My friend is right, one thing is for sure, this place is guaranteed to be safe as the law enforcement customers were packing more heat than the charcoal grill. 1/2 Chicken with Rice and beans, $5.00.  The chicken was juicy and delicious.   1/2 Ribs with Rice and beans, $5.00, not as good as the chicken, a bit tough, but my buddy tells me that it is usually tender. Good place to eat if you are in the area, but not really a place I would go out of my way to get to.w

To be honest, all BBQ joints in the Ironbound taste exactly the same.  These spots are absolutely amazing though.  They churn out decent BBQ and they all come with Rice and Fries.  They fed 7 of us for a grand total of $60.  Now that's chizzeeap!!  Now, what sets them apart from the other Ironbound favorite, Ferry Street BBQ, is the chicken.  The chicken here, most of the time, is very moist.  You don't expect that because everybody else's chicken in the Ironbound comes out the same, dry.

Came here a few weeks ago and the food was amazing-best brunch I've had in a while.  Our server was Brendan and he was so knowledgable about the restaurant and about the area. He gave us advice of where else we should visit while in town and nothing was a disappointment. I would recommend Orlin and Brendan!

WE waited on line for over half hour and was served chicken and chicken/lamb over rice without salad. And this was 7PM.  How disappointing.  An incomplete meal. You would think they would be prepared for their demand .

In a word: Repulsive. Got delivery of an incredibly greasy, slimy cheese pizza lacking in seasoning. It had no flavor and was overcooked, as were the rubbery chicken "tenders" and mozzarella triangles that were just too gross-looking to try: sloshed with tomato paste and breading the color of burnt sienna. This food actually made me nauseous. Never again. Recommend Cappies instead.
Roast Pork, I heart you!  Possibly the best sandwich in the city of Philadelphia?

The food was outstanding. The bread at the beginning came immediately and the butter was unbelievable. It added a sweet taste to the freshly baked bread. I was not a big fan of fish and chips (fried with fried) so I got a side caesar instead. But both were outstanding dishes and I would eat there almost every day. The fish was crispy and yum yum yum. The caesar was amazing but I would recommend asking for dressing on the side. The dessert took a while to come but it was amazing. The chocolate cream pie was rich and was much like pudding. And it was covered in whipped cream. (Maybe too much) Overall, this restaurant  was so good and yummy. (The train that comes by is pretty cool too at a quarter to seven) **This review was written by my 10 year old - but I endorse it!
Excellent food, super authentic. I would have given it 5 stars if it wasn't because we were expecting to sit at the table in front of the chefs
Amazing food with reasonable price....a must go! You will love it if you like unique flavors ans both indian and Chinese food
Great little place to satisfy the craving.  So many sandwiches to choose from.  Did i mentioned that this is cheaper than McDonald and Taco Bell.  Go try it out

Love everything about the place, except the tables being so stucked together! I guess is usual for a NY place!  Food is delicious and they do this rotation os special Margaritas.. A must if u like drink!!

Myself and 3 friends decided to do a cheesesteak taste tour of Philly to determine which place had the best cheesesteak. We picked the top 5 yelp locations, went to each one on concession, ordered exactly the same item at each place (cheesesteak with Provolone cheese and grilled onions), split it in 4 and gave our verdict. Findings as follows (in order of preference): #1 - Sonny's: soft bread, delicious cheese and flavorful meat. Our absolute fave. Next time we'd consider asking for more cheese to make it even more perfect. #2 - Pat's: a close 2nd. In comparison to Sonny's, the bread was slightly chewier, the cheese was more prominent tasting (an advantage over Sonny's), the onions tasteful but the meat was slightly greasier. #3 - Ishkabibble: the meat was on the dryer side and lacking in cheese quantity. Bread was decent and chewy. Flavor was decent. #4 - Geno's: food was a little bland and on the greasier side. Despite this, the cheesesteak was still tastey, but not our top choice. #5 - Jim's: the greasiest of all the cheesesteaks with the blandest meat. I would skip. Hopefully our little taste testing endeavor will help anyone visiting Philly for a brief time, looking to try the best cheesesteaks this city has to offer.

I had my birthday dinner at this restaurant and the food was delicious!  I had a steak medium rare cooked to perfection! The crab cakes seemed to be popular as all my guests ordered it! The service was great, and the restaurant itself is beautiful! The staff was very accommodating to my large dinner party, and the server was prompt with everyone's needs!
